agnews:train:11215.para: Newcastle emerged as strong contenders in the race for Wayne Rooney after Everton turned down Manchester United's 20 million pound offer, with Ameobi potentially serving as bait in the negotiations.

agnews:train:11250.orig: French investigators probe copy-protected CDs EMI and retailer Fnac face legal challenge over antipiracy technology that blocks discs from playing on some devices.
agnews:train:11250.para: French authorities are investigating CDs protected by copy restrictions, as EMI and retailer Fnac face legal challenges over antipiracy technology that prevents certain devices from playing the discs.

agnews:train:11314.orig: Vioxx Linked To Increased Cardiac Death A new study shows that the prescription drug Vioxx can drastically increase a person #39;s risk of sudden cardiac death, and that risk is greater if you take a higher dose, or if you take it for a long time.
agnews:train:11314.para: A Recent Study Reveals Vioxx Significantly Boosts Risk of Sudden Cardiac Death. This Risk Is Higher with Larger Dosages and Prolonged Use.

agnews:train:11408.orig: Thursday #39;s Golf Capsules Corey Pavin sank seven birdies and matched his career low with an 8-under-par 62 for a three-stroke lead at the inaugural Buick Championship on Thursday.
agnews:train:11408.para: On Thursday, Corey Pavin achieved a 62, which is 8 under par and his career low, by making seven birdies. This performance gave him a three-stroke advantage at the Buick Championship's opening round.

agnews:train:11439.orig: U.S.C.'s Star Receiver Will Not Be Reinstated Mike Williams learned Thursday that the N.C.A.A. had denied his request for reinstatement because of questions concerning his academic eligibility and amateur status.
agnews:train:11439.para: Mike Williams discovered on Thursday that his appeal for reinstatement had been rejected by the N.C.A.A., due to doubts about his academic standing and amateur status.

agnews:train:11442.orig: 4 killed, 54 wounded in three separate attacks in India #39;s restive <b>...</b> Residents of northeastern India were bracing for more violence Friday, a day after bombs ripped through two buses and a grenade was hurled into a crowded market in attacks that killed four people and wounded 54.
agnews:train:11442.para: Four people were killed and 54 injured in three distinct attacks in a turbulent region of northeastern India. On Friday, locals prepared for potential further violence following bombings on two buses and a grenade attack on a crowded market, which resulted in the deaths of four and left 54 others wounded.

agnews:train:11518.orig: Iraqis flock to shrine after deal Thousands of Iraqis walk through Najaf to the city's great shrine as a peace deal takes effect.
agnews:train:11518.para: Thousands of Iraqis are streaming to Najaf to visit the city's significant shrine following the implementation of a peace agreement.

agnews:train:11531.orig: Players refuse to let CBA talks become a distraction Don #39;t mention the NHL #39;s collective bargaining agreement in the Team Canada dressing room. The 26 players are polite when asked about the subject, but they #39;re not going to get into any heavy discussions regarding
agnews:train:11531.para: Players are determined not to let CBA discussions divert their focus. When brought up, the 26 Team Canada players are courteous, but they avoid delving into any detailed talks about the issue.

agnews:train:11637.orig: Pavin in Buick driver #39;s seat Corey Pavin finished with a flourish for one of the best rounds of his career and a three-stroke lead at the inaugural Buick Championship on Thursday at Cromwell, Conn.
agnews:train:11637.para: Corey Pavin, sitting in the driver's seat of the Buick, concluded his round with a strong finish, achieving one of his career's finest performances and taking a three-stroke lead at the first Buick Championship on Thursday in Cromwell, Connecticut.

agnews:train:11638.orig: Horror at execution of Italian journalist Enzo Baldoni Reporters Without Borders expressed revulsion today at the  quot;barbaric quot; death of Italian freelance journalist Enzo Baldoni, 56, who was executed in Iraq last night by his kidnappers, according to the pan-Arab TV news station Al-Jazeera and the Italian news
agnews:train:11638.para: Reporters Without Borders expressed profound disgust today over the "cruel" execution of Italian freelance journalist Enzo Baldoni, 56, who was killed by his captors in Iraq last night, as reported by Al-Jazeera and Italian news sources.

agnews:train:11681.orig: Sudan criticised over Janjaweed Sudan is allowing armed pro-government groups to operate at least 16 militia camps in the western region of Darfur, a human rights group claims.
agnews:train:11681.para: A human rights organization alleges that Sudan is permitting armed pro-government militias to run at least 16 camps in the western Darfur region.

agnews:train:11772.orig: Oil Steadies, Investors Wary Ahead of GDP  LONDON (Reuters) - European equities clung to three-week  highs on Friday as oil steadied around the \$43 a barrel mark.
agnews:train:11772.para: European stocks maintained three-week highs on Friday, supported by stable oil prices hovering around the \$43 per barrel level.

agnews:train:11839.orig: Bryant Rape Trial to Begin Today On one point, both sides agree: The sexual encounter in Kobe Bryant #39;s hotel suite was over in a matter of minutes. But that episode on a summer night in the Colorado mountains
agnews:train:11839.para: The Bryant Rape Trial Commences Today. On one aspect, both sides are in agreement: The encounter in Kobe Bryant's hotel room was brief, lasting just a few minutes. However, this incident from that summer evening in the Colorado mountains remains a point of contention.

agnews:train:12189.orig: Presidential Campaign to Nov. 2, 2004 (Reuters) Reuters - The following diary of events\leading up to the presidential election on Nov. 2.
agnews:train:12189.para: Presidential Election Diary Up to November 2, 2004 (Reuters) Reuters - Here is a daily account of events approaching the presidential vote on November 2.

agnews:train:12366.orig: US to Syria: Don #39;t interfere in Lebanese election BEIRUT: In the first such statement since President Emile Lahoud said he would stand for re-election as president earlier this week, the White House on Friday asked Syria
agnews:train:12366.para:
US to Syria: Avoid Intervening in Lebanon's Election

BEIRUT: Following President Emile Lahoud's announcement this week that he would seek re-election, the White House issued a request to Syria on Friday, urging it not to get involved in Lebanon's presidential election.

agnews:train:12416.orig: California pharmacies sue drug giants A lawsuit filed by San Francisco attorney Joseph Alioto on behalf of 19 California pharmacies accuses 15 major drug companies of conspiracing to inflate drug prices.
agnews:train:12416.para: San Francisco attorney Joseph Alioto has filed a lawsuit on behalf of 19 California pharmacies, alleging that 15 prominent drug companies have colluded to drive up drug prices.

agnews:train:12592.orig: Hewlett Packard gets new mp3 players...iPod style One of the biggest talked about items around the consumer electronics world was an announcement earlier this year that computer giant Hewlett Packard would be partnering with Apple to put out an HP-branded iPod.
agnews:train:12592.para: Hewlett Packard introduces mp3 players with an iPod-like design... This year, a major development in the consumer electronics sector was Hewlett Packard's announcement of a collaboration with Apple to release iPod-styled mp3 players under the HP brand.

agnews:train:12604.orig: Fed chief warns of  #39;painful #39; decisions WASHINGTON - The nation will face  quot;abrupt and painful quot; consequences unless the government moves quickly to fix the finances of Social Security and Medicare, Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said Friday.
agnews:train:12604.para: Federal Reserve Chief Alan Greenspan warned on Friday that the country will confront "sudden and distressing" outcomes if it does not promptly address the financial health of Social Security and Medicare.

agnews:train:12613.orig: FBI Suspects Israeli Spy at Pentagon -- Govt Sources (Reuters) Reuters - The FBI is investigating whether\Israel had a spy at the highest level at the Pentagon who\obtained classified documents about Iran for the Jewish state,\U.S. government sources told Reuters on Friday.
agnews:train:12613.para: Reuters reports that U.S. government sources have informed the agency that the FBI is probing whether Israel may have had a spy at the Pentagon. This individual allegedly accessed classified information on Iran and passed it to the Jewish state.

agnews:train:12667.orig: Siemens Says Cellphone Flaw May Hurt Users and Its Profit Siemens, the world's fourth-largest maker of mobile phones, said that a flaw that can create a piercing ring in its newest phone models might hurt earnings.
agnews:train:12667.para: Siemens, a global leader in mobile phone manufacturing, has acknowledged a defect in its latest models that could result in disruptive ring tones, potentially impacting both user experience and company profits.

agnews:train:12711.orig: Russia Confirms Plane Crash Terror Link A widely-suspected terrorist connection became an official claim when Russian authorities said they found traces of explosives in the wreckage of one of two passenger jets that crashed almost simultaneously, killing all 90 people on board.
agnews:train:12711.para: Russian Authorities Confirm Terror Link in Plane Crashes Official confirmation emerged as Russian officials announced the discovery of explosive residues in the wreckage of one of the two passenger aircraft that crashed nearly simultaneously, resulting in the deaths of all 90 passengers on board.

agnews:train:12770.orig: US team #39;s class clown grip-and-rips #39; his way to a pole vault <b>...</b> He #39;s a California surfer dude, an air guitar virtuoso -- and the US Olympic team #39;s resident class clown. Toby Stevenson also happens to be very good at what he does: the pole vault.
agnews:train:12770.para: Toby Stevenson, the US team's comedic relief and an expert air guitarist, has also proven to be a skilled pole vaulter. This California surfer is known for his light-hearted antics but excels in his athletic discipline.

agnews:train:12792.orig: Iraqi rebels leave Najaf shrine left. The fighters had defied US military firepower and the interim Iraqi government for three weeks. accept a peace deal to halt the fighting, after a day of violence in which 110 Iraqis were killed and 501 wounded.
agnews:train:12792.para: For three weeks, rebels in Iraq had withstood US military power and the interim government. They eventually accepted a peace agreement to end the conflict, following a day of intense violence that resulted in 110 Iraqi deaths and 501 injuries.

agnews:train:12799.orig: US horse hurt while winning jumping bronze; Ireland takes gold American rider Chris Kappler won bronze in show jumping Friday, but his accomplishment was bittersweet. Kappler #39;s horse, Royal Kaliber, broke down on course in a timed jumpoff and was taken from the Olympic
agnews:train:12799.para: American rider Chris Kappler secured the bronze medal in show jumping on Friday, but the victory was marred by a tragic incident. During the timed jumpoff, Kappler's horse, Royal Kaliber, suffered a breakdown and had to be removed from the Olympic competition.

agnews:train:12871.orig: Newman not happy with lackluster year The expression on Ryan Newmans face wasnt that of somebody who had qualified fourth for tonights Sharpie 500 at Bristol Motor Speedway.
agnews:train:12871.para: Ryan Newman didn't appear pleased with his performance this year. His demeanor didn't match someone who had qualified fourth for tonight's Sharpie 500 at Bristol Motor Speedway.

agnews:train:12994.orig: Nokia  amp; Vodafone help define Java - yawn TALK ABOUT HAVING a finger in every pie, Vodafone has come up with another software initiative to make mobile phones more advanced and cheaper to make for the business user.
agnews:train:12994.para: Vodafone and Nokia are involved in a new Java-based software project aimed at enhancing mobile phones and reducing their production costs for business users, which just goes to show how diverse their initiatives are.

agnews:train:13113.orig: #39;Gamble #39; pays off for Trulli and Alonso Jarno Trulli grabbed his second pole position of the season at Spa on Saturday after taking a gamble and qualifying on intermediate tyres.
agnews:train:13113.para: Trulli and Alonso's risky strategy paid off handsomely as Trulli secured his second pole position of the season at Spa by qualifying with intermediate tyres.

agnews:train:13128.orig: Relay debacle ends Jones #39; jinxed games HERE in the land of myth, that familiar god of sports -- karma -- threw a bolt of lightning into the Olympic stadium yesterday. Marion Jones lunged desperately with her baton in the 4 x 100m relay final, but couldn #39;t reach her target.
agnews:train:13128.para: In this realm of legends, the sports deity known as karma struck the Olympic stadium with a lightning bolt yesterday. Marion Jones made a frantic attempt to pass the baton in the 4 x 100m relay final, but failed to connect with her teammate.

agnews:train:13219.orig: Bush Acknowledges  #39;Time of Change #39; for Workers President Bush on Saturday acknowledged US manufacturing workers have seen a  quot;time of change quot; in the economy but said his private sector-based policies were the way to boost growth.
agnews:train:13219.para: President Bush recognized on Saturday that US manufacturing workers are experiencing a period of change in the economy. However, he maintained that his focus on private sector policies is the key to fostering growth.

agnews:train:13222.orig: 2 Arrested in Alleged NYC Subway Bomb Plot NEW YORK - A U.S. citizen and a Pakistani national were arrested in an alleged plot to bomb a subway station in midtown Manhattan, and possibly other locations around the city, police said Saturday...
agnews:train:13222.para: In New York, authorities apprehended a U.S. resident and a man from Pakistan in what is suspected to be a scheme to detonate a bomb at a subway station in midtown Manhattan, as well as other areas in the city, according to police reports on Saturday.

agnews:train:13243.orig: Server Market Share Research has lately shown that enterprises are going to spend a lot of money on IT hardware and infrastructure during the rest of the year, and both Gartner and IDC have new numbers tracking ongoing growth in the server market.
agnews:train:13243.para: Recent server market share studies indicate that businesses plan to invest significantly in IT hardware and infrastructure for the remainder of the year. Both Gartner and IDC have released updated figures showcasing continued growth in the server market.

agnews:train:13270.orig: British Stun US in Sprint Relay Britain took a shock gold in the men #39;s Olympic 4x100 meters relay Saturday, pipping favorites the United States by one hundredth of a second.
agnews:train:13270.para: Britain delivered a surprising gold medal win in the men's Olympic 4x100 meters relay on Saturday, narrowly beating the favored United States by just one hundredth of a second.

agnews:train:13290.orig: US basketball loses to Argentina It didn #39;t need any dramatic comeback. No amazing flurry of three-pointers. No tough defensive stand. No bogus referee #39;s call in the closing seconds.
agnews:train:13290.para: The US basketball team fell short against Argentina. There was no thrilling late-game turnaround, no surge of long-distance shots, no strong defensive finish, and no controversial officiating decision at the end.

agnews:train:13374.orig: Russia Finds Trace Explosives on 2nd Plane MOSCOW - Russian investigators found explosive residue on the wreckage of the second of two airliners that crashed minutes apart, a security spokesman said Saturday, adding to evidence that terrorists breached security at one of the country's most up-to-date airports.    The high explosive hexogen was found on the Tu-134 airliner that went down Tuesday south of Moscow, said Sergei Ignatchenko, spokesman for the Federal Security Service, or FSB, Russia's domestic security agency...
agnews:train:13374.para: Russian investigators discovered explosive remnants on the second plane that crashed near Moscow, just minutes after the first one, according to a security official. This finding, reported by Sergei Ignatchenko from Russia's FSB, adds to the evidence suggesting that terrorists may have breached security at one of the country's modern airports. The explosive identified was hexogen, a high-grade explosive, found on the Tu-134 aircraft that crashed on Tuesday.

agnews:train:13409.orig: Mrs A could mean far more to London than Mrs B Many said these Games would be a shambles, but they turned out to be sensational. Sensational not just because of the virtual dope-of-the-day revelations but in their ancient concept and their modern execution.
agnews:train:13409.para: Mrs. A has the potential to contribute much more to London than Mrs. B. Initially, many believed these Games would be a disaster, but they ended up being spectacular. This spectacle was not just due to daily doping scandals but also because of the Games' timeless ideals and their contemporary implementation.

agnews:train:13474.orig: Canada Ties Slovakia in Hockey World Cup (AP) AP - Jarome Iginla scored midway through the third period to give Canada a 2-2 tie with Slovakia in a World Cup of Hockey exhibition game Saturday night.
agnews:train:13474.para: In a World Cup of Hockey exhibition match on Saturday night, Canada and Slovakia drew 2-2 when Jarome Iginla netted a goal mid-way through the third period.

agnews:train:13515.orig: New version of Windows planned for 2006 Microsoft Corp., world #39;s largest software maker, announced yesterday that it will release the next version of Windows operating system, code-named Longhorn, in the second half of 2006.
agnews:train:13515.para: Microsoft, the world's largest software company, announced on Tuesday that the new Windows operating system, currently known as Longhorn, is set to be released during the latter part of 2006.

agnews:train:13556.orig: Yemen sentences one to death, 14 to jail on terror charges A Yemeni court on Saturday sentenced one militant to death and 14 others to prison terms of three to 10 years on terror charges, according to local reports.
agnews:train:13556.para: On Saturday, a Yemeni court handed down a death sentence to one militant and prison terms ranging from three to ten years for 14 individuals on terrorism-related charges, as reported locally.

agnews:train:13578.orig: Here's the Nobel. Now Explain It to Your Grandmother. Life, and how it functions, is at the center of Dr. Gnter Blobel's research.
agnews:train:13578.para: Here's the Nobel Prize. Now, can you explain it to your grandmother? Dr. Gnter Blobel's work revolves around understanding life and its functioning.

agnews:train:13646.orig: Legendary double for El Guerrouj ATHENS -- In a historic 5,000-meter race, Hicham El Guerrouj of Morocco, who won gold at 1,500 meters last week, outkicked Ken enisa Bekele of Ethiopia in the final straightaway to record the first such double victory since the great Paavo Nurmi of Finland, El Guerrouj's hero, accomplished the feat 80 years ago at the 1924 Paris Olympics.
agnews:train:13646.para: In a historic 5,000-meter race in Athens, Morocco's Hicham El Guerrouj, who secured gold in the 1,500 meters just last week, outpaced Kenya's Kenenisa Bekele in the final stretch, achieving a double victory that hadn't been seen since Finland's Paavo Nurmi accomplished the same feat 80 years ago at the 1924 Paris Olympics.

agnews:train:13666.orig: South Korea Files Petition on Scoring Error With CAS After 10 days of deliberation, the South Korean delegation to the Athens Olympics finally filed a petition on the case of Yang Tae-young, bronze medallist in the mens gymnastics individual
agnews:train:13666.para: After 10 days of consideration, the South Korean Olympic team submitted a petition to CAS regarding a scoring discrepancy involving Yang Tae-young, who won the bronze medal in men's gymnastics individual all-around.

agnews:train:13705.orig: BROADSHEET/ COMPACT VIEWS Norwegian police trying to track down The Scream could do worse than check out the Blackburn Rovers technical area. Graeme Souness was on his feet and incandescent with rage for much of this game, and with good reason.
agnews:train:13705.para: BROADSHEET/ COMPACT VIEWS If Norwegian police are searching for The Scream, they might find some inspiration in the Blackburn Rovers' technical area. Graeme Souness was intensely angry for most of the game, and it was justified.

agnews:train:13842.orig: Equatorial Guinea coup plotters deserve firing squad: president (AFP) AFP - The alleged plotters of a coup in Equatorial Guinea are "blood-thirsty pirates" who deserve the firing squad, the country's President Teodoro Obiang Nguema said.
agnews:train:13842.para: President Teodoro Obiang Nguema described the alleged coup plotters in Equatorial Guinea as "blood-thirsty pirates" and stated that they should face the firing squad.

agnews:train:13931.orig: Ward Wins Gold Andre Ward beats Magomed Aripgadjiev of Belarus for gold in the light heavyweight division.
agnews:train:13931.para: Andre Ward secures the gold medal by defeating Magomed Aripgadjiev from Belarus in the light heavyweight category.

agnews:train:13945.orig: Olympics: Baldini wins Olympic men #39;s marathon marred by <b>...</b> ATHENS : Stefano Baldini of Italy won a dramatic men #39;s marathon at the Olympic Gamesafter long-time race leader Vanderlei de Lima of Brazil was attacked by a spectator in the latter stages of the race.
agnews:train:13945.para:
Olympics: Baldini Secures Men's Marathon Victory Amidst Tragedy

ATHENS: Stefano Baldini from Italy emerged victorious in the men's marathon at the Olympic Games, following a dramatic turn of events where Brazil's Vanderlei de Lima, who had been leading for much of the race, was attacked by a spectator near the end.

agnews:train:13965.orig: Conoco Said in Talks for 25 of LUKoil US oil major ConocoPhillips is seeking to buy up to 25 percent in oil giant LUKoil to add billions of barrels of reserves to its books, an industry source familiar with the matter said Friday.
agnews:train:13965.para: An industry source familiar with the matter reported on Friday that ConocoPhillips is in discussions to acquire up to 25 percent of LUKoil, aiming to boost its reserves by billions of barrels.

agnews:train:14002.orig: Ochoa wins LPGA Wachovia Classic Lorena Ochoa birdied three of the last four holes Sunday to overcome a five-stroke deficit and win the Wachovia LPGA Classic. Ochoa finished with a 65 to score a 19-under 269 for her second career win.
agnews:train:14002.para: On Sunday, Ochoa birdied three of the final four holes, turning a five-stroke deficit into a victory at the Wachovia LPGA Classic. She concluded with a 65, totaling 269 at 19 under par, securing her second career title.

agnews:train:14041.orig: Agni II missile test-fired again Indias indigenously built Agni II missile was successfully test-fired again from the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)s missile testing range at the Wheelers Island in the Bay of Bengal off the Orissa coast on Sunday afternoon.
agnews:train:14041.para: On Sunday afternoon, India's homegrown Agni II missile was successfully tested once more at the Defence Research and Development Organisation's (DRDO) missile testing site on Wheelers Island, located in the Bay of Bengal off the coast of Orissa.

agnews:train:14046.orig: Palestinians Mourn Hero's Defeat in Arab Pop Contest  SALFIT, West Bank (Reuters) - Thousands of Palestinians  gathered at a West Bank park on Sunday, defying Islamic  militant disapproval, in the hope their pop idol would become  the first Palestinian to win an Arab song contest.
agnews:train:14046.para: Thousands of Palestinians gathered at a West Bank park on Sunday, despite opposition from Islamic militants, to support their pop star in the Arab song contest, hoping she would become the first Palestinian to win.

agnews:train:14049.orig: Silicon to help explain origins of the universe ST. PETERS, Mo. - The origins of the universe could soon be uncovered with the help of silicon and other materials. In 2001, NASA launched a robotic spacecraft from Cape Canaveral, Fla.
agnews:train:14049.para: ST. PETERS, Mo. - The mysteries of the universe's beginnings might soon be revealed thanks to silicon and other materials. In 2001, NASA sent a robotic spacecraft into space from Cape Canaveral, Fla.

agnews:train:14052.orig: Spectator assaults marathon leader Italian Stefano Baldini won the Olympic men #39;s marathon overnight after a spectator dashed on to the course late in the race and bundled the then leader Vanderlei de Lima into the crowd.
agnews:train:14052.para: In the Olympic men's marathon, Stefano Baldini emerged victorious. Just as the race neared its end, a spectator entered the course and pushed the then-leading runner, Vanderlei de Lima, into the crowd.

agnews:train:14057.orig: Bolton hands Liverpool first EPL loss Liverpool slumped to its first league defeat of the season on Sunday, surrending a first-half goal to 1-0 at Bolton. Kevin Davies scored in the 38th minute on a Henrik Pedersen cross, lifting
agnews:train:14057.para: On Sunday, Liverpool suffered its initial league loss of the season, falling 1-0 to Bolton. Kevin Davies netted in the 38th minute from a Henrik Pedersen pass, securing the win for Bolton.

agnews:train:14098.orig: US anglers big impact on fish stocks Recreational anglers may be responsible for landing nearly 25 percent of over-fished salt water species caught off US coasts, a study released Thursday suggests.
agnews:train:14098.para: A study released on Thursday indicates that recreational anglers might account for nearly 25 percent of the over-fished saltwater species caught along US coastlines.

agnews:train:14143.orig: Stunning triumph vindicates relay team Four British athletes sat together on the poolside terrace of the Politia Tennis Club yesterday, the realisation of what they had done the previous evening soaking into them like
agnews:train:14143.para: Four British athletes gathered on the poolside terrace of the Politia Tennis Club yesterday, the full impact of their achievement from the previous evening sinking in deeply.

agnews:train:14229.orig: Higher Technology for Drier Courts to Prevent a Rain-Soaked Repeat After heavy rainfall forced numerous delays last year, the United States Tennis Association will rely on new machines to dry the courts faster.
agnews:train:14229.para: Following significant delays due to rain last year, the United States Tennis Association will utilize advanced machinery to expedite the drying process of the courts.

agnews:train:14268.orig: Iran, Iraq want to bury the past TEHRAN, Aug 29: Iran and Iraq want to bury the past and start a new era of neighbourly relations, visiting Iraqi interim Deputy Prime Minister Barham Salih said here on Sunday.
agnews:train:14268.para: Iran and Iraq aim to put the past behind them and embark on a new chapter of friendly neighborhood ties, according to Iraqi interim Deputy Prime Minister Barham Salih, who made the statement in Tehran on Sunday.

agnews:train:14485.orig: Pulling the PBA Out of the Gutter Rob Glaser and his geek pals from Microsoft wanted to revive pro bowling. So they bought the whole damned league. By Tom McNichol from Wired magazine.
agnews:train:14485.para: Reviving Pro Bowling: Rob Glaser and His Microsoft Colleagues Rescued the Entire League from Decline. Adapted from an article by Tom McNichol in Wired magazine.

agnews:train:14538.orig: MRPL to invest Rs 1,300 crore The Mangalore Refineries and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) proposed to invest Rs 1,300 crore over a period of time in improving plant and upgrading products, Oil and Natural Gas Corp Ltd (ONGC) Chairman Subir Raha said today.
agnews:train:14538.para: Mangalore Refineries and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) plans to allocate Rs 1,300 crore over time for enhancing its facilities and upgrading its products, according to ONGC Chairman Subir Raha.

agnews:train:14756.orig: Langer fills out a strong team for the Ryder Cup Well, it #39;s not quite great, but it might be good enough to do the job. With the conclusion of the BMW International Open on Sunday came also the final reckoning in the constitution of the Europe Ryder Cup team.
agnews:train:14756.para: Langer has assembled a robust team for the Ryder Cup, though it may not be perfect. Following the conclusion of the BMW International Open on Sunday, this also marked the final determination of the European Ryder Cup squad.

agnews:train:14773.orig: Republicans Sharpen Attacks on Kerry NEW YORK - Republicans sharpened their attacks on John Kerry ahead of the opening of their national convention Monday, with Sen. John McCain suggesting it was fair game to criticize the Democratic candidate's anti-war protests three decades ago...
agnews:train:14773.para: Republicans Intensify Criticism of Kerry NEW YORK - As the Republican national convention kicked off on Monday, the party intensified its criticism of John Kerry, including Senator John McCain implying that it was permissible to question Kerry's anti-war demonstrations from three decades ago.

agnews:train:14865.orig: Thanks And Good Riddance To Sir Bobby Who do you think is more disappointed by the departure of Sir Bobby of Robson? Do you think it will be the News of the World or Barclaycard?
agnews:train:14865.para: Thanks and Farewell to Sir Bobby. Who do you reckon is sadder about Sir Bobby Robson's departure—the News of the World or Barclaycard?

agnews:train:14915.orig: Juniper boosts end-point security Juniper Networks is beefing up security on its VPN gear to make sure that machines connecting to a network are safe. On Monday, the company announced updates to its NetScreen Secure Access SSL VPN product.
agnews:train:14915.para:
Juniper Enhances Endpoint Security
Juniper Networks is strengthening security measures for its VPN devices to ensure that connected machines are secure. On Monday, the company introduced updates to its NetScreen Secure Access SSL VPN product.

agnews:train:15006.orig: Britain seeking support to stop stem cell ban LONDON - Britain #39;s leading scientific institution said yesterday it is calling for support from other countries to stop a possible ban on stem cell research as part of a global treaty to ban human cloning.
agnews:train:15006.para: Britain's top scientific body is urging international cooperation to prevent a potential ban on stem cell research, which could be included in a worldwide agreement aimed at prohibiting human cloning.

agnews:train:15092.orig: Microsoft Taking on Apple's Music Store (AP) AP - Microsoft Corp., hoping to take a bite out of Apple Computer Inc.'s highly popular online music service, is gearing up to launch its own Web site for selling songs over the Internet.
agnews:train:15092.para: Microsoft Aiming to Compete with Apple's Music Service (AP) AP - Microsoft Corporation is preparing to enter the online music market with its own website for selling songs, seeking to challenge Apple Computer's widely beloved music store.

agnews:train:15106.orig: Expedition 9 Crew Prepares for Final Spacewalk (SPACE.com) SPACE.com - The two astronauts aboard the International Space Station (ISS) will step outside their orbital home one more time next week during the fourth and final spacewalk of their mission.
agnews:train:15106.para: The two astronauts on the International Space Station (ISS) are set to conduct their last spacewalk next week, marking the fourth and final excursion of their current mission.

agnews:train:15218.orig: Bombing Suspect Detained At Afghanistan Airport KABUL, Afghanistan -- NATO troops in Afghanistan have detained a man at Kabul airport who had traces of explosives on his hands, a day after a US security firm was bombed, killing 10 people, including three Americans.
agnews:train:15218.para:
A Suspect in the Bombing Held at Kabul Airport
KABUL, Afghanistan -- NATO forces have apprehended an individual at Kabul airport who was found to have explosive residue on his hands. This occurred following a bombing of a U.S. security firm that resulted in 10 fatalities, among them three Americans.

agnews:train:15267.orig: High Court Petitioned on Cable Net Access Rule (washingtonpost.com) washingtonpost.com - The Bush administration has asked the Supreme Court to overturn a decision that requires cable companies to open their high-speed Internet networks to rival online providers.
agnews:train:15267.para: The Bush administration has requested that the Supreme Court revoke a ruling mandating that cable companies allow competing internet service providers access to their high-speed networks.

agnews:train:15437.orig: Interstate Bakeries falls on auditor report warning Interstate Bakeries Corp. , maker of Wonder bread and Hostess Twinkies, said yesterday its auditors' report may raise questions about its ability to continue as a going concern, sending its shares tumbling more than 42 percent. The company said in a statement that its annual report would again be delayed because of uncertainty over whether it will ...
agnews:train:15437.para: Interstate Bakeries Corp., known for Wonder bread and Hostess Twinkies, saw its stock drop by over 42% yesterday after its auditors' report raised concerns about its ability to operate as a going concern. In a statement, the company announced that its annual report would be further delayed due to uncertainties regarding its future.

agnews:train:15530.orig: Volz in the clear over injury to fan Fulham full-back Moritz Volz will not face police action after he collided with a pensioner during the Premiership match with Portsmouth at Fratton Park.
agnews:train:15530.para: Moritz Volz, Fulham's full-back, is uninjured following his collision with an elderly fan during the Premiership game against Portsmouth at Fratton Park, and as a result, he won't face any police action.

agnews:train:15632.orig: Convention Boasts State-of-Art Technology The Republican National Convention has more than 40,000 miles of cabling to operate high speed computer systems, telephone lines and live television broadcasts.
agnews:train:15632.para: The Republican National Convention features advanced technology with over 40,000 miles of cabling for high-speed computer networks, telephone connections, and live TV feeds.

agnews:train:15827.orig: Video Game Sales Seen Pausing After Record 2003 (Reuters) Reuters - Video game sales soared to a record\ #36;18.2 billion last year, but the days of strong growth are on\pause as players await a new generation of consoles in 2005 and\2006, a new study showed on Wednesday.
agnews:train:15827.para: Video game sales hit a record high of $18.2 billion in 2003, but robust growth is expected to slow down as consumers wait for the next generation of consoles in 2005 and 2006, according to a recent study released on Wednesday.

agnews:train:15883.orig: UK no longer top asylum nation The UK has been replaced by France as the top destination for asylum seekers in the industrialised world, says the UN.
agnews:train:15883.para: The UN reports that France has now become the leading destination for asylum seekers among industrialized countries, surpassing the UK.

agnews:train:15913.orig: For CEOs, offshoring pays U.S. companies that send the most jobs overseas handsomely reward their CEOs, a new study says.
agnews:train:15913.para: A recent study indicates that CEOs of U.S. companies which outsource the greatest number of jobs receive substantial rewards as a result of this practice.

agnews:train:16074.orig: Miss Universe, Olympians in Australia Poll Bout  SYDNEY (Reuters) - The first face-to-face bout in  Australia's election campaign was staged inside an airport  hangar on Wednesday with prime ministerial contenders sparring  with Miss Universe and hundreds of Olympians before a phalanx  of cameras.
agnews:train:16074.para: In Sydney, the initial in-person clash of Australia's election campaign took place in an airport hangar on Wednesday, where leading contenders for prime minister faced off against Miss Universe and numerous Olympians, all captured by a lineup of cameras.

agnews:train:16130.orig: Microsoft strips Longhorn of WinFS NEW YORK, September 1 (New Ratings) - Microsoft (MSFT.NAS) reportedly intends to ship Longhorn, its next version of Windows operating system, without WinFS, the next-generation file system.
agnews:train:16130.para: Microsoft is set to release Longhorn, its upcoming Windows operating system, without including WinFS, the advanced file system it was originally planned to feature.

agnews:train:16202.orig: Tougher policy in works In the wake of leaked grand jury testimony that implicated superstars Barry Bonds and Jason Giambi in the BALCO steroid scandal, Major League Baseball and the Players Association may be close to forging a tougher new policy on drug testing.
agnews:train:16202.para: In response to the leaked grand jury testimony linking Barry Bonds and Jason Giambi to the BALCO steroid scandal, Major League Baseball and the Players Association might soon agree on a more stringent drug-testing policy.

agnews:train:16366.orig: Mitsubishi Pleads Not Guilty to Cover-Up TOKYO Sept. 1, 2004 - Mitsubishi Motors Corp. and three former executives pleaded not guilty Wednesday to falsifying data on a vehicle defect that caused a wheel to fly off a truck and kill a pedestrian, the company said.
agnews:train:16366.para: Mitsubishi Motors Corp. and three former executives denied guilt on Wednesday in a case involving the falsification of data related to a vehicle defect that led to a truck wheel detaching and resulted in a pedestrian's death, according to the company.

agnews:train:16395.orig: Cybercafe nets nomination for style A funky Melbourne cybercafe in an Elizabeth Street basement has been named one of the best internet cafes in the world in a survey by search engine company Yahoo.
agnews:train:16395.para: A stylish Melbourne cybercafe located in the basement of Elizabeth Street has been recognized as one of the top internet cafes globally, according to a survey conducted by Yahoo.

agnews:train:16487.orig: Stocks Are Mixed as Oil Prices Rise Stocks were trading mixed today following a lower reading on manufacturing activity and a spike in oil prices
agnews:train:16487.para: Today, stock markets showed mixed performance after a weaker manufacturing report and a sudden increase in oil prices.

agnews:train:16565.orig: Mountaineers prepared to lead the new-look Big East The Mountaineers open the season in The Associated Press top 10 for the first time in school history. There are great expectations in Morgantown these days.
agnews:train:16565.para: The Mountaineers are set to kick off the season in the AP top 10 for the first time ever, and there's a lot of anticipation in Morgantown.

agnews:train:16702.orig: Three Killed in Rush for IKEA Vouchers Three men were trampled to death in a rush to claim vouchers at the first IKEA furniture showroom in Saudi Arabia Wednesday, hospital officials said.
agnews:train:16702.para: In Saudi Arabia, three individuals died after being trampled during a rush to collect vouchers at the inaugural IKEA furniture store on Wednesday, according to hospital authorities.

agnews:train:16735.orig: Longhorn cuts delay Microsoft Business Framework By cutting WinFS from Longhorn and indefinitely delaying the storage system, Microsoft Corp. has also again delayed the Microsoft Business Framework (MBF), a new Windows programming layer that is closely tied to WinFS.
agnews:train:16735.para: By removing WinFS from Longhorn and indefinitely postponing the storage system, Microsoft has once more pushed back the Microsoft Business Framework (MBF), a key Windows programming layer that is closely linked to WinFS.

agnews:train:16772.orig: Powell Says U.N Must Act Now on Iran Weapons  WASHINGTON (Reuters) -  Secretary of State Colin Powell  said on Wednesday the time had come for the United Nations to  take punitive action against Iran for its alleged nuclear  weapons program.
agnews:train:16772.para: Colin Powell, the Secretary of State, stated on Wednesday that it is now imperative for the United Nations to impose sanctions on Iran in response to its suspected nuclear weapons program.

agnews:train:16818.orig: Yankees unfazed the day after George Steinbrenner was noticeably silent after Tuesday night #39;s 22-0 loss to the Indians, but the Yankees #39; owner had some words for his club less than 24 hours after the worst defeat in franchise history.
agnews:train:16818.para: The Yankees remained unfazed the day after George Steinbrenner was notably quiet following Tuesday night's 22-0 loss to the Indians. However, less than a day later, Steinbrenner addressed his team regarding their worst defeat in franchise history.

agnews:train:16827.orig: Hundreds Held Hostage at Russian School, UN Demands Their Freedom The UN Security Council has strongly condemned the seizure of up to 400 people at a school in Russia, as the tense standoff enters its second day Thursday.
agnews:train:16827.para: The UN Security Council has firmly denounced the abduction of around 400 individuals at a school in Russia, as the situation remains volatile on Thursday, now in its second day.

agnews:train:16889.orig: Spam shows signs of levelling off but don #39;t hold your breath It might be too early to celebrate, but according to Symantec #39;s numbers, the rate of increase of internet spam is easing a bit.
agnews:train:16889.para: Spam appears to be stabilizing, though it's premature to rejoice. Symantec's data suggests that the growth rate of internet spam is slowing down slightly, but it's still too soon to declare victory.

agnews:train:16911.orig: U.N. Tribunal Convicts Bosnian Serb (AP) AP - The Yugoslav war crimes tribunal convicted a high-ranking Bosnian Serb leader Wednesday of torture, deportation, and other crimes against Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats, but acquitted him of genocide. He was sentenced to 32 years in prison.
agnews:train:16911.para: The Yugoslav war crimes tribunal found a prominent Bosnian Serb leader guilty of torture, forced displacement, and other offenses against Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats on Wednesday, though he was not found guilty of genocide. The judge sentenced him to 32 years in prison.

agnews:train:17037.orig: Sorry, E.T., but Parcel Post May Beat Phoning Home A physicist and an electrical engineer claim it is more efficient to send a long message as a physical package, a cosmic FedEx, than as radio wave or laser pulse.
agnews:train:17037.para: I apologize, E.T., but sending a lengthy message via physical mail might be more efficient than using radio waves or a laser pulse, according to a physicist and an electrical engineer.

agnews:train:17049.orig: Cubs scratch out a win MONTREAL -- If this were gymnastics, the Cubs would get low scores from the judges for awkward form at times in Wednesday night #39;s 2-1 victory in 11 innings over the Montreal Expos.
agnews:train:17049.para: In gymnastics terms, the Cubs would receive low scores for their awkward movements on Wednesday night, securing a 2-1 win in 11 innings against the Montreal Expos.

agnews:train:17183.orig: Eurozone rates unchanged at 2 The European Central Bank leaves eurozone interest rates on hold at 2, and upgrades its economic growth forecasts.
agnews:train:17183.para: The European Central Bank maintains eurozone interest rates at 2% and enhances its projections for economic growth.

agnews:train:17195.orig: Up to the Challenge The Redskins contend that last week's debacle in the secondary against the Rams isn't a true gauge of life after Champ Bailey.
agnews:train:17195.para: Facing the Test The Redskins argue that last week's poor performance in defense against the Rams doesn't accurately reflect their situation without Champ Bailey.

agnews:train:17256.orig: Firefox Toolbar: A set of search toolbars for Mozilla users Firefox Toolbar: A set of search toolbars for Mozilla users\\Yet another search toolbar! But fortunately unlike most Internet Explorer only toolbars it is for the users of the alternate open source browser Firefox and Mozilla. Firefox Toolbar is a set of free toolbars made by a company called Vpop Technologies ...
agnews:train:17256.para: Firefox Toolbar: A collection of search toolbars designed for Mozilla users. Another search toolbar option! Fortunately, unlike many toolbars created for Internet Explorer, this one is tailored for users of the alternative open-source browser, Firefox. Developed by Vpop Technologies, these toolbars are available free of charge.

agnews:train:17266.orig: NFL Game Summary - Dallas at Seattle Rice finished with 145 yards on eight catches, and Jackson had 113 yards on nine grabs...Testaverde broke Steve DeBerg #39;s NFL record with his TD pass to Copper, the 63rd receiver he #39;s hooked up with for a score...Alexander has scored 15 or more touchdowns
agnews:train:17266.para: NFL Game Recap: Dallas vs. Seattle - Rice ended with 145 yards and eight receptions, while Jackson had 113 yards and nine catches. Testaverde surpassed Steve DeBerg's NFL record with his touchdown pass to Copper, his 63rd receiver to score a touchdown. Additionally, Alexander has scored 15 or more touchdowns.

agnews:train:17267.orig: Update 5: European Central Bank Ups Growth Forecast The European Central Bank on Thursday raised its economic growth forecast for the 12 nations using the euro and kept its key interest rate steady at record lows as it waits for the recovery to firm up.
agnews:train:17267.para: Update 5: The European Central Bank Increased Its Growth Projections The European Central Bank, on Thursday,上调了对使用欧元的12个成员国经济增速的预测，并维持关键利率在历史低位不变，等待经济复苏更加稳固。

agnews:train:17296.orig: Microsoft hones SharePoint update The first major revamp of the collaboration package includes overhauled support, search and update features.
agnews:train:17296.para: Microsoft refines its SharePoint update, which now features enhanced support, search, and update functionalities.

agnews:train:17435.orig: Risks on both sides seen in Kobe Bryant civil case EAGLE, Colo. -- In pressing on with her civil suit against NBA star Kobe Bryant, the woman accusing him of rape will not have to meet the higher standard of proof required in a criminal case.
agnews:train:17435.para: In the civil case against NBA star Kobe Bryant, the accuser faces risks, but she does not need to meet the higher burden of proof typically required in criminal cases.

agnews:train:17449.orig: Target to pay \$1m in item price suit Target Corp. has agreed to pay \$1 million to settle a class-action lawsuit alleging it failed to stamp prices on merchandise, the fourth in a string of agreements over the past two years costing major retailers more than \$8 million in fees and millions more in compliance measures.
agnews:train:17449.para: Target Corp. has agreed to pay $1 million to resolve a class-action lawsuit claiming the company did not properly mark prices on its goods. This settlement is the fourth such agreement in two years, involving major retailers and resulting in over $8 million in fees, along with substantial additional costs for compliance measures.

agnews:train:17450.orig: 'Zippy' chipper despite loss A couple of the somebodies around here are going to walk away from Flushing Meadow with a million bucks apiece in their petty cash stash. You can call them champ.
agnews:train:17450.para: Despite the loss, the "Zippy" chipper players here are set to take home a million dollars each. You could certainly refer to them as champions.

agnews:train:17465.orig: Three Turkish hostages believed killed  BAGHDAD -- A Paris newspaper editor said there had been positive movement in the effort to free two captive French journalists yesterday, while a separate militant group said it had killed three Turkish captives.
agnews:train:17465.para: Three Turkish captives are thought to have been killed, while progress was reported in freeing two French journalists, according to a Paris newspaper editor. Meanwhile, a different militant group claimed responsibility for the deaths of three Turkish hostages.

agnews:train:17481.orig: Red Sox Sweep Angels Derek Lowe pitches effectively into the eighth inning, and Boston takes control of the wild-card race Thursday night by completing a three-game sweep of Anaheim.
agnews:train:17481.para: On Thursday night, Derek Lowe pitched well into the eighth inning, helping the Red Sox secure a three-game sweep over the Angels and take the lead in the wild-card race.

agnews:train:17591.orig: Security alert identifies Oracle holes Software security companies and US-Cert, the US government #39;s computer monitoring body, have issued warnings about security vulnerabilities in Oracle software.
agnews:train:17591.para: Security warnings have been issued regarding Oracle software vulnerabilities. Both security firms and US-Cert, the U.S. government's computer monitoring agency, have flagged potential security flaws in Oracle's products.

agnews:train:17619.orig: EU commission proposes new interpretation of eurozone budget rules (AFP) AFP - The European Commission said it had adopted a plan to adapt eurozone rules intended to control budget deficits in order to improve the way they work and their credibility.
agnews:train:17619.para: The European Commission has introduced a revised approach to the eurozone's budget regulations, aimed at enhancing their effectiveness and reliability in managing national budget deficits.

agnews:train:17664.orig: Calif. Schools Warned of Identity Theft California university officials have warned nearly 600,000 students and faculty that they might be exposed to identity theft following incidents where computer hard drives loaded with their private information were lost or hacked into.
agnews:train:17664.para: California University Officials Alert Nearly 600,000 Students and Staff About Potential Identity Theft Risks Following Incidents of Lost or Hacked Computer Hard Drives Containing Private Information.

agnews:train:17782.orig: Iraqi Sunni Leaders Aim to Build on Shia Peace Gains It has been a week since a peace deal was struck in the Iraqi city of Najaf, bringing an end to three weeks of fighting and opening the predominantly Shia city up to millions of dollars in reconstruction aid.
agnews:train:17782.para: Following a peace agreement reached in the Iraqi city of Najaf a week ago, which concluded three weeks of conflict, the city, predominantly Shia, is now poised to receive substantial reconstruction funding, marking a significant step forward.

agnews:train:17950.orig: Hundreds die in commando raid MORE than 200 people - including children - are believed to have died after the school hostage crisis in Russia came to chaotic and bloody end today.
agnews:train:17950.para: Over 200 individuals, among them children, are thought to have perished as the school hostage situation in Russia concluded in a chaotic and violent manner.

agnews:train:17961.orig: Job Picture Brightens with August Hiring The US job market brightened modestly in August as employers added 144,000 workers to payrolls and weak hiring tallies for the two prior months were revised up, the Labor Department said on Friday.
agnews:train:17961.para: In August, the US job market showed a slight improvement, with employers taking on an additional 144,000 workers. The Labor Department reported on Friday that weak hiring numbers from the previous two months have been adjusted upward.

agnews:train:18060.orig: EU fines 7 firms for price-fixing BRUSSELS Outokumpu, IMI and five other companies were fined a total of E222.3 million on Friday by the European Commission for fixing the prices of copper tubing used in household plumbing.
agnews:train:18060.para: The European Commission penalized seven firms, including Outokumpu and IMI, with a combined fine of €222.3 million for their involvement in setting fixed prices for copper tubing utilized in domestic plumbing systems.

agnews:train:18081.orig: Ch. 11 threat for US Airways flier miles US Airways is at risk of filing Chapter 11 bankruptcy, which has frequent fliers thinking about cashing in miles, Boston.com reports.
agnews:train:18081.para: Chapter 11 bankruptcy concerns for US Airways fliers: With US Airways potentially facing Chapter 11 filing, frequent travelers are considering redeeming their miles, according to Boston.com.

agnews:train:18121.orig: Statham Moves Forward Quarterback Joel Statham has emerged as the team's clear starter who will lead 22nd-ranked Maryland against Northern Illinois on Saturday.
agnews:train:18121.para: Quarterback Joel Statham is set to continue as the team's primary quarterback, leading the 22nd-ranked Maryland squad in their upcoming game against Northern Illinois on Saturday.

agnews:train:18214.orig: Spoon #39;s summer drought JD WETHERSPOON embarked on a fresh round of price promotions yesterday to win back drinkers after a dismal summer for the pubs chain.
agnews:train:18214.para: JD Wetherspoon, known as Spoon #39;, launched new price discounts yesterday in an effort to attract more customers following a disappointing summer for their pub chain.

agnews:train:18223.orig: Keller Plays for U.S. but Not for Club (AP) AP - Kasey Keller plays only in World Cup qualifiers these days. After starting nearly every game for Tottenham Hotspur for two years, he hasn't appeared once this season. Yet, he's been in goal for all three World Cup qualifiers for the United States, which plays El Salvador on Saturday at Foxboro, Mass., then goes to Panama for a Wednesday game in a pair of semifinal-round matchups.
agnews:train:18223.para: Kasey Keller, who recently hasn't featured for Tottenham Hotspur this season, continues to represent the U.S. in World Cup qualifiers. Despite not playing a single match for his club in this campaign, Keller has been the goalkeeper for all three recent qualifiers for the United States. The team is set to face El Salvador on Saturday at Foxboro, Massachusetts, and then travel to Panama for a match on Wednesday, both as part of the semifinal round.

agnews:train:18247.orig: Report: More than 200 dead after troops storm school The operation to end the school hostage crisis in Russia is over but more than 200 people have died after troops stormed the building.
agnews:train:18247.para: Report: Over 200 fatalities following military assault on school During the operation to conclude the Russian school siege, more than 200 individuals lost their lives after the military entered the building.

agnews:train:18366.orig: Away on Business: Islands of Refuge  CHICAGO (Reuters) - Today's highly stressed business  travelers may need islands of respite to restore the spirit and  calm the tensions that build with security checks, crowded  flights and navigating a car in unfamiliar territory.
agnews:train:18366.para:
On Business Trips: Seeking Havens of Tranquility  
CHICAGO (Reuters) - Modern business travelers, often under significant stress, might benefit from finding tranquil oases to rejuvenate their spirits and alleviate the tensions that arise from security screenings, crowded flights, and navigating unfamiliar roads.

agnews:train:18370.orig: Woods right on course There have been signs of danger he has read about, warnings of trouble told to him.
agnews:train:18370.para: Woods is aware of the potential hazards, having been informed of the risks and challenges ahead.

agnews:train:18526.orig: Pakistan swears in 27 more ministers for new cabinet ISLAMABAD (AFP) -- Pakistani President Pervez Musharraf on Saturday swore in another 27 ministers, three days after inducting a 32-member cabinet headed by newly elected Prime Minister Shaukat Aziz, officials said.
agnews:train:18526.para: On Saturday, President Pervez Musharraf administered oaths to an additional 27 ministers, following the induction of a 32-member cabinet three days earlier. The new cabinet, led by Prime Minister Shaukat Aziz, was recently elected, officials reported.

agnews:train:18580.orig: Judge Won't Delay Tobacco Trial  WASHINGTON (Reuters) - A federal judge on Saturday denied a  tobacco industry request to delay the government's \$280 billion  racketeering case against the industry which is scheduled to go  to trial on Sept. 21.
agnews:train:18580.para: A Federal Judge Rejects Delay Request for Tobacco Trial WASHINGTON (Reuters) - On Saturday, a federal judge refused to postpone the government's \$280 billion racketeering case against the tobacco industry, which is set to go to trial on September 21.

agnews:train:18589.orig: Pierce Beats Wimbledon Champ Sharapova (AP) AP - Maria Sharapova's drive to win another Grand Slam title got dashed Saturday when tennis' newest "It" girl lost to Mary Pierce 4-6, 6-2, 6-3 in the third round of the U.S. Open.
agnews:train:18589.para: In a surprising turn at the U.S. Open, Maria Sharapova's quest for another Grand Slam title was thwarted as she fell to Mary Pierce in the third round, with scores of 4-6, 6-2, 6-3.

agnews:train:18645.orig: Good Deals for Banks, Both Coming and Going With so few mergers and acquisitions these days and with fees for them shrinking, bankers have found a new way to milk more cash out of deals: working with both buyer and seller.
agnews:train:18645.para: Banks Are Finding New Ways to Generate Revenue As Mergers and Acquisitions Decline and Fees Shrink, financial institutions are now assisting both buyers and sellers in deals to boost their earnings.

agnews:train:18689.orig: NL Wrap: Giants Rally for Big Win  SAN FRANCISCO (Reuters) - Marquis Grissom hit a grand slam  homer and the San Francisco Giants rallied from a six run  deficit to defeat the Arizona Diamondbacks 9-7 in National  League play on Saturday.
agnews:train:18689.para:
NL Update: Giants Stage Late Comeback Victory

SAN FRANCISCO (Reuters) - In a thrilling National League game on Saturday, Marquis Grissom delivered a grand slam homer, helping the San Francisco Giants stage a remarkable comeback from a six-run deficit to secure a 9-7 win against the Arizona Diamondbacks.

agnews:train:18901.orig: Massive Hurricane Frances Smothers Florida (Reuters) Reuters - Hurricane Frances smothered eastern\Florida on Sunday with drenching rains and fierce winds that\ripped away roofs, trees and boat moorings and cut power to 1.3\million homes and businesses.
agnews:train:18901.para: Hurricane Frances, a powerful storm, blanketed eastern Florida on Sunday with heavy rainfall and strong winds that tore off roofs, uprooted trees, and dislodged boat moorings, leaving 1.3 million homes and businesses without power.

agnews:train:18918.orig: Pope Celebrates Mass Near Hilltop Shrine A frail Pope John Paul II traveled to a hilltop shrine near the Adriatic Sea on Sunday, putting three more Catholics on the road to sainthood during an open-air Mass attended by some 200,000 pilgrims.
agnews:train:18918.para: On Sunday, Pope John Paul II, in a frail state, made his way to a hilltop shrine close to the Adriatic Sea, where he led an outdoor Mass attended by approximately 200,000 pilgrims. As a result of the service, three additional Catholics were placed on the path to sainthood.

agnews:train:18975.orig: First-night nerves for England, France England and France opened their 2006 World Cup campaigns with frustrating draws while European champion Greece crashed back to earth with an embarrassing defeat in Albania.
agnews:train:18975.para: England and France experienced anxious first-match outcomes, settling for unsatisfying draws, as European champion Greece suffered a humiliating loss to Albania.

agnews:train:18978.orig: Former Saddam Deputy Arrested in Iraq Iraqi forces Sunday captured Izzat Ibrahim al-Douri, the most wanted member of Saddam Hussein #39;s ousted dictatorship, Iraq #39;s top information official told The Associated Press.
agnews:train:18978.para: Iraqi authorities apprehended Izzat Ibrahim al-Douri, Saddam Hussein's top former deputy, on Sunday, according to Iraq's leading information officer, as reported by The Associated Press.

agnews:train:19002.orig: Newbiz: an Unconventional Asset-The Past  WASHINGTON (Reuters) - When businesses consider their  assets, they may look at obvious things like products,  buildings, equipment, patents, even valued employees. But the  company's history?
agnews:train:19002.para:
Newbiz: An Unconventional Asset—The Past
WASHINGTON (Reuters) - While companies typically assess their assets by looking at tangible items such as products, buildings, equipment, patents, or even valuable employees, they might overlook one significant element: the company's history.

agnews:train:19058.orig: Yanks #39; righthander could miss rest of season BRONX -- New York Yankees righthander Kevin Brown underwent surgery Sunday for a broken left hand and is expected to miss at least three weeks and perhaps the rest of the season.
agnews:train:19058.para: New York Yankees right-handed pitcher Kevin Brown had surgery on his broken left hand on Sunday and is anticipated to be out for at least three weeks, with the possibility of missing the remainder of the season.

agnews:train:19071.orig: Coke to alter sales practices Coca-Cola on Friday agreed to alter its sales practices in some European markets, an offer likely to bring to an end a five-year investigation by the European Commission into whether the soft drinks giant was stifling retail competition.
agnews:train:19071.para: Coca-Cola has agreed to modify its sales methods in certain European regions, following a five-year probe by the European Commission. This move is expected to conclude the investigation, which questioned whether the company might be restricting retail competition.

agnews:train:19089.orig: Zimmer Defensive Coordinator Cowboys Need (AP) AP - Coach Bill Parcells has always had his own philosophy about defense, and he knew little about coordinator Mike Zimmer when Parcells joined the Dallas Cowboys.
agnews:train:19089.para: Coach Bill Parcells brought his unique defensive philosophy to the Dallas Cowboys, where he initially knew little about new defensive coordinator Mike Zimmer.

agnews:train:19128.orig: U.S. Muslim Leaders Undecided on Candidate (AP) AP - As both Democrats and Republicans sought their support, American Muslim leaders wrapped up their community's largest convention Sunday still debating whether to endorse a presidential candidate.
agnews:train:19128.para: As Democrats and Republicans both courted their support, American Muslim leaders concluded their biggest community convention on Sunday, still in deliberation over endorsing a presidential candidate.

agnews:train:19205.orig: Serena, Capriati, Roddick Advance at Open (AP) AP - Serena Williams served notice that her shaky knee is holding up just fine, sweeping past Patty Schnyder 6-4, 6-2 Sunday to reach the quarterfinals of the U.S. Open. She faces yet another matchup with Jennifer Capriati, who beat Ai Sugiyama 7-5, 6-2.
agnews:train:19205.para: Serena Williams demonstrated that her knee is in good condition, easily defeating Patty Schnyder 6-4, 6-2 on Sunday and advancing to the quarterfinals of the U.S. Open. She will next face Jennifer Capriati, who triumphed over Ai Sugiyama 7-5, 6-2.

agnews:train:19217.orig: Prosecutor to drop rape charge against Kobe Bryant Prosecutors in the Kobe Bryant rape case will ask a judge on Wednesday to drop the rape charge against the basketball player, a source close to the case said.
agnews:train:19217.para: A source close to the case reported that prosecutors in the Kobe Bryant rape case plan to ask a judge on Wednesday to dismiss the rape charge against the basketball player.

agnews:train:19622.orig: Warriors hold on against Celtics Troy Murphy had his fourth straight double-double with a career-high 30 points and 15 rebounds, and the Golden State Warriors won consecutive games for the first time this
agnews:train:19622.para: Troy Murphy achieved his fourth consecutive double-double, scoring a career-high 30 points and grabbing 15 rebounds, as the Golden State Warriors secured back-to-back victories for the first time this season against the Celtics.

agnews:train:19638.orig: Developers to gather at Intel forum This week, chip giant Intel is hosting its twice-a-year Intel Developer Forum, where PC hardware and software developers will hear the company #39;s plans for future products.
agnews:train:19638.para: This week, Intel is organizing its biannual Intel Developer Forum, and developers focused on PC hardware and software are expected to attend. At the event, they will learn about the company's future product plans.

agnews:train:19730.orig: Lebanese Minister Resigns to Protest Presidential Term Extension A Lebanese cabinet minister has resigned to protest parliament #39;s controversial decision to extend the term of Syrian-backed President Emile Lahoud.
agnews:train:19730.para: A Lebanese minister has stepped down in opposition to the contentious parliamentary move that prolongs the tenure of President Emile Lahoud, who is backed by Syria.

agnews:train:19808.orig: Pakistan, India to cooperate in energy exploration Pakistan Foreign Minister Khurshid Mehmood Kasuri said Monday India and Pakistan have decided to cooperate in exploring different energy sources in the South Asian region.
agnews:train:19808.para:
Pakistan and India Agreed to Collaborate on Energy Exploration
On Monday, Pakistan's Foreign Minister Khurshid Mehmood Kasuri announced that India and Pakistan have reached an agreement to work together in exploring various energy resources within the South Asian region.

agnews:train:19866.orig: Many Users Are Unfazed by Scaled-Back Longhorn Plan SEPTEMBER 06, 2004 (COMPUTERWORLD) - The next major Windows release, code-named Longhorn, is due to arrive so far into the future that many corporate users aren #39;t particularly bothered by Microsoft Corp.

agnews:train:24484.orig: Jamaica Possibly Spared Ivan's Worst Fury KINGSTON, Jamaica - Hurricane Ivan lashed Jamaica with giant waves and winds nearing 155 mph early Saturday, but as panicked residents braced for a direct hit, the storm unexpectedly wobbled and lurched west, possibly sparing the island the worst of its fury.    The change in course could be good news for hurricane-weary Florida, since Ivan may now head off into the Gulf of Mexico...
agnews:train:24484.para:
Jamaica Might Escape Ivan's Harshest Impact

KINGSTON, Jamaica - Hurricane Ivan unleashed powerful waves and winds close to 155 mph on Jamaica early Saturday. As anxious residents prepared for a direct hit, the storm inexplicably shifted its path and moved westward, potentially avoiding the island's most severe consequences. This unexpected turn could bode well for hurricane-fatigued Florida, as Ivan might now veer into the Gulf of Mexico.

agnews:train:26929.para: US hurricane forecasters warn that the most severe conditions could still lie ahead for the 2004 Atlantic season, given the pattern of above-normal activity in seven out of the last nine seasons.

agnews:train:27223.para: On September 13, 2004 (COMPUTERWORLD), Sara Lee Corp. is experimenting with RFID tags on certain product packages and shipping pallets, as they comply with a requirement to use RFID technology for items destined for

agnews:train:27303.orig: Kroger Profit Falls, Warns on Sales  NEW YORK (Reuters) - Kroger Co. on Tuesday posted a 25  percent drop in quarterly profit and warned it may miss a key  2004 sales target because of lingering woes from a Southern  California strike, sending its shares down sharply.
agnews:train:27303.para: Kroger Reports 25% Decrease in Quarterly Earnings and Cautions About 2004 Sales Forecast Due to Ongoing Issues from a Strike in Southern California, Leading to a Significant Drop in Stock Prices.

agnews:train:27421.para: On Monday, a U.S. air strike in Fallujah resulted in at least 20 deaths and 29 injuries. The Iraqi Red Crescent ambulance that was targeted in the attack is also shown in the AFP report.

agnews:train:27492.orig: Microsoft release patch to fix security flaw in Windows, Office SEATTLE -- Microsoft Corp. on Tuesday released a patch to fix a critical security flaw that could allow an attacker to infiltrate someone else #39;s computer, if the user was persuaded to open a specialized file.
agnews:train:27492.para: Microsoft has issued a fix for a significant security vulnerability in Windows and Office. The flaw could enable an attacker to gain access to a user's system if they were tricked into opening a specific type of file.

agnews:train:27513.orig: Microsoft Eyes Video for Business IM (PC World) PC World - Software giant teams with Polycom to boost sales of Live Communications Server.
agnews:train:27513.para:
Microsoft Seeks to Boost Business Video Sales with Polycom (PC World)
Software giant Microsoft is partnering with Polycom to enhance the marketing and sale of Live Communications Server, focusing on business video solutions.

agnews:train:27521.orig: Stocks End Barely Higher  NEW YORK (Reuters) - Stocks ended barely higher  on Tuesday  as oil prices rose and investors tried to anticipate the  economic fallout from Hurricane Ivan as it moved through the  Gulf of Mexico toward a possible landfall in the United States.
agnews:train:27521.para: Stocks Slightly Gain  NEW YORK (Reuters) - On Tuesday, stock markets closed with minimal gains, influenced by rising oil prices and investors' efforts to gauge the economic impact of Hurricane Ivan, which was advancing through the Gulf of Mexico with potential landfall in the U.S.

agnews:train:27624.orig: Weightless Trip to Nowhere Yields Thrills, Nausea (Reuters) Reuters - Fancy an airplane trip that takes you\nowhere, costs about  #36;3,000, and may make you vomit?
agnews:train:27624.para: An Expensive, Nauseating Journey into Nowhere (Reuters) Reuters - Feeling adventurous? How about a flight that goes nowhere, priced around $3,000, and might leave you feeling queasy?

agnews:train:27711.orig: Tokyo Stocks Open Lower on Profit Grab  TOKYO (Reuters) - Tokyo's Nikkei stock average opened down  0.15 percent on Wednesday as investors took a breather from the  market's recent rises and sold shares of gainers such as Sharp  Corp.
agnews:train:27711.para: Tokyo's Nikkei Index Started Lower as Investors Took Profits  TOKYO (Reuters) - On Wednesday, Tokyo's Nikkei stock average opened 0.15 percent lower as investors chose to take profits from recent market gains and sold shares of companies like Sharp Corp.

agnews:train:27727.orig: Citigroup apology on bond deals LONDON Citigroup told employees on Tuesday that it regretted executing a recent E11 billion bond trade that angered its peers in Europe and sparked an investigation by Britain #39;s market regulator.
agnews:train:27727.para: Citigroup Apology on Bond Trade LONDON - On Tuesday, Citigroup informed its staff about its regret over a recent €11 billion bond transaction that irritated European counterparts and led to an investigation by Britain's market watchdog.

agnews:train:27765.orig: Production Quota Hike Opposed by OPEC Ministers Several OPEC members argued that the organization should raise its price band, but ministers remained deadset against hiking its official production quotas in a bid to stabilize the oil market.
agnews:train:27765.para: Several OPEC ministers opposed increasing the organization's production quotas, despite some members advocating for a higher price ceiling. Their stance was aimed at stabilizing the oil market.

agnews:train:27818.orig: US eases Sudan sanctions threat The United States has toned down its threat of UN sanctions against Sudan, but said oil sanctions should be considered if the African nation does not stop the violence in the troubled Darfur region.
agnews:train:27818.para: The U.S. has softened its stance on imposing UN sanctions on Sudan, though it still suggests considering oil sanctions if Sudan fails to halt the conflicts in Darfur.

agnews:train:27827.orig: Doan Goal Lifts Canada to World Cup Glory Shane Doan scored 34 seconds into the third period to break a 2-2 tie and give Canada a 3-2 win over Finland in the championship game of the World Cup of Hockey on Tuesday.
agnews:train:27827.para:
Shane Doan's Goal Secures Canada's Victory in World Cup Action
Just 34 seconds into the third period, Shane Doan's goal broke the 2-2 deadlock and propelled Canada to a 3-2 triumph over Finland in the World Cup of Hockey final on Tuesday.

agnews:train:28059.orig: Before hiatus, Canada wins The hockey season started early this year and, after two entertaining weeks of the World Cup, it ends for who knows how long. Despite the impending announcement of an NHL lockout today
agnews:train:28059.para: At the start of the hockey season this year, Canada performed well in the initial two weeks of the World Cup. Now, the season is drawing to a close, possibly for an indefinite period. Today, there's an expected announcement about an NHL lockout.

agnews:train:28246.orig: Poll indicates crushing defeat for Megawati in Indonesian election An opinion poll published in Jakarta shows Indonesia #39;s President Megawati Sukarnoputri is set for a crushing defeat in next Monday #39;s presidential election run-off.
agnews:train:28246.para: An opinion poll released in Jakarta indicates a significant loss for President Megawati Sukarnoputri in next Monday's presidential election runoff.

agnews:train:28328.orig: India's cellphone market set to grow 20 percent each year: official (AFP) AFP - India's booming cellphone market is adding 1.7 million customers every month and will grow between 15 percent and 20 percent annually, a senior industry official said.
agnews:train:28328.para: India's cellphone market is expected to expand by 15% to 20% annually, according to a senior industry official. Currently, it is gaining 1.7 million new customers each month.

agnews:train:28331.orig: Best Buy 2Q Earnings Rise on Cost Controls (AP) AP - Consumer electronics retailer Best Buy Co. said Wednesday that second-quarter earnings rose on cost controls and improved margins to beat Wall Street expectations.
agnews:train:28331.para: Best Buy reported a rise in second-quarter earnings on Wednesday, attributing the increase to effective cost management and better margins, which exceeded Wall Street forecasts.

agnews:train:28492.orig: Three Beheaded Bodies Found in Iraq BAGHDAD, Iraq Sept. 15, 2004 - Security forces discovered three beheaded bodies Wednesday on a road north of Baghdad, and a car bomb exploded in a town south of the capital, killing two people amid a surge
agnews:train:28492.para: On September 15, 2004, in Baghdad, Iraq, security personnel found three decapitated bodies on a road to the north of the city. Simultaneously, a car bomb detonated in a town to the south of Baghdad, resulting in two fatalities, as violence escalated.

agnews:train:28509.orig: Alitalia pursues rescue talks with Italian unions MILAN : Alitalia headed into eleventh-hour talks with unions to clinch plans to avoid bankruptcy, after winning a key deal with pilots.
agnews:train:28509.para: Alitalia engages in final negotiations with Italian unions to prevent bankruptcy, following a crucial agreement with the pilots' union.

agnews:train:28539.orig: J.P. Morgan cancels IBM outsourcing contract The termination of the \$5 billion deal stands in opposition to a trend toward more IT outsourcing.
agnews:train:28539.para: J.P. Morgan has ended its \$5 billion outsourcing agreement with IBM, going against the current trend of increasing IT outsourcing.

agnews:train:28547.orig: Sudanese Peace Talks Hit Impasse (AP) AP - Peace talks between the Sudanese government and two rebel factions from the troubled Darfur region hit an impasse, and the sides agreed to break for at least three weeks before resuming efforts, one rebel faction said Wednesday.
agnews:train:28547.para: Sudanese Peace Negotiations Stalled (AP) - The discussions between the Sudanese government and two rebel groups from the strife-torn Darfur region have reached a deadlock, and both sides have decided to pause the talks for at least three weeks, according to one of the rebel groups, who made the announcement on Wednesday.

agnews:train:28593.orig: Three Decapitated Corpses Found North of Baghdad  BAIJI, Iraq (Reuters) - The decapitated bodies of three  men, their heads strapped to their backs, were found dumped in  bags by a roadside north of Baghdad Wednesday, Iraqi police and  U.S. officials said.
agnews:train:28593.para: On Wednesday, Iraqi police and U.S. officials reported the discovery of three decapitated male bodies, whose heads were tied to their backs, found in bags by the roadside north of Baghdad.

agnews:train:28682.orig: Tennis: 3 Seeded Players Knocked Out of Wismilak Tournament Three seeded players have been knocked out of the first round of the Wismilak International tennis tournament in Nusa Dua, Indonesia, with third seed Ai Sugiyama leading the way.
agnews:train:28682.para: In the Wismilak International tennis tournament held in Nusa Dua, Indonesia, three seeded players have been eliminated in the first round, with third-seeded Ai Sugiyama being the first to exit.

agnews:train:28713.orig: Adobe expands push for video, photo hobbyists The company releases new applications aimed at amateur photographers and video shooters.
agnews:train:28713.para: Adobe broadens its focus on casual photographers and videographers by launching new software tools.

agnews:train:28762.orig: PlaylistMag.com iTunes, iPod Web site launches (MacCentral) MacCentral - PlaylistMag.com launched this week as a resource for digital music enthusisasts using a Mac or Windows operating systems.
