agnews:test:395.para: Colin Jackson: Valuable Lessons from the Human Test Yesterday's Olympics showcased the spectrum of athletics, from the grueling endurance race that pushes the body to its limits to the mental battle of the sprint.

agnews:test:400.orig: Prototype copter-cam: Here, there, everywhere It can only remain aloft for three minutes but weighs less than an empty soft drink can -- and it can take and transmit pictures in flight.
agnews:test:400.para: Prototype aerial camera: It can hover almost anywhere, lasting just three minutes in the air, yet it weighs less than an empty soda can. It's capable of capturing and sending images while in flight.

agnews:test:404.orig: Taiwan votes on leaner parliament A vote is due to be held in Taiwan on plans to halve the number of seats in the island's famously heated legislature.
agnews:test:404.para: Taiwan is set to vote on a proposal that would reduce the size of its notoriously contentious legislature by half.

agnews:test:416.orig: US women avoid disaster, advance ATHENS -- Preliminary-round elimination would have been a disaster for the United States women. Desperate for a victory, the Americans avoided embarrassment by finally playing like a gold medal contender -- and like a team.
agnews:test:416.para: US women narrowly escape disaster, advance in ATHENS -- A loss in the preliminary round would have been a major setback for the U.S. women's team. With a desperate need for a win, they managed to avoid embarrassment by finally competing as a gold medal contender and as a cohesive team.

agnews:test:417.orig: Australia Airline Announces Fuel Surcharge Australian budget airline Virgin Blue announced Monday it will increase the fuel surcharge it adds to ticket prices from Aug. 26 because of soaring oil prices.
agnews:test:417.para: Virgin Blue, an Australian budget carrier, announced on Monday that it will raise its fuel surcharge effective August 26 due to rising oil prices.

agnews:test:429.orig: Stunt pilots to snag a falling NASA craft NASA #39;s three-year effort to bring some genuine star dust back to Earth is set for a dramatic finale Sept. 8 when Hollywood helicopter pilots will attempt a midair retrieval
agnews:test:429.para: On September 8, Hollywood stunt pilots are scheduled to execute a thrilling midair capture as NASA concludes its three-year mission to return authentic meteorite samples to Earth.

agnews:test:437.orig: Leeds students figure high on working curve Undergraduates in the city earn more than 90 a week on average, just behind Glasgow, Cambridge and Cardiff. Their hard-earned cash is likely to be spent on looking good and socialising, the
agnews:test:437.para: Leeds students rank among those with the highest earnings, averaging over 90 pounds per week, second only to students in Glasgow, Cambridge, and Cardiff. This income is likely to be spent on enhancing their appearance and enjoying social activities.

agnews:test:443.orig: Oil price down as Iraq fears ease The price of oil has fallen as fears about interruptions to supplies being pumped out of Iraq eased slightly.
agnews:test:443.para: Oil prices have dropped due to a reduction in concerns over potential supply disruptions from Iraq.

agnews:test:451.orig: Congo Ex-Rebel Group Pulls Out of Government (Reuters) Reuters - The former main rebel group during\Congo's civil war pulled out of a power-sharing transitional\government on Monday, dealing a major blow to the country's\already fragile peace process.
agnews:test:451.para: A Key Former Rebel Group Withdraws from Congo's Transitional Government (Reuters) Reuters - A major rebel group that played a central role in Congo's civil war has exited the power-sharing transitional government, significantly undermining the nation's tenuous peace efforts.

agnews:test:455.orig: Wariner Succeeds Johnson as 400 Meter Champion  ATHENS (Reuters) - American 400 meters champion Jeremy  Wariner succeeded Michael Johnson as the Olympic gold medallist  Monday with a personal best of 44.00 seconds.
agnews:test:455.para: Jeremy Wariner Takes Over as 400 Meter Gold Medalist from Johnson  In Athens, Reuters reports that American athlete Jeremy Wariner won the Olympic gold medal in the 400 meters, matching his personal best time of 44.00 seconds, thus succeeding Michael Johnson in the title.

agnews:test:458.orig: Chicago OKs Cubs to Play at Wrigley Field (AP) AP - The city gave the Chicago Cubs the go-ahead to play ball at Wrigley Field on Monday night after the stadium passed another round of inspections of repair work done on its crumbling upper deck.
agnews:test:458.para: Chicago Approved the Cubs to Resume Games at Wrigley Field (AP) - On Monday, the city granted the Chicago Cubs permission to play at Wrigley Field following successful inspections of the repair work on the deteriorating upper deck.

agnews:test:467.orig: Deal has S2io champing at the gigabit OTTAWA -- A local firm that says it can help shrink backup times at large data centres is growing its business thanks to an alliance with Sun Microsystems Inc.
agnews:test:467.para: A local company claiming to reduce backup times at major data centers is expanding its operations through a partnership with Sun Microsystems Inc., according to Deal has S2io.

agnews:test:472.orig: Arafat Meets With Gaza Critic A former Palestinian security minister who could be key to keeping order among rival factions in Gaza after an Israeli pullout held a fence-mending meeting Monday with President Yasser Arafat, officials said.
agnews:test:472.para: A former Palestinian security minister, potentially crucial for maintaining order among Gaza's rival factions following an Israeli withdrawal, met with President Yasser Arafat on Monday to mend fences, officials reported.

agnews:test:474.orig: Japanese joy and British tears IT WAS the night of the longest race and the shortest, a night of distress for Britain #39;s Paula Radcliffe and delight for America #39;s Justin Gatlin.
agnews:test:474.para: IT WAS a night of intense emotion, with Japan celebrating while Britain mourned. The evening belonged to America's Justin Gatlin, who won the shortest race, and brought sorrow to Britain's Paula Radcliffe in the longest race.

agnews:test:475.orig: SAP Gets \$35 Million Post Office Pact SAP has landed a \$35 million deal to help the US Postal Service overhaul its human resources systems. According to sources close to the deal, the agreement includes a \$21 million consulting component, and
agnews:test:475.para: SAP Secures \$35 Million Contract for US Postal Service's HR Systems Upgrade The US Postal Service has entered into a \$35 million agreement with SAP to modernize its human resources systems. Details from sources familiar with the deal indicate that this package comprises a \$21 million consulting element, among other provisions.

agnews:test:476.orig: US beats Germany 2-1 in OT, to face Brazil in women #39;s soccer final Heather O #39;Reilly, minutes after missing a wide open net, scored in the ninth minute of overtime Monday to give the United States a 2-1 victory over World Cup champion Germany and a place in Thursday #39;s gold-medal game.
agnews:test:476.para: The United States defeated Germany 2-1 in overtime and will play Brazil in the women's soccer final. Heather O'Reilly scored for the U.S. just nine minutes into extra time, after narrowly missing an earlier opportunity, securing the win and advancing to the gold-medal match on Thursday.

agnews:test:479.orig: Dollar Holds Gains, Fed Comments Help  TOKYO (Reuters) - The dollar held on to the previous day's  gain on Tuesday, supported by a retreat in oil prices and  upbeat comments on the U.S. economy from Federal Reserve  officials.
agnews:test:479.para: The Dollar Maintains Gains, Backed by Fed and Lower Oil Prices  TOKYO (Reuters) - The dollar retained its gains from the previous day, bolstered by a decline in oil prices and positive remarks from Federal Reserve officials regarding the U.S. economy.

agnews:test:483.orig: #39;Marathon mouse #39; doubles stamina Scientists in the United States have genetically engineered mice which can run twice as far as normal before becoming exhausted. The researchers say their finding could lead to drugs or gene
agnews:test:483.para: Scientists in the U.S. have developed "marathon mice" through genetic engineering, enabling them to run twice the distance of regular mice before tiring. The researchers believe this discovery may pave the way for the development of drugs or gene therapies that could enhance human endurance.

agnews:test:485.orig: CAO executives hand over passports Executives at the collapsed China Aviation Oil Singapore have voluntarily handed over their passports to Singapore #39;s police, a spokesman said Tuesday.
agnews:test:485.para: Executives from the defunct China Aviation Oil Singapore have willingly surrendered their passports to the Singapore Police, according to a spokesperson on Tuesday.

agnews:test:490.orig: Chiefs #39; offense too much for Rams in 24-7 victory The NFL #39;s highest-scoring offense is averaging two touchdowns every three possessions during the preseason. If Kansas City #39;s woeful defense can get its act together, too, the Chiefs could be in for big things.
agnews:test:490.para: The Chiefs' offensive prowess was too strong for the Rams in a 24-7 win. During the preseason, Kansas City's scoring attack is putting up an average of two touchdowns every three possessions. If their struggling defense can improve, the Chiefs have the potential to achieve significant success.

agnews:test:491.orig: Marathoning mice could have Olympian effects on obesity A molecular switch known to regulate fat metabolism appears to prevent obesity and turns laboratory mice into marathon runners, a Salk Institute study has found.
agnews:test:491.para: A molecular switch that controls fat metabolism seems to thwart obesity and transform lab mice into endurance athletes, according to a study by the Salk Institute.

agnews:test:504.orig: Japan to Deport Ex-Chess Champion Bobby Fischer (Reuters) Reuters - Japan issued a deportation order on\Tuesday against former world chess champion Bobby Fischer, who\is wanted in the United States for defying sanctions on\Yugoslavia, an immigration official said.
agnews:test:504.para: On Tuesday, Japan announced its intention to deport former world chess champion Bobby Fischer, who is sought in the U.S. for violating sanctions against Yugoslavia. An immigration official made this statement.

agnews:test:506.orig: Nairobi police disperse Maasai Police in Kenya disperse Maasai protesters in the capital who are seeking the return of leased colonial land.
agnews:test:506.para: In Nairobi, the capital of Kenya, police have dispersed Maasai protesters who are demanding the return of land that was previously leased during colonial times.

agnews:test:518.orig: Martian Weather Blamed for Loss of Beagle 2 Description: An investigation into the loss of Britain #39;s Beagle 2 spacecraft last December suggests the cause may have been unusual Martian weather.
agnews:test:518.para: An investigation into the disappearance of Britain's Beagle 2 spacecraft in December points to unusual Martian weather as the potential cause.

agnews:test:523.orig: US not involved in Afghan vigilante trial-official An Afghan court was following proper procedures in its trial of three US men accused of torture and kidnapping and the United States would exert no influence on next week #39;s verdict, a US official said on Tuesday.
agnews:test:523.para: A US official stated on Tuesday that an Afghan court was conducting the trial of three US men charged with torture and kidnapping according to the correct procedures, and the US would have no impact on the verdict due next week.

agnews:test:532.orig: Cisco and Microsoft Partner for CRM 8/24/2004 -- Cisco Systems yesterday announced a new Customer Relationship Management (CRM) Communications Connector for Microsofts CRM offering.
agnews:test:532.para: On August 24, 2004, Cisco Systems revealed a new Customer Relationship Management (CRM) Communications Connector designed for Microsoft's CRM platform.

agnews:test:533.orig: Apple Tops in Customer Satisfaction Dell comes in a close second, while Gateway shows improvement, study says.
agnews:test:533.para: Apple leads in customer satisfaction, with Dell following closely behind in second place, according to the study. Gateway has also shown some improvement.

agnews:test:534.orig: Sabre, NWA Trade Barbs Over Ticketing Fee AUGUST 25, 2004 -- The Sabre Travel Network yesterday responded quickly to Northwest Airlines #39; decision to impose a fee on all domestic tickets issued through global distribution systems, firing back with its own policy changes and concluding the
agnews:test:534.para: On August 25, 2004, Sabre Travel Network swiftly reacted to Northwest Airlines' move of adding a fee to all domestic tickets sold through global distribution systems. In retaliation, Sabre announced its own policy adjustments, marking the beginning of a contentious exchange between the two companies.

agnews:test:537.orig: Tiny telescope detects a giant planet A tiny telescope has spotted a giant planet circling a faraway star, using a technique that could open a new phase of planetary discovery, scientists say.
agnews:test:537.para: A small telescope has identified a large planet orbiting a distant star through a method that researchers believe may lead to a new era in planetary exploration.

agnews:test:539.orig: Playboy Posts Unused Google Excerpt to Web Site (Reuters) Reuters - Playboy magazine on Tuesday\posted to its Web site an unpublished portion from its\interview with Google's founders, which raised regulatory\eyebrows not for what it revealed, but for its timing -- just\before the Internet search engine's much-anticipated initial\public offering.
agnews:test:539.para: Playboy Released Unpublished Google Interview Segment on Its Website (Reuters) Reuters - Playboy magazine published an untitled part of its interview with Google's founders on its website on Tuesday. This move drew regulatory attention, not because of the content, but due to its timing—just prior to Google's highly anticipated initial public offering.

agnews:test:540.orig: Williams' Status at USC Still Unresolved (AP) AP - Standout receiver Mike Williams is all but certain not to play Saturday night when top-ranked Southern California opens its season because of continuing delays in the school's appeal process to the NCAA. After that, who knows? USC has applied to the NCAA for a progress-toward-degree waiver and reinstatement of Williams' eligibility.
agnews:test:540.para: Mike Williams, a standout receiver, is almost certainly unable to play in USC's season opener on Saturday due to ongoing issues with the school's appeal process to the NCAA. The future remains uncertain. USC has submitted a request to the NCAA for a progress-toward-degree waiver and to reinstate Williams' eligibility.

agnews:test:548.orig: ASCAP Shakes Down Burning Man for Music Royalties LOS ANGELES, CA -- Officials from ASCAP today indicated they intend to pursue music royalties from the organizers of Burning Man, an artist's gathering and celebration held over the Labor Day holiday near Reno, NV.   The unconventional event, held annually since 1986, has never paid fees for any of the music played at the event, says ASCAP.  "We intend to pursue all available avenues to get this issue resolved," said Tony Wilcox, ASCAP spokesperson.
agnews:test:548.para: ASCAP Plans to Collect Music Royalties from Burning Man LOS ANGELES, CA -- ASCAP representatives announced today that they will seek music royalties from the organizers of Burning Man, an annual artist gathering near Reno, NV, that takes place around Labor Day. The event, which has been held since 1986, has not previously paid for the music used, according to ASCAP. "We will explore all options to address this matter," stated Tony Wilcox, an ASCAP spokesperson.

agnews:test:550.orig: Second Prisoner Abuse Report Expected WASHINGTON - Inattention to prisoner issues by senior U.S. military leaders in Iraq and at the Pentagon was a key factor in the abuse scandal at Abu Ghraib prison, but there is no evidence they ordered any mistreatment, an independent panel concluded...
agnews:test:550.para: Second Report on Prisoner Abuse Released WASHINGTON - An independent panel has determined that the neglect of prisoner issues by high-ranking U.S. military officials in Iraq and at the Pentagon played a crucial role in the Abu Ghraib abuse scandal. However, there is no indication that these officials directed any mistreatment.

agnews:test:559.orig: UN organizes open-source software day across Asia The United Nations, through its International Open Source Network (IOSN) will organize the first annual Software Freedom Day on Saturday in an effort to educate Asian users about the benefits of Free and Open Source Software (FOSS) and encourage its wider use in the region.
agnews:test:559.para: The United Nations, via its International Open Source Network (IOSN), is hosting the inaugural Software Freedom Day this Saturday across Asia. The aim is to inform Asian users about the advantages of Free and Open Source Software (FOSS) and promote its broader adoption in the region.

agnews:test:563.orig: Jamaican Government to Provide Free Internet Access in Poor <b>...</b> Jamaica #39;s government on Tuesday announced a US\$5 million (Jamaican \$308 million) plan to provide free Internet access in poor communities across the island.
agnews:test:563.para: Jamaica's government announced a $5 million (JMD 308 million) initiative on Tuesday aimed at offering free internet access in underprivileged areas across the island.

agnews:test:568.orig: EU to probe Microsoft-Time Warner buy The decision is a setback for the two companies and their plan to acquire ContentGuard, a digital rights management firm.
agnews:test:568.para: The EU has decided to investigate the Microsoft-Time Warner merger, which is a blow to both companies and their strategy to purchase ContentGuard, a digital rights management company.

agnews:test:572.orig: Tiny telescope #39;s big discovery opens new doors WASHINGTON - A tiny telescope has spotted a giant planet circling a faraway star, using a technique that could open a new phase of planetary discovery.
agnews:test:572.para: A small telescope recently made a significant find by detecting a large planet orbiting a distant star, potentially paving the way for a new era in planetary exploration.

agnews:test:579.orig: UN says Afghan vote can legitimise postwar scene (AFP) AFP - Afghanistan has a chance for real political legitimacy when voters go to the polls in the country's first post-Taliban presidential election, the UN's envoy to the nation said.
agnews:test:579.para: The UN's representative in Afghanistan stated that the upcoming presidential election, the country's first since the Taliban era, offers an opportunity for genuine political legitimacy through voter participation.

agnews:test:583.orig: Pittman misses out Fani Halkia (1980), of Greece, clears a hurdle en route to winning a gold medal ahead of fifth place finisher Jana Pittman, of Australia.
agnews:test:583.para: Pittman is left out as Fani Halkia, from Greece, successfully clears a hurdle on her way to securing a gold medal, with Jana Pittman, Australia's fifth-place finisher, trailing behind.

agnews:test:585.orig: Ford to Repair Faulty Heated Seats in Focus Cars Ford Motor Co. said on Wednesday it will fix malfunctioning heated seats in 33,000 Focus cars, two-thirds of which were sold in Canada.
agnews:test:585.para: Ford Motor Company announced on Wednesday that it will address issues with malfunctioning heated seats in 33,000 Focus vehicles, with two-thirds of these cars having been sold in Canada.

agnews:test:588.orig: Dell May Soon Unveil More Consumer Goods -Analyst (Reuters) Reuters - Dell Inc. (DELL.O), the world's\largest PC maker, could announce an expanded selection of its\consumer electronics line in the next several weeks, a retail\industry analyst said on Wednesday.
agnews:test:588.para: A retail industry analyst told Reuters that Dell Inc., the global leader in PC manufacturing, might introduce a broader range of its consumer electronics products in the coming weeks.

agnews:test:591.orig: Northwest sues Sabre over ticket fees Northwest Airlines Corp. filed suit against Sabre Travel Network in the US District Court for the District of Minnesota alleging that Sabre instituted measures that will make it more difficult for the carrier to sell tickets.
agnews:test:591.para: Northwest Airlines Corp. has initiated legal action against Sabre Travel Network in the US District Court of Minnesota, claiming that Sabre has implemented policies intended to complicate Northwest's ticket sales process.

agnews:test:593.orig: Kuwait assures help on hostages NEW DELHI, Aug. 25. - Kuwait has promised to leave no stone unturned to ensure the safe return of the three Indians who were taken hostage in Iraq.
agnews:test:593.para: Kuwait pledges full support for the safe return of three Indian hostages in Iraq. NEW DELHI, August 25.

agnews:test:597.orig: U.S. Justice Department Cracks Down Internet Crime The FBI seized computers, software and equipment as part of an investigation into illegal sharing of copyrighted movies, music and games over an Internet "peer-to-peer" network, Attorney General John Ashcroft announced Wednesday.
agnews:test:597.para: The U.S. Justice Department Took Action Against Online Piracy The FBI recovered computers, software, and hardware in an operation aimed at curbing the unauthorized distribution of movies, music, and games via an internet peer-to-peer system, as Attorney General John Ashcroft announced on Wednesday.

agnews:test:600.orig: Belarus Bank Denies Money Laundering Charge A bank in Belarus has denied US charges that it laundered money for former Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein. Infobank, in a statement, said it has strictly followed international agreements related to the fight against illegal transactions.
agnews:test:600.para: A Belarusian bank has refuted US allegations that it engaged in money laundering for former Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein. In a statement, Infobank affirmed that it adhered to international agreements aimed at combating illegal financial activities.

agnews:test:602.orig: Global server sales on the rise Sales of server systems rose 7.7 percent globally in the second quarter to \$11.55 billion as demand for Information Technology remained strong after a three year downturn, market research firm Gartner said in a statement.
agnews:test:602.para: Server system sales increased by 7.7 percent worldwide during the second quarter, reaching \$11.55 billion, according to a Gartner report. This growth reflects persistent strong demand for IT, following a three-year decline.

agnews:test:603.orig: Oil Prices Alter Direction After a month-long rally that repeatedly pushed prices to new highs, the cost of a barrel slumped for the fourth day, leaving the price \$10 higher than year-ago rate.
agnews:test:603.para: After a sustained increase over the past month, which saw oil prices reach record highs multiple times, the price of a barrel of oil dropped for the fourth consecutive day, now standing \$10 above last year's level.

agnews:test:604.orig: Warner to Start for Giants This Week (AP) AP - Kurt Warner will start at quarterback for the New York Giants this week, although his competition with rookie Eli Manning for the regular-season job continues.
agnews:test:604.para: Kurt Warner Will Start for the Giants This Week (AP) - Despite ongoing competition with rookie Eli Manning for the starting quarterback position, Warner will take the field for the New York Giants this week.

agnews:test:605.orig: Pinochet Immunity Weighed by Chile Court (AP) AP - Lawyers pressed Chile's Supreme Court on Wednesday to uphold a lower court decision stripping retired Gen. Augusto Pinochet of immunity from prosecution, saying the former dictator should face justice for past human rights abuses.
agnews:test:605.para: Chile's Supreme Court Examines Pinochet's Immunity (AP) - On Wednesday, lawyers argued before Chile's Supreme Court to maintain a lower court's ruling that removed former dictator Gen. Augusto Pinochet's immunity, asserting he must be held accountable for previous human rights violations.

agnews:test:608.orig: MLB, Va. Officials Meet Chicago White Sox owner Jerry Reinsdorf led a team of negotiators from Major League Baseball in a three-hour meeting Wednesday with the leaders of the Virginia Baseball Stadium Authority.
agnews:test:608.para: Major League Baseball representatives, including Chicago White Sox owner Jerry Reinsdorf, held a three-hour discussion Wednesday with the Virginia Baseball Stadium Authority's leadership.

agnews:test:612.orig: Sistani Urges Supporters to Wait at Najaf Gates  BAGHDAD (Reuters) - Iraq's top Shi'ite cleric Grand  Ayatollah Ali al-Sistani urged his supporters converging on  Najaf on Thursday not to enter the battered holy city until he  arrived, a senior aide said.
agnews:test:612.para: Grand Ayatollah Ali al-Sistani, Iraq's leading Shi'ite religious figure, instructed his followers gathering in the vicinity of Najaf to refrain from entering the damaged holy city until his arrival, according to a senior advisor.

agnews:test:616.orig: White House Shifts Its Focus on Climate The administration issued a report indicating that emissions of carbon dioxide and other heat-trapping gases were the only likely explanation for global warming.
agnews:test:616.para: The White House转向关注气候变化问题，并发布了一份报告，指出二氧化碳和其他温室气体的排放可能是全球变暖的唯一合理解释。

agnews:test:618.orig: Charges reduced for Iraq jail MP MANNHEIM, Germany -- A US military policewoman accused in the Abu Ghraib prison abuse scandal had the charges against her reduced yesterday as a set of pretrial hearings wrapped up at an American base in Germany.
agnews:test:618.para: In Mannheim, Germany, the charges against a US military policewoman involved in the Abu Ghraib prison abuse case were lowered yesterday, concluding a series of pretrial hearings at an American base there.

agnews:test:628.orig: BlackRock Buys State Street Research  NEW YORK (Reuters) - BlackRock Inc. <A HREF="http://www.investor.reuters.com/FullQuote.aspx?ticker=BLK.N target=/stocks/quickinfo/fullquote">BLK.N</A>, one of the  largest U.S. fixed income managers, on Thursday said it will  buy its far smaller competitor State Street Research    Management Co., marking the biggest takeover in the asset  management business this year.
agnews:test:628.para: BlackRock Acquires State Street Research NEW YORK (Reuters) - BlackRock Inc. BLK.N, one of the largest U.S. fixed income managers, announced on Thursday its acquisition of State Street Research Management Co., a much smaller competitor. This deal represents the largest takeover in the asset management sector for the year.

agnews:test:631.orig: British sailors bag bronze Britain's Chris Draper and Simon Hiscocks win bronze in a tense final 49er race on the Saronic Gulf.
agnews:test:631.para: In a closely contested 49er race on the Saronic Gulf, British sailors Chris Draper and Simon Hiscocks secure a bronze medal for their country.

agnews:test:638.orig: McClaren happy with striking duo Middlesbrough boss Steve McClaren believes Mark Viduka and Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink could forge one of the most dangerous strike partnerships in the Barclays Premiership.
agnews:test:638.para: Steve McClaren, the manager of Middlesbrough, is pleased with the striking duo of Mark Viduka and Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink, seeing them as a potential threat that could make one of the most formidable attacking pairs in the Barclays Premier League.

agnews:test:645.orig: Intel Gives Centrino Chip Line a Wireless Upgrade (Reuters) Reuters - Intel Corp. (INTC.O) on Thursday\said it has upgraded the wireless networking capabilities of\its Centrino line of notebook computer chips to allow broader\network access with improved security.
agnews:test:645.para: Intel Enhances Centrino Chip Wireless Features (Reuters) Reuters - Intel Corp. (INTC.O) announced on Thursday that it has improved the wireless networking capabilities of its Centrino notebook chip lineup, enabling wider network access while enhancing security.

agnews:test:646.orig: Panama pardons Castro 'plotters' Four men accused of planning to kill Cuba's Fidel Castro have been pardoned by Panama's president.
agnews:test:646.para: Panama's president has granted pardons to four individuals who were charged with plotting to assassinate Fidel Castro, the former leader of Cuba.

agnews:test:652.orig: No Evidence Of Abuse At Guantanamo, says Australian Foreign <b>...</b> Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer says a US investigation has rejected allegations that Australian terror suspect David Hicks was abused while in US custody in Afghanistan and Cuba.
agnews:test:652.para: Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer states that there is no evidence of abuse for Australian detainee David Hicks during his time in US custody in Afghanistan and Cuba, as per a US investigation.

agnews:test:655.orig: Japan Won't Have U.S. Beef Anytime Soon (Reuters) Reuters - Japan's lucrative market for U.S.\beef, ruptured by mad cow disease worries, is likely to remain\closed for the rest of this year, U.S. meat industry officials\said on Thursday.
agnews:test:655.para: U.S. beef exporters are facing a prolonged closure in Japan's key market, which is expected to stay shut for the remainder of the year, according to statements made by officials from the U.S. meat industry on Thursday. This situation is largely due to concerns over mad cow disease.

agnews:test:659.orig: 103 arrests for Internet fraud, related crimes since June: US (AFP) AFP - US authorities arrested at least 103 suspects and filed 117 criminal complaints since June 1 in a crackdown on various forms of online fraud, Attorney General John Ashcroft said.
agnews:test:659.para: Since June 1, US law enforcement has apprehended 103 individuals and initiated 117 criminal charges in an effort to combat various types of internet fraud, according to Attorney General John Ashcroft.

agnews:test:669.orig: Visit to a Potemkin village Gongzhong does not resemble any Tibetan village in Tibet. It is a village more from Epcot Center in Walt Disney World.
agnews:test:669.para: A visit to Gongzhong reveals a place that bears no resemblance to genuine Tibetan villages. Instead, it feels more like a themed village from Epcot Center in Walt Disney World.

agnews:test:673.orig: Nigerian Senate approves \$1.5 bln claim on Shell LAGOS - Nigeria #39;s Senate has passed a resolution asking Shell #39;s Nigerian unit to pay \$1.5 billion in compensation to oilfield communities for pollution, a Senate spokesman said.
agnews:test:673.para: Nigeria's Senate has adopted a resolution requesting that Shell's local operations in the country pay out $1.5 billion in compensation to communities affected by pollution in oilfields, according to a statement from the Senate.

agnews:test:674.orig: Goosen takes lead in the BMW Open Retief Goosen, a two-time US Open champion, grabbed the first-round lead in the BMW Open in Nord Eichenried, Germany, with a 6-under-par 66, while Colin Montgomerie improved his European Ryder Cup chances by finishing one stroke back on Thursday.
agnews:test:674.para: Goosen, the two-time US Open champion, secured the lead after the first round of the BMW Open in Nord Eichenried, Germany, with a score of 66, which was 6 under par. Meanwhile, Colin Montgomerie narrowed his gap in the European Ryder Cup standings by finishing just one stroke behind Goosen on Thursday.

agnews:test:675.orig: Hewitt cruises to quarterfinals Former Wimbledon and US Open winner Lleyton Hewitt cruised to a 6-1, 6-4 victory over Michael Llodra on Thursday to advance to the quarterfinals of the TD Waterhouse Cup.
agnews:test:675.para: Former Wimbledon and US Open champion Lleyton Hewitt easily secured a 6-1, 6-4 win against Michael Llodra on Thursday, progressing to the quarterfinals of the TD Waterhouse Cup.

agnews:test:683.orig: Bush, Kerry Bow to McCain's Wishes on Ads NEW YORK - President Bush and Sen. John Kerry bowed to the wishes of popular maverick John McCain on Thursday, as the president embraced the Republican senator's legal fight against big-money special interest groups airing negative ads and the Democratic nominee scrapped a commercial that featured McCain...
agnews:test:683.para: President Bush and Sen. John Kerry complied with John McCain's preferences on Thursday. The president supported McCain's legal battle against high-spending special interest groups that were running negative ads. Meanwhile, the Democratic candidate canceled a commercial that included McCain.

agnews:test:687.orig: Union leaders held under ESMA on Day 6 of strike New Delhi, August 26: The sixth day of the truckers strike on Thursday saw 12 more truckers being arrested under the Essential Services Maintenance Act (ESMA)in the Capital.
agnews:test:687.para: On the sixth day of the truckers' strike, which was Thursday, 12 additional truck drivers were detained under the Essential Services Maintenance Act (ESMA) in New Delhi, as of August 26.

agnews:test:689.orig: Vote 2004 - a guide to the primary Get ready for the primary with the Herald-Tribunes special news section profiling all the federal, state and local candidates in races in Tuesdays election.
agnews:test:689.para:
Vote 2004 - A Special Guide for the Primary Election
Dive into the Herald-Tribune's special news section to learn about all the federal, state, and local candidates running in Tuesday's election.

agnews:test:700.orig: Exec, wife give Stanford \$43.5 million SAN FRANCISCO (CBS.MW) -- Berkshire Hathaway vice-chairman Charles Munger and his wife Nancy Munger on Thursday donated \$43.5 million to Stanford University and its law school.

agnews:test:2754.orig: Supernova Warning System Will Give Astronomers Earlier Notice Duke University -- A Supernova Early Warning System (SNEWS) that detects ghostlike neutrino particles that are the earliest emanations from the immense, explosive death throes of large stars will alert astronomers of the blasts before they can see the flash.     SNEWS "could allow astronomers a chance to make unprecedented observations of the very early turn-on of the supernova," wrote the authors of an article about the new system in the September issue of the "New Journal of Physics."     They also noted that "no supernova has ever been observed soon after its birth."     Big stars end their lives in explosive gravitational collapses so complete that even the brilliant flashes of light usually announcing these extremely rare "supernova" events stay trapped inside, unseen by astronomers, for the first hours or days...
agnews:test:2754.para: A Supernova Early Warning System (SNEWS), which identifies elusive neutrinos from the initial stages of massive stars' catastrophic demise, will notify astronomers before the visible explosion occurs. This system, as described in the September edition of the "New Journal of Physics," could enable astronomers to observe the early stages of a supernova for the first time. Currently, no supernova has ever been observed immediately after its onset. yelp:train:130.orig:
I usually have nothing but good things to say about this place. I've dealt with Fran and others and have had very good experiences. However, this time was very different. I called to find out how much they might charge to install some brakes and rotors that I had, i was reffered to Mark, the mechanic. I made the appointment with him for Tuesday Sept 30th, he quoted me between $179 - $200 for the work (though the first person I spoke to quoted $150-$179) and told me to bring it at 8am and it would be finished the same day.when I brought it on Tuesday, Septempber 30th at 8 am, Mark forgets that i even made the appointment with him (or didnt bother to make a note of it) saying, ""oh, I thought you were supposed to bring this by yesterday"". He says I should expect this to probably be done before 3pm. 

I soon recieve a call from Mark at 10:25am, where he tells me the charge will actually be $240 (for four hours of labor + $13 worth of materials, before even getting started to see how long the job would actually take) and that the car would be ready by 3pm, if not possibly before that. Also for good measure he decides to randomly throw in, ""oh, and we don't take checks"". 

Th
yelp:train:130.para: I generally have only positive things to say about this place, but this time was quite different. When I called to inquire about brake and rotor installation costs, I was referred to Mark, the mechanic. I scheduled an appointment with him for Tuesday, September 30th, and he initially quoted me a price range of $179 to $200, though another person had previously quoted me $150 to $179. He assured me the work would be completed by 3 pm on the same day, with me dropping off the car at 8 am. However, when I arrived on Tuesday at 8 am, Mark seemed unaware of my appointment, saying, "I thought you were supposed to bring this in yesterday." He then estimated the total cost to be around $240, including four hours of labor and $13 in materials, without even assessing the work. Additionally, he mentioned that they don't accept checks.

yelp:train:679.para:
Sharia and Becky both didn't enjoy their experience. 

On a warm Tuesday evening, Boy and I visited Casbah. The restaurant was not crowded, and we were seated on the welcoming outdoor patio. Our waitress was very friendly and provided excellent information about both the drink and food menus.

We shared a bottle of Mission la Caminade (Malbec, French). This was a good, medium-bodied wine.

While many reviewers praise Casbah's bread and pesto, I found them unimpressive. I've had better sourdough elsewhere, and the pesto was merely average.

For an appetizer, I had asparagus soup with crab. The soup was cold and tasted fresh, but something was amiss; I barely managed to finish half of it.

My main course was orecchiette pasta with grilled chicken, cranberries, and a goat cheese cream sauce. Unfortunately, the dish was quite bland, with the cranberries being the only flavorful element.

Boy ordered ricotta cavatelli pasta in a marinara sauce with sausage and ricotta. Sadly, this dish was also tasteless, with the ricotta merely sitting on top without enhancing the flavor. 

We briefly looked at the dessert menu, but neither of us felt like ordering.

yelp:train:1071.orig: Nick's used to be good with the previous owner, that all changed. Which is pretty sad.
yelp:train:1071.para: Nick used to be well-maintained under the previous owner, but that's no longer the case, and that's quite disappointing.

yelp:train:1296.orig: I used to live in the area and would always patronize and recommend this business.  However with the last experience I will have to rethink that. My aunt and uncle ordered a gift basket for my grandmother for her birthday. When it was delivered it looked beautiful.  However once opened not so much.  Inside it was filled with....Dollar General brand goods. When I stopped down to tell them the owner and another worker told me what do you expect. If it was a busy season we would have gotten stuff from the strip. So moral of the tale. If you want to pay a whole lot of money for stuff from the Dollar Store you know where to go. To make it even more special the owner will provide a blank stare and a warm welcoming attitude that clearly shows she does not care.
yelp:train:1296.para: Previously, I frequently shopped at and recommended this store. But after my aunt and uncle's recent order, I may need to reconsider my stance. They bought a gift basket for my grandmother's birthday, and while it looked nice upon delivery, the contents were disappointing. Inside, it contained Dollar General items. When I confronted the owner and another employee, they responded that it's what we should expect during slower seasons. The moral is, if you want to spend a lot on Dollar Store goods, this is the place to go. Moreover, the owner's lack of interest is evident in her blank stare, despite her friendly greeting.

yelp:train:1629.orig: This rating is for the drinks only and atomosphere, and based on my personal taste a bit ok  a big bit. This is definately a \""I'm a young professional pittsburgh business person and I've arrived.\"" Status bar or \""I'm a young college girl and I've just had my first boob job care to help fund my nose job too?\"" Bar , I did not try the food becaused I moved from a place where we have awesome brazilian restaurant where fresh meats melt in your mouth accompanied by tart sweet grilled pineapple, and real slow cooked brazilian beans mmmm. Soooo after seeing how pittsburgh does Mexican food I'm not willing to drop my pennies to risk the disapointment of pittsbugh attmepts brasilian. \n\nThe bar is roomy with nice lounge seating which is nice for those who don't want to participate in the round the bar meat market. The guys make for fun people watching, either all suits or in their pirates jerseys. Or the occaisional jersey shore look a like meat heat in his v neck t shirt who is too good to attempt so much as a toe tap to the beat of the music. Then there's the balding old man with twenty something on his arm who already looks like she has botoxed up her face in an attempt to mirror
yelp:train:1629.para:
This review focuses solely on the drinks and ambiance, and from my perspective, it's just okay, albeit a bit more so. This place feels like a "status symbol" for young professionals in Pittsburgh or a "post-boob job" hangout for college girls. I didn't try the food because I come from a place with fantastic Brazilian restaurants that serve melt-in-your-mouth meats with tart grilled pineapple and slow-cooked beans. Given Pittsburgh's approach to Mexican cuisine, I'm hesitant to spend my money there and risk disappointment.

The bar is spacious with comfortable lounge seating, which is great for those who prefer to observe rather than engage in the bar scene. The patrons are entertaining to watch—ranging from well-dressed professionals to those in pirate-themed attire, or even Jersey Shore lookalikes in v-neck t-shirts. There's also an older man with a younger companion who seems to be trying to keep up a youthful appearance.

yelp:train:1799.orig: First time ever in Pittsburg and had to have Primanti Bros. Sandwich was awesome! (Cheesesteak) and a tall Yuengling to go with. Perfection!
yelp:train:1799.para: My very first visit to Pittsburgh, and I had to try Primanti Bros. The cheesesteak was outstanding, and I paired it with a tall Yuengling. Truly perfection!

yelp:train:1817.orig: So an honest review.  Bland.  Service good prices cheap but food very bland and pre made.  I ordered the new black bean burger sandwich.  Bread not toasted, burger tasted a lot like my morning star black bean burger that I get frozen.  Cole sale was a lot better with the hot sauce I smothered on it.  The best part was by far the fries which weren't all that great.  I am glad that those were home made.  I picked all the bread off ate mostly the fries and was not very impressed.  The beer makes everything tastes better so order at least two beers before eating.  I'm not a big foodie but I like my food taste better.  I still ate because I was hungry and it's not uneatable, just bland and kinda of boring.  It's still a must do in Pitts so go ahead and do it at least once, but skip the rest of your stay.
yelp:train:1817.para: An honest take: The place is decent with good service and affordable prices, but the food is quite bland and seems pre-prepared. I tried the new black bean burger sandwich; the bread wasn't toasted, and the burger tasted similar to my frozen Morning Star version. The cole slaw was much better with some hot sauce. The fries were the highlight, though not stellar. I removed the bread and ate mostly the fries, finding the meal unimpressive overall. I recommend ordering at least two beers to enhance the experience. As a non-foodie, I prefer more flavorful food, but I ate because I was hungry. It's not inedible, just bland and somewhat boring. It’s a must-try in Pittsburgh, but you can skip the rest of your visit.

yelp:train:2062.orig: We came here to see the play \""You say Tomato I Say Shut Up!\"" and what fun we had! The stage is visible from any seat, the waitress was never too far and the food was satisfying. We really had a great time and enjoyed watching a play while eating and drinking. Great time and we can't wait to come back for another show.
yelp:train:2062.para: We attended the play titled "You Say Tomato I Say Shut Up!" and we thoroughly enjoyed ourselves! Every seat offers a clear view of the stage, the staff was always nearby, and the food was delicious. We had a fantastic time, relishing the play while we ate and sipped our drinks. We had such a great experience and we're looking forward to returning for another performance.

yelp:train:2436.orig: After walking around the Strip District, this certainly hit the spot. We did the buffet, and I got the pasta trio. I was not disappointed. Endless amounts of great pasta, plus everything else that came with the buffet table. It's a classy place, but people from all walks of life were eating there, from people dressed in Steelers gear to older, well-dressed couples. I'd definitely come back or go to her other restaurant.
yelp:train:2436.para: After exploring the Strip District, this buffet was just what I needed. I tried the pasta trio, and I wasn't let down. The buffet offered an abundance of delicious pasta options, along with a variety of other dishes. It has a sophisticated ambiance, yet it's welcoming to everyone, from fans in Steelers attire to elegantly dressed seniors. I'd definitely return or check out her other establishment.

yelp:train:3078.orig: This is up there in my top 5 thrift stores. While it doesn't have a lot in the way of furniture (a few pieces downstairs), it has plenty of everything else. My first visit was meant to be a short browse, but it turned into a marathon 2.5 hour shop. There were shelves and shelves of bric-a-brac to sort through, kitchen supplies galore, and so many clothes I couldn't even think about looking through them all. The only downsides were the out of control kids running around, and the constant traffic jams of shopping carts in the aisles. Otherwise, I highly recommend this place for the serious thrifter/new apartment dweller/anyone looking to kill a few hours.
yelp:train:3078.para: This thrift store ranks among my top five favorites. Although it lacks a wide range of furniture (just a few pieces downstairs), it offers an abundance of other items. My initial plan was to quickly browse, but it ended up being a 2.5-hour shopping spree. The store is filled with endless shelves of various knick-knacks, an overwhelming array of kitchen supplies, and so many clothes that it's impossible to examine them all. The main drawbacks are the energetic children running around and the frequent congestion from shopping carts in the aisles. However, I strongly recommend it for serious thrifters, new apartment residents, or anyone looking to spend a leisurely afternoon.

yelp:train:3123.orig: If you're seeking bland, salty, Chinese food where every entree tastes exactly the same as the other...this is your place!
yelp:train:3123.para: If you're looking for unremarkable, salty Chinese cuisine where all the dishes taste identical...this restaurant is just what you need!

yelp:train:3150.orig:
The appetizer was bruschetta.  Essentially three pieces of toast with various toppings.  Two of the three were good, but the brocolinni topped one was not my taste.  Certainly, this was NOT worth the $12 price.  Our dinner was pizza.  The crust was very good - almost like a soft, warm, flat breadstick.  Sadly, the pizza was sparsely topped with cheese and sausage.

Our server was attentive, almost to a fault.  The restaurant was excessively loud - we couldn't hear the waitress rattle off the soup, appetizer or entree specials (seven specials in total).

While the food was not bad, I can't justify the prices or quantities.  In fact, I really didn't pull up Yelp to rate this restaurant...I'm actually looking for a place to go eat since I'm still famished after ""eating"" here.
yelp:train:3150.para:
The appetizer served was bruschetta, which comprised three slices of toast with different toppings. While two of them were enjoyable, the broccoli-topped one did not appeal to me. The $12 price tag for this was definitely not justified. For our main course, we ordered pizza. The crust was excellent, almost like a soft, warm breadstick. However, the pizza itself was lightly topped with cheese and sausage.

Our server was very attentive, perhaps a bit too much so. The restaurant was extremely noisy, making it difficult to hear the specials for the day, which included seven options. Although the food wasn't terrible, the prices and portion sizes don't seem reasonable. In fact, I'm still hungry after what I thought was a meal here, and I'm now searching for a better place to eat.

yelp:train:3364.para:
I had the well-known "Birthday Coupon" and wanted to make it count with a free entree. This restaurant had been on my radar for some time, and I managed to convince my husband to join me for a romantic evening out. The only available seating without a reservation was at the bar, which suited us just fine. We were among the few patrons, and the quiet atmosphere was perfect.

The bartender greeted us warmly and was both knowledgeable and friendly. He offered us drink menus and gave us plenty of time to choose our drinks.

We began with the hamachi sashimi, a delightful combination of pomegranate, pear, avocado, and amber jack tuna. A spicy sauce accompanied it, and the flavors melded beautifully. The presentation was stunning.

For my main course, I tried the Thaikkal curry, which was both an educational and enjoyable experience. The eggplant was fire-grilled, enhancing its flavor when paired with the curry sauce. It was served with bean sprouts and slices of fresh mango, a pairing I had never considered before. However, the roti was fried, which I didn't particularly enjoy.

My husband opted for the seafood hot pot, which came with a generous portion of seafood and a side of rice.

yelp:train:3471.orig:
One of my favorite things to do is consignment shop. On a dreary day I decided to look up a few local shops to hit up and my finale trip was to Hey Betty's.

Hey Betty's seemed to be very organized. It was a small area, but had a lot to offer without seeming to give you a garage sale vibe. The men's clothing was next to none but I can still appreciate nice things even when they are not for my gender. There were tons of hat boxes and great jewelry pieces to pick from.

The reason for the 2 star review is the service. The woman working the counter who I'm assuming to be the owner was not friendly at all. We greeted her before she greeted us which I find rude. She did not ask us anything when we were shopping. She just sat there and read a magazine. The only time she interacted with us is when we basically forced her. It was quite the turnoff.

To me customer service is everything. If you cannot greet your customers or educate them about your items/services you're providing then that's one less store I need to go back to. I would recommend it to someone who is looking for vintage clothing but not to someone who is looking for a great customer service experience.
yelp:train:3471.para:
I enjoy visiting consignment shops, and on a gloomy day, I checked out a few local ones, concluding my trip at Hey Betty's. 

Hey Betty's appeared well-organized. Despite its small size, it offered a wide range of items without feeling like a garage sale. While there was little men's clothing, I still admired the quality of the other items. There were numerous hat boxes and excellent jewelry pieces to choose from.

The primary reason for my 2-star rating is the service. The woman at the counter, whom I believe is the owner, was not at all friendly. She greeted us before we did, which I found impolite. She didn't engage with us while we were shopping, merely reading a magazine. She only interacted with us when we practically forced her to. This was quite off-putting.

To me, customer service is crucial. If you can't greet customers or provide information about your items, it means one less store I'll return to. I would suggest it to someone seeking vintage clothing but not to someone looking for good customer service.

yelp:train:3591.orig:
Best doughnuts in Pittsburgh. 

I generally pass on other baked goods. Mediocre bread.

Generally unfriendly staff, but Walnut St. attracts pretty arrogant customers - so it makes sense.
yelp:train:3591.para:
The best doughnuts can be found in Pittsburgh. 

Typically, I avoid other baked goods, as the bread tends to be subpar.

While the staff is usually not very friendly, Walnut Street draws rather arrogant customers, which might explain the attitude.

yelp:train:3611.orig:
Pittsburgh has a Four Seasons!

From Paris to Shanghai, London to Bangkok, the care with which this little B&B operation is run in Pittsburgh exceeds the best that I have experienced in any of these cities.

It may not have the conference facilities of a larger hotel, the business center, or in-house spa, but as a B&B, this is about as good as it gets. 

The structure in which the whole thing is held (do we call it a 'house'?) is old (perhaps we could say it generically to be 'victorian') with decor to match. These are far from our tastes, but they compensate (in our eyes) by taking good care of what they have. The TVs aren't even old flat screens, but they do stock the rooms thoroughly with l'occitane.

Where this place really shines is in the staff and the food. I actually find this aspect to be _better_ or even _much_ better than many celebrated big-city five-star properties. When was the last time that the night staff pulled some food from the refrigerator (gratis) after a midnight arrival caused by flight delays?

They make everything in-house and it is all extraordinary. On this last visit, I indulged in their traditional french toast with a side of eggs. I forgot t
yelp:train:3611.para:
Pittsburgh boasts a Four Seasons-like B&B that surpasses many upscale hotels I've stayed in, from Paris to Shanghai.

While it lacks the conference rooms and amenities of a larger hotel, this B&B excels in its intimate, well-maintained setting. The building, perhaps Victorian in style, has decor that, while not to our personal taste, is well-cared for. The TVs are not the latest models, but the rooms are generously stocked with L'Occitane products.

What truly sets this place apart is its staff and cuisine. The service and food are exceptional, often surpassing those in many famous five-star hotels. For instance, the night staff has been known to provide free food from the refrigerator after late-night arrivals due to flight delays.

Everything is made in-house and is of extraordinary quality. On my last visit, I enjoyed their traditional French toast with eggs, and I almost forgot to mention...

yelp:train:4177.orig: Red lobster was not the place to be tonight. Saturday-8/11!!!! The service was horrible. The waiter messed up so bad that we had more free food then we ordered. The appetizer came out after the salad. It seem to be over before it started. It only went down hill from here. I am done with this location. Come on red lobster!!!
yelp:train:4177.para: Tonight wasn't a good time to visit Red Lobster. Saturday, August 11th! The service was terrible. The waiter made such a mistake that we ended up with more free food than what we ordered. The appetizer arrived after the salad, and it felt like the meal barely began before it ended. Things only got worse from there. I won't be returning to this location. Red Lobster, please step it up!

yelp:train:4841.orig: TWC IS THE WORST!\n\nUnfortunately, TWC has basically monopolized the Charlotte area.  I am very jealous of all the people who have AT&T Uverse available to them.  I have contemplated DirectTV because TWC is so awful.  Every few months the \""promotion\"" on my plan runs out and when I call they say they are giving me the best possible promotion that they usually don't give to any other customer by taking $5 off...how generous.  They really don't care if their customers are unhappy because they know they have no other choice for digital TV.  If you have other options, USE THEM!
yelp:train:4841.para:
TWC IS THE WORST!

Sadly, TWC dominates the Charlotte market. I'm envious of those with AT&T Uverse as an option. I've considered switching to DirectTV due to TWC's poor service. Whenever my promotional offer expires, they offer me a $5 discount, which feels like a meager gesture. It's clear they don't prioritize customer satisfaction since they know they're the only game in town for digital TV. If you have alternatives, definitely use them!
