4) Yams were good!
5) Corn bread was just ok
6) Banana Pudding was very good!
7) Red beans rice and sausage was not good.

All and all, the Merts was just ok,  However, if in town again, I
yelp:train:4932.para:
I had high hopes given that I was in the South, where I adore the cuisine. Unfortunately, my experience was quite disappointing. Growing up, I frequently enjoyed most of the dishes on the menu, and I often compare them to my home cooking. Additionally, I have a broad palate, having sampled foods from various regions.

The food was served to me extremely hot, making it impossible to eat comfortably for about 7 to 10 minutes. I ordered Fried Chicken, Greens, Yams, Catfish, and Banana Pudding. The day before, my colleague had tried the red beans and rice.

The service was satisfactory, but the menu could use some improvement.

1) The Fried Chicken seemed more like baked chicken that was dry and lacked seasoning. It wasn't crispy, and it wasn't very flavorful.
2) The Catfish was whole with bones, which made each bite a bit of a challenge. The taste was decent, but it would have been better without the bones.
3) The Greens were good!
4) The Yams were good!
5) The Cornbread was just okay.
6) The Banana Pudding was very good!
7) The Red Beans and Rice and Sausage were not good.

Overall, Merts was just okay. If I'm in town again, I might give it another chance.

yelp:train:4972.orig:
I'm somewhat embarrassed about this review as I work in Uptown, love this kind of cooking, have known Mert's existed but have never gone!  Remedied that on Wednesday morning and seriously had perhaps the best breakfast I've ever had.

I got just the basics - scrambled eggs, sausage, home fries, biscuit and a buttermilk pancake on the side.  OMFG!  Perfectly cooked eggs, two huge sausage patties that were seared on the outside and moist/tender on the inside (yes they were cooked through!)  :)  Everything was just as I would order a breakfast if it were my last breakfast on earth.  My wife had similar but substituted bacon, grits and a sweet potato pancake. she was in breakfast nirvana as well.  Even the coffee was a notch above your typical breakfast joint fare.

AND...  As I sat there eating this deliciousness, I had to stare at the lunch special menu board and there was not one thing on it I wouldn't have ordered.  There is no doubt I'm coming back soon for lunch.

On the service side it was fast, friendly and really nice teamwork among the servers with everyone paying attention to coffee cups getting low, etc.  What a jewel for the Queen City!
yelp:train:4972.para:
I feel a bit sheepish writing this review since I work nearby and adore this type of cuisine, but I've never actually visited Mert's until Wednesday morning. And let me tell you, it was hands down the best breakfast I've ever had!

I ordered the standard fare: scrambled eggs, sausage, home fries, a biscuit, and a buttermilk pancake. It was absolutely amazing! The eggs were perfectly cooked, the sausage was seared on the outside and juicy on the inside, and everything was just as good as if it were my last meal. My wife had a similar experience, opting for bacon, grits, and a sweet potato pancake, and she was equally delighted. Even the coffee was superior to what you'd typically find at a breakfast place.

Moreover, as I savored this delicious meal, I couldn't help but look at the lunch specials menu and found everything appealing. I'm certain I'll be back soon for lunch.

On the service front, it was prompt, friendly, and the servers worked well together, ensuring everything was just right. Mert's is truly a gem for the Queen City!

yelp:train:5153.orig:
Oowee. This is some seriously great Italian. If you like your meals to take time, then this place is five stars. The food is five stars. But the slooooow service drops it a notch.

Our server didn't have an extensive knowledge of the beer list. This probably shows my naivete with regard to what you're supposed to order at a restaurant like Luce, but still, a good server knows EVERYTHING, or at least acts like it. Thus, Peroni. [sigh]

My appetizer was the veal cutlets, just little thin slices of tender baby calf with a dallop of sauce and capers. I'm going to spend a few more months in Purgatory for eating veal, but MAN, it will be worth it!

My main course was the cheese rolled in pork, the Fraciti I believe it was called (I can't seem to pull up the menu online) with gnocchi. Seriously great stuff. I ended with the custard and berries, which was okay. I wouldn't send it away, but perhaps I was expecting something more after the faaaaaantastic appetizer and entree.

Whew. Again, the only drawback was the 2.5 hour meal. An entire tenth of my day was spent at this restaurant. In some sense it was worth it, just be prepared. Go GO GO!
yelp:train:5153.para:
Wow, this Italian cuisine is outstanding! If you enjoy a leisurely dining experience, this restaurant is perfect, earning top marks. However, the service, while delightful, could be quicker.

Our server wasn't as well-versed in the beer selection, which might reflect my inexperience with high-end restaurant choices. Still, a good server should know everything—or at least pretend to. So, we went with Peroni. [sigh]

For my starter, I had veal cutlets—thin slices of tender calf meat with a sauce and capers. I'll be in Purgatory for a while for eating veal, but it was absolutely worth it!

My main course was a dish of cheese rolled in pork, likely called Fraciti (I couldn't find the menu online). It was superb, paired with gnocchi. For dessert, I had custard and berries, which was decent but couldn't match the fantastic flavors of the starter and main course.

The meal took a whopping 2.5 hours, which is a significant chunk of my day. But it was worth it. Just be prepared for the long wait. Go!

yelp:train:5210.orig:
I was here this past weekend for a charity event.  It was absolutely packed and the bartenders were working extra hard.  I mean literally breaking a sweat!    Despite it being very crowded, the restaurant stayed clean and cool!  

We ordered a Margarita pizza which was freaking delicious.  Every ingredient was fresh and tasty.  Even the mozzerella was fresh, not the shredded typical stuff.  I would definitely order this pizza again.  Although this time I did not order a salad, I have in the past ordered the Brixx Salad and it is also quite excellent.  

The price point is nice on the wallet.  Our pizza was $9.95 and can easily serve 2 people for dinner.  

In terms of atmosphere, it is more casual but in a classy, Italian way, not a sports bar type of way.  I will be going back for sure!
yelp:train:5210.para:
Last weekend, I attended a charity event here, and the place was bustling with people, making the bartenders work really hard—literally drenched in sweat! Despite the crowd, the restaurant managed to stay clean and comfortable.

We got a Margarita pizza, and it was outstandingly delicious. Each ingredient was fresh and flavorful, and even the mozzarella was the real, whole ball kind, not the usual shredded variety. I'd definitely order this pizza again.

In the past, I've also enjoyed the Brixx Salad, which is equally excellent. 

The pricing is quite reasonable; our pizza at $9.95 could easily feed two for dinner. 

The atmosphere is casual yet sophisticated, with a touch of Italian elegance, not the typical sports bar vibe. I plan to return soon!

yelp:train:5361.orig:
Connolly's is a great Irish Pub with no food, but great bartenders and an even better time. Beware though, if you have never been, you will be floored at how dark it is! I have a friend who told me the story of when he first moved to Charlotte and stumbled into what he thought was pronounced ""Cannolli's"". He walked in, ran into a table, couldn't see anything and ran back out because he had no idea what he had just walked into. Ha! 

But your eyes will adjust and you will be fine after you grab a Guinnes or a cider. Most of the people that work there are actually from Ireland or another country such as Australia. The experience in a pub is just that much more enjoyable when accents are involved (especially with hot guys). 

While you're there, take in the music, which is sometimes Irish, sometimes hip hop, and the decor of the room. On the walls you will find all authentic effects from Ireland, such as street signs and sports memorabilia. If you are there on a busier night (which sometimes can be every night) head upstairs if you can. The upstairs is usually open Thursdays through Saturdays, I think. It's much roomier up there and you can always find a few young people danci
yelp:train:5361.para:
Connolly's is an excellent Irish Pub without any food, but it boasts fantastic bartenders and a terrific atmosphere. Be warned, though; if you're new, you'll be surprised by how dimly lit it is! I recall a friend who once moved to Charlotte and mistakenly entered what he thought was "Cannolli's." He bumped into a table, couldn't see a thing, and quickly left, bewildered. Haha!

Your vision will adjust, and you'll be fine once you have a Guinness or a cider. Many of the staff are actually from Ireland or other countries like Australia. The pub experience is even more enjoyable with the accents and, let's not forget, the presence of some hot guys.

While you're there, enjoy the music, which alternates between Irish and hip hop, and take in the room's decor. The walls are adorned with authentic Irish items, such as street signs and sports memorabilia. On busier nights, try to head upstairs if possible. The upstairs is usually open Thursday through Saturday and offers more space, where you can often find some young people dancing.

yelp:train:5382.orig:
The bagels here aren't as good as everyone said they would be. I actually think I like the Einstein's Bagel's bagel-cream cheese combo better. I personally prefer the plain bagel and cream cheese over the egg sandwiches because the eggs are kind of weird and microwavy tasting. The nice thing about this location is that it's on the 2nd floor of the epicenter and you can get there directly from the Aloft.

They have some very good deals on breakfast bagels that are CHEAPER than Smoothie King. Damn you delicious expensive smoothies!

Tip: I wasted $2 on a very very disgusting and watered down Iced Coffee. Avoid at all costs. Minus 1 star for that.
yelp:train:5382.para:
While the bagels here aren't as impressive as I'd heard, I actually prefer Einstein's Bagel's bagel-cream cheese combination. I find the plain bagel with cream cheese more appealing than the egg sandwiches, as the eggs taste a bit odd and microwaved. The plus side is that this place is conveniently located on the 2nd floor of the epicenter, making it easy to access from the Aloft.

They offer some great deals on breakfast bagels that are even cheaper than Smoothie King's prices. Those smoothies are definitely overpriced and not worth it!

A tip: I spent $2 on an extremely unpleasant and watery iced coffee, which I would absolutely avoid. This experience cost me a star.

yelp:train:5853.orig: We were in Charlotte this past weekend and we were in the mood for Italian, so we went to Mama Ricotta's. I am glad we made the choice to come here. From the moment we walked in, the staff was pretty friendly and accommodating. We got the Burrata & Prosciutto appetizer, it was lovely. Our entrees were Penne Alla Vodka and Rigatoni with Meat Sauce. The ingredients were fresh and flavorful; just like Italian food should be. \n\nWe noticed that the dessert portions were enormous so we asked if we could be served just half of a tiramisu. Our waitress was absolutely accommodating and she made it happen. We weren't expecting to pay half price for the dessert we just didn't want the rest to go to waste, but she did charge us half price. I wish this place was in DC, we would be here all the time.
yelp:train:5853.para:
Last weekend, we were in Charlotte and craved Italian cuisine, leading us to Mama Ricotta's. I'm delighted we chose this place. The staff greeted us warmly from the start and were very helpful. We ordered the Burrata & Prosciutto appetizer, which was delightful. For our main courses, we had Penne Alla Vodka and Rigatoni with Meat Sauce. The ingredients were fresh and packed with flavor, just as authentic Italian dishes should be.

We observed that the dessert portions were quite generous, so we inquired if we could have just half a tiramisu. Our waitress was incredibly accommodating and arranged it for us. We didn't expect to pay half price, but we didn't want the rest to go to waste, and she honored our request. I wish this restaurant were in DC; we'd visit frequently.

yelp:train:6760.orig: This is by far the best Japanese place in Charlotte.  We had our nephew who lives in Japan come by to see how authentic it was.  He said it felt just like home.  The food is always great and the employee there are very kind.\n\nMy family and I go there for lunch all the time!
yelp:train:6760.para: This Japanese restaurant in Charlotte is undoubtedly the best we've found. We invited our nephew from Japan to experience it, and he felt it was just as authentic as being in his home country. The food is consistently delicious, and the staff are extremely friendly. My family and I enjoy lunch there regularly!

yelp:train:6858.orig: Late afternoon dinner at the Palm... I wanted to leave when we were not received for about 10 minutes, but we gave them some time to realize there were customers up front. After someone in the kitchen finally noticed us, we were seated at a table, with no menus... Then, our waiter introduced himself, took away extra silverware, and gave us no menus. We asked... Should we get out own menus? He said he would get us some. He then proceeded to chat with some waiter buddies in plain view. Since the restaurant was almost completely empty, it looked like we were interrupting a break. After several minutes of chit-chat, the waiter finally delivered some menus (how hard is that?). Perusing the menu, it was clear the Palm doesn't believe in meals, which I guess is because meals are... gauche. You can order a steak for $45, but you won't get a salad or a side unless you buy a separate $8 plate of veggies or $8 salad. I just couldn't believe a 9 oz. piece of meat would be worth that much (plus, I'd rather a 6 oz. filet). So, we ordered the Veal and Chicken Parm. (~$35), which do not come with any noodles unless you pay $4 extra (thus bringing the Parms. up to ~$40). I also ordered a coffee, wh
yelp:train:6858.para: At the Palm for an evening meal, I considered leaving after waiting for about 10 minutes without being attended to, but we decided to wait a bit longer. Eventually, someone from the kitchen noticed us, and we were seated without menus. Our waiter introduced himself, removed extra silverware, and didn't offer menus. We inquired if we should get our own menus, and he said he would fetch them. He then spent several minutes chatting with other waiters in plain sight, which seemed out of place given that the restaurant was nearly empty. After a few minutes, the waiter finally brought us menus. Looking over the menu, it was evident that the Palm doesn't offer full meals, perhaps because they consider them old-fashioned. A steak was priced at $45, but you had to pay an additional $8 for a side salad or vegetables. I found it hard to believe that a 9 oz. steak would cost that much, and I preferred a 6 oz. filet instead. So, we opted for the Veal and Chicken Parmesan, which cost around $35 and didn't come with pasta unless we paid an extra $4. I also ordered a coffee.

yelp:train:7211.orig: Had the tamales and chimi. Food was excellent. Don't let the location intimidate you. It conveniently located near CLT airport and the nearby hotels.
yelp:train:7211.para: I enjoyed the tamales and chimi. The food was outstanding. Don't be deterred by the location; it's conveniently situated close to the CLT airport and surrounding hotels.

yelp:train:7703.orig: CVS Pharmacy is your basic drug store. Ample parking, large store, pretty clean, decent selection, lots of sale items. The pharmacy here is very busy, at times you will have to wait for your pickup. Some days it seems that there are too many pharmacists and not enough people for customer service; however they are generally very apologetic when things run behind.  Everyone must be using CVS Covermark, busiest pharmacy in the area.
yelp:train:7703.para: CVS Pharmacy operates as a standard drugstore with plenty of parking and a sizable interior. It's fairly clean and offers a good range of products, with many items on sale. The pharmacy can be quite busy, leading to wait times for prescriptions. On some days, it feels like there are more pharmacists than customer service staff, but the staff is typically apologetic when things get delayed. It seems everyone in the area uses CVS Covermark, making it the busiest pharmacy around.

yelp:train:7842.orig: The service was great but the food was not. All the pasta for our party was undercooked; there were 14 of us. Other customers also were returning meals. The manager told us they were using a new pasta and had to \""learn to cook it\"". She did make an adjustment on our bill to make up for the bad meals.
yelp:train:7842.para: The service was excellent, but the food quality was disappointing. Our entire party of 14 found the pasta to be undercooked. Other diners were also returning their meals. The manager explained that they were using a new type of pasta and needed to "learn how to prepare it." She did offer to adjust our bill to compensate for the subpar meal experience.

yelp:train:8325.orig:
Was here for a gala at the adjoining conference center.  Service was terrible. The waitress kept slamming food and drinks on the  table. She only brought dinner for half the table and the rest had to wait for 15 minutes. One of the guests had to wait about 20 minutes for the meal. Horrible!
I've been to many Marriotts before and hold a frequent visitor card, but this one has been the worst experience so far.

I know this isn't a review that completely reflects the hotel or any restaurants inside it, but the fact that this service was under the Marriott name prompted this review and rating
yelp:train:8325.para:
Attended a gala at the nearby conference center, and the service was extremely poor. The waitress was rather rough, repeatedly placing food and drinks on the table roughly. Only half the table received their dinner, while the others had to wait 15 minutes. One guest had to wait about 20 minutes for their meal. This was truly awful.

I've stayed at numerous Marriott properties and am a frequent guest, but this experience was the worst I've had. Although this review doesn't necessarily reflect the hotel or other restaurants within, the Marriott name was associated with this service, which is why I'm sharing this feedback and rating.

yelp:train:8448.orig:
Authentic Italian food! Our goal of the night was to have a nice Italian dinner and not feel rushed to eat. Vin Santo successfully met our goal and went beyond. Walking in to Vin Santo felt like walking into your Italian Grandmothers kitchen (in the best ways). Our server was fantastic and remained attentive to us throughout the meal. Most may find it expensive, however, for $99 two people were able to share a bottle of wine, share a desert, and we both had an entree that provided leftovers for the next day. 

CON: Too many good options and I could only order one entree.

We will definitely be going back there soon to try their other items on the menu.
yelp:train:8448.para:
Delicious Italian cuisine was our aim for the evening, and we wanted to enjoy our meal without feeling hurried. Vin Santo exceeded our expectations and fulfilled our goal admirably. The ambiance upon entering Vin Santo was reminiscent of stepping into a beloved Italian grandmother's kitchen. Our server was exceptional and stayed attentive throughout the meal. While some might consider the prices high, for $99, two of us were able to share a bottle of wine, enjoy a dessert, and each have an entree that left us with leftovers for the next day.

CON: There were too many tempting options, making it difficult to choose just one entree.

We're planning to return to Vin Santo soon to sample more of their menu items.

yelp:train:8848.orig: A wash may be better priced than others but you'll get what you pay for. My husband brought out 2008 Prius for a wash and vacuum and it doesn't look like anything has been cleaned! The carpet in the hatch and floors are still dirty and none of the interior was wiped down. We will be going to Octopus or we'll just do it ourselves next time.
yelp:train:8848.para: While a wash might seem more affordable, you often get what you pay for. My husband recently had our 2008 Prius washed and vacuumed, but the car doesn't appear any cleaner. The carpet in the hatch and floors remain dirty, and the interior wasn't even wiped down. We might consider taking it to Octopus or doing the cleaning ourselves next time.

yelp:train:8861.orig: The bacon commercial with non stop fries, only says \""HEART ATTACK!!!!!\""   Thanks Applebee's
yelp:train:8861.para: The Applebee's ad featuring non-stop bacon displays the message "HEART ATTACK!!!!!". Thanks, Applebee's.

yelp:train:9109.orig: I have only been to cafe Zoma once, and I didn't even order anything.  My friends got coffee to go, and there were two customers ahead of them in line.  I had no idea that it could take a half hour to serve four people coffee, but the Clap your Hands Say Yeah listening idiots behind the counter at Cafe Zoma made it possible.\n\nI gave this place an extra star because my friends thought their coffee was pretty good.
yelp:train:9109.para: My single visit to Cafe Zoma was brief; I didn't even place an order. My friends picked up their coffee, and there were two other customers in front of them. I was surprised to learn that serving four people coffee could take half an hour, but the customers playing Clap Your Hands Say Yeah at the counter made it seem even longer. However, I gave the place an extra star due to my friends' positive feedback on the quality of their coffee.

yelp:train:9227.orig:
My first ever trip to Woody-Anne's involved a lady at the bar a) showing off a pic that proved ghosts exist cuz of an ""orb"" that is inexplicably present(?), b) flashing me her boobs for a drink that she never actually took me up on, and c) giving me an epicly gross (DRIPPING) wet willy, all in the span of Fleetwood Mac's ""Landslide"" which soundtracked the whole experience.

The evening ended with me and the bartender watching a M.A.S.H. rerun in what was by then an otherwise empty bar.

Needless to say, this is my New Favorite Place.
yelp:train:9227.para:
My initial visit to Woody-Anne's featured a bartender who, during Fleetwood Mac's "Landslide," a) displayed a photo she claimed proved the existence of ghosts due to an unexplainable "orb," b) offered to show me her breasts in exchange for a drink, though she didn't follow through, and c) gave me a disgustingly wet willy that dripped profusely. The entire experience was set to the music of Fleetwood Mac.

The night concluded with the bartender and I watching a M.A.S.H. rerun in an otherwise empty bar.

Needless to say, this has become my new favorite spot.

yelp:train:9449.orig:
Although it wasn't totally terrible, David's Jamaican Cuisine is not a restaurant to which I will return. A friend and I met for lunch at David's a few days ago -- he had previously eaten there and didn't love it, but agreed to go again because I wanted to try it after reading all the great reviews on Yelp and other review sites. When we arrived, I was surprised to see a lunch buffet set up. Previous experience with lunch buffets at other restaurants has caused me to interpret buffets as warning signs, but, since we were already there, we decided to stay.

We ordered sodas, which arrived in cans. Not a big deal, but worth mentioning because I know some people prefer to drink out of cups.

The lunch buffet had approximately 15 options ranging from jerk chicken and jerk pork to plantains to rice to mango chicken to pineapple slaw with tofu. The jerk chicken was good, though not as flavorful as I had expected or hoped, but the other foods I tried ranged from blah to bad.

Based on the outstanding reviews David's has received, I was very surprised and disappointed by my experience. I'm tempted to give this restaurant one more try, but really can't decide if it's worth the money a
yelp:train:9449.para:
While it wasn't entirely unsatisfactory, I don't see myself returning to David's Jamaican Cuisine anytime soon. My friend and I dined there a few days ago; he had previously visited and wasn't a fan, but agreed to go again because I wanted to try it after reading numerous positive reviews online. Upon arrival, we were surprised to find a lunch buffet set up, which usually signals a red flag for me, but we decided to give it a chance.

We ordered sodas in cans, which was fine but noteworthy for those who prefer cups.

The buffet offered about 15 items, including jerk chicken, jerk pork, plantains, rice, mango chicken, and a pineapple slaw with tofu. The jerk chicken was decent but lacked the flavor I anticipated, while the other dishes were either unremarkable or poor.

Given the glowing reviews David's has received, I was both surprised and disappointed by my experience. I'm considering giving the restaurant another chance, but I'm struggling to justify the cost.

yelp:train:9519.orig: Upswing in furniture recently which has made this my go-to before St. Vinny when it comes to looking for random pieces to add to my pad! The staff is lovely, quick to help me load things in my coche, and prices are unbeatable for pieces that are in really great shape. Nabbed a desk recently for $20 that's super solid and looks swell in my space. \n\nYou might have to bounce around to a few ReStores before you find what you're looking for, and you have to wade through all the tile, cabinets and random pieces of wood. But you're down to do some digging, stellar furniture finds await!
yelp:train:9519.para:
Recently, there's been a surge in the availability of furniture at St. Vincent de Paul ReStores, making them my首选之地，尤其是在寻找随机家具添置我的小窝时！店员非常友好，迅速帮我把东西装进车里，而且价格超值，尤其是那些状况很好的家具。最近我花20美元买了一张非常稳固且非常适合我的空间的书桌。

你可能需要在几家ReStores之间逛逛才能找到你需要的东西，而且你得在瓷砖、橱柜和各种木头碎片中翻找。但只要你愿意花点时间挖掘，那里就有惊人的家具发现等着你！

yelp:train:9715.orig:
I've been going to Long's Garage for about 5 years now and have been very happy with their service.  They've always been honest with me.  The prices are comparable to other shops. The repairs are done quickly and professionally.  My truck is 16 years old, yet it drives like it's only a few years old thanks to Long's. 

The only criticism I would have would be if you need something done with a truck topper.  I didn't know what to do with the rubber seal that was falling off.  Their body work person offered to epoxy it, but that didn't stay on very long.  I didn't know at the time that I could get a new seal at Truck Trends in Champaign.
 
Something that really impressed me though was how honest their detail person was about the state of the paint on my truck.  I wasn't sure how salvageable it was, and he was honest in telling me that my paint was too thin to try polish on (would rub the last of the paint off), but he did give me some recommendations on how to keep what paint I have left on the truck for years to come.  I followed the recommendations and get compliments on how good my truck looks all the time.  What impressed me was that the detail person didn't try to convince m
yelp:train:9715.para:
For the past five years, I've been a customer at Long's Garage and have consistently been satisfied with their service. They've always been upfront with me. The pricing is similar to other garages. Repairs are completed swiftly and professionally. My 16-year-old truck still drives like it's brand new, thanks to Long's.

The only feedback I have is regarding truck toppers. When the rubber seal started falling off, I wasn't sure what to do. The body work staff suggested epoxy, but it didn't last. I later learned that I could get a new seal from Truck Trends in Champaign.

What really stood out to me was the honesty of the detail person about the condition of my truck's paint. Initially, I wasn't sure if the paint was salvageable, but he was straightforward, telling me that the paint was too thin for polishing. Instead, he offered advice on how to preserve what paint remained. Following his suggestions, my truck continues to receive compliments. What impressed me was that he didn't try to sell me unnecessary services.

yelp:train:10658.orig: I would have ordered from this place again if the driver hadn't of scammed me for an extra dollar.  Look at your receipt!
yelp:train:10658.para: I would have placed another order with you, but the driver tried to scam me out of an extra dollar. Check your receipt!

yelp:train:11475.orig:
The Blue Fin is my favorite Teriyaki stop in the valley.  

To begin, the service here is awesome!  For such a casual restaurant, they really know how to make you feel welcome.

I absolutely love the food here too.  Great appetizers, spring rolls, inari, sunomono, etc.  Being vegetarian, I always order the same...Steamed Vegetable Bowl.  For the money, you get a TON of food here.  The teriyaki sauce is perfect, not too sweet like some of those chain places.

Did I mention that the service here is the best?

The only thing wrong with The Blue FIn; they are not opened on the weekends, Monday through Friday only.
yelp:train:11475.para:
The Blue Fin stands out as my top choice for Teriyaki dining in the valley. 

Firstly, the service is outstanding! Despite being a casual place, they genuinely make you feel at home.

I'm a big fan of the food too. The appetizers, like spring rolls and inari, are fantastic, along with the sunomono. As a vegetarian, I consistently order the Steamed Vegetable Bowl. For the price, you receive a generous portion. The teriyaki sauce is just right, not overly sweet like some chain restaurants.

And let's not forget, the service is top-notch.

The only downside is that they are closed on weekends, operating only from Monday to Friday.

yelp:train:11675.orig: I am only giving -THIS- location a 1 star because of their horrible early hours!! They close like at 7 pm during the week, & they already closed at 3 pm on Sunday! ...I was pissed! The new Chipotle a block away at City scape is open til 10 pm daily! ...So there! What is it with everything closing sooo damn early in Phoenix! This is such an early city! Some eating places even close at 2:30 pm, like The Good Egg & First Watch... They wouldn't DARE close that early in LA because they would lose a lot of profit!  (...I am from LA).
yelp:train:11675.para: I'm giving this location only 1 star due to its extremely early closing times! They shut down at 7 pm on weekdays and were already closed by 3 pm on Sunday... I was really frustrated! The Chipotle just a block away at Cityscape stays open until 10 pm every day! ...There you go! Why do so many places in Phoenix close so early? It's such an early-closing city! Some restaurants even close at 2:30 pm, like The Good Egg and First Watch... They wouldn't DARE do that in LA, where they'd lose a lot of business! (...I'm from LA).

yelp:train:11965.orig: When HRC was on Camelback, we frequented the bar for happy hour.  During that time, we befriended the bartenders, who are still there  They create a neighborhood feel to this international chain.  Phoenix HRC is different than the other ones I've been to because of this.  When they moved downtown we continued to frequent the bar.  Number 1 reason to drive downtown for happy hour - the bartenders Javier and Eddie.  They have incredible memories and pick up the conversation you ended with the last time you were there, and that could have been 8 months ago.  They are quick with the drinks and with their wit. \n\nThe food is ok and over-priced, but that comes with the HRC name.  We have found the entire staff to be friendly and accommodating.  A neighborhood HRC bar...hmmmm.  Sure feels like it.
yelp:train:11965.para:
At HRC on Camelback, we often visited for happy hour and got to know the bartenders, who are still there today. Their presence gives this international chain a local feel. Phoenix HRC stands out from others because of this community atmosphere. Even after they moved downtown, we kept going for happy hour. The main draw is the bartenders, Javier and Eddie—they remember our conversations from months ago and keep the bar lively. They are efficient and witty.

The food is decent but pricey, which is typical for HRC. However, the entire staff is friendly and accommodating. It feels like a neighborhood bar, which is exactly what it is.

yelp:train:13310.orig:
I did a driveby of this place earlier in the day, and did some research.  I heard it closed at 8pm, and was told they have Chihuly glass on display.  That is all I needed to hear.

Parking was free, and was plenty of it- I managed to get a front row spot!  We got there around 5:30 pm, thinking there would be plenty of time to see everything...

Well I was wrong!  It started to get dark around 6:30, and for that, I missed out on about 2-3 trails- that sucked because I wanted to see everything... Hopefully since it is daylight savings now, you can enjoy the gardens now at a later time...

The parts that I did see were fascinating, although at parts it did get kind of boring (we started from the left and worked our way around).  I was told there was even a concery there for the evening- which sounded cool- but I wanted to explore, having never been there.

I would like to go back and see what the entire garden has to offer, since the desert portion at the Atlanta Botanical Garden just doesn't do it justice.

I think it is cool how it is next to the zoo (which I didn't get to visit), and two parks.
yelp:train:13310.para:
I took a quick look at the place earlier and did some research. I learned it closes at 8 pm and they have Chihuly glass exhibits, which piqued my interest.

Parking was free and plentiful, allowing me to park right up front. We arrived around 5:30 pm, expecting to have ample time to see everything...

Unfortunately, by 6:30 pm, it was getting dark, and I missed out on about 2-3 trails, which was disappointing since I wanted to see everything. Hopefully, with daylight savings, you can enjoy the gardens later.

The parts I did see were intriguing, though some sections became a bit monotonous as we moved around. I was informed there was a concert in the evening, which sounded appealing, but I was eager to explore since it was my first visit.

I'd like to return to see the full garden, as the desert section at the Atlanta Botanical Garden doesn't fully capture its essence. It's also cool that it's adjacent to the zoo and two parks, which I didn't have time to visit.

yelp:train:13701.orig:
Spent the day at the zoo with my niece and nephew. We took advantage of a google offer for $6.00 instead of the 18.00 usual price.

First of all this place is HUGE - and they have a lot of exhibits. Kids will love the place, but some words of warning.

1) wear REALLY comfortable shoes.

2) if you buy a general admission ticket, be prepared to shell out $2 - $5 for additional attractions such as Camel rides, Giraffe Feeding, Paddle Boats, Safari Train, Sting Ray Touch Pool etc.  (might be a good idea to buy one of the package deals)

3) Certain attractions are seasonal, so check the schedule. There is a water play area only open in summer.

4) The petting zoo closes at 3:45pm so take kids to see this before you do the other exhibits.

5) If you have stroller age kids - you can bring a stroller or rent one, its a good idea because there is a ton of walking and kids WILL poop out  before you get back to the zoo entrance at the end of the day. They have 2 seater strollers too.

Some great features to note:

1) Yes, we take credit cards! They have them everywhere - even on vending machines. Awesome for me because I hate carrying cash.

2) Bring in what you want and nee
yelp:train:13701.para:
Spend the day at the zoo with my niece and nephew, taking advantage of a Google offer that cut the price from $18 to just $6. This place is enormous, with numerous exhibits that kids will adore. However, here are a few tips to keep in mind:

1. Wear extremely comfortable shoes.
2. If you opt for a general admission ticket, be ready to spend an extra $2 to $5 on additional attractions like camel rides, giraffe feeding, paddle boats, the safari train, and the sting ray touch pool. Consider buying a package deal.
3. Some attractions are seasonal, so check the schedule. The water play area is only open during the summer.
4. The petting zoo closes at 3:45 pm, so make sure to visit it early in the day.
5. For stroller-age kids, you can bring your own or rent one. It's a good idea to have a stroller because there's a lot of walking, and kids will likely get tired by the end of the day. They also offer two-seater strollers.

Some highlights include:

1. Credit cards are accepted everywhere, even on vending machines, which is great for me since I don't like carrying cash.
2. Feel free to bring your own food and drinks.

yelp:train:14340.orig:
this was my first visit &

I will NEVER go back 
I will NEVER go back
I will NEVER go back
I will NEVER go back
I will NEVER go back
I will NEVER go back
kicking, dragging, screaming I will NEVER go back

ordered fish & chips, shepherd's pie & steak 'n kidney pie & beers
fish & chips = blah, nothing special or memorable, just plain cheap cod that was NOT cheap in $
shepherd's pie = this was not shepherd's pie it was cottage pie and it was bland, tasteless, boring!
steak 'n kidney pie = where was the kidney?
(chips = blah)

yelp:train:14340.para:
This was my first time visiting, and I absolutely won't return—ever. 

I ordered fish and chips, shepherd's pie, steak and kidney pie, and beers. 

The fish and chips were just ordinary, not particularly special or memorable, and the cod wasn't worth the price. 

The shepherd's pie wasn't even shepherd's pie; it was cottage pie, and it was bland and uninteresting. 

The steak and kidney pie lacked the kidney meat. 

The chips were just as unremarkable. 

If you've never tried traditional British food before, you might think this was good, except for the bland cottage pie. 

They only earned two stars because the bartender or server wasn't terrible. 

I wonder if you prioritize regular customers over new ones, or if you try to make new customers feel welcome to become regulars. 

And at $5 per beer...? 

The place is also very dirty, with decor that hasn't been cleaned or dusted since 1995.

yelp:train:14378.orig: This place is dirty, the owner is miserable and the food is terrible. It's amazing they have been in business this long.
yelp:train:14378.para: This location is quite untidy, the proprietor seems unhappy, and the cuisine is awful. It's surprising they've managed to stay in operation for so long.

yelp:train:14389.orig:
This location is right next to my house, convenient, and have always had great service, but I will remember to never try and ship something from here again.

I needed to ship a few T-shirts and a small picture to California. I was approached by a trainee who was training a trainee and when I asked for one box, he proceeded to put the picture into a separate box with bubble wrap. I told him I didn't want two boxes to be shipped that I wanted it all together and he said he couldn't do that because it was a fragile item. Instead I would have to pay $12 for the additional small box. I told them I preferred one box and they could put the small frame between the shirts and he said they were not allowed to do that... I even asked for a size and price sheet for their boxes but because they were remodeling they didn't have one?
Forcing individuals to buys separate boxes and packaging is a poor way of 
up-selling. Then they messed up on the address and after that I just decided to cancel everything all together.
The process seemed unorganized, took way too long, and the staff did not help out with any shipping options.
yelp:train:14389.para:
This place is conveniently close to my home and has consistently provided excellent service, but I now plan to avoid shipping anything from here in the future.

When I needed to send some T-shirts and a small picture to California, a trainee, who was training another trainee, approached me. Initially, he placed the picture in a separate box with bubble wrap. I requested a single box for all items, but he insisted on using two boxes, claiming the picture was fragile and I had to pay an extra $12 for the additional box. I insisted on one box, suggesting they could place the picture between the T-shirts, but they said it wasn't allowed. Even when I asked for a size and price list for their boxes, they couldn't provide one due to renovations.

The forced purchase of separate boxes and packaging seemed like an ineffective upselling strategy. Moreover, they made an error with the address, and in frustration, I decided to cancel the entire shipment.

The whole process felt disorganized, took far too long, and the staff didn't offer any helpful shipping options.

yelp:train:14452.orig: Terrific service.  Was having problems changing out pedals; took it in late on a Saturday and they changed them out right away, explaining the maintenance as they went.
yelp:train:14452.para: Excellent service! I had trouble swapping out the pedals and brought it in late on a Saturday. They promptly fixed it, walking me through the maintenance process.

yelp:train:14722.orig: CLOSED for good.  Lost their lease, building to be torn down. Closed, closed, Closed, closed, clothes, clothes, clothes, clothes, clothes.!
yelp:train:14722.para: The store is permanently closed due to losing their lease, and the building is set to be demolished. Closed, closed, closed, with all their clothes, clothes, clothes, clothes, clothes.!

yelp:train:14843.orig:
SunUp makes some decent brews, but the food leaves a lot to be desired. Here's what we had:

Ahi Sliders: Bland coleslaw and tuna were overpowered by the oversized and mediocre bun.

Shrimp tacos: Way too salty and overcooked. Fortunately, there were only two shrimp per taco, so the disappointment at how they tasted was mitigating by the sheer lack of content.

Macaroni & Cheese: Not bad, but it's mac & cheese.

The service was great and there's plenty of space, but there's really no reason to eat here, and, in my opinion, there are better places to get beer.
yelp:train:14843.para:
SunUp produces some acceptable beers, though their food offerings fall short. Here’s what we tried:

Ahi Sliders: The coleslaw and tuna were overshadowed by the large, subpar bun.
Shrimp Tacos: Excessively salty and overcooked, with only two shrimp per taco, which somewhat alleviated the disappointment.
Macaroni & Cheese: Decent, but it’s just mac and cheese.
The service was excellent, and the venue is spacious, but there’s no compelling reason to dine there. In my view, there are superior options for beer.

yelp:train:15135.orig:
Well let me just say I did not go here on my own. Dear sister raved and raved about it until I agreed to go with her. I will break it down like this, I thought there was to much on the menu yet nothing caught my eye maybe I just wasn't in the mood to have so many choices. 

1. Our server was an ass! There was no one in the place yet he waited on us like they were full to capacity and he was the only server. He couldn't have been less concerned about serving us. 

2. The tempura we ordered was very blah, nothing to write home about. 

3. My sister went on and on about how good her dish was. Mine was way to spicy I asked for mild. So the manager offered to change it to something else. I ordered pad Thai no tofu again mild. How can you go wrong with Pad Thai. You can it was a glutenous mess. The noodles were so over cooked it was disgusting. 

4. The decor was cute. That's the only good thing I can say. 

I have not been back. My sister has but my experience left a bad taste in my mouth literally. You get 2 stars one for decor and one because my sister likes it.
yelp:train:15135.para:
To be clear, I didn't choose to go here on my own; my sister kept talking about it until I finally agreed to join her. Here’s how it went down: I felt overwhelmed by the extensive menu, but nothing really appealed to me, possibly because I wasn't in the mood for so many options.

1. Our server was really unhelpful. Even though the restaurant was nearly empty, he treated us as if we were the only customers. He seemed indifferent to our needs.

2. The tempura we ordered was quite ordinary, nothing special.

3. My sister was very enthusiastic about her dish, but mine was way too spicy, even though I had asked for it to be mild. The manager offered to change it to pad Thai without tofu, which I also requested mild. I was hoping for the best with pad Thai, but it was a disaster. The noodles were overcooked and unappetizing.

4. The decor was cute, but that was the only positive aspect of the experience.

I haven’t returned since, and my sister has, but my experience left a bad taste, both literally and figuratively. I’d give it 2 stars: one for the decor and one because my sister likes it.

yelp:train:15246.orig:
Came to this place on a random yelp find for lunch.  The first thing to mention is if you don't get here before noon good luck finding a parking spot.  You will need to park in the neighborhood and take a nice walk.  

Walking in the front door it's a very small and quaint place with a few tables and some booth seating.  

We were seated by the door and it was definitely a little warm like some of the tips said.  

I ordered the Korean spicy beef.  The portion size was perfect and the flavors were on point.  Just enough spice to make you sweat a little but not burn your mouth off.  The beef was tender and had a good mix of veggies.  Over all great price and portion size for the dish. 

I also ordered one of slices of blueberry banana bread which was a perfect finish to the meal. 

All in all great place and I will be back for sure.
yelp:train:15246.para:
I stumbled upon this place through a Yelp recommendation for lunch. One key tip is to arrive before noon; otherwise, parking can be challenging. You'll likely need to park nearby and walk in.

Upon entering, the space is small and charming, with limited seating. We were seated by the door, and it felt a bit warm, as some reviews mentioned.

I ordered the Korean spicy beef. The portion was just right, and the flavors were spot-on. It had a nice balance of spice, making my mouth water without being too hot. The beef was tender, and there was a good mix of vegetables. Overall, it was a great value for the dish.

I also tried a slice of blueberry banana bread, which was the perfect ending to the meal.

In summary, it's a fantastic spot, and I plan to return.

yelp:train:15569.orig:
I am really shocked at all of the decent reviews for this place.  The only reason I am giving it one star is because the service was fast and friendly.  I ordered the Seafood Bento box and my husband got the chicken teriyaki and a beef bowl. 

Midway through, we discussed going through the Wendy's drive through.  It just seemed like the lowest quality of everything was used- gross rice, fish with a weird texture, even the chicken seemed of a lower quality then you get at the Asian food places in the mall.

Tokyo Express actually was recommended to us, unfortunately, we wish we would have stayed home and cooked.

I would not recommend.
yelp:train:15569.para:
I'm genuinely surprised by the positive feedback for this restaurant. The sole reason for my one-star rating is the fast and friendly service. My partner and I ordered the Seafood Bento box, chicken teriyaki, and a beef bowl. 

As we were halfway through our meal, we considered ordering from Wendy's drive-through. The food here felt subpar, with gross-tasting rice, fish with an odd texture, and chicken that seemed inferior to what we typically get from mall-based Asian food places.

We were actually recommended to try Tokyo Express, but we regret not staying home to cook instead. I wouldn't recommend this place to others.

yelp:train:15638.orig: Good pizza, not the best I've ever had.  It's cheap; you can get 2 cheese slices & a drink for $4. $0.50 per topping per slice.  Friendly staff, but the service is a little bit slow.  My friend had to wait 47 min for his pizza last Tuesday, but usually it's not that bad.
yelp:train:15638.para: The pizza is decent, though not the best I've tasted. It's affordable—two cheese slices with a drink cost just $4—and each additional topping adds $0.50 per slice. The staff is friendly, yet the service can be a bit slow; my friend waited 47 minutes for his pizza last Tuesday, but it's usually not that lengthy.

yelp:train:15858.orig: Went there for Arizona Restaurant week and discovered a gem!    Food was excellent, service great and ambiance charming.  The only negative is that it is located in an area that seems a little run down.
yelp:train:15858.para: I participated in Arizona Restaurant Week and found a real hidden gem. The food was outstanding, the service was fantastic, and the atmosphere was delightful. The only drawback is that the restaurant is situated in an area that appears somewhat dilapidated.

yelp:train:16116.para: I really enjoy the chicken fried steak.

yelp:train:16465.orig:
Marshall's Rocks.

I love coming by here to pick up any house stuff, stationary, decorations, wrapping supplies like gift bags, fancy soaps-- just a bunch of stuff I don't NEED but like to BUY.

The shoe department is sad but the clothes are a great deal and lots of variety, you just have to go looking thru everything.  SO if you have the time, it's worth it.  But basically I purchase house stuff and crap I don't need and then I go home and look at it all and wonder why I just spent all this money of ""stuff""-- but I get the shopping rush at a bargain price. What more can you ask for?
yelp:train:16465.para:
Marshall's Rocks is a place I enjoy visiting for household items, stationery, decorations, and wrapping supplies like gift bags and fancy soaps—things I don't necessarily need but like to buy.

The shoe section is disappointing, but the clothing is a great bargain with plenty of variety, though you do need to sift through everything. So, if you have the time, it's definitely worth it. Primarily, I buy household items and unnecessary items, then I return home and wonder why I spent so much on "stuff." However, I get the thrill of a good deal, and that's all I really need.

yelp:train:16593.orig: Im drooling just thinking about this place!!! Once again, had a bad craving for Mexican food and was across the street. SOOOOOO good. First, the fact that they brought out salsa AND bean dip, I love. Not everyone likes salsa, I liked having a little of both. Both were good. I ordered the 3 cheese chimi with jalapeno cream cheese. OHHH MY GOSH!!! One of the best items ive had, of all Mexican food dishes!!! Obsessed. Probably will only order that from here on out at this place. The waitress was so nice, and attentive. Margarita was cheap and good. AND on sundays kids eat free. Good food cheap liquor and free to feed the kid?! Winner in my book!
yelp:train:16593.para: I'm practically drooling just imagining this place! I had a sudden craving for Mexican food, and it was right across the street. It was absolutely fantastic. They served both salsa and bean dip, which I really appreciated. I ordered the 3 cheese chimi with jalapeno cream cheese, and it was incredible—possibly the best Mexican dish I've ever had! I'm hooked. I'll likely only get that from here now. The waitress was super nice and attentive. The margarita was both affordable and tasty. And on Sundays, kids eat for free. With great food, cheap drinks, and free kids' meals, it's a total win in my book!

yelp:train:16834.orig: Where else are you going to buy Big and Tall guy stuff with style?  Come on!  Ever been to the \""old guy style\"" B &T shops?  If it weren't for Casual Male (and the new form of it:  Destination XL, there would be nothing but epaulettes and high rise pants on my man!  Just say NO!
yelp:train:16834.para: Where can you find stylish options for big and tall men? Don't you remember the outdated styles at traditional B&T stores? Thanks to Casual Male and its modern iteration, Destination XL, there are still stylish choices available. Say no to those outdated epaulettes and high-rise pants!

yelp:train:16903.orig: Lamb tikki masala and garlic naan are delicious. I try to come at least once every couple weeks for lunch. Great food every time and the owner and his wife are hands on and very kind. Definitely recommend this place.
yelp:train:16903.para: I enjoy the lamb tikki masala and garlic naan so much that I make it a point to visit at least every couple of weeks for lunch. The food is consistently great, and the owner and his wife are very hands-on and kind. I highly recommend this place.

yelp:train:17315.orig: First time eating here and they were very busy. The service was good not fast and not slow. Really good flavorful pizza not a bad price
yelp:train:17315.para: On my first visit, the place was quite crowded. The service was decent—neither too rushed nor too sluggish. The pizza was exceptionally flavorful, and the price was quite reasonable.

yelp:train:17472.orig:
Going down hill fast and signs of stopping! Sorry I have not reviewed this joint sooner. I have been going to Deemo's since they first opened at the Esplanade. The food and the service used to be fantastic! The Portabello mushroom burger was my fav! Now they can't get nothin right. 

The last time I had the burger it was different they swear its the same meat and everything but my taste buds don't lie. This burger was awful, maybe even freezer burnt. The huge mushroom was the best part. 

I tried the Philly cheese recently and um I really to prefer to have meat on my sandwich! This was the sorriest Philly steak ever! Barely to bites of meat all bread and not good bread either! 

Their crab cakes are awesome but the last time I got those they were under cooked and had bits of shell in them YUCK! 

Today I ordered eggs over medium and crisp bacon. I got eggs over easy and under cooked precooked bacon that was so thin you could see through! All this for 6.17! Plus tax! This is bad eggs and really bad bacon! YUCK!

Don't bother dropping in here for the free app unless you go for the crab cakes and then leave. Just not what they used to be and it just keeps getting worse.

A
yelp:train:17472.para:
I've been frequenting Deemo's since they opened at the Esplanade, and the food and service used to be outstanding. My favorite was the Portabello mushroom burger, but now everything is off. 

The burger I had last time was disappointing; despite assurances that it was the same quality, my taste buds disagreed. It was terrible, possibly even freezer-burned. The large mushroom was the only redeeming feature.

I recently tried the Philly cheese steak, but I much prefer meat on my sandwich. This was the worst Philly steak I've ever had—barely any meat, just a lot of bread, and not even good bread at that!

Their crab cakes are still great, but the last time I had them, they were undercooked and had shell fragments, which were unpleasant. 

Today, I ordered eggs over medium and crispy bacon. Instead, I got eggs cooked too easily and undercooked, thin bacon that was almost transparent. All this for $6.17 plus tax! It's a real letdown.

Unless you're there for the crab cakes, there's no point in stopping in. The quality has declined, and it's only getting worse.

yelp:train:17657.orig:
I like Jamba Juice.

I like this particular location as well.

Like Alicia, the place was JAMbING loud with music-- like really loud, like I thought I turned into my parent's b/c I almost wanted to say, ""Can you turn the music down, it's hurting my ears.""

I bit my tongue and anxiously awaited for my Orange-A-Peel.  It was good.  It was exactly what I expected and wanted at that very moment. 

Clean, nice staff, good smoothie.  Just loud.
yelp:train:17657.para:
I enjoy Jamba Juice, and I particularly like this store.

The place was incredibly noisy, much like Alicia described, with the music blasting so loudly that I felt like I was about to tell my parents to turn it down, as it was hurting my ears.

I managed to hold back and waited for my Orange-A-Peel, which was delicious and perfectly matched my desires at that moment.

The staff was clean and friendly, and the smoothie was great, though the noise level was high.

yelp:train:17801.orig: Food mediocre, pastries days old, service lousy (3 other tables arriving after me were served first), dirty dishes, floors, windows, bathroom.  Place is a dump!
yelp:train:17801.para: The food was subpar, and the pastries seemed stale. The service was poor (other tables that arrived later were attended to before me), and the place was filthy, with dirty dishes, floors, windows, and a bathroom in dire need of cleaning. It's a real mess!

yelp:train:17947.orig: They need to change the oil, fries both regular and greek came out brown and well done. Everything was bland. Greek salad tasted like nothing.  Calamari fried in old oil as well. Gyro sandwich was bland too. Beer selection limited. I'm not sure how this place is still running? Service was outstanding but we will never go back.
yelp:train:17947.para: The oil needs changing; both the regular and Greek fries were overcooked and dark. Everything lacked flavor— the Greek salad tasted flat, and the calamari seemed fried in stale oil. The gyro sandwich was also unexciting. The beer choices were limited. I wonder how this place stays open? Despite the excellent service, we won't be returning.

yelp:train:18075.orig: Great coffee and friendly people makes for a 5 star experience
yelp:train:18075.para: A 5-star experience is created by excellent coffee and welcoming staff.

yelp:train:18247.orig: I usually won't give a one-star review, but in extreme cases. I was horrifically disappointed with the food and the service. We were there on New Year's Eve, which should be a night in which they are on their A-game, but I guess they don't find that important. I ordered a steak, cooked medium. When I got the steak, it was cooked well done. It is very sad when a restaurant can't cook a steak. Then the service was disappointing as we hardly saw our waitress. I surely hope there is a new chef since I was there, because I think he worked at McDonald's before there.
yelp:train:18247.para: While I generally avoid one-star reviews, I felt compelled to do so in this extreme case. The food and service were both terrible, especially on New Year's Eve when one would expect top-notch performance. I ordered a medium-rare steak, but it was overcooked. It's disheartening when a restaurant can't get a simple steak right. The service was also subpar; we barely saw our waitress. I sincerely hope a new chef has taken over, as the current one seems inexperienced, perhaps even lacking the skills of a McDonald's worker.

yelp:train:18506.orig: Don't bother scheduling your appointment in advance online(they never received my reservation even though I had a confirmation number.). Also make sure you give your name at \""check-in\"" to at least three different people to make sure you get on the list.  Worst customer service.
yelp:train:18506.para: Avoid trying to schedule your appointment online in advance (they never acknowledged my reservation despite having a confirmation number). Be sure to mention your name at the "check-in" process to at least three different people to ensure you're included. The customer service here is the worst.

yelp:train:18604.orig: Found Framin Works on Yelp. and was not disappointed. I had a very large picture that needed framing. In the past, I had gone the easy route, and gone to Michaels for all my framing needs. The picture I had was so large that I decided to call them with the dimensions of the picture and tell them what I was looking to have done. The lowest prices they quoted me was almost $400, and that was with a 60%+20% off coupon!!! i decided to try Framin works, and saved over $100 off the lowest price that Michael's had quoted me. Granted, this price included a 25% off coupon, but I still thought the price was very fair. When I brought the picture in, the owner was very fair and didn't try to oversell me. He actually, told me that all I really needed for the picture was a new frame. He said the glass was fine, and that matting was in pretty good shape. I ended up replacing the matting and the frame. The finished product was great. I will definitely be back!
yelp:train:18604.para: I discovered Framin Works on Yelp and was pleasantly surprised. I needed to frame a very large picture, and in the past, I had used Michaels for all my framing needs. When I called Michaels with the dimensions, they quoted me almost $400, even with a significant discount. Deciding to give Framin Works a try, I ended up saving over $100 compared to Michaels' lowest price. Although Framin Works offered a 25% discount, I felt the price was reasonable. Upon bringing the picture in, the owner was honest and didn't try to upsell me. He suggested that the glass and matting were in good condition and only needed new frames. I opted to replace the matting and frames, and the final result was excellent. I plan to return!

yelp:train:19737.orig: After hearing about this place for years, and finally being able to get a parking spot close by, I decided to try it. But low and behold the pizzeria was full so I was directed to a very cluttered and crowded market with the same menu. Besides the uncomfortable claustrophobic atmosphere, it was frustrating finding a spot to wait for my food without being pushed in a corner or up against a display. And sorry, the food was good but those had to be magic avocados for the price I paid for that personal pizza.
yelp:train:19737.para: For years, I had heard about this place and managed to find a nearby parking spot, leading me to give it a try. However, upon arrival, I discovered the pizzeria was packed, so I was directed to a bustling market with the same menu. The environment was cramped and uncomfortable, making it difficult to find a comfortable spot to wait without feeling pushed into a corner or against a display. While the food was decent, the price for a personal pizza seemed too high, especially considering the quality of the avocados used.

yelp:train:19870.orig:
This place has to be one of the most overrated restaurants... ever.

So this review is for dinner and maybe that is why I was so utterly disappointed.

Food:
Brushcetta- We sampled the artichoke, pesto with salmon, roasted red peppers with goat cheese, and the fig spread with green apple.  I mean all of them were decent nothing was amazing.  In fact, i think I could easily put together a couple of them myself and have them taste just as good if not better.

Nine Iron-  Once again, it was OK.  Nothing special at all.  Just exactly as was described on the menu.

Italian Picnic Salad-  Once again, nothing special at all.  Could have made it myself.

Service:
So on vacation we tend to eat out.  This was our 4th dinner out in a row and the first 3 had impeccable service.  This place did not.  I felt like it was a lot of waiting and waiting more.   We ordered something they did not bring and when we asked for that something we waited and waited....  Servers were nice enough though but they didn't seem that busy on a Sunday night so I would have expected service to be better.

Ambiance:
Servers-Well, the servers I would classify as Arizona hipsterish.  Like not real hipster
yelp:train:19870.para:
This establishment is undoubtedly one of the most overhyped restaurants I've ever visited.

My experience with the food was quite disappointing, especially since it was dinner time.

Brushcetta: We tried the artichoke, pesto with salmon, roasted red peppers with goat cheese, and fig spread with green apple. While they were acceptable, nothing was outstanding. In fact, I believe I could recreate a couple of these myself and perhaps even improve upon them.

Nine Iron: It was just okay, nothing exceptional. It matched the description on the menu.

Italian Picnic Salad: Again, it was unremarkable. I could have prepared something similar at home.

Service: During our vacation, we dined out four nights in a row, and the first three places had excellent service. This one fell short. We had to wait a lot, and when we requested something that wasn't brought, we waited even longer. The servers were friendly, but given that it was a Sunday night and not overly busy, I expected better service.

Ambiance: The servers had a distinct Arizona hipster vibe, though not quite genuine hipsters.

yelp:train:20005.orig: I totally 100% agree w Serianna T.\n\nI have felt the same way about the seating, and parking and mediocre foods... Postino and LGO are complete cluster F***s for anyone who plans on driving there. I also feel like the general atmosphere is trying so hard to be relaxed and casual that it is stressful for the guests.
yelp:train:20005.para: I completely agree with Serianna T. on my feelings about the seating, parking, and the food quality. Postino and LGO are really problematic for drivers. The overall atmosphere seems to be attempting to create a relaxed and casual vibe, but it ends up being stressful for the guests.

yelp:train:21129.orig:
I just left this restaurant 15 minutes ago and decided to sign up for Yelp to write this review. 

Listen, Aunt Chilada's, before tonight... was a mediocre restaurant near where my boyfriend works. We'd sometimes go there for lunch if we needed a quick bite, and the salsa was good. So it was there to fill our need if we really had nowhere else to go. That being said, tonight was a disaster.

I'm sure it's because they had a few large groups of people who'd already sat down before us in the banquet room, wherever that is. But we waited for over an hour for our food. When it arrived, my burrito had cheese in it (I am lactose intolerant and asked for none). The waiter was courteous and zipped back to get me my correct order, but came back a mere ten seconds later with a cold burrito. Really? I know I've already waited, but at least give it to me warm.

All in all, the server generally ignored us because the table to our left was angry they weren't getting any food, and the table to the right of us had a solid 30 people in it. So, I get it in a sense. But it would've been nice to have them tell us straight out that they had a 46 person table on the other side of the restuarant th
yelp:train:21129.para:
I recently visited Aunt Chilada's for the first time and decided to write this review right after leaving. 

Before tonight, the restaurant was just okay, located near my boyfriend's workplace. We occasionally went there for a quick lunch, and the salsa was decent. However, tonight was a complete letdown.

I suspect it was due to a few large groups already seated in the banquet room. We waited over an hour for our food. When it finally arrived, my burrito contained cheese, which I specifically asked to be excluded since I am lactose intolerant. The waiter was polite and returned to correct this, but the burrito was cold, which was disappointing. I understand the wait, but at least it could have been warm.

Overall, the server mostly ignored us because the table to our left was upset about not receiving their food promptly, and the table to our right had a large group. While I can see the server's perspective, it would have been better if they had informed us about the large group on the other side of the restaurant.

yelp:train:21611.orig: I have a passion for great pizza.  It's been my favorite food since I was a kid. I've outgrown my fondness for the typical pep & sausage as my tastebuds have been seeking out new flavors. The first time I tried the Gourmet White Pizza at Stumpy's I believe I heard the chorus to Hallelujah! Another favorite of mine is the Hot Blue Chicken Wing Pizza...an explosion of flavorful deliciousness! So good...I am actually salivating over my keyboard just thinking about it! Anyway...Stumpy's is by far one of my most favorite pizza places. Another giant plus? The owners and staff are the most amazingly friendly people I have ever met. They greet everyone with a warm smile and a wonderful pizza!
yelp:train:21611.para: I've always had a deep love for pizza, and it's remained my go-to food since childhood. My taste buds have evolved, moving beyond classic pepperoni and sausage. When I first tried the Gourmet White Pizza at Stumpy's, it was like hearing the opening notes of Hallelujah! Another standout is the Hot Blue Chicken Wing Pizza—it's a burst of flavor that's simply divine! Just thinking about it makes me crave it. In fact, Stumpy's is one of my absolute favorite pizza spots. What really sets them apart is their incredibly friendly owners and staff, who greet everyone with a warm smile and a delicious pizza!

yelp:train:21641.orig:
I wanted breakfast that didn't require a long wait or making it myself.  I was probably off best by just sucking it up and making breakfast at home because Lantana Grille was pretty disappointing.
We arrived and thought the place was actually closed because there was not a single car in the parking lot and when we walked in, there was no hostess.  But we saw some people sitting so I asked if we just seat ourselves and they replied with ""Sure!""-- I guess that is what I would say too if someone asked me mid breakfast at Lantana Grille what to do upon walking in.

There was a large party in the back, they mentioned that they were in town for a wedding so I am guessing they must have walked over from the Pointe Hotel.  (this explained no cars in the lot).

It is set up like a breakfast buffet, you pay $15 or $16/person and eat whatever in the buffet.  The choices are limited and not that good.  The best part was the made to order omlets and that is it.  Even the sauasage and bacon seemed to taste off.  HOW does that happen?  So the buffet had scrambled eggs (don't eat those-ick), sausage, bacon, french toast, syrup, cereal, fruit.  oh and the omlets-- best bet are the omlets.
yelp:train:21641.para:
I was looking for a quick breakfast option without having to cook, but Lantana Grille turned out to be a letdown. Upon arrival, we thought the place might be closed since there were no cars in the parking lot, and there was no hostess when we entered. However, we saw some people seated and asked if we could just find a spot, to which we were told "Sure!"—which, I suppose, is what one would say at Lantana Grille during breakfast.

There was a large group in the back, likely from a wedding at the Pointe Hotel, which explained the empty parking lot. The restaurant operates as a buffet, with a $15 to $16 per person price tag, offering a limited selection that wasn't particularly impressive. The standout was the made-to-order omelets, but even the sausage and bacon tasted off. The buffet included scrambled eggs (which were unappetizing), sausage, bacon, French toast, syrup, cereal, and fruit. The omelets were the best choice overall.

yelp:train:21948.orig: As I try to chew my rubbery, non-spicy General Tso's chicken, I'm writing this review with a feeling of  regret for spending $30 at this place. I'm pretty sure the chicken is seasoned with beef flavor Top Ramen spice, and the pad Thai is made with the noodles from the same package. I contemplated finishing the food but I think I'm going to have to wave the white flag. Never. Again.
yelp:train:21948.para: Feeling disappointed after spending $30 on my meal, I'm now regretfully writing this review while trying to eat the rubbery, non-spicy General Tso's chicken, which tastes suspiciously like it was seasoned with beef flavor from Top Ramen. The pad Thai seems to be made with noodles from the same package. I considered finishing the meal, but I might as well admit defeat. I'll definitely not return here again.

yelp:train:22080.orig: About what one would expect from a conglomerate fast food chain as far as the food quality goes, but what was especially remarkable today was the very poor customer service. I sat outside, and when the employee brought my lunch out and did not bring a fork, she acted almost joyous that she got to tell me that I have to go inside to get my own fork. She will have no future in customer service I'm sure of that.\n\nThis was at 2:30 on 11/2/13.
yelp:train:22080.para: The food quality aligned with what one would expect from a large fast-food chain, but today's experience was notably disappointing due to the poor customer service. I was seated outdoors, and when the staff member delivered my lunch without a fork, she seemed almost delighted to inform me that I needed to go inside to retrieve one myself. I have no doubt she won't last long in customer service roles. This incident occurred on November 2, 2013, at 2:30 PM.

yelp:train:22223.orig: I would give negative stars if I could. I went in last weekend to purchase/look for a helmet, jacket and gloves. I spent 45 minutes in there looking at various items and trying on helmets. No one that worked there ever looked in y direction or said \""hi\"". I left and bought a jacket online and a helmet gloves, tee shirt at the helmet store on 35th ave. I can walk to cycle gear from my house and drove out of my way and spent good $$$ at a place way more deserving than cycle gear. I'm not sure because I'm a female or because I didn't come in on my bike. Either way it's inexcusable.
yelp:train:22223.para: If possible, I'd give this place negative stars. Last weekend, I visited to find a helmet, jacket, and gloves. I spent 45 minutes browsing and trying on helmets, but no staff members even glanced my way or greeted me. In the end, I bought a jacket online, a helmet, gloves, and a t-shirt from another store on 35th Ave. I could have walked to Cycle Gear from home, but I drove out of my way and spent a significant amount of money at a store that was far less deserving. Whether it was because I'm a woman or I didn't arrive on my bike, the lack of customer service was unacceptable.

yelp:train:22523.orig: PetSmart is the only place you should be shopping for pet supplies because they're an Arizona-based business, and we should all be supporting the \""shop local\"" movement. They always provide good customer service and I've never had an issue with returns.The company is also a good corporate  citizen, putting lots of money and effort into its charity division. The company supports homeless shelters and food service for people as well as all they do for homeless pets.
yelp:train:22523.para: PetSmart stands out as the ideal destination for pet supplies, being a local Arizona business that aligns with the "shop local" ethos. They consistently offer excellent customer service and have never caused any problems with returns. Moreover, the company is actively involved in community service, dedicating substantial resources to its charity initiatives. This includes supporting homeless shelters, food services for people, and the care of homeless pets.

yelp:train:22657.orig:

my bill should be $131.22....yes they CHARGED me for a free tablet!! What a rip off...BAIT and SWITCH!!   These phone companies should be held responsible for all added fees. When I called Verizon direct I spoke to 3 supervisors for over an hour and they too could not figure it out and told me to call store...
 I love the coverage of VERIZON, but service is horrible....and cheat their customers. My plan is the same as a friend has and she pays $49.00 a month...why all the differences. The longer you stay with a company it should be cheaper...SHE'S a NEW customer..VERY UNHAPPY!!!!
BUYER BEWARE!!!
If I could give a ZERO rating I would.
yelp:train:22657.para:
Visited to pick up a free tablet advertised online, only to receive a bill of $187.55, which is usually $75.00 for me. I contacted Nick, the manager, to clarify. My bill includes a $49.00 charge, even though I only paid $56.22 for accessories. My total should be $131.22, yet I was charged for a free tablet—what a scam! This is clearly bait and switch. Phone companies must be accountable for all additional fees.

When I called Verizon directly, I spoke to three supervisors for over an hour, but they couldn't resolve it and advised me to contact the store. I love Verizon's coverage, but their service is terrible and they cheat customers. My plan is the same as a friend's, yet she pays only $49.00 a month. Why the disparity? She's a new customer, and I'm very unhappy. BEWARE! If I could, I'd give them a zero rating.

yelp:train:22988.para: I'm not sure I could rate this place even 1 star. My experience at the one in Paradise Valley Mall was terrible. The attendant barely spoke to me, just urging me to move.
