yelp:train:103733.para:
Pros: The airport is compact and convenient to navigate.

Cons: My wait in the security line was lengthy—over half an hour—due to just one security checkpoint being operational. Fortunately, I had a later flight to catch. 

There are several dining options available post-security, including Wendy's and Coffee Bean and Tea Leaf. Additionally, there's a good variety of airlines, with Southwest offering a direct flight from Las Vegas to Burbank, CA.

yelp:train:103782.orig:
It's really bad. I get it, it's Vegas so you need to be all show but forgetting everything else while bells and whistles are going off everywhere else? Not cool.

The signage is pretty much non-existent especially if you are looking to pick up your luggage. You are just in one huge auditorium but lights, videos and loud sounds just kinda circling praying for your baggage to show up. 

The taxi line is insane but it does seem to move pretty quickly, they just really pack 'em in everywhere in this airport. Overall thought, it def does the job of welcoming you to Sin City.
yelp:train:103782.para:
It's really poor quality. I understand that Vegas requires a lot of spectacle, but neglecting everything else while all the bells and whistles are going off? That's not acceptable.

The signage is practically nonexistent, especially if you're trying to retrieve your luggage. You're in one massive auditorium, and the lights, videos, and loud sounds just swirl around as you wait for your bag to appear. 

The taxi line is incredibly long, but it does seem to move fairly quickly. They really cram people everywhere in this airport. Overall, it definitely serves to welcome you to Sin City.

yelp:train:104137.orig: A visit to Aloha Specialties has been a tradition on all my trips to Vegas.  The reason is the great food.  I guess you can categorize the place as \""fast casual\"".  You order at the counter, take a number and food is brought out to you.  Service was quick.  This past weekend, my boys and I tried the Kim Chee Saimen, Korean Chicken , and Tripe Stew.  Everything was hot and delicious.  The Saimen had a nice kick from the spicy kim chee and it included large blocks of tofu.   That bowl of soup was huge.  The Korean Chicken was also well flavored, moist and has a nice grilled crust.  We all agreed that the Tripe Stew was amazing.  Tender pieces of tripe in a not-so-thick tomato based sauce.  That was comfort food at it's best.  I would order that again.  Overall, it was a great visit to the hawaiian restaurant.
yelp:train:104137.para: My trips to Vegas have always included a visit to Aloha Specialties, primarily for their excellent food. The restaurant operates in a "fast casual" style, where you place your order at the counter, get a number, and your food is brought to you. The service was prompt. Last weekend, my sons and I tried the Kim Chee Saimen, Korean Chicken, and Tripe Stew. Everything was piping hot and delicious. The Saimen featured a good kick from the spicy kim chee and included generous portions of tofu. The soup was particularly large. The Korean Chicken was well-seasoned, moist, and had a nice grilled crust. We all agreed that the Tripe Stew was outstanding—tender pieces of tripe in a flavorful, not-too-thick tomato-based sauce. It was truly comfort food at its best. I would definitely order it again. Overall, it was a fantastic experience at this Hawaiian restaurant.

yelp:train:104316.orig: This hotel is run by con artists and scammers.  Wouldn't doubt if they are the hookers and drug addicts that other reviewers talked about. I booked a room for tonight (New Year's Eve) and was unable to go due to a medical emergency. I had to take my friend to the ER and we were there for hours. Can't say the same for the hotel staff.  The booking company said that CHRIS the general manager would not give a refund due to the fact that he wouldn't be able to re-book the room. When I called the hotel directly I was told that CHRIS no longer works for the company.  Clearly someone is lying and I doubt it's the booking company. This hotel and it's staff are just shady and criminalistic.
yelp:train:104316.para: This establishment is managed by con artists and fraudsters, and it's not a stretch to think they might be the hooker and drug dealer that other reviewers mentioned. I made a reservation for New Year's Eve but had to cancel due to a medical emergency. I had to rush my friend to the ER, where we waited for hours. After learning my friend was stable but unable to travel, I attempted to cancel the booking. The booking company was helpful, but the hotel staff were uncooperative. They claimed that the general manager, CHRIS, wouldn't issue a refund because the room couldn't be rebooked. Are you serious? In Las Vegas on New Year's Eve, you can't rebook the room? It seems someone is fibbing, and I believe it's the hotel staff. I understand the cancellation policy, but I've received refunds from other hotels in similar situations. This place and its staff are clearly suspicious and possibly criminal.

yelp:train:104731.orig:
I love Downtown Las Vegas also known as the 9th island. I'm a Hawaii girl living in Los Angeles, so when I go to Vegas, I always stop at the Cal for a slice of home. The local style food at Market Street Cafe (they have bomb Butterfish) and the plate lunch style grinds at Aloha Specialties are ONO! 

If you're not from Hawaii, you probably won't understand why a 30-something would want to hang at the Cal, the place is like a Hawaiian version of the movie Cocoon. But I love seeing the old Japanese and local people from Hawaii gambling with their wheel chairs and sometimes even oxygen tanks. They go! 

I've been staying at the Cal since small kid time, so its very nostalgic for me, lots of memories there. I love seeing the mixed faces and pidgin accents :) Also I've been brainwashed since childhood (they mail regulars a magazine with pictures of all the Hawaii winners) that I will win if play at a Sam Boyd hotel. Sure enough, I won 1000 quarters on Wheel of Fortune on my last visit, must be because I rubbed the shaka buddha's belly :) 

See you in March 2014, yay :)
yelp:train:104731.para:
I adore Downtown Las Vegas, often called the 9th island. As a native of Hawaii now living in Los Angeles, I always make a point to visit the Cal for a taste of home with a slice of pizza. The local cuisine at Market Street Cafe, especially their delicious Butterfish, and the plate lunch offerings at Aloha Specialties are fantastic.

For those not from Hawaii, it might be puzzling why a 30-something would frequent the Cal, as it feels like a Hawaiian version of the movie Cocoon. However, I enjoy watching the elderly Japanese and local Hawaiians play their games, sometimes even using wheelchairs or oxygen tanks. They truly embrace the experience.

I've been staying at the Cal since I was a child, making it a very nostalgic place for me with many cherished memories. I love the mix of faces and pidgin accents there. Since childhood, I've been conditioned to believe that playing at a Sam Boyd hotel increases my chances of winning, thanks to the regular newsletters sent to regulars featuring Hawaii winners. During my last visit, I won 1000 quarters on Wheel of Fortune, and I attribute it to rubbing the shaka buddha's belly.

See you in March 2014, yay!

yelp:train:104753.orig: Went there and we were told to wait for our food but since we had to wait the cashier was super nice and offered free ice cream and drinks friendly worker
yelp:train:104753.para: We went there and were asked to wait for our food, but the cashier, who was exceptionally nice, compensated our wait by offering free ice cream and drinks; the staff member was very friendly.

yelp:train:105303.orig: Really so so with that price range. However, we enjoy the view that we can see people enjoy sun tanning and swimming. However, the bread pudding was pretty good there. Worth to try
yelp:train:105303.para: While the price point is average, we do appreciate the view, which lets us watch people enjoy sunbathing and swimming. The bread pudding was quite satisfactory, making it worth a try.

yelp:train:105669.orig:
It's a crappy tourist trap now.  Everything is over priced for a pawn shop. Other than jewelry, there wasnt much inventory to speak of.  The only things that were flying out the door were t shirts and refrigerator magnets. 

Stay away from their parking lot and stick with the metered street parking.

Go just to say you went...then go to Luv-It for a custard and make the trek worth your time.
yelp:train:105669.para:
It has become a disappointing tourist attraction, with everything priced like a pawn shop. Apart from jewelry, the inventory is quite sparse. The only items selling quickly are T-shirts and refrigerator magnets.

Avoid their parking lot and use the metered street parking instead.

Visit just to check it off your list, then head to Luv-It for some custard to make the trip worthwhile.

yelp:train:106235.orig:
My husband and I were married at Graceland Wedding Chapel 6/14/14 and we had the best experience ever! Rachel was so very helpful from the very beginning. She provided me with a great list of vendors and services to make our special day go smoothly. Our family and friends had such a great time. The dueling Elvis wedding package was worth every penny. Jaime and Mark
yelp:train:106235.para:
On June 14, 2014, my husband and I got married at Graceland Wedding Chapel, and it was an unforgettable experience. Thanks again for everything, Jaime and Mark.

yelp:train:106597.orig: $5.50 for a large soda & NO REFILL!!!!! I get it unlimited refills won't fly but none....not even a discount for a refill???? No sign either??? In case you haven't noticed refills are the industry norm.
yelp:train:106597.para: A large soda costs $5.50, and there are no refills at all—no refills whatsoever, not even a discounted one. There's no sign indicating this policy either. Given that refills are standard practice in the industry, this seems unusual.

yelp:train:106610.orig: I had to come here 4 times during posted business hours to finally find it actually open to pick up my clothes. When I informed the woman I was unhappy with that, she told me that was impossible and didn't happen. Don't think you're going to call me a liar and get it away with it when you're a cash only business. Maybe the IRS would be interested.
yelp:train:106610.para: I visited during regular business hours four times to collect my clothes, only to find the place closed each time. The woman I spoke to denied this, saying it was impossible. yelp:train:106760.orig:
I met some friends who were already here and I must say ALL of us were impressed. Right as I got there they were ordering food, which was Sheppard's Pie, Irish Nachos, and Sticky Toffee Pudding! All of it was DELICIOUS!!! The staff was Great and we all determined we will be coming back! 

I also like the fact, if you didn't want to sit at the bar or by the bar they had a separate eating area too. More cozy and quite if you can believe for a bar.

yelp:train:106760.para:
Upon meeting up with some friends who were already there, I must confess that we were all thoroughly impressed. As soon as I arrived, they were ordering Sheppard's Pie, Irish Nachos, and Sticky Toffee Pudding! Everything we tried was absolutely delicious! The service was fantastic, and we all agreed we'll be returning soon.

Additionally, I appreciated that there was a separate, more intimate dining area if you preferred not to sit at the bar. It was surprisingly cozy and quiet for a bar setting.

P.S. - We enjoyed a second serving of the Sticky Toffee Pudding! Mmm Mmm Good.

yelp:train:106796.orig: This is a great little Mexican supermarket that i come to when I am craving some pan dulce. Their pastries are really good, love their conchas!
yelp:train:106796.para: This small Mexican grocery store is perfect for when I crave pan dulce, especially their conchas, which are outstanding.

yelp:train:106912.orig:
Great Chinese lunch buffet option. A true hole in the wall that is sure to leave your stomach & wallet satisfied. *Disclaimer* I am only reviewing their lunch. 

Pricing: Amazing deal. Only $6.49 for all you can eat? I'll take it.

The food quality here is excellent considering it's a buffet. The reason behind this is because unlike most Chinese buffets, Golden Dragon makes smaller proportions of food they put out, thus rendering a fresher and tastier result. They don't serve alcohol here but their Thai tea is off the damn chain. 

Service is good, fast, and friendly. They were quick to refill our drinks and take away dirty plates. 

Personal recommendation: get the chicken wings. I'm convinced this place could survive as a chicken wing joint. So crisp and delicious. I will be back :]
yelp:train:106912.para:
A fantastic choice for a Chinese lunch buffet, this hidden gem is perfect for satisfying both your appetite and budget. *Disclaimer* My review is specifically for their lunch service. 

Pricing: An incredible value at just $6.49 for all you can eat—definitely a steal.

The food quality is top-notch for a buffet, thanks to Golden Dragon's approach of serving smaller portions, which ensures the food is fresher and more flavorful. While they don't offer alcohol, their Thai tea is outstanding. 

Service is prompt, efficient, and friendly. They quickly refilled our drinks and cleared away used plates. 

Personal recommendation: The chicken wings are a must-try. They are so crispy and delicious that I think this place could thrive as a chicken wing specialist. I plan to return soon :]

yelp:train:106993.orig:
I really like the food here. the restaurant itself is really cute from the outside looks like something that belongs in Mexico! I love it

they sang me happy birthday with a full mariachi it sounded like. the staff is really nice and attentive. 

good place to come if your in Vegas and in the mood for some Mexican food.
yelp:train:106993.para:
I absolutely adore the food at this place. The restaurant has a charming exterior that gives off a distinctly Mexican vibe. I absolutely adore it.

They surprised me with a mariachi performance for my birthday, which was incredibly touching. The staff is exceptionally kind and attentive.

It's a great spot to visit if you're in Las Vegas and craving some Mexican cuisine.

yelp:train:107012.orig: I just went here for an oil change after Terribles screwed me for the last time on lying about the price. Auto Pro offers great service at a great price. Their facility is clean, the employees are professional and nice, and you can tell they've been working there for awhile. I will definitely go back. And I used the 10% off on Yelp.
yelp:train:107012.para: After Terribles misled me on the price one too many times, I decided to get an oil change at Auto Pro. The service and pricing there are excellent. The place is tidy, and the staff are both competent and friendly, giving the impression of long-term experience. I plan to return, and I took advantage of the 10% discount on Yelp.

yelp:train:107300.orig:
What a great off the strip Italian restaurant!!! Such a refresher from all the cookie cutter really over priced restaurants located inside the hotels!
The service was impeccable from the minute you walk in. The staff look like they stepped out of a Al Pacino move.. I mean that in a good way by the way...

The ambiance and the vibe were so up beat that just looking at their menu mad my mouth water. They make all their own pasta fresh, wow no Chef Ragu/Prego working there..

We ordered the antipasti appetizer. It was filled with different kinds of cheese, olives, pickled artichokes, prosciutto, spicy ham. I'm not a fan of olives but the red ones weren't all that bad. It was really good and pair that up with the bread they bring you at the table and you practically have your meal right there. But better save some room for your dinner because you have to try their pasta dishes. I ended up ordering the seafood spaghetti meal that had scallops, huge pieces of shrimp and calamari. I admit it was good but a little too much on the seafood. My BF had the Sea Bass and it was really melt in your mouth type of meal. The fish was cooked to perfection! 

I would have given them five stars
yelp:train:107300.para:
What an excellent Italian restaurant away from the strip! It's such a refreshing change from the overpriced, generic hotel dining options.

The service was outstanding from the moment we entered. The staff seemed like they were straight out of a classic Al Pacino film, in a good way, of course.

The atmosphere was lively and energetic, making us hungry just by looking at the menu. They prepare all their pasta fresh, which is impressive—no pre-made sauces here.

We started with the antipasti, which included various cheeses, olives, pickled artichokes, prosciutto, and spicy ham. While I didn't enjoy the olives much, the rest was delicious. Paired with the bread they serve, it felt like a complete meal. However, we definitely need to save room for the pasta dishes. I opted for the seafood spaghetti with scallops, large shrimp, and calamari, which was quite good but a bit heavy on the seafood. My boyfriend had the sea bass, which was incredibly tender and cooked perfectly.

I would have given them a perfect score.

yelp:train:107694.orig:
I know that Walmart as a whole is pretty trashy and low-quality, but this location seems to take the stereotype to the limit. There are so many terrible qualities to this store that I could probably write separate reviews just for each one. So I will try to condense it into one angry rant.

First of all, the service in this store is terrible. What makes this worse is the fact that they close off entire sections for cleaning - and none of the employees are particularly willing to help someone retrieve an item from the closed sections. I've literally had to come back the next day because no one would help me. Great customer relations. Really.

Next is the selection - I'm sure that they have a lot of the same things as other stores, but without willing help from the staff finding these items, you're pretty much out of luck. This applies doubly at nighttime, where the night stockers won't even point you to someone who knows anything about what is beyond their particular aisle. 

This is also the only Walmart that I've been to with a completely decimated meat section. Literally, the only beef I found on the shelves was that wonderful shade of grey with a shelf life of the previous
yelp:train:107694.para:
I find Walmart generally to be of poor quality, but this particular store seems to epitomize the stereotype. There are so many issues here that I could write a separate review for each one, but I'll try to summarize them in this rant.

To start, the service is abysmal. They close off sections for cleaning, and the staff are not helpful at all when you need something from those areas. I've had to return another day because no one assisted me. Their customer service is truly terrible.

Moving on to the selection, while they do have many common items, the lack of assistance from the staff makes it nearly impossible to find what you need. This is especially true at night, when the night stockers won't even direct you to someone who knows the layout beyond their specific aisle.

Additionally, this Walmart has the worst meat section I've ever seen. The only beef available was a disappointing shade of grey with a questionable shelf life.

yelp:train:107744.orig: I love me some breakfast, but given the ability to choose between all the meals of the day is a winner. My friend and I decided to give this place a try after a few unsuccessful attempts. Finally getting out here and looking at the menu, lunch won out. \n\nI got the tri-tip dip with a green salad. The cuts of meat are thick and generous without being jaw dislocating. With three large slices of perfectly seasoned beef, grilled onions and mushrooms, it was perfect. The vegetables were not drowned in oil and the roll was not soaked through. The tri-tip was cooked to a medium/medium-well. I normally prefer medium rare, so next time I will request it and see if they offer that option. The green salad was standard. My friend got the hobo omelet and you have to be starving to finish it. It is a gigantic monster stuffed and topped with bacon, sausage, ham, spinach, onion, and cheese. The red potato chunks are tender, not too salty, but not crispy. It comes with a bread as well. He got the biscuit. They are big, not dense and light.  Both entrees cost around nine dollars. We were shocked by how generous the portions were for the price and that it tasted good too. I could not finish the meal
yelp:train:107744.para:
I'm a big fan of breakfast, but when given the chance to enjoy any meal of the day, lunch is my go-to. My friend and I decided to give this restaurant a try after a few failed attempts. When we finally checked out the menu, lunch seemed like the best choice.

I ordered the tri-tip dip with a side salad. The meat slices were thick and plentiful, though not so large that they were hard to chew. With three generous slices of well-seasoned beef, grilled onions, and mushrooms, it was just right. The vegetables weren't overly oily, and the roll was just damp enough. The tri-tip was cooked to a medium/medium-well, which was perfect for me. Next time, I'll ask for it medium rare to see if they offer that option. My friend had the hobo omelet, which is enormous and packed with bacon, sausage, ham, spinach, onion, and cheese. The red potatoes were tender, not too salty, and not crispy. It came with a bread roll, and he had a biscuit that was big, light, and not dense. Both dishes cost about nine dollars. We were impressed by how generous the portions were for the price, and they tasted great. I couldn't finish my meal.

yelp:train:108149.orig: The old girl needs a facelift. The hotel decor is tired on the inside - room had poorly functioning AC, 150,000 watts of old bulb lamps that heated up the bathrooms, and crappy beds.  Also the hotel had no water for 20 minutes while I was there.   It WAS good for our conference though - good food at conference, good staff, and can't beat those room rates. Still though would not say here other than for conference.
yelp:train:108149.para: The establishment could use some updates. The interior design feels outdated, with a malfunctioning air conditioning system, 150,000-watt old bulbs that made the bathrooms uncomfortably warm, and subpar beds. Additionally, we experienced a water outage for about 20 minutes during our stay. On the positive side, the conference was well-organized, the food was excellent, and the staff were very accommodating. The room rates were also very competitive. However, I wouldn't recommend staying there unless it's for a conference.

yelp:train:108599.orig:

If you don't know how, they'll definitely tell you how or even refer !

The people here, most of them are good at their craft so definitely knowledgeable. 

Watch out for their DYI classes usually on Sat morning. Check different locations for different lessons. They often have something kiddo friendly as well.
yelp:train:108599.para:
I have a strong appreciation for the customer service at Home Depot in general.

They are always willing to guide you if you're unsure, and sometimes even direct you to the right resources.

The staff members are typically skilled in their roles, making them quite knowledgeable.

Be sure to look into their DIY classes, usually held on Saturday mornings. Different locations offer various sessions, and they often include activities suitable for kids.

yelp:train:108756.orig: I love their food, but hate the service. Every time I call to make an order the man is very rude and I hate it. yelp:train:108756.para: While I enjoy the food, I really dislike the service. Each time I place an order by phone, the person is extremely rude, which I find very frustrating. yelp:train:108880.para: My last visit was 5 years ago, and I discovered an ant in my dish. There was no apology, and I still had to pay. Tonight, I tried again, and there was hair in the food. yelp:train:109141.orig: Amazing views, service and food!  Go for the tasting course, it is beyond awesome.  Great seafood and steaks!  Alize is far superior when compared to the poor service and overpriced Paris Eiffel tower competitor.
yelp:train:109141.para: Absolutely stunning views, service, and cuisine! I highly recommend trying the tasting menu; it's outstanding. The seafood and steaks are top-notch! Alize clearly outshines the Paris Eiffel Tower restaurant in terms of service and value.

yelp:train:109330.orig:
Restaurant rating is a 3. 

As for it's dive bar rating, it's a solid 5. Hence the overall 4 rating. Ice cold schooners of beer on tap for $2.25, if you can get a seat at the bar. Almost got in a fist fight there arguing the merits of my favorite American Idol contestant one night. Another time a chick drunk-dialed everyone she knew in her addrress book and then fainted. Enjoyed a few free coldies while the paramedics revived her....  Cigarette stench is quite strong, and the assorted collection of waitstaff and bartenders is straight out of a sitcom. Watch for derelicts coming out of the laundromat next store looking for change on the bar.

As for the famous stromboli- skip it and get the deep dish pizza instead. Guy Fiore doesn't know shit.
yelp:train:109330.para:
The restaurant has a rating of 3, but the dive bar aspect scores a solid 5, leading to an overall rating of 4. They serve ice-cold schooners of beer for $2.25, though securing a bar seat can be challenging. One evening, we nearly came to blows discussing my favorite American Idol contestant. Another time, a woman made a drunken phone call to everyone in her address book before passing out, and the paramedics had to revive her. The place is heavily imbued with cigarette smoke, and the staff, both waiters and bartenders, seem like characters from a sitcom. Be wary of homeless individuals from the laundromat next door who might be looking for change on the bar.

As for the famous stromboli, it's best to avoid it and opt for the deep dish pizza instead. According to the owner, Guy Fiore, he doesn't know much about pizza.

yelp:train:109511.orig: Other than the delicious cheddar biscuits, I find the service horrible and the food way over-priced. I ordered the 4-course meal. Soup & salad came out pretty quickly. They were OK. Not great/not awful. I wasn't even 1//4 of the way through either when the main course showed up. As a former server, there's no excuse for that. You watch the table and drop the order for the rest of the meal to approximately coincide with the customer finishing soup &/or salad. (And they weren't busy.) The waitress brought the check before bringing the dessert that is included in the 4-course meal. I had to ask for a refill of tea. The scallops in the linguine were the size of mini-marshmallows and poor quality. Sorry, but the cheddar biscuits aren't enough to bring me back. Las Vegas has many excellent choices for seafood and Red Lobster is not one of them.
yelp:train:109511.para: Apart from the tasty cheddar biscuits, I was disappointed with the service and found the meal to be overpriced. I ordered a 4-course meal, and while the soup and salad arrived promptly, they were merely satisfactory—neither exceptional nor terrible. The main course arrived before I was halfway through my starter, which is inexcusable for a former server. Proper timing should align the main course with the customer finishing their soup or salad. The waitress brought the bill before the dessert, and I had to ask for more tea. The scallops in the linguine were tiny and of poor quality. Unfortunately, the cheddar biscuits alone won't entice me to return. Las Vegas offers many superior seafood options, and Red Lobster doesn't make the cut.

yelp:train:110227.orig:
Last minute stay in Vegas with kiddos. Felt this would be a better fit than the hard rock for them. 

Room was clean and service was good. Just a dated hotel. 

Biggest issue was. After check in we were stopped 3 times by sales people. Sign up for this and win two free nights, or oh they didn't give you your welcome package. Come here real quick. Go to desk and its same thing. A sales gimmick. I already paid to stay here. I don't need them to push a return stay worse than pan handlers. Especially with kids. 

We walked the strip and were stopped twice more on way in. And this is all by official hotel people. Quite unprofessional and annoying I thought 

We won't be returning. With kids or without.
yelp:train:110227.para:
Our recent Vegas stay with the kids was at a different hotel than the Hard Rock, as I thought it would suit them better. The room was tidy and the service was satisfactory, though the place felt a bit outdated.

The main problem was the constant sales pitches we encountered. After check-in, we were approached three times by hotel staff trying to sign us up for deals or offering the welcome package. This happened at the front desk as well. It felt like a pushy sales tactic, especially since I had already paid for our stay. I didn't appreciate them trying to sell us another stay, which was as intrusive as dealing with street vendors.

We were stopped by hotel staff twice more on our way to the strip. This behavior from official hotel personnel was unprofessional and quite annoying. 

We won't be coming back, whether with the kids or not.

yelp:train:110335.orig:
I was so scared reading the reviews.  Not sure why people gave it 1 star.  I had an absolutely amazing time and I will definitely come back again.  I arrived around 1030am so I thought I was going to have to wait around till 3. Not at all. $20 for early check in?? heck yeah I'm in and I got a $20 food or drink credit. As I walked through the halls I was  a bit scared looking at the outdated decor. Oh My, when I Walked in, what a beauty.  Huge flat screen tv, ( forgot what channel it wad but they had done great information)nice view, plenty of space and clean room.  Oh, my bathroom was huge and bed was comfy with lots of pillows.  

Pool- 5 decent size pools with 2 hot tubs to relax in.   what more can you ask for.  Chairs weren't the best but it worked.  They close at 7pm fyi.  There was a lot of garbage but that's bc us humans don't know how to pick up garbage and throw it away. So if its dirty, its bc YOU DID IT.  People would just leave the beer cans laying around.

yelp:train:110335.para:
I was really worried about the reviews I read, but I can't understand why people gave it only one star. My experience was fantastic, and I plan to return. I arrived at 10:30 AM and thought I'd have to wait until 3 PM, but that wasn't the case at all. For just $20, I got an early check-in and a $20 food or drink credit—definitely worth it. As I explored the place, the outdated decor initially made me a bit nervous, but when I entered, I was impressed. The room had a huge flat-screen TV, a great view, ample space, and was very clean. The bathroom was spacious, and the bed was comfortable with plenty of pillows.

The pool area had five decent-sized pools and two hot tubs for relaxation. It had everything you could want. The chairs weren't the best, but they did the job. The pools close at 7 PM, so keep that in mind. There was a lot of trash, but that's because people don't clean up after themselves. If the place is dirty, it's because of the guests.

The casino was nice, but I didn't win any money there. There was a Starbucks near the exit, and it often had long lines, so go early. You can find pretzels, yogurt, and McDonald's upstairs.

yelp:train:110372.orig: It was okay.  We stayed two nights.  Family of five in two rooms.  We stayed in Tower 2 which is supposedly the nicer of the two.  It really was fine, nothing bad or gross.  The bathrooms were quite nice.  However, the furnishings are tired and worn.  It was definitely not a fresh hotel.  I imagine it's because these rooms see non-stop action and abuse.  \n\nAs for location, I would have preferred to stay in New York, New York instead.  Anytime we wanted to go to the strip we had to make our way through casinos, tunnels, stairs, escalators, etc. just to get to NYNY and then we were on the strip.
yelp:train:110372.para:
It was satisfactory, and we spent two nights there with a family of five in two rooms. We opted for Tower 2, which is said to be more comfortable, and it lived up to the expectation. There was nothing particularly bad or unpleasant. The bathrooms were quite pleasant. However, the furnishings appeared old and worn out, indicating it wasn't a freshly renovated hotel. I suspect the constant use and wear and tear contribute to its condition. 

Regarding the location, I wished we had chosen to stay at New York, New York instead. Every time we wanted to reach the strip, we had to navigate through casinos, tunnels, stairs, and escalators before finally arriving at our destination.

yelp:train:110373.orig: Pros: Fairly clean, free parking\n\nCons: No WiFi, shower is 5'8\"" tall, constantly berated by staff to purchase packages for the future, zero mildly healthy restaurant choices, few TV stations, no decent bars
yelp:train:110373.para:
Pros: The place is relatively clean and offers free parking. 

Cons: There's no WiFi, the shower is quite tall at 5'8", the staff keeps urging us to buy future packages, there are no mild or healthy food options at the restaurants, the TV channels are limited, and there are no good bars available.

yelp:train:110476.orig:
Nice 
Big

yelp:train:110476.para: Nice and spacious, it appeared quite clean, but everything was on the pricey side, with parking costing a whopping $10.

yelp:train:111148.orig: Honestly the best place to eat in Vegas... and The best part ... it's NOT on the strip.  Whatever you order you will be impressed.  The wait for this place is sometimes one hr. and there's a reason for it.  Tuna Tar Tar, Steak Sliders and Dates and the apple salad.  I can go on for ever.  This is a LAS VEGAS Must Eat.
yelp:train:111148.para: Truly, the top dining spot in Vegas... and the best thing is, it's not located on the strip. No matter what you choose, you'll be wowed. The wait can be up to an hour, but it's well worth it. Try the Tuna Tar Tar, Steak Sliders, Dates, and the apple salad—there are so many delicious options. This restaurant is an absolute must-try in Las Vegas.

yelp:train:111232.orig: This place has really gone down hill, I hope they reopen with a better quality and brand.
yelp:train:111232.para: This location has significantly declined in quality, and I sincerely hope they revitalize it with improved standards and a stronger brand.

yelp:train:111364.orig: Cheap place to stay. Good location but that's about it- HEAVY smokers in this hotel and little to do other than gamble. Charge for gym use (as a guest paying to stay) is an extra $25 per person per day. This place needs a clean up!
yelp:train:111364.para: While it offers a budget-friendly option and a decent location, the hotel has significant issues. It's heavily smoked in, and the only real entertainment is gambling. There's a $25 daily fee for using the gym, which seems unfair for guests. The place really needs some thorough cleaning.

yelp:train:111659.orig:
Yum!  Everything I had was excellent!  

Burrata and prosciutto : needed more basil and bread, otherwise a superb combination.  

Fettuccine with mushrooms : not overbearing sauce, just perfect

Crab cakes : same as other Puck'n restaurants but with different sauce, tasty old bay aoili.  

Bloody mary and the doorway cocktail (gin and red grapefruit juice base) were fresh and energizing.  

So far, all Wolfgang Puck restaurants surpass most other celebrity chef places.
yelp:train:111659.para:
Yum! Everything I tried was fantastic! 

The burrata and prosciutto were a great match, though they could have added more basil and bread. 

The fettuccine with mushrooms had just the right amount of sauce, making it perfect. 

The crab cakes were similar to those at other Puck'n restaurants but had a tasty Old Bay aioli. 

The Bloody Mary and the doorway cocktail (based on gin and red grapefruit juice) were both fresh and invigorating. 

So far, all Wolfgang Puck restaurants have exceeded my expectations compared to other celebrity chef establishments.

yelp:train:111849.orig: I don't know how this nice, but not too expensive restaurant right on the canal in The Venetian got so overlooked, but the three of us were seated right away on Valentine's Day.  We weren't in the \""patio\"" (along the canal), but were beneath a graceful arch and close enough to see the gondolas drifting by - actually they were maneuvering quite a bit because it's near the embarkation point.  In fact, the only thing separating us was a small group celebrating a wedding - I thought it a very suitable venue for a Vegas reception....more of a choice to forego the big church wedding and Italian honeymoon instead of a we-can't-afford-it substitute.  Well, that's the vibe I got since they had obviously put in a lot of attention to detail with the nicest spot, table set up, cake table, etc.  Well, it lent some romance to our dinner since we weren't a menage a trois, but there with our teenage son.  The menu was very tempting - there were a few things we couldn't decide between.  Looking over at the next table, I recommended that my son order a dish full of shell fish, chicken skewers, and delicious looking bread; it turned out not to be quite enough for him.  The ceviche appetizer was su
yelp:train:111849.para: I'm puzzled as to why this charming, reasonably priced canal-side restaurant in The Venetian was overlooked. Yet, on Valentine's Day, we were promptly seated. We weren't at the patio, but under a beautiful arch, close enough to watch the gondolas navigate nearby. The only other party was a wedding celebration, which I thought was fitting for a Las Vegas reception—more about a personal celebration than a budget constraint. The venue was clearly well-designed, with a romantic ambiance that suited our dinner with our teenage son. The menu was enticing, and we had a hard time choosing. I suggested my son try a seafood dish, chicken skewers, and some bread, but it wasn't quite enough for him. The ceviche appetizer was...

yelp:train:111970.orig: Everything LOOKED fun..Its all broken. Anything worth a damn is out of order. Waste of time.
yelp:train:111970.para: Everything seemed like it would be enjoyable, but it's all fallen apart. Nothing worthwhile is functioning properly. It's a complete waste of time.

yelp:train:112060.orig: A great place to grab a burger with the boyz while watching the game of the week on their plasma TV's hanging all over the place.  If there's just a few of you, get a booth to eat at and get your very own little touchscreen TV!  (NICE TOUCH but not HD) Still cool though and would love to have something like that at home!\n\nRecommendations: ESPN Burger
yelp:train:112060.para:
It's a fantastic spot to enjoy a burger with friends and watch the weekly game on their numerous plasma TVs. If you're with a small group, opt for a booth to have your own personal touchscreen TV! (It's a nice touch, though not HD) It's still really cool, and I'd love to have something similar at home. 

Recommendations: ESPN Burger

yelp:train:112149.orig: Really, I have no problem with the company that is Apple. But they must do something about their follow through with customer service. After a month of leaving messages about a replacement we were supposed to receive, still have not heard back. We ended up pursuing another route to fix the problem and were successful. I hope we don't have to deal with the Apple Store again *knock on wood*.
yelp:train:112149.para: While I have no issue with Apple as a company, I do wish they could improve their customer service follow-up. Despite leaving messages for a month regarding a replacement, we haven't received any response. Eventually, we found an alternative solution that worked for us. Fingers crossed we won't need to contact the Apple Store again; let's hope for the best.

yelp:train:113209.orig: The food is ok, and the atmosphere is ok, and the prices are a little too high for the amount of food.  There is nothing spectacular about this place.  It is a solid, not great, but it is always good.  I never had a great meal, but I never had a bad one.\n\nOne thing really irked me.  The menu said that the Cannelloni is stuffed with chicken, then I was told after I ordered that it is stuffed with beef.  I was very unhappy. Change the menu!
yelp:train:113209.para:
The food is decent, the ambiance is fine, but the prices feel a bit steep for the quantity served. This place isn't particularly impressive; it's just consistently average. I've never had a standout meal here, but I've never had a bad one either.

What really bothered me was a discrepancy on the menu: it stated the Cannelloni was filled with chicken, but when I ordered, I was informed it actually contains beef. I was quite upset about this. Please update the menu to avoid confusion.

yelp:train:114079.orig: Heaven on earth. Great food, drinks, and atmosphere.
yelp:train:114079.para: A paradise on Earth, featuring delicious food, wonderful drinks, and an excellent ambiance.

yelp:train:114686.orig: Mmm ribs are the best I've tried by far! they cook them fresh with their outdoor grill. I suggest you call ahead to make sure what time theyre serving bbq.  we had to get a # at the restaurant side and wait. Bbq food starts at 4p.m. On the tuesday I was there. Simple menu. Just bbq ribs and chicken. I had the combo. Chicken was ok, but the ribs are soooooo good. My boyfriend had a full rack and shockingly killed it! It was that good.definitely better than lucilles. All food comes with corn, bread, bbq beans, and cole slaw. Portions are gigantic! Our bill was about 28 pretty cheap! Service that day was great.
yelp:train:114686.para: Ribs are hands down the best I've had, and they grill them fresh using their outdoor grill. I recommend calling in advance to confirm their BBQ serving time. We had to get a number and wait at the restaurant. The BBQ starts at 4 p.m. on Tuesdays. The menu is straightforward, offering just BBQ ribs and chicken. I got the combo; the chicken was decent, but the ribs were outstanding. My boyfriend devoured a whole rack and couldn't stop raving about how delicious they were. They were definitely superior to those at Lucille's. Every dish comes with corn, bread, BBQ beans, and coleslaw. The portions are enormous! Our total came to around $28, which was very affordable. The service that day was excellent.

yelp:train:114838.orig: WOW. what a best kept secret.  steak,  potato,  green beans,  salad and a sour dough dinner roll. along with a 20 oz. draft beer for $8.99. very tasty and very good\nand service from Karla was the best.
yelp:train:114838.para: WOW, this place is a real gem! They serve a delicious steak, crispy potatoes, steamed green beans, a fresh salad, and a sour dough dinner roll—all for just $8.99, including a 20 oz. draft beer. The food is absolutely delightful. And the service, especially from Karla, was outstanding.

yelp:train:114840.orig:
i can't say that if we had other plans (or with women) that we would've made the effort to come here for the $8.99 steak special. but, it was March Madness weekend with the boys, so, who cares! 

on the back side of Bally's, Ellis Island reminds me of Casino Royale. dungy and old and cheesy, but, Oh So Vegas. this is the type of institution that Oshea's and Bill's used to be, till they turned their noses up and became snooty. small and basic with slots and bj/roulette/craps and also a sportsbook. lively spot, probably cause of MM. 

the hard part was having to sign up for the player's card to get the steak. the line was long, and you still had to wait for a table for 40mins at the cafe. but, and this ain't no lie.... it was worth it. man, i started with the house salad with ranch. it was at Denny's quality. soooo effing good! the steak was a pretty good size and cooked to your liking. easy on the season with A1 on the table. oh, and they also give you a beer with the steak special. the house brewed Heffeweizen was really good. 

overall, a really worthwhile meal for $8.99 and old school vegas vibe. might be a litle too far for us to come back again to. but, who knows. give it
yelp:train:114840.para:
If we had other plans or were with women, we probably wouldn't have made the effort to come here for the $8.99 steak special, especially on March Madness weekend with the guys. But, who cares! 

Located behind Bally's, Ellis Island gives off a Casino Royale vibe—dungy, old, and cheesy, yet quintessentially Vegas. This place reminds me of when Oshea's and Bill's were more down-to-earth, before they became snooty. It's a small, basic spot with slots, blackjack/roulette/craps, and a sportsbook. It's lively, likely due to March Madness.

The hardest part was signing up for the player's card to get the steak, and there was a long line. We had to wait 40 minutes for a table at the cafe. But, it was totally worth it. I started with a house salad with ranch dressing, which was surprisingly good, like something from Denny's. The steak was a decent size and cooked just right. They served A1 on the table, and they even gave us a beer with the special. The house-brewed Heffeweizen was really good.

Overall, it was a great meal for $8.99 with an old-school Vegas atmosphere. It might be a bit too far for us to return, but who knows? Give it a try.

yelp:train:116035.orig: Spazzing bartender started a shouting match with some friends of mine. If you like the smell of sewage over cigarette smoke, then this place is for you.
yelp:train:116035.para: A chaotic bartender sparked a heated argument with my friends. If you enjoy the aroma of sewage mixed with cigarette smoke, this establishment might be just what you're looking for.

yelp:train:116859.para: I arrived 12 minutes late for my daughter's appointment, even though I had pulled her out of school and was running a few minutes behind. yelp:train:117809.orig:
Vegas has a gazillion restaurants to choose from, so the list of places that I want to visit is quite extensive. I definitely knew that wanted to go to a place that would have more locals than tourists. After running through my list and seeing the great Yelp reviews, I finally decided on India Palace.

Wow, I was not disappointed! Started the meal off with the Vegetable Pakora and the Onion Bhaji. The Onion Bhaji, which are onions dipped in spicy batter and then deep fried, was amazing!!! It had the perfect amount of spiciness to start with, and when I felt like upping the spice meter, I just added a little of that really hot dipping sauce. I don't know the name of that sauce, but you know, the one that burns your mouth off.

I went for my usual Chicken Vindaloo for my main course. Chicken Vindaloo is chicken cooked in a hot spicy sauce with diced potatoes, and of course, you can request the level of spiciness. I went for ""hot""! To die for... it was sooo good!!! It was so spicy that I started sweating while eating it....yeah, that's some good shit! I gobbled this down with some garlic naan and cheese naan, and was quite full. I didn't even have room for dessert, which is us
yelp:train:117809.para:
Vegas boasts an enormous array of dining options, making my list of desired restaurants quite long. I aimed to find a place frequented by locals rather than tourists. After reviewing my list and checking Yelp, I settled on India Palace.

Wow, I was thoroughly impressed! I began with the Vegetable Pakora and Onion Bhaji. The Onion Bhaji, deep-fried onions coated in a spicy batter, was outstanding! It had just the right level of heat, and I could adjust it further with the extra spicy dipping sauce, which really packs a punch.

For my main course, I opted for my favorite, Chicken Vindaloo. This dish features chicken in a spicy sauce with diced potatoes, and you can choose the level of spiciness. I went with "hot," and it was incredible... absolutely delicious! The heat was so intense that I started sweating while eating it—it was truly amazing. I devoured it with garlic naan and cheese naan, feeling quite satisfied. I was so full that I didn't even have room for dessert, which is us.

yelp:train:118033.orig: I knew I wanted to look at rings before I walked in.  I was not greeted.  As soon as I got someone's attention.  I asked if the gold ring came without stones.  He said no, and turned his attention to other customers.  I had more questions and wanted to find the right gift for my brother.  I was turned off he made no suggestions and did not care to help me.  I waited minutes longer to at least try them on and see them outside of the case.  A lady finally came, she was pleasant and answered my questions.  Ultimately I wasn't interested in making a purchase from the experience I had.
yelp:train:118033.para: Before entering, I had already decided to look at rings. No one greeted me upon arrival. As soon as I caught someone's attention, I inquired if the gold ring was sold without stones. They replied no and then focused on other customers. I had several questions and was looking for the perfect gift for my brother. I was disappointed because they didn't offer any suggestions or assistance. I waited for a few more minutes to try the rings on and see them outside the case, but still, no one helped me. Eventually, a lady approached and was friendly, answering my questions. However, my experience wasn't positive enough to make a purchase.

yelp:train:118605.orig:
Service is awful and management is even worse. this place is not worth the price point. A complete tourist trap. I've lived in Las Vegas for 8 years and have never received such appalling service. That is probably why I have never eaten at Rainforest before. I should have stuck with my intuition. 

On a Friday night around closing time with a small rush from the club next door my friends and I ordered a few drinks and an appetizer. The drinks came slowly as the bartenders were more focused on closing the bar and the appetizer almost never came. We waited 45 minutes for an appetizer and if we hadn't made three unsuccessful attempts to alert management before finally getting their attention a fourth time then we probably would have never received it. 

Management was not only unresponsive but upon contact with management (Erika) they seemed to have lack of concern and offered absolutely no resolution. This is just food and beverage. Making me happy is as simple as showing some sympathy and throwing me a concession for my time and satisfaction for which you have frivolously wasted. 

The lifetime value of this customer was never valuable to the management of this place.
yelp:train:118605.para:
The service was terrible, and the management was even more disappointing. This place doesn't justify the cost. It's clearly a tourist trap. After living in Las Vegas for 8 years, I've never experienced such poor service anywhere. That's why I've never dined at Rainforest before; I should have trusted my instincts.

On a Friday night, just before closing, with a rush from the adjacent club, my friends and I ordered a few drinks and an appetizer. The drinks arrived slowly, as the bartenders were focused on closing the bar. The appetizer took an agonizing 45 minutes to arrive, and we had to make three unsuccessful attempts to get management's attention before finally getting a response on the fourth try.

Management was unresponsive and seemed indifferent when we finally reached out to Erika. They offered no solution. In a business that relies on customer satisfaction, showing some empathy and offering a concession for my time and effort would have been a basic courtesy. Clearly, the management didn't value my patronage.

yelp:train:118816.orig:
My lovely gfs took me here for the big night of my bachelorette party weekend.  I'm such a lucky girl!!! :)

Yum I love Lawry's....it's almost as good as House of Prime Rib in SF.  Minus one star....b/c the salad at House of Prime Rib is better and the creamed spinach costs extra here.  The prime rib tastes just as good as HOPR and the customer service was excellent....so I'm giving it 4 stars.

I would definitely come back here again!  I'm drooling just thinking about it.
yelp:train:118816.para: My girlfriend surprised me with a dinner at Lawry's for my bachelorette party weekend, and I feel incredibly lucky! :)\n\nDelicious food, that's for sure—I really enjoy Lawry's. It's nearly as tasty as House of Prime Rib in San Francisco, though it falls short in a couple areas. I'd give it 4 stars. The salad at House of Prime Rib is superior, and the creamed spinach is an additional charge here. The prime rib is just as delicious as at House of Prime Rib, and the service was fantastic. I definitely want to return, and I'm already craving it.

yelp:train:119337.orig: To synopsize: \n  This is five star- but not 100% perfection (I have yet to find that anywhere).  Food was a 9/10, view was a 10/10, service was a 9/10, location was 10/10, drinks (Fall in Paris or something) was an 11/10, and I had a great time.  Portions were not as small as in fancy restaurants and for the price ($300 for two with two cocktails, two appetizers, and two entrees), the experience cannot be beat in Las Vegas.  Ask for a seat overlooking the fountain, it was seriously breathtaking!
yelp:train:119337.para: In summary: This place is five-star quality, though not flawless—perfection remains elusive. The food scored 9/10, the view was a perfect 10/10, and the service also earned 9/10. The location was outstanding at 10/10. The drink (perhaps the Fall in Paris cocktail) was exceptional, rated 11/10, and I thoroughly enjoyed my stay. The portions were generous, not as petite as in high-end restaurants, and considering the cost ($300 for two, including two cocktails, two appetizers, and two main courses), the experience is unbeatable in Las Vegas. Request a table with a view of the fountain; it was truly stunning!

yelp:train:119479.orig: My family and I visited this place yesterday to celebrate a birthday.  Let me tell you that it was the worst experience I've ever had at a restaurant.  The fish was horrible and the shrimp taste like it came straight from the freezer section of the local grocery store...actually that's giving them too much credit, because I've had frozen food from the market and it taste 110% better. Not only was the food inedible, but the entire restaurant had a strange smell...that should have been our first clue.  A couple of people in our group had the Gumbo and I wouldn't recommend that dish either.  My son had something as simple as a hamburger, and that was just barely edible. Everyone had stomach issues immediately after leaving the restaurant.  We are all from Los Angeles and have had our share of good fried fish all over LA, so we know good food. All I can say is don't do it, unless you like giving your money away. Let me make one thing clear, they are only receiving 1 star, because I don't believe have any other choice to select lower than 1.
yelp:train:119479.para: Yesterday, my family and I went to this place to celebrate a birthday, and it turned out to be one of the worst dining experiences ever. The fish was terrible, and the shrimp tasted as if it had come straight from the freezer section of a local grocery store—actually, it was even worse than that. The food was inedible, and the entire restaurant had an odd smell, which should have been our first warning. Even the Gumbo, which a few of us tried, wasn't any better. My son had a hamburger, which was barely tolerable. Everyone in our group experienced stomach issues right after leaving. We're from Los Angeles and are accustomed to good fried fish, so we know quality when we see it. In short, avoid this place unless you want to waste your money. I'm giving them only one star because I don't think there's a lower option available.

yelp:train:119702.orig: 1 cashier on the day after Thanksgiving- one of the busiest movie days of the year.  Line a mile long as you might expect.  No worries- we go to the \""Express Kiosk\"" inside the lobby.  Except that it isn't really \""Express\"", and there's a long line here as well (and only 1 kiosk).  Then the scanner to read your \""Club Card\"" doesn't work- so the holds people up even longer trying to get their 100 points so some year they an get a free Pepsie. Then buying popcorn the scanner doesn't work again.  Then the attendant ignores a request for \""extra butter\"" and puts on almost no butter.  It really gets a bit comical at some point and I almost start looking for cameras to see if I'm on candid camera.  Save the stress and rent a DVD- or go to a chain that's cares enough about it's customers to hire enough human beings on busy days.
yelp:train:119702.para: On Black Friday, one of the busiest movie days, the line outside the theater stretches for a mile, as anticipated. Fortunately, we opt for the "Express Kiosk" in the lobby. However, it turns out this isn't truly "Express," and there's a long queue here too (with only one kiosk). The scanner for the "Club Card" also malfunctions, causing delays as people wait to earn their 100 points for a free Pepsi. When we try to buy popcorn, the scanner fails again. Moreover, the attendant ignores our request for "extra butter" and only applies a minimal amount. The situation becomes quite amusing at times, and I almost imagine we're being filmed for a Candid Camera show. To avoid the stress, consider renting a DVD instead, or choose a chain that prioritizes its customers by having sufficient staff on busy days.

yelp:train:119840.para:

We knew he had been vomiting, but the Animal Foundation suggested it was due to yogurt and milk, which turned out to be a mistake. 

A few days later, at VCA, he was vomiting 10 to 20 times daily. I brought this to the doctor's attention, who did some initial tests, gave him his shots, said he seemed healthy, and sent me on my way. Despite the Animal Foundation covering the shots, I still had to pay. He vomited again on the way home.

A week later, with no improvement, I took him to a different vet for a second opinion. The doctor noticed something was wrong when she examined his neck.

yelp:train:119915.para:
This review scores 4.5 stars and is from an Entertainment Book Coupon participant (bogo).

Part One: We enjoyed the lunch buffet with friends a few weeks ago, but I first heard about this place from a former colleague at another office a few years back. I was already familiar with it, knowing that the colleague's son often had his birthday parties there due to the available games and coupons, similar to a smaller version of Chuck E. Cheese. The menu offered a wide variety, though it seemed smaller compared to casino buffets. However, quality trumps quantity here. Considering that most local Vegas buffets are mediocre at best—offering mystery foods, lacking flavor, overcooked meat, and poor-quality dishes—I found this place to be quite good. The options included two salads, multiple dressings, five to six types of pizza (cheese, supreme, meat, Hawaiian, pepperoni, BBQ chicken), pasta with sauce, macaroni and cheese, garlic knots, cheese calzones, a sandwich round (served pie-style), soups, cinnamon buns, brownies, and fruit pizza. The fountain drink station offered free refills. It was very satisfying. I tried several items, being cautious due to dietary restrictions. I'm eager to return! After this buffet, I'm even more excited to come back.

yelp:train:121643.orig: Love this place. Best BBQ in Vegas. What's even better is that the food and service are consistently great. Our favorites: ribs, brisket, the king, burnt ends, cream corn, sticky Vegas style chicken wings and the best BBQ nachos you've ever imagined. If you haven't tried Memphis yet, run don't walk.
yelp:train:121643.para: I adore this spot; it's the premier BBQ joint in Vegas. The food and service are always top-notch. Must-try items include the ribs, brisket, the king cut, burnt ends, cream corn, sticky Vegas-style chicken wings, and the absolute best BBQ nachos you can imagine. If you haven't visited Memphis yet, make sure to go—don't hesitate!

yelp:train:121721.orig:
Poor quality, too expensive, dirty.

I give up on this place for their all-you-can-eat salad and pizza buffet which costs way too much (about $10). Consistently poor quality pizza, stained carpet, unmotivated staff. I've eaten here for lunch for almost three years now, and every time I go back I keep asking myself ""Why do I bother coming back to this place?"" Today, tables were unclean, and the salad bar had cottage cheese that tasted spoiled and the pizza was really poor quality. I know how hard it is to run a pizza establishment, and I feel for anyone who tries, really I do, but if you have time to lean, you have time to clean. Somebody needs to learn how to pick up a rag instead of texting on their cell phone.

Hint: take down the tip jar. We all know you expect a tip for nothing. It shows.
yelp:train:121721.para:
I've stopped going to this place for their all-you-can-eat salad and pizza buffet, which is excessively priced at around $10. The pizza quality is consistently poor, the carpet is stained, and the staff seem unmotivated. I've been dining here for nearly three years, and each time, I question why I return. Today, the tables were dirty, the salad bar had cottage cheese that tasted spoiled, and the pizza was of very poor quality. Running a pizza place is tough, and I understand that, but if you have time to text, you should have time to clean. Someone needs to learn to pick up a rag instead of being on their phone. 

By the way, consider removing the tip jar. It's clear that you expect a tip for nothing, and it's not appreciated.

yelp:train:122052.para: To sum up my experience in one word, it was disappointing. yelp:train:122149.orig:

We had a large group, so that might have been the problem, but it took forever to get our drinks. Some of us didn't get them at all. Then refills took forever rather they were alcoholic or non!!

I know its Vegas but if you are going to pay $10 for guacamole at least give me one whole avocados worth of dip!!

The service was also very slow and not what you would expec
yelp:train:122149.para:
During our stay at Mandalay Bay, this restaurant provided the worst experience among all the places we dined at. Our large group faced significant delays; some of us didn't receive our drinks at all, and refills were extremely slow, regardless of whether they were alcoholic or non-alcoholic.

The chips were enjoyable, but the salsa was disappointing. Getting salt for my chips was a challenge; I had to ask three people. The menu offered a wide range of New Mexican and traditional Mexican dishes, including nachos, quesadillas, ceviche, tortas, tacos, and guacamole. The guacamole was the highlight, but there simply wasn't enough for the price. In Vegas, I expect at least a full avocado's worth of dip for $10.

The tacos were very small, more akin to street tacos, so if you prefer larger portions, this might not be the best choice. However, they were very tasty. The nachos were a big hit, with both the crab and steak varieties being plentiful and shareable between two people. The service was also disappointingly slow.

yelp:train:122257.para:
I wish reviews were categorized by meal times. This review is specifically for the unlimited tapas brunch.

The experience began well. We started with quesadillas, which were exactly as I hoped—cheesy and slightly spicy. Then came the biscuits and gravy, which were fantastic. (I should mention I’m from Texas.) However, things took a downturn after that. The huevos ranchero was rather bland and unexciting. The salmon sliders were a letdown; the goat cheese was too strong, and I couldn’t finish them. The next dish, a PBJ with jalapeño, was overhyped by the waiter, who was wrong. It left me feeling disappointed. The other items seemed repetitive, just variations on biscuit, egg, and sauce. They were so uninteresting I can barely recall them. The churros were a major letdown—basically donut holes with Hershey’s syrup and an unpleasant orange sauce. The bacon bloody mary was okay, and we got unlimited mimosas for an extra $10, but it didn’t salvage the meal. Susan Feniger is one of my favorite chefs, and this brunch was a significant disappointment.

yelp:train:122632.para: While this spot is budget-friendly, a slight increase in price would significantly enhance the quality. In truth, this place isn't up to par. yelp:train:123548.para: This English pub is a favorite of mine, as it's one of the few places in town that offers raspberry cider. It's hard not to chuckle at the concept, but it's a fantastic idea. The pub boasts an extensive selection of draft beers on tap. In fact, their menu is more impressive than the one at Spring Mtn.

yelp:train:124763.para: Each time I visit Vegas, I always make sure to drop by Blueberry Hill for a meal. yelp:train:124805.orig:

yelp:train:124805.para:
Dan Dee stands out as the premier choice for dry cleaning. My family has relied on them for decades, and they've always been our go-to. The owners, a loving couple, are exceptionally kind, and you leave with a smile every time you drop off your clothes.

I also bring my husband's Air Force uniform to them, ensuring it's safe and secure. In today's busy world, it's comforting to find a place where you can trust the owners and appreciate the service you receive. Even though it's just dry cleaning, it's a crucial part of our routine.

yelp:train:125215.orig:
I have to give Deseret Industries credit for presenting a thrift store in a bright, clean, department store fashion. Kudos to them for knowing how important merchandising is! The store is exceptionally well organized, well lit, wide isles with an abundance of sales personnel who are dressed up in a tie and vest (!) All this in a thrift store! amazing.

But I am not overly impressed with the pricing here as it is a hit or miss. For some reason thrift stores tend to price Ralph Lauren at top dollar and this place is no exception. True it is an expensive brand, but Marshall's and TJ Maxx sell RL polos for $20, so I'm not gonna pay $20 for a used one. 

They sell better merchandise in a locked glass case and of course the price tags are hidden so you have to call over an employee just to get a price (annoying). Anything that is higher quality (which is often in the eye of the beholder) is priced accordingly. I once asked a clerk if he can open the case and he said he didn't have a key. He then rudely told me to ""find someone else"" to open it then walked away. What a jerk!

Out back is a covered patio with furniture and other larger items. Sometimes it is chock full of stuff,
yelp:train:125215.para:
Deseret Industries deserves praise for transforming a thrift store into a bright, clean, and well-organized shopping experience, reminiscent of a department store. The store is impressively well-lit and spacious, with a plentiful staff dressed in ties and vests. This level of presentation is quite remarkable in a thrift store setting.

However, I'm not particularly impressed with the pricing, which can be inconsistent. Thrift stores often price high-end brands like Ralph Lauren at premium prices, and Deseret Industries is no different. While Ralph Lauren is indeed an expensive brand, Marshall's and TJ Maxx offer similar polo shirts for around $20, so I find it hard to justify paying the same price for a used item.

The store also has some higher-quality items displayed in locked glass cases, but the price tags are hidden, requiring you to ask an employee for a price, which can be frustrating. Additionally, when I asked a clerk to open one of these cases, he didn't have the key and rudely suggested I find someone else, then walked away. This behavior was quite unprofessional. 

Behind the store, there's a covered patio with furniture and larger items, which can be quite crowded at times.

yelp:train:126449.orig: I still consider myself a sushi noob, but with the AYCE at Sushimon I'll be a pro in no time! Half-rolls so you can try new ones, chef specials with awesome names, very tasty fish, and the dessert was yum (tempura ice cream woohoo!). There cooked sides were kinda blah, but that might be because I was mesmerized by the sushi feast. Order as you go so you don't over-order and pay extra for what you don't eat. They're open super late (like 2am I believe) so, if like me, you crave your sushi at midnight this is the place to get your fix.
yelp:train:126449.para: Despite considering myself a sushi beginner, I'm confident I'll become proficient after trying Sushimon's AYCE offer. They offer half-rolls to explore new varieties, chef's specials with intriguing names, and the fish is very delicious. The dessert, tempura ice cream, was particularly enjoyable. While the cooked sides were a bit lackluster, I was so engrossed in the sushi that I didn't notice. It's best to order as you go to avoid excess spending. Plus, they stay open until very late, making it the perfect spot for a midnight sushi craving.

yelp:train:126489.orig: Place is our favorite....the fish is great and the people are cool. Place gets packed in the evenings which is always a good sign.\n\nWe have been going weekly for several years and can't say anything bad.   Hiro and Eddie are the best!!!!
yelp:train:126489.para: This place is our top choice; the fish is fantastic, and the staff are terrific. It tends to get very busy in the evenings, which is a positive indicator. We've been visiting regularly for years and have never had a negative experience. Hiro and Eddie are outstanding!

yelp:train:126559.para:
This review, much like several others I've written, is long overdue. For the past four years, Sushi Mon has been my go-to spot right around the corner whenever I crave sushi. I live just a short distance away. Apart from a single, extremely unpleasant incident a few years ago when a roach was found on our table as our waitress was handing us our bill, everything has been fine. yelp:train:127850.orig: Great baguettes! Really, truly, great baguettes!\n\nSal at the checkout line is awesome too, and I always make sure to stop and say hi!
yelp:train:127850.para: Absolutely fantastic baguettes! In fact, they are truly excellent!\n\nSal at the checkout is fantastic as well; I always take the time to greet him!

yelp:train:127867.orig: Disgusting is an under statement!! Doesn't even deserve a star. What a waste of money.  Be warned the food is nasty, we ordered general tso's and sesame chicken... neither were even close to what they should taste like.. the food was burnt and chewy. The lo mein is awful. Nothing good to say about the incompetent dtaff who told me twice that the forks and soy sauce was in the bag I checked and it wasn't.  I want my $30 back!!
yelp:train:127867.para: Absolutely disgusting—far below any reasonable rating. It's a total waste of money. Beware; the food is terrible. We had General Tso's and sesame chicken, but both were far from the expected taste, burnt and chewy. The lo mein is awful too. The service was also poor; the staff twice assured me the forks and soy sauce were in the bag I checked, but they weren't. I demand a refund of my $30!

yelp:train:128403.orig: Nothing bad to say. Have your group ready to be seated when you get there. Food choices are outstanding. Quality is superior, service quick and friendly. Portions great, hot, fresh. Priced RIGHT!!! Many regulars there each visit & they know all the friendly staff. Won't go anywhere else now for breakfast! Hostess Devyn is the best!\nHated The Griddle :-(
yelp:train:128403.para: No complaints at all. Ensure your group is seated promptly upon arrival. The menu offers exceptional choices, with top-notch quality, fast, and courteous service. The portions are generous, served hot and fresh. Prices are very reasonable! Regulars often return and are greeted warmly by the staff. I won't go elsewhere for breakfast! Hostess Devyn is outstanding. However, I disliked The Griddle :-(

yelp:train:128543.orig:
Terrible service! The waitress was extremely slow even slower after we mentioned we were catching a movie.  We had to practically jump up and down waving our arms to call her over.  It honestly looked as if she would serve other tables and avoid eye contact at our table and pretend we weren't calling her just so she could go to the kitchen. 

As for the food most everything tasted pretty salty especially the double pan-fried noodles...YUCK!  BUT, if you're into ALL that SALT  I guess go.

P.s.  We were harassed by a homeless person from the parking lot all the way to the front door walkway.
yelp:train:128543.para:
Horrible service! The waitress was dreadfully slow, even more so after we told her we were heading to a movie. We had to practically wave our arms and jump up and down to get her attention. It seemed like she would serve other tables and deliberately avoid eye contact with ours, as if trying to ignore us until she could go to the kitchen.

Regarding the food, most dishes were overly salty, particularly the double pan-fried noodles... YUCK! If you enjoy food that's extremely salty, then perhaps this place is for you.

P.S. We were also bothered by a homeless person from the parking lot all the way to the front door walkway.

yelp:train:128963.orig: Sexy!!! Sat outside in front of an outdoor firepit while enjoying a bottle of wine and crabcakes! Very classy! Waitress was sweet as pie and everybody there seemed to be happy and enjoying themselves.\nSuch a romantic place to gaze in your loved one's eye and let the ambience take you away!
yelp:train:128963.para:
Absolutely sexy! I sat outside by the firepit, sipping wine and munching on crabcakes. It was very elegant! The waitress was as sweet as pie, and everyone appeared to be having a great time. 

What a romantic spot to gaze into your loved one's eyes and let the ambiance transport you!

yelp:train:129154.orig: More than party of 4 are force to pay 18% tips! Not that I am too cheap to pay for it, is I felt the food was not fresh, felt sick after we ate, service was terrible, no matter how many times we ask them to take the order. They never stay long enough to actually finish take your order. We have to order more than 8 times to finish our first decision of ordering 2 sashimi combo, 5 different type sushi order, and 4 appetizers. \n\nPlease don't go, it is waste of time, waste of money and it affect your health.  And most important: u will spend a quality time in bathroom typing a review on yelp. It is only 4 hours after we ate there and I already spend an hour in and out of the bathroom.  Alright, is enough of that. Please go if u want to want to experience what I did. Good luck!
yelp:train:129154.para:
More than four people in our party were required to leave a 18% tip, even though I'm not particularly frugal. I found the food to be unfresh, and we felt unwell after eating. The service was poor; no matter how many times we asked to place our order, they never stayed long enough to actually take it. We had to place over eight orders to complete our initial request for two sashimi combos, five different types of sushi, and four appetizers.

I strongly advise against going there. It's a waste of time, money, and can affect your health. Most importantly, you'll spend a significant amount of time in the bathroom writing a review on Yelp. Four hours after our meal, I had already spent an hour in and out of the bathroom. Enough said. If you decide to go, prepare for a similar experience. Good luck!

yelp:train:129346.orig: Wow I am really disappointed. Food was very bland and tasteless. I have three kids and they all ordered from the kids menu. The two \""funny face\"" pancakes were awful. The design on them was pitiful and it was caked with so much whip cream I wasn't sure there was a pancake under it. My daughters Mac and cheese was chewy and gummy. Apparently the drink isn't included with a kids meal so each drink my small children drank was $1.30 a piece! Talk about nickel and diming. I had good memories as a kid but as an adult ihop was a huge let down.
yelp:train:129346.para: I'm truly let down. The food was extremely bland and lacked flavor. My three kids each chose from the kids menu, but the "funny face" pancakes were terrible. The design was poor, and the whipped cream was so thick, I wondered if there was even a pancake underneath. My daughters' mac and cheese was overly chewy. Moreover, the drinks weren't included with the kids' meals, so each one cost $1.30—quite a surprise. My childhood memories were positive, but IHOP fell short for me as an adult.

yelp:train:129500.orig: We stood in 3 lines to pay a bill. We got up to the SELF-SERVICE MACHINE and it doesn't take plastic - only cash or check. WHUUUUTTTTT????!!!!!! What is this, 1970? Hey, Nevada Power.... in case you people have been on Mars for the last 35 years, this is the 21rst century. Have a nice day, Nevada Power..... well, not really.
yelp:train:129500.para: We formed three lines to pay our bill, only to reach the SELF-SERVICE MACHINE that accepts only cash or checks. WHAT THE HECK?!?! Isn't this the 21st century? Nevada Power, if you've been living on Mars for the last 35 years, this is the modern era. GET WITH IT! I want to swipe and go.
