They make you jump through hoops to get your power on, but they won't hesitate to turn it off. Have a nice day, Nevada Power... but not really.

yelp:train:129501.para: The quality of customer service is extremely poor.

yelp:train:129759.orig: Stopped here never reading reviews or anything about the place... It looked nice and classy so I figured it would be awesome. Our waitress, Sharon just wasn't pleasant at all... She slammed our drinks and plates down. Then we asked for more bread and she said \""well I'll have to charge you\"" so that is fine but when she gave us the basket it only had two small pieces in it, which before each basket had about 4, so that was kinda crappy. Then one of us ordered another beer and she poured it and just let it over flow all onto the table and didn't even say a word.  The crab in the stuffed mushroom app and the stuffed shrimp dinner has mostly imitation crab in it, which for the price is just unacceptable. I had just plain fettuccine Alfredo and it was great I ate the whole thing....  The lighting is just so bright and it's around dinner so I don't want to be under a heat lamp during dinner... I'm not sure if I'd go back ....
yelp:train:129759.para: I visited without checking any reviews, drawn in by the place's appearance and ambiance. However, my experience was far from ideal. Our waitress, Sharon, was not very friendly; she roughly placed our drinks and food on the table. When we requested more bread, she insisted on charging us, which was acceptable, but the basket she provided only contained two small pieces, whereas previously, each basket had about four. This was disappointing. Additionally, when one of us ordered another beer, she carelessly poured it, causing it to spill onto the table without any apology. The appetizer of stuffed mushrooms with crab and the stuffed shrimp dish were mostly filled with imitation crab, which seemed inappropriate given the price. My fettuccine Alfredo, however, was delicious, and I enjoyed it thoroughly. The lighting was excessively bright, making it uncomfortable during dinner. Overall, I'm unsure if I'd return.

yelp:train:130074.orig:
This is the most overrated establishment in the Madison area. If I hear one person talk about the food and the PIE, how GREAT the pie is, I will scream. Yup.

My friend and I got there and we are waiting to be seated. We were acknowledged and asked to just step aside because a person with a walker was coming through. No problem. Then another party of two walks in and they are seated immediately. WHAT?!  We had been waiting and did a nice thing and were skipped over.

So we waited more and more. The place was cold and it was raining so the wait was even worse. Finally we are seated. Our server took over ten minutes to get to our table. When she got there, there was no greeting. She just asked us what we wanted. Wow. So much for service.

So then, we order. My order: coffee and a cobb salad. Coffee does not take too long. It took almost another ten minutes to get coffee. I am not kidding. This was probably the WORST service I have ever received. 

I get my coffee and shortly after my salad comes. Here is the thing, I never saw my server again until I was done with my salad. thank goodness the salad was fresh and delicious. If I had needed anything, I would have been SOL. Yeah
yelp:train:130074.para:
This place is the most overhyped in Madison. If someone mentions how great the pie is, I'd lose it. 

My friend and I arrived and had to wait to be seated. We were acknowledged but asked to step aside for someone using a walker. Meanwhile, another couple walked in and was seated right away. What's going on here? We had waited and done a favor, only to be bypassed.

We waited longer, the place was chilly and it was raining, making the wait even more unpleasant. Finally, we were seated. Our server took over ten minutes to reach us, and there was no greeting. She just asked what we wanted. Service? What service?

We placed our order: coffee and a Cobb salad. The coffee took almost another ten minutes. This was the worst service I've ever experienced.

My coffee arrived, and shortly after, my salad. The server didn't return until I finished my salad, which was a relief because it was fresh and delicious. If I needed anything, I'd have been on my own.

yelp:train:130260.orig: Every student at U of I knows that Gumby's is the place to go for Pokey Sticks..I don't even think I can count how many times I ate these late at night! They are basically bread sticks with cheese on them and marinara sauce to dip them in...soooo good!
yelp:train:130260.para: At the University of Illinois, everyone agrees that Gumby's is the go-to spot for Pokey Sticks. I can't even remember how many late-night meals I've enjoyed there! These are essentially bread sticks topped with cheese and served with marinara sauce for dipping...they are simply delicious!

yelp:train:130308.orig: Over priced vodka and gin drinks in martini glasses. I thought for the price you would get a really good martini but they didnt even make it correctly.  A little pretentious but the servers are nice, just too expensive for poorly made cocktails.
yelp:train:130308.para: Expensive vodka and gin cocktails served in martini glasses didn't meet my expectations. I believed the price would warrant a high-quality martini, but it wasn't even prepared properly. The place has a touch of pretension, and the staff is friendly, but the cocktails are too pricey for the subpar quality.

yelp:train:130559.orig: Very long wait for a mediocre pizza. \nNot worth the hype. Definitely had better pizzas elsewhere including Phoenix. Grimaldi's in Scottsdale have way better Margarita pizzas.
yelp:train:130559.para: The wait was excessively long for a pizza that was merely average. It didn't live up to the excitement it generated. I've tried much better pizzas in other places, including Phoenix. The Margherita pizza at Grimaldi's in Scottsdale is significantly superior.

yelp:train:130622.orig: I've been wanting to go there for years. Finally had the opportunity. I was so excited like I was going to Disney. What a let down. I really didn't think that it had any flavor.
yelp:train:130622.para: For years, I've had this desire to visit, and finally, I got the chance. I was thrilled, almost as excited as going to Disney. But it was a major disappointment. I truly didn't expect it to have any taste at all.

yelp:train:130783.orig:
I have only been to Durant's a couple of times for drinks and dessert, but it was just such a cool place that now I have to go back for dinner. 

The beginning: Even though I know it's commonplace, I still felt weird entering through the kitchen.  

The atmosphere: If the cast of Mad Men were on location in Phoenix, they'd totally be at Durant's inhaling scotch. 

The lowdown: Our server was professional and helpful-suggesting wines for us as well as dessert options. We went with the strawberry shortcake and received a gynormous plate heaped with enough delectable amazing-ness to feed six people easily! The moist, spongy shortcake was topped with fresh berries, lots of whipped cream and then sprinkled with chocolate flakes. DEEEElicious!   

The verdict: Two thumbs up! 
To do list: Eat dinner here.
yelp:train:130783.para:
I've visited Durant's a few times for drinks and dessert, and it's such a unique spot that I can't wait to return for dinner.

First impression: Despite knowing it's typical, I still felt a bit odd entering through the kitchen.

Ambiance: If the characters from Mad Men were in Phoenix, they'd definitely be at Durant's sipping scotch.

Server: Our server was both professional and helpful, suggesting wines and dessert options. We chose the strawberry shortcake, which came on a massive plate packed with enough deliciousness to feed a small army! The shortcake was moist and spongy, topped with fresh berries, generous dollops of whipped cream, and a sprinkle of chocolate flakes. It was truly DEEEElicious!

Conclusion: Two thumbs up!
Next steps: I plan to have dinner there.

yelp:train:131308.orig:
This place has been here for a long time now. It has a lot of reviews, it does not need another. But, I will just put my 2 cents in.
It is a lovely place right on Central. My daughter lives within walking distance to it.
So she is the one that had me go there first.
Breakfast ,lunch, and dinner ,coffee and even the drink!
I have to say my favorite is the Breakfast.
Nice little place to go, I do not like it when it is packed and too many people here.
 
But, on off times it is better. Parking is limited.
Very worth a try. I really love downtown Phoenix, even though it is much different than most major cities. They are growing and developing ever so slowly.
yelp:train:131308.para:
This establishment has been around for quite some time and has garnered numerous reviews, yet it doesn't need more praise. Still, I'll share my thoughts.

It's a charming spot conveniently located in the heart of Central. My daughter, who lives nearby, was the one who introduced me to it.

We've enjoyed breakfast, lunch, dinner, coffee, and even drinks there.

To be honest, I particularly love the breakfast.

It's a nice place to visit, but I prefer it when it's not too crowded.

Parking can be a bit of a challenge, but it's definitely worth a try.

I genuinely adore downtown Phoenix, despite its differences from other major cities. The area is gradually growing and developing.

yelp:train:131350.orig: Went to Lux on a Saturday morning for the first time. It was packed and the line was from the counter to the door. Lucky for me, I was in line in front of John a frequent customer who told me that during the week there is not usually a line and he is usually in and out. I ordered the Egg sandwich and a caramel latte both were very good and the prices were not bad. I was very happy that they offer both almond and soy milk as an option. I look forward to returning during the week  or on a weekend night and having a more relaxed experience.
yelp:train:131350.para: On my first visit to Lux on a Saturday morning, the place was bustling, with a line stretching from the counter to the entrance. Fortunately, I was ahead in line with John, a regular who informed me that during the week, the place is usually less crowded, and he can come and go quickly. I ordered an egg sandwich and a caramel latte, both of which were excellent, and the prices were reasonable. I was pleased to see that they provide both almond and soy milk options. I'm eager to return either during the week or on a weekend evening to enjoy a more relaxed atmosphere.

yelp:train:131512.orig:
Back in the mid-Nineties, studio-apartment-dwelling, student-loan-burdened me would come here and get great deals on things like Ecco shoes, Kenneth Cole shirts, fashionable jeans, and other things I never could have afforded new from Nordstrom's. Sometimes the condition was questionable, but the price always reflected that. I wore out several pairs of high-line shoes purchased here for $11-$12. 

Those days are long gone. Now, can't find a pair of shoes here for less than $30. The clothes are picked over. And mainly, going there is an opportunity for me to  bump into the future ex-Mrs. Bill B., or perhaps the exit strategy from the current prospective Mrs. Bill B. 

Because If you're looking for young or not-quite-so-young-anymore shoppers in 5-inch heels, miniskirts and too much make-up, this is a great place to find them.

Just don't offer to buy them shoes. Anymore. These days.
yelp:train:131512.para:
In the mid-1990s, as a studio apartment resident and student loan debtor, I would frequent this store and find fantastic deals on items like Ecco shoes, Kenneth Cole shirts, and trendy jeans—things I couldn't have bought new from Nordstrom. The quality was sometimes questionable, but the prices were always right. I wore out several pairs of high-end shoes I bought for as little as $11-$12.

Those days are a thing of the past. Now, I struggle to find a pair of shoes here for less than $30. The clothing selection is sparse, and mostly, visiting there is an opportunity to run into the future ex-wife of Bill B., or perhaps the current prospective Mrs. Bill B.

If you're searching for young or not-so-young shoppers in 5-inch heels, miniskirts, and heavy makeup, this store is a great place to find them.

But don't offer to buy them shoes anymore. These days.

yelp:train:131698.orig: I have been a regular at Via for over 20 years. The food was always great but the service often lagged. They fixed that over the recent years but the food quality is now sagging and the portions are shrinking. Went there the other night...ordered chicken tacos. When they came we found they were rancid...stunk so bad we almost got ill right there. The server they told us they make them in the morning...yuck. That does it for us...moving on.
yelp:train:131698.para: For more than two decades, I've been a frequent customer at Via. While the food has consistently been excellent, the service has been lacking. That has improved recently, but now the food quality is declining and the portions are getting smaller. Last night, I ordered chicken tacos. Upon arrival, they smelled so bad that it was almost unbearable; we almost became ill. The server mentioned they prepare them in the morning, but it was still inedible. This is the final straw for us; we'll be seeking other dining options.

yelp:train:131918.orig:
All I have to say is......W.....T......F?

Scene: 6 people in their early to mid 20's walks into Barcelona. Half of them from New York, the other half from San Francisco (or San Fran as the folks in Scottsdale likes to say). Their mouths have dropped and they sit in udder amazement. A band from 1994 gets up on stage and tries to get the crowd of 40 year olds going.  With every song played, the folks from separate coasts, just stand there in complete shock....and then THEY DRANK because THEY HAD TO!

This place is oh so bad! OH SO BAD!!! Go if you need a good laugh.
yelp:train:131918.para:
Here's the paraphrased text:

The reaction was nothing short of astonishment as six young adults, aged early to mid-20s, entered Barcelona. Three were from New York, and the remaining three hailed from San Francisco (or as some from Scottsdale jokingly refer to it as, "San Fran"). Their jaws dropped as they took in the scene. A band from 1994 took the stage, attempting to energize a crowd of 40-somethings. With each song, the visitors from different coasts remained in utter disbelief, and eventually, they had to drink to cope with the surreal experience.

This place is truly ridiculous! TRULY RIDICULOUS!!! If you're looking for a good laugh, give it a visit.

yelp:train:132194.orig: I attended a happy hour at Bamboo Club and was not very impressed. The happy hour prices were nice and they had both veggie and meat-dishes on the list. The food was plated nicely and was relatively tasty. HOWEVER, the service was not great. There were probably 40 customers in the restaurant when we were there. I would say that about 35 of them were crammed into the tiny bar area set aside for happy hour. We had a group of four people and asked if we could use one of the many, many vacant tables on the \""restaurant\"" side, but were declined. Then we tried to move a chair over to a table so that all of us could sit together. Again, a server came over and told us that we could not move chairs. Eventually someone got up from a 4-seater table and we could sit down. I understand that the restaurant wants to provide some incentive for people to eat dinner there, but seriously? The entire restaurant was almost vacant except for people crammed into the bar area. The servers w
yelp:train:132194.para: At the Bamboo Club's happy hour, I wasn't particularly impressed. While the happy hour prices were reasonable and the menu offered both vegetarian and meat options, the food presentation and taste were decent. However, the service left much to be desired. The Bamboo Club seems to offer happy hour specials to attract customers, but then struggles to accommodate those who just want to enjoy drinks and light bites. When we visited, there were around 40 people in the restaurant, with about 35 squeezed into the small bar area designated for happy hour. Our group of four requested to use one of the many empty tables on the "restaurant" side but were denied. We then tried to move a chair to sit together, only to be told by a server that we couldn't do that either. Eventually, we found a spot at a 4-seater table. It's clear the restaurant aims to entice diners with happy hour deals, but the lack of available seating and staff made the experience frustrating. The entire restaurant was nearly empty except for the crowded bar area, and the servers were overwhelmed.

yelp:train:132230.orig: Horrible service. Our waiter forgot one of our dishes and was rude. The food was mediocre. Do not come here!! Worse experience ever.
yelp:train:132230.para: Terrible service was provided; our waiter neglected to bring one of our dishes and was impolite. The food quality was subpar. Avoid this place at all costs! It was the worst experience I've ever had.

yelp:train:132477.orig:
Don't make early reservation on those online deals from credit cards, rewards, etc
By the time u get to the hotel u will not be in their priority list. The best room could probably give u is a 2 beds facing a parking lot or back area of the hotel ughhh.. Trust me its not pretty specially if u wanted it to be a nice romantic room! We got ripped off paid 20 bucks more cause we reserved it early and got a crappy room.. 

The bathroom was too small.. Everything was so standard! Don't expect it to look like the one's in the pictures. Lol

Pool is so low 3ft only and drinks were alright..

Their buffet and attraction were the only good thing about this place..but pricey...
yelp:train:132477.para:
Avoid booking early for online deals through credit cards or rewards programs. By the time you arrive, you might not be a priority, and the best room you could get is likely to be a two-bed room facing a parking lot or the back of the hotel—definitely not what you want for a romantic stay. We paid $20 extra for a subpar room because we booked early, and it wasn't pretty at all.

The bathroom was tiny, and everything was quite standard. Don’t expect the rooms to look like the ones in the pictures. The pool was only 3 feet deep, and the drinks were just okay.

The buffet and attractions were the only positive aspects, but they came at a high cost.

yelp:train:132726.orig: i don't get why everyone seems to love this place. service is pretty slow and the food is just ok. the emphasis seems to be on volume over quality.
yelp:train:132726.para: I can't understand why everyone thinks this place is great. The service is rather slow, and the food is just mediocre. It appears they prioritize quantity over quality.

yelp:train:132776.orig: Amazing fresh, authentic food... wish I'd thought to ask for more guidance before ordering... It would be great to go with a big group in order to be able to sample more...
yelp:train:132776.para: Delicious, genuine cuisine here... I regret not seeking more advice when placing my order... It would have been ideal to have a larger party so we could try a wider variety.

yelp:train:132822.orig:
The only thing that Lotus of Siam did wrong was being in the wrong place at the wrong time. What do I mean? Well, it had the misfortune of 1) being the dinner we ate AFTER having gone to Jose Andres' e' and 2) being visited a few months AFTER the wife and I had eaten in Portland's Pok Pok.

If it weren't for those two things, this would've been a five star review all the way. But alas, it wasn't the best meal I'd eaten in 24 hours (though, yes, an unfair comparison) let alone the best Thai I'd had (by which I mean the aforementioned Pok Pok.)

So let me stop the comparisons and just talk about our experience. It's in a strip mall--a sketch strip mall at that. Some (my overly critical parents, for example) might find that a turn off. Others (a-hole Yelpers like me for example) add points given a genuine hole-in-the-wall status. Thankfully, the sketch doesn't extend to the interior.

We had a group of six. We'd made reservations about a month previous so we had few (if any) hiccups (though we did heed the advice of showing up exactly on time.) The wine list was impressive by hole-in-the-wall Thai joint standards. Actually, it wasn't bad from an objective standpoint either. We'd
yelp:train:132822.para:
Lotus of Siam's only flaw was being in the wrong place at the wrong time. Let me explain: 1) We dined there after enjoying a meal at Jose Andres' e', and 2) it was a few months after we had visited Pok Pok in Portland.

If not for these circumstances, this review would have been a perfect five stars. However, it wasn't the best meal of the day (though, admittedly, a tough comparison) or the best Thai food I've ever tasted (which, again, was Pok Pok).

Now, let's focus on our experience. It's located in a strip mall, which some might find unappealing. But for those who appreciate a true hole-in-the-wall, it adds character. Thankfully, the interior is quite pleasant.

We had a party of six and had made reservations a month in advance, ensuring a smooth experience (though we did arrive exactly on time as advised). The wine list was impressive for a small Thai restaurant, and even objectively, it wasn't bad.

yelp:train:132904.orig: We were told to arrive early so we arrived before they opened. The outside of the restaurant is a little seedy but the inside is completely different with very efficient and friendly wait staff.\nThe yellow curry was the best I've ever had outside of Thailand. The tom yum soup was divine. I wish we had this kind of Thai food in the east coast!
yelp:train:132904.para: We got there early as instructed and beat the crowds. While the exterior of the restaurant gave a slightly sketchy impression, the interior was a pleasant surprise, featuring courteous and efficient service. The yellow curry was outstanding—arguably the best I've tasted outside Thailand. The tom yum soup was exquisite. It's a shame we don't have such authentic Thai cuisine on the east coast!

yelp:train:132914.orig:
Best Thai food in Las Vegas?  Hell, you could put it up as best Thai food anywhere.  Some of the best Thai food I've ever had.

Came here for a lunch, since my old roommate works in Las Vegas now.  I must say that it was a bit of a pain in the ass to find this place, given that it's in the part of Vegas that I'd classify as the middle of absolutely nowhere.  But at least there's a lot of parking.  Additionally, the interior is really nothing to go crazy over...it's good for one thing, and that's stuffing a lot of people in it.

Anyways, I'm just glad that Yelp reviews has all those tips for what to eat.  Because my god, this menu is MASSIVE.  I could literally spend like 15 minutes trying to parse down the 25 things I want to eat, but can't because I don't want to be a massive fatass.  So I settle on the soft shell crab pad kee mao because I've never seen it before on any Thai menu (and under my cardinal rule, ALWAYS get something you've never gotten before if you're somewhere new).  Did not disappoint at all.  Good amount of spice and minty flavor, and the soft shell crab was fantastic.  Excellent choice, good work Yelpers!

Little more expensive than I'd prefer, but pretty
yelp:train:132914.para:
The best Thai food in Las Vegas? Absolutely, it rivals the best in the entire world. It's some of the best Thai food I've ever tasted.

I visited for lunch, as my former roommate now works in Las Vegas. Finding the place was a bit challenging, as it's in a rather remote area of the city. However, there's ample parking, which is a plus. The interior is basic, designed more for容纳不了，请尝试简化您的请求以获得更准确的帮助。

yelp:train:133232.orig: Food is not anything special and hibachi is way overpriced. While dining an ant crawled off my sisters plate and when we told them about it they made it seem like we were making it up, however later on in the night more ants appeared on our table and when we told the sever she wiped the table down with a dish rag and went on with no care. For a meal that was over $150 I expected better service and a much cleaner atmosphere. If you're thinking of coming here maybe try Ohjah instead; cleaner atmosphere, tastier food, fresher sushi, and much better customer service.
yelp:train:133232.para: The food isn't particularly special, and the hibachi dining experience is quite pricey. During our meal, an ant wandered onto my sister's plate, and when we brought it to their attention, they seemed dismissive. Later, more ants appeared, and the server merely cleaned the table with a dish rag and continued serving without concern. Given that our meal cost over $150, I expected superior service and a more hygienic environment. If you're considering visiting, you might want to try Ohjah instead; it offers a cleaner setting, better-tasting food, fresher sushi, and far superior customer service.

yelp:train:133307.orig: nice club! looks super cool inside... kinda goth but def. not the crowd! got super wasted with bottle service... was on one of the balconie tables and jenna jameson and her ufc bf was there... this club is crackin. young and live!\n\noh and i like the name!!! really slick. and creative. :)
yelp:train:133307.para:
What a great club! It's incredibly cool inside... with a goth vibe, but definitely not the usual crowd! I got really tipsy with bottle service... sat at one of the balcony tables, and surprisingly, Jenna Jameson and her UFC boyfriend were there... this place is fantastic. It's young and lively!

And I really love the name—it's really stylish and creative. :))

yelp:train:133313.orig:
went here with girlfriends on a saturday night- got to skip the line and hang out in the VIP area downstairs, here are my thoughts-

1. it is PACKED - like, i was getting shoved / pushed over everywhere except in the VIP area.
2. the VIP area is the one non-air conditioned part of the club.  combine this with the fact that it is mostly guys who have tables in there, and yeah... makes you want to be in the mosh pit disaster of a dance floor
3. rude, rude rude - even more so than your typical vegas doorguys and busboys, for what reason i have no idea.
4. the DJ here was the WORST DJ i have ever heard (this was saturday, 8/22/09).  we're talking like, full second pauses (with just silence) between songs, no attempt to mix into the next upcoming song, would switch tracks mid-chorus when people were singing along, was playing some fun upbeat techno and then went into a journey tribute for an hour, old school hiphop no one could dance to... really anything he could have done wrong, he did.  singlehandedly put a damper on the night.

the crowd was poor, the music was terrible, can't speak for the weekday crowd but if it's a weekend, go to tryst or xs or rain or anywhere else.  my g
yelp:train:133313.para:
Visited the club with friends on a Saturday night and managed to bypass the line and enjoy the VIP area downstairs. Here are my observations:

1. The club was extremely crowded; I was bumped into everywhere except in the VIP area.
2. The VIP area is the only part without air conditioning, and since it's mostly occupied by guys, it feels like being in a mosh pit.
3. The staff was extremely rude, even more so than typical club employees, and I can't fathom the reason.
4. The DJ was the worst I've ever encountered. There were long silent gaps between songs, no effort to blend tracks, and he even switched mid-song when people were singing. He played some fun techno but then switched to an hour of old-school hip-hop that no one could dance to. He ruined the entire night.

The crowd and music were subpar. If it's a weekend, I recommend checking out Tryst, XS, or Rain instead.

yelp:train:133657.orig: Food poisoning alert. My husband and I dined at Emerils on 03/8/13. 3 hours after dining there he was violently ill with food poisoning. My guess was either the salmon or the banana crime pie. This had all the ear marks of staph poisoning . My shrimp was over cooked and cold,his salmon was undercooked and blah. The wine was ordered incorrectly and the staff became surly and indifferent when it was brought to their attention. It was restaurant week in Vegas and the menu was there but concealed behind other menu pages. Stay away from this restaurant it is hazardous to your health.
yelp:train:133657.para: Warning: Food poisoning experienced after dining at Emeril's on 3/8/13. Three hours post-meal, my husband fell ill. I suspect either the salmon or the banana cream pie caused it, as the symptoms pointed to staph poisoning. My shrimp was overcooked and cold, while his salmon was undercooked and unappetizing. The wine order was incorrect, and the staff grew surly and unhelpful when we pointed it out. During restaurant week in Las Vegas, the menu was present but hidden behind other pages. Avoid this establishment; it poses a health risk.

yelp:train:133851.orig:
I love this place!  Yes, it's pricey, but if you want to complain, go to Mickey Ds, ok?  What I will tell you is that you don't need to upgrade to the Kobe beef, go with the Angus beef and you'll get a great burger.  

They have composed burger offerings and they have the any way you want it option, which is the way I roll at The Burger Bar.  Great fries, the pass the Mickey D's test.  Don't be shy about calling an audible and going to the onion rings, they are tasty!  The selection of beers is fantastic.  The staff is awesome, they will take good care of you while you're there.

Just go there and I promise you'll have a great burger.
yelp:train:133851.para: I adore this spot! Sure, it's a bit on the expensive side, but if you're looking to grumble, head over to McDonald's instead. My advice is to skip the Kobe beef and opt for the Angus; it's just as delicious and more wallet-friendly. They offer a variety of burger options, and you can customize them to your liking, which is exactly what I do at The Burger Bar. The fries are fantastic—they pass the McDonald's test with flying colors. Don't hesitate to try the onion rings; they're quite tasty! The beer selection is outstanding. The staff is top-notch and will ensure you have a wonderful experience. Just give it a shot, and I guarantee you'll enjoy a fantastic burger.

yelp:train:133959.orig:
American Kobe Burger - Ordered med-well, got it at med.  Pretty good sized burger, but not amazing taste.  Was decent.  Tomato was tiny.

Sweet potato fries were just ok.  I've had way better.  They were a little cold and seemed like they were about 1-2 hours old

Good selection of beers if you aren't spoiled by the Northwest like I am
yelp:train:133959.para:
American Kobe Burger - I asked for it medium-well, and it came out medium. The burger was reasonably sized, though the flavor wasn't outstanding. It was alright. The tomato slice was quite small.

The sweet potato fries were just mediocre; I've enjoyed much better ones. They seemed a bit cold and probably hadn't been freshly prepared, maybe around 1-2 hours old.

They had a decent variety of beers, though if you're used to the Northwest's beer scene, you might find it lacking.

yelp:train:134087.orig: The food here is always pretty good. It's also pretty decent for a vegetarian as well. The best part about this place is the beer. I always find some of the more hard to find Dogfish Head brews at this place. I always stop by this place when I'm in Vegas. The hard part is deciding between Hussong's or Burger Bar for food, which are both very amazing restaurants that are located right next to each other.
yelp:train:134087.para: The cuisine here is consistently tasty, and it's quite satisfactory for vegetarians too. What I particularly enjoy is the selection of beer; I often discover rare Dogfish Head brews here. This is one of the places I visit whenever I'm in Vegas. Deciding which to choose between Hussong's and Burger Bar can be tricky, as both are outstanding restaurants situated right beside each other.

yelp:train:134109.orig: great sliders! great restrooms! great servers! Not so great casino-hotel, the hotel or mandalay bay are horrible.
yelp:train:134109.para: fantastic sliders! excellent restrooms! wonderful servers! The casino-hotel isn't great, and the hotel at Mandalay Bay is really disappointing.

yelp:train:134336.orig: Wasn't sure what to expect but it was not cheesy, which I really appreciated. They are funny, a little political, and they do neat illusions.\n\nBefore the show, there's a guy on piano and one on bass. The bass player is an unassuming Penn. There's audience interaction throughout the show. Afterwards, Penn and Teller meet and greet people as they exit until every last person gets a chance for a photo or autograph, which I think is really, really nice.
yelp:train:134336.para:
I wasn't sure what to expect, but I was pleasantly surprised; it wasn't cheesy at all, which I really appreciated. They are quite funny and a bit political, and they perform some neat illusions.

Before the show, there's a pianist and a bassist. The bassist is Penn, who is quite unassuming. There's audience interaction throughout the performance. Afterward, Penn and Teller stay to meet and greet people as they leave, ensuring that everyone gets a chance for a photo or autograph, which I think is really nice.

yelp:train:134370.orig: I had a great time at the show. Not to surprising some of their tricks will blow you away. Definitely recommend the show and if you have the patience you can get your picture with penn and teller after the show. Tickets are a little pricey but they're less then some of the other shows on the strip.
yelp:train:134370.para: The show was fantastic, and it's no surprise that some of their performances are truly impressive. I highly recommend it. If you're patient, you can even get a photo with Penn and Teller afterward. The tickets are a bit expensive, but they're more affordable compared to some other shows on the strip.

yelp:train:134869.orig: Ate here once and was very very pleased with my meal, and would recommend this place to anyone. Food is priced as you would expect to eat here. Located inside a casino. They loose a star because the tables were placed a bit to close to each other and should of been more spread apart. Trying to enjoy my conversation yet being able to listen to everyone else's is not that great.
yelp:train:134869.para: I had a great dining experience at this place and highly recommend it to others. The prices are reasonable for the quality of food. It's situated within a casino. However, they lost a star due to the tables being too close together, which could have been better spaced. It's challenging to have a private conversation without being disturbed by the noise from nearby tables.

yelp:train:135223.orig: I see a lot of people have reviewed this place. Well here is my 2 cents. There food is sloop it's the kind of thing I would expect to be served to college kids on  a budget. \n\nI had a hot sausage sandwhich the bread was hard enough to cut a person's gums the sauce  tasted like ragu straight out of a jar and the hot sausage was under cooked!!! who does that? Yep this is a place to be avoided.
yelp:train:135223.para:
Many have shared their thoughts on this establishment, so here’s my take. The food is quite basic; it’s the type you’d expect from budget-conscious college students. 

I ordered a hot sausage sandwich, and the bread was so hard it could potentially damage your gums. The sauce tasted like store-bought pasta sauce, and the sausage was undercooked—how is that acceptable? This is definitely a place to steer clear of.

yelp:train:135819.orig: I almost feel sad to write a bad review but this place used to be my favorite Chinese restaurant of all time up until recently. Recently the inside of the restaurant smells bad and the last time I went a roach fell from the ceiling onto my fianc\u00e9's plate!!! It was traumatizing and we have not been back since that day (last fall). I used to love this place but it is just not what it used to be. If anyone from the restaurant is reading this, please work on the sanitation so life long customers will return for the food we love so much.
yelp:train:135819.para: I almost feel reluctant to leave a negative review, as this used to be my absolute favorite Chinese restaurant. However, things have changed recently. The place now has a bad smell inside, and during our last visit, a roach fell from the ceiling onto my fiancée's plate! It was a traumatic experience, and we haven't returned since that fall. I used to adore this restaurant, but it's just not the same anymore. I hope the management takes action on sanitation issues so that we and other long-time customers can return to enjoy the food we love.

yelp:train:136263.orig:
Before going, I read all of the reviews here on Yelp and elsewhere.  The ratings seemed inconsistent, and it was hard to gauge how eating here would really be.  So, I went last night (4/24/10) with my girlfriend, a colleague from work, and two other friends.

We arrived on time for our reservation, and we were seated promptly.  Menus were already placed at our table, along with the wine/drink list.  Water glasses were full.

We waited for about 15-20 minutes before anyone came over to us.  The first person to do so was a voiceless girl with a pitcher of water.  She filled our glasses and moved on.  A couple of minutes later, a server walked over and asked if anyone had been with us.  We told her no, and she noted that and went to get someone.  Moments later, we had a waiter at our table ready to take our order.

We ordered a bottle of wine (a Chilean Carrignan), and he was off to get it.  The wine was served shortly after, and the only complaint here is that the waiter was terrible at wine service.  He struggled with getting the bottle open, and then he poured wine on the tablecloth and the menu.  It wasn't too much though, and maybe he was new.  In any case, after pouring th
yelp:train:136263.para:
Before my visit, I thoroughly read the reviews on Yelp and elsewhere, finding the ratings confusing and unsure about the actual dining experience. So, I went with my girlfriend, a colleague, and two friends on April 24, 2010.

We arrived on time for our reservation and were promptly seated. The menus and wine list were already at our table, and our water glasses were full.

We waited around 15 to 20 minutes before anyone approached us. A silent girl with a pitcher of water came first, refilling our glasses and then leaving. A few minutes later, a server asked if anyone had joined us. We said no, and she went to get someone else. Soon, a waiter arrived to take our order.

We ordered a bottle of Chilean Carrignan, and he went to fetch it. The wine was served shortly after, but the waiter struggled with the wine service. He had trouble opening the bottle and accidentally spilled some wine on the tablecloth and menu. It wasn't much, and perhaps he was new. Nonetheless, after pouring the wine,

yelp:train:136760.orig: Service out weighs food. Food is decent, but I'd rather give my business to a place with better service.
yelp:train:136760.para: Service is more important than the food. While the food is acceptable, I prefer to support a establishment that offers superior service.

yelp:train:136776.orig:
Here I go again, singing the praises of Chicago food.

As someone who was spoiled by having every type of food at her fingertips for eight glorious years, I really missed good Thai when I moved to Madison. I had a beef Pad Si Ew hankering from hell one day, so we ordered Sa-Bai Thong. 

Thai food should be cheap (under $10) and delicious. This was mediocre and more pricy. The sauce was thick, bland and jelly like, and there was barely any beef. 

I have given this place another shot, ordering Pad Thai the second time, and it was no better. What kind of a Thai place can't make decent Pad Thai?!
yelp:train:136776.para:
Here I am once more, praising the culinary delights of Chicago.

After living in Madison and missing authentic Thai cuisine for eight years, I was eager to try Sa-Bai Thong, which had a beef Pad Si Ew I craved. 

Thai food ought to be affordable (under $10) and tasty. However, this place was overpriced and merely average. The sauce was thick, lacking flavor, and almost gelatinous, with very little beef. 

I gave them another chance by ordering Pad Thai, but the result was the same. How can a Thai restaurant fail to produce decent Pad Thai?

yelp:train:136919.orig:
Wub wub wuuuub AZ88 b/c:
1.  Never been rushed, EVER in the years I've been going here.  
2.  And we spend alot of time enjoying the Burger Au Poivre (peppery and wine-y) + Picnic Chicken + St Petersburg app
3.  Out of towners staying in OldTown, this is walking distance for them for a meetup.
4.  Drinks are Scottsdale prices, but the food for sure is not... a great deal for this chill atmosphere!


Is the over diligent Give-Money-for-Pet-Charity man still lurking in the parking garage??  I've stopped parking there a few years ago for the Buckboard parking lot -- dude, I love helping out but that little old man was worse than a used car salesman...
yelp:train:136919.para:
Wub wub wub AZ88, definitely worth a visit:

1. I've never experienced any rush during my visits over the years.
2. We enjoy the Burger Au Poivre (peppery and wine-flavored), the Picnic Chicken, and the St Petersburg appetizer.
3. For out-of-towners staying in Old Town, this place is conveniently close for meetups.
4. While drinks are priced like in Scottsdale, the food is definitely more expensive, making it a good spot for a relaxed atmosphere.

Is that persistent charity-pet-asking man still around in the parking garage? I stopped parking there a few years ago to use the Buckboard lot—while I appreciate the help, that man was more pushy than a used car salesman.

yelp:train:136954.orig:
Went here for dinner with girlfriends on Tues. Wasn't blown away.

It was difficult for me to find as there is no signage. I finally had to ask someone after wandering around for 15 mins. 

The service was lackluster. Our server gave us the impression we were inconveniencing her more than anything. Not warm or friendly at all.

The menu was mostly sandwiches and salads all of which I wasn't particularly in the mood for. I was expecting more choices. I ended up ordering the Burger Au Poivre II...for $14.50, I was expecting WAY better quality.

I will give them credit for their very extensive cocktail list and the bar is well stocked with every type of quality liquor you can imagine. I had the celebration champagne which was tasty.

Beautiful atmosphere. I'd probably return for drinks at the bar but not the food or service.
yelp:train:136954.para:
Visited for dinner with friends on Tuesday and wasn't particularly impressed.

I struggled to locate the place due to the lack of signs and had to ask someone after wandering for about 15 minutes.

The service was unsatisfactory; our server seemed more bothered by our presence than anything else. She wasn't warm or friendly.

The menu was predominantly sandwiches and salads, which didn't appeal to me. I was hoping for more variety. I opted for the Burger Au Poivre II, priced at $14.50, but found the quality lacking.

They do have an impressive cocktail list and well-stocked bar with a wide range of high-quality liquors. I enjoyed the celebration champagne, which was quite good.

The ambiance was lovely, but I would only return for drinks at the bar, not for the food or service.

yelp:train:137355.orig: It's over rated. Thought my daughter would get a kick out of the place but she was over it as fast as we got there.
yelp:train:137355.para: It's not as highly regarded as it seems. I expected my daughter to enjoy it, but she lost interest almost immediately upon arrival.

yelp:train:137423.orig: Got a free room for two nights here after gambling for probably only an hour! This place is great, but I still prefer the Gold Coast for gambling. Very friendly patrons and dealers here, with a wide selection of things to do here.
yelp:train:137423.para: Scored a complimentary room for two nights after just an hour of gambling! The place is fantastic, though I still have a soft spot for the Gold Coast for gambling. The patrons and dealers are very welcoming, and there's a diverse range of activities available.

yelp:train:137516.orig:
The rooms are nice for off strip hotel and not very expensive.
The service though is consistent with the price.I guess that's why they are understaffed.
There are no signs when you drive up for check-in and was very confusing. The rude valet admonished us for being so dumb and had us drive around again.
If you want a taxi you are on your own as well as cocktail service in the casino bars. I guess alcohol is not a profit center.
yelp:train:137516.para: The rooms are decent for a non-strip hotel and not overly pricey. However, the service aligns with the budget, which might explain the understaffing. Upon arrival, there were no check-in signs, making things confusing. The valet was unhelpful and criticized us for our perceived lack of knowledge, making us circle the property again. Additionally, you'll need to arrange your own taxi and cocktail service in the casino bars, as these aren't provided. It seems alcohol isn't a focus for generating revenue.

yelp:train:138336.orig: This is by far my favorite place on the strip. The energy at the Bellagio is radiant and I always feel happy and relaxed whenever I'm spending time here. The casino is huge and there are a nice variety of games. It's also very clean and well kept. \n  My favorite thing is the interior design with this hotel. There's a indoor botanical garden that is absolutely magnificent and they change it every season. There's also floral blown glass on the lobby ceiling. It's breathtaking. Outside they have a huge water design with fountains and lights. Every night they do a water show where there's music, fountains shooting up and lights to go along with the show. LOVE this place. It's gorgeous. :)
yelp:train:138336.para:
This location is undoubtedly my top choice on the strip. The Bellagio exudes an incredible energy that always leaves me feeling joyful and at ease. The casino is expansive, offering a diverse range of games. It's also impeccably clean and well-maintained.

What I adore most is the hotel's interior design. There's an indoor botanical garden that's stunning, with a different display each season. The lobby ceiling features breathtaking floral blown glass. Outside, there's a grand water feature with fountains and lights, and every evening, there's a spectacular water show set to music. I absolutely adore this place; it's simply gorgeous. :))

yelp:train:138597.orig: Very dirty seriously needs updated. Stains on chairs in room, horrible shower will not stay here again. To top it off a homeless bum urinated in middle of casino and guest services did nothing to remove him or even care. He was allowed to wander around casino. Dont stay there.
yelp:train:138597.para: The place is extremely dirty and needs a major update. There are stains on the chairs, and the shower is in terrible condition. I won't be staying there again. To make matters worse, a homeless person urinated in the middle of the casino, and guest services did nothing to address the situation or remove him. He was allowed to roam freely. I strongly advise against staying there.

yelp:train:139053.orig: This was my third time staying at the LVH. With my company,I travel to numerous trade shows, many of which are held in Las Vegas. This hotel is very dated but always seemed to be the best option for location and proximity to the convention center. Well, this particular trip turned ugly when on the second morning of my stay I woke up, went to the restroom and when I returned to bed, there were bed bugs crawling on the pillow. I had never seen one before but a quick search on my phone confirmed their identity. I called house keeping right away and they sent up a security guard that collected the bugs in little baggies. They sent up a bell hop to carry my things to my new room in the old unrenovated tower (downgrade). The security guard said you need to wash those clothes as soon as possible in hot water. I happened to agree. I had one more night to stay at the LVH and I in NO WAY wanted to transport those nasty creatures back to my home in FL. When I got to my new room and I made a call to find out about laundry services. I was passed around to about 4 different people before someone was able to tell me if my clothes could be laundered. House keeping passed me to the Bell hop, bell h
yelp:train:139053.para: On my third visit to the LVH, I stayed there while traveling with my company to various trade shows in Las Vegas. Despite the hotel's outdated appearance, it was usually the most convenient choice due to its proximity to the convention center. However, this trip took a turn for the worse when, on the second morning, I found bed bugs on my pillow after returning from the restroom. I immediately contacted housekeeping, who dispatched a security guard to collect the bugs. A bellhop then brought my belongings to a room in the older, unrenovated tower (a downgrade). The security guard advised me to wash the clothes in hot water as soon as possible. Given the risk of transporting the bugs back to my home in Florida, I agreed. With only one night left at the LVH, I called to inquire about laundry services but was transferred to several people before finally getting an answer on whether my clothes could be cleaned.

yelp:train:139304.orig: Upgraded to the red room premier and was glad I did.  The room was super cute, very clean and the bathroom was huge.  The view was the best feature - looked right over the Bellagio fountains and the pool.  However...don't go to this hotel if you want a nice pool.  The pool is very boring by Las Vegas standards.  And it closes really early - 6PM.  Other than that, a very nice, reasonably priced hotel on the strip.
yelp:train:139304.para: I upgraded to the red room premier and was pleased with the decision. The room was adorable and exceptionally clean, with a particularly impressive bathroom. The view was outstanding, offering a direct sight of the Bellagio fountains and pool. However, if you're seeking a great pool experience, this hotel might not be ideal. The pool is rather unexciting by Las Vegas standards and closes quite early at 6 PM. Overall, it's a well-priced, enjoyable hotel located on the strip.

yelp:train:139305.orig:
We won't stay here again.  We only booked this place because Caesars, where we normally stay, was hosting an event and so the rooms were 4x the normal rates.  And now that we've seen the new Cosmopolitan hotel, I doubt we'll stay anywhere else!

We booked a king non-smoking, but when we arrived, there were no king N/S rooms available, so they put us in a room with 2 double beds.  They agreed to move us the next day for a room with a king bed and a view (you can get a great view of the Bellagio fountains from Paris) for our troubles, and when we finally re-packed and got moved, we had no view of the fountains, instead we were one floor above the pool.  I don't really care to stare at sunbathers all day, and being only one floor up made for very loud mornings, when people started partying at the pool and music was thumping.

The beds are horrible.  There are no comforters, just a blanket with sheets on either side of it (a fake ""duvet""?), the mattresses are hard and the pillows are bad.  The rooms are also so dated, with old furnishings, old school tvs, etc, and our shower had giant cracks in the floor (the tiles)... I was a little concerned about where that water was going!
yelp:train:139305.para:
We won't be returning to this hotel. We initially chose it because Caesars, our usual accommodation, was hosting an event and the room rates were four times higher. Now, after experiencing the Cosmopolitan, we're unlikely to stay anywhere else.

We reserved a king non-smoking room, but upon arrival, we found no such rooms available, so we were given a room with two double beds instead. They promised to switch us to a king bed with a view the next day, and although we were moved, the promised view of the Bellagio fountains was not what we got; we ended up one floor above the pool, which wasn't ideal.

The beds are subpar. There are no comforters; just a blanket with sheets on either side (a fake "duvet"?), and the mattresses are quite hard. The pillows are also unsatisfactory. The rooms are outdated, with old furniture and televisions, and our shower had significant cracks in the floor tiles, which made us worry about the water drainage.

yelp:train:139320.orig:
(+)
- Cheaper rooms
- Very nice front desk people
- good location

(-)
- food options slightly limited
- not as many mirrors in hotel room

First time staying here my past Vegas trip. I was expecting something like Treasure Island but their room was much better lit and didn't look old at all. We took an early flight in, got to check in early and even got the adjoining rooms we wanted woot! Quick tip, if you want adjoining rooms that actually connect by a door, then your rooms will have to be one King bed and the other with 2 queens. The lady at the front desk who helped us was wonderful and talked us through our options.

We got our rooms for a really great price from hotels dot com, Paris isn't the cheapest option out there for hotels but it has great rates without sacrificing location and too much quality. It is within walking distance of cosmopolitan and a quick cab ride to Wynn.

There aren't that many food options. A couple nicer places and a few ""10 dollars for a sandwich/salad"" places. No food court for those on a budget but you can always walk to nearby Planet Hollywood and get a cheap 6 dollar sandwich at the much hyped over Earl of Sandwich

Oh and the
yelp:train:139320.para:
First time visiting this hotel during my recent trip to Vegas, I was pleasantly surprised by the room quality, which was much better lit and newer than I expected, akin to a Treasure Island room. We managed to check in early and secure the adjoining rooms we desired. A helpful front desk attendant guided us through our options. For a great price from Hotels.com, the Paris hotel offers good value without compromising on location or quality. It's close to Cosmopolitan and a short cab ride to Wynn.

Food options are somewhat limited, with a few upscale choices and budget-friendly places offering sandwiches and salads for around $10. While there's no food court, you can easily walk to Planet Hollywood for a cheap $6 sandwich at Earl of Sandwich, which is quite popular.

yelp:train:139436.orig:
The worst hotel on the strip unless you enjoy poor service, an extremely slow check Ballys gaming company, who operates the hotel.. It took 48 minutes to check in. 

I would stay at an MGM or WYNN property before ever staying here. 

I have a laundry list of issues from starting up the iron to iron my clothes and it not working. 45 minutes later getting a replacement to getting water from the hall way vending machine for $3.00 and it not dispensing water. I called the front desk and they state, sorry, we can't help you. 

Worst hotel on the strip bar none.
yelp:train:139436.para:
This hotel on the strip is the worst unless you enjoy subpar service and extremely slow check-ins, handled by Ballys Gaming Company, which operates it. It took 48 minutes just to check in.

I'd prefer staying at an MGM or Wynn property over this one.

I encountered numerous problems, like the iron not working when I tried to iron my clothes. After 45 minutes, I got a replacement iron, only to find that the water from the hallway vending machine, which cost $3.00, wouldn't dispense water. When I called the front desk, they said they couldn't assist me.

This hotel is undoubtedly the worst on the strip.

yelp:train:139764.orig:
Truly disappointing on several levels.  The quality of the fish was simply not that good. This is not it.

The service was, and I'm not sure if this makes sense, but obsessively and (worse) aggressively obsequious.  This guy would continually hover over us explaining to us how (and exactly) whatever we wanted would be taken care of by him of the sushi chef.  Very intrusive, and I realiz
yelp:train:139764.para:
Regrettably, this experience fell short on multiple fronts. The fish quality was subpar, without even being compared to Sugarfish, which I highly recommend, or to local LA spots like Brothers Sushi in Woodland Hills. For the price of Nobu, I expected sushi of a higher caliber than what’s available in Woodland Hills.

The portions were quite small, to be honest. They did serve a genuine salmon roll, which is commendable, as many places use pre-cooked meat. However, the prices were exorbitant and seem unjustified, especially since they source their fish from the same suppliers as others.

I’ve had sushi in Japan and even paid for it, which made me acutely aware of what constitutes good and great sushi. This place does not meet those standards.

The service was overly attentive and intrusive. The waiter constantly hovered, explaining in great detail how the sushi would be prepared, which was quite intrusive and unsettling.

yelp:train:139846.orig: I really enjoyed staying here. The staff is awesome. They have a wave pool and their own brewery!  You can't go wrong with a place that's making the beer!  The rooms are comfy and the beds are super soft, which suits me just perfectly.  \n\nThe staff here really went out of their way for us and were so very helpful, I do have to remove 1 star though because of one particular blackjack dealer who seemed to be having a bad day and was a little rude - but, even with that I still recommend this hotel/casino to everyone!
yelp:train:139846.para: I had a great time at this place. The staff is fantastic, and they offer a wave pool and their own brewery. It's hard to beat a hotel that brews its own beer! The rooms are very comfortable, and the beds are incredibly soft—just what I needed. The staff went above and beyond to assist us, but unfortunately, one blackjack dealer had a bad day and was a bit rude. Despite that, I still highly recommend this hotel and casino to everyone!

yelp:train:140251.para:
I'm awarding this place two stars solely due to the check-in guy, who was really kind and helpful; I just can't recall his name. 

That said, this hotel is terrible in every way. It's outdated, the beds are uncomfortable, and the rooms appear very dirty due to their age. The air conditioning often fails to reach the stated temperature; for instance, it might claim to be at 60 degrees, but it feels much warmer. The bathroom fixtures are from the 1980s, and the shower head looks like it was bought from a discount store. The casino is disappointing, and the drinks are pricey. We stayed here only because we couldn't find a better option for SEMA, and we instantly regretted our choice. If you want a pleasant stay, avoid this hotel.

For me, I fell in love with Cirque du Soleil for the amazing feats and distinguishing acts that set these people apart from those of us who cannot walk on our pinkies while twisted into a pretzel and I didn't really find that much of an ooh aah factor in this show.
yelp:train:140282.para: The performance was incredibly artistic and visually captivating, featuring acts like lesbian water contortionists and a midget performing with a tall blond on aerial silk. Each act seemed tailored to satisfy various forms of sexual curiosity. Personally, I was drawn to Cirque du Soleil for their extraordinary skills and unique performances that set them apart from the rest. yelp:train:141107.para:
I'm writing this from the 12th floor of the Venetian tower, and my room is stunning, spacious, and spotless. While I would love to settle in and enjoy my vacation indefinitely, I've only been here for a few hours and am quite disappointed with the hotel's customer service. My first indication was when I called a couple of days before our trip to request special accommodations due to a medical condition, and the person on the line was unhelpfully dismissive. My husband then tried the concierge, hoping for better service, but was quoted a $70 daily charge for assistance, which was again met with a non-apologetic and dismissive attitude.

Today, after navigating what I find to be a tacky check-in process, we were informed of a $28 daily resort fee for access to the pool and fitness center. A resort fee! For using the pool and fitness room! I don't need the fitness room, and I've never had to pay to use a hotel's pool before. This vacation, which was a gift from a friend with a stipend for spa services, now comes with an unwelcome resort fee that I have no choice but to pay.

yelp:train:141756.para:

My friend opted for the foie gras with his steak. If you enjoy foie gras, you absolutely must try this combination. While it might seem unconventional to pair a rich foie gras with a hearty rib-eye, when I did, it created an incredible explosion of flavors in my mouth.

yelp:train:141775.para:
This review will present a balanced view of our experiences, as they were mixed. I've visited three Emeril's restaurants in Vegas, and while the other two, Fish House and Table 10, often offer discounts through the half-priced ticket booth, this steakhouse in The Venetian does not. We dined here on December 30th, prior to a Maroon 5 concert, and managed to secure a reservation by phone a few days in advance without much trouble. We enjoyed wine, appetizers, two main courses, two side dishes, and a dessert.

The service and customer service were outstanding. We sampled the lobster bisque, a pasta special appetizer, BBQ shrimp, Cajun Ribeye, Filet Mignon, Gratin potatoes, Mushrooms, and Chocolate cake. Most dishes were delightful, but a few did not meet expectations. The Ribeye was overcooked, not very tender, and lacked seasoning. The Chocolate cake was dry and seemed previously frozen. The pasta appetizer was good but not exceptional, something I wouldn't order again. The Filet Mignon was outstanding, with the demi glaze sauce being the standout. The BBQ shrimp were delicious, as were the little biscuits that accompanied them. The lobster bisque was creamy and satisfying.

yelp:train:142069.para: I've consistently ranked MGM among the best Vegas hotels. Now, it seems they're targeting lower-end customers. Despite offering lower rates, the service and overall experience were subpar. This is a major disappointment.

yelp:train:142149.para:
When we began organizing a large group trip to Vegas for around 60 people flying in from various parts of the country, I initially expected it to be a chaotic and costly affair. Most of our group was booked at the Flamingo with a group rate, but my roommate and I found fantastic deals at the MGM. We secured a double occupancy room for just $69 per night for two of the four nights, which is better than what I can get in my hometown.

The rooms were immaculately clean, and they provided enough furniture to make us feel at home, not just with two beds and a TV. The staff was always available to assist us. For instance, one night we returned to our room at 5 AM after a theme party, with fake eyelashes glued to one of my eyes (we were 80s glam rockers, by the way). We decided to order a pizza, and the delivery person even placed water on our bedside tables. She seemed genuinely interested in our wild stories from the night.

Moreover, we ordered the pizza using their iPhone app while walking down the strip, and they were more than willing to accommodate us, even though we weren't registered guests.

yelp:train:142731.orig:
The Happiest Place On Earth!

Best punk bar in Vegas!

I loves me the Double Down. Reminds me of the old Comet Tavern in Seattle (maybe a mix between ages compared to this), or Zeitgeist in SF (smaller than that, no amazing burgers), only a lot, lot dirtier. As punk rock bars goes, this one has it all. A great jukebox with real punk on it, graffitied walls, dirty bathrooms, regular men and women (you know, with ink and piercings, etc), friendly atmosphere, gambling, cocktails, and sometimes a band or two. I meet the friendliest people here: tourists and locals. 

On this trip I was proud to purchase an ""I Love Double Down Pussy"" t-shirt, which I can now proudly wear in cities where people will have no idea what the fuck it means (I'll try to post a pic when I can). 

There's a great metal sculpture over the bar (centipede) and a metal cockroach sculpture on the wall near the men's room. Pool, video poker and slots at the bar, and a small stage for bands.

I never miss the DD when in Vegas and you shouldn't either.
yelp:train:142731.para:
The Happiest Place On Earth!

The Double Down is the top punk bar in Vegas!

I absolutely adore the Double Down. It brings back memories of the old Comet Tavern in Seattle (though perhaps a bit more mixed in terms of age compared to this place) or Zeitgeist in San Francisco (though smaller and without the amazing burgers). It's definitely one of the best punk bars out there, with everything you could want. It features a fantastic jukebox filled with real punk music, graffiti-covered walls, and dirty restrooms. You'll find regular folks here, often with tattoos and piercings, in a friendly and welcoming atmosphere. There's gambling, cocktails, and sometimes live bands. I've met some of the friendliest people here, both tourists and locals.

During this trip, I was proud to buy an "I Love Double Down Pussy" t-shirt, which I can now proudly wear in places where no one will have a clue what it means (I'll try to post a picture when I can). 

There's a striking metal centipede sculpture above the bar and a metal cockroach sculpture near the men's room. The bar also offers pool, video poker, and slots, along with a small stage for bands.

I never miss the Double Down when I'm in Vegas, and you shouldn't either.

Upon arrival, we attempted to secure our reserved room (two queens, non-smoking), but the front desk informed us that our room was double-booked and the only option available was a smoking one-bedroom.
