yelp:train:143256.para:
Since my initial visit in July 2008, I've been to Las Vegas 11 times, and TI remains a favorite. It was my first hotel in Vegas, which adds to its appeal.

CHECK-IN/FRONT DESK - 4 Stars
The front desk staff is exceptionally friendly, and the check-in process is swift. They use a single, zigzagging queue line that spans the check-in/lobby area, which I find more efficient than the separate lines at other hotels. This setup ensures that no one at the back of the line gets ahead of you.

HOTEL ROOM - 4 Stars
The rooms I've stayed in are clean, modern, and inviting. Standard rooms feature a good-sized LCD (or plasma) TV, a safe, an ironing board, a desk, and a comfortable chair by the window.

CASINO - 3 Stars
While I enjoy gambling at TI, the casino's theme and decor don't particularly draw me in. I prefer to play at The Mirage or Harrah's or Bally's nearby. However, the casino staff is always friendly and helpful, especially when it comes to improving my gambling skills.

yelp:train:143294.orig: I would gladly tell visitors to stay ANYWHERE else in Vegas.  There is nothing good about this hotel except location and the rooms were nice.  The customer service is non-existent.   Rude workers at check in. Waiting for 15 minutes at most food places before even being acknowledged. (there was NO line) Then another 20 minutes before any service.  Pool is small and SUPER crowded.  By 2:00, you cant even move if your in the water.  Not fun, not relaxing.  There are many more reasons NOT stay at this hotel.  The prices arent even great.  Definitely consider staying at one of the MANY other hotels on the strip.  I even emailed a complaint to the the hotel direct and havent heard a thing back.  Again, horrible customer service.
yelp:train:143294.para: I'd recommend visitors stay at any other hotel in Vegas instead. This place has only two positives: its location and room quality. Customer service is lacking. The check-in staff was rude, and we had to wait up to 35 minutes for service at most food places, despite no lines. The pool is tiny and extremely crowded; by 2:00, it's impossible to move around. It's not enjoyable or relaxing. There are numerous reasons to avoid this hotel. The prices aren't even competitive. Definitely opt for one of the many other hotels on the strip. I even emailed a complaint directly to the hotel, but haven't received a response. Again, the customer service was terrible.

yelp:train:143411.orig:
This Hotel is ghetto! 

I'm here on a conference and we booked at the Imperial Palace because all the flamingos were booked or so. First thing first, when you check your bags, the bell hop practically begs you for a tip, he will not stop bothering you about how he ""checked 23 bags"" til you tip him and tip him right! 
The rooms yell cheap motel quality all over! Their TV looks like its straight up out of the 80s yes I am talking about the 1980s. Square and fat, with the words MAGNAVOX. The beds were like bam, uneven parts hard parts soft. and sheets that dont even get you warm. 

But that's all forgivable until the next day, when I went out, they changed the locks on the door, on all the doors in the hotel.without prior notice! I mean it would've been at least courtious of them to tell you they would be doing that  especially if you just checked in the day before! Instead of going all around just to get new keys, talk about lost time!
yelp:train:143411.para:
This hotel is really budget and not up to par! I'm attending a conference and we ended up at the Imperial Palace since all the Flamingos were booked. The first issue is with the bellhop who persistently asks for a tip, practically begging you until you give him one, even going so far as to boast about having handled 23 bags.

The room quality is clearly subpar, reminiscent of a cheap motel. The TV looks like it dates back to the 1980s—square and bulky, with the brand name MAGNAVOX emblazoned on it. The beds are uneven, with some parts feeling hard and others soft, and the sheets are so thin they barely provide warmth.

However, the most egregious issue came the next day when they changed the locks on all the doors without any prior notice. It would have been at least considerate to inform us about this, especially since we had just checked in the day before. Instead, we had to go around getting new keys, which wasted a lot of time.

yelp:train:143790.orig:
Huge disappointment - after reading all the great reviews on Yelp, I decided to have my family's Christmas dinner at Mon Ami Gabi.  Perhaps it was Christmas and the chef wasn't around or there was no delivery of fresh steak on Christmas day or whatever, but the steaks were the worst we've ever had at a restaurant that claimed to be a steakhouse of any sort.        

We had the following: 

- French onion soup - standard, decent, not spectacular
- Frisee & bacon salad - tasty
- Steak au poivre
- Steak roquefort
- Filet mignon with merlot butter  and red wine reduction

I think the problem is with quality of the steaks, the sauces were fine, but my mom's steak roquefort had the texture of cotton, my sister's steak au poivre had the texture of cotton with lots of veins and fat lumps, my filet mignon had a stringy texture like a inferior cut of meat and was not at all firm.  It was so bad that we left much of the entree untouched and left right after the main course, we didn't even have dessert on Christmas!!  This was a very disappointing meal and ruined our Christmas.  

On the other hand, the service was fine and the  prices were definitely cheaper than traditional steak
yelp:train:143790.para:
Extremely letdown - following all the positive Yelp reviews, we chose Mon Ami Gabi for our family's Christmas dinner. Despite the high expectations, the steaks, which the restaurant markets as its specialty, were the poorest we've ever tasted. 

Here’s what we ordered:

- French onion soup - average, nothing exceptional
- Frisee & bacon salad - quite tasty
- Steak au poivre
- Steak roquefort
- Filet mignon with merlot butter and red wine reduction

The issue seemed to stem from the quality of the steaks. While the sauces were acceptable, my mother’s steak roquefort was as soft as cotton, my sister’s steak au poivre was similarly soft with visible fat and veins, and my filet mignon was stringy and inferior in texture. The meal was so subpar that we barely touched our main courses and left immediately after, missing dessert entirely. This ruined our Christmas dinner, which was a significant disappointment. 

On the bright side, the service was satisfactory, and the prices were more affordable than at traditional steakhouse restaurants.

yelp:train:144614.orig:
I had one of the best French dinners here!
It was outstanding and we were really quite surprised at how wonderful the food was.

Escargot was buttery but not too greasy and had a parsley mixture which added to its unique flavor.

The bone in ribeye is a must u have to order it medium rare and it will melt in your mouth with the perfect combination of herbs for the rich beefy flavor.

The goat cheese in tomato sauce appetizer was magnificently seasoned as it burst in your mouth and filled your tastebuds with a tantalizing taste of balanced goat cheese and fresh tomatoes.
I'm returning!
yelp:train:144614.para:
I enjoyed an exceptional French dinner here, and we were genuinely surprised by how delicious the food was.

The escargot was perfectly buttery, not overly greasy, and enhanced with a parsley blend that gave it a unique taste.

The bone-in ribeye, when ordered medium rare, was a must-try; it melted in the mouth with a harmonious blend of herbs that complemented the rich, beefy flavor.

The goat cheese appetizer in tomato sauce was superbly seasoned, bursting with flavor and offering a delightful balance of tangy goat cheese and fresh tomatoes.

I plan to return!

yelp:train:144651.orig: The food was very good. I had the skate wig and beet salad and i was very happy with both. The tables were a little to close for comfort.
yelp:train:144651.para: The meal was excellent, and I particularly enjoyed the skate wig and beet salad. I was quite satisfied with both dishes. However, the tables were a bit too close for my comfort.

yelp:train:144795.orig: Beautiful place. Steak is great! Outside sitting and amazing views of the Bellagio fountains. Service is top notch and the vibe is perfect for a romantic outing.
yelp:train:144795.para: A stunning location indeed! The steak is outstanding. Enjoying dinner al fresco offers breathtaking views of the Bellagio fountains. The service is exceptional, making it the ideal setting for a romantic evening.

yelp:train:144980.orig: Husband and I celebrated his birthday over a long weekend in Vegas.  The restaurant was small but elegant and intimate with just 15 tables or less.  We had initially decided on the 5 course tasting but after speaking with our server, we were immediately sold on ordering from the a la carte.  For the first course, husband had pan-seared foie gras which paired perfectly with caramelized apple.  My escargots were juicy, flavorful and the sauce was great for dipping.  We both ordered the lobster thermidor for entree - 2 lbs of lobster cooked in a brandy cream sauce with asparagus and mushrooms.  The service was impeccable, food was well-prepared and I highly recommend it.
yelp:train:144980.para: My husband and I marked his birthday with a long weekend in Vegas, dining at a charming, intimate restaurant with fewer than 15 tables. Initially, we planned to enjoy a 5-course tasting menu, but our server convinced us to opt for the a la carte instead. For the first course, my husband savored pan-seared foie gras that complemented the caramelized apple. My escargots were succulent and flavorful, with a delightful sauce for dipping. We both relished the lobster thermidor, featuring 2 pounds of lobster in a rich brandy cream sauce, accompanied by asparagus and mushrooms. The service was outstanding, the food was expertly prepared, and I wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant.

yelp:train:145130.orig:
The word dump doesnt cover it.

The place smelled of carpet deodorizer and lysol.  No fridge, broken knob on the thermostat, all night leaking shower.  Really?  $120?

Lower budget shouldn't mean run down - it was like a vagrant hotel.

There is no reason to stay in this place.
yelp:train:145130.para:
The description falls short of capturing the full extent of the issues.

The air was filled with the scent of carpet deodorizer and Lysol. There was no refrigerator, a faulty thermostat knob, and a shower that leaked all night. Really, for $120?

Lowering the budget shouldn't equate to a rundown place—it felt more like a homeless shelter.

There's no justification for staying here.

yelp:train:145538.orig:
My sister swears that she saw a cockroach strolling across her bedspread when we stayed here last.  I never saw it, so I cannot confirm nor deny the sighting.  But regardless, that's still pretty sick.  It happens to the best of hotels, and I am sure it's an isolated incident.

Now that I think about it, we should have complained. Oh well.  I like the central location of this places and its OG status as one of the oldest casinos on the Strip.  Go Flamingo!

The Flamingo habitat and the crab leg buffet are highlights.  Haven't stayed here in a while, but wouldn't mind it if I got a good deal.
yelp:train:145538.para:
My sister claims she spotted a cockroach on the bedspread during our last visit, but I didn't see it, so I can't verify or dismiss her claim. Still, it's pretty unsettling, considering it could happen in any top hotel and likely was just a one-off incident.

Thinking back, we should have reported it. Anyway, I appreciate the central location and the Flamingo's history as one of the oldest casinos on the Strip. Long live the Flamingo!

The Flamingo's ambiance and the crab leg buffet are standout features. Although I haven't stayed here recently, I'd consider it again if there's a good deal.

yelp:train:145656.orig: Nice hotel and cool pool party, beautiful garden with (real flamingos!). Starting to cater to a lot of young folks. We got a non renovated room, the furniture was old and the bathroom was not appealing at all. Really thin walls, because we know when our neighbors are in. The good part was that we had a nice view of the strip.
yelp:train:145656.para: The hotel was pleasant, and there was an enjoyable pool party with a stunning garden featuring real flamingos. It seems to attract many young people now. Our room wasn't updated, with outdated furniture and an unappealing bathroom. The walls were very thin, so we could hear our neighbors clearly. On the bright side, we had a nice view of the strip.

yelp:train:146142.orig:
We def had to wait in line a good while to check in.  The line wrapped around the lobby at least three times. 

I read reviews about TVs in the bathroom mirror...but we did not have that. The room was pretty basic and it was supposed to be a deluxe king (we had two queens instead). 

The pillows feel short and kept slipping off the bed. The closet and bathroom were small but adequate. My room was $56 on week nights and over $100 on weekends. The resort fee was $25 for one day...which was nearly half of the room cost. 

They were working on the casino so whole sections had machines pulled out And caution tape roping it off. We spent all of our time in nicer casinos like Paris, Caesars, and others.
yelp:train:146142.para: We had a long wait to check in; the line circled the lobby multiple times. Reviews mentioned TVs in the bathroom mirror, but we didn't have that feature. The room was fairly basic and was supposed to be a deluxe king, but we got two queens instead. The pillows were uncomfortable and kept falling off the bed. The closet and bathroom were small but sufficient. My room cost $56 on weekdays and more than $100 on weekends. The resort fee was $25 for a single day, which was nearly half the room price. The casino was under renovation, with sections closed off by caution tape, so we spent our time in nicer casinos like Paris and Caesars.

yelp:train:146463.orig:
I filled out a survey for this hotel for my stay. (Yes I was still pissed).

The manager or whatever did offer us a 1 night comp stay..

But I dont think I will be coming back.

Sorry Luxor I'm staying with your sister hotel. The Mgm.
yelp:train:146463.para:
After completing the survey for my recent stay, I was still quite upset. 

The manager offered a complimentary one-night stay, but I doubt I'll return.

I'm sorry, Luxor, but I'll be choosing your sister hotel, MGM, instead.

yelp:train:146531.orig: The bathtub and separate showers are nice, granite and tile, but the shower head and the towels are low rent. Other than this the tower deluxe room wasnt anythig special nothong particularly bad, just decent. If i wasnt hwre for work I would absolutely stay at least at the mandalay bay or nicer more mid-strip.  I had multiple problems with my keycard not working in the door, and an issue with my reservation thatr I called ahead to avoid and once there nothing was done and I was misinformed/lied too.  I will go out of my way not to stay here and make sure nobody else has to deal with their incompetence.  Too many bettere options to stay at on the strip to stay at the \""Sux\""ur.
yelp:train:146531.para: The bathtub and separate showers are nice, with granite and tile, but the showerhead and towels are of lower quality. Apart from that, the tower deluxe room wasn't particularly special or bad; it was just average. If I weren't here for work, I'd definitely choose to stay at Mandalay Bay or a nicer hotel on the mid-strip instead. I experienced multiple issues with my keycard not working and had a reservation problem that I had called to avoid, but nothing was resolved, and I felt misled. I'll go out of my way to avoid staying here and ensure others don't face their incompetence. There are too many better options on the strip to stay at the "Sux"ur.

yelp:train:146988.orig:
We stayed here for five days while visiting family in town.

I have no complaints at all, it was a great stay!

I did book online at hotels.com, and that was cheaper than the front desk price, but I assume everyone can find a price they are comfortable with one way or another.

We got a room with two queen beds, on the 28th floor of the main pyramid. The room was super spacious, which is always nice. The bathroom had a nice big shower, but no tub. I'm not sure if other rooms have tubs or all of them only have showers.

The wi-fi is free with the resort fee, but only in public areas, not your room...I guess I do have one complaint, but it didn't cause any issues, just not convenient.

All the staff we interacted with was friendly and helpful.

I would definitely stay here again!
yelp:train:146988.para:
We spent five days here while visiting family in town, and I have nothing but praise for our stay—it was fantastic!

I booked through hotels.com, which turned out to be more affordable than the front desk price, but everyone can find a comfortable rate either way.

We were in a room with two queen beds, located on the 28th floor of the main pyramid. The room was very spacious, which was great. The bathroom featured a large shower but no bathtub; I'm not sure if other rooms have a bathtub or if all have showers.

The Wi-Fi, included with the resort fee, was available only in public areas, not in the room. This is one minor issue, but it didn't cause any problems, just a bit of inconvenience.

The staff we encountered were all very friendly and helpful.

I definitely want to return!

yelp:train:147100.para:
Pros: The hotel has an exciting appearance from the outside and a nice structure. Inside, it's also appealing with three Starbucks locations, a spacious lobby, and a large casino with numerous slot machines. The bell hops were particularly helpful, providing the only decent customer service in the hotel. These are the only reasons this place managed to receive even a single star.

Cons: The rooms are outdated and everything is old. There's no refrigerator, and the bed comforter was just a sheet and a brown blanket, which was uncomfortable. I stayed in a deluxe tower room on the 14th floor, which was supposed to be "updated." Cleanliness was terrible; the hotel is actually quite dirty. Bathroom floors look like they haven't been mopped, and the shower head is terrible, with poor water pressure that hurts. The valet area is always crowded. Additionally, a lady knocked on my door very loudly on the first day, refusing to stop, even though we had just arrived after a 10-hour drive from San Francisco. She thought we were the previous guests who were supposed to check out and tried to...

yelp:train:147218.orig:
Just stayed at MB for the second time and it was nowhere as nice as the first time, which was about 4 years ago. 

In the past twelve months  I have stayed at Caesars and the Wynn, and would choose either of these two for the next time I visit.

Why? Let me list the many reasons...

As others mentioned, it's way too far away from everything else on the strip. 

Ridiculously long check in. The average time per guest on a Friday afternoon was 10 minutes. 

EVERY morning at 9 a.m. the maid was chomping to get in the room. That's a bit early in Vegas, people.

1 towel per guest at the pool? Towels were grayish or brownish and thin. The Wynn had thick and fluffly and sparkly white ones...

Lounges at the pool were neighborhood pool quality with plastic slats. I chose not to pay $25 per chair + $50 for an umbrella. The Wynn has comfy padded chairs.

I'm not visiting a water park, I'm a guest at a hotel. Therefore I find it ridiculous that you have to buy tubes for the lazy river. Really poorly made tubes.  Both of ours mysteriously popped in the water the second day.

In four days, I  was never approached at any point while gambling and offered a players card. Compared
yelp:train:147218.para:
My recent stay at MB, my second visit, was significantly less enjoyable than my initial stay about 4 years ago. 

In the last year, I've stayed at Caesars and the Wynn, and I'd opt for either of those for my next trip.

Why? Here are the reasons:

MB is much farther from the strip compared to other hotels. 

Check-in was extremely lengthy; on a Friday afternoon, it took about 10 minutes per person.

Maid service started at 9 a.m. every morning, which is quite early for Vegas.

Each guest was given just one towel at the pool, which was grayish and thin. The Wynn offered thick, fluffy, and sparkly white towels.

The pool lounges were of poor quality, similar to neighborhood pools with plastic slats. I opted not to pay $25 per chair plus $50 for an umbrella, as the Wynn had comfortable padded chairs.

I expected a hotel experience, not a water park. It was absurd to have to buy tubes for the lazy river, and ours popped mysteriously on the second day.

During my four days of gambling, I was never offered a players card, which I found surprising.

yelp:train:147943.orig:
Being a big carnivore myself, i enjoy a big piece of red meat from time-to-time.   I was told by friends this place might fit the bill.
 
We were promptly greeted upon our arrival and were seated along the back booths.  The decor and the lighting was 'fitting' for the place and as well as the menu.   After several minutes pondering the menu, we had the shrimp cocktail to start which was nothing special and I should have expected that this being a steak place.  

We shared the 32 oz Porterhouse for two with assortment of mushrooms, fingerling potatoes and roasted corn.  And yes the porterhouse was delicious - juicy, perfectly seasoned and the fillet was outrageous.  The side dishes were somewhat ordinary BUT the surprise of the dinner was the roasted corn.  We just had to ask the waiter for the recipe which he was more than happy to share.  Just delicious.
The service was impeccable as well as the ambiance.  Was it the best steak I have ever had?  Perhaps if it wasn't for the roasted corn, it might have been......


Cheers,
yelp:train:147943.para:
As a big meat lover, I occasionally indulge in a hearty piece of red meat. My friends recommended this place, and I decided to give it a try.

Upon arrival, we were greeted promptly and seated at the back booths. The ambiance and lighting were well-suited to the restaurant, as was the menu. After some deliberation, we started with the shrimp cocktail, which, as expected for a steakhouse, was unremarkable.

We ordered the 32 oz Porterhouse for two, accompanied by a variety of mushrooms, fingerling potatoes, and roasted corn. The porterhouse was indeed delicious, juicy, and well-seasoned, with the fillet being particularly outstanding. The side dishes were somewhat ordinary, but the roasted corn was a delightful surprise. We even asked the waiter for the recipe, which he happily shared. It was truly delicious.

The service and atmosphere were exceptional. While it might not have been the absolute best steak I've ever had, the roasted corn certainly elevated the dining experience.

yelp:train:147971.orig:
Is it still considered a martini if it's just straight up gin?  Would I be considered an alcoholic because these are the kinds of questions that I ponder?

I'm only asking, because I was batting around ideas on what to order at the bar here while waiting for our showing of Kà to kick off, and none of the specialty drinks really called to me.  Instead, I just asked for a simple martini.  Um.  Extra dry.  Like... the gin, shaken, with a twist kinda dry.

And it was delicious.

It better have been, considering the price.  Although, admittedly, there was enough booze in my giant martini glass to account for the cost.  Still, when we're talking a Colicchio restaurant in one of the higher end megahotels on The Strip... with a gorgeous interior, personable bartender, and a generous pour...

Ain't got no complaints here.
yelp:train:147971.para:
Is a martini still a martini if it's just gin? Am I an alcoholic for even questioning this? 

I was just mulling over my bar options while waiting for our Kà screening to start, and none of the fancy drinks appealed to me. So, I opted for a straightforward martini—extra dry, with the gin shaken and a twist of citrus. 

It was absolutely delicious.

It had better be, given the price. But considering the Colicchio restaurant in one of the top hotels on The Strip, with its elegant interior, friendly bartender, and generous pour, I can't complain.

yelp:train:148287.orig:
I must first start off and say I've never had steak before. I was advised by my friend if you're gonna have steak, you might as well have the best. So we decided Tom Colicchio might know a thing or two about steak. Therefore if you are a steak connoisseur, look at someone else's review! 

Pros:
Very nice casual atmosphere

My water glass was always filled... always... like if I just think about my water I see a water person waiting in the corner ready to refill my glass

Very little noise,  not like creepy deserted quietness, more like a nice low murmur. 

Waiter and all the staff we met were very kind and courteous about everything

Cons:

I don't know if it'll be too memorable. The food was good, the service was good but when I come back to Vegas again I'm not going to be like ""I have GOT to go to Craftsteak, like OMG gurl.""

4 stars
yelp:train:148287.para:
I've never tried steak before, so when my friend suggested going for the best, we decided to seek advice from Tom Colicchio. If you're a steak aficionado, you might want to check out another review! 

Pros:
- The place has a very pleasant, casual vibe
- My water glass was constantly refilled, as if someone was always watching to make sure it stayed full
- There was a nice, low-level background noise, not an eerie silence, but a comfortable hum
- The staff, including the waiter, were exceptionally kind and attentive

Cons:
- The experience wasn't particularly memorable. The food and service were good, but I doubt I'll be rushing back to Vegas just to visit Craftsteak. 
- Overall, I'd give it 4 stars.

yelp:train:148347.orig: The hostess are very obviously not hired for the size of their brains, but hey, its vegas. The food is subpar, even for the prices it;s a ripoff. I got a sangria and it was bad news. Didn't even drink it. I bet the margaritas are better. I will give it another shot I guess but honestly, I would rather go to firefly down the street.
yelp:train:148347.para: The hostesses clearly weren't chosen for their intellect, but hey, it is Vegas. The food quality is poor, and the prices feel like a scam. My sangria was terrible, and I couldn't even finish it. I assume the margaritas might be better. I'll give it another try, though I'd much prefer to visit Firefly down the street.

yelp:train:148554.orig: Ate here Feb 13.  If you are at the Venetian for a trade show and you need convenience, this is an all around winner.\nThat night was very windy so unfortunately the terrace was closed, but it looked like the terrace would be a lovely place to eat.  Someone said it was noisy, it might depend where you sit.  I thought it was quiet.  The service was excellent.  Like another Yelper here on the same night, we  enjoyed the trout. The side of garlic spinach was delicious.  Prices are high but typical for the location, so we didn't think it was over-priced.
yelp:train:148554.para:
Visited on February 13th, and if you're at the Venetian for a trade show and need convenience, this place is a standout choice overall. 

That evening, it was quite windy, which meant the terrace was unavailable, though it seemed like a pleasant spot to dine. Some mentioned it could be noisy, but I found it relatively quiet. The service was top-notch. Similar to another reviewer on the same night, we both enjoyed the trout, and the garlic spinach side was particularly delightful. While the prices are on the higher side, they are consistent with the area, so we didn't find them excessive.

yelp:train:148563.orig:
This place is hidden on the 10th or 11th floor of the Venetian and there's this hilarious guy dressed up in faux military garb standing sentry across from the restrooms.  Considering all that pomp, Bouchon is a pretty laid back and fun restaurant.  I arrived in flip flops and jeans after killing my feet in heels the night before and I felt perfectly comfortable.

If you dine here, make sure you order the foie gras.  It's such a wonderful thing.  It's like...you're eating it and thinking...this is so delicious....it's a .....highly caloric cholesterol raising schmear....it's so rich....salty....yum....illegal in certain areas.....mmmmm......  It's served in the same jar that  you can pick up at Bouchon Bakery in Yountville, but in Vegas they serve it with bottomless fingers of warm toast. aaah.  It is so good.

I had the pork shoulder.  It was a frickin HUGE serving and I couldn't get through more than half of it.  Very tender.  Very good.  My husband had the monkfish and he enjoyed it.  I like the fact that they serve on All-Clad at T. Keller restaurants.  It's a nice touch.  We had beignets for desert because after dining on foie gras and pork shoulder, you may as well go all
yelp:train:148563.para:
Located on the 10th or 11th floor of the Venetian, Bouchon is a surprisingly relaxed and enjoyable restaurant, featuring a comical guard in mock military attire guarding the restrooms. Despite the formal setting, the atmosphere is quite casual. I arrived wearing flip-flops and jeans, having worn heels the previous night, and felt completely at ease.

If you visit, don't miss the foie gras—it's truly exceptional. It's so delectable that you'll think, "This is so rich and salty, it's... a highly caloric, cholesterol-raising spread... so good." It comes in the same jar as at the Bouchon Bakery in Yountville, but here in Vegas, it's served with endless slices of warm toast. It's simply divine.

I ordered the pork shoulder, which was a massive portion that I barely managed to finish. It was incredibly tender and delicious. My husband enjoyed the monkfish. I appreciate that they use All-Clad cookware at Thomas Keller's restaurants; it's a nice touch. For dessert, we had beignets because after the foie gras and pork shoulder, it was the perfect way to cap off the meal.

yelp:train:149184.orig: Our friends have been raving about this place, every time they come to Vegas they have brunch here.  So they wanted us to experience this place and me, being a green horned foodie in training, was looking forward to the experience.  It was what I expected with impeccable service and a place to live in the moment and enjoy each bite.  We order the pastry basket, American breakfast, chicken and waffles and shared them all and the gravy for the chicken had bits of bacon and chives - among the four of us which was plenty for a light breakfast.  Tip for the brunch, come early as we came at 9 AM and there was no waiting.  But by the time we left, long waits.  So enjoy the experience, come early!  All were delightful and I normally don't eat a big breakfast so sampling these dishes was just perfect for my small appetite.  I can't wait to come here for dinner to try the mussels!
yelp:train:149184.para: Our friends have been highly recommending this place, and every time they visit Vegas, they go for brunch here. They wanted us to try it out, and as a food enthusiast still learning, I was excited. The experience met my expectations with outstanding service and a chance to savor each bite. We ordered the pastry basket, American breakfast, and chicken and waffles, sharing everything. The chicken gravy included bits of bacon and chives, making it more than enough for a light meal among the four of us. A tip for brunch: arrive early, as we came at 9 AM and didn't have to wait, but by the time we left, there were long lines. So, come early to enjoy the experience! Everything was delightful, and since I don't usually eat a big breakfast, trying these dishes was just right for my appetite. I can't wait to return for dinner to try the mussels!

yelp:train:149189.orig:
The best brunch on the strip!!!

Since they don't take reservations for brunch but recommend coming in earlier to avoid longer wait, I along with my friends got there around 9:30 and were seated within a few mins.

From the first moment you step on you can feel the cheerful/bright ambiance. Service, decor, and creativity all are bound to win your heart.

The food is definitely authentic french and hence even the French toast aren't the traditional ones you get at the American brunch restaurants. Not to say it was anything short of delicious.

Overall I had a great time and can't wait to get back for round 2 the next time I'm in that city.
yelp:train:149189.para:
The absolute best brunch spot on the strip!!!

Although they don't accept reservations for brunch and suggest arriving early to cut down on wait times, my friends and I managed to secure a table by 9:30 and were seated within minutes.

The moment you enter, you're greeted by a vibrant and cheerful atmosphere. The service, decor, and creative offerings are sure to captivate you.

The food is genuinely French, with the French toast being a standout, quite different from what you'd typically find at American brunch places. It was absolutely delicious.

In summary, I had an incredible experience and can't wait to return for another visit the next time I'm in town.

yelp:train:149195.orig: Didn't live up to its Yelp rating. It's so hard to find. Casino direction was not clear. We went there for Brunch. We had the famous Croque Madame and French Toast. The Croque Madame was good, but not worth the price tag. French Toast was too moist and lack flavors. The wait was an hour, if it was not for the Roulette Table that kept me busy, I would not have waited.
yelp:train:149195.para: The place didn't meet our expectations based on the Yelp reviews. It was quite challenging to locate. The casino directions were confusing. We went for brunch and tried the famous Croque Madame and French Toast. The Croque Madame was decent but overpriced. The French Toast was overly moist and lacked flavor. We waited for an hour, but the presence of a busy Roulette Table kept us occupied, otherwise, we might not have waited that long.

yelp:train:149402.orig:
I always look forward to come to Olives when I come to Vegas. It is somewhere you definitely need to make reservations or else you prob gonna have to wait. I never tried it for dinner but lunch is good and inexpensive. 

Service is usually good. They usually have lunch specials and I usually get that but i guess it depends on what pasta lunch special they have. Their pastas are really good because it's hand toss/house made. I also really recommend sharing a beef capraccio with a friend which is SUPER GOOD. There are like stuffing inside the middle of the plate and kind of a salad. I don't really like the stuffing but besides that It is super good. 

I recommend anybody coming here for lunch(never tried dinner) when they're in vegas.
yelp:train:149402.para:
I always anticipate visiting Olives whenever I'm in Vegas. You really should make a reservation, as otherwise, you might have to wait. I haven't tried it for dinner, but the lunch is great and affordable. 

The service is typically good, and they usually offer lunch specials, which I usually opt for, though it varies depending on the pasta options available. Their pastas are excellent, as they are hand-tossed and house-made. I also highly suggest sharing the beef capraccio with a friend; it's outstanding. There are fillings in the middle of the plate, along with a salad, but I don't particularly enjoy the fillings. Despite that, it's still super delicious.

I recommend that anyone visiting Vegas for lunch (I haven't tried the dinner menu) should definitely go to Olives.

yelp:train:149520.orig: Tourist trap! The decor and ambience of the club is pretty cool but other than that this place is nothing special.
yelp:train:149520.para: A tourist trap, really! While the club's decor and atmosphere are quite appealing, the overall experience isn't particularly noteworthy.

yelp:train:149780.orig: I recently found my new favorite Ted Baker dress here for an unbeatable price.  I can easily see myself making this a regular stop on my LV trips!  Aside from the parking fiasco (we ended up driving over a curb and parking in some dirt, which apparently is OK!), this place is great  :)\n\nPlenty of shops, great deals, nice outdoor feel.  Maybe it's just that folks are nicer in LV than they are in LA, but I was super impressed by how calm and chill the shoppers are here -- It was the day after Christmas and nobody was yelling or pushing or being a general nuisance!  Way to go, civilized peeps!
yelp:train:149780.para:
I just discovered my new favorite Ted Baker dress at a fantastic price, and I'm already looking forward to making this a regular stop on my Las Vegas shopping trips! The only hiccup was parking (we ended up on some dirt, but it seemed acceptable), but everything else was great :).

There are plenty of shops, amazing deals, and a pleasant outdoor atmosphere. Perhaps it's just that people are more relaxed in Las Vegas, but I was really impressed by how calm and courteous the shoppers were—especially on the day after Christmas, when there was no yelling or pushing or general chaos! Kudos to the civilized folks in Vegas!

yelp:train:149794.orig:
After a brief stay in Vegas, we decided to head on over to 4-star rated Premium Outlets. Oh my, oh my, oh my. 

Tips:

1. I implore you to get there before noon to shop or be prepared for carmageddon in the parking structure. 

2. The VIP coupon book available for purchase at the information booth: don't get it. It's really not worth your money considering you're NOT allowed to combine the sales within the coupon book with the deals already occurring in the store. And chances are, the ones in the store are better anyway. Unless you're planning on dropping hundreds for a Kate Spade handbag to get a 15% deal, not worth your $5. You can preview it if you'd like though.

3. If you manage to get there early with fewer people, the crazy packed stores include Polo Ralph Lauren and Banana Republic. The line for Banana was insanely long so I'd suggest you hit that store first if it's one of the stores on your list. 

Otherwise, this outlet was huge! We didn't even shop all of it because our feet were so dang tired already. The only downside to this outlet would be like sometimes it doesn't seem like an outlet at all because the prices are still the same for some stores. It was a h
yelp:train:149794.para:
After a short visit to Vegas, we ventured to the 4-star rated Premium Outlets. Oh my, oh my, oh my.

Tips:

1. I strongly advise arriving before noon to shop, or you might face a parking nightmare.
2. The VIP coupon book, available at the information booth, isn't worth buying. You can't combine the sales in the book with existing store deals, and the store deals are usually better. Unless you're looking to buy a Kate Spade handbag for a 15% discount, it's not worth the $5. You can still preview it if you're interested.
3. If you can get there early, the most crowded stores are Polo Ralph Lauren and Banana Republic. The line for Banana was extremely long, so I recommend hitting that store first if it's on your list.
Otherwise, the outlet was enormous! We didn't manage to explore it all due to our tired feet. The only downside is that sometimes the prices in some stores don't seem to reflect the outlet status.

yelp:train:149881.orig: Get the 7.77 deal, you won't regret it. That is, if they haven't stopped serving it. I first saw it on Rachael Ray's 40 Dollars A Day and had to try it. Steak, shrimp, baked potato and salad? And it was all pretty good, and just the right amount of food. And I think you even get a vegetable with that...
yelp:train:149881.para: Don't miss out on the 7.77 offer; you won't regret it, assuming they still serve it. I came across it on Rachael Ray's 40 Dollars A Day show and had to give it a try. The meal includes steak, shrimp, a baked potato, and a salad, and it was quite satisfying, with just the right portion size. I believe you also get a vegetable with this option...

yelp:train:150349.orig: This bar STINKS!! - LITERALLY!\n\nThis is the stinkiest, slimiest, stickiest bar I've ever been to. If you are drunk enough to not use any of your sense, KAMs is your place.
yelp:train:150349.para: This bar is absolutely horrendous—literally reeking of unpleasant odors. It's the smelliest, slipperiest, and stickiest bar I've ever visited. If you're so intoxicated that you can't rely on your senses, then KAMs might be the place for you.

yelp:train:150625.orig:
Translates to ""night play"" or ""after party"" in Norwegian -- as you can imagine, this place is open late in the night all week.

I'd like to think of this Madison's hidden gem of a bar (no sign outside, no phone)! 

Good drinks; Great ambiance  - Intimate; Asian influenced- one of the owners spent a lot of time in China. 

Their wood-burning oven roasted pizzas are very good. Love their three-cup tofu - an amazing blend of flavors served with rice and pickled veggies. I usually have them go a little easy on the soy and it is perfect for me. Their hummus plate is also delicious and a good value for the money.

Seating -- if it is winter, find a seat further inside - the door opening can get pretty drafty.  If there is a DJ, the back of the place can get loud. The best, most intimate space is at the furthest back wall on the left -- there is a little alcove with about 4 tables! If it is summer, their front windows open out, so you can sit either up front or outside and it is quite nice.

Note: Small food menu and No credit cards accepted (ATM on site though)
yelp:train:150625.para:
This place, known as a "night play" or "after party" in Norwegian, stays open late every night. Think of it as Madison's well-kept secret bar (no visible sign or phone number needed to find it).

The drinks are top-notch, and the atmosphere is intimate and Asian-inspired, with one of the owners having spent significant time in China. Their wood-burning oven pizzas are excellent, and I particularly enjoy their three-cup tofu, a delightful blend of flavors served with rice and pickled vegetables. I recommend asking them to use a bit less soy for a perfect taste. The hummus plate is also delicious and offers good value for the price.

When it's cold, look for a spot further inside to avoid the drafty entrance. If there's a DJ, the back of the place can get noisy. The most intimate seating is on the left side at the back, where there's a cozy alcove with about four tables. In warmer weather, you can sit either inside or outside, as the front windows open up, making it quite pleasant.

Note: The menu is small, and they don't accept credit cards, but there is an ATM on-site.

yelp:train:150672.orig: There's really no way to describe the place without experiencing it. It's definitely one of the coolest clubs I've ever been to. The drinks are definitely pricey, but the eye candy, mouth candy, or whatever floats your boat makes it worthwhile. They really should change the name of this place to PURE DEBAUCHERY. Thanks to Harrahs MBA poker tournament, we got to go in early, and they had an open bar for 2 hours.  Of course, when you ask for water, you will get a 9 dollar plutonium container, called Voss. So I had 9 bottles of water along with all my drinks.  Pretty much every time you walk to the bar, you will be out 20 bucks. That said, the views of the strip are amazing and it remains one of favorite places in Vegas..
yelp:train:150672.para: Experiencing the place is truly the only way to understand it. It's undoubtedly one of the most exciting clubs I've ever visited. While the drinks are on the expensive side, the visual and sensory experiences more than justify the cost. The club should probably be renamed to PURE DEBAUCHERY. Thanks to the Harrahs MBA poker tournament, we were able to enter early and enjoy an open bar for two hours. When you request water, it often comes in a nine-dollar bottle called Voss. I ended up with nine bottles of water alongside my drinks. Essentially, every trip to the bar costs around twenty dollars, but the views of the strip are spectacular, and it remains one of my favorite spots in Vegas.

yelp:train:150817.orig: Nice place..I mean I really like it...except...The way you run your shit! How can you hire a bunch of douchebag guys that talk to people like their assholes? Yeah I told the security guard to go \""F\"" himself but that's only cuz he was rude when I was trying to be ever so polite. Also, $68 bucks for fout Jager bombs!? Seriously!? I thought this was a recession period, not an inflation period....Go fuck yourself Pure!
yelp:train:150817.para: It's a great place overall, but there's one big issue I have with how things are run. The staff, especially the security, are really unprofessional and rude. I even had to tell one of the security guards to "go to hell" because he was being particularly unpleasant, even though I tried to be very polite. And the price of $68 for just four Jager bombs is outrageous—seriously, is this during a recession or an inflation period? Go to hell, Pure!

yelp:train:150852.orig: was very disappointed in this club i heard alot of thing bout it and couldnt wait to go and i felt robbed of my money i was better off going to Tabu..they played good music thats one star the club was nice and big thats the second star but besides that id never go back...the main dance floor was sooo crowded i couldnt get in and the put the restrooms way in the back so u have to go thru the crowd. you cant just stand either u either have to keep walking around in circles or be on the dance floor seriouslt wtf is that?! \n\noverall i was not impressed and definatly not go back
yelp:train:150852.para: I was quite disappointed with this club. I had heard a lot about it and was eager to visit, but it felt like I wasted my money. I wish I had gone to Tabu instead, as they play good music, which is the only reason I gave them one star. The club itself was nice and spacious, which is the second star, but that's about it. I wouldn't return. The main dance floor was extremely crowded, making it impossible to move, and the restrooms were located far back, requiring me to navigate through the crowd. You can't just stand there; you either have to keep walking in circles or stay on the dance floor, which is frustrating. Overall, I was not impressed and definitely won't be going back.

yelp:train:150884.orig: i hate this place. but i always seem to end up here every trip, so they must be doing something right.
yelp:train:150884.para: I really dislike this spot, yet I find myself returning on each trip. It must be doing something well, then.

yelp:train:150992.orig:
Pure is a nice looking place that provided a mediocre experience.  I know that exclusivity is something that is important for night clubs in Las Vegas to have, but an upscale image becomes meaningless when you make your customers feel unwelcomed and uncomfortable.

This past Sunday was my first visit to Pure. From the time we arrived, I felt like they could care less about our enjoyment.  It was as if they were doing us a favor by even letting us in.  Our names were on a VIP list through a Las Vegas promoter that I have had great experiences using before, and they still gave us a hard time getting in.  They pushed bottle service, sent us to the wrong line, and then told me that I was lucky to get in since I was wearing sneakers as I was walking in.  I can understand that they would like for people not to wear sneakers, but they should keep the comments to themselves since we were already headed in.  There was no one else there on a Sunday night...of course they were going to let us in!  They just didn't need to make it like we were entering a maximum security military base.

Once inside, we saw that the whole lower level was closed.  The upstairs balcony was the only area open,
yelp:train:150992.para:
Pure is an attractive venue that offered a subpar experience. While exclusivity is crucial for nightclubs in Las Vegas, an upscale image loses its value when customers feel unwelcome and uncomfortable.

My recent visit to Pure on Sunday was my first, and from the moment we arrived, it was clear they didn't prioritize our enjoyment. It seemed they were merely accommodating us by allowing entry. Despite our names being on a VIP list through a Las Vegas promoter I've had positive experiences with, we faced difficulties getting in. They aggressively promoted bottle service, directed us to the wrong line, and even commented that we were lucky to be admitted because we were wearing sneakers. While it's understandable they prefer no sneakers, such comments are unnecessary once we were on our way in. Given that it was a Sunday night with no one else around, they should have let us in without making it feel like we were entering a secure facility.

Upon entering, we noticed that the entire lower level was closed, leaving only the upstairs balcony open.

yelp:train:151158.orig:
My fiancé and I both agree that we will never visit again. Over priced, cheesy, and lacking in both authenticity and flavor. Don't order their radish appetizer. Just don't. The sausage tower was decent, but boring.

Who plays Margaritaville in a German establishment.?

We did enjoy ourselves though, we were drunk and drinking. Big mugs of beer. I think my biggest annoyance was that at the outside bar, they can't make a cocktail that's not on their menu, for a reasonable price- $5 per liquor involved per pour if you want something ""obscure"" e.g. a classic Sidecar.. And they don't even pour it, it's all measured out and done for them. Seems like the owners are a bit hard up. Where's the trust for their own employees?
yelp:train:151158.para:
My fiancé and I have decided we'll never return. The place is overpriced, clichéd, and fails to deliver on authenticity or taste. Avoid the radish appetizer; it's a no-go. The sausage tower was okay, but quite mundane.

What kind of Margaritaville experience is this in a German bar?

Despite the issues, we had a good time, especially when we were tipsy and sipping from large mugs of beer. My main frustration was the outside bar, where they charge $5 per liquor pour for any "unusual" cocktail, and even then, they don't let you mix it yourself; they just measure it out. It seems the owners are being overly cautious with their staff.

yelp:train:151335.orig: unless you're a soccer (futbol) hooligan do not go here during world cup soccer !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!  holy crap at 5pm there were so many drunk doucheburgers (and i like to party yo) i actually had to leave fearing i'd end up in a fight and in a lv jail.
yelp:train:151335.para: Unless you're a soccer fan who enjoys the chaos, stay away during the World Cup! Man, by 5 PM, it was packed with drunk revelers (and I love a good party). I had to leave because I was worried about getting into a fight and ending up in jail.

yelp:train:151612.orig: Please don't use Jamie C's review as a deciding factor as she has also rated Jack in the Box with 4 stars.  No wonder you had to add salt to your burger.  And gross.  Anyway, I've only had great experiences here especially when I get off of work starving and this place is the only restaurant in the area smart enough to stay open late.  Service has always been friendly...then again, I know how to be respectful and not wave my hands in the air like a total douche.  See you guys soon!
yelp:train:151612.para: Avoid letting Jamie C's review sway your decision, as she also gave Jack in the Box 4 stars. That's why you might need to add salt to your burger—yuck. Anyway, my experiences here have been fantastic, particularly when I'm starving after work, as this is the only late-night restaurant in the area. The service is always friendly, and I make sure to be respectful. See you soon!

yelp:train:151979.orig: Quite forgettable, at least I hope I forget about it. There's better food at an employee cafeteria with an atmosphere comparable to that. Very little selection and what was there was dry.  Not everything was awful; some items were good but not good enough to justify the effort of going there again.  There are so many great buffets in Vegas; this wouldn't make the top 1000.
yelp:train:151979.para: I find it quite forgettable, and I hope I don't remember it much. The employee cafeteria has a similar atmosphere and offers much better food. The selection was limited, and what was available was rather dry. While some items were decent, they weren't great enough to warrant a repeat visit. With so many excellent buffets in Vegas, this place wouldn't even make it into the top 1000.

yelp:train:152072.orig: I wish I could say I enjoyed this show, But instead I found myself struggling to stay awake so that I could see the interludes which were entertaining. The show followed no cohesive storytelling while appearing to try and tell a story, and while the sets were elaborate and well made, as were the costumes, it seemed like the dancing stayed the same or similar as it pertains to the large numbers while there seemed to be very few multifaceted members of the cast. I seriously fell asleep and was woken up by my wife no less than 3 times. She loved it by the way, I guess it's the Y chromozone that caused me to be so vexed by this show. I would not recomend this show.
yelp:train:152072.para: While I couldn't say I enjoyed the show, I had to fight to stay alert just to catch the interludes, which were the only entertaining parts. The show lacked a coherent narrative despite its attempts to tell one. Although the sets and costumes were impressive, the choreography seemed repetitive, with only a few actors showing significant depth. I dozed off multiple times—my wife had to wake me up at least three times. She adored it, but it clearly didn't resonate with me. I wouldn't recommend this show.

yelp:train:152114.orig: Yes, I love dive restaurants as well as dive bars.  Nothing fancy here, just a drugstore diner.  It is open 24 hours!  I don't eat here enough!
yelp:train:152114.para: Certainly, I enjoy dive restaurants just as much as dive bars. This place is a simple drugstore diner with no frills. It's open round the clock, and I find myself not visiting often enough!

yelp:train:152195.orig: Of all the buffets at the casinos in Vegas, this is the worst yet...not bad, but there was a re-occuring theme of just-ok-ness throughout the meal. I'm referring to the overcooked cuts of meat, crappy dessert selection, cold food (when it should have been hot) and most of all, the lack of labeling the food stations (which pissed me off the most). It was aggravating to have to go to the front of the lines just to see what the food was or to view the itty-bitty food description signage.\n\nI will say, good selection of shrimp.
yelp:train:152195.para: Among all the buffets in Las Vegas casinos, this one stands out as particularly disappointing. While not terrible, the overall experience was just okay. The issues included overcooked meats, a subpar dessert menu, and cold dishes that should have been served hot. What really annoyed me was the lack of clear labeling for the food stations. It was frustrating to have to wait at the front of the line just to figure out what was being served or to read the tiny descriptions. On the positive side, the shrimp selection was quite good.

yelp:train:152277.orig: The dessert case will bring you to your knees in reverence for the hallowed pastry chefs of Las Vegas.\n\nThe bacon is a little rubbery in texture. But I would quit my job to travel to the sprawling pastures (read: feedlots) where the prime rib is raised. Mmm. Prime rib.
yelp:train:152277.para:
The dessert selection is so impressive that it could make you bow in admiration of the skilled pastry chefs in Las Vegas.

While the bacon has a slightly rubbery texture, I'd resign from my position to visit the expansive feedlots where the prime rib is raised. Oh, how delicious that prime rib sounds!

yelp:train:152340.orig:
Food never made us happier! This is by far THE BEST dinner buffet money can buy.

Yes it's worth the wait, and yes it's worth the $40 per person.

You will find something for even the most pickiest eater and still get your money's worth!

We will be coming back here again and again.
yelp:train:152340.para:
Dining here is always a joy; this buffet is undoubtedly the pinnacle of what you can get for your money. The wait and the $40 per person are definitely worthwhile.

There's something for everyone, even the most discerning palates, and you'll feel like you've gotten your money's worth. We're looking forward to returning time and time again.

yelp:train:153028.orig:
Service was great... food was satisfying and ummmmm... 4th star was for their CANNOLIs!!! 

HOLY CANNOLI... they were amazing!!! Get the 24hr BUFFET pass and hit this one up on the list... Loved their breakfast choices and Middle eastern food!! YUM!!! 

:) Definitely satisfied!!!!
yelp:train:153028.para:
The service was excellent, and the food was quite satisfying—especially their cannolis, which earned a 4-star rating! 

OH MY CANNOLI, they were incredible! I highly recommend getting the 24-hour buffet pass and trying this place. I adored their breakfast options and the Middle Eastern cuisine—it was delicious! 

:) I am definitely pleased!

yelp:train:153033.orig:
Went here for brunch on a Saturday with a friend. We got here between 10:30 and 11 am. Line wasn't long (especially when compared to some other places we passed), which was really the determining factor in going here.

There were a lot of options on the buffet, but a bit heavier on the lunch vs. breakfast. The mimosas are included in the buffet price, which was cool. And I will say that I did enjoy the mimosas - they had a good balance of sparkling wine and orange juice. But the overall price was a bit expensive for my taste (probably pretty much in line with most buffets in Vegas).

They had omelettes made to order, which was cool. But that was the only really special breakfast stuff they had. Other than that I got some fried potatoes, smoked salmon, french toast. I tried some of the desserts too and didn't really enjoy a single one.

Overall, nothing was amazing, but everything was ok.
yelp:train:153033.para:
On a Saturday, I visited for brunch with a friend, arriving between 10:30 and 11 am. The line wasn't long, which was a key factor in choosing this place. 

The buffet offered a variety of items, with more lunch options than breakfast. Mimosas were included in the price, which was a plus. I particularly liked the mimosas, as they had a good mix of sparkling wine and orange juice. However, the overall cost felt a bit steep for me, similar to most Vegas buffets.

They provided made-to-order omelettes, which was nice. Beyond that, the breakfast offerings were limited. I had fried potatoes, smoked salmon, and French toast. I also sampled some desserts but didn't enjoy any of them.

In summary, while nothing was outstanding, everything was satisfactory.

yelp:train:153296.orig: One of the biggest varieties of all Vegas buffets. We had lunch and it was excellent. The food isn't all 5-star quality, but given the sheer variety of foods available, I enjoyed my experience here.
yelp:train:153296.para: This buffet in Vegas offers an extensive range of options, which is one of the best around. I had lunch and found it to be very good. While the food doesn't all reach 5-star standards, the sheer variety made my visit enjoyable.

yelp:train:153333.orig:
Maybe it's just me! Every time I'm in Vegas I'm always being told you gotta see a show, go check out Mystere. Then the person goes on to say how they have seen it multiple times and how great it is. 

So, me and my ruca decide to check it out. It was kinda of a last minute thing so we had to spend a little extra and get ""good"" seats. By a little extra I mean a little over 200.00 for 2 tickets, not bad I guess since it is such a ""great show"".  Don't fall for that good seats bullshit either. The theater isn't that big, so any seat is a good seat.

Don't get me wrong the guy that comes out before the show to warm up the audience is funny and the shit they do is incredible. But I can only tolerate so much tumbling, acrobats and whatever else they do. Long story short I fell asleep. I don't get how people say they have seen this show more than once, I mean come on once is really enough. 

Maybe I'm just not a ""show"" guy, but I would save my money and spend it else where in Vegas. Mystere is a one time only thing, and even that might be too much.
yelp:train:153333.para:
Perhaps it's just my experience! Everyone in Vegas keeps recommending I see Mystere, insisting it's a must-see. They always mention how they've watched it multiple times and how fantastic it is.

So, my partner and I decided to give it a try. It was a spur-of-the-moment decision, which meant we had to pay a bit more for "good" seats. The cost was around $200 for two tickets, which seemed reasonable given the show's reputation as "great."

Don't believe the hype about "good" seats; the theater isn't that large, so any seat is decent. 

To be clear, the performer who warms up the audience before the show is amusing, and the acts are impressive. However, I can only handle so much tumbling and acrobatics. In short, I fell asleep. I can't fathom how people watch this show more than once; once is plenty.

Maybe I'm just not a "show" person, but I'd advise saving your money and spending it elsewhere in Vegas. Mystere is a one-time experience, and even that might be too much for me.

yelp:train:153507.orig:
From the minute you walk in the door...this place has a great BBQ hickory smell.  It also feels like home.  Many people complain about the crowd.  I seem to always come in here by myself and always find one lonely spot at the bar.  The bar also has a ton of beers too...in fact 150 Wisconsin beers in the house...which makes for a long beer picking process.

Personally I trust them and go for the beer of the month, which is only 2.50 for a pint...nice...June 2011 is the Fatty Boombalatty beer of the month.  Not only is it good but it is fun to say when you order it!!!

I also had the Sheboygan's Grand Champion Miesfeld Market Double Bratwurst with raw onion , pickles and brown mustard in a buttered Highway Bakery hard roll.  $7.95 or as it is listed in the menu the No.32.  The brats are amazing...so good!!!  I was not happy with the hard roll...it seemed like the thing that was wrong with the sandwich.  Maybe a soft roll like they serve in Sheboygan would be better?  Just maybe.

There are also great bar eats too...I tried the spicy pickled egg for a buck...it was okay. I've had a better one in a small bar north of Sheboygan years ago. I need to find that place again!!!

Alwa
yelp:train:153507.para:
As soon as you enter, this place exudes a delightful hickory BBQ aroma, reminiscent of home. Despite the crowds, I often find a solitary spot at the bar. They offer an impressive 150 Wisconsin beers, which can take some time to choose from.

Personally, I rely on their beer of the month, which costs just $2.50 for a pint. In June 2011, it was the Fatty Boombalatty, a fun name to say!

I also enjoyed the Sheboygan Grand Champion Miesfeld Market Double Bratwurst, served with raw onion, pickles, and brown mustard in a buttered roll. It costs $7.95 or is listed as No.32. The brats were outstanding, but I wasn't thrilled with the hard roll; perhaps a softer roll would enhance the sandwich.

The bar menu also features tasty options, like a spicy pickled egg for a dollar, which was merely okay. I've had better versions in a small bar north of Sheboygan, and I need to revisit that place!

yelp:train:154196.orig: it is ridiculously over priced! and not worth it. When they say some big celeb is coming, they bump up the price and then the person performs for 2 songs. I've now been here for \""black eyed peas\"" (only one of them) and Drake. There are many clubs in Vegas and honestly tao is not worth it.
yelp:train:154196.para: It's absurdly overpriced, and it's not worth the cost. Celebs often drive up the prices, but their performances are brief—usually just a couple of songs. I've been to see "Black Eyed Peas" (just one member) and Drake, and there are so many other clubs in Vegas; Tao just doesn't justify the expense.

yelp:train:154891.orig:
Hands-down, theeee best steak I have ever had in my entire life and I grew up in the food and beverage industry and have been eating fliet mignon and lobster bisque before I could even add and subtract.  When I go to a steakhouse, I always measure them by their filet mignon.  (So obviously this review excludes any kobe varieties cause that would not be a fair comparison).  

What i loved about the steak here was the crispy crust, the seasoning, tenderness, and juiciness.  It was like no other.  It was mind-blowing.  And at their price-point, compared to their neighbors, like Cut etc., this is a steal!

oh, and we also had oysters, truffled cream corn, truffled asparagus, and the banana dessert, some nice wine and a fantastic water show outside, all which were great accompaniments to our steak.
yelp:train:154891.para:
Without a doubt, this is the absolute best steak I've ever tasted, and I come from a background in the food and beverage industry, having enjoyed filet mignon and lobster bisque since I was a child. When I visit a steakhouse, I always base my judgment on the quality of their filet mignon. (Of course, this review doesn't include Kobe beef, as that would be an unfair comparison.)

What I adored about the steak was its crispy exterior, perfect seasoning, exceptional tenderness, and remarkable juiciness. It was truly unparalleled. At its price, it's a real bargain compared to places like Cut. 

We also enjoyed oysters, truffled cream corn, truffled asparagus, and a banana dessert, along with some fine wine and a spectacular water show outside, all of which complemented our steak beautifully.

yelp:train:154910.orig: Ok, so you know how family is important to me? Well, if you didn't you do now. We, my niece and I, spent six days total at the Wynn. It was her birthday. We requested (from the concierge) a great table with a view. My partner flew in for the occasion. We were told 9:30 was a good time. We knew to schedule and plan. We showed up at 9:30 ready to go. We were told to wait for a table.  45 minutes later we were ushered to the very back near the kitchen. Do you eat at 10:30? I don't. What would you do? What could I do? How about just be humiliated? Talked to the hotel manager. He said he'd look into it.  Wow,  hotel manager offers Allegro as a compromise. Really?  A walk in bar off the gaming tables at 10:30 at night.  Thanks Steve Wynn, great staff, great experience.
yelp:train:154910.para:
Sure, here's the paraphrased version:

Family means a lot to me, and it was clear to me that it should be important to you too. My niece and I spent six days at the Wynn for her birthday. We asked the concierge for a good table with a view. My partner came in for the celebration. We were told 9:30 was a good time to arrive. We were prepared and arrived on time. However, we were made to wait and eventually seated in the far corner near the kitchen at 10:30. Would you eat at that time? I wouldn't. What could we do? We felt humiliated. We spoke to the hotel manager, who promised to look into it. His solution was to offer Allegro, a bar near the gaming tables, at 10:30 at night. Steve Wynn, your staff and experience are great, but this was a disappointing experience.

yelp:train:154953.orig:
While my friends and I were planning a Vegas trip, we wanted to spare a night for fine dining. After some research we elected SW Steakhouse to be our destination.

Made a reservation 2 weeks beforehand, Saturday evening at 5:30pm. It's located at Wynn hotel ground floor. Not difficult to find this place at all so we got there a bit early. Checked in to make sure the staff knew we were there already, and decided to chill at the bar a bit. I myself got a Mojito and it was pretty good - it was quite strong and I knew this is gonna be a nice dinner.

Got sit in right on time. Once stepped in and looked to the right, there was a large door/window openings and a man made, tall waterfall was there - not sure they did any sound effect but it really sounded like a huge waterfall inside a forrest. Nice environment with the natural light! Now the prime time for food:

-) The Bread: A. What a nice start. There were two different kinds of breads, all garlic based and they were just so good and fresh and couldn't stop eating until my friends asked me to stop and save for the steak. Alight... but man that was good.

-) Mushroom soup: A-. The whole soup was concentrated with chopped mushro
yelp:train:154953.para:
When my friends and I were planning our trip to Vegas, we decided to allocate a night for a fancy dinner. After some research, we chose SW Steakhouse as our destination.

We made a reservation two weeks in advance for Saturday evening at 5:30 PM. The restaurant is located on the ground floor of the Wynn hotel, and it was easy to find. We arrived a bit early and checked in to let the staff know we were there. We spent some time at the bar, where I had a Mojito that was quite strong and tasted great, making me confident it would be a memorable dinner.

We were seated on time. As soon as we entered, we noticed a large door or window opening to the right, with a man-made tall waterfall. It sounded like a real waterfall inside a forest, though no sound effects were used. The natural light made the ambiance very pleasant. Now, for the main event:

- The Bread: A+. It was a fantastic start. There were two types of garlic bread that were so fresh and delicious, I couldn't stop eating until my friends asked me to stop and save some for the steak. It was truly delightful.

- Mushroom Soup: A-. The soup was very concentrated with chopped mushrooms, and it was quite flavorful.

yelp:train:155062.orig:
Summary...overpriced imitation Mexican food located in the MGM grand. 

The good...the table side guac. That was the highlight and very very tasty. The service was also fast and friendly. If the chips served with the guac hadn't been overcooked to slightly burned (you know that burnt chip flavor) this would have been very good. 

The bad...the food was average to poor and everything was overpriced. I've had excellent Mexican food and this falls into the inauthentic imitation gourmet bucket. When you order a combination plate you're receiving three small versions of typical fair. I ordered the ""Diego"" combo plate. The fish taco was ok (pretty salty), the chicken enchilada was AVG at best, and the beef tamale was terrible.

With all the options in Vegas, even at the MGM grand, I would highly advise going somewhere else. You can do better. Really, you can do a lot better.
yelp:train:155062.para:
Summary...overpriced and inauthentic Mexican food at MGM Grand.

The positives...the table-side guacamole was outstanding and very tasty. The service was prompt and courteous. If the chips hadn't been overcooked and slightly burned, this would have been a much better experience.

The negatives...the food quality was mediocre to poor, and everything was overpriced. I've had much better Mexican food, and this fits into the category of imitation gourmet. The "Diego" combo plate included three small, typical dishes. The fish taco was just okay (quite salty), the chicken enchilada was average at best, and the beef tamale was terrible.

Given the numerous dining options in Vegas, even at MGM Grand, I strongly recommend trying somewhere else. There are definitely better choices available.

yelp:train:155192.orig:
*4.5 stars* (because I was hung over the entire weekend)

This is the place that did me in during my bachelorette weekend in Vegas...  why why why did I have to take that last shot???  (OK, my fault but still!)

Hot vibe, expensive drinks, fun times and a fantastic view of Vegas, baby!
yelp:train:155192.para:
*4.5 stars* (due to my hangover the whole weekend)

This spot was the culprit during my bachelorette party in Vegas... why did I have to down that final shot? (Sure, it was my choice, but still!)

It had a hot atmosphere, pricey drinks, great fun, and an amazing view of Vegas, baby!

yelp:train:155386.orig:
My first and favorite Cirque show ever! 

The stage is awesome... i love watching the stage transform back and forth from pool to dry floor. 

Love the stunts, cirque du soleil performaces always amazes me. But This whole water theme just took my breath away. 

I saw this show few years ago and i cannot wait to see it again! There's just way too much stuff going on that I'm sure I have missed out on.  It is definitely a must see show when you're in vegas. And book early!
yelp:train:155386.para:
My all-time favorite Cirque show, and one of the most memorable!

The stage is incredible, with its seamless transformation from a pool to a dry floor. 

I'm in awe of the stunts, but the entire water-themed performance left me speechless. 

I watched this show a few years ago and I'm eager to see it again. There's so much happening that I'm sure I missed some of it the first time around. It's a must-see in Vegas, and I recommend booking tickets well in advance.

yelp:train:155891.orig: It seemed like a good show but we arrived just after it started and our expensive seats were taken. When we got there and picked up the tickets. They didn't say anything about our seats being filled or possibly accidentally taken. When sat they made it seem like it was a big deal and had us sit in partial view spots. Thinking it might be ok, I waited till the end to talk to box office but they said I should have just walked out. The manager of the theater said it was our fault. I have never been treated like just a dollar sign. They just want your money.
yelp:train:155891.para: We thought the show looked promising, but we arrived late and found our pricey seats occupied. Upon picking up our tickets, no mention was made of our seats being taken. When we sat down, they acted as if it was a significant issue, placing us in less-than-ideal viewing spots. Hoping for a resolution, I waited until the end to speak with the box office, but they suggested we should have left. The theater manager blamed us entirely. I've never felt so undervalued; it's clear they only care about the money.

yelp:train:155971.orig: Must visit if you are craving seafood.  had the crab cakes and albacore appetizer that looked so simple but packed some awesome flavor.  will go back and try the seafood tower.
yelp:train:155971.para: If you're in the mood for seafood, this place is a must-visit. I tried the crab cakes and albacore appetizer, which, despite their simplicity, were incredibly flavorful. I plan to return to try the seafood tower.

yelp:train:156046.orig: I don't like writing bad reviews because I don't like the notion of negatively affecting someone's livelihood. On the other hand, however, I wouldn't want someone to waste hard earned money at this place either.  So here goes . . . The food is passable, nothing special and everything was oversalted (and I am a saltaholic), but horribly overpriced, even for Vegas.  I'm no cheapskate and am perfectly willing to pay for quality food and service. But this was offensively priced for what you get. And the waiter's blatant upsell efforts were an affront.  This place isn't even close to being the high-end seafood mecca it bills itself as.  I mean it's edible so if you're stuck without other choices, don't care about wasting money and overall don't care that much, fine.  But if you have limited meals in Vegas, and know food and restaurants, there are literally hundreds of other places I'd rather eat in Vegas. Sorry.  (This is for downstairs.)
yelp:train:156046.para: I hesitate to write a negative review as I don't want to harm someone's business, but I also wouldn't want others to spend their hard-earned money here. So, here we go. The food is just okay, not exceptional, and everything was excessively salty (I love salt). It’s also way overpriced, even for Las Vegas. I’m not a cheapskate and am willing to pay for good food and service, but this place was outrageously priced for the quality. The waiter’s aggressive upselling was particularly offensive. This restaurant is far from the high-end seafood destination it claims to be. If you’re desperate, short on options, and don’t mind spending money, it might be tolerable. But if you have limited dining options in Las Vegas and know your food, there are countless better places to eat. Sorry. (This is for the downstairs location.)

yelp:train:157085.orig: Chicken fettuccine alfredo was delish, tasted very authentic! The service was fast & friendly, we had a large party (10+) and they had no problem accomodating us. No one at my table had any complaints so I guess that's a good thing. I think it was a good all ages / family restaurant...we didn't have kids with us but I saw some in there for those who are curious. I would recommend this place for quality food late at night.
yelp:train:157085.para: The chicken fettuccine alfredo was superb and very authentic-tasting. The service was prompt and friendly, and they easily accommodated our large group of over ten people. Everyone at our table was satisfied, which is a positive sign. I believe it's a suitable restaurant for all ages and families, even though we didn't bring any kids. I'd recommend this place for its quality food, especially if you're looking for a late-night dining option.

yelp:train:157563.orig: The sandwiches here are fine but incredibly plain. Why should I go to a restaurant to have a sandwich that I can make at home?
yelp:train:157563.para: The sandwiches are acceptable, yet very basic. What's the point of dining out when I can prepare a similar sandwich at home?

yelp:train:157875.orig: I always have a good time at Tryst. Although, Tryst is not as big as XS, the employees are nice and the dance floor is spacious. The crowd is always pumped to be there. Great music and people with tables always offer you drinks because everyone is nice there and wants to have a good time!
yelp:train:157875.para: I consistently enjoy my visits to Tryst. While it's not as large as XS, the staff is friendly, and the dance floor is ample. The atmosphere is always energetic and enthusiastic. The music is terrific, and patrons with tables are always willing to buy drinks for others, as everyone there is kind and eager to have a great time.

yelp:train:158422.orig:
This place was really fun. I've never partied off the strip before (well, been to other places). 

We had 17 girls (bachelorette) and so we got in no problem. This place was pretty. It had a outside area and a inside area. 

Ambiance
There was a pole (spinning pole)... I'm not used to a spinning pole but was able to get one spin... But the rest were hard haha. I have a stationary pole so I'm used to spinning on that. So spinning pole at the outside dance floor.

Inside dance area had mini stages for girls to dance on. That was fun. With glowing lights... It was like a stripper joint. But it's not. The music is different inside the club and outside. Outside more hip hop and the inside had more house electronic. 

Drinks
Didn't buy any. Pre partied and I didn't really drink cuz I was sick. 

Location
