At the Rio. The bachelorette party was staying there so very convenient for the drunk girls - and yes we had some. 

Bathroom
Expect lines ladies

Crowd
Very mixed crowd - very little Asians... But everything else was there. We were really the only Asians. 

It wasn't crowded as the other dance places. We actually had room to dance and that's all we wanted to do. So,
yelp:train:158422.para:
This venue was a lot of fun. I hadn't partied outside the strip before, so it was new for me. We had 17 girls for the bachelorette, and we easily got in.

The place was quite pretty, with both an outdoor and an indoor area. 

Ambiance
There was a spinning pole, which I wasn't used to but managed to get one spin on. The rest were challenging, though. I'm more accustomed to a stationary pole, so the spinning pole on the outdoor dance floor was different.

Inside, there were mini stages for the girls to dance on, which was enjoyable. The lighting was glowing and vibrant, making it feel like a strip club, but it wasn't. The music varied: hip hop outside and house electronic inside.

Drinks
I didn't purchase any. I had pre-partied and wasn't drinking because I wasn't feeling well.

Location
It was at the Rio, which was convenient since the bachelorette party was staying there. This made it easy for the girls who got a bit tipsy.

Bathroom
Expect long lines for the ladies.

Crowd
The crowd was diverse, with very few Asians. We were the only Asians there, and the rest of the crowd was well-represented.

It wasn't as crowded as other dance spots, so we had plenty of room to dance, which was all we wanted to do.

yelp:train:158428.orig:
This is probably my most favorite of all Vegas clubs.  The ride to the club is beautiful if you like that whole, glass elevator, see for miles thing.  Once inside you're greeted by a very dim lit room and the sound of music in the distance.  Walk a few more feet and you're at, most importantly, a huge bar with extremely friendly bartenders.  Once you grad you're drink you have to head outside where the view is breath taking.  

Besides getting in for free, the drinks are good and if you're celebrating something special, the bartenders hook it up.

I would go back a million times.
yelp:train:158428.para:
This club in Vegas is undoubtedly my top pick. The journey to the club is stunning, especially with the glass elevator offering panoramic views. Upon entering, you're welcomed by a dimly lit room and the distant sound of music. A few steps further, you'll find a massive bar with incredibly friendly bartenders. After getting your drink, you need to step outside, where the view is breathtaking. 

Not only does entry cost nothing, but the drinks are of good quality. If you're celebrating a special occasion, the bartenders go above and beyond. I'd love to return countless times.

yelp:train:158756.orig: Oh Shady Grove you have improved! Or maybe it's the fact that I'm getting old and hit you up for the early bird special (compared to late night service). Either way the pizza is amazing (try the new shrimp option) and service was on point.
yelp:train:158756.para: Shady Grove, you've really stepped up your game! Or perhaps it's just that I'm getting older and prefer the early bird special over late-night dining. Regardless, the pizza is outstanding (especially the new shrimp option), and the service was top-notch.

yelp:train:158985.orig: Went down to Hogs n Heifers last night on our bikes to meet several friends. Used to be bike friendly parking. Not anymore. Our plan was to sit outside and eat at Triple George's (closes at 10pm) and socialize (includes drinks which are normally purchased from H&H in 'go cups').  The H&H security team swooped down on us and advised us that since it wasn't our intention to go in to H&H and spend our time there - we couldn't park in front of their bar and ran us off!  Fortunately - I went in to Triple George's and received permission from them to park the bikes in their Valet section. Now THAT was service!  Hogs n Heifers can say goodbye to my patronage. PS - I'd prefer to give them  'no star' rating.
yelp:train:158985.para: Last night, we rode our bikes to Hogs n Heifers to meet up with friends. We used to be able to park there easily, but that's no longer the case. Our intention was to dine at Triple George's (which closes at 10pm) and socialize, including getting drinks from H&H in 'go cups.' However, H&H's security team approached us and told us that since we weren't planning to enter their establishment, we couldn't park in front of their bar and they escorted us away! Thankfully, I was able to park at Triple George's valet area, where I received permission to leave our bikes. That was excellent service! Hogs n Heifers can expect to lose my business. PS - I would give them a zero-star rating if possible.

yelp:train:159769.orig: We love mama mia's pizza. LOVE it. It's just unfortunate that they can't figure out whether they deliver to is. We have ordered at least six times (we've only been here for two months) and we either a) get a delicious pizza and antipasto salad in minimal time, b) get the pizza and get told we're lucky to get a pizza delivered. I literally asked him, \""should I order from someone else?\"" Or c) take our chances by attempting to order, only to be told, \""nope. Sorry. We don't deliver to your area.\""  So sad. I would love to stay local, but I am done \""hoping\"" to get pizza.
yelp:train:159769.para: We adore Mama Mia's pizza; we truly love it. However, it's frustrating that they haven't sorted out their delivery issues. In the six times we've ordered (we've only been here for two months), we've experienced three scenarios: a) receiving a tasty pizza and antipasto salad quickly, b) getting the pizza but being informed we're fortunate to have it delivered, or c) attempting to order and being told they don't deliver to our area. This is so disappointing. I wish to remain local, but I'm tired of hoping for pizza delivery.

yelp:train:159824.orig:
Solid pizza and my favorite in Phoenix by a landslide.

Last night went for a work dinner and showed a few newbie Patsy eaters what real pizza should taste like. 

We had two pies one pesto and one regular and both were simply amazing like always.  I recommend always adding sun dried tomatoes to a pie it really adds to the sauce.  

This location is great as well especially now with the holiday season they have lights up everywhere and it's just a nice experience.
yelp:train:159824.para:
My absolute favorite pizza place in Phoenix, and the solid pizza was outstanding last night.

For a work dinner, I introduced a few new Patsy's pizza enthusiasts to the true taste of pizza. We ordered one pesto and one regular pie, both of which were simply incredible, as they always are.

I highly recommend adding sun-dried tomatoes to your pizza; it enhances the sauce significantly. 

The location is fantastic, particularly during the holiday season when it's adorned with lights, making for a delightful experience.

yelp:train:159836.orig: Be forewarned:  the food is alright but this place is like freaking  Romper Room with spoiled North Scottsdale brats running the joint!  It is really no better then the McDonalds kiddie jungle gym with one exception... I have never found a dirty diaper tucked into the corner here.
yelp:train:159836.para: Be prepared: the food is just okay, but this establishment feels more like a chaotic playroom with spoiled kids from North Scottsdale in charge! It's not much better than a McDonald's playground, except for one thing—I've never come across a dirty diaper hidden in the corner here.

yelp:train:160323.orig: RUDE staff!  We accidentally left something behind on our table an tried to go back in to get it, but the doors were locked because they had just closed.  The bartender refused to let us in, refused to look for it himself, and instructed the rest of the staff to ignore us.  How rude!!  Will never go here again.
yelp:train:160323.para: The staff was extremely rude. We mistakenly left an item on our table and attempted to return to retrieve it, only to find the doors locked as they were closing. The bartender wouldn't let us in, wouldn't search for the item himself, and told the other staff to ignore us. This was very discourteous, and I won't be returning to this establishment.

yelp:train:160362.orig: Second time here, and this one was for breakfast. Everything seems to be about alcohol, so we tried a mango margarita, and it was great. Can't say that about the breakfast selection. I wasn't impressed, but of course, will be back. The atmosphere\nis great and so is the gift shop.
yelp:train:160362.para: On my second visit, I came for breakfast this time. The place is clearly focused on alcohol, as that's the main offering, so we decided to try a mango margarita, which was excellent. However, I found the breakfast options lacking. While I wasn't satisfied, I plan to return. The ambiance is fantastic, and the gift shop is also top-notch.

yelp:train:160562.orig: This is by far the best club in Old Town Scottsdale, babes everywhere who are totally willing to rub up on your junk while the DJs spin the dopest shiz around! I love how I can get crunk with some Hip-Hop on one side of the club then find Molly and House out on the other.
yelp:train:160562.para: This club in Old Town Scottsdale stands out as the best, with plenty of receptive people who enjoy giving attention to guests while the DJs play top-notch music. I appreciate that I can dance to hip-hop on one side and then switch to Molly and House music on the other.

yelp:train:160600.orig: This is my first YELP review, but I felt motivated to do it for this place. WOW! The very best mole I've ever had. And the fish dish (pescado a la versceruzana) was outstanding. This just wasn't the best Mexican food I've had in a while, but the best meal I've had in quite some time. Don't miss it! The atmosphere is great, staff very friendly and even a wonderful guitar player.
yelp:train:160600.para: This marks my first YELP review, yet I felt compelled to share my experience here. Wow! This is the finest mole I've ever tasted. The fish dish (pescado a la veracruzana) was also exceptional. This meal was not just one of the best Mexican dishes I've enjoyed recently, but the best meal I've had in a long time. You shouldn't miss it! The ambiance is fantastic, the staff is very friendly, and there's even a wonderful guitar player.

yelp:train:160928.orig: The sushi was good, the service absolutely sucked!  2 of us did all you can eat.  Ordered two rolls and two nigiri, first round took 20 minutes plus to get to us.  2nd round took even longer!  Will not return.
yelp:train:160928.para: The sushi was enjoyable, but the service was terrible. My partner and I opted for all-you-can-eat. We ordered two rolls and two nigiri, but the first batch arrived after 20 minutes, and the second batch took even longer! I won't be going back.

yelp:train:161544.orig:
Overall, not that impressed. I've only been to one other buffet before, at the Bellagio, and I prefer that one over the Wynn. We went on a Tuesday night, after a long day of hiking at Zion National Park, so we were starving. To be honest, I didn't feel like the buffet was that big. I went back 2 times for a heaping of crab legs & shrimp cocktail, which are the only foods I really enjoyed there. They have some dim sum like dumplings and such at the Chinese food station, which was awful. Most of their cooked fishes were overcooked and not impressive. Their cheese ravioli in their pasta section was good, as was their miso soup.

They have a huge dessert section, but to be honest, none of the desserts really impressed me. One of my dining companions loved their coffee ice cream, as he is a big fan of coffee and it tastes very very strongly of coffee.

I would not go to their dinner buffet again. Also, it is very pricy, comes to about $37 with tax per person. A friend of mine said their breakfast buffet was great though, and only $25, so would be willing to try that sometime.
yelp:train:161544.para:
In general, I wasn't particularly impressed. The last buffet I visited was at the Bellagio, and I preferred that over the Wynn's. We dined on a Tuesday evening, feeling quite hungry after a day of hiking at Zion National Park. To be honest, I didn't find the buffet to be very extensive. I returned twice for the crab legs and shrimp cocktail, which were the only items I really enjoyed. The Chinese food station had some dim sum, like dumplings, which were terrible. Most of the cooked fish were overcooked and not very appealing. The cheese ravioli and miso soup from the pasta section were decent.

There was a large dessert selection, but none of the desserts really stood out to me. One of my dining companions really liked the coffee ice cream, as he is a big coffee fan and it had a very strong coffee flavor.

I wouldn't return to this dinner buffet again. Additionally, it's quite expensive, costing around $37 per person including tax. A friend mentioned that their breakfast buffet is excellent and only $25, so I might give that a try sometime.

yelp:train:161548.orig:
Yes, yes, and yes. 

I am still thinking about the smoked salmon salad and the roast turkey. I have not had tiramisu like that in...hmm.. EVER. The crab legs are served chilled and I prefer them room temp. But I don't mind putting those aside while I take a taste of everthing else. 

Definitely worth the money and the 20-30 minute wait. 

My only regret is that I did not hire a babysitter because my toddler did not have the patience for us to completely bust ourselves open.
yelp:train:161548.para:
Absolutely, yes, and yes. 

I keep thinking about the smoked salmon salad and the roast turkey. I haven't tasted tiramisu like that in... hmm... forever. The crab legs are served cold, but I prefer them at room temperature. Still, I can set those aside to savor the rest of the dishes.

It was definitely worth the price and the 20-30 minute wait.

My sole regret is that I didn't hire a babysitter, as my toddler couldn't sit still long enough for us to fully enjoy the meal.

yelp:train:161706.orig:
I could see why everyone raves about this place as the one of the best buffets in Vegas. 
The decor is beautiful and there seems to be almost everything you can imagine to eat.  
I'll be honest, I ate so much that I don't remember what tasted like what.

The King Crab Legs were a favorite for everyone there.  They just kept on refilling it too.

There are so many entrees, but don't forget about the dessert.  I really loved their cream puffs.  I'm saving more room for dessert next time.
yelp:train:161706.para:
This establishment is undoubtedly one of the top buffets in Vegas, and I can understand why it's so highly praised. The ambiance is stunning, and the food selection is incredibly diverse, offering virtually everything you could desire. To be frank, I consumed so much that I can't recall the flavors of each dish.

The King Crab Legs were a hit with everyone, and they kept replenishing the serving. There's a wide array of main courses, but do not overlook the desserts; I particularly enjoyed the cream puffs. I plan to make room for more sweets next time.

yelp:train:161741.orig:
Got to admit, I dont understand why people RAVE about this place. At a price at 36.99 it is MUCH more expensive than Bellagio ($10). My question for Steve Wynn himself is why?

One of the misses already is that you dont have King crab, Bellagio does.
You guys have food that is mediocre at best. There was not a single thing that was great, just decent.

One plus is that the dessert hall was quite cool. Trees and such and candied apples is cool, but very hard and bad for your teeth.

Tip: Bellagio is way better.
yelp:train:161741.para:
I must admit, I don't get the enthusiasm surrounding this place. At $36.99, it's significantly pricier than Bellagio ($10). I wonder, Steve Wynn, why?

One downside is that they lack King crab, which Bellagio offers.

The food quality is at best mediocre; nothing stood out as exceptional, just average.

The dessert hall was a highlight, with its tree-like decorations and candied apples, though they were quite hard and not great for your teeth.

Tip: Bellagio is clearly the superior choice.

yelp:train:161941.orig:
Definitely not worth the price. Yes there were tons of choices but what buffet doesn't have variety. Question is...do they deliver? And deliver they didn't!
Oh Mr Wynn...where oh where did the quality go here?  please get rid of that awful waffle-battered fried chicken and what is up with the purple colored prime rib?  The prime rib should be the showstopper for most buffets, but The Buffet got it all wrong. Crab legs looked plentiful from afar but once you get up to the station for your pickings, there's nothing but slim pickings.  And I see steamed is not an option huh - for the price we pay?!?
And please teach your service folks to do other things and not just stand 4 feet away along the wall watching diners' every move - it was so awkward having her walk up to our table right when we place our utensils down - dang lady, give us some space to breath or something...get more drinks, don't ask if we would like another drink...who only needs one drink during a buffet dinner???  If the glass is empty, fill it up!
Head over to PH, Cosmo, MGM or The M Resort - neither of those have ever disappointed.
After such a failure at Bellagio buffet and now Wynn buffet - I've lost all faith
yelp:train:161941.para:
Clearly, it's not a worthwhile experience for the cost. While there are many options, which is common in most buffets, the real question is: do they deliver on quality? And the answer is no—they definitely do not. 

Oh Wynn, where has the quality gone? Please remove that terrible waffle-battered fried chicken. What’s with the oddly colored prime rib? It should be the highlight of any buffet, but The Buffet missed the mark. The crab legs seemed abundant from a distance, but upon closer inspection, there were very few to choose from. And steaming options? Not an option? That’s unacceptable for the price!

Also, train your staff to be more helpful rather than just standing four feet away by the wall, watching every move. It was awkward when she approached our table right after we put down our utensils. Give us some space to enjoy our meal. If we need more drinks, we’ll ask for them ourselves; who needs more than one drink during a buffet dinner?

Instead, head to PH, Cosmo, MGM, or The M Resort—they’ve never let us down.

After such disappointing experiences at both Bellagio and Wynn buffets, I’ve lost all faith.

yelp:train:161985.orig: The lunch buffet is not worth the money! I had pretty high expectations but they definitely were not met. My favorite part of casino buffets is the seafood, however I was so disappointed that they didn't have any shrimp, or crab legs and the sushi was a very limited selection. Last time I was in Vegas I went to the Bellagio buffet and that was amazing so if you have a choice, go for Bellagio.
yelp:train:161985.para: I found the lunch buffet to be overpriced and fell short of my expectations. My top choice at casino buffets is the seafood, but this one lacked shrimp and crab legs, and the sushi options were quite limited. On my previous visit to Vegas, the Bellagio buffet was outstanding, so if you have the option, I recommend trying that instead.

yelp:train:162004.orig:
We got very lucky with the wait as there were only a handful of people in front if us.

The atmosphere was whimsical. It's beautifully decorated with flowers and bright colors, really stunning. I wish we were sat in that center area with all the flowers but it's okay maybe next time.

I actually thought there would be a bit more to choose from but of the items I did try were quite good. I had the prime rib, sausage, lime corn, potatoes and a few other items that were quite tasty. I also tried the crab legs. I had wished they were freshly steamed and hot like at Caesars Bacchanal Buffet. I thought they were...ok but not great.

The desserts were also really good. There was alot to choose from and everything we tasted was delicious. 

We would likely go back as it was pretty good. I just wish, being that it's The Wynn, there was a bit more to choose from, and that their crab legs were served hot instead of on ice.
yelp:train:162004.para:
We were fortunate to have a short wait since there were just a few people ahead of us.

The ambiance was charming, with lovely floral decorations and vibrant colors that were truly impressive. While I preferred the central seating area with all the flowers, it was still acceptable, and I hope to try it next time.

I expected a wider selection, but the dishes I sampled were quite enjoyable. I had the prime rib, sausage, lime corn, and a few other items that were quite delicious. The crab legs, however, were a bit underwhelming; I wished they were freshly steamed and hot like at Caesars Bacchanal Buffet. They were okay but not exceptional.

The desserts were also very good, with a wide variety to choose from, and everything we tried was delightful.

We might return as it was a pleasant experience, but I do wish there was a greater variety given the prestige of The Wynn, and that the crab legs were served hot instead of on ice.

yelp:train:162435.orig:
Mediocre. Overpriced. Rude.

If you read those three words and still need to know the details, here you go: 

1) I guess me and my two buddies were just too embarrassing for a Sunday morning - we got shunted off into a weird pseudo-private room that felt like a cage (bars on the windows) where you could hear the constant binging of slot machines.

2) I ordered a drink with no ice.  So they watered it down.  

3) The food was just ordinary.  

4) The staff was annoying - repeatedly trying to take out dishes away before we were done.  My friend was half-done his meal and went to the bathroom; the waitress actually tried to take his food - instead of classily folding his napkin and just chilling the fuck out.
yelp:train:162435.para:
Poor quality. Expensive. Unfriendly.

To clarify further, here are the details:

1) On a Sunday morning, my three friends and I were seated in a peculiar, almost private area that resembled a cage (with bars on the windows), where we could hear the constant noise from slot machines.

2) I requested a drink without ice, but it was served diluted.

3) The food was merely average.

4) The service was irritating, with staff repeatedly trying to clear our dishes before we were finished eating. When my friend went to the bathroom and was still halfway through his meal, the waitress attempted to remove his plate, instead of politely folding his napkin and waiting patiently.

yelp:train:162840.orig:
Located on the back side of the Wynn, overlooking the golf course and a massive waterfall, I don't think I fell for Steve Wynn's hotel video hype about feeling like you're in the Carolinas. I was treated to an exceptional meal that was beautifully prepared and well served.  They don't have a menu for children but they were more than happy to split a plate for my kids.

They have a Kobe beef carpaccio infused with a garlic truffle oil on the appetizer menu that is truly remarkable. ($21.00)

Yes, prices are on the high side, like all Wynn restaurants, with the chicken, my steakhouse bellwether at about $38.00.  Sides run about $8.00 average.

The restaurant is just a part of the hotel, not located away in some remote golf building. Just pass the slots and head out to the other end of the building and you're there.
yelp:train:162840.para:
Situated behind the Wynn, with a view of the golf course and a large waterfall, I didn't quite buy into Steve Wynn's hotel promotional video about the Carolinas vibe. However, the dining experience was outstanding, with dishes that were expertly prepared and served. While there's no kids' menu, they happily accommodated my children by splitting a plate.

One standout appetizer is the Kobe beef carpaccio, infused with garlic truffle oil, priced at $21.00.

Prices are on the higher side, typical of Wynn's restaurants, with a steak at the local steakhouse benchmark costing around $38.00. Side dishes average about $8.00.

The restaurant is part of the hotel, not far from the main area. Just walk past the slot machines and continue to the far end of the building to find it.

yelp:train:163031.orig: I think the show is entertaining, eccentric, funny, and odd all rolled into one. It has a bit of comedy, some excellent music, some silly jokes and some bright paint. My favorite part was the lights featuring the \""Cowboys\"". If you go to the show, you'll know what I'm talking about. Toilet paper is also a part of the show. I won't tell you how :-) You will have to go and experience it for yourself. Honestly, I liked it okay. But my kids and husband absolutely LOVED it! It's worth it to go just once and try it out. You never know!
yelp:train:163031.para: I find the show to be a delightful mix of entertainment, quirkiness, humor, and peculiarity. It includes some comedy, fantastic music, amusing jokes, and vibrant colors. My favorite element was the lighting design featuring the "Cowboys." If you attend the show, you'll understand why. There's also toilet paper as part of the performance, but I won't reveal how it's used. Truly, I enjoyed it moderately, but my children and husband adored it! It's definitely worth seeing at least once to experience it firsthand. You might be surprised!

yelp:train:163570.orig:
UPDATE 5/1/14:  I see where someone from Hilton made a response to my post but interesting enough, no one was able to give me any feedback or a return call on the investigation into my missing item when I called their insurance provider (Sedwick) and emailed their lost prevention person (Caleb R).  I finally got a generic letter in the mail today basically saying SCREW YOU--NOT OUR PROBLEM.  So much for good Hilton Honors Customer Service - NOT!!!!  Needless to say once I replace the laptop I will be seeking to invest/purchase timeshare property with another organization and NOT Hilton!!!  I thought the LVH (formerly Las Vegas Hilton) was the only bad seed int he bunch but now I think the entire chain is corrupt.



This review is regarding the housekeeping staff.....  BEWARE-- they are thieves. Laptop was left in room upon checkout but when I called the security/lost & found department there was no record of the cleaning crew turning it in -- which is standard procedure at any business.  Nice rooms but be  careful of your valuables being left out.
yelp:train:163570.para: UPDATE 5/1/14: A Hilton representative responded to my post, yet no one addressed my missing item during the investigation with their insurance provider (Sedwick) or the lost prevention contact (Caleb R). Today, I received a generic letter essentially stating that they are not responsible. This is far from the excellent Hilton Honors customer service I expected - NOT! Consequently, after replacing my laptop, I will look for other options for timeshare properties and definitely not Hilton. I believed the LVH was the worst, but now I suspect the entire chain has issues. This review focuses on the housekeeping staff... BEWARE—they are thieves. I left my laptop in my room after checkout, but the security/lost & found department had no record of it being turned in, which is standard practice. The rooms are nice, but be cautious with your valuables.

yelp:train:163685.orig: This was the most romantic place i have ever been. It came with delicious food and great view of the bellagio fountain show. I was sad that i wasnt able to have a professional photo of us taken by their photographer that goes around, but ill be sure to hang on to her next time. Maybe next time we could sit outside in the summer so we can have the full romantic experience with the water show and scenery of Paris!! Overall, we had a wonderful and unforgettable dinner here. I will definitely be back.
yelp:train:163685.para: This was the most romantic spot I've ever visited, complete with delectable cuisine and a stunning view of the Bellagio fountain display. While I was disappointed not to have a professional photo taken by their photographer, I'll make sure to catch her next time. Perhaps on our next visit, we can enjoy the full romantic experience by sitting outside during the summer, when we can watch the water show and admire the Parisian scenery! In summary, we had an incredible and unforgettable dinner here, and I look forward to returning.

yelp:train:163917.orig:
ok, i arrived at 11:15p on a Saturday night and the line was about 20 deep, mostly with dudes with the obligatory seven year old fad of untucked dress shirt, 3 front buttons open, and cuffs flared with some kind of TJMaxx jeans and pleather shoes.  But there was some ass in line that made me wish I could bag a 21 year old.  Since my posse was inside, I played the older dude knowing even older people inside da club and thus got waved by all the young twats & rots yearning to go into the PCL as if it was fockin' OZ.  Mind you, I was with a hot piece who was my friend so my review is not jaded by the ""ah fuck it's 2:05a and I'm going home to beat my drunken ass off by myself AGAIN"".

+++'s:
nice ass for us guys; big pecs for you ladies; stiff drinks from the bartenders who were mildly attentive; latest hip-pop mixes

- - -'s:
all those rice bag carrying meat heads that stand in the VIP area thinking that if they have an Ed Hardy tee and a fedora on and occasionally raising their non-needed in this Darwinian age big biceped arms in the air, that they will get some candy to come up and grind on their nub.  fortunately, and not surprisingly, a fight broke out and about a half d
yelp:train:163917.para:
I got there at 11:15 PM on a Saturday night, and the line was around 20 people long, mostly guys sporting the trendy untucked shirt with three buttons open and flared cuffs, paired with TJMaxx jeans and pleather shoes. However, there were a few attractive individuals in line that made me wish I was 21. Since my friends were already inside, I pretended to be older, and the young, eager club-goers let me in without much hassle. I was with a hot friend, so my opinion isn't clouded by the "ah, fuck, it's 2:05 AM and I'm going home alone again" sentiment.

+++'s:
- Nice ass for guys
- Big pecs for girls
- Strong drinks from attentive bartenders
- Latest hip-hop music

- - -'s:

yelp:train:163966.orig:
My buddies and I decided to eat here while all of us suffered from hangovers.  The delicious food here will restore your apetite from whatever came back out from the previous night.  The family style is a great way to enjoy the meal.  They provide a lot of food for their prices.

We started with the potato soup which relly jump started my apetite.  It's rich, creamy, and flavorful.  Next up was the Beef Braciole.  This dish was quite interesting.  The texture was weird yet it was edible (may have been my hangover dulling my senses).  I can't quite remember the name of the next dish, but it was a spicy spaghetti and meat balls, I believe.  The spiciness brought back all my senses and pretty much kicked me out of my intoxicated state.  You can never go wrong with spaghetti and meatballs.  We also had the Rigatoni ""D"".  The chicken was tender and the protein gave me energy for more partying.  

They gave us enough food to take back to the hotel and have for dinner.  If you love Italian food and pastas, this place would be a place to stop by.
yelp:train:163966.para:
My friends and I chose to dine here when we were all dealing with hangovers. The tasty food here can help you regain your appetite after whatever you might have thrown up the night before. The family-style service makes for a great dining experience. They offer a generous amount of food for the prices.

We began with the potato soup, which really sparked my appetite. It was rich, creamy, and full of flavor. Next was the Beef Braciole, an intriguing dish with a texture that was somewhat unusual but still palatable (perhaps my hangover dulled my taste buds). I can't recall the name of the next dish, but it was likely spicy spaghetti with meatballs. The spiciness brought me back to my senses and practically ended my hangover. Spaghetti and meatballs are always a safe bet. We also had the Rigatoni "D," which featured tender chicken that gave me the energy to keep partying.

They provided enough food to take back to our hotel for a second meal. If you enjoy Italian cuisine and pasta, this place is definitely worth a visit.

yelp:train:164245.orig: Looked alot like a restaurant chain called \""China Buffet\"" with lots and lots of fried food. Majority of selections were greasy, oily and unhealthy. There is absolutely no comparison between this one and the Wynn buffet or the Bellagio buffet where you find quality salads and delicious sea foods. The desserts were totally uncreative, regular apple pies that you can get everywhere. The seating area was just like a food court in a mall. No luxury or class whatsoever. 1 star is good enough.
yelp:train:164245.para: It resembled a restaurant chain named "China Buffet," featuring an abundance of fried foods. The majority of the options were greasy, oily, and unhealthy. In comparison to the Wynn or Bellagio buffets, which offer quality salads and delicious seafood, this place falls far short. The desserts were unoriginal, just typical apple pies available elsewhere. The seating area was similar to a mall food court, lacking any luxury or class. A rating of one star is generous enough.

yelp:train:164485.orig:
Before Bacchanal,  Before Wicked Spoon, Before the Buffet at the Bellagio, Before everyone else got on the bandwagon, This buffet started it all
Buffet Stations, each serving a different cuisine. What a great concept. 

I can remember when this was the ""It"" or should I say the ""Must Eat"" buffet in Las Vegas. But alas, It's old, the ambiance is not as vibrant, the food quality and presentation has been surpassed by the restaurant I mentioned above and more, but the Carnaval Buffet still has its mojo. 

I've always enjoyed the Chinese station here. Dim sum, BBQ pork, steam buns & pork and preserved egg congee. I always get the same things. Yum!

Pricing is in line with other buffer. 

Tip: look into the 24 hour pricing. The lady at the register told us it is good for all Caesars casino group for a 24 hour period. Buffet feast for 24 hours? my stomach might not be able to handle that.  Lol. 

Everything was good. The only thing is, Las Vegas is into Great things, newer and better buffets. It might not be as good as the glory days, but it holds its own as far as I'm concern.
yelp:train:164485.para:
Before Bacchanal, Wicked Spoon, or the Bellagio buffet gained popularity, this particular buffet was the pioneer. It featured diverse buffet stations, each offering unique cuisines, a concept that was groundbreaking at the time.

I recall when this buffet was the "must-try" option in Las Vegas. However, it has aged, and the ambiance and food quality have been outshone by newer establishments. Yet, the Carnaval Buffet still retains its charm.

I particularly enjoy the Chinese station, which includes dim sum, BBQ pork, steamed buns, and preserved egg congee. I consistently order the same items, and they are delicious.

The pricing is comparable to other buffets in the area. 

A tip: the 24-hour pricing option is available for all Caesars casino guests. While the idea of a 24-hour feast sounds tempting, my stomach might struggle with that. 

Overall, everything was good. While Las Vegas now offers newer and better buffets, this one still stands strong in my opinion.

yelp:train:164523.orig: I ordered the steak omelet...When my order arrived it had no steak...Then I had the waitress take it back...She gave me a new order that had steak on it...but then the egg wasn't cooked all the way...and I mean it was almost raw. I sent it back for the third time and finally got the right order.
yelp:train:164523.para: I placed an order for a steak omelet, but when it came, there was no steak in it. So, I asked the waitress to take it back. She gave me a new order with steak, but the eggs weren't fully cooked; they were almost raw. I had to send it back a third time before I received the correct order.

yelp:train:164775.orig: Use to come here all the time! What happened? Very rude staff. Sat inside dust all over every where lamps etc. food does not carry the same quality! Sad to experience this... NEVER COMING BACK!!!!!
yelp:train:164775.para: I used to visit here frequently, but now I'm very disappointed. The staff were extremely rude, and the place was covered in dust everywhere—on the lamps and more. The food quality has dropped significantly! I'm really sad about this experience... I WILL NEVER RETURN!!!!!

yelp:train:165163.orig:
The menu is pretty lameski if you don't go in for a lot of meat.  Here's my problem with Matt's: if you order the cheese omelet and have their paltry selection of veggies added to it, you're paying more than you would for a meat omelet.  That's pretty stupid; meat costs more than vegetables, and is a bigger deal to store and prep.  How hard is it to offer a reasonable vegetarian option?  

I've eaten there twice for breakfast and lunch, and quality each time was middling.  The hashbrowns were not good, really slimy and squishy on the inside.  

Not worth the wait.
yelp:train:165163.para:
If you're not a big meat eater, the menu at Matt's is rather disappointing. My main issue is that the cheese omelet, with its limited vegetable options, costs more than a meat omelet. This doesn't make sense, as meat is more expensive and requires more effort to prepare and store. Why can't they offer a decent vegetarian option?

I've dined there twice, once for breakfast and once for lunch, and the quality was mediocre both times. The hashbrowns were particularly poor, being overly slimy and squishy inside. It’s not worth the wait.

yelp:train:166358.orig: I'm  not a big Vegas guy, but I do enjoy the buffets there. I used to think that the buffet at The Rio was the best, and it would still be but in my humble opinion, it has been eclipsed by Le Village at Paris LV. The food stations are arraigned by the provinces of France. They have the Burgundy station with foods representative of what is prepared in Burgundy. There is also a Provence station, a Normandy station and a Alsace-Lorraine station. Being my mother's mother's family is from Alsace-Lorraine, I am immensely interested in what they have to serve. True it's a bit pricy, but if you wanted to take a gastronomic tour of France, it would cost you a hell of a lot more than the 28 bucks, or whatever they charge these days.
yelp:train:166358.para: While I'm not particularly fond of Vegas in general, I do appreciate its buffets. I used to consider The Rio's buffet the top choice, but in my view, it has been surpassed by Le Village at Paris LV. The food stations at Le Village are organized by French provinces; they have a Burgundy station, a Provence station, a Normandy station, and an Alsace-Lorraine station. Given that my maternal grandmother's family is from Alsace-Lorraine, I'm particularly keen on what they serve there. Although it's a bit pricey, if you want to experience a culinary journey through France, it's far more affordable than doing so individually, which would likely cost much more than the current price of $28.

yelp:train:166448.orig:
Nothing special. I waited in a line for 30 mins for the much appraised crepes line. I got two different kinds the berry one and the banana nutella one. I enjoyed the nutella one more than the berry only because the berry one was way too sweet. 

We made it in at the end of breakfast going into lunch so we got to eat both! eggs were bad............bacon was ok........i liked some of the pastas they had for lunch...the scallopped potatoes were ok...the desserts were not too shabby, some chic was trying to call this cheesecake square...""flan""...i wanted to say something but i held my breath and walked away shaking my head.

this buffet was ok. the line was long too. if youre in vegas there are always lines at every buffet...

My husband and I were not impressed with any of the buffets, reading reviews online and recommendations....did not help. maybe we have high expectations? Don't know, if we knew we would of just spent all that money on a high end place and gotten one meal...at least we would of known it was ONE excellent one.
yelp:train:166448.para:
Not much to write home about. We stood in a queue for 30 minutes for the popular crepe line. I tried both the berry and banana-nutella varieties. I preferred the nutella one, as the berry one was excessively sweet.

We managed to grab some food as the breakfast transitioned into lunch. The eggs were subpar, the bacon was just okay, and I enjoyed some of the lunchtime pastas. The scalloped potatoes were decent, and the desserts, though not outstanding, were still acceptable. One of the desserts was labeled as a cheesecake square but tasted more like flan. I considered voicing my opinion but decided against it, shaking my head as I walked away.

Overall, the buffet was mediocre, and the lines were long. In Vegas, it's common for buffets to have lines, so it wasn't a surprise.

My husband and I were unimpressed with the buffets, despite reading positive reviews and recommendations beforehand. Perhaps we had higher expectations. Either way, we felt it would have been better to spend our money on a high-end restaurant for a single meal that would have been excellent.

yelp:train:166458.orig: Big disappointment.  Was seated in a broken down area of the buffet section by hostess.  Ceiling was peeling.  Quality of food was not as expected.  Very poor. Not worth it.  No bang for your buck.
yelp:train:166458.para: A significant letdown. The hostess seated me in a deteriorated part of the buffet area. The ceiling was flaking off. The food quality fell short of expectations. It was very subpar and not worth the price. Essentially, there was no value for the money spent.

yelp:train:167275.orig: Very tasty. Clean and fast. I ate too much. Only cause I had half of my wife's dinner.  Pot stickers are a very good starter.
yelp:train:167275.para: It was very delicious, and the place was neat and served quickly. I ended up eating a lot, mostly because I had half of my wife's meal. The pot stickers make for a great starter.

yelp:train:167598.orig:
We have been here for breakfast and dinner (x2).  Who your server team is makes a difference!  Alfredo was excellent. His team was attentive and on the spot for service. I forget my breakfast team but she was amazing.  

For our second dinner, Rey and Wilson seemed distracted and overworked! I suspect they are good, however we felt ignored and our plates stayed on our table way to long after we were done. Rey seems nice and tried to make up for it, however a little to late.  Food took way to long!

Food was good, make sure they know that you want your meat medium rare not medium.

Cheesecake came with the special... Delicious!
yelp:train:167598.para:
We've visited for breakfast, dinner (twice), and the quality of the server team really matters. Alfredo and his team were outstanding—attentive and responsive. I can't recall the names of our breakfast servers, but they were fantastic.

On our second dinner, Rey and Wilson seemed overwhelmed and not fully present. I believe they are capable, but we felt neglected, and our dishes lingered on the table long after we finished eating. Rey tried to compensate, but it was too late. The food took a very long time to arrive.

The food was good, but make sure to specify if you want your meat cooked medium rare. The cheesecake that came with the special was delicious!

yelp:train:167650.orig: This buffet was very disappointing. I would have gave it 1 star if I payed full price for it. No wonder they were offering it for $6.99 with Sahara Player's Card, which by the way is free to sign up if you think the reviews here are wrong.\n\nI seriously think Hometown Buffet is better. What stood out here was they had flavored water on their choices of fountain drinks. The Pasta and pizza station was ok. Several different pizzas rotating every so often. Usual pasta selections that you would expect/see from a buffet like Hometown or any other big chain buffet. The main entries they had on a Tuesday dinner was nothing special. Rice pilaf, Beef Goulash, chicken, squash and zucchini, friend calamari, some other items that didn't look too appealing to be quite honest. Carving station consisted of ham, turkey, and prime rib. The prime rib was WAY too rare for me. But I believe some people like that. I mean the juices were straight red. along with most of the cut I had. I went for another try, and same thing. They had a Chinese and Mexican station. Make your own taco, if you saw the one at Sizzler, its almost identical. The Chinese station had your sweet and sour chicken, Veggie chow mie
yelp:train:167650.para:
This buffet was quite disappointing, and I might have rated it just one star if I had paid the full price. That's why they were offering it for $6.99 with a Sahara Player's Card, which is free to sign up for, by the way. I actually think Hometown Buffet is better.

The standout feature was the flavored water in their fountain drinks. The pasta and pizza station was decent, with several rotating pizzas and usual pasta options. The main dishes on Tuesday evening weren't particularly impressive—items like rice pilaf, beef goulash, chicken, squash, and zucchini, along with fried calamari, which didn't look very appealing to me. The carving station had ham, turkey, and prime rib, but the prime rib was way too rare for my taste; the juices were almost entirely red. I tried again, and it was the same. They also had Chinese and Mexican stations, with customizable tacos similar to what you'd find at Sizzler. The Chinese station offered sweet and sour chicken and veggie chow mein.

yelp:train:167877.orig:
Place has a nice ambiance, a nice feel to it. I liked the jars of ingredients and its calm, hip tone to the restaurant. Fresh from playing cards from Caesars, my buddies wanted some asian noodles in the bellagio. The wait to get in was about 20-30mins. I wasn't pissed at line to get in (other people in the line were, especially a group of trekkies?) 

I mean its Vegas and gamblers have to eat sometime? 

So, we sat down ordered and I decided to go with some spicy chicken noodle dish. It was quite hot and spicy when I tasted it. It took a total of 5 mins for them to muster it up. I was shocked at the cooking times of this noodle joint and I think I knew why.... Because 10mins after my meal, I could not hold it down. I spent prolly the next hour in the casino's well maintained bathrooms. I was hurling my brains out and spewing chunks. 

This was one of the worst food experiences.
yelp:train:167877.para:
The place exuded a pleasant atmosphere and a relaxed, trendy vibe. After playing cards at Caesars, my friends and I decided on some Asian noodles at Bellagio. We faced a wait of around 20 to 30 minutes, but I wasn't upset about it. Others in line, particularly a group of Star Trek fans, seemed more agitated.

In Vegas, gamblers need to eat, so we sat down and ordered. I opted for a spicy chicken noodle dish, which was extremely hot. It took only 5 minutes to serve, which surprised me. The cooking speed was so quick that 10 minutes later, I couldn't keep it down. I spent about an hour in the casino's well-maintained bathrooms, throwing up.

This was one of the worst dining experiences I've ever had.

yelp:train:168057.orig:
So I recently got a job in the city of Mesa conveniently near T.C. And when I had to make a day trip to the joint (hardly a joint, more Scottsdale-esque) I was quickly floating on breakfast cloud 9.

I love food, and I love to eat, and I LOVE a great breakfast brunch.  This place had it all!!! We went there after my graduation from college with a bunch of family, mostly of the elderly.  Let me first explain that going anywhere with my Grandpa is a mission in itself, nothing is ever cooked right and service is always too slow however he could not stop complimenting the staff on how great everything was (first time I have ever witnessed this in 22 years).  

TC is a great place for family and celebrations or just to enjoy a great weekend brunch.  LET ME WARN YOU IF YOU GO ON A WEEKEND GO EARLY OR YOU WILL BE WAITING AROUND 30 minutes!
yelp:train:168057.para:
Recently, I secured a job in Mesa, conveniently close to T.C., and decided to make a day trip there. The experience was delightful, especially for breakfast, which was almost brunch-like. I have a deep appreciation for good food, and I absolutely adore a fantastic breakfast. This place truly delivered on all fronts!

I celebrated my college graduation with family, including many elderly relatives, at T.C. Typically, dining with my Grandpa is challenging; the food is rarely cooked to his liking, and service is often slow. However, this time, he couldn't stop praising the staff, which was a first for me after 22 years.

T.C. is an excellent spot for family gatherings and celebrations, or simply for enjoying a great weekend brunch. I must warn you, though: if you visit on a weekend, plan to arrive early to avoid waiting around 30 minutes.

yelp:train:168086.orig: We have lived here for almost 5 years and we just found this place!  We are always on the hunt for a great bfast place.   I
yelp:train:168086.para: After nearly 5 years in this area, we recently discovered a fantastic breakfast spot. We're constantly searching for excellent bfast options.

yelp:train:168106.orig:
T.C. Eggington I heard had a great reputation so I decided to attend with my hiking group.  

We came real early so it was pretty quiet plus only a few regulars.  The place itself is very old fashion and homey.  We ordered our coffees and drinks then started with the food.  I went plain jane with scrambled eggs, bacon, and potatoes, while my buddy ordered some pancakes.  

I didn't think it was anything special truthfully.  Eggbeater eggs, bacon was okay, and the potatoes where definitely not freshly cut.  The pancake was huge, but real dry because the thickness of it made it hard to swallow!  

Overall, I think the place is cute, but need to revamp some of the menu items to attract a more vibrant crowd.  I worked at mom/pop places like these before and we've always attract the same people in and out.  They can't always keep coming and eventually you have to reinvent. - Enjoy!
yelp:train:168106.para:
T.C. Eggington has a good reputation, so I joined my hiking group there early. It was quite quiet with just a few regulars around. The place has a classic, cozy feel. We ordered our drinks and then started on the food. I had simple scrambled eggs, bacon, and potatoes, while my friend opted for pancakes.

To be honest, I didn't find it particularly impressive. The eggs were just okay, the bacon was decent, but the potatoes weren't freshly prepared. The pancakes were enormous but very dry due to their thickness, making them hard to swallow.

Overall, the place is charming, but it needs to update its menu to draw in a more lively crowd. I've worked at similar mom-and-pop spots before, and they tend to attract the same regulars. Eventually, you need to reinvent yourself to keep things fresh. Enjoy!

yelp:train:168209.orig: Bad food. Bad service. Bad drinks. I guess we caught our server on an off night, but the next day we ate here again after leaving the pool and the food was even worse than the night before.
yelp:train:168209.para: The food was subpar, the service was poor, and the drinks were disappointing. It seems our server was having a tough day, but the following visit, after coming from the pool, the food was even worse than the previous night.

yelp:train:168469.orig:
I can't believe I'm going to say this, because I've eaten so many places, but I think the dinner I had at Fleur de Lys is the best meal I've ever eaten. I had the four-course Elegance prix fixe menu, and each dish is etched in my memory -- the tuna tartare with an amazing blend of herbs and a minty note, the barely-there slivers of veal ravioli floating in jus and foam, the filet mignon that remade the flavors of a basic dish into its own unique thing, and the chocolate souffle.

Service was excellent and attentive. There's a bit of the overindulgent goofiness that strikes me at any fancy restaurant, but to their credit the descriptions of each dish were succinct and useful (not the litany you sometimes get, where a waiter is explaining to you the name of the farmer's cousin who picked the radicchio).

Something else I noticed is that you can have a sublime meal here for a variety of price points. One of my dinner companions had the three-course Lion King prix fixe, at $45 or $55; I had the four-course at $89; and two others had the four-course with wine pairings for about $150. And we each came away bowled over.

Again I feel sheepish saying this, but at least right now I fe
yelp:train:168469.para:
I never thought I'd say this, given how many restaurants I've tried, but the dinner at Fleur de Lys stands out as the best meal I've ever had. I enjoyed the four-course Elegance prix fixe menu, and every dish is vivid in my memory—starting with the tuna tartare, which had a fantastic mix of herbs and a refreshing minty taste, the delicate veal ravioli in jus and foam, the filet mignon that transformed a simple dish into something extraordinary, and the chocolate soufflé.

The service was impeccable and attentive. While there was a touch of the fanciful atmosphere often found in upscale restaurants, the descriptions of each dish were clear and helpful, not the lengthy explanations that sometimes come with overly detailed descriptions.

Another noteworthy aspect is the variety of price points for a sublime dining experience. My dinner companion had the three-course Lion King prix fixe for $45 or $55, I opted for the four-course at $89, and the others chose the four-course with wine pairings for around $150. Despite the different price points, we all left thoroughly impressed.

I feel a bit hesitant to say this, but for now, I truly believe this was the case.

yelp:train:168536.orig:
Extremely disappointing.  My wife and I were so excited about experiencing Hubert Keller's food.  And small plates!  Love small plates.  We were that maybe this restaurant would be able to compete with Joel Rubuchon's L'Atelier...?

No.  Not even in the same league.

We ask to sit inside as we assumed it would be quieter than the patio area opposite the loud rock band that were murdering some old classics across the walkway.  Instead, we find that the room is dominated by a large crowd of obnoxiously loud guests, clearly much to the chagrin of all the other guests in the restaurant.  The hostess just laughs at the fact that we chose to come inside and it is louder there.

The wait staff were not much more impressive.  Our waitress was somewhat apathetic.  In between courses, the table did not get cleaned and the drops of sauce and various crumbs just continued to build up.  Our table was not bussed between courses, and it seemed that the staff expected us to eat our fish dishes using our fig jam covered silverware off dirty plates.  When we had complaints about the food (see below), there was no acknowledgement to the problem, let alone an apology.  We also ordered 7 dishes a
yelp:train:168536.para:
Extremely let down. My wife and I were really looking forward to trying Hubert Keller's cuisine, especially the small plates, which I adore. We thought this place might rival L'Atelier by Joel Robuchon.

Unfortunately, it fell far short.

We opted for an indoor seat, assuming it would be quieter than the patio area, which was hosting a loud rock band playing oldies. However, the room was filled with a noisy crowd, clearly upsetting other diners. The hostess seemed indifferent to our choice.

The service was underwhelming. Our waitress seemed disinterested, and between courses, our table wasn't cleared, leaving sauce and crumbs accumulating. There was no bussing between dishes, and we were expected to eat our fish from dirty plates covered in fig jam. When we pointed out issues with the food (more to come), there was no acknowledgment or apology. We ordered seven dishes,

yelp:train:168850.orig: After a good run on the craps tables we thought we'd splurge on a good meal.  Unfortunately, this place was a real disappointment.  While it had a nice atmosphere and great service, the food was very mediocre and very\nexpensive.  I would rate it a few notches above diner food, for about \n1000 times the price.  If you're going to be in Vegas, you can do better.
yelp:train:168850.para: Despite doing well at the craps tables, we decided to treat ourselves to an excellent meal. Unfortunately, our experience was quite letdown. Although the ambiance was pleasant and the service was top-notch, the food was subpar and overly priced. It felt more like diner food at a price point that was a thousand times higher. If you're in Las Vegas, there are definitely better options available.

yelp:train:169693.orig:
I am a stickler for service and UGGGH this sucked.  I had to track down the server several times for water. I had to ask for a place setting and out food took a year to get to us.  

I ordered hot tea and a cup of chicken noodle soup (O_o) oh, and water with lemon.  My mom and sister ordered a fish, shrimp and fries platter and shared it.  We did get bread on the table which was very good.  My soup was barely warm, hot tea was warm and no lemon in my water. The soup tasted like canned soup, but I did track down lemons and hot water eventually.  For the price of my meal, I was NOT HAPPY.

NEVER AGAIN will I spend my money here. BLAH!
yelp:train:169693.para: I am very particular about service, and this experience was terrible. I had to repeatedly ask for water, and it took a long time to receive our place settings and food. My order included hot tea, chicken noodle soup, and water with lemon. My family ordered a fish, shrimp, and fries platter to share. The bread was quite good, but the soup was barely warm and tasted like canned soup. I eventually found lemons and hot water, but my soup was still not hot enough. Given the price, I was extremely dissatisfied. I will never return here; it was a waste of money.

yelp:train:170337.orig: Lame... Had I reviewed this show when I first saw it, I might have given it four stars.  It was back in 2003 and my group of girlfriends was deciding between this and Chippendales, but this won over for being cheaper.  I had a great time then.  One of the guys ran on our table and I slapped his butt.  I even splurge for the overpriced Polaroid of me lying across the men's laps.  Fast-forward to this year, and a bigger group of us went for a bachelorette activity.  There were so many screaming women.  It's like this was the best experience they ever had.  I really hated the long video that was played before the show of all their guest spots on tv shows.  Really bad lip-synching.  An experience best had only once.
yelp:train:170337.para: Disappointing... If I had reviewed it right after my first viewing in 2003, I would have given it four stars. At that time, my group of friends and I chose this show over Chippendales because it was cheaper, and we had a fantastic time. One of the performers even ran onto our table, and I enjoyed giving his butt a playful pat. I even indulged in the pricey Polaroid photo of me lying across the men's laps. However, when we revisited it recently for a bachelorette party, it was a different story. The place was filled with women who were screaming, acting as if it was their highlight ever. I really disliked the long video shown before the performance, which featured their guest appearances on TV shows; the lip-synching was terrible. Overall, it's an experience that's best enjoyed just once.

yelp:train:170693.orig: I'm so sorry to give them 2 stars! But, alas, I had to do it.  This isn't about the service (which is great) or the location (location, location). Their onions penetrate every facet of the menu.  Everything! I just can't stomach it anymore, even after visiting 3-4 times.  some of my friends even work here! Anyway, don't come here if you don't like onions or sitting one foot away from the next table.
yelp:train:170693.para: I really regret giving them only 2 stars! Still, I had no choice but to do so. This isn't about the service, which is excellent, or the location, which is fantastic. The onions are a pervasive element in every dish on the menu. I simply can't handle it anymore, even after visiting several times. Some of my friends even work there! In any case, avoid this place if you dislike onions or prefer more privacy at your table.

yelp:train:170800.orig: Great quaint neighborhood and good drink prices! I love the ambiance, will be back soon.
yelp:train:170800.para: What a charming neighborhood with fantastic drink prices! I adore the atmosphere here and plan to return soon.

yelp:train:171131.orig:
I was here for the Michael Jackson Immortal Tour last year and the Muse concert on St. Patty's Day 2013.  Some of the ushers don't seem to know where to send paperless ticket holders like me.  Two guys gave me the right direction, however, once I got to the security area, I was asked to go somewhere else.  Wasted my time in a line I wasn't even supposed to be in.  I went back to the same security area and told him I was at the right place from the very beginning but he told me to go somewhere else and all he said to me was ""oh!  You found your answer huh?""  WHAT???

On getting my wristband, I got yelled at by an usherette for going under the stanchion instead of walking all the way around to get to the end of the line...as if there was anybody behind me! DUH?!

The venue itself is pretty ok.  Crowd control is pretty bad though.  They yell at people unnecessarily but don't do anything when there's a group of rowdy guys.
yelp:train:171131.para:
Last year, I attended the Michael Jackson Immortal Tour and a Muse concert on St. Patrick's Day 2013. Some ushers were unclear about directing paperless ticket holders like me. Two ushers provided the correct guidance, but when I reached the security area, I was directed elsewhere. I ended up standing in a line I shouldn't have been in, wasting my time. When I returned to the security area, I informed them I had been in the right place from the start, but I was again told to go somewhere else. The response was dismissive, with the usherette saying, "Oh! So you found your way, huh?" - WHAT THE HECK?

Additionally, an usherette yelled at me for going under a stanchion instead of walking around the line, even though there was no one behind me. It was quite unnecessary.

The venue itself is decent, but crowd control is poor. They shout at people for no reason but do nothing when there's a group of loud individuals.

yelp:train:171142.orig:
Went to see Maroon5 here for New Year's Eve.  It was an easy walk through the casino and then the food court to get to the events center.  Even though the walking areas are packed, you never feel like cattle.

The venue itself was great.  Security was very efficient in getting everyone through and the lines were never long.

We had floor seats and security was really good about keeping the walkways clear from those who were blocking the views.  Concert was great! Definitely will be going back!
yelp:train:171142.para:
I attended Maroon5's New Year's Eve performance, and it was a straightforward journey from the casino to the food court, then to the events center. Despite the crowded walkways, the atmosphere never felt crowded or chaotic.

The venue was excellent, with security efficiently managing the crowd, ensuring lines remained short. We had floor seats, and security did a great job maintaining clear walkways to ensure unobstructed views. The concert was fantastic, and I definitely plan to return!

yelp:train:171244.orig: This place is really cute and fun. My husband and I are in our thirties early thirties and love this place. It's great for all ages!
yelp:train:171244.para: This location is genuinely charming and enjoyable. My spouse and I, who are in our early thirties, absolutely adore it. It's perfect for people of all ages!

yelp:train:171363.orig:
I give it four stars not because I had a good time but because if you love roller coasters (I don't ) you will love this ride.

My bf and I had a deal when we came to Vegas.  He wanted to take me on the NY NY roller coaster and I said ok, if you will go to the top of the Stratosphere and look out with me.  

The above is crazy talk for me as I hate heights but I thought I should test myself.

So, we went first thing when they opened at 11am to the NY NY roller coaster.  My bf struggled to keep up with me as I charged to the top of the escalator taking the stairs on it two at a time.  I got to the top and rented a locker to place my backpack in.

All the while, I'm ready all the safety notifications as if I have no knowledge of carnival rides whatsoever. 

We get in line and he pays for two tickets and everything is a blur for me.  I ask the cashier for a couple of tissues as ""there might be crying"" and she smiled as I walked toward my doom.

We selected a car near the back of the ride, which in retrospect was probably a poor idea as I was later told by others that the back is the more bumpy ride (great).

As we headed straight up initially, I could only see the bl
yelp:train:171363.para:
I awarded it four stars not for my enjoyment but because if you're a roller coaster enthusiast (which I'm not), you'll likely adore this ride.

My boyfriend and I made a pact before our trip to Vegas: he would take me on the NY NY roller coaster, and in return, I would accompany him to the top of the Stratosphere. 

For me, who dislikes heights, this was a bold challenge, but I decided to push myself.

We arrived early, at 11 am, when the roller coaster opened, and I raced up the escalator, taking two steps at a time. At the top, I secured a locker for my backpack.

Throughout, I attentively listened to all safety announcements, despite already knowing a lot about carnival rides.

We joined the queue, and he bought two tickets. Everything was a whirlwind for me; I asked for tissues, saying, "There might be tears," and the cashier smiled as I approached what I considered my fate.

We chose a car near the rear of the ride, which turned out to be a less-than-ideal choice, as others later informed me that the back is bumpier.

As we ascended, I could only see the blurs below.

yelp:train:172377.orig:
I've stayed at the Flamingo numerous times, but I've never eaten here before.  However since we had just arrived in Vegas that morning (& were still a little jet lagged), we decided just to eat dinner at the hotel.

My experience at Steakhouse 46 was wonderful.  The service was superb.  Our waiter and her assistant were so attentive.  I could never see them throughout the restaurant, but when I needed something poof they were right there.

I started off with the lobster bisque which was excellent and for dinner I had the surf & turf (Filet Mignon & Alaskan King Crab Legs) with yukon gold french fries on the side.  Everything was so delicious . . . so tasty and cooked to perfection.  Even though I was stuffed, I ate it all and ended up rolling out of there.  My mom ate the rack of lamb and she loved her meal too.

So glad that we decided to go there and would definitely go back to try their tapas.
yelp:train:172377.para:
I have visited the Flamingo several times, yet I had never dined there until our recent trip to Vegas, where we were still adjusting to the time change. We opted to have dinner at the hotel’s Steakhouse 46.

My experience was fantastic. The service was outstanding; our waiter and their assistant were incredibly attentive. They were always there when we needed them, even though we didn’t see them much around the restaurant.

I began with the lobster bisque, which was superb, and for my main course, I chose the surf and turf (Filet Mignon and Alaskan King Crab Legs) served with Yukon gold French fries. Everything was delicious, perfectly cooked, and so flavorful that I managed to finish it all despite being very full.

My mother enjoyed the rack of lamb, and she was equally pleased with her meal. We were so happy we chose this restaurant and are eager to return to try their tapas menu.

yelp:train:172379.orig: Came back again this year and was underwhelmed. The food was pretty good, but the service was truly awful. The hostess could teach the old guys working the room a thing or two about hospitality (she was great!), but I doubt they'd listen. The meal didn't live up to the price.
yelp:train:172379.para: This year's visit left me feeling disappointed. While the food was satisfactory, the service was dismal. The hostess was exceptional, setting a high standard that the other staff members seemed to fall short of. Overall, the experience didn't justify the cost.

yelp:train:172381.orig:
If you enjoyed jumping on trampolines as a child, this is your place to go as an adult!  And I don't mean just one trampoline here, there are over twenty trampolines - all connected together! So you literally get to jump from one trampoline to another.  And they also have trampolines on the side walls too!  This is your chance to try all those aerial stunts you wanted to try as a kid.  You can jump onto the wall, do a flip and just keep on jumping!  They even offer 3-D Dodgeball and hoops for you to try to fly through.

I found myself here on a Sunday night after my friend suggested this idea months before.  Sure, I've done my share of trampoline jumping in someone's backyard.  But this setup, you just can't find in someone's yard.  So, there I was practicing my front and back somersaults.  And sure, I ate it a few times...everyone needs a few good face plants every now and then.  But the idea of just jumping your ass off and getting your heart rate up reminds me of jumping on my bed until it felt like my heart was going to explode.  

For Open Court Jumping, you can pay by the hour on the hour or half for $8.50/hr.  (At our age, we figure an hour was plenty and it was!
yelp:train:172381.para:
If you had fun jumping on trampolines as a kid, this place is perfect for adults like you! With more than twenty trampolines connected together, you can jump from one to another. They even have trampolines on the side walls. It's your chance to try those aerial stunts you dreamed of as a child—jump onto the wall, do a flip, and keep jumping! They also offer 3-D dodgeball and hoops for you to fly through.

I visited on a Sunday night, following my friend's suggestion from months ago. While I've jumped on trampolines in backyards before, this setup is unique. I was practicing front and back somersaults, and yes, I took a few face plants—everyone needs a few now and then. Jumping until your heart feels like it's about to burst is exhilarating, just like jumping on your bed as a kid.

For Open Court Jumping, you can pay by the hour for $8.50 per hour, or half that for a half-hour session. (We found an hour was more than enough for us.)
