This is all while we were waiting to be seated. The customer said \""I wouldn't\"" and she made a dash for the side door heading to the parking lot. The customer turned to us and said he had never seen anything like that before. Wait...there's more. We turned around and left to find a different place to eat and I made a call to the manager to let him know what had happened. He listened, but offered no resolution and took my information to pass to the owner. Five minutes later my cell phone starts ringing and it is the server (seriously!?) we called about asking why we thought it was not right that she did that and told me that she had the RIGHT to tips because she was not paid hourly. I briefly spoke to her about the rudeness of speaking to customers about oth
yelp:train:172712.para:
Absolutely not returning to this place ever again...

The server's complaints about tips upon our arrival were extremely off-putting. When we entered Autumn Court, she was grumbling to a man at the bar about the customers she just served not leaving tips. (To be frank, I might have considered not tipping after hearing that.) She then had the nerve to ask the customer if she should go out and ask for a tip! This happened while we were waiting to be seated. The customer replied, "I wouldn't," and she rushed to the side door towards the parking lot. The customer then told us he had never seen anything like that before. Wait, there's more. We left to find another restaurant and called the manager to report the incident. He listened but offered no solution, merely taking down my information to pass on to the owner. Five minutes later, my phone rang, and it was the server (really!?) we had complained about, asking why we thought it was wrong for her to ask for tips. She insisted she had the right to tips because she wasn't paid hourly. I briefly spoke to her about the rudeness of speaking to customers that way.

yelp:train:173162.orig:
Went here with my wife & her family for dim sum.  

They are chinese and they hated the place, her mom even sent back the taro cake which was reheated in the first place.

I hate dim sum in the first place, but I had a better experience here than I did in one philly & one nj dim sum restaurant...

My favorite was the malaysian dessert cake - definitely worth a try.  Not much to write about the rest since it was just a bunch of mediocre food.
yelp:train:173162.para:
My wife and her family visited this place for dim sum, and they weren't impressed at all. Her mother even returned the reheated taro cake.

I don't particularly enjoy dim sum, but this place was better than the ones in Philadelphia and New Jersey that we've been to.

The Malaysian dessert cake was my standout choice; it was definitely worth trying. The rest of the food was just average, so there's not much to comment on.

yelp:train:173448.orig: I found this place using this site and so glad I did. The tacos are amazing and great prices! The owner was very friendly.
yelp:train:173448.para: I discovered this spot through the website, and I'm really happy I did. The tacos are outstanding, and the prices are fantastic! The owner was also very welcoming.

yelp:train:173858.orig:
9 times out of 10, when faced with a choice of restuarants, I prefer locally owned joints over chains. This place is a good reminder of why that is. 

We ended up going here because someone had given us a gift certificate.   So, we stopped in for a late lunch - we arrived well after  the ""busy"" time.   We thought we'd have quick, attentive service, but that was not quite the case.  Our server was friendly, but rather slow in getting drinks out to us & taking our order. 

I decided to go simple and have a chicken burrito with rice & beans.  The food tasted ok but was not what I would consider to be particularly good. It was just meh. I can definitely make better chicken burritos with beans & rice at home.  

But the worst part was about an hour after eating here, I started to feel yucky.  I was not ""sick-sick"" but felt as if I had eaten too much of something that I am senstive to - like too much MSG . 

I think that most fast food and big corporate chains use some MSG in their food but I try to avoid the ones that use way too much of it.  (The problem is that it doesn't always show up in an ingredient list as MSG - sometimes it is just labled as ""natural flavorings
yelp:train:173858.para:
In most cases, I opt for locally owned restaurants over chains when choosing where to dine. This experience reinforced that preference. 

We visited this place due to a gift certificate and decided on a late lunch, arriving past the typically busy hours. We expected prompt and attentive service, but it didn't quite meet our expectations. Our server was polite but took a while to serve drinks and take our order.

I opted for a simple chicken burrito with rice and beans. The food was acceptable but not particularly delicious; it was just average. I could easily prepare a better version at home.

The most disappointing aspect was that about an hour after eating, I started feeling unwell. Not severely ill, but as if I had consumed too much of something I'm sensitive to, possibly too much MSG.

I generally avoid fast food and large corporate chains that heavily rely on MSG, as it often isn't clearly listed in the ingredients and can cause discomfort.

yelp:train:173887.orig: A salad.  It consisted of two leaves of Romaine lettuce, with a few beans, a few chunks of ham fat, and other assorted small things scattered about.  In a pool of about a teaspoon of pesto.  Very pretty dish.  Not much to eat though.  And pretty tasteless.  The main was so unimpressive I can't even remember what it was a week later.  But I do remember it was expensive.  I could have had a good steak for that price.
yelp:train:173887.para: The meal was a salad with just two Romaine lettuce leaves, a couple of beans, some ham fat in chunks, and a few other small ingredients. It was drizzled with a tiny amount of pesto, making for a visually appealing dish. However, there wasn't much to actually eat, and it tasted rather bland. The main course was so unremarkable that I can't recall what it was a week after the meal. What I do remember is that it was quite pricey; I could have gotten a decent steak for the same amount of money.

yelp:train:174118.orig: Only ate here because we stayed at the hotel and were hungry!  The $30 all day buffet is pretty cool.  We only had lunch though.  The food was mediocre.  Nothing special.  I would go somewhere else for the price.
yelp:train:174118.para: We only dined here since we were staying at the hotel and felt peckish! The $30 all-day buffet is quite appealing. We only tried the lunch though. The food was just okay—nothing exceptional. I'd opt for a different place for that price.

yelp:train:174257.orig:
Best buffet I've ever been to.  Yet! :) I'm surprised by the low rating, but maybe people missed out on the dinner buffet?  In an hour I consumed:

Two different types of crab legs
Shrimp
Sushi
Fresh fruit
Veal
Chicken 8 ways
Roast
Fish
Salads
Pasta
Spinach dumplings
Pizza
Plus all the fixings...

The ONLY thing that was lacking was the dessert section.  I wasn't impressed with any of the offerings, though they were all very cutely displayed.  Then again, I was too full of crabs to really care.  

The best, by far, has to be the crab.  Oh, the crab!  I must have consumed my body weight in crab, the number of empty legs that were left on my plate!  Someone get me a towel to wipe the drool off my keyboard...
yelp:train:174257.para:
This buffet is hands down the best I've ever experienced. However, I'm puzzled by the low ratings; perhaps people didn't try the dinner buffet? In just an hour, I enjoyed a variety of dishes:

Different types of crab legs, shrimp, sushi, fresh fruit, veal, chicken prepared in eight different ways, roast, fish, salads, pasta, spinach dumplings, and pizza—plus all the accompaniments.

The only thing missing was a decent dessert selection, but even the desserts were attractively presented. Honestly, I was so stuffed with crab that I barely noticed.

The crab was outstanding, really outstanding. I must have eaten my body weight in crab, and there were so many empty crab legs on my plate! I need a towel to wipe the drool from my keyboard...

yelp:train:174318.orig: For the same price, the M buffet is a lot better.\nNo alcohol include. Small selection. Cutting the prim rib was like cutting grandma's meatloaf. For that price, I wanted more.
yelp:train:174318.para: The M buffet offers much more value for the same cost; however, it lacks alcohol and has a limited drink selection. The prime rib was difficult to cut, almost as challenging as grandma's meatloaf. Given the price, I expected a greater variety.

yelp:train:174371.para: We were among the customers who utilized the restaurant.com coupon. I had visited this restaurant previously and found it satisfactory enough to return. Both my daughter and I enjoy salmon sashimi, so we ordered it again. However, what was served on our table was not salmon sashimi; it appeared and felt like smoked salmon. We brought this to the staff's attention. It was unbelievable that they genuinely thought it was supposed to look that way. I have had my share of sashimi over the years, and I've never encountered such a mistake. How can you serve sashimi that has been cooked and clearly isn't raw? The staff member took it back and brought out another serving of the same thing. We had the same conversation again. Eventually, I asked him to take it back and got the tuna instead, which I didn't want but was acceptable. I can't return to this place knowing that their sushi chef can't distinguish between types of fish; it's embarrassing for them. Even before the food was served, my three-year-old knocked over a small cup of water. Not a single staff member, who were just chatting behind the counter, offered us a towel to clean the table or the floor. We managed to clean it ourselves.

yelp:train:174870.orig: I was worried that nothing could come close to my absolutely amazing meal at Carnevino I had the night prior, boy was I pleasantly surprised!!! This place has it all: great drinks, great food and a great ambiance!!! If you like Gin, the Pear Blossom Martini is out of this world... I can't stop dreaming about it even weeks later! For dinner, I had the halibut and the mashed potatoes, both which were out of this world. Love everything about Sensi, and I will absolutely be back, probably the 2nd best dinner and dining experience I've ever had in my life.
yelp:train:174870.para: The meal I enjoyed at Carnevino the previous night was so fantastic that I doubted anything could match it, but I was thoroughly delighted! This restaurant excels in every aspect: the drinks, the food, and the atmosphere are all top-notch! If you're a fan of gin, the Pear Blossom Martini is absolutely outstanding—my thoughts about it still linger weeks later! For dinner, I savored the halibut and the mashed potatoes, both of which were incredible. I adore everything about Sensi and plan to return soon; it's likely one of the best dining experiences I've ever had.

yelp:train:174876.orig: I just ate here with my sister last weekend. We stayed in the Bellagio and were walking by looking for an early dinner. We got right in at 6:15 pm for the tasting menu and wine pairing at Sensi. It started with the Thai coconut shrimp soup. Hands down the best soup we have ever had in our entire lives!!! We both are determined to find out the recipe. Mmmm. Next course was Flank steak with kimchi and tempura bone marrow. Delicious!! Didn't love the entire dessert, but the mango anglaise and rice pudding were yummy. Great job on the wine pairing too. \nI will come back for that soup again someday.
yelp:train:174876.para: Last weekend, my sister and I dined at Sensi in the Bellagio, where we arrived at 6:15 pm for their tasting menu and wine pairing. We began with the Thai coconut shrimp soup, which was undoubtedly the best soup we've ever tasted—so delicious that we're eager to recreate it. The next dish, flank steak with kimchi and tempura bone marrow, was also delightful. While we didn't enjoy the dessert entirely, the mango anglaise and rice pudding were quite tasty. The wine pairing was excellent as well. I look forward to returning for that soup again.

yelp:train:175038.orig: 3 words: Mini Kobe Burgers!!! This place is a little pricey, but those yummy pieces of goodness won me over. Minus one star because we were originally going to be seated outside and have a good view of the recurring TI show, but the seats were wet. Blah. Oh well, I still enjoyed our mini kobe burgers!! MMM.
yelp:train:175038.para: 3 words: Mini Kobe Burgers!!! While a bit expensive, these delicious morsels convinced me. However, one star less due to the wet outdoor seats that prevented us from enjoying the TI show. Still, the mini Kobe burgers were a delight! Mmm.

yelp:train:175139.orig: pretty good, I liked it better than sushi samba
yelp:train:175139.para: I preferred it to Sushi Samba, finding it quite satisfactory.

yelp:train:175569.orig:
This place is very professional and clean. Started with a consultation. It took almost a month to get in with an appointment. I worked with Adam and he was great.

They also have a big drive in December partnering with WJJO and the USMC for toys for tots.

Love my new ink and I will definitely go back. This is the only place in Madison I will go to!
yelp:train:175569.para:
This establishment is highly professional and maintains excellent cleanliness. I began with a consultation, and securing an appointment took nearly a month. Adam was my point of contact and was outstanding.

Additionally, they participated in a significant drive in December, collaborating with WJJO and the USMC for Toys for Tots.

I am thrilled with my new tattoo and plan to return. This is the sole place in Madison that I will visit!

yelp:train:175712.orig:
I love coming here.  Not only is the Chicago style Italian food great, the staff is always outstanding!  They actually take time to get to know the guests-That is how you are treated -as guests not just customers.  they are on top of their game and I have never had anything less than great service.  Especially Austin and Paige at the Bar!
Since it is close to where I live, I get to go fairly often.  The swervers know me and my partner pretty well.
We usually get the same things too because they are terrific.  The ceasar  sald is a good portion to share while you wait for your pizza slice, spinach and onion for me and peperoni with extra sauce for my BF.  Sometimes I will get the Turkey stuffed-which is how you'll feel if you eat the whole thing along with it's yummy cottage fries.  I like dipping them in the incredibly hot wing sauce.  They warn me about it everytime and my guts hate it but my mouth loves it!!!
They are also famous for their ""pizzookie"", although it is called something else.  It is a rich decadant cookie with ice cream and chocolate sauce.  I am always too full to try it, but I see alot of them going out to other tables.  So it must be pretty darn good.
The
yelp:train:175712.para:
I really enjoy visiting this place. The Chicago-style Italian food is fantastic, and the staff is consistently excellent! They take the time to get to know the guests, treating them as valued visitors rather than just customers. They are always on their game, and I've never received anything but top-notch service. Austin and Paige at the bar are particularly outstanding.

Since it's near my home, I frequent the restaurant often. The regulars here know me and my partner well.

We typically order the same items because they are so good. The Caesar salad is a great size to share while waiting for our pizza slices; I have spinach and onion, while my boyfriend prefers pepperoni with extra sauce. Sometimes, I opt for the turkey-stuffed option, which is so delicious that it feels like a meal in itself, especially when paired with their yummy cottage fries. I love dipping them in the very spicy wing sauce, which they always warn me about, but my taste buds crave it!

They're also renowned for their "pizzookie," though it has a different name. It's a rich, decadent cookie with ice cream and chocolate sauce. I'm usually too full to try it, but I see many others enjoying it, so it must be quite good.

yelp:train:175733.orig: I have been going to this place mostly for carryout since shortly after it opened.  I mainly bought the pizza.  I noticed a while back that they were skimping on the toppings somewhat, but after my last visit, they are off the list.  I ordered a large numero uno and it was awful.  I'm not sure if they even put sauce on it.  The toppings were very limited ( as I could only see or taste onions and sausage ) and it cost $28 for this garbage.  Being from Chicago, I have some experience with pizza and this ain't it!  You've ruined a good thing folks!  Enjoy your profits!
yelp:train:175733.para: Since the place opened, I've mostly ordered takeout, primarily for their pizza. Recently, I noticed they were using less toppings, but my last order was a real disappointment. I got a large Numero Uno, and it was terrible. I'm not sure if there was even any sauce. The toppings were minimal, as I could only detect onions and sausage, and it cost $28 for this poor quality. As someone from Chicago, I know good pizza, and this doesn't cut it! You've ruined a good thing, folks! Enjoy your profits!

yelp:train:176051.orig:
Not Impressed!  Told they were out of draft beer, then it was available.
Food just OK for the price.  Side order arrived after our dinners were finished!  We ate at the bar and thought it was tacky that the employees
Joined us at the bar for their staff dinners.  For a high end restaurant , the staff should not dine with the customers.  Came again in Nov 13. The veal chop was excellent except the rub on it made it almost inedible.  Get a chef who can do real. High end Italian food.  A 38 $ veal chop should not be over powered  by a nasty crust.
By the way, the staff ate in the bar room again tonight.  Tacky again!
yelp:train:176051.para: Not Satisfied! They said they were out of draft beer, but it became available later. The food was merely adequate for the price, and the side order arrived after we had finished our main courses. We sat at the bar and found it inappropriate that the staff joined us for their meals. For a upscale restaurant, the staff should not dine with customers. We returned in November 2013, and while the veal chop was excellent, the seasoning made it almost inedible. We need a chef who can prepare authentic, high-end Italian cuisine. A $38 veal chop should not be dominated by an unpleasant crust. By the way, the staff is again dining in the bar area, which is tacky once more.

yelp:train:176071.para:
Since I tried their Big Boy mac and cheese at Yelp's Western Adventure in March, I've been a fan of this place. I adore mac and cheese, but my husband isn't a big fan. When I had the chance to sample a version with beef brisket, I thought, "Edgar will absolutely love this!" A few months later, during our staycay at the Pointe Hilton Squaw Peak, we decided to visit the Hole-in-the-Wall for breakfast on our last day. Although the dish is typically served as a dinner meal, the waitress managed to get the chef to prepare a small portion for my husband to try. The service was outstanding throughout our meal, and I appreciated the Old West decor, which felt authentic rather than like a theme park.

For breakfast, my husband had the Hole-in-the-Wall Breakfast, which was incredibly generous. He enjoyed most of it and found the food to be excellent. I opted for The Sonoran, which included scrambled eggs mixed with spinach, peppers, chicken, and cheese. It was so...

yelp:train:176121.orig:
I like to hike here as it is not as steep as the Camelback.

My daughter was five when she first made it to the top. At that time it took her 60 mins one way but she did it in 40 mins today.

This summit course was my fall back plan whenever I couldn't find a parking at the Camelback while I was training. I seemed to find a parking here and most I had to wait was 5 mins.  1.2 miles one way and about 20-25 mins to get to the top gave me the workout I needed.

There is no public bathroom near the parking, otherwise, I would hike twice to get the workout I wanted. 

On sunny clear day, the view from the summit is beautiful. I can see as far as the four peaks mountain.
yelp:train:176121.para:
I enjoy hiking here because it's less steep than Camelback.

My daughter, who was five, reached the top for the first time, taking 60 minutes one way then, but she did it in just 40 minutes today.

This summit was my backup option when I couldn't find parking at Camelback during my training. I usually managed to find a spot here, often waiting only 5 minutes. The 1.2-mile one-way hike, taking about 20 to 25 minutes to the top, provided the workout I needed.

There's no public bathroom near the parking area, which is why I sometimes hike twice to get the workout I want.

On a sunny, clear day, the view from the summit is stunning, extending as far as the Four Peaks mountain.

yelp:train:176311.orig: My GF and I decided to eat here we hadn't had much to eat all day and by this time it was pretty close to 5pm.  I ordered the ribs and my GF ordered the Chicken Fried Steak.  The ribs were not that good, they seems a bit dry and tough on the top part of the rib almost like it had sat under a heat lamp for a while.  I wouldn't order those again.  I had a bit of the CFS and it was ok nothing special.  Overall I wouldn't go back for the food, the service was ok.  The only really nice thing was the view of the strip and people watching.
yelp:train:176311.para: My girlfriend and I chose to dine here since we hadn't eaten much that day, and it was nearly 5 pm. I got the ribs, while she had the Chicken Fried Steak. The ribs weren't great; they felt dry and tough, especially on the top part, as if they'd been exposed to heat for too long. I wouldn't reorder them. I tried a bit of her meal and found it satisfactory but not exceptional. Overall, I wouldn't return for the food, though the service was decent. The highlight was the view of the strip and people-watching.

yelp:train:176509.orig:
Rumbi is a great spot for rice bowls in North Scottsdale. The place is kind of cute--the interior is totally decked out Hawaiian style, so it's a welcomed change from the usual lunch routine. 

The rice bowls are pretty good. I almost always get the chicken bowls with teriyaki sauce, and I'm never disappointed. In particular, the chicken is really good--none of that scary brown meat that other rice bowl places have as their standard. 

The only time I had a meh experience was when I got the noodles with the spicy Thai peanut sauce. The noodles looked and tasted like greasy spaghetti, so I now know better and stay away from that. 

A tip to know is that the bowls come in two sizes, full size and half size. The full size is like a buck or two more than the half size, but you're pretty much paying for more rice. The half size is is pretty good portion for most, so stick with that unless you're uber hungry.
yelp:train:176509.para:
Rumbi is an excellent choice for rice bowls in North Scottsdale. The ambiance is charming, with a Hawaiian theme that adds a refreshing twist to typical lunch settings. 

The rice bowls are quite satisfactory. I frequently opt for the chicken bowls with teriyaki sauce, and I'm consistently pleased with the quality. The chicken is particularly delicious, unlike the often unappealing brown meat found at other places. 

My only less-than-stellar experience was with the noodles served in spicy Thai peanut sauce. They tasted greasy and resembled spaghetti, so I now avoid that option. 

It's worth noting that the bowls come in two sizes: full and half. The full size is about a dollar or two more than the half, but it mainly offers more rice. The half size is a generous portion for most, so it's usually the better value unless you're extremely hungry.

yelp:train:176656.orig:
Garden Buffet at South Point, has its ups and downs. It is very spacious and roomy, where its easy to get to and from the buffet line. It does have nice furniture and a nice staff. But of course, we didn't come here for the room itself. 

They do have a good selection of food, even a good selection of seafood. Usually a place that serve sushi at buffet is always a plus for me. But I guess the time that we went, wasn't very pleasant. I guess with the fact, that we went was probably late lunch, we didn't know that there was a time set for lunch and dinner. So we basically got the left overs of lunch in other words. Mainly food that's been sitting out there for a few hours, rice that hasn't been changed and over cooked. Sushi tend to be dry and hard, as well as some seafood. Luckily we didn't get sick, but it was kind of nasty that some of the food on our plate was as hard as a rock. But again, we did go during the end of lunch hour. 

I'm probably sure, if we did go earlier for lunch, it may have been different. But the fact that it has time limits for breakfast, lunch, and dinner, I guess they don't circulate food as much, and probably stop at a certain hour so they can start wi
yelp:train:176656.para: The Garden Buffet at South Point has its pros and cons. It offers plenty of space and is easy to navigate, with comfortable furniture and a friendly staff. However, we didn't visit primarily for the ambiance. The food selection is decent, including a good variety of seafood and sushi, which I usually appreciate. Yet, our visit wasn't ideal. We arrived during late lunch, unaware of the specific times for lunch and dinner. As a result, we ended up with leftover lunch dishes, including rice that hadn't been refreshed and overcooked meals. The sushi was dry and hard, and some seafood was similarly tough. Thankfully, we didn't fall ill, but some of the food on our plates was as hard as rock. If we had come earlier, it might have been better. The establishment's timed service might limit food circulation and stop serving at a certain point to prepare for the next meal.

yelp:train:177072.orig:
Over priced, too salty, and not enough toppings.... 

I am from Chicago so I'm partial to Chicago Style... but I'm not picky when it comes to a good dog... and Nathan's wasn't my cup o' tea....

Sigh... Wrigley and US Cellular field's hot dogs are so delicious..... I'd rather eat that...
yelp:train:177072.para:
Expensive, overly salty, and lacking in toppings... 

As a Chicago native, I have a preference for Chicago-style hot dogs, but I don't have high standards for a good hot dog. Nathan's just didn't meet my expectations... 

Sigh... The hot dogs at Wrigley and US Cellular Fields are so delightful; I'd much rather enjoy those.

yelp:train:177800.orig:

So my boy Hap walks past the entryway into the main room as we follow.  Still, dead silence.  ""What, does this fucking place run on headphones or some
yelp:train:177800.para:
It's true that what happens in Vegas stays in Vegas, especially during a bachelor party, but this story is too exciting not to share.

On the final day of my week-long Vegas stag party, most of the group had already left early in the morning, but a handful of us, the true diehards, were staying for the evening flights and planned to hit one last session of blackjack, Crown Royal, and some fun.

In the early morning, we had some luck at the blackjack tables at the Rio, leaving us with a decent amount of cash to spend. Around 10 AM, we decided to grab breakfast, and coincidentally, the limo driver from the previous night recognized us and offered to take us directly to a titty bar. We couldn't resist.

We headed to Treasures, the only place open at that time. They waived the cover charge for us, which was a plus, but the atmosphere was eerie—no lights, no music, and no girls. 

Us: Is this place really open?

Hostess: Of course, just come on in!

As we entered the main room, my friend Hap walked past the entryway, and the silence was palpable. "What, does this place run on headphones or something?"

yelp:train:177888.orig: Very good food. Comparable to fast food in price but quality is far superior.
yelp:train:177888.para: The food is excellent and offers better quality at a price similar to fast food.

yelp:train:178117.orig: My wife and I are Downtown regulars, and after a night of strolling around Fremont St. gambling and drinking we used to stroll over to the Golden Gate Casino's Bay City Diner, but since it became Du-par's prices have gone up and the food simply blows. Anyway, we now generally find our way to Magnolia's Veranda Cafe in the Four Queens, and while it's not dirt cheap, it's reasonable and the food is quite good, but like any place you visit it enough times and you long for change. After kicking around this place or the other, we settled on walking over to Sam Boyd's California Hotel and Casino to see what they had going on; all I can say is what a pleasant surprise Market Street Cafe was, remember we're talking about tasty/cheap \""after drinking food.\"" I'd say if you want a great Downtown dinner, try the Grotto or Hugo's Cellar, but if you're staggering around and need to put food in your stomach and don't care about atmosphere and are thinking cheap, good food, Market Street Cafe is as far as you need to look.
yelp:train:178117.para: My wife and I are frequent visitors to Downtown, and after a night out on Fremont Street, we used to head to the Golden Gate Casino's Bay City Diner. However, since it changed to Du-par's, the prices have risen, and the food quality has declined. Nowadays, we tend to go to Magnolia's Veranda Cafe in the Four Queens. It’s not the cheapest option, but it’s reasonably priced and the food is quite good. Yet, after frequent visits, we start to crave something new. Exploring other options, we decided to check out Sam Boyd's California Hotel and Casino, and the Market Street Cafe there was a delightful surprise, especially for post-drinking meals. If you're looking for a great Downtown dinner, consider the Grotto or Hugo's Cellar. But if you're looking for affordable, tasty food after a night out and don't mind a more casual atmosphere, the Market Street Cafe is an excellent choice.

yelp:train:178901.orig: Don't be a victim of Yelp and TV Hype.  This is a MASS QUANTITIES establishment, with no flavor, and questionable quality.  Front staff good, kitchen staff bad.  I ordered the \""famous\"" chicken and waffles.  Good grief, man.  The chicken (boneless breast) was dry and flavorless = cotton.  The waffle was far too dense, and tasted like cardboard.  I'm serious.  If you like Roscoe's, please heed my advice.  Wait staff was good, and apologetic when our food took over 30 minutes to get to us.  This was on a Sat. morning.  People that were seated after us were even done eating before we started.  Booooo.
yelp:train:178901.para: Avoid being misled by Yelp reviews and TV advertisements. This place is all about quantity over quality, with no taste to speak of. The front desk staff were helpful, but the kitchen staff were not. I tried the "famous" chicken and waffles, and I must say, it was terrible. The chicken (boneless breast) was dry and lacked any flavor, like cotton. The waffle was overly dense and tasted like cardboard. Seriously. If you enjoy Roscoe's, take my advice and steer clear. The service was decent, and the staff apologized for the long wait, which took over 30 minutes on a Saturday morning. Even the people seated after us had finished eating before we even started. Boo.

yelp:train:179057.orig:
Let me preface this review by saying, I've been to both this hash house and the one at Imperial Palace and this by far is a shitton better in terms of wait time, service, and dare I say even the food. 

I had a large group of famished, sunday-after-vegas-weekend-exhausted friends. All of them more than ready to show hash's infamously large plates what was up. Okay well maybe that could've just been my thoughts, really.

I was fortunate enough to have an eating partner willing to partake in my fatty adventure. The original request of a not so detrimental eggs benedict had been replaced by the andy's sage fried chicken benedict and a chorizo hash. Mind you, two very gargantuan orders. What a good sport, I almost kind of felt bad. Almost. 

Everyone got a variety of things which was of course, more food than anyone should ever force to digest in one sitting. We really enjoyed the sage fried chicken and chorizo orders --and were also the only two who finished all of our food. 

Side note, the fried chicken in and of itself was a bit dry. Luckily there was enough fat off the bacon, and the fried cheese to keep it moist. LOL. 

My friend got the kiwi watermelon drink thing whic
yelp:train:179057.para:
To start, I've visited both this hash house and the one at Imperial Palace, and this one is undoubtedly superior in terms of wait time, service, and even the food.

We had a large, famished group after a long night out on a Sunday. They were eager to try the hash house's famous large portions.

Fortunately, I had a friend willing to join me for this fatty meal. We decided on the Andy's sage fried chicken benedict and a chorizo hash, both very large orders. It was a bit of a challenge, but they were good sports about it.

Everyone ordered a variety of dishes, resulting in more food than anyone could realistically eat in one sitting. We particularly enjoyed the sage fried chicken and chorizo, and we were the only ones who finished our meals.

As a side note, the fried chicken was a bit dry, but the bacon and fried cheese provided enough moisture to make it palatable. My friend also tried the kiwi watermelon drink.

yelp:train:179207.orig:
Absolutely amazing food and service here. Waiters are very attentive, and the meal portions are gigantic! No wonder there's always a wait for a table. We had a party of 5 people, and waited for about 30 minutes for a table. But lemme tell ya - it was SO worth it. Everyone in our group loved their food, and there were certainly left overs when we were done!

The ingredients used in the food are such good quality, that you can really taste the freshness. The prices aren't too bad (most plates under $15), which is a great perk! Most trendy/high quality meals are much more expensive.

There is another restaurant location on the strip, but that wait is even worse than this one. It would be worth the drive into the surburbs of Vegas for a visit here!
yelp:train:179207.para:
The food and service at this place are absolutely fantastic. The waiters are super attentive, and the portions are enormous! It's no wonder people have to wait for a table. Our group of five had to wait about 30 minutes for a seat, but it was totally worth it. Everyone enjoyed their meal, and there were leftovers to boot.

The quality of ingredients is top-notch, making the freshness really stand out. The prices are quite reasonable—most dishes are under $15—which is a real bonus! Most high-end meals cost much more.

While there's another location on the strip, the wait there is even longer. It's definitely worth the drive to the suburbs for a visit here!

yelp:train:180209.orig:
VERY disappointing, especially for a Vegas restaurant that charges an arm and a leg. Just for a restaurant itself, very very disappointing. 

This was supposed to be an Asian fusion type restaurant but it really lacked in Asian authenticity in terms of flavor. It seemed like the chefs just used different types of sauces  to compensate for lack of flavor which resulted in chaos. 

Fried rice with sausage: Very SMALL portion. Weird ""sweet and sour"" sauce spread over the rice. I would not order again. 

Pad Thai: Lacking flavor. Some type of sweet taste that I knew after one bite, I would get sick of it after subsequent bites. Very unauthentic. I would not order this again either.
yelp:train:180209.para:
EXTREMELY disappointing, particularly for a Vegas restaurant that comes with a hefty price tag. The restaurant itself was very underwhelming. 

This place was meant to be an Asian fusion spot, but it fell short in terms of authentic flavors. It appeared the chefs relied on various sauces to mask the lack of taste, creating a confusing mix of flavors. 

The fried rice with sausage was a small portion, and the "sweet and sour" sauce didn't complement the dish well. I wouldn't order this again. 

The Pad Thai lacked flavor and had an off-putting sweetness that became more noticeable with each bite. It was very unauthentic, and I wouldn't order it again either.

yelp:train:180754.orig: I have been using Gordon Biersh weekly for a team event for almost a year, and every time I have had incredible staff, great food, and every convenience.  The manager's treat you professionally and have really done a great job for us.  I highly recommend this location!
yelp:train:180754.para: For nearly a year, my team and I have been visiting Gordon Biersch for our events, and each time, we've been impressed with the excellent staff, delicious food, and all the amenities provided. The management treats us with professionalism and consistently exceeds our expectations. I strongly recommend this location!

yelp:train:180869.orig: Just went for the first time last Friday night (5.2.08).    It's a small, independently owned restaurant that lends itself to conversation with your neighbors and a beer with the chef.   It's not your typical chain restaurant, nor does it try to be.   We had a huge table (14 people), which was hilarious considering the small/intimate size of the restaurant.     We ordered a couple of appetizers (Calamari and a Hummus Platter) - both of which were great.\nMy wife had the trout and I had the mussels and frites; they were both good enough that we were still talking about them the next day.   A good time was had by all and we'll be back soon.
yelp:train:180869.para: Last Friday night (5.2.08), I visited for the first time, and it was a charming, small, independently run place that encourages chatting with your neighbors and having a drink with the chef. Unlike typical chain restaurants, it maintains a cozy, intimate atmosphere. Our large table for 14 was quite amusing given the restaurant's compact size. We enjoyed a couple of appetizers—Calamari and a Hummus Platter, both delicious. My wife had the trout, and I had mussels and fries; they were so good that we were still discussing them the next day. Everyone had a great time, and we plan to return soon.

yelp:train:181188.orig: I am very sad that I agreed to eat here.  The food was barely palatable and my drink came out COMPLETELY wrong twice.  Service was acceptable, but in the end we paid $40 for the pleasure of crappy food and a generally bad dining experience.  Blegh.
yelp:train:181188.para: I feel extremely disappointed that I consented to dine at this place. The food was barely enjoyable, and my drink was served incorrectly on two occasions. While the service was tolerable, we ended up paying $40 for a meal that was subpar and an overall unsatisfactory experience. Ugh.

yelp:train:181277.orig: Breakfast service was good, prompt and friendly. This place offers your typical American breakfast fare at a price which is average for Vegas but more expensive that anywhere else in the USA. We had the corned beef hash with poached eggs. Nice. However table over from us had to send their breakfast steak back because it was gristly.\n\nI was tossing up to give this 3 stars. But the main thing that let it down was the $3.75 charge for brewed coffee.  The coffee was just terrible and I resented paying for it at any price.
yelp:train:181277.para:
The breakfast service was timely and courteous. The menu features standard American breakfast items, priced averagely for Las Vegas but higher than elsewhere in the U.S. We enjoyed the corned beef hash with poached eggs, which was good. However, the table next to us had to return their breakfast steak due to its toughness.

Initially, I considered rating it three stars. Yet, the primary issue was the $3.75 fee for brewed coffee. The coffee tasted poor, and I felt it was unjustified to pay for such a subpar beverage.

yelp:train:181543.orig: Really good, cost effective specials and the steak was amazing
yelp:train:181543.para: Truly excellent specials that offer great value, and the steak was outstanding.

yelp:train:181887.orig: Excellent service from the staff.  This hotel is a perfect choice if you don't want to stay in a casino (no smoking throughout!) but also want easy strip access.  While attached to the MGM Grand, access to The Signature is restricted only to those staying there so there is less hustle and bustle.  All amenities of The Signature as well as the MGM Grand are available to you.\n\nRooms are gorgeous and very well-appointed.
yelp:train:181887.para: The staff provides outstanding service. If you prefer not to stay in a casino and want a non-smoking environment, this hotel is an ideal choice. It offers convenient access to the Las Vegas Strip while being connected to the MGM Grand. However, the MGM Grand's hustle and bustle are minimized for guests of The Signature, as access is restricted. You have access to all amenities of both The Signature and the MGM Grand. The rooms are exceptionally beautiful and well-furnished.

yelp:train:181967.orig: I had high expectations for the \""penthouse junior suite\"" we booked for our anniversary trip... Which is unfortunate because those expectations were squashed, to say the least. And shame on me for booking thru Blue Chip Vegas because they offered a better deal.. I can't emphasize more how much I DO NOT recommend making that same mistake. \n\nWe got to Vegas at 8am. Went to the hotel to see if we were lucky enough to check in early. The front desk rep stated that if we booked thru them, we could check in now, but our room thru blue chip is separate (rooms managed by a separate company on behalf of some rich guy that bought up a bunch of rooms as an investment) and she couldn't help me. Here's a cell phone number you can call -she says. OK... Call that, get VM. Call again, VM. Call again, they say - call back at 1 and we'll see. Ok...I can handle this, nothing to get upset about yet. I call at 1pm...VM. Three calls later, they say we can go check in. Great!! But then we get to the room and granted its a nice room with a beautiful view, as I check out the place I not only find someone's garbage in the silverware drawer, and someone's long black hair on the bathroom floor, but there
yelp:train:181967.para:
For my anniversary trip, I was very excited about the "penthouse junior suite" we had booked... Unfortunately, my hopes were dashed, to say the least. I really shouldn't have used Blue Chip Vegas for the booking; their deal was too good to be true. I strongly advise against making the same mistake.

We arrived in Vegas at 8 AM and headed to the hotel to see if we could check in early. The front desk told us that since we booked through them, we could check in immediately, but our room through Blue Chip was managed by a different company and she couldn't assist. She gave me a phone number to call. Okay... I called, but got voicemail. I called again, got voicemail. They said to call back at 1 PM and see if they could help. Okay... I thought I could manage this. At 1 PM, I called again and got voicemail once more. After three more calls, they finally said we could check in. Great! But when we arrived at the room, although it was a nice room with a beautiful view, as I started to look around, I found someone's garbage in the silverware drawer and long black hair on the bathroom floor.

yelp:train:182005.orig: The rooms here were really really nice...fully stocked suite complete with microwave, stove, blender, and coffee maker. Actually finding the place is another story...the signage isnt real clear and I had to first go to the mgm counter to find out I was booked at the signature. I guess in the future I will be more aware of the layout, but new comers be prepared to get a little lost on your way in...
yelp:train:182005.para: The accommodations were truly excellent...I stayed in a fully equipped suite that included a microwave, stove, blender, and coffee maker. However, locating the place was quite challenging; the signage wasn't very clear, and I had to go to the MGM counter to discover I was checked into the Signature. In the future, I'll be more mindful of the layout, but newcomers should expect to navigate a bit to find their way in.

yelp:train:182102.orig:
This hotel was fabulous and the staff were a pleasure to work with. We arrived at the hotel around midnight and the front desk staff greeted us with smiles and they went above and beyond for us. We was in tower 2 on the 37th floor and the view was to die for. 

Our one bedroom suite was flawless and everything was outstanding.  Anything you needed they made sure you received it. I love how each tower connected and how they all had a different theme, scent and flower arrangements. We also loved how it connect to the MGM grand. 

I stayed here for 7 days and I have no complaints. We would call housekeeping at 2am and they would come to assist us with smiles. This is by far the best hotel I've every stayed in and when I return to Vegas I'll be staying here again.
yelp:train:182102.para:
The hotel was outstanding, and the staff were incredibly accommodating. We checked in around midnight, and the front desk team greeted us warmly, going above and beyond to assist us. Our suite was in Tower 2 on the 37th floor, and the view was breathtaking.

The one-bedroom suite was perfect, with everything impeccable. They ensured we had whatever we needed. I appreciated how each tower had a unique theme, scent, and floral arrangements, and how they all connected seamlessly. Additionally, the proximity to the MGM Grand was a plus.

I stayed for seven days and had no complaints. We even called housekeeping at 2 AM, and they promptly arrived with smiles. This hotel is undoubtedly the best I've ever stayed in, and I will definitely return to this hotel when I visit Las Vegas again.

yelp:train:182143.orig:
I dont write too many yelp reviews, and my goal is not to write this and make it sound too negative. My goal is to literately give the owner some business advice.
So last week my sister brought home lunch from Thai Basil. I was so impressed, and did not know that it was literately a minute down the road from our house. I thought wow, why have I never heard of this place before? The food is amazing, and the price is really good. 
Tonight my friends and I decided to go for dinner. The place was a little awkward (ex, a sign in the ladies restroom asking to ""dispose of toilet paper in the trash can"" vs the toilet as if we are in Mexico & the place reaking of bad cleaning chemicals). We were all ordering and I had pointed to something on the menu asking the waiter if it was what I was describing (seeing if it were the same thing my sister had brought home last week). He said yes, that it is. I said okay, I will have that.
Dishes came out one by one in 7-10 minute increments. We awkwardly sat waiting for everyone to get their food. Finally mine comes, (the photo posted seperately is what it is). Literately a dollar store bag of salad with thin chicken strips on top sprinkled with
yelp:train:182143.para:
I don't typically write Yelp reviews, and my intention isn't to be overly critical. Rather, I aim to offer some constructive feedback to the owner. 

Last week, my sister brought home lunch from Thai Basil, and I was really impressed. I had no idea it was just a short distance from our home and wondered why I hadn't heard of it before. The food was fantastic, and the prices were reasonable.

Tonight, my friends and I went for dinner. The atmosphere was a bit off-putting (like the sign in the ladies' room asking to "dispose of toilet paper in the trash can" instead of the toilet, and the strong smell of cleaning chemicals). We were all looking at the menu, and I pointed to something, asking the waiter if it was the same dish my sister had enjoyed. He confirmed it was, so I ordered it.

The dishes took a long time to arrive—about 7 to 10 minutes each. We sat awkwardly waiting for everyone to get their food. Finally, mine came (the photo posted separately shows what it looked like). It was essentially a dollar store bag of salad with thin chicken strips on top, sprinkled with...

yelp:train:182472.orig: If you like big German style, then this is the place for you.\n\nAll the classic meals, friendly wait staff, and you can get your beer in a fish tank.
yelp:train:182472.para:
If you enjoy the big, hearty German cuisine, this restaurant is perfect for you.

You'll find all the traditional dishes, served with a welcoming touch from the staff, and there's a unique twist: you can even get your beer from a fish tank.

yelp:train:182685.orig: I like local coffee houses. I prefer ANY local place over the big companies.
yelp:train:182685.para: I have a preference for local coffee shops. In fact, I'd choose any local spot over the larger chains.

yelp:train:183204.orig:
We've been at least a half-dozen times, and have had above average service and excellent food the majority of our visits.  Especially loved the Sunday night discount ;-P.   When will they bring it back?!?

On our last visit, I tried the pulled-pork sandwich.  Oh. My. Lord!  It was delicious!  I have also enjoyed the ahi tuna salad.  The chiles rellenos are my least favorite dish, because they quickly get soggy in their sauce.  That said, my dear sissy LOVED hers. 

Don't know why it's listed as being a place you wouldn't take kids - our 6-year old LOVES their grilled cheese!  We, at least, have had good luck taking him there so far.  There seem to be families there every time we go, so I'd call it fairly kid-friendly.

Best feature - it's right off the AZ canal bikepath!  An easy ride if you'd rather not drive.
yelp:train:183204.para:
We've visited at least six times and have generally enjoyed above-average service and excellent food. We particularly liked the Sunday night discount. When will they bring it back?

On my last visit, I tried the pulled-pork sandwich, and it was absolutely delicious! I've also enjoyed the ahi tuna salad. The chiles rellenos are my least favorite because they get soggy in the sauce, but my sister really loved hers.

I'm not sure why it's listed as not suitable for kids, as our 6-year-old loves their grilled cheese. We've had good experiences bringing him along so far, and families seem to be there every time we visit, making it fairly kid-friendly.

The best feature is its location right off the AZ canal bikepath, which makes it easy to get to without driving.

yelp:train:183836.orig: I saw Jerry Seinfeld at Caesars Palace Las Vegas on Jan 30, 2009 and I wasn't impressed. He just wasn't that funny. It totally ruined my perception of him. However, his opening act was awesome.  I'm not sure, but it could have been comedian Tom Papa as the opening act.  I'd see Seinfeld again only if the tickets were free and I just wouldn't expect much. HUGE disappointment.  Save your money or go see Celine Dion, Bette Midler, or Jeff Dunham instead.
yelp:train:183836.para: On January 30, 2009, I attended Jerry Seinfeld's show at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas, and I found it lacking in humor. It significantly dampened my view of him as a comedian. The opening act, though, was fantastic; I believe it might have been Tom Papa. I would only watch Seinfeld again if the tickets were complimentary, and even then, I wouldn't have high expectations. It was a major letdown. Consider saving your money and watching Celine Dion, Bette Midler, or Jeff Dunham instead.

yelp:train:184002.orig: I really am not a Chili's fan, but for dinner this was the best of all my options while I waited for my flight.  Thanks for seeming super annoyed that I was your customer, waiter.  And for literally flinging my paper napkin wrapped silverware at me.  Right into my face.  That was awesome.  At least you realized it quick enough and apologized, but you should have never done that in the first place.
yelp:train:184002.para: While I generally don't enjoy Chili's, this dinner turned out to be the most satisfactory option available while I was waiting for my flight. The waiter's attitude was incredibly frustrating, seeming genuinely annoyed at my presence. Moreover, he threw my silverware back at me, wrapped in a paper napkin, directly into my face. While he did apologize promptly, it was clear that such behavior should never have occurred in the first place.

yelp:train:184262.orig: Our last visit in June was very disappointing, but since I have been following Mario for nearly 23 years I passed it off as everybody has bad nights.  Went back after 4 months, had the pizza, was average, dough was soggy but had good flavor.  What really blew me was the wine list, pretty good, but whoa! serious price increases!  I love wine with good Italian food but they have gone into the stratosphere on pricing.  I guess all good things do come to an end, time to find another place, shouldn't be hard, lots of competition out there.
yelp:train:184262.para: My visit in June was quite disappointing, yet, given my nearly 23-year following of Mario's, I chalked it up to everyone having off nights. After waiting four months, I returned and ordered the pizza, which was just average; the dough was a bit soggy, but the flavor was decent. The wine list was a pleasant surprise, but the price hikes were shocking! The prices for wine with good Italian food have skyrocketed. I suppose all good things do come to an end, so I'll need to find another place; it shouldn't be too difficult, considering the competition.

yelp:train:185042.orig:
i came here 3-4 years ago and remember enjoying it. however this time around it wasnt nearly as great. we came in for brunch and with 12 people gratuity was included for a total of ~  $28 per person. 

the majority of my meal consisted of breakfast choices....waffles, sausage(rubber?), eggs, hashbrowns...

the highlight for mee was the fresh pineapples, grapefuit, &the prime rib...the prime rib + horseradish was the only thing that made me feel like i got my moneys worth. it was really tasty considering that the carved meats usually arent that appealing to me at buffets.

 the chinese section, seafood, churro, ESPECIALLY dessert was all very mehhhh...soo not worth wasting my hunger. 

cravings....psh i never have nor will i ever crave you!
yelp:train:185042.para:
I visited about 3-4 years ago and had a good time, but this time it wasn't as enjoyable. We had a group of 12 for brunch, and with gratuity included, the bill came to around $28 per person.

Most of my meal was made up of breakfast items like waffles, sausage (which seemed rubbery), eggs, and hashbrowns.

The standout for me was the fresh pineapple, grapefruit, and the prime rib. The prime rib with horseradish was the only part that felt worth the price, as it was quite tasty, considering I usually don't find carved meats very appealing at buffets.

The Chinese dishes, seafood, churros, and especially the dessert were all rather lackluster. They didn't satisfy my hunger or justify the cost.

To be honest, I never have, nor will I ever, crave your offerings!

yelp:train:185533.orig:
People have paid a Cover Charge here? 
Kidding right?
That is just plain dumb. 

It's a counter top with 8 stools, and then a smattering of low small square cushioned seats for another 20? 
It is just a space, not a room.
I didn't even hear one Beatles tune piped in.

Popped in at 5:30 before dinner and a show here at the Mirage.
I guess we made it in under the Cover Charge wire. Just ended up here. Nice visit. Could become crowded easy. I suppose it does too.

The waitress was a sweetheart. And it looked like a couple of ""Hostesses"" were setting up. One didn't fit in somehow...she had pert natural breasts.
yelp:train:185533.para:
People actually paid a cover charge here? Are you kidding? That's just ridiculous.

It's a small place with just 8 bar stools and about 20 low, square cushioned seats. It's more of a space than a room. I didn't even hear any Beatles music playing.

I stopped by at 5:30 before dinner and a show at the Mirage. We managed to get in without paying the cover charge, just by arriving early. It was a nice visit, but it could get crowded quickly. That's probably true for them too.

The waitress was very nice. It seemed like a couple of hostesses were setting up, but one didn't seem to fit in—she had natural-looking, perky breasts.

yelp:train:185709.orig:
Service: Spotty
Food: Above Average
Atmosphere: Awesome
Cleanliness: Top Notch
Music: Did not get it......
Mafioso wanna be factor: High

Service started out a little strained but got better as the evening went along.

Music was a little to loud, did not get the music selection for the  type of establishment.......

Place looks great, clean and fun.....

Food: Octopus appetizer was good not enough food on the plate though, Caprese salad was excellent, Brodo soup was bland, Sausage and Cabbage dish was excellent, Bolognaise was excellent , Vongole was excellent.

Server forgot to bring butter with the bread.

The wanna be mafioso's were out in full force, it was quite entertaining to watch how the old school get's it done!

I would go back and recommend this restaurant.

It is a bit over-priced but isn't everything in Vegas!
yelp:train:185709.para:
Service: Initially a bit tense but improved as the night progressed.
Music: Too loud and not quite fitting for the venue.
Ambiance: The place looks fantastic, clean, and lively.
Food: The octopus appetizer was decent but lacked quantity. The Caprese salad was outstanding. The Brodo soup was bland, while the Sausage and Cabbage dish, Bolognaise, and Vongole were all excellent.
Bread was served without butter.
The "made-in-Vegas" mobsters were in full display, providing an entertaining show.
I'd return and recommend this place.
It's a bit pricey, but then again, isn't everything in Vegas?

yelp:train:185996.orig: Never said I went on 8/2... Just posted my review that day. (: \nYes, they did try to follow up after I posted my opinion, but if you have a low quality product as it is, then I'm not sure how one can make it up to the customer? Coupons? A discount? I clearly don't plan to return. Layers Bakery's rude reply to mine and others' honest reviews of their product completely validates the dozen reviews that complain about their poor customer service and terrible employee attitudes. \nWell, glad I could rate you guys again! Tootles!
yelp:train:185996.para: I didn't say I visited on August 2nd; I just shared my review that day. Yes, they did attempt to contact me after I posted my feedback, but if your product is of low quality to begin with, what can offering coupons or discounts really fix? I have no intention of returning. Layers Bakery's disrespectful response to my and other customers' genuine product reviews strongly supports the dozen complaints about their poor customer service and employees' negative attitudes. Well, at least I got to rate you again! Goodbye!

yelp:train:186014.orig:
Wow! I've never felt more like a burden to an operation. I've never posted a review (I usually just don't come back).

Tried to make some changes on a lunch order and you would think it was the craziest thing ever! ""Do you have any bread other than the honey whole wheat?"" ""No."" Can I switch the pretzel roll to the tuna sandwich?""  ""No we can't switch breads."" ""Why not?"" ""Those are the rules.""

I didn't want to mention that they serve panini as well (on honey whole wheat, I think not).

The baked ham and cheese sandwich (on a pretzel roll!) was pretty good although the side of garlic mash is pretty weird as a side.

C'mon guys.  Get a grip.  You have  ""Bakery"" in your name and I can't substitute bread on a sandwich?  You had more employees than customers this morning.   Think about changing your rules...
yelp:train:186014.para:
Wow! I've never felt so burdensome to an operation before. I've never written a review before, usually just not returning.

When I tried to make a change to my lunch order, it seemed like the most unusual request ever. I asked, "Do you have any bread other than the honey whole wheat?" and was told, "No." Then I inquired if I could switch the pretzel roll to a tuna sandwich, but was denied with, "No, we can't switch breads." When I asked why, the response was, "Those are the rules."

I didn't mention that they serve paninis as well (though I doubt they use honey whole wheat for those).

The baked ham and cheese sandwich (on a pretzel roll) was quite good, but the side of garlic mashed potatoes was a bit odd.

Come on, guys. Get a grip. With "Bakery" in your name, it's absurd that I can't substitute bread on a sandwich. You had more employees than customers this morning. Consider changing your rules.

yelp:train:186213.orig:
I got introduced to Stinkweeds Records in Tempe while I was in college, and was blown away.  Up until that time, I was buying my music at the Memorial Union, and was blown away by their knowledge.

Stinkweeds is simply the best place to enjoy music.  As I got into records, and finding smaller, lesser known, indie artists, punk bands, and underground rappers, I discovered Stinkweeds.  They were able to discuss the artists that I liked, and recommend others.

Unfortunately, I don't buy much music any more and stick to the internet for most of my finds.  But every now and again, I will pop my head in to see what is going on.  Look at a few records, and talk a little underground music face to face.  

Unfortunately, record stores are going by the wayside, so support your local experts and keep them in business.  Yes, you might pay an extra couple of bucks for a cd then you would for the digital version online.  I know.  It's painful, but they appreciate it, and so will you.  Tell me the last time that someone at Best Buy or Barnes & Noble dropped a no-name band on you that you were impressed with.  

My guess is never.
yelp:train:186213.para:
I encountered Stinkweeds Records in Tempe during my college days and was thoroughly impressed. Prior to that, I had been purchasing music from the Memorial Union, and their staff's extensive knowledge left a lasting impression on me.

Stinkweeds is undoubtedly the best spot for music enthusiasts. As my interest in records grew, leading me to explore smaller, lesser-known indie artists, punk bands, and underground rappers, I found Stinkweeds to be a treasure trove. Their staff could discuss the artists I enjoyed and suggest new ones.

Now, I primarily rely on the internet for my music finds, but occasionally, I visit Stinkweeds to browse records and engage in face-to-face discussions about underground music.

Unfortunately, record stores are becoming scarce, so it's crucial to support local experts and keep them in business. Although you might pay a bit more for a CD than you would for a digital version online, it's worth it. They appreciate your support, and so will you. Can you recall a time when someone at Best Buy or Barnes & Noble introduced you to an unknown band that impressed you?

My guess is that it never happened.

yelp:train:186523.orig: Went to Brio with another couple last Saturday night for restaurant week. We were seated upon arrival which is always nice. Our server, Kelly, came to the table quickly and provided excellent service throughout the meal. I have been to Brio several times before and it was always a good experience and so was this time. All of us enjoyed our meals. The atmosphere is very nice too. Restaurant Week in regards to the price is an ok deal but nothing to go out of your way for.
yelp:train:186523.para: Last Saturday night, I dined at Brio with another couple during restaurant week. We were promptly seated upon our arrival, which was appreciated. Our server, Kelly, was quick to attend to us and offered excellent service throughout the meal. This visit, like previous ones, was a pleasant experience for all of us, and we enjoyed our dishes. The ambiance was also very appealing. While the price during restaurant week was reasonable, it wasn't so compelling that it warranted special effort to dine there.

yelp:train:186942.orig:
Ok, let me start off by saying, we didn't really eat here. We had reservations and we had every intention of eating here, but couldn't. Let me tell you why. It was LOUD. And I don't mean that kind of loud where you might have to speak a little louder to chat with your dinner mates. I mean the kind of loud where the music is at nightclub level and you have to yell to have a conversation. 

Now this might be a generation thing as my party of four are all in their 40s, but seriously, I just couldn't stay there. We asked the hostess for another recommendation and she immediately got us into Nove Italiano which was outstanding. They poured our drinks into plastic cups (so we could take them with us) and apologized - although they didn't owe us an apology...apparently we're just old! 

The girls at the hostess desk and at the bar were great. It wasn't them. It was us. I just hadn't read any other reviews that mentioned the noise level so I just wanted others to be aware.
yelp:train:186942.para:
Sure, here's the paraphrased version:

We didn't get to dine here as planned. We made reservations and were eager to eat, but we couldn't due to the environment. The place was extremely loud, not just a bit noisy, but so loud that you had to shout to converse. This level of noise was overwhelming, especially for our group, all in our 40s.

This might be a generational difference, but we simply couldn't stay. We asked the hostess for an alternative recommendation and she promptly suggested Nove Italiano, which turned out to be fantastic. They even provided us with disposable cups for our drinks and apologized, though they didn't need to—apparently, we were just considered old-fashioned!

The staff at the hostess desk and the bar were very accommodating. The issue wasn't with them; it was the noise level. I just wanted to warn others about this before they have the same experience.

yelp:train:187045.orig: N9NE was the place to be 5 years ago, let alone 10. It felt like a shell of its former self tonight. Half full on a Friday night, the magic is gone. Prices have gone up over the years, don't mind paying for solid cuisine but $59 for fatty lamb chops, no thanks. Staff worked hard and meant well, but the sizzle is out of this steak.
yelp:train:187045.para: Five years ago, N9NE was bustling, but even ten years ago, it was much more vibrant. Tonight, it seemed much quieter, barely half full on a Friday. The charm that once drew people in is no longer there. While I appreciate that prices have increased over the years, I can't justify paying $59 for fatty lamb chops. The staff were clearly putting in effort, but the excitement and quality of the steaks have definitely diminished.

yelp:train:187051.orig: The food at this steakhouse was amazing and the service was also very good. I give it 4 stars because it's located in the Palms which, maybe it was just the weekend I went, does not have the same appeal it used to. The restaurant was not very crowded and the casino outside was basically empty. So while the food was fantastic, the trip over to the Palms seemed like a waste. I probably wouldn't take the cab ride over there again.
yelp:train:187051.para: The steakhouse's food was outstanding, and the service was excellent too. I rated it 4 stars, though. The location at the Palms might have been less appealing during my visit, perhaps due to it being a weekend. The restaurant wasn't busy, and the casino outside was nearly empty. Despite the delicious food, the trip to the Palms felt unnecessary, and I likely won't use a cab to get there again.

yelp:train:187056.orig: We started going here for my daughters 21st bday and have been coming back last 7 years on our trips to vegas. I love this place everything is cool. Love the atmosphere steaks are yummy. desserts are great. Had one bad experience with a tasting menu they tried Christmas 2012 but just learned to stick with their awesome steaks. Service always good.
yelp:train:187056.para: We began visiting here for my daughter's 21st birthday, and we've returned every trip to Vegas for the past 7 years. I absolutely adore this place; everything is fantastic. I particularly enjoy the ambiance and the steaks, which are delicious. The desserts are also wonderful. My only negative experience was with a tasting menu in Christmas 2012, so now we always stick to their excellent steaks. The service is consistently great.

yelp:train:187120.orig:
Haven't been back to this place for at least 10 years, so much has changed! They used to give a tour of  Coca Cola's history and how it came to become so popular, but it is no longer there :( The lady told me it is not just a retail store.. Booo! 

One neat thing was being greeted by the live Coke Polar Bear. The photographer will take a picture with your own camera as well as take a ""Professional"" photo of you and whoever else you're with. We ended up buying the photo, because it was so darn hilarious when the Coca Cola bear bit my friend in the head (in a playful way of course). 

They do offer a Taste from around the World ($8), which is 16 small cups of different Coca Cola products from around the world. I must say, some of the samples tasted like mouthwash and some others tasted like bitter sprite.. Haha, so glad we live here in the US I guess :) 

All in all, a good place to visit when you want a break from the Casino and partying. It's right across the street from the Monte Carlo and a short walking distance from the Aria and the Bellagio.
yelp:train:187120.para:
It's been over a decade since I last visited this place, and it's amazing how much has changed! The old tour about Coca Cola's history and rise to fame is no longer available, which is a shame. The lady I spoke to mentioned it's not just a regular store, which was disappointing. 

One highlight was seeing the live Coke Polar Bear. The photographer would take a picture with your camera and also a professional one. We ended up purchasing the photo because my friend got playfully "bitten" on the head by the Coca Cola bear, which was quite amusing. 

They do offer the Taste from Around the World ($8), which includes 16 small samples of Coca Cola products from various countries. Some of the samples tasted like mouthwash, while others were as bitter as Sprite. I'm glad we live in the US, where the taste is generally better. 

Overall, it's a nice spot to visit if you want a break from the casinos and parties. It's conveniently located across from the Monte Carlo and within walking distance of the Aria and Bellagio.

yelp:train:187200.orig: I am a fan of this place, though the last time the wings were anemic, but the boneless ones were pretty good.  Love the Coke super soda machine.  The only real issue I have are the fries.  They put something on them that makes them sweet and they just don't taste rift.
yelp:train:187200.para: While I generally enjoy this spot, the wings I had recently were rather lackluster, but the boneless varieties were quite satisfactory. I really appreciate the Coke Super Soda machine here. The only real drawback is the fries—they have a sweet coating that doesn't give them a satisfying flavor.

yelp:train:187950.orig: Best pizza in Vegas. Great atmosphere too! Also seeing true italians who were there for a long time enjoying their food and their Italian beers has to mean that it must taste like original Italian made pizza. The pizza defenetly tastes like no other pizza I've had before. My girlfriend has been to Italy and she says that it tastes just like it did in Italy. The service was good too. We can't wait to go back again.
yelp:train:187950.para: The pizza here in Vegas is outstanding, and the ambiance is fantastic as well. Notably, I observed genuine Italians who had been there for a while relishing their meals and Italian beers, which suggests the pizza must be authentically Italian. The taste is truly unique, unlike any pizza I've tried before. My girlfriend, who has visited Italy, confirms that it tastes just like the pizza there. The service was also excellent. We're looking forward to returning soon.

yelp:train:188084.orig: Natalia was great.She is the restaurant manager and there was a problem with the ordering of the kids meals. We we're told the kids meals were drink, pizza and desert. When the waitress came back after we ate  she said sorry there is no more left for desert. She said sorry nothing we can do. But then Natalia came to the table and took care of the kids meals and said sorry for the inconvenience. I would of never gone back to there if it wasn't for Vanessa the waitress and natalia doing what they did and taking care of us. Food was awesome also.
yelp:train:188084.para: Natalia did an excellent job. She manages the restaurant, and there was an issue with the kids' meals. We were promised drinks, pizza, and dessert, but when the waitress returned after we finished eating, she apologetically said there was no dessert left. She couldn't do much about it. However, Natalia stepped in and resolved the issue, apologizing for any inconvenience. If not for Vanessa the waitress and Natalia's efforts, I wouldn't have returned. The food was fantastic as well.

yelp:train:188122.orig: I know I know. The rule of thumb is that cool people have dogs. Well, I'm pretty cool. But I am also just a me. And I also have a job. And I also volunteer. Which means I also don't have the time a dog deserves. So instead I have cat dogs. They may look like cats, but please don't let that fool you. I have dogs that use a litter box and that can jump fences. And that fetch. And that always want to play. \n\nI also have cats that can find nearly nothing of interest in wag n' wash. Even though they mention having cat supplies. And even though there's a cat in the store. And even though my cats wag their tails.  Probably great for dogs. But not cats.
yelp:train:188122.para:
Sure, here's the paraphrased version:

I get it, the general idea is that cool folks have dogs. And, I consider myself pretty cool. However, I'm just an ordinary person with a job and volunteer commitments. This means I don't have the time a dog truly needs. So, I opted for cat dogs instead. Although they appear cat-like, don't be misled. My "cat dogs" use litter boxes, can jump fences, and love to fetch and play. 

On the other hand, I have cats that show no interest in the toys at wag n' wash, despite the presence of cat supplies, a cat in the store, and their wagging tails. These cats might be perfect for dog owners, but not for me.

yelp:train:188767.orig: This place is OK, nothing special and if you come mid afternoon there is not much dim sum to choose from.  There are better places to get dim sum.
yelp:train:188767.para: While this spot is satisfactory, it lacks any standout qualities. Moreover, if you visit around late afternoon, your selection of dim sum will be limited. I would recommend checking out other establishments for a more impressive dim sum experience.

yelp:train:189148.orig: Wanting to surprise my fianc\u00e9 with a trip to Vegas, I planned everything in advance including dinner reservations. We ended up dining at STRIPSTEAK and Bouchon for our main dinners, and STRIPSTEAK took a notable second place for me out of those two experiences. The food is delicious and the service is great -- there's not a question there. I had the tuna and it was cooked to perfection. My fianc\u00e9 had the bone-in ribeye and seemed to be in heaven. We split the bleu cheese scalloped potatoes as a side and started with the hamachi poppers, both of which were exceptional. Aside from that, we each had a couple of cocktails and noshed on their complimentary trio of fries (the truffle fries and aioli -- nom!). Still, we somehow managed to tally up quite the bill, which is where my uncertainty lies. Around $230 for the two of us. Again, no wine. Just a couple of cocktails each (sub-$15). We did have a restaurant.com gift certificate which helped, but we were still both a little surprised by the cost of the meal. It was good, but not so memorable where it was worth that investment (at least not in my book). \n\nThe ambiance wasn't totally what I expected either. I was expecting so
yelp:train:189148.para: I wanted to surprise my fiancé with a trip to Vegas, so I meticulously planned everything, including dinner reservations. We dined at STRIPSTEAK and Bouchon for our main meals, and STRIPSTEAK stood out as my favorite among the two. The food was outstanding, and the service was top-notch. My fiancé enjoyed the bone-in ribeye, which seemed to delight him. We shared the bleu cheese scalloped potatoes and started with hamachi poppers, both of which were exceptional. We each had a couple of cocktails and sampled their complimentary trio of fries, including the truffle fries and aioli. Despite all this, our bill came to around $230 for the two of us, which included just a couple of cocktails each (under $15). We had a restaurant.com gift certificate, which helped, but we were still surprised by the cost. While the food was good, it didn't feel worth the investment, at least in my opinion. Additionally, the ambiance didn't quite meet my expectations.

yelp:train:189647.orig: very very let down. service was super slow and food was garbage. I got the duck quesadilla thinking it was going to be great because of the reviews and everything but I was sadly mistaken. Perhaps I should have gotten the crispy quesadilla instead of the large soft one and there is where I went wrong. But in any case, the soft one is cut up and served covered in sauce and salad. So you have to eat it with a knife and fork. I am guessing my order was done and sitting for a while in the kitchen while they were finishing the other plates because it was super super soggy and had absolutely no other texture. It was super salty and very one-note. So maybe I was supposed to order the crispy small quesadilla or maybe this was a fluke on their part but I am not going back because of it.
yelp:train:189647.para: I was extremely disappointed with the service and the food. The service was unbearably slow, and the food was terrible. I ordered the duck quesadilla, expecting it to be fantastic based on the reviews, but I was sadly mistaken. Perhaps I should have opted for the crispy quesadilla instead of the large soft one, which was my mistake. The soft quesadilla was cut up and served with a lot of sauce and salad, requiring utensils to eat it. It seemed like my order was prepared and kept in the kitchen for a while, as it was extremely soggy and lacked any other texture. It was overly salty and bland. Either I should have ordered the crispy small quesadilla, or this was a rare mishap. In any case, I won't be returning.

yelp:train:189824.orig:
Mediocre food and the worst attitude I have experienced in a long time. 

Went for dinner on July 3 and ordered 4 Biryanis which were OK but the Raita which came with it was good for one Biryani. When pointed it out they said that's the standard quantity so we ordered more Raita, no Problem still. Ordered some desserts but nothing great there as well.
