Gajar Halwa was too sweet and luke warm, Ras Malai pieces were broken (happens if they are not fresh) and was not cold as its supposed to be. When the bill came it had few (4-5) items we didn't order. Thankfully my buddy caught it and when he pointed out to the manager he was not apologetic at all and behaved as if he is doing us a favor by correcting his mistake.  

Anyway next day we saw a deal on Groupon next day so we thought lets give it another shot and try their Buffet.  We were a big group so bought two different coupons and they said one coupon per table. We offered to sit on two different tables but the waiter smiled and said it's ok and pointed us to a big table.The spread was good but the food was again OK and very heavy, one positive was that they brought fresh Nans to the table which were soft.  When the waiter got u
yelp:train:189824.para:
The food was subpar, and the service was the poorest I've encountered recently. On July 3, we dined and ordered four Biryani dishes, which were acceptable, but the Raita served with one of them was the only good part. We requested more Raita, and they provided it without issue. We also ordered some desserts, but they were not impressive. The Gajar Halwa was overly sweet and lukewarm, the Ras Malai pieces were broken, suggesting they weren't fresh, and it wasn't cold as it should be. The bill included items we hadn't ordered, and when we pointed this out to the manager, he showed no remorse, acting as though he was doing us a favor by correcting the mistake.

The following day, we saw a Groupon deal and decided to try their buffet again. We purchased two coupons for a large group and were told one coupon per table. We suggested splitting into two tables, but the waiter agreed and directed us to a large table. The buffet selection was decent, but the food was merely satisfactory and quite heavy. A positive was that fresh Nans were brought to the table, which were soft.

yelp:train:190245.orig:
When passing through Phoenix last week, we had dinner here on the recommendation of Yelp. Who knew you could get good British pasties in Tempe?

The pasties themselves were incredible. I had the bangers and mash, the wife had the chicken tikka masala. We loved each of them, and believe me that one pasty is enough to satisfy a big appetite.

We were not as huge fans of the fries/chips. Also, the waitress really had no idea about any of the beers on the menu. Since I am not knowledgable about British beer, this led me to order something I didn't really care for. Next time (oh yes, there will be a next time) I'll stick with the Lagunitas IPA.
yelp:train:190245.para:
Last week, while in Phoenix, we dined here based on a Yelp recommendation. We were surprised to find excellent British pasties in Tempe.

The pasties were outstanding; I tried the bangers and mash, and my wife had the chicken tikka masala. We both adored them, and one pasty truly filled us up.

The fries weren't as appealing to us, and the waitress was unfamiliar with most of the beers on the menu. Since I'm not well-versed in British beers, I ended up choosing something I didn't particularly enjoy. For our next visit (which will definitely happen), I'll opt for the Lagunitas IPA.

yelp:train:190552.orig: So this was my first time trying this restaurant and it will certainly be my last. I went in with positive expectations for this place after reading reviews here on yelp. First off my fianc\u00e9 and I came an hour and a half before closing and were told that we couldn't do the AYCE. We sat down looked at the menu, ordered some drinks and if you're like me and hate tea and sodas you are screwed and will have to suffer with disgusting tasting water. Seriously, no juices or anything... For starters we ordered some gyoza which was nice until we tried what we thought was soy sauce and turned out tasting like pure vinegar. For our main we both had ramen with sushi on the side. I had tonkotsu with California rolls and I have never eaten ramen and sushi so bad. The broth was REALLY salty, the noodles and the pork were super chewy and the Cali rolls tasted so plain. Same with his meal might I add. Also, total mood killer! The music. It might just be me but I don't want to hear \""what does the fox say\"" on full blast while I'm eating my dinner... Last thing (I promise) when we left it was about half an hour till closing and I had noticed some of the chefs go out front. To get some fresh a
yelp:train:190552.para: My first visit to this restaurant was disappointing, and I doubt I'll return. I had high hopes based on the positive reviews I read on Yelp. We arrived an hour and a half before closing, only to be informed that the all-you-can-eat (AYCE) option wasn't available. We settled in, ordered drinks, and were left with no choice but to drink water, as there were no juices or other options. The gyoza was okay, but when we thought we were ordering soy sauce, it turned out to be pure vinegar. For our main course, both of us had ramen with sushi on the side. My tonkotsu ramen with California rolls was the worst I've ever tasted—the broth was extremely salty, the noodles and pork were overly chewy, and the sushi rolls were bland. His meal was equally disappointing. The music was also a major distraction; I found it intrusive, especially the loud, repetitive song "What Does the Fox Say." Finally, when we left, it was nearly closing time, and I noticed some chefs hanging out in the front area.

yelp:train:191275.orig:
This place is great! Went for Happy Hour and had the best time. 
Best bartenders -so attentive and great. Made the best drinks. 
Delicious food! I mean so tasty! 
Great atmosphere. 
All in all -LOVE THIS PLACE!
yelp:train:191275.para: I had an amazing time at this place during Happy Hour! The bartenders were fantastic—so attentive and skilled, crafting the best drinks. The food was absolutely delicious and so tasty! The atmosphere was great too. Overall, I absolutely adore this place!

yelp:train:191315.orig:
I use to love Kona Grill!  We decided to go today for Mother's Day and I thought it would be hit, but boy was I wrong!!  The place was not busy. The bar - YES, but the restaurant..not so much.  We ordered the calamari and it was horrible!!! The calamari had no meat! It seemed like they scraped off the bottom of the fryer and served it.  I thought it had to get better, but then we ordered our entree.  We ordered the Hawaiian Ribeye and I don't even think it was ribeye! I think a porterhouse or something, but definitely not a ribeye.  We also ordered a couple rolls of sushi which weren't bad, but my whole dining experience was already ruined.  My mom ordered their asian salad and she said it was too sweet.  The whole experience was horrible.  Our server forgot to give us soy sauce for our sushit and we waited quite a bit to get it. 

Towards the end of the meal I'm thinking I just wasted $100 on garbage!

I'm going to take the survey tomorrow and hopefully it will change something. I really liked Kona Grill and I would like to return, but based on my last visit - I doubt it.

It may just be a hit or miss kind of thing and I hope that others don't have the same dining experience
yelp:train:191315.para:
I used to adore Kona Grill, but my recent visit for Mother's Day was a major disappointment. The restaurant wasn't very busy, and while the bar area was great, the dining section was not. We started with the calamari, which was terrible; it seemed like they served the leftovers from the fryer. My expectations for the main course were high, but the Hawaiian Ribeye didn't meet them. I'm not sure if it was even ribeye; it might have been a porterhouse. The sushi rolls were okay, but the overall experience was awful. My mother found the Asian salad too sweet. Our server forgot to bring soy sauce for the sushi, and we had to wait a long time for it. By the end of the meal, I felt I had wasted about $100 on subpar food.

I plan to fill out the customer survey tomorrow, hoping it will make a difference. Although I enjoyed Kona Grill in the past, I'm skeptical about returning after this experience. It might just be inconsistent, but I hope others don't have the same frustrating dining experience.

yelp:train:191598.orig: What is there to say about Nothing Bundt Cakes that hasn't been said a million times before. These are some of the best tasting cakes I've had and they come at a fairly decent price considering the quality of ingredients, packaging, etc. This was my first time actually going into the shop although I've had the cakes several times. I was surprised to see it so busy 30 minutes before closing. Even saw Scotty Nguyen (professional poker star) carrying out 3 cakes as he left. Staff was friendly and they had a small but decent selection of cakes in the display.\n\nRed Velvet, Marble and Chocolate Chocolate Chip all left with me and I honestly can't decide which is my favorite. They are all so delicious. While it may not be in budget for your \""everyday\"" cake, it is most certainly worth it for any special occasion. Now that I live only few minutes away, I'm sure I'll be back more often.
yelp:train:191598.para:
There's not much new to say about Nothing Bundt Cakes, but I can attest that they serve some of the best-tasting cakes I've ever had, and the quality of ingredients and packaging justify the price. This was my first visit to the shop, despite having enjoyed their cakes multiple times before. I was surprised to find it quite busy even 30 minutes before closing, and I even spotted Scotty Nguyen, the professional poker player, leaving with three cakes. The staff was friendly, and they offered a modest yet satisfying selection of cakes on display.

I came home with Red Velvet, Marble, and Chocolate Chocolate Chip cakes, and I'm still undecided on which is my favorite—they're all incredibly delicious. While these cakes might not be a regular part of your budget, they are definitely worth it for special occasions. Now that I live just a short distance away, I'm looking forward to visiting more often.

yelp:train:191606.orig: Never again. I absolutely LOVE Thai and was thrilled to find a local spot not too far from my new condo... however,  my excitement was short lived. We ordered crab rangoons, chicken satay, green beef curry and shrimp pad thai... where do I even start?!! First off, the crab rangoons had no undetectable crab and only a hint of cream cheese, the chicken satay was flavorless and tough, the beef curry was an odd consistency with a sad amount of meat and to top off this unfortunate meal, the shrimp on the pad thai was DISGUSTING! It tasted muddy and had absolutely NO seasoning. I tried to explain to the server about the flavor of the shrimp and she wanted to stand there and explain how the shrimp come frozen from the vendor... I could not care less where it came from lady IT'S GROSS! I kept telling her to have the cook make one yo taste and she just looked at me like no one was home. I honestly thought I was going to get sick from eating the one. I am totally bummed that I had such a horrible experience... the search for local Thai continues.
yelp:train:191606.para: Never again. I was overjoyed to discover a nearby Thai restaurant after moving to my new condo, but my joy was fleeting. We ordered crab rangoons, chicken satay, green beef curry, and shrimp pad thai—where do I begin? The crab rangoons lacked any discernible crab and barely had any cream cheese. The chicken satay was bland and tough, the beef curry had an odd texture with insufficient meat, and the shrimp on the pad thai were particularly revolting—they tasted muddy and had no seasoning at all. When I mentioned the shrimp's flavor to the server, she insisted on explaining the source of the shrimp, which was frozen from the vendor. I couldn't care less about the origin; it was just gross! She refused to have the cook taste it, which was frustrating. I almost felt ill from the shrimp. I'm deeply disappointed by this terrible experience and will continue searching for a better Thai restaurant nearby.

yelp:train:192593.orig:
OK, my foodie friends...what follows is a description of one of my top 3 Restaurant meals, from last night at Yasu Sushi Bistro on Cactus and Tatum. Hands down the best sushi place in AZ.  We have been going there for about 5 years, but this is the first time we left it all in the hands of our Chef, Yasu Hashino and ordered Omakase.
We sat at the sushi bar, and Chef seemed delighted to create a special experience for us... he asked if anything was off limits, only Uni I said. Sea Urchin is not my bag...but everything else was on the table.  We placed an order from his small, but exquisite wine list and picked a 2010 Byron Pinot Noir Santa Maria Valley.  All of his seafood is less than 24 hours old, flown to Phoenix from the Tokyo fish market daily.  What follows is a description of foodie heaven....
Yuzu Kanpachi - 6 perfect slices of baby yellowtail from Hawaii, finely slivered Japanese peppers and lemon, topped with ponzu.
6 fresh, briny, on ice fresh Coromandel oysters from New Zealand
Ocean Trout Carpaccio - another delightful sashimi type dish of a fatty, fresh fish also from New Zealand  with a warm olive oil and slivered garlic chips and shaved daikon radish
Mushroom sa
yelp:train:192593.para:
Sure, here's the paraphrased version:

My food-loving buddies, I want to share a description of one of my top three restaurant meals from last night at Yasu Sushi Bistro on Cactus and Tatum. It's undoubtedly the best sushi place in Arizona. We've been frequenting this spot for about five years, but this time, we let Chef Yasu Hashino take the reins and prepared an Omakase menu.

We sat at the sushi bar, and Chef was excited to craft a personalized experience for us. He inquired if anything was off-limits, and I mentioned that sea urchin wasn't my preference, but everything else was fair game. We selected a 2010 Byron Pinot Noir from Santa Maria Valley from his small yet exquisite wine list. All his seafood is less than 24 hours old, flown daily from the Tokyo fish market.

Here's a taste of foodie paradise:

Yuzu Kanpachi - six impeccably sliced baby yellowtail from Hawaii, garnished with finely diced Japanese peppers and lemon, and drizzled with ponzu.

Six fresh, briny, ice-cold Coromandel oysters from New Zealand.

Ocean Trout Carpaccio - a delightful sashimi-style dish featuring a fatty, fresh fish from New Zealand, served with warm olive oil, slivered garlic chips, and shaved daikon radish.

yelp:train:192704.orig: The food here was great! Wish there was more indoor seating, but the seating both indoor and outside is nice, live music sometimes, nice decor.  I've tried a few of the specialty drinks, some are good some are so/so but isn't it always that way? Just preferences.  The prices are a bit high, but the portions are worth it, we can split a meal typically.  The Deserts are awesome too!
yelp:train:192704.para: The food is fantastic, though I wish there were more indoor tables. Both the indoor and outdoor seating are pleasant, and there's sometimes live music, which adds to the ambiance. The decor is also quite nice. I've sampled a few specialty drinks; some are excellent, while others are just okay—personal taste varies, after all. The prices are on the higher side, but the portion sizes are generous enough that we can share. The desserts are outstanding!

yelp:train:194183.orig: Should've just stopped at McDonald's. SLOW service and unfriendly waitress. Any request was answered with a sour look. Took so long for the food to come and it was not anything special. The table next to us was sitting with dirty plates and old food the entire time we were here. Will not go back.
yelp:train:194183.para: I wish I had gone to McDonald's instead. The service was extremely slow, and the waitress was unfriendly, giving a sour expression to any request. The food took a long time to arrive and wasn't particularly impressive. Our neighbors at the adjacent table had leftover dirty plates and old food the whole time we were there. I definitely won't be returning.

yelp:train:194341.orig: this place is always on our list of things to do downtown(where the actions at) ...it is a small casino packed with action...a good scene to observe...tourists and locals, yukkin it up, getting hopped up on cheap drinks...(football beers and high octane yards) and great snacks....live a little and have the deep fried oreos,twinkies and one of several hot dog variations.....nothing stuffy about this place....ive seen pimps, ho's, bro's and an assortment of drunks...all getting along....everyone needs a little mermaid in there life!
yelp:train:194341.para: This spot is consistently on our list of must-dos downtown where all the action happens. It's a compact casino brimming with excitement, a great place to watch the scene unfold. You'll see tourists and locals alike having a blast, getting tipsy on affordable drinks, cheering for football, and enjoying high-energy games. The food is fantastic too—try the deep-fried Oreos, Twinkies, and various hot dog options. There's no pretense here; you might spot pimps, models, friends, and a mix of drunks all mingling together. Everyone could use a little mermaid in their life!

yelp:train:194411.orig: We been going to Vegas since 1978 an this is the first year to stay downtown, easy walking everywhere friendly people an found the Mermaid Casino by accident, wow what a great place to have relaxing fun, we spend 4 nights there playing the slots an the video poker, didn't win a lot but we won every night, Connie was our main waitress an she took very good care of my wife an I with a smile on her face all night, she would give us a quick story on the downtown district an was always there with fresh drink for us even when we walked in the door, Mermaids will always be our gaming place from here on out, all the girls working there were very nice to us, its a lot bigger inside that it looks so give it a try one evening an you wont be sorry. Thank You Connie for making us feel at home an for your kindness, we will be back.   Bill & Ellen Woods
yelp:train:194411.para: Since 1978, we've visited Vegas, and this year, we decided to stay downtown for the first time. It was a pleasant surprise to stumble upon the Mermaid Casino by accident. We had a fantastic experience there, enjoying relaxing fun and playing slots and video poker for four nights. Although we didn't win much, we did win every night. Our server, Connie, was incredibly attentive and friendly, always smiling and ready with a quick update on the downtown area. She ensured we had fresh drinks whenever we entered. We're committed to making Mermaid our go-to casino from now on. All the staff there were very kind to us. The casino is much larger inside than it appears from the outside, so it's definitely worth a visit. Thank you, Connie, for making us feel at home and for your kindness. We look forward to returning. Bill & Ellen Woods

yelp:train:194425.orig:
In keeping with the Italian theme today, I decided gelato would make nice sweet treat after my delightful experience at Best of Italy (see how I interweave these things together...but wait, there's more!).
In a rare ""daily double"" I am able to interweave National Pizza Party Day (come on...pizza is mostly Italian) with National Strawberry Month...That's right...strawberry Gelato!!!!
There has been much less attitude and better  service by the staff on my recent visits to the G-Spot, and for that they get my thanks and my gelato dollars.
It's funny, ever since Gabi posted the thread about strawberries...I've had a bit of a craving.
G-Spot...you scratched my itch very nicely today:)
yelp:train:194425.para:
Following the Italian theme of the day, I opted for gelato as a sweet treat following my enjoyable visit to Best of Italy (see how I connect these elements?). Today, I managed to blend National Pizza Party Day (after all, pizza is largely Italian) with National Strawberry Month, resulting in strawberry gelato!

The service at G-Spot has improved significantly during my recent visits, and I appreciate that; I’ll be sure to support them with my gelato purchases.

It’s interesting how Gabi’s thread about strawberries sparked a craving in me. G-Spot really hit the spot today, satisfying my desire perfectly.

yelp:train:194836.orig:
Awww man!!  This has been my favorite sushi joint for a year-ish!  The Japanese Lasagne is to die for.

We got the all you can eat sushi and was ignored the whole time we were there.  It was taking 20 minutes in between each order. WHA???  It wasn't even busy. The waitress was evil, she was rude and I swear she shit in my food because after I left I was sick!  I was so nice to her and tried to give her the benefit of the doubt, she had helped me two times before and it was the same story. So now, here I am venting my experience here.

WA, ditch that waitress, she's tainting your business. The runners were delightful and very sweet. 

Really sucks, I would gleam over Sushi Wa but after this visit, I won't be going again :(
yelp:train:194836.para:
Aww man! This place has been my go-to sushi spot for about a year, and their Japanese Lasagne is amazing.

We tried the all-you-can-eat option, but we were completely ignored. There was a 20-minute wait between each order, even though the place wasn't busy at all. The waitress was really unhelpful; she was rude and I felt like she might have tampered with my food because I got sick after eating it. I tried to be nice to her, as she had helped me before, but it was the same disappointing experience. Now, I'm sharing my frustration here.

Switch to a different waitress; she's ruining the experience for customers. The runners, on the other hand, were very sweet and helpful.

This really disappoints me. I was considering giving Sushi Wa another chance, but after this visit, I won't be returning.

yelp:train:194848.orig:
I found this place about a year ago and it is the best sushi I have had in Vegas, which I know is a biiiiiiig statement. 

Over the past 10 years or so I have eaten at dozens of sushi restaurants in this town (on the strip as well) and I can't say I have enjoyed any as much as this place. The fish is stellar, the customer service is amazing, and the rolls are innovative and flavorful.

What brought me back is the fact that I can easily eat $100 worth of sushi in one sitting. I prefer all-yo-can-eat venues because frankly, it's cheaper. Most of the time you find yourself at one of these places, the rolls are basic and not very good, or you are prohibited from ordering any of the ""good"" rolls. Not this place!!! If it is on the menu, you can order it (and as much as you like). Any app, roll, sashimi, nigiri; it's all fair game. The funny thing is the place is almost always empty! It's a really nice place right next door to Shakespeare's (a trendy bar). I am positive that this is just a secret among those who live in Green Valley. This place is a must-go for any Vegas sushi-addict.
yelp:train:194848.para:
I discovered this sushi spot about a year ago, and it's the best I've had in Vegas—quite a bold claim, I know. 

In the last decade, I've dined at numerous sushi restaurants in this city, both on and off the strip, and I haven't found any that match this place. The fish is top-notch, the service is outstanding, and the rolls are both inventive and delicious.

What keeps me coming back is the ability to indulge in $100 worth of sushi in one sitting. I favor all-you-can-eat places because they're more cost-effective. Typically, at these venues, the rolls are either mundane or of poor quality, or you're restricted from ordering the "premium" options. Not here! If it's on the menu, you can order it, and as much as you want. Whether it's an appetizer, a roll, sashimi, or nigiri, it's all available. Interestingly, the place is often nearly empty, despite its quality. It's a lovely spot right beside Shakespeare's (a popular bar). I'm convinced this is a well-kept secret among locals from Green Valley. This place is a must-visit for any sushi enthusiast in Vegas.

yelp:train:195086.orig:
Three cheers for a good restaurant right next door to the movies! Yea!

We've been countless times, both for lunch and dinner and always enjoy a delicious meal. If you get there at the right time, there's live music as well.

On to the food! The Tostones are so good...smashed fried plaintains topped with either ground beef, shredded beef or shrimp. We always get the shrimp and they're always tender, crisp perfection. My favorite appetizer is the Papas Rellenas. I could eat these every day. They're a humble, comforting dish...mashed potatoes rolled into a ball with a surprise of seasoned ground beef hidden in the middle. They are then fried to a delicate brown on the outside and served with a crispy plaintain chip. This and a salad is lunch perfection for me! Also nice on the appetizer menu is a mini cuban sandwich when you just can't handle the big one. My kids always order it as the kids menu only has ham and cheese. The black bean soup is everything you want a black bean soup to be. The only salad I order is the Ensalada Havana...sliced green apples, oranges, cashews and chicken over greens with shaved manchego and a sweet vinaigrette...so good!
Let's see to the entrees... T
yelp:train:195086.para:
Praise for a fantastic nearby eatery that's perfect for movie nights! Hooray!

We frequent it often, enjoying delightful meals for both lunch and dinner. Sometimes, if you arrive at the right time, you can catch live music too.

Now, let's talk about the food! The Tostones are outstanding—smashed fried plantains, topped with ground beef, shredded beef, or shrimp. We always opt for the shrimp, which are always tender and perfectly crispy. My go-to appetizer is the Papas Rellenas. I could eat these daily—they're simple yet comforting, mashed potatoes rolled into balls with seasoned ground beef inside. They're fried to a light brown and served with a crispy plantain chip. This, paired with a salad, makes for the perfect lunch. For a lighter option, there's a mini Cuban sandwich on the appetizer menu, which my kids prefer over the ham and cheese option on the kids' menu. The black bean soup is just as it should be. My favorite salad is the Ensalada Havana, featuring sliced green apples, oranges, cashews, and chicken over greens, topped with shaved manchego and a sweet dressing—it's delicious!

Moving on to the main courses...

yelp:train:196005.orig: Taco Bell, it is what it is man. But they always deliver! and HEALTH... hey man, you DO get lettuce, tomato, cheese.... they havent found those to cause cancer yet!! TACO BELL.. the only thing worth eating after midnight!
yelp:train:196005.para: Taco Bell is what it is, but they consistently deliver. And when it comes to health, you do get lettuce, tomato, and cheese—ingredients that haven't been linked to cancer! In fact, Taco Bell is the only place worth visiting after midnight!

yelp:train:196120.orig:
The rooms are clean and the service is decent, but the walls are thin enough to follow the television programming in the room on one side of your own while simultaneously enjoying the ecstatic moans and mattress squeaking from your neighbors on the other side. Thankfully the rooms come equipped with a refridgerator, and the constant grumbling  of the ancient cooling unit will do its best to drown out the ruckus in the adjacent rooms. If you're not the type of person who is lulled to sleep by the groan of struggling machinery, unplugging it will only give you the peace and quiet necessary to truly focus on the aforementioned activities of your neighbors.

If you're checking in here because it's stumbling distance from the establishment next door with women in various states of undress displaying their vertical barre workouts, then this place is for you, and you'll no doubt be either too drunk or too busy to mind the noises coming from the adjacent rooms or your ailing fridge.

However, if you're interested in an uninterrupted night of sleep, you'd best look elsewhere. Weeknights or weekends, the pattern is the same. Checking in here is like unwittingly signing a release to take
yelp:train:196120.para:
The accommodations are tidy and the staff is satisfactory, yet the walls are so thin that you can hear the TV and the excitement from the room next door while you're trying to relax. Fortunately, each room has a fridge, and the noisy compressor will help mask the commotion from neighboring rooms. If you're not soothed by the hum of old machinery, unplugging it will provide the silence needed to focus on your neighbors' activities.

If you're staying here because it's close to the nearby venue where women showcase their fitness, this place suits you. You might be too tipsy or engrossed to notice the noise from adjacent rooms or your malfunctioning fridge.

However, if you seek a peaceful night's sleep, you should consider other options. Whether it's a weekday or weekend, the disturbance remains consistent. Staying here feels like you're agreeing to a deal that includes sharing your room with the sounds of others.

yelp:train:197044.orig: this is a nice hotel that's located in a good spot in scottsdale as it is right by a stop for the free trolley which is decent but has some interesting drivers but i digress.  the lobby and the rest of interior has a very ultra contemporary feel to it.  the rooms are cool and the bathrooms are unique.  the pool area is really nice and the i don't if it was that particular day or not but the temperature was perfect.  the water was a bit salty but that's all good.
yelp:train:197044.para: This hotel in Scottsdale is quite pleasant, situated conveniently near a free trolley stop. While the trolley has some quirky drivers, that's not the main focus. The interior, including the lobby, exudes a modern, ultra-contemporary vibe. The rooms are stylish, and the bathrooms are distinctive. The pool area is particularly enjoyable, and the weather that day was ideal—though the water was a tad salty, which was fine.

yelp:train:197370.orig:
Terrible bar and terrible service. Every time I have come here I've waited twenty minutes to get a drink while some fratboy high school all star has gotten free drinks all night because they know the bartender. Owners also own the train wreck that is Andrew Blair's next door. 

This bar along with Andrew Blairs is a recreation of the Charlotte high school scene. If you did not go to high school in Charlotte, you will not get drinks and not know anyone here. I was completely miserable. 

Let's not forget the bartender who gave free drinks to young men who paid her for haircuts during the week. This kind of stuff is not how you run a business and I won't be coming back.
yelp:train:197370.para:
This establishment and its service are both poor. Each visit, I've had to wait about 20 minutes for a drink, while a local high school star gets free drinks due to knowing the bartender. The owners also run the nearby bar, Andrew Blair's, which is equally problematic.

This place and Andrew Blair's recreate the Charlotte high school experience. If you didn't attend Charlotte high school, you won't fit in and won't get served. I found the entire experience extremely unpleasant.

Additionally, the bartender doled out free drinks to men who paid her for haircuts during the week. This kind of behavior is unprofessional and won't lead to a successful business. I won't be returning.

yelp:train:197496.orig:
Everything started out great for my purchase of flooring material to replace aging tile in the living room.  I stopped in yesterday to see laminate hardwood flooring as well as vinyl planks and Associate Chris was very knowledgeable and helpful.  I had also taken a look at the flooring at Lowe's, but I was so impressed with the help I had been given here that I drove twice as far to buy here from Chris.

Chris wasn't on duty when I arrived, but Associate Jamie was also friendly & able to answer my remaining questions as I decided what to buy.  So far, we're at 5 Stars!

THEN, I got up to the checkout & THEY TRIED TO OVERCHARGE ME!  As a matter of policy, any business that cheats me on the money gets ONE STAR & I never return.  The flooring was clearly priced at $1.59/sq. ft. at the display & it rang up at $1.79.  Now this wasn't the fault of the cashier, but then she wanted to make it ""iffy"" whether or not I would get it at the advertised price.  NO IT ISN'T!

Ok, so after a few minutes of delay & hassle I left with my flooring at the posted price.  The service was so good from both Chris & Jamie that they saved this Home Depot from getting a vote to send it to Yelp 1-Sta
yelp:train:197496.para:
My flooring purchase began well, with the replacement of old tiles in the living room. Yesterday, I visited to check out laminate hardwood and vinyl planks, and Associate Chris was extremely knowledgeable and helpful. Although I had already looked at flooring at Lowe's, I was so impressed by the assistance here that I drove a longer distance to buy from Chris.

When I arrived, Chris wasn't there, but Jamie, another associate, was just as friendly and answered my questions. Everything was going smoothly until checkout. They tried to overcharge me, which is a policy I cannot tolerate. Any business that cheats on prices gets a one-star rating and I won't return. The flooring was clearly marked at $1.59 per square foot, but it was charged at $1.79.

While the cashier wasn't at fault, she made it unclear if I would get the advertised price. No, I would not. After a bit of delay, I left with the flooring at the correct price. Despite the overcharge, the service from Chris and Jamie was so good that it saved this Home Depot from a one-star rating on Yelp.

yelp:train:197542.orig: Not only is this an awesome theme restaurant, it's also one of the Best Italian food in the Country. The entire atmosphere is a great place to take friends or even on a romantic date. The singer who does Frank Sinatra is FANTASTIC!!!!!  Order the Meatballs to start and you will be hooked. The bread, Butter, Pasta, Drinks, I could go on and on. You should be privileged to even get to eat at Capo's. This is a Legit Wise guy place. If your stuffy or have a stick up your ass or drink your wine with your pinkie finger out, or  you don't like the Italian attitude stay home or go to Wolfgang pucks. hahahaha
yelp:train:197542.para: This restaurant isn't just fantastic; it's also among the top Italian eateries in the country. The ambiance is perfect for both friends and romantic dinners. The singer performing Frank Sinatra is absolutely amazing! Start with the meatballs, and you'll be hooked. From the bread and butter to the pasta and drinks, everything is top-notch. You're lucky to dine at Capo's. This place is genuinely authentic and old-school. If you're pretentious, sip your wine with your pinky out, or dislike the Italian vibe, you might want to stay home or go somewhere else like Wolfgang Pucks. Hahahaha.

yelp:train:197805.para:
The sole reason to visit this place is if you have a precise idea of what you're looking for and don't require assistance—staff often gather in groups, discussing topics unrelated to customer support. Although they offer a broad range of computer components, other retailers provide similar items at competitive prices with more helpful staff.

yelp:train:198110.orig:
Been coming to Jason's since they had a location across the street from PV Mall back in the early 90's. Their restaurants are always pretty decent and the food is tasty good. This location on Shea appears to have had a remodel since we were here last time and the inside looks really nice.

The menu has changed a bit over the years and is smaller than I remember. They used to have a larger selection of stuffed potatoes and now only have a few. My favorite was a smokey BBQ Beef stuffed potato with tons of other goodies. I think you could even build your own at one time.

The wife and I usually go with the famous New Orleans 9"" FULL size Ham and Salami Muffaletta. It is hard to resist some additional Olive spread on the side and a little hot sauce to kick things up a notch. The sandwich is giant and we normally have a good portion to bring home for a snack later.

There are plenty of other options that are also fresh and tasty. Cool all you can eat Salad Bar to indulge yourself. Yummy Soups, maybe a bowl of Chili, as well as Wraps and Pasta if you desire. They also have a nice Kid's menu with the typical favorites for the little ones.

Friendly service and a casually comfort
yelp:train:198110.para:
I've been visiting Jason's since there was a location near PV Mall in the early 90s. Their restaurants have generally been good, and the food has always been tasty. The Shea location seems to have undergone a remodel, and the interior now looks really nice.

The menu has changed a bit over the years and is smaller than I recall. They used to offer a wider variety of stuffed potatoes, but now only a few remain. My favorite was the smokey BBQ Beef stuffed potato, packed with various ingredients. It seems you could even customize your own at one time.

My wife and I typically order the famous New Orleans 9" FULL size Ham and Salami Muffaletta. It's hard to resist adding some extra olive spread and a bit of hot sauce to spice things up. The sandwich is enormous, and we usually take a good portion home for a snack later.

There are many other options that are also fresh and delicious. They have a cool all-you-can-eat salad bar, yummy soups, maybe a bowl of chili, wraps, and pasta if you prefer. They also have a nice kids' menu with typical favorites for the little ones.

The service is friendly, and the atmosphere is casually comfortable.

yelp:train:198522.orig: Not my favorite buffet, but definately a good value.  Good selection, a little bland, but still tasty.  And very convenient.
yelp:train:198522.para: While it's not my top choice for buffets, it offers great value. The variety is good, though it could be more flavorful, and it's quite convenient.

yelp:train:198683.orig:
Got another coupon for 2 free dinner buffets at the palms - i haven't been there since they opened ( also a freebie ) didn't care for the place then...like it even less now...

salad bar -  ehhhh - they make a big deal about ""freezing"" the salad bowls...they have 2 sushi choices...looks like they were purchased at the deli counter at albertson's...but hey...it's a salad bar...who cares !?!

they have sections based on cuisine - mediterranean, chinese, italian, american, etc.. ...for the most part , i think the food is prepared in big microwaves in the back room.  

the carving station - saw a big chunk of meat - asked the carver is that brisket ??  yes...i'll take a piece...one bite...it's ham !!!  are you shittin' me ?  i almost wanted to go up a 2nd time and ask , "" is that shit ??"" answer ...yes....ok gimme a slice !

i actually liked the turkey...big deal....

geez palms...you outta be ashamed !!
yelp:train:198683.para:
Received another coupon for two free dinner buffets at The Palms—haven't visited since it opened, and my impression hasn't improved. 

Salad bar: Meh—there's a big fuss about "freezing" the salad bowls. They offer two sushi options, which seem to be from the deli at Albertson's. But who cares, it's a salad bar!

The menu is divided into cuisine sections like Mediterranean, Chinese, Italian, and American. Most of the food appears to be microwaved in the back.

At the carving station, I saw a large piece of meat and asked if it was brisket. The carver confirmed it was, so I took a bite. It turned out to be ham! Are you kidding me? I almost asked again, "Is that really ham?" The answer was yes, so I asked for a slice.

The only thing I liked was the turkey, but that's not much to be excited about.

The Palms, you should be embarrassed!

yelp:train:198935.orig: had watch Ride Along with my date. Its upscale I get it but even for Upscale its ridiculously high priced. Popcorn is 8? Seriously? Skip it and order food. My shrimps were cooked to perfection. Drinks on the other hand were over priced. Next time ill try the recliners and see what the fuss is about. I really use to like Studio Movie grill until they decided to change their menu and got rid of all the good items. Never going there for sure.
yelp:train:198935.para: I watched Ride Along with my date, and while it's an upscale place, the prices are shockingly high—popcorn costs 8 dollars? That's ridiculous. I'd rather skip it and get food elsewhere. My shrimp was cooked perfectly, but the drinks were overpriced. Maybe next time I'll try the recliners to see what all the hype is about. I used to really enjoy Studio Movie Grill, but after they changed their menu and removed the good items, I won't be going back for sure.

yelp:train:200227.orig: Great time, great people, well recommended
yelp:train:200227.para: A wonderful experience with fantastic individuals; I highly recommend it.

yelp:train:200545.orig: Overall this is now my favorite hotel in Vegas for several reasons.   Location, price, room, and spa.   We enjoyed our stay and will be back in Aug 2014.  Room was clean and great view of strip.  Central location you can walk right on to the strip.  Hugh spa very relaxing, and decent price for room we got.
yelp:train:200545.para: This hotel in Vegas has become my top choice for multiple reasons: its location, price, room quality, and spa. We had a pleasant stay and plan to return in August 2014. The room was clean, and we had a fantastic view of the strip. Its central position allows for easy walking access to the strip. The large spa was very relaxing, and the room price was reasonable.

yelp:train:200714.orig:
OYSTERS OYSTERS OYSTERS.

I don't think I'd get anything else here...the Penazzi features oysters for a great price. You can get 'em raw, baked, or deep fried. The Rockerfellers are too rich for my taste (as oysters pack enough cholesterol for me) so getting a few dozen raw oysters to share with friends is what I normally do.

The ambiance here isn't great and yeah, it's Harrah's, but damn those oysters are good!
yelp:train:200714.para:
OYSTERS OYSTERS OYSTERS.

I'm pretty sure I'd only order oysters here...the Penazzi menu offers them at a great price, and you can enjoy them raw, baked, or deep fried. While the Rockerfellers are too rich for my preference, I usually opt for a dozen raw oysters to share with friends. The atmosphere isn't top-notch, and it is Harrah's, but those oysters are truly delicious!

yelp:train:201142.orig: Food is not very good, atmosphere isn't either. Lots of TVs is all they have going for them.
yelp:train:201142.para: The food and atmosphere are both lacking. The only positive aspect is the numerous TVs they have.

yelp:train:201215.orig: This place has the most delicious treats, the best part is it's less than 5 minutes from my work!
yelp:train:201215.para: The food here is incredibly tasty, and the best thing is its location—just under 5 minutes from my office!

yelp:train:201248.orig:
Sorry to be the bearer of bad news, but I went here to get a rejuvenating yummy bowl of goodness, which I could eat every day, and my hopes were thwarted.

I got about 1/2 way though my rare beef & flank Pho, when I was overcome with a deathly feeling.  My poor colleague said I turned pale white and looked awful.  I broke into a sweat and quickly paid our bill, dropped him off at work, and headed home.  

Thank goodness I live nearby.  I barely got through the front door before all systems went full reverse.  

With all the options out there, I think I'll have to scratch this place of my list.  Sorry :(  I had such high hopes.
yelp:train:201248.para:
I apologize for the disappointing experience. I was excited to enjoy a delicious Pho that I could savor daily, but my expectations were dashed. 

I managed to eat only half of my rare beef and flank Pho when I suddenly felt extremely unwell. My colleague noticed I had turned pale and looked terrible, and I started sweating profusely. I quickly settled the bill, dropped him off at work, and rushed home. 

Fortunately, I live close by. I barely made it to the door before I felt even worse. 

Given the many other options available, I'll have to remove this place from my list of favorites. I was really looking forward to it.

yelp:train:201651.orig: Love this place! All of their breakfast entrees are solid across the board - you really cant wrong ordering anything. Pancakes and omelets are outstanding and equally important, they are consistent - tastes great every time and this has been our regular breakfast stop for well over a year now. Just like any quality breakfast joint, you really need to get there early to avoid the rush otherwise, be prepared to wait and while.
yelp:train:201651.para: I adore this spot! Their breakfast options are consistently excellent—pretty much any choice you make will be great. The pancakes and omelets are particularly outstanding and consistently delicious. We've been frequenting this place for over a year, and it remains our go-to for breakfast. Like any good breakfast place, you should arrive early to avoid the crowds; otherwise, you might have to wait.

yelp:train:201699.orig: Decent all you can eat but a bit dirty inside. I'd rather eat at the Denny's next door then risk getting sick here again. Yes, I said again. The meat looks like its been left over from the night before and the cooks are American so this is an americanized sushi place that just doesn't cut it.
yelp:train:201699.para: The all-you-can-eat option is okay, but the place is a bit messy inside. I prefer eating at the Denny's nearby to avoid getting sick again. Yes, I mean it this time. The meat seems to have been left out overnight, and since the cooks are American, this place feels more like an Americanized sushi joint that falls short of expectations.

yelp:train:201711.orig: I have visited this store many times looking for just the right piece for my loft. When ready to make a purchase, I found a dining table and chair set that I very much liked and thought would fit nicely with my decor. The table was marked at $2,100.00 but the chairs had no price tags. I asked to speak to the owner so as to negotiate a price for the entire set and was asked to wait, as he was on his way in. I waited for 20 minutes, when he finally showed. When I casually asked if the price included the chairs, the \""gentleman\"" literally laughed at me, turned around, and walked away without saying a word. Humiliated, I followed him into the other room and stated that I should assume that it didn't. His very flippant reply to me was, \""The chairs cost $800 a piece!\""...and proceeded to turn his back on me once again. I had $4,000.00 cash in my pocket that day to make a purchase and he and his business not only lost out that day, but I will never make a purchase from that man if that's the way he's going to treat his customers!
yelp:train:201711.para: On multiple visits to this store in search of the perfect item for my loft, I found a dining table and chair set that I adored and believed would complement my decor well. The table was priced at $2,100, but the chairs lacked price tags. I requested to speak with the owner to discuss the total cost of the set, and was told to wait as he was en route. After 20 minutes, he appeared. When I casually inquired if the price included the chairs, the "gentleman" laughed at me, turned around, and left without a word. Feeling humiliated, I followed him into another room and assumed the chairs were not included. His dismissive response was, "The chairs cost $800 each!"—and he turned his back on me again. With $4,000 in cash that day, I felt this store and its owner not only missed an opportunity that day but also lost a potential customer like me.

yelp:train:202181.para:
I never imagined I'd set foot in The Palms Hotel & Casino, but the Pearl venue and The Cure's performance there compelled me to go. I braced myself and waited at a small indoor bar for my credentials, which I received. Did you know who I am? A woman in her 50s did, and she joined us, eventually convincing us to buy her a drink. She didn't recognize me, but called me "thick," which I found amusing.

"Thick, you know, like a girl with some curves! You might be Latino or Mexican, with those curves! " 

"So, you're saying I'm fat?" 

"No, girl! Thick. Thee-ick! That's a good thing. Brothers love thick! " 

The Pearl is a fantastic venue, reminiscent of a smaller indoor Greek Theatre. Every seat offers an excellent view, though it's not cheap; GA floor tickets for The Cure were around $150. My Mezzanine tickets, three rows from the front, were in the center, providing a great view, sound, and comfortable seating. The bar has a full menu, but the prices are quite steep.

yelp:train:202226.orig:
Had a great time here... if only I could recall more of the night... :) 

I understand the cover is high... although we didn't pay I would have paid to get in. The playboy bunny's are adorable and happy to take photos with those who ask. The gents working door and what not were super sweet. 

I didn't gamble at all but, but, when I go again I will plan to drink less so I can.
yelp:train:202226.para:
Enjoyed my visit immensely... it's just a shame I can't remember more details from the night... :) 

The cover charge is on the higher side, but even if I had to pay, it would still be worth it. The Playboy bunnies are charming and willing to pose for photos with guests. The staff at the entrance and elsewhere were exceptionally kind. 

Although I didn't gamble, for my next visit, I'll make sure to drink less so I can participate more.

yelp:train:202617.orig: Great selection of wine.\nStaff is friendly and helpful\nThe Som is a amazing man to speak with.
yelp:train:202617.para: A wonderful variety of wines is available. The staff is both friendly and helpful, and the Som is an exceptional person to converse with.

yelp:train:202921.para:
The worst offenders. Check the reviews and online feedback; they frequently scam customers with web hosting or domain services.

yelp:train:202994.para: Eating extremely spicy buffalo wings and limp french fries at 2am following a night of drinking long margaritas from cheesy cups with tambourines is never a wise choice. This kind of indulgence, especially at the All American Bar and Grille, is particularly problematic and is likely to cause heartburn.

yelp:train:203351.orig: Always wander through this store but never end up buying much. They were having a Moscato wine tasting today.  Picked up some EVOO and a wine glass since we broke one recently.
yelp:train:203351.para: I frequently browse this store without making many purchases. Today, they were hosting a Moscato wine tasting. I decided to grab some extra virgin olive oil and a new wine glass, as we had broken ours recently.

yelp:train:203543.orig:
First ride on the light rail and nowhere to go.  I have absolutely no need for this thing, but I wanted to try it anyway.  So, one evening in downtown my friend and I decided to see what kinda shenanigans we could find.  

Positive #1.  Crazy people.  God do I love crazy people.  A lovely lady sang Marvin Gay's ""Let's Get it On"" word for word to another passenger.  She even reached out and touched him as she belted ""lovin' you could never be wrong.""  I'm not sure if he liked it because he wasn't smiling on the outside, but I sure loved it.

Positive #2.  While riding I spotted some fun looking lights.  I ended up on the grass looking up at Sky Bloom in some downtown Phoenix park.  It was a nice little surprise.  

Positive#3.  Super clean and air conditioned.  It's nothing special, but it's not gross or smelly. 

Negative #1.  I have a dream, a dream where I can stumble out of the bar at 2am and ride the light rail all the way home.  In my dream the light rail actually takes me places, places I want or need to be.  

For now it's just a novelty- like, hey look at me!  I'm a big city, I have a light rail, wawawewoo, king of castle, bla bla bla.  Someday I will not
yelp:train:203543.para:
My first experience with the light rail was quite amusing, even though I didn't really need to use it. One evening, my friend and I explored downtown to see what interesting things we could encounter. 

Positive #1: Encountering eccentric individuals was delightful. A woman sang Marvin Gaye's "Let's Get It On" flawlessly to another passenger, even reaching out to touch him as she sang "loving you could never be wrong." While I'm unsure if he appreciated it, I found it endearing.

Positive #2: During the ride, I noticed some captivating lights. I ended up on the grass, admiring Sky Bloom in a downtown Phoenix park, which was a pleasant surprise.

Positive #3: The train was exceptionally clean and air-conditioned. While it wasn't extraordinary, it was certainly not unpleasant or smelly.

Negative #1: I dream of a scenario where I can exit a bar at 2 AM and use the light rail to get home, but in reality, it doesn't take me to the places I want or need to go.

For now, it's more of a novelty—like saying, "Look at me! I'm a big city with a light rail, hooray!" Hopefully, one day it will serve its intended purpose.

yelp:train:204017.orig:
D'lish doesn't need another review, but I love it so much that I couldn't resist.  

If I can help you out with anything, the key is to drench their sandwiches/wraps/flat breads in their chipotle aioli - game changer.  Makes their super delicious food even better.  

While it's 'fast food,' be prepared to wait as everything is made to order.  Totally worth it, and you will be occupied by reading the rest of the menu items, plotting your next order a week later.
yelp:train:204017.para:
D'lish is already fantastic, but I had to share my experience because I adore it so much. To enhance your meal, soak their sandwiches, wraps, or flatbreads in their chipotle aioli—it truly transforms the dish. This dressing elevates their already exquisite food even further.

Although it's categorized as fast food, be prepared for a wait since everything is made to order. It's definitely worth the time, and you'll likely spend the wait browsing the menu, already planning your next visit.

yelp:train:204132.orig: Nick's is a great little neighborhood Italian place. Of which there are not many in Phoenix.  It's small and intimate, the food is consistently good; my husband is always impressed with how fresh the fish and seafood is - we do live in the desert. He grew up on the east coast, lots of good Italian and fresh seafood so the fact that they make him happy says something.  Service is always good, Orlando always knows who we are and takes good care of us. There was a time in the past where service was lacking, and it was something they were aware of which is why they had a \""now hiring servers\"" sign up. Shortly after, they had some new people about the place and service was back on point.  I've never had a dish I didn't like here, and I'm the kind of person who likes to try all the menu has to offer; sometimes seafood, sometimes chicken, sometimes veggie - ravioli, linguini etc... It's all good. A favorite of mine is the farfalle salmon, it's a repeat on occasion.  Check out Nick's!
yelp:train:204132.para: Nick's is a wonderful, cozy Italian restaurant in the neighborhood, quite rare in Phoenix. It’s compact and warm, with consistently delicious food that impresses my husband, who grew up on the East Coast where fresh seafood is a staple. The fish and seafood here are always so fresh, considering we live in a desert. The service is consistently excellent; Orlando, our server, always remembers us and takes great care of us. There was a time when service was a bit lacking, but they addressed it by hiring new staff, and now the service is top-notch again. I’ve never found a dish I didn’t enjoy here, and I love trying everything on the menu—seafood, chicken, veggies, ravioli, linguini, and more; it’s all great. A particular favorite is the farfalle salmon, which I often order again. Give Nick's a try!

yelp:train:204145.orig: Went here for a manicure after previously having a shellac manicure elsewhere.  Instead of soaking my nails in remover for 5-10 minutes to take off the old polish, the nail technician pried/chiseled the old polish off with a fake nail.  It hurt and left my nails brittle until they grew out (over a month).  \n\nThere are plenty of great nail salons in the area that provide top notch service at an affordable price - don't waste your time here.
yelp:train:204145.para:
I visited this salon for a manicure following a previous shellac manicure at another place. Rather than using remover to gently remove the old polish, the technician forcibly removed it with a tool, which was painful and left my nails brittle for over a month until they regrew.

I recommend avoiding this salon, as there are many other excellent nail salons nearby that offer high-quality service at reasonable prices.

Luckily, my trusty crappy spare was still working, so on it went and off I went.  A mile or two out, still deep in the forest with no cell coverage, a two inch rock shaped like a fucking triangular arrowhead gashed its way into my spare which then hissed itself to death.

yelp:train:204174.para:
Discounts are great! I'd rate it around 4.5 stars (not 5 because they don't negotiate prices as much as they used to).

A few weeks after a flat tire on a remote trail, I hit another flat on a forest road between Strawberry and Camp Verde. Fortunately, my old spare was still functional, and I continued on my way. A mile or two later, in the deep forest with no cell service, a two-inch rock shaped like a triangular arrowhead punctured my spare, causing it to deflate.

My 13-year-old daughter and our two dogs then embarked on a moonlit, muddy hike back to the campsite, a journey that took about half an hour. We stayed until morning, and with everyone's kindness (campers are amazing!), we enjoyed a hearty breakfast and had a spare tire installed with plenty of help (can I leave a review for these folks? Five stars!).

Now back home, I've been shopping for tires at Pep Boys (the old guy provided poor customer service), Walmart (charges extra for everything if you have TPMS), and Firestone (decent price with a buy one get one free offer).

yelp:train:204749.para:
BEWARE OF THE $35 EYELASH EXTENSIONS EXPERIENCE

My first attempt at two-week lashes was a painful one, not due to an allergic reaction. I thought the price was reasonable, so I decided to give it a try. 

- The extensions should be placed ON TOP of your natural lashes, not below.
- The manager at Mirage Salon placed my extensions below my natural lashes, close to the water line.
- I informed her that it felt uncomfortable and that I could feel the lashes in my eyes. She claimed the lashes were just "stiff" and would relax in a few days.
- I experienced pain for a couple of days, even after using a hot washcloth to soften them multiple times.
- Some lashes fell out after a week, and my natural lashes came out with them.
- I ended up with thinner, damaged lashes.

When I complained to the salon manager, she said, "I warned you might have a reaction," and ignored the fact that the extensions were placed incorrectly. She offered a refund, but that wasn't satisfactory. The owner, who called me and was more pleasant, offered to remove the extensions and give me a refund. I went in for the refund and removal.

yelp:train:204873.orig:
This is a terrific homewares store!  Great selections of many categories of merchandise.  It ain't cheap, but it's all *quality* stuff. 

Most of the people are knowledgeable & happily helpful.

Almost everything I've bought here is completely satisfying.  On a rare occasion I've taken something back -- they simply replaced it or refunded my money.  No big deal about it.

Whenever I need something along their line, BB&B is where I go first.   Then I don't have to go anywhere else second.
yelp:train:204873.para:
This is an excellent homewares store with a wide range of quality merchandise across various categories. While it may not be budget-friendly, the products are of superior quality.

The staff is generally knowledgeable and very helpful. 

Almost all of my purchases have been highly satisfactory. On rare occasions, I've returned items, and they either replaced them or refunded my money without any hassle.

Whenever I need homewares, I always start with BB&B, and I never need to look elsewhere.

yelp:train:205171.orig: Overpriced items both in the store and on the menu compared to other kosher places in the area.
yelp:train:205171.para: Compared to other kosher establishments in the vicinity, the prices for items both in the store and on the menu are perceived as excessively high.

yelp:train:205207.para: As a Wells Fargo customer for a year and having deposited a significant amount, my account recently overdrafted due to economic difficulties and unemployment. yelp:train:205251.orig: Just got home from a private event at Polar Ice and it went great! yelp:train:205251.para: After returning from a private event at Polar Ice, everything turned out splendidly! Leanne, the event coordinator, was exceptionally cooperative and simplified the setup process, which was particularly helpful as we are a student organization at ASU. I arrived a bit early to ensure all was in order, and the event proceeded smoothly. yelp:train:205463.orig: its not the best mexican food, buts its good..  the homemade tortillas are very good..
yelp:train:205463.para: While it may not be the pinnacle of Mexican cuisine, it's still quite enjoyable. The homemade tortillas are particularly excellent.

yelp:train:205563.orig:
This place rocks. I chose it as payment from a buddy at work whom I had picked up a couple of pounds of chorizo from Bill's Market over the weekend for.  Man am I glad that we went here. I had read the reviews on yelp and even reached out to my fb network.  Most of the pre-meal feedback I had received was positive and I was confident that I was going to get a good meal.  

I drove up there (the place is at Via Linda and 90th next to Teakwoods) after viewing the menu on-line and had already narrowed down my sandwich choices to a couple.  Walking up to the restaurant I noticed seating for about a dozen or so folks outside. Walking inside I was immediately hit by the aromas of warm bread, baked goods, and other goodness. 

After double checking the menu and seeing that the soup of the day was chili (sounded good but not enough to deter me from ordering a sandwich today), I was ready to order one of their signature  sandwiches, the Long Trail. However I will have to wait for another day to get properly introduced to a sandwich that is constructed by their own roasted beef with crumbled bacon on sourdough with peppered horse radish mayo, muenster cheese, lettuce, tomato, red onion,
yelp:train:205563.para:
This spot is fantastic. My colleague from work recommended it to me after I picked up a couple pounds of chorizo from Bill's Market over the weekend. I'm really happy we decided to eat here. I had checked the Yelp reviews and also asked my Facebook friends for their thoughts. Most of the pre-meal feedback was positive, which made me confident about the quality of the food.

I drove there (it's located at Via Linda and 90th, next to Teakwoods) after looking at the menu online and had already decided on a couple of sandwich options. As I approached the restaurant, I noticed a seating area for about a dozen people outside. Entering the place, I was immediately greeted by the delightful aromas of warm bread, baked goods, and other delicious treats.

After reviewing the menu again and noting that the soup of the day was chili (which sounded good but wasn't enough to make me skip a sandwich), I was eager to order their signature Long Trail sandwich. It's made with their roasted beef, crumbled bacon, on sourdough bread, topped with peppered horseradish mayo, muenster cheese, lettuce, tomato, and red onion.

yelp:train:205865.orig: When I moved into my place a year ago, I was talked into \""locking in my rate\"" for 5 yrs. OK, it was a little higher than the standard rate, but they assured me in the long run, it would be worth it since the rates will never go up. OK, I fell for it, I signed up- at the higher rate. 7 months later, I got a price increase.....what??? So I called COX. Customer service reps says I'm not on the plan where rates are locked in, and supposedly had no idea what I was talking about and could find no notes relating to the conversation I had less than a year ago. I worked in a call center- I KNOW conversations are captured.  I promptly cancelled and called Dish. Service has been great and price is way cheaper. And the techs that come out actually WORK for Dish...not the shady contractors that COX hires that don't even have the right equipment for the job (the idiot they sent to me didn't even have a ladder!). Not a big fan of Century Link for my internet, but I wont give COX another dime.
yelp:train:205865.para: A year ago, I agreed to lock in my rate with Cox for five years, even though it was a bit higher than the regular rate. They assured me it would be beneficial in the long run, as rates would never increase. I signed up, thinking it was a good deal. Seven months later, I received a rate hike, which was surprising. When I contacted Cox, the customer service representatives claimed I wasn't on the locked-in rate plan and couldn't find any records of our conversation. I know from experience that calls are recorded, so I canceled my Cox service and switched to Dish. Dish's service has been excellent, and the prices are much lower. Additionally, the technicians from Dish actually do their work, unlike the shady contractors Cox uses, who often lack the necessary equipment. I'm not a fan of CenturyLink for my internet, but I won't be giving Cox any more of my money.

yelp:train:206032.orig: I thought Canada was bad with communication companies, but COX in Phx AZ. is the worst , at least in Canada you have three choices and they are more technological advanced, then COX. everything in these previous reviews have also happened to us. no need to repeat the same lousy customer service, reliability issues and tech product offering.\nWhy worry about ISIS when you have Cox.
yelp:train:206032.para: I found Canada's communication companies to be problematic, but COX in Phoenix, AZ, takes the cake. At least in Canada, you have multiple options with more advanced technology compared to COX. All the issues mentioned in previous reviews have also affected us—no need to rehash the poor customer service, reliability problems, and limited tech offerings. Why even bother with ISIS when you have COX?

yelp:train:206242.orig: Great food at a great price and always with a smile. The atmosphere is bright and friendly. I have been going to AZ Bread since it opened and there isn't a better breakfast or lunch place in the Valley. It just doesn't get any better.
yelp:train:206242.para: Since AZ Bread opened, I've been a regular, and I haven't found a better spot for breakfast or lunch in the Valley. The food is delicious and reasonably priced, and the staff always greets you with a smile. The place has a bright and welcoming ambiance. It truly is unbeatable.

yelp:train:206364.orig:
This is one of the dirtiest gas stations I have ever encountered.  A little power-washing would go a long way.  Or, if that is too difficult, perhaps try simply emptying the overflowing trash cans periodically?  

At any given time, a minimum of 3 of the 12 pumps are out of order.  The ones that do work are covered with scratched-in graffiti markings.  Classy.

The only redeeming quality is that the gas is usually a few cents cheaper than nearby competitors.  The only reason I keep coming back.

I guess you really do get what you pay for...
yelp:train:206364.para:
This gas station is one of the filthiest I've seen. A thorough power-washing would greatly improve it. Alternatively, regularly emptying the overflowing trash cans could help.

At any moment, at least three out of the twelve fuel pumps are non-functional. The ones that are operational are marred by scratched graffiti. Not exactly elegant.

The only positive is that the gas is typically a few cents cheaper than at nearby stations, which is why I continue to return. It seems you really do get what you pay for.

yelp:train:206745.orig: Been doing business with bookman's for years but I guess the economy finally caught up to them. The store credit offer on collectables or music related items is really low ball nowadays. It is not even worth the time and gas to be honest. I suggest doing some checking as what the value of your items are so you are not scammed at trade in OR purchase. Some of the items for sale are overpriced and going more than new retail. If the tag says rare that means you can find it on the internet in abundance. Heck sell your stuff on the internet or give it to goodwill. I hope things improve but for now I'm moving on.
yelp:train:206745.para: I've been dealing with Bookman's for a long time, but it seems the economic situation has finally affected them. The store credit they offer for collectibles or music items is quite low, making it not even worth the effort and gas to go there. I recommend checking the value of your items before trading or buying to avoid being cheated. Some of the items for sale are overpriced, often more than new retail prices. If something is labeled as rare, it's usually available online in abundance. You might as well sell your items online or donate them to Goodwill. I hope things get better, but for now, I'm looking for other options.

yelp:train:206784.para:

Spraying window cleaner by my plate is not a good idea. :)  \nThe food was so-so and service OK.  What else to say?  Wish I could like the place, its close to home.
yelp:train:207006.para:
The buffet offers Chinese cuisine, but I don't see myself returning. I really don't appreciate the staff cleaning windows right beside my table while I'm eating; it's not a pleasant experience. The window cleaner near my food is definitely a no-go. 

The food was mediocre, and the service was just okay. There's not much else to comment on. I wish I could enjoy this place more, as it's conveniently located near my home.

yelp:train:207109.orig:
Ok, so this ISN'T new.  It is actually a correction.  I didn't realize until I dropped off my car this morning that there's another place with a VERY similar name--SORRY!  

I kept getting coupons in the mail for this place, so I decided to check it out.  I recently had an auto repair shop tell me I needed to replace both front & rear brakes and wanted a second quote before forking over cash I didn't really want to part with.  

They did a full inspection and not only negated what the first auto place told me but provided a report showing how much 'brake' life I had left before I needed to bring it in for replacement.  They could've just taken my money but this demonstrated they wanted to keep me as a customer and that's exactly what they got.

I now take my car there for routine oil changes and other work (e.g., engine flush, etc) when necessary.

7/1/08  Just dropped off my car for routine service.  They've now added free wifi for customers who want to wait @ the shop.  I luv me some free wifi.
yelp:train:207109.para:
Sure, here is the paraphrased text:

Previously, I thought this was something new, but it turns out it's actually a correction. I only realized there's another place with a strikingly similar name when I dropped off my car this morning—my apologies! 

I had been receiving coupons in the mail from this place, so I decided to visit. Recently, an auto repair shop suggested I needed to replace both front and rear brakes, and I sought a second opinion before spending money I wasn't eager to part with.

Upon inspection, they not only contradicted the first shop's assessment but also provided a detailed report showing how much brake life I had left. Instead of just taking my money, they demonstrated a commitment to keeping me as a customer, which is exactly what they achieved.

Now, I regularly take my car there for routine oil changes and other necessary work, such as engine flushes.

On July 1, 2008, I dropped off my car for routine service. They've recently added free Wi-Fi for customers waiting at the shop, and I really appreciate having free internet access.

yelp:train:207464.orig: If you're looking for a dining experience at Fry's deli area you're better off going to an actual sit down restaurant.  Fry's \""dining style\"" food in the deli area is very substandard at the best.
yelp:train:207464.para: For a proper dining experience, it's advisable to choose a traditional sit-down restaurant rather than Fry's deli area. The food served in Fry's deli is of very poor quality, even at its best.

yelp:train:207763.orig: This is a busy BofA location. There are plenty of tellers though being near a light rail location and mall may be why this location stays pretty active. There are in house representatives to assist with all your banking needs including personal loans, business banking, finical and other banking services. This location has plenty of bilingual Spanish speaking tellers to meet the needs of those whom may need to speak Spanish. \n\nThe teller who helped me with both my personal and business needs was friendly. yelp:train:207763.para:
This BofA branch is quite busy, likely due to its proximity to a light rail station and a mall. It has a good number of tellers available to handle various banking needs, including personal loans, business banking, and other financial services. The branch offers bilingual Spanish-speaking tellers to cater to Spanish-speaking customers.

yelp:train:208101.orig:
Studio 3-26 is legit!  I get my haircut by Luis and haven't been disappointed once!  I was nervous, just having moved to Phx to try someone new, but Peter, the owner, recommended him and he lived up to his billing!
Every stylist there is talented and friendly....you can tell they all enjoy what they do and where they're at.  Peter has done an awesome job at finding the right group of stylists that genuinely care about the quality of their work.
