Made by the same development company, the layout of the place is similar (but worse) to D.R. with ""The District"" in the center, and the big stores surrounding it, separated by a vast impenetrable wasteland of parking lot. The District is an admirable concept I think. It's like a traditional mall but at least there's an attempt to move forward on it by making it outdoors? That's cool when it's nice out, but when it's 139 degrees out, the misters are in full amazon jungle force. The biggest gripe I have about the place is the layout of the place. The design is horrendous. 

First of all, it just irritates me how the giant flashy signs face the 202, beckoning unknowing, random passersby to come shop there. Meanwhile, the entire shopping center's fat ass is planted firmly and stubbornly toward Tempe, the city it's supposed to represent. The drive past Tempe Marketplace on Rio Salado features a glorious view of the backs of Pier One and Old Navy and Target's loading docks. It's ugly. And most importantly, it didn't need to be designed that way. 

Secondly, this place is one of the leas
yelp:train:246905.para:
Tempe Marketplace can be seen as Desert Ridge's larger, more robust, and more intense sibling, albeit with a slightly less intelligent approach. Developed by the same company, it shares a similar layout to Desert Ridge, but with notable shortcomings. The central "The District" and the surrounding big stores are separated by a vast, impenetrable parking lot. While the concept of "The District" is commendable, it feels outdated when the weather is hot, with misters creating a dense, jungle-like atmosphere. My primary issue with the place is its layout, which I find to be poorly designed.

Firstly, it annoys me how the large, eye-catching signs are oriented towards the 202, enticing random passersby who might not even be aware of the area. Meanwhile, the bulk of the shopping center faces away from Tempe, the city it aims to represent. Driving past on Rio Salado offers a view of the backs of various stores, including Pier One, Old Navy, and Target's loading docks, which is unattractive. This design was not necessary and could have been improved.

Secondly, this place is one of the least... appealing in terms of its overall aesthetic.

yelp:train:246995.orig:
WOWOWOW! Holy crap, but this place is beyond awesome! Finally was able to try this place! I've been to swish and this place is soooooo much more better! All you can eat vegetables, need I say more?! I, like everyone else, love those tofu noodles. They are a little chewy, but no way near as chewy as udon noodles are. I love the fact that you can get shabu shabu broth AND sukiyaki broth! 

First off, the one lady who works there all by herself is just... I'm speechless. She works so hard. And she is so efficient! 

I got the Queen 1/2 beef and 1/2 scallops. Both soooo juicy and tender! I had to take advantage and ended up getting two orders of salad and veggies! Mmmm. Vegetables include napa cabbage, carrots, bamboo shoots, tofu, snow peas, and the tofu noodle. The bamboo shoots & snow peas were really delicious... never would have thought to use those! The real reason behind second order of veggies were for those tofu noodles!

The place is easy to find and very clean. And did I mention that service is friggin' great?! And the food is even better. I will definitely be visiting this little joint much more often now.

OH! And I forgot to mention you get a complimentary vanilla
yelp:train:246995.para:
WOW! This place is incredible! I finally got to try it, and it's even better than Swish! The all-you-can-eat vegetables are amazing, and I have to say, the tofu noodles are a game-changer—they're just the right amount of chewy. I also loved that I could choose between shabu shabu and sukiyaki broths. 

Firstly, the lady who works there by herself is truly remarkable. She's incredibly hardworking and efficient. 

I ordered the Queen combo with half beef and half scallops, and they were both incredibly juicy and tender. I couldn't resist getting extra salad and vegetables. The options included napa cabbage, carrots, bamboo shoots, tofu, snow peas, and the tofu noodles. The bamboo shoots and snow peas were surprisingly delicious, and the tofu noodles were the main reason for my second order of veggies.

The place is easy to find and super clean. The service is fantastic, and the food is even better. I'll definitely be visiting this place more often. Oh, and you get a free vanilla dessert to top it all off!

yelp:train:247047.orig: explain yourselves, trader joe's. i found a human hair in my kale chips.
yelp:train:247047.para: Trader Joe's, can you please clarify this for me? I discovered a human hair in my package of kale chips.

yelp:train:247319.orig:
Talk about visual orgasms! As a Beatles fan, I was so excited to watch LOVE as my first Cirque show during my first trip to Vegas, and it actually exceeded expectations.

Favorite performances were Lucy In The Sky With Diamonds and Octopus's Garden, but all of the song interpretations were amazing. I'm also glad they included my much beloved Eleanor Rigby.

Pro-tip: After asking at will-call if they had better seats available, we were moved from Section 209 Row R to Section 200 Row N. There really is no bad seat in the theatre, but it's good to note that Row N is at the edge of the bedsheets/clouds used to cover the lower audience during one number. We were able to see what went on above the sheets as well as the actors moving underneath. Double win!
yelp:train:247319.para:
What a visual feast! As a die-hard Beatles fan, I was thrilled to experience LOVE at my first Cirque show in Vegas, and it surpassed my expectations.

My favorite performances were Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds and Octopus's Garden, but every song interpretation was outstanding. I was also delighted to see Eleanor Rigby included.

A tip for others: When we inquired at will-call about better seats, we were upgraded from Section 209 Row R to Section 200 Row N. While there's no bad seat in the house, Row N is positioned at the edge of the bedsheets/clouds used in one act, allowing us to see both above and below the sheets. It was a win-win!

yelp:train:247660.orig:
I was taken here while visiting from Chicago and had one of the best margaritas of my life.  I tried the house (on ice with salt) and it was fantastic, but what I couldn't get enough of was the strawberry-lime one.  I couldn't taste a drop of alcohol...and that's when you know you have a good mixed drink on your hands. I honestly could have had three more it was so tasty, but my childlike tolerance for boozin did not allow it.  

The bartender was super nice and friendly, we had many refills of the chips and salsa (damn you, I can never resist), and it was all in a southwestern chill environment.  Supposedly the tacos are top-notch, I will have to give them a whirl next time I'm in town.  

I highly suggest going here for a happy hour or dinner.
yelp:train:247660.para:
During my visit from Chicago, I savored one of the finest margaritas I've ever had. The house margarita, served on ice with salt, was outstanding, but the strawberry-lime version was my absolute favorite. It was so well-balanced that I couldn't detect any alcohol, which is a sign of a great mixed drink. I wanted to order more, but my tolerance for alcohol, much like a child's, prevented me from having another. 

The bartender was exceptionally friendly, and we enjoyed numerous refills of the chips and salsa (I couldn't resist). The atmosphere was wonderfully southwestern, relaxed, and inviting. They say the tacos are exceptional; I plan to try them next time I'm around. 

I strongly recommend visiting for happy hour or dinner.

yelp:train:247696.orig:
Would I go back here if/when I return to Scottsdale? Heck yeah!!!!!  When we were there last November there were 5 adults and one child in our family group wandering around the area looking for something to eat.  The one place we tried to get into you couldn't get in without a crowbar so we wandered past this, took a look at the menu and said why not!

So glad we did!  Good sangria, interesting patio area (felt more like an alley but cool), great chips and salsa, and good food at a good price.  No one, not even the kid complained about their food.  And this was the first time in my life I had fajitas with zucchini in them! YUM!  Plus, most veggies that come with fajitas are usually limp beyond limp and on the bland side.  Theirs had some spice to them.  

With drinks and food our whole bill for all of us was around 100$.  Not bad for a place in Old Scottsdale.
yelp:train:247696.para:
Would I revisit this place if I return to Scottsdale? Absolutely! Last November, our family of six, including one child, explored the area for a meal. We stumbled upon this place, found the entrance challenging without a crowbar, and decided to check out the menu.

We're so glad we did! The sangria was excellent, and the patio area, though narrow like an alley, was intriguing. The chips and salsa were fantastic, and the food was delicious and reasonably priced. Nobody, not even the child, complained about their meal. It was a first for me to have zucchini in my fajitas, and they were delightful! Typically, the vegetables that come with fajitas are often overcooked and bland, but these were spicier and more flavorful.

Our total bill, including drinks and food, was about $100 for the whole group. Considering it's in Old Scottsdale, that's a great value.

yelp:train:248033.orig: Decided to check out Ground Control last night based on a reviews on AZ Central as one of the best wine bars.. I totally disagree.  Service was terrible, one person I particular was rude when we interrupted time with his girlfriend.  Had to ask for water, plates, napkins, check, etc.  The wine was decent as well as a couple of appetizers. But pass on the cheese board...  3 small slices for $14. I was looking forward to the European concept but in Europe, they are more helpful and friendly...
yelp:train:248033.para: Last night, I visited Ground Control after reading positive reviews on AZ Central, expecting it to be one of the best wine bars. I was quite disappointed. The service was poor; one server was particularly rude when we interrupted him to talk to his girlfriend. We had to repeatedly ask for water, plates, napkins, and the check. The wine and a couple of appetizers were okay, but the cheese board was a letdown—only three small slices for $14. I was hoping for a more European experience with helpful and friendly service, but that wasn't the case.

yelp:train:248393.orig:
We've been here twice because well, we are new to AZ and didn't know anywhere else.  They have a big menu...but that's it.  I mean we didn't expect anything more than cheesecake factory but yeah...from my point of view, it wasn't even to cheesecake level.  The service was descent though.

*Food = ordinary, quickly prepared American food
*Service = descent 
*Atmosphere =....interesting...
*Price = ok
yelp:train:248393.para:
We visited here twice since we're new to AZ and hadn't discovered any other options yet. They offer a wide menu, but that's about it. Honestly, we didn't have high expectations, similar to a Cheesecake Factory, but the food didn't even meet those. The service was decent, though.

*Food = average, quickly made American dishes
*Service = decent
*Atmosphere = somewhat unique
*Price = reasonable

yelp:train:248708.orig:
do yourself a favor and go to sushi roku across the street.

the spicy tuna wasn't spicy.
the bottom fell out of my boyfriend's water glass inexplicably (ok, not their fault necessarily).
the rolls were microscopic.

i should have tried some of the entrees instead of ordering just sushi. but when you're known for being a sushi restaurant, your rolls should be on par.

i did really appreciate the wonderful customer service, though. when the mysterious water debacle occurred, the staff was apologetic and comped our $27 kobe gyoza appetizer, in addition to bringing us another dish on the house.
yelp:train:248708.para:
I think you'd enjoy visiting Sushi Roku next door.

The spicy tuna lacked the expected heat. My boyfriend's water glass inexplicably tipped over (though it wasn't necessarily their fault).

The rolls were tiny.

I should have tried the entrees instead of just ordering sushi, but given that the restaurant is known for its sushi, the rolls should have been better.

Despite that, I really appreciated the excellent customer service. When the water glass incident happened, the staff apologized and compensated us with a free $27 kobe gyoza appetizer, plus another dish for free.

yelp:train:248775.orig:
Koi was very good!! 

Me  and one of my girls went to Koi for dinner on our first evening in Vegas. We weren't hella hungry so we just ordered something to share btwn us. To make the review easier to read, Ill just list what we had:

Spicy Tuna Roll: Good...same as any other spicy tuna roll I've had.

Dragon Roll: Consisted of bbq eel, shrimp tempura, crab and seaweed (obviously). That was the BEST dragon roll I ever had! They sprinkled the roll with tempura shavings I think. The roll literally melted in my mouth. Very good.

Miso Soup: Good...same as any other miso soup

Sake: we got the blueberry infused one. BOMB! Definitely recommend that,it was like soda...and had me buzzin even more than I was before we got there hahaha.

Will definitely come back!
yelp:train:248775.para:
Koi was fantastic!

On our first night in Vegas, my friend and I dined there, not feeling very hungry, so we opted for a shared dish. Here’s what we ordered:

- Spicy Tuna Roll: It was decent, similar to other spicy tuna rolls I've tried.
- Dragon Roll: This included barbecued eel, shrimp tempura, crab, and seaweed. It was the absolute best dragon roll I've ever had! They sprinkled it with tempura shavings, and it practically melted in my mouth. Very good.
- Miso Soup: It was good, just like any other miso soup.
- Sake: We chose the blueberry-infused variety, which was amazing! I highly recommend it; it tasted like soda and gave me an extra buzz, even more than before we arrived, hahaha.

I definitely plan to return!

yelp:train:249474.orig: I went to Target this week to buy an I-pod after a less-than-stellar experience at the Best Buy @ Midtown.  I was asked immediately by a sales associate if I needed help.  He was enthusiastic to serve me; he showed me the jogging wristbands that would fit my new I-pod and thoroughly explained the tech support and warranty for electronic products purchased at Target. A far cry from the hand-off customer service \""specialists\"" at Best Buy!\n\nA side note: this Target is adding a full grocery section, woo hoo!
yelp:train:249474.para:
This week, I visited Target to purchase an iPod following a disappointing experience at Midtown Best Buy. A sales associate greeted me promptly and offered assistance, showing me compatible jogging wristbands and detailing the tech support and warranty for electronic items bought at Target. This was a stark contrast to the disjointed service I received at Best Buy.

As a side note, Target is expanding to include a full grocery section, which is exciting!

yelp:train:249721.orig: 5th time here! 5th great experience! Place has a great lay out lots of space. Caters to my kids  ( owner brings them fried dough) while we enjoy our food to keep them happy. Prices are great. They remember you! Jessica is very efficient and great person ! I'm new to yelp because looking for good restaurants like this. Oh yeah try the brechetta it's the best
yelp:train:249721.para: I've visited here five times now, and each time has been fantastic! The place is well-organized with plenty of room. The owner is considerate, offering fried dough to entertain my kids so we can focus on our meal. The prices are very reasonable. They even recognize regulars! Jessica is both efficient and a wonderful person to deal with. I recently joined Yelp to find restaurants like this one. By the way, you really should try the brechetta; it's outstanding!

yelp:train:249873.orig:
This place made me ANGRY!!
It's been a while since I've been in, and I remember how delicious it was, but I guess I forgot how expensive it was for what I was getting. I remember the crawfish etouffe was delicious, so I can recommend that, but for $20.00?? I skipped it. 
My friend and I ordered the frog legs, 1 dozen gulf oysters (the only thing worth coming in for @ $3.95) and we split the Bay Platter.
My main gripe here is that EVERYTHING TOOK FOREVER and we even arrived early before the crowds!! The people behind us were seated long after us, were served and finished and left before we even got our entree (they had a female waiter who seemed totally on it), and meanwhile our waiter's presence was bordering Bigfoot mythical. 
The beers took 10 minutes even with the bar in sight, the frog legs took a while and there weren't many on the plate (delicious though), and the oysters came THIRTY MINUTES LATER. 
""I don't know WHY the oysters are taking so long...."" OH COME ON!! There's ZERO PREP involved with these, don't play me for a damn fool!! I sure wish I could remember the waiter's name so his inattentive chicanery can be fully exposed. I was too angry to remember 2 minute
yelp:train:249873.para:
This place really irritated me! I hadn't been there in a while and recalled how tasty it used to be, but I realized it was quite pricey for the quality. I particularly remembered the crawfish etouffe being delicious, so I thought I'd give it another try, but at $20, I decided against it.

My friend and I ordered the frog legs, a dozen gulf oysters (the only items worth the $3.95 price tag), and shared the Bay Platter.

My biggest complaint is that everything took so long, even though we arrived early. The group behind us was seated later, served, and finished their meal before we even got our main course (they had a attentive female server). Meanwhile, our waiter was nowhere to be seen, almost like a mythical creature.

The beers took 10 minutes even though the bar was in sight, the frog legs took a while and there weren't many on the plate (though they were delicious), and the oysters arrived 30 minutes after ordering. 

"‘I don’t know why the oysters are taking so long...’ Come on! There’s no preparation needed for these, don’t treat me like a fool!" I wish I could remember the waiter's name to expose his inattentiveness. I was too upset to recall the exact details.

yelp:train:249950.orig: Good atmosphere, good service and awesome food, Lobster tails are HUGE and always seems to be fresh. I love going there for the seafood, it's a nice treat. The wait staff always seem to be helpful and the service is good. They can also handle large groups looks like to me.
yelp:train:249950.para: The ambiance is great, the service is excellent, and the food is outstanding, particularly the massive lobster tails that appear to be very fresh. I enjoy dining there for the seafood, which is a delightful experience. The staff is always attentive, and they handle large groups well.

yelp:train:250006.orig: I agree this place kind of sucks.  Food is average. and although it looks really nice no one ever seems to be there.  It is always dead.  they have great TV's and I think the place should hop but instead it is not.\n\nGo to tanked fish next door. everyone else does.  This place looks really good and I like the bar set up. reason for 2 stars.
yelp:train:250006.para:
I think this place isn't great. The food is just okay, and despite its appealing appearance, it's rarely occupied; it feels quite empty. They have excellent TVs, but the place isn't buzzing with activity. 

Instead, head to Tanked Fish next door; that's where everyone goes. It looks fantastic, and I really like their bar setup. That's why I gave it two stars.

yelp:train:250203.orig:
It is a must do in Vegas- a ritual. 

Caramel hazelnut napolean with coffee. Nothing beats it. I don't even like dessert but this is an addiction, a new delicious addiction I must fix every time I come to Vegas. 

I also had the Chicken Cocktail sandwich. It was yummy but I thought the tomato wasn't fresh enough for my taste. 

Just go already. Trip out on the mock silver plastic utensils. On a totally separate tangent: why do they call it silverware when it's not silver???
yelp:train:250203.para:
It's a must-try in Vegas—a ritual. The caramel hazelnut Napoleon with coffee is unparalleled. Even though I usually don't enjoy desserts, this is a new, irresistible addiction that I crave every time I visit Vegas.

I also had the Chicken Cocktail sandwich, which was delicious, though I found the tomato to be a bit lacking in freshness.

Just go already and experience the fun with the mock silver plastic utensils. On a different note, why do they call it silverware when it's not actually silver?

yelp:train:250847.orig: The Santan Brewery Octoberfest is a bust. $15 bucks a head plus $5 dollars a beer to look at commercial tents. They need a lot more \""bling\""  or vendors to make it worthwhile.  We spent two hours and looked at everything twice.
yelp:train:250847.para: The Santan Brewery Oktoberfest isn't very appealing. It costs $15 per person plus $5 for each beer, but the commercial tents aren't very impressive. To make it more worthwhile, they need to add more attractive features or vendors. We spent about two hours, thoroughly checking everything out.

yelp:train:250861.orig:
The computer was down with no way to conduct any business after the long Memorial Day weekend.  I waited a few minutes and then decided to go work out at SCC.  Upon returning a couple of hours later the computer was still down.  I asked if this happens often and it has happened before after long holiday weekends. So how much time was lost by the public today?  How much gas was wasted because there was no Plan B?  

I received a notice in the mail and have two months to update my driver's license  photo.  However, you can bet I will not be at Motor Vehicles on Monday July 7th for a repeat (?) performance.  I actually like my old photo and think I look like the photo so why do I have to get a new one?

Update: On my second visit there were hardly any customers so the photo update went smoothly.  My number was quickly called with pleasant chit chat.  The only "" problem"" was the new photo didn't show as much hair as there should have been.  I  commented the camera must be broken which drew a chuckle but I am sure my remark is made hundreds of times.   Maybe the camera will be fixed the next time around?
yelp:train:250861.para:
After the Memorial Day weekend, the computer was out of service, preventing any business from being conducted. I waited a bit and opted to go to SCC for a workout. Upon returning a couple of hours later, the computer was still down. I inquired if this was a common occurrence, and learned it had happened before following long holiday weekends. This made me wonder how much time the public lost today and how much gas was wasted without a backup plan.

I received a notice in the mail for updating my driver's license photo, with two months to comply. However, I won't be heading to Motor Vehicles on July 7th; I'll likely find a different way to handle it. I actually like my current photo and think it suits me well, so why do I need a new one?

Update: On my second visit, there were few customers, making the process smooth. My number was called quickly, and there was pleasant conversation. The only issue was that the new photo didn't capture as much hair as I had. I joked about the camera being broken, which elicited a chuckle, but I'm sure this comment is made frequently. Perhaps the camera will be fixed next time?

yelp:train:251660.orig:
I get why they have four stars, it's a hip place with electronica music playing in the background, and that seems to be a Vegas standard now.  However, I can't say ill be making my way back.

They have a variety to choose from for AYCE, with the whole inside menu strictly rolls.  When I do AYCE, I only go for nigiri.  As I've posted before, I'm not really into rolls because its usually covered in sauce, with very little filling.  I guess it's what Americans love though... Sauce on everything.  I'm guilty as well, just not on my sushi.

Anyway, the fish was really poor quality.  After my initial order, I couldn't bring myself to order any more.  I love my fish to taste like fish (if that even makes sense).  The fish here had no taste whatsoever.  All I could taste was the vinegar from the rice.

I thought it was cool they served oysters, but it was pretty blah.  There was no flavor at all.  It tasted like water.  It did not have that ""taste like the sea"" quality.  I don't know.  It just didn't taste like anything.  The baked mussels were not very good. Overcooked. No flavor.  Too chewy.

Tofu was ok, but too much sauce, and it was overly sweet.  Desserts were boring.  No
yelp:train:251660.para:
I understand why it has four stars; it’s a trendy spot with electronic music, which is typical in Vegas. But I don’t see myself returning.

They offer a range of options for all-you-can-eat, but the menu is strictly rolls. Since I usually stick to nigiri, I find rolls less appealing because they’re often drenched in sauce with little filling. While Americans might enjoy that, I prefer my sushi to taste more like actual fish.

The fish quality was poor; after my first order, I couldn’t bring myself to order more. I love my fish to have a distinct fishy flavor, but this one tasted mostly of vinegar from the rice.

The oysters were served, but they were bland, lacking any flavor. They tasted like water and didn’t have the “taste of the sea” quality. The baked mussels were overcooked, flavorless, and too chewy.

The tofu was acceptable but had too much sauce and was overly sweet. The desserts were unexciting.

yelp:train:252186.orig:
Warm butter cake! It is the signature dessert of the restaurant that is sweet and fluffy in a round cake that can feed 2 or 3 easily. I really don't have the words to describe it but suffice it to say you need to get it. And do what we did...have your dessert first! That suggestion got the server an extra tip!

As for the rest of the meal, it was heavenly. The steaks and the sides were huge. I had the prime rib and my companion had the ribeye. Both were delicious. There wasn't anything bad about the meal. 

We were there two weeks ago and the restaurant was full particularly the bar. The dining room is dimly lit and intimate. For those who are visually challenged in dim light, bring your readers!
yelp:train:252186.para:
Delicious butter cake! This is the standout dessert at the restaurant, a round, sweet, and fluffy treat that easily serves two or three people. I can't find the right words to describe it, but I strongly recommend you try it. And follow our lead—enjoy your dessert first! That tip for the server earned us an extra gratuity.

The rest of the meal was equally delightful. The steaks and sides were generously portioned. I had the prime rib, while my companion opted for the ribeye, and both were outstanding. There wasn't a single negative aspect to the meal.

We visited two weeks ago, and the restaurant was bustling, especially at the bar. The dining room has a cozy, dimly lit atmosphere. If you have difficulty seeing in low light, bring a reader!

yelp:train:252383.orig:
Having just sampled Capriotti's again, this time at Night of the Living Neon, where they were very generous sponsors, I took my break from the slots at Red Rock for my Wednesday night Food Court Feast.  :)   Their Bobby was calling to me, but I decided to lower the carb quotient by going for their Cole Turkey sandwich.  I guess I didn't realize that, unlike all the other sub joints, Capriotti's uses REAL, FRESH turkey!!, and that helps explain why their prices are a bit higher than the competition.  

The sandwich was super.  I asked for the Russian dressing on the side, and I was given a container big enough to dress my next four salads.  The turkey was moist, the provolone really good, and the cole slaw just the way I like it.  My only complaint is that their Small sandwich, at 9"", is just too big for me.  I'd love to see a smaller one at a smaller price, but I bet not too many people would share this nit.  

I'm a fan!
yelp:train:252383.para:
After trying Capriotti's again at Night of the Living Neon, where they were generous sponsors, I took my break from the slot machines at Red Rock for my Wednesday night Food Court Feast.  :) Bobby from Capriotti's was calling out to me, but I opted for their Cole Turkey sandwich to lower my carb intake. I hadn't realized that Capriotti's uses real, fresh turkey, which explains why their prices are a bit higher than others. 

The sandwich was excellent. I requested the Russian dressing on the side, and I was given a generous container that would last me several salads. The turkey was moist, the provolone was delicious, and the coleslaw was just how I like it. My only gripe is that their Small sandwich, at 9 inches, is a bit too large for me. I would love to see a smaller option at a lower price, but I doubt many would share this opinion. 

I'm a fan!

yelp:train:252399.orig: I need to start by saying that I am NOT the type of person that gets a manicure or even goes to a spa. The reason I went today is that I needed a pro to fix my cuticles before my wedding.\n\n That being said, I enjoyed my time here. I went for a regular manicure. Overall, I enjoyed the process and was relaxed, but a few things would keep me from returning soon:  1) My tech was funny and easy to talk to, but I was a bit skeeved by the fact that she blew big bubbles with her gum while clipping my cuticles. 2) They had a limited choice of polish colors. I usually paint mine something crazy (neon pink, black, obnoxious glitter) and the various shades of red and pink weren't to my liking. The meadow green I picked was the loudest color there and while it's cute, I'd like something weirder. All in all, I'll definitely go back in the winter when my skin and nails are particularly awful.
yelp:train:252399.para:
To begin, I am not typically someone who gets manicures or visits spas. My reason for coming today was to have a professional fix my cuticles before my wedding.

Despite that, I had a pleasant experience. I opted for a standard manicure. While I was generally satisfied with the process and felt relaxed, there are a few reasons I wouldn't return soon: 1) The technician was humorous and easy to chat with, but I was uncomfortable because she was blowing bubbles with gum while trimming my cuticles. 2) The selection of nail polish colors was limited. I usually go for something bold like neon pink, black, or glittery, and the available shades of red and pink didn't appeal to me. The meadow green I chose was the brightest option, and while it's cute, I prefer something more unconventional. In summary, I will likely return in the winter when my nails and skin are in poorer condition.

yelp:train:253158.orig: It's always amazing how the garden is set up to wow the crowds of tourists and locals who stop in on a daily basis. I try to get here for each theme to see what they have come up with next. I recently went for Christmas and was impressed. From penguins to polar bears and a canopy where it looks like you are standing in a snow storm this place is a must see for all.
yelp:train:253158.para: The garden consistently manages to impress both tourists and locals with its daily displays. I make an effort to visit for each theme to see the latest creations. Recently, during Christmas, I was particularly struck by the displays. Featuring penguins, polar bears, and a snowstorm-like canopy, this garden is a must-visit for everyone.

yelp:train:253438.orig: In 5 years of coming to LV, this has to be the saddest buffet in LV.  We had enjoyed the Spice World Buffet at Planet Hollywood the morning before but opted to \""eat local\"" Sunday morning.  What a mistake!  I don't know where Ryan T.  ate as there was NO wait service at all. The food and drinks were totally self service.   No half and half for coffee (non dairy creamer only).  An extremely limited selection with powdered scrambled eggs, frozen pastries, no egg white omelets, watered down juices, Eggo waffles, soupy oatmeal and a fruit bar consisting of  tired looking melon evoked a Days Inn free breakfast buffet rather than a $20+ Vegas Sunday brunch.The shrimp looked so old no one in my party dared take anything from the fish area (lox and two kinds of boiled shirmp)  The carvery had a Hormel type ham and a turkey breast evoking Louis Rich, but no one to cut it. It was truly pitiful.  The take away is ask to view the buffet before committing to purchasing and avoid the Luxor MORE as a breakfast option,
yelp:train:253438.para: After five years of visiting Las Vegas, this buffet at the Luxor stands out as the most disappointing one I've experienced. The day before, we enjoyed the Spice World Buffet at Planet Hollywood, so we decided to "eat local" on Sunday morning. What a regrettable choice! If Ryan T. had a better experience, I'm not sure where he was, as there was no waitstaff; everything was self-service. There was no half-and-half for coffee, only non-dairy creamer. The food selection was very limited, with powdered scrambled eggs, frozen pastries, no egg white omelets, watered-down juices, Eggo waffles, soupy oatmeal, and a fruit bar that looked like a Days Inn free breakfast buffet rather than a $20+ Vegas brunch. The shrimp appeared so old that no one in my group dared to take any from the fish area. The carvery featured a Hormel-like ham and turkey breast, reminiscent of Louis Rich, but there was no one to cut it. It was truly a letdown. My advice is to view the buffet before buying and to avoid the Luxor for breakfast.

yelp:train:253553.orig: I just had breakfast at More and paid $18 (with tax) and I feel that the Luxor should be ashamed of this place. The selection is incredibly sparse and bland. There are multiple stations with food, but they all have the same items: bacon, biscuits & gravy, breakfast potatoes, etc.. The only edible food available was the fresh fruit, and that's all I could eat after sampling the hot options. $18 for a banana and some melon. This experience has written me off of Las Vegas buffets; thank you More buffet.
yelp:train:253553.para: After breakfast at More, which cost me $18 including tax, I believe the Luxor should feel embarrassed about this establishment. The menu is extremely limited and uninteresting. Despite having several food stations, they mostly offer the same items like bacon, biscuits & gravy, and breakfast potatoes. The only food I found palatable was the fresh fruit, which was all I could manage after trying the hot dishes. Paying $18 for a banana and some melon is outrageous. This experience has convinced me to avoid Las Vegas buffets; thanks, More buffet.

yelp:train:253894.orig: Great first impression!! I called to place a to-go order and although they literally were closing in ten min, the gentleman on the phone was super cool & acted as though it was hours earlier. There was absolutely no hint in his voice of annoyance at the last minute order, as so many restaurant workers would have displayed. I cannot express how accommodating he was on the phone, it was such a relief after having just gotten home from the airport. Exceptional food, had the chicken pita, tzatsiki, and their signature crazy fries (with feta!). Can't wait to return.
yelp:train:253894.para: What a fantastic initial experience! When I called to place a takeout order, the staff member on the line, who was closing up in just ten minutes, was incredibly patient and friendly, as if it were much earlier in the day. There was no trace of frustration in his voice regarding the last-minute request, which is often the case with restaurant workers. His demeanor was exceptionally accommodating, which was a huge relief after my recent arrival from the airport. The food was outstanding; I tried the chicken pita, tzatziki, and their famous crazy fries (topped with feta). I'm eagerly looking forward to my next visit.

yelp:train:254280.orig: My family and I were in the shopping plaza this morning.  Our 4 year old son needed a haircut so he and I walked into the salon and asked if they could do a children's haircut.  Instead of a \""good morning\"", a smile, and an answer to the question, the lady sitting at the front desk replied, \""we don't do children's prices\"".  That wasn't my question and her delivery was such that I felt like I was somehow being judged financially.  It gave me flashes of Julia Roberts in Pretty Woman when she was trying to buy a dress.  I didn't care about the price.  I was asking a question because some salons prefer to not do such a young person's hair.  Your salon missed out on 2 clients today and a lesson in etiquette and good customer service is needed by those greeting customers as they walk in the door.
yelp:train:254280.para: This morning, my family and I were at the shopping plaza when our 4-year-old son needed a haircut. We went into the salon, and instead of a friendly "good morning," a smile, or a response to our request for a children's haircut, the woman at the front desk said, "We don't offer children's prices." Her response felt like a financial judgment, making me think of Julia Roberts in Pretty Woman when she was trying to buy a dress. I wasn't concerned about the price; I was simply asking because some salons prefer not to cut hair for very young children. Your salon lost two potential customers today, and there's a clear need for better etiquette and customer service training for those greeting people at the door.

yelp:train:254970.orig: Terrible experience, ordered to go from the bar and the order was incorrect.  Very simple order, only 2 items from the menu and they did not get it correct.  The worst part of the experience was chasing down a bartender/waitress when I showed up just to get my order in.  Service to the customers was clearly the last thing on all of their minds as I stand there waiting just to place my order.  I am a very understanding person when it comes to being busy but the place was fairly quiet.
yelp:train:254970.para: Had a really poor experience; my takeout order from the bar was wrong. Such a straightforward order, just two items from the menu, yet it was incorrect. What made it even worse was having to track down a bartender/waitress to place my order when I arrived. It was clear that serving customers wasn't a priority as I waited to place my order. Despite being understanding about being busy, the establishment seemed fairly quiet at the time.

yelp:train:255325.orig:
Thank goodness we didn't pay to get in this place.... YIKES!!!

it's good to be a girl in Vegas... you get random people coming up to you, asking you if you want to go to certain clubs, and the beauty of this is that if the place is not so good (like this one), you didn't just waste $20...

First, there was the tiniest of crowds outside and lots of people leaving, yet we waited the longest to get in this place.  First place we head is the bar...ordered 3 drinks, and the waitress tells me that it's $54.... 

wait, what?  I'm confused.  Those 3 short little drinks cost how much?  Now, I expected to pay a lot for drinks, but that's obscene.  Especially considering that the club was not very nice.  We kept saying that it was like an 80's club, not because they played 80's music but because the effects were reminiscent of that era....smoke hitting me in the face every 5 seconds coming down from the ceiling....and the music!  My lord, it was painful!  It was SO much base that you could feel it in your head, your arms, your legs, I think my heart stopped a few times...

Definitely not our scene.  Nothing impressive about the crowd, the decor, the horribly painful music... we could
yelp:train:255325.para:
Phew, glad we didn't pay to enter this place... YIKES!!!

Being a woman in Vegas has its perks... you get approached by strangers inviting you to clubs, but the silver lining is that if the place isn't great (like this one), you haven't wasted money.

We had the smallest crowd outside, with many leaving, yet we waited the longest to get in. Our first stop was the bar, where we ordered three drinks, only to be told they cost $54 by the waitress.

What? That's confusing. Three small drinks cost that much? I didn't expect drinks to be expensive, but that's outrageous, especially considering the club wasn't very nice. We thought it resembled an 80s club, not because of the music but due to the effects, like smoke hitting us every five seconds from the ceiling. The music was excruciating too! It was so bass-heavy that it felt like it was vibrating through every part of me, and I think my heart almost stopped a few times...

Definitely not our scene. The crowd, decor, and the painfully loud music were all disappointing...

yelp:train:255430.orig:
East End is a brewery, not a restaurant. Don't expect to sit down for pizza and brews. Most of the space is filled with brewing equipment - tanks and such. What you can do is sample a bunch of beers, and walk away with some.

It's a challenge to find East End. There's no sign. Just an open door in a brick warehouse. And an empty keg sitting outside. Our first time, we didn't think we could possibly be in the right place. Until we saw people leaving with beer.

You can only visit during growler hours. Inside there's a low bar straight out of high school chem. You can sample the eight or so beers on tap. And chat about the beers or anything else. And be impressed at how many people manage to find the place. The beers are tasty.

Then when you're ready, pick a beer or two to get a growler of. A growler is a half gallon jug they filled from the tap. They also usually have a special beer or two in bottles. Typical brewery swag is also available - pint glasses, t-shirts, etc., to prove that you actually found the place.
yelp:train:255430.para:
East End is a brewery, not a dining establishment, so don't expect to enjoy pizza and drinks indoors. The majority of the space is occupied by brewing equipment like tanks. You can sample a variety of beers and take some home with you.

Finding East End is a challenge; there are no signs, just an open door in a brick warehouse and an empty keg outside. On our first visit, we weren't sure if we were in the right place until we saw people leaving with beer.

Visits are limited to growler hours. Inside, there's a low bar reminiscent of a high school chemistry lab. You can sample about eight beers on tap and chat about them or any other topic. It's impressive how many people manage to locate the place. The beers are quite tasty.

When you're ready, you can choose a couple of beers to get in a growler, which is a half-gallon jug filled from the tap. They also typically have a couple of special beers in bottles. You can also pick up typical brewery merchandise like pint glasses and t-shirts to show that you found the place.

yelp:train:255928.orig: So lame. They don't have the decency to let people know on their restaurant.com ad that they no longer accept certificates, so we drove all the way there for nothing. We LOVE Mexican food, but this place lost present and future business from us. Shame on you Loco Patron.
yelp:train:255928.para: So disappointing. Their restaurant.com advertisement doesn't mention that they no longer accept certificates, which is why we made the trip and ended up wasting our time. We truly enjoy Mexican cuisine, but this experience has cost us both current and future business. You should be ashamed, Loco Patron.

yelp:train:255957.orig: Better than Macayos, but we all know that's not saying much. Unfortunately, it's a little pricey for mexican food and really not all that great. If I really have a craving for good authentic Mexican food I usually find myself driving into tow to Carolinas at Peoria and 91st ave.
yelp:train:255957.para: While it surpasses Macayos, that's not high praise. Unfortunately, it comes with a hefty price tag for Mexican cuisine and just doesn't measure up. When I truly crave authentic Mexican food, I often head to Peoria and 91st Ave to visit Carolina's.

yelp:train:256018.orig:
From the moment my fiance and I stepped foot in this place we were IN LOVE! I will be getting married at Inspirador next March and we're super excited! The venue itself is gorgeous as it contains an outdoor and indoor option for the ceremony, a beautifully decorated reception area and the chic looking Tryst art gallery that can be utilized for cocktail hour!

When we first met with Andrea to take a look at the venue, she blew us away! She wanted to get to know us, how we met, the proposal, and she wanted to get a feel as to what kind of wedding we were looking for. From the minute we met, she exemplified customer service, she indeed 'sold' us the venue. We have kept in contact and she has been answering my e-mails promptly which shows her dedication in this industry! The price for the venue was a little above our projected budget, however the services provided in the all inclusive package was a must. Oh and you have the option to bring your own alcohol rather than pay per individual, love it!

We are so looking forward to our wedding next March and I will be writing an update as far as how everything went! Woohoo, can't wait! :)
yelp:train:256018.para:
The instant my fiancé and I set foot in Inspirador, we were enchanted! We are getting married there in March and we are thrilled! The venue boasts both an outdoor and indoor ceremony space, a stunningly decorated reception area, and the chic Tryst art gallery perfect for cocktail hour.

Our initial meeting with Andrea was outstanding. She wanted to understand our story, from our meeting to our proposal, and what kind of wedding we envisioned. From the start, she demonstrated exceptional customer service and 'sold' us on the venue. We've stayed in touch, and she has been responsive to our emails, showing her commitment to this industry.

While the venue price was slightly higher than our budget, the all-inclusive package was a necessity. Plus, the option to bring our own alcohol is a big plus! We are eagerly anticipating our wedding in March and will share our experience once it's over! Excited, can't wait! :))

yelp:train:256087.orig: Super friendly and attentive service, from the front desk, to the wait staff to the sommalier - they anticipated our very large group's every need.  And this was on a VERY busy Monday evening at NAB. The food was decent, although was a bit disappointed there was no grass fed meat on the menu at those prices.  Wine selection fantastic, we had a bottle of the Hansel Pinot (one of the few under $100) and it blew everyone away.  The Stonestreet Upper Barn Chardonney on the Som's recommendation was fantastic as well.  It's not too noisy so you don't have to yell to be heard or keep asking people to repeat themselves.  \n\nWhat else can I say, with all the options you have at the Venetian, you can't go wrong here.
yelp:train:256087.para: The service was exceptionally friendly and attentive, from the front desk to the wait staff and the sommelier, who anticipated all the needs of our large group, even on a very busy Monday evening at NAB. The food was satisfactory, though we were a bit let down by the absence of grass-fed meat options at those price points. The wine selection was outstanding; we particularly enjoyed the Hansel Pinot (one of the few under $100), which was a hit with everyone. The Stonestreet Upper Barn Chardonnay, recommended by the sommelier, was also fantastic. The ambiance was pleasant, not too noisy, so we could converse without shouting or constantly asking people to repeat themselves. Given all the options at the Venetian, this place is a great choice.

yelp:train:256584.orig:
When I first saw this place I was little like ummm we are really going in there? But I am so glad we did! Most of the bars were really crowded except for one in the corner where no one was. Me and my friends went over and the super friendly bartender was more then happy to serve us. She gave us some great deals. The first was that she gave me a 2 for 1 on my rum and coke (2 shots for the price of 1). She then offered to give us free shots if we bough a bandanna. (There was some sort of contest and her boss told her she needed to up her numbers.) My friend got a bandanna and we all come some delicious shots. 
We then all took a turn riding the bull which was such a blast. Sadly I was too tipsy to be much good, but it was still fun none the less. Even if you sucked the crowd was on your side. 
As we were getting ready to leave I had to have a bandanna of my own. I went back to my favorite bartender and she offered up another round of shots for my bandanna.
Free shots, fun bandannas, and a mechanical bull. What else do you need?
yelp:train:256584.para:
Initially, I had my doubts about entering, wondering, "Are we really going in there?" But I'm so glad we did! Most of the bars were bustling, but one in the corner was empty. My friends and I approached it, and the incredibly friendly bartender was eager to serve us. She offered some fantastic deals. First, she provided a 2 for 1 on my rum and coke (two shots for the price of one). She then suggested we get a bandanna for free shots, as there was a contest and her boss wanted her to boost her numbers. My friend got a bandanna, and we all enjoyed some tasty shots. 

Next, we tried the mechanical bull, which was a blast. Although I was a bit tipsy and not as skilled, it was still fun. The crowd was supportive even if you weren't doing well. 

Before leaving, I wanted my own bandanna. I returned to my favorite bartender, who offered another round of shots in exchange. 

Free shots, fun bandannas, and a mechanical bull—what more could you want?

yelp:train:257478.para: When I arrived the day before Christmas Eve last year, we waited for about 15-20 minutes before the waitress finally approached us. Her attitude was unacceptable. yelp:train:258059.orig: Not just a chophouse, every dish is infused with true & authentic cuisine. Beyond extraordinary -- try the veal chop, it will change your life.
yelp:train:258059.para: Not just any chophouse, each dish here embodies genuine and authentic flavors. Absolutely extraordinary—don't miss the veal chop; it could transform your dining experience.

yelp:train:258446.para: not very good, almost bad, but you can't refuse the kid who really wanted to go.

yelp:train:259632.orig:

We ate there once several months ago. In fact, I think it was their first week open for business. My girlfriend and I were impressed, and did come back, even though their tasty veggie meat was out of stock, and couldn't make us the veggie meals we came seeking that day.

Fast forward to last weekend. Some friends scored four Diamondbacks tickets, and I thought, since we'll have some drinks at the stadium, why not try Breadfruit again? We could take the light rail, and it's only two or three blocks from the light rail station.

We brought a six pack of Red Stripe to complete the experience, and it was a delight to be back. We saw one of the owners, who we recognized and liked when we met her, but didn't see her partner, who is the cook and is Jamaican. Our friends were impressed by the food, which held it's own.

We had fish escovich, jerk chicken, coconut curry tofu and side orders of plantains. All hits. Everything was cooked to order, and impressed our friends. The steamed veggies and rice and beans on my plate we
yelp:train:259632.para:
Breadfruit stepped into a gap in Phoenix's dining scene by offering genuine Jamaican cuisine and drinks, which was lacking in the downtown area due to a shortage of exciting restaurants.

We visited there a few months ago, specifically during their inaugural week. My partner and I were quite impressed and decided to return, even though the veggie meat they serve was unavailable that day.

Recently, some friends acquired four Diamondbacks tickets, and I thought, since we'd be having drinks at the stadium, it would be a good idea to revisit Breadfruit. It's conveniently located just a couple of blocks from the light rail station, and we brought a six-pack of Red Stripe to enhance the experience.

We were delighted to be back, and we recognized one of the owners, whom we liked from our previous visit, but didn't see her partner, the cook who is Jamaican. Our friends were thoroughly impressed by the food, which was excellent.

We enjoyed fish escovich, jerk chicken, coconut curry tofu, and side orders of plantains, all of which were delicious. Everything was cooked to order and left a strong impression on our friends. The steamed vegetables and rice and beans on my plate were also fantastic.

yelp:train:259659.orig:
Hmmm....where do I start...SAVE YOUR MONEY!!! 

Honestly, if you don't mind paying through the ear for a mediocre meal, then feel free and pay a visit, but don't say yelp reviewers didn't give you fair warning. 

So I was taken here for my birthday, and I was super excited! I had heard good reviews and could not wait to get my hands on some stew chicken!! 

We started out with the drink menu, the mango drink with mint is very good and reasonably priced compared to everything on the menu. 

Since we heard the portions were small, we decided we would each get an app, share, and then each order entrees. 

The Festival with mango chutney...taste was good, price was ridiculous!!!!!! They seriously make 2 tiny breadsticks, cut them in half and stick it in a small bowl of chutney. I don't care what fancy ingredients you use, but for $5.95, at least add some more breadsticks!!! 

The plantain and avocado rolls were also small, the plantain was not even fully ripened, and the cost was $7.95..., these ingredients are not fancy, or expensive, and the flavor was disappointing. 

I decided that I was going to get the the jamaican patty with fish, but after being slightly confused
yelp:train:259659.para:
Hmm... where should I begin? SAVE YOUR MONEY!!! 

If you're okay with spending a lot for an average meal, go ahead and give it a try, but don't complain to Yelp reviewers if you're not satisfied. 

I went there for my birthday and was really looking forward to it, having heard good things and especially excited about the stew chicken. 

We started with the drink menu; the mango drink with mint was quite good and reasonably priced compared to the rest of the menu. 

Given the small portions, we each ordered an appetizer to share and then got our main courses. 

The Festival with mango chutney tasted okay, but the price was outrageous!!!!!! They serve just two tiny breadsticks, cut in half, with a small bowl of chutney. For $5.95, they should at least add more breadsticks! 

The plantain and avocado rolls were also small, with the plantain not fully ripe, and they cost $7.95... the ingredients weren't fancy or expensive, and the taste was disappointing. 

I was planning to get the Jamaican patty with fish, but got a bit confused...

yelp:train:259769.orig:
Overall, I'd tend to choose Trader Joes over F/E. In most cases the food tastes better. That and F/E sells some of the same stuff as Safeway for more.

F/E is supposed to be a healthy affordable store. Milk isn't healthy (and it's in too many of their products that don't need it -- fail for someone lactose intolerant), and the prices on some of your the meals here are just slightly lower than going to a restaurant for better food. 

If they would price match and produced better food without lactose all over the place, I'd give this place a better rating. Otherwise, it's just a place to go if I'm in the area or the rest of the places are closed.
yelp:train:259769.para:
Generally, I prefer Trader Joe's to F/E, as the food often tastes better. Additionally, F/E sometimes offers items similar to Safeway at higher prices.

F/E claims to be a healthy, affordable option. However, milk isn't healthy, and it's used excessively in products that don't require it, which is a major issue for those who are lactose intolerant. The meal prices here are only slightly lower than restaurant prices, but the food quality is inferior.

For F/E to improve, they need to match prices and provide better food without lactose. Until then, it's merely a convenient stop if other options are unavailable.

yelp:train:259813.orig: Ok place. Good for beer and relaxing. Just plan on staying a while. Sat at a table for 15-20 minutes before a server took our drink order. It took 30 minutes to get food and after asking for the check it took aboit 20 minutes before our server dropped it off. I might come back if I'm planning on staying a while. Other wise I'll try a place that pays more attention to the service.
yelp:train:259813.para: Sure spot. It's nice for a beer and unwinding, but you'll want to stick around. We waited about 15-20 minutes at our table before a server took our drink order. The food took 30 minutes to arrive, and even after asking for the check, it was another 20 minutes before our server brought it. I might return if I plan to stay longer, but otherwise, I'll look for somewhere with better service.

yelp:train:260447.orig:
I kind of feel bad giving this place only 1 star but I've given them many chances and 1 star is what they deserve. 

The food is overall pretty good. Whoever the chef is, bravo. It's worlds better than the typical Italian slop in this area. However, the variety and selection are lacking. As for the service, if there were stars that went the other way, I would give it a -5. I've been here three times and have never had good service. As a matter of fact, the last time I was there we had to walk out leaving a big fat 0 on the tip line. I really hate doing that too but when you're ignored for 20 minutes when there's no one else in the place you deserve it. 

This restaurant is also wayyyyyy too stuck up for its own good. I roll my eyes just thinking about it. None of the times I've been there has there been a decent crowd either. Maybe that should tell you something.
yelp:train:260447.para:
While I hesitate to give this place such a low rating, I feel it's warranted after multiple visits. The food is actually quite good; the chef deserves praise for the quality. It surpasses the usual subpar Italian food in the area. But the menu lacks variety, and the selection is limited. Regarding service, if there were negative stars, I'd give it those. I've been here three times, and each time, the service has been poor. On my last visit, we had to leave without leaving a tip, which I regret but felt justified due to the 20-minute wait with no one else in the restaurant. 

The restaurant also comes across as overly pretentious, which is off-putting. I can't help but roll my eyes at the experience. Additionally, there's never been a decent crowd during my visits, which might indicate something about the place.

yelp:train:260983.orig:
I went here today for my bi-monthly eyebrow wax and I made a note that I have to update because since my last review this has really been my go-to place for eyebrows and they've always been great. This in large part has to do with the fact that they appear to now have a dedicated wax lady on hand, instead of just letting whoever isn't doing a pedicure take care of you.

I'm really mad at myself for this, but I cannot remember her name! I know it starts with a Z, so that should narrow it down for you. For the sake of this review, I'll act like we're old friends and Z is my cute little best friend nickname for her. Z is great. She always compliments my eyebrows and never asks if I ""want upper lip"". She is quick and accurate and she hardly ever has to go over my eyebrows with a tweezer to get all the strays she missed with the wax. I really hate that. I have pretty strong eyebrows. Not sure if that makes things easier or harder on her, but she always does a good job. Well worth the $8+Tip (bring cash though, because they charge $1 to use the card swiper). 

G + Z = BFF 4 Life
yelp:train:260983.para:
I visited for my regular eyebrow wax today and I need to revise my previous review because this place has become my favorite spot. The quality has consistently been excellent. A key factor is that they now have a dedicated wax specialist, rather than relying on whoever isn't doing a pedicure.

I'm frustrated with myself, but I can't recall her name. I know it begins with a Z, which should help. For this review, let's pretend she's my old friend, my cute Z. Z is fantastic. She always praises my eyebrows and never asks if I want an upper lip wax. She's efficient and precise, and rarely needs to use tweezers to remove any stray hairs missed by the wax. I really dislike that. My eyebrows are naturally strong, so I'm not sure if that makes her job easier or harder, but she always does a great job. It's definitely worth the $8 plus tip (make sure to bring cash, as they charge $1 for using the card swiper). 

Z + G = BFF 4 Life

yelp:train:261380.para: The egg was quite undercooked, and in general, it was of very poor quality.

yelp:train:262066.orig: This review is for the Xtreme Couture MMA camp.  Randy Couture hosts these camps about twice per year and they are limited to 40 people.  My significant other recently attended the camp and had nothing but positive things to say about the experience.  Not only did he receive instruction from top trainers, but Randy also provided the attendees with coaching and took the time to talk to every one in the class.  I watched a couple of the sessions and was amazed at how large and clean the gym area is.  I have been inside several MMA gyms and most are much smaller and don't always smell so great.  Not only is the gym extremely nice, but Randy Couture seems to be a class act.   He definitely wants to go back for another session.\n\nAdditional note--the gym also sells punch cards that allow people who are just visiting the area to drop in and train.
yelp:train:262066.para: This review pertains to the Xtreme Couture MMA camp, led by Randy Couture, who conducts the camps approximately twice a year with a maximum of 40 participants. My partner recently attended and spoke highly of the experience. He not only received training from skilled instructors but also benefited from Randy's personal coaching and attention to each participant. I observed a few sessions and was impressed by the spacious and well-maintained gym. Compared to other MMA gyms I've visited, this one is notably larger and more hygienic. Additionally, Randy Couture appears to be a professional individual who genuinely wants to return for another session. The gym also offers punch cards for visitors to drop in and train.

yelp:train:262609.para: This place has really declined in quality. In my last few visits, the food wasn't properly prepared, the fries were still frozen, and they didn't include the items that should have come with my order. It's now a total disappointment. I used to enjoy eating here.
