yelp:test:97.orig:
When there's this much hype about a place, it's hard to live up to, but they did a pretty damn good job. Maybe not the best sandwich I've ever had in my life, but if it was any random sandwich shop I'd happened to stumble into, it would definitely be five stars without a second thought.

The chili cheese fries were among the best I've ever had. I don't know what they do to them - it's not the chili that's particularly great, it's not the cheese that's particularly great, and it's not the fries that are particularly great. But somehow, putting them all together just turns it into unbeatable awesome.

The sandwich itself (I got the corned beef) was very good despite the fact that I hate coleslaw. But they don't mean the typical mayo-and-carrot-and-purple-onion coleslaw; they make it with vinegar and oil, so it's basically just like seasoned lettuce. They put a bit much of it on, which overwhelmed the rest of the ingredients at first, but just pull about half of the slaw off and you have a kick-ass sandwich. The hot sauce goes really well on it too. And for a pretty reasonable price, I might add. Normally, I'd expect it to be about twice as much with that kind of reputation and do
yelp:test:97.para:
Despite the high expectations, they managed to impress me quite a bit. While it wasn't the best sandwich I've ever had, if it were just another random sandwich shop, I'd give it a perfect five-star rating without hesitation.

The chili cheese fries were outstanding. The combination of the fries, the chili, and the cheese was simply unbeatable. Each component wasn't particularly remarkable on its own, but together, they created an extraordinary dish.

The corned beef sandwich was very good, even though I usually dislike coleslaw. Their version, made with vinegar and oil instead of mayo, was more like seasoned lettuce. Initially, the coleslaw was a bit overpowering, but removing some of it revealed a fantastic sandwich. The hot sauce also complemented it well. And to top it off, the price was quite reasonable for the quality and reputation it enjoys.

yelp:test:110.orig:
Last weekend my mother and I headed down to the strip to get some weekly goods - lunch meat and cheese from Penn Mac - veggies at Stans - needed some new spices from Penzeys for a chili I was going to make that day....we were both a little hungry and knew we wanted to have a snack before shopping.

We parked in front of Roland's and see the sign: Famous for Lobster Rolls and Bloody Mary's!

Perfect. 

My mother got the Lobster Roll, which she said was 'good'. The bread, from Mancini's, was of course tasty - toasted and buttery - delicious mostly because it was Mancini's bread. I had the Lobster Roll minus the carbs on a salad - and the lobster was tasty, no doubt , I mean, lobster is just - good. For the price though, not sure that I got enough bang for my buck. The salad was something I could have picked up at Get-Go in the pre-made section. I just didn't feel satisfied at the end of my meal. I couldn't even drink my Bloody Mary (this is a rare affair), way too much horseradish, and I often like horseradish in my Bloodies!

And it was cold - didn't even take my winter coat off. So, needless to say, not the best experience.

Talk about false advertisement...
yelp:test:110.para:
Last weekend, my mom and I went to the strip to buy some weekly essentials—lunch meat and cheese from Penn Mac, veggies from Stans, and new spices from Penzeys for a chili I planned to make that day. We were a bit hungry and wanted a snack before shopping, so we parked in front of Roland's, where we saw a sign advertising famous lobster rolls and Bloody Marys.

Perfect timing.

My mom ordered the lobster roll, which she found satisfactory. The bread, from Mancini's, was deliciously toasted and buttery. I opted for a lobster salad without the bread, and the lobster was indeed tasty. However, I felt the price didn't justify the portion size. The salad could have been bought at Get-Go's pre-made section. I wasn't fully satisfied with my meal and couldn't even enjoy my Bloody Mary, which was too spicy with too much horseradish. Additionally, it was cold, and I didn't even take off my winter coat. Overall, it wasn't a great experience, and it felt like a case of false advertising.

yelp:test:123.orig: Worst Brazilian wax I have ever gotten. Extremely Painful and inefficient, still had a red welt 3 days later. She also used the same stick the entire time which is not sanitary. Eyebrow waxing is significantly overpriced at $18. Do not go here for waxing!
yelp:test:123.para: I had the worst Brazilian wax experience; it was extremely painful and not at all efficient. I still had a red welt three days after the waxing. Moreover, she used the same waxing stick throughout, which is unhygienic. Considering the price of $18 for eyebrow waxing, it's way too expensive. Avoid this place for any waxing needs!

yelp:test:158.orig:
My boyfriend and I stayed here for a long weekend because we both had interviews in the North Shore area, which was a short car ride away. We got a very good rate on Hotwire--otherwise I don't think we would have been able to stay here. Although the hotel was very comfortable and in a good location, we could hear every noise from the hallway and adjacent rooms (including the bathroom). I was sitting up in bed reading, and every time the people next door closed a drawer in their bureau the whole headboard would shake.

Parking was also expensive. We needed to use the car several times during our stay, so we had to valet park, which was over $20/day (plus tips each time we picked up or dropped off the car).

The coffee shop attached to the hotel is just OK. The breakfast/lunch place was not very good. You will probably have to venture a bit to find affordable and good quality food (other than the hotel restaurant, which I can't comment on because we did not eat there given the high prices).

One perk--the hotel does offer free internet, but it is a low bandwidth version. We didn't need the internet for work or anything so it was hard to justify paying for the high speed, so we
yelp:test:158.para:
For a long weekend while we both had interviews in the North Shore area, my boyfriend and I stayed here, taking advantage of a great deal on Hotwire. The hotel was comfortable and conveniently located, but the noise from the hallway and neighboring rooms was quite disruptive. For instance, when the people next door closed a drawer, it caused the headboard to shake noticeably.

Parking was costly; we had to valet park each day, which cost over $20, plus tips for picking up and dropping off the car.

The hotel's coffee shop was merely satisfactory, and the breakfast and lunch options were not impressive. We would likely need to explore nearby areas to find affordable and good-quality food, except for the hotel restaurant, which we didn't use due to its high prices.

A positive aspect was the free internet, though it was of lower bandwidth. Since we didn't need it for work, we didn't find it worth paying for the faster connection.

yelp:test:160.orig: I had great expectations that were sadly not met. For the price of the room, I was expecting a LOT more for my buck, maybe I was just too optimistic. I will say the whole hotel was clean and didn't have any unsanitary conditions. But it just seemed outdate for the top price paid, it could use a spruce up. Our room was ready before posted check-in time and when we got to the room there were no problems. The wi-fi was free and the tv channel selections were pretty good. I would say this is an average hotel for amenities with a high price tag.\n Usually when you pay top tier rates, I usually expect the service staff to be very friendly, didn't get that here, I think I had one of the service staff actually talk to me unsolicited. I would not revisit The Westin Convention Center.\n My wife would probably give it 4 star just for the shower head, it was pretty amazing, but when that is the highlight, I don't think there is value here.
yelp:test:160.para: My expectations were high but sadly fell short. Given the room rate, I anticipated much more, perhaps I was overly optimistic. The hotel was clean throughout, with no sanitation issues, but it felt outdated for the price, needing some updates. The room was ready early, and there were no issues upon arrival. The free Wi-Fi and decent TV channel options were positives. Overall, it felt like an average hotel with premium pricing for its amenities. Typically, when paying top rates, I expect friendly service, which was lacking here; I only had one staff member approach me. I wouldn't return to The Westin Convention Center. My wife might rate it 4 stars for the shower, which was exceptional, but that's the only highlight, making the overall value questionable.

yelp:test:166.orig: Great spot for weird or obscure parts, general maintenance items, and to  borrow a wrench or two.  Gerry is like a wise eccentric uncle.   I remember going there for my first time in the early 90's and it hasn't changed in almost 20 years.
yelp:test:166.para: This place is perfect for finding unusual or rare parts, as well as for general maintenance needs. You can also borrow a wrench or two if needed. Gerry is akin to a wise and quirky uncle. I recall visiting for the first time in the early 90s, and it hasn't altered much in nearly two decades.

yelp:test:173.orig: I just moved to the area and went here for the first time the other day. Tomaso did a great job! I high recommend this place.
yelp:test:173.para: When I recently relocated to the area, I visited this place for the first time, and I must say, Tomaso exceeded my expectations. I highly recommend it.

yelp:test:200.orig: My favorite pizza in the city. Hoagies are also pretty good but the pizza takes the spotlight. One of the best places to shoot pool in the south hills next door, what more do you need?
yelp:test:200.para: This is my top pick for pizza in the city, though the hoagies are also quite tasty. The pizza really stands out. Right next door, there's one of the best pool halls in the south hills—what else could you want?

yelp:test:207.orig: This place has the best pizza I've ever had besides Keste and Paulie Gs in NYC.  Wood fired greatness.  Expect to wait on weekends in a crowded wine bar.  FANTASTIC red sauce and olive oil.  Not extensive on the wine list but good by the glass selection. A gem in Pittsburgh.
yelp:test:207.para: This location offers pizza that rivals the top spots in NYC, like Keste and Paulie G's, known for its wood-fired excellence. On weekends, you might need to wait in a bustling wine bar. The red sauce and olive oil are outstanding. While the wine list isn't extensive, they have a good selection by the glass. It's a hidden gem in Pittsburgh.

yelp:test:251.orig: Two words: grossly overrated. If I am going to wait an hour for breakfast/brunch, it needs to not only be good, but also unique. Unfortunately, Pamela's is neither of these things. Then again, the hour-long wait does provide you will ample time to find a ATM because they only take cash. If you want to wait in line for an hour for food that is both good and unique, try Coca Cafe.
yelp:test:251.para: Two words: overly hyped. For a one-hour wait on breakfast or brunch, the food must be both excellent and distinctive. Sadly, Pamela's fails to meet these criteria. On the flip side, that long wait gives you plenty of time to locate an ATM since they accept cash only. If you're willing to stand in line for an hour for quality and uniqueness in your meal, consider Coca Cafe instead.

yelp:test:256.orig: This restaurant is in a great location and has nice ambiance. That is where the positive ends. The food is LOUSY. I paid $9 for a stainless steel mixing bowl of iceberg lettuce with a little frozen (OK, it was thawed, but had previously been frozen) corn, about 4 tablespoons of black beans and the same amount of feta. As a vegetarian, this salad was one of two that had some sort of substance to make one think of a meal. What a disappointment - I won't be back.
yelp:test:256.para: While the restaurant's setting and atmosphere are commendable, the experience ends there. The food quality is extremely poor. I spent $9 on a salad that consisted of a small portion of iceberg lettuce, some thawed corn, and a minimal amount of black beans and feta cheese. As a vegetarian, this was one of the few salads that offered any substance. It was a letdown, and I won't be returning.

yelp:test:282.orig: I have been a long time fan but after having a issue with an item I purchased online this Christmas I will not be shopping here again. I tried to take a item back with the packing slip that came on the item, the associate told me I was unable to do the return with the packing slip but she could do it if I had the email confirmation.. I didn't have it on my phone so I went.. I found the email sent it back to my phone and tried the return again.. todays associate told me I could not do the return with the confirmation email but needed the packing slip.. which I could not find at the time. I asked to speak with the manager on duty which the associate called.. Valencia the manager on duty would not come up to speak with me but told the associate that they couldn't do the return.. I still have this 100.00 worth of stuff I don't need.. I would not recommend anyone from purchasing from Kmart!
yelp:test:282.para: As a longtime customer, I had a disappointing experience this holiday season when trying to return an item. Initially, the staff member said I needed the email confirmation for the return, but I didn't have it on my phone. After retrieving the email, I was then told I needed the packing slip, which I couldn't locate. When I asked to speak with the manager, she refused to come to me and told the associate that the return couldn't be processed. Now, I have $100 worth of items I can't return. I won't be shopping at Kmart again and I don't recommend it to others.

yelp:test:289.orig:
On Yelp, a 500th review is a milestone.  It's a big deal and for those of us that have written hundreds of reviews, it's a place to talk about a business that has had an impact on our lives  Fairpoint Communications is such a business.  Fairpoint took over Verizon's local phone service in this area recently and this is a review of their ability to deliver.  In a nutshell, it has been a disaster.

Fairpoint took over my land line at home and billing was screwed up.  They got the new business when my office moved to Portsmouth.  One day the landlines stopped working and our customers got a message that the number was no longer in service.  When that was fixed, the lines didn't roll over properly.  The billing was never correct.  The internet connection required rebooting the DSL modem up to 15 times a day.  Calls about all of these issues rarely went well.  People were apologetic but problems remained.  Calling about the same problem twice usually resulted in two different answers.  Two different people in my office were reduced to tears.  Most people and companies I know with Fairpoint in New Hampshire and Maine are having similar troubles..

My company switched carriers recentl
yelp:test:289.para:
On Yelp, reaching the 500th review is a significant milestone, especially for those who have penned hundreds. For such individuals, it's an opportunity to discuss a business that has significantly affected their lives. Fairpoint Communications, which recently took over Verizon's local phone service in this area, is one such business. Their performance in delivering services has been a major disappointment.

Fairpoint assumed responsibility for my home landline, but the billing was a mess from the start. When they took over my office's landline after a move to Portsmouth, the lines stopped working one day, and customers received a message that the number was no longer in service. Even after this was resolved, the lines didn't transfer correctly. The billing was consistently incorrect, and the internet connection required rebooting the DSL modem up to 15 times daily. Customer service calls rarely resolved issues satisfactorily; representatives were apologetic but the problems persisted. When the same issue was reported twice, two different answers were given. Two colleagues in my office were left in tears. Many people and businesses in New Hampshire and Maine with Fairpoint are experiencing similar difficulties.

Our company recently switched carriers.

yelp:test:306.orig: We just received the worst service ever I will never come back. Its shocking that on wing special night it was merly 6 tables. One person actually went to the back to fix their own drinks. We had To ask for everything numerous of times. Service was very slow ass and the management was not customer friendly. I personally was not thinking to take pictures of all the screw ups due to all of the complaints the whole table was making. I hated to make so many complaints but I've never experienced such horrible service. It was awful We couldn't find any positive in it. As a matter of fact the waitress didn't even come back to pick up all the checks. It Was 7 of us and 6 ppl got their checks. We told the management We needed to pay another check and that We didn't know why the waitress would leave one out, his response was unprofessional.  :(
yelp:test:306.para: We received the absolute worst service last night, and I won't be returning. It's astonishing that during the Wing Special Night, there were only six tables. We had to ask for everything multiple times, and the service was extremely slow. The staff wasn't very customer-friendly, and the management didn't help much. We were so focused on the numerous issues that we didn't even take pictures of the problems. I didn't want to complain, but this was the worst service I've ever experienced. It was terrible, and we couldn't find any positives. To make matters worse, the waitress didn't return to collect our checks; six of us had to pay for an extra check, and the management's response was unprofessional. :-(

yelp:test:327.orig:
There are much better choices in uptown Charlotte!  Let me start with the good...the front desk staff. The three people who assisted me at the front desk were extremely friendly and helpful. Great customer service!

Now the bad...stains. There is no other way to describe everything in my room. Multiple stains on the carpeting and the comforter. The bathrobe hanging on the back of the bathroom door had a huge brown stain on the sleeve that I kept telling myself was makeup from the last occupant. Every, yes every, bath towel had a stain (either black or yellow). There was stained grout behind the toilet like it had leaked sometime in the past. Even the shower curtain was stained. Then there was the hair dryer. It was sooooo sticky that I didn't even want to touch it. It appeared to be covered in about 15 years worth of cheap hairspray. 

I can appreciate that the hotel is getting older and may need a renovation soon, but come on people!  How about you splurge and replace your bath towels and hair dryers now!  

Let me be clear that I think the cleaning staff is doing the best they can with what they have been given. They just need a better starting product!
yelp:test:327.para:
In uptown Charlotte, there are far superior options available! To begin with the positives, the front desk staff was exceptionally friendly and helpful. They provided great customer service.

However, the negatives are significant. My room was covered in stains. The carpet and comforter had multiple stains, and the bathrobe on the bathroom door had a large brown stain. Every bath towel, whether black or yellow, was stained. There was also stained grout behind the toilet, suggesting a past leak, and the shower curtain was stained as well. The hair dryer was so sticky that I hesitated to touch it, seemingly coated in years of cheap hairspray.

While I understand the hotel is aging and may need renovation, it's time to invest in new bath towels and hair dryers. The cleaning staff is doing their best with what they have, but they deserve better quality products to work with.

yelp:test:409.orig: ate there recently for dinner, it was wonderful. i ordered the goat curry and was excited to try goat for the first time right after i found out it is the most consumed meat on earth outside of the US BUT the table of 12 Indian gentleman behind us had ordered it all....which led me to believe these guys know what they are doing. instead i tried the lamb and it was perfect. i really liked the candor of our waiter \""andrew\"", which was not his name but he called himself that with a grinning smirk; i told him i had ordered kingfisher lagers before and would love to try another beer since they had a few indian beers, he told me to stay with the kingfisher. also, once he told me the goat curry wasn't available i ordered tandoori lamb, he assured me it was good but encouraged me to try the curried lamb since i originally ordered goat curry. my ladyfriend ordered a veggie dish and loved it, we got some bread as well, she ordered some REASONABLY (which is becoming more rare these days) priced wine. all in all the food was very good and the service was near perfect, i like when a waiter can read what you are looking for, makes reco's on that judgment and nails them. i will be going back t
yelp:test:409.para: Recently, I dined there for dinner and it was fantastic. I decided to try the lamb instead of the goat curry, which I had learned is the most consumed meat globally outside the US. However, a table of 12 Indian gentlemen behind us ordered all the goat curry, making me think they know their cuisine well. The lamb I tried was perfect. Our waiter, whom I affectionately called Andrew despite his grin, was very candid. He recommended staying with the Kingfisher lager, which I had previously enjoyed, and suggested the curried lamb when the goat curry wasn't available. My girlfriend loved her vegetable dish, and we had some bread. She also ordered reasonably priced wine. The food was excellent, and the service was nearly flawless. I appreciate when a waiter understands what I'm looking for and makes good recommendations. I plan to return.

yelp:test:422.orig: HOHO CHERRY HOUSE, not to be confused with a brothel, offers average food at cheap prices. Fast delivery and friendly staff. No matter what protein you pick it pretty much tastes the same.
yelp:test:422.para: HOHO CHERRY HOUSE, distinct from any brothel, serves up ordinary food at budget prices. They provide quick delivery and have a pleasant staff. Regardless of the protein you choose, the taste is fairly consistent.

yelp:test:434.orig: Honestly wish I could give it zero stars based on today... ? Security is beyond the worst. Check in with the airline was smooth, thats about it.\nI'm sure its not this bad everyday, or it would be on the news and or shutdown from the lack of business....
yelp:test:434.para: I really wish I could rate it zero stars based on today. The security was terrible. While the check-in with the airline went smoothly, that's about it. I'm sure it's not this bad every day; otherwise, it would be all over the news and closed down due to lack of business.

yelp:test:445.orig: Great little airport. Now direct connection to Europe. Live piano music in terminal. Us airways hub. Rental car shuttles run every few minutes. Lots of charging stations for electronic devices. Airport is also small enough to make transfers easy.
yelp:test:445.para: This is a charming little airport with a new direct flight to Europe. It features live piano music in the terminal. It serves as a hub for US Airways, and rental car shuttles operate every few minutes. There are numerous charging stations for electronics. The airport is conveniently small, making it easy to transfer between gates.

yelp:test:457.orig:
Having grown up in North Carolina, I've had lots of Barbecue (and I also smoke my own).  I feel I can adequately judge the quality of BBQ.  This particular establishment was unique in that it's right off the side of a highway and has drive-in microphones and ordering stations straight out of the 50's.  I did feel a little uneasy in the parking lot as it was in a shady part of town, but not a big deal.  I ordered the 1/4 Barbecue chicken meal and substituted potato salad for the slaw and onion rings for the fries.  In addition I ordered a ""Minced"" barbecue sandwich, which is the classic barbecue that people would think of when talking about North Carolina style BBQ.   

First let me say that FoodNetwork came to this establishment for the unique nature of the 50's style drive-in and for the unique way that the pieces of barbecue chicken are prepared.  They are deep fried and then dunked in barbecue sauce.  I will say that it is unique; however as the above would suggest, it is quite greasy.  It was ""okay"" but I wouldn't say it is anything to specifically come here for.  

As for the barbecue, it is also ""okay;"" I can safely say that the meat is not smoked (there is no
yelp:test:457.para:
Growing up in North Carolina, I've had plenty of barbecue, and I even smoke my own, so I feel confident in my ability to judge its quality. This place stood out because it's located right off the highway with 1950s-style drive-in microphones and ordering stations. While I felt a bit uneasy in the parking lot, which was in a less safe area, it wasn't a major concern. I ordered a quarter-pound barbecue chicken meal, substituting potato salad for coleslaw and onion rings for fries. Additionally, I got a "minced" barbecue sandwich, which is the classic North Carolina-style barbecue.

Firstly, the FoodNetwork visited this place because of its unique 1950s drive-in setup and the distinctive preparation method for the barbecue chicken. The chicken is deep-fried and then dipped in barbecue sauce, which is indeed unique but also quite greasy. While it was acceptable, I wouldn't recommend it as a must-try dish.

Regarding the barbecue itself, it was also just okay. I can confirm that the meat isn't smoked, as there's no evidence of that process.

yelp:test:471.orig:
I've heard this restaurant from listening to NPR in Charlotte, so I went and invited some of my friends and decided to come here to check it out. Here are my reviews.

Venue - the ambiance inside the restaurant is like being in Japan. If you have a large group of people, your group will be sitting as if you're sitting on a floor, but your not. The sits are elevated and the center piece is wide open. It's a comfortable sitting arrangement.

Sushi - the Unagi (Eel) was cooked perfectly. The softcrab shells are not bad, but I had better ones before.  The rice was cooked very well not to sticky or clumpy. They need better selections in sushi.

Presentation - the restaurant lacks in presentation.  It was a very simple dish put together.  

Sake - they are pricey. $15.00 minimum. 

Ramen - the soup was very tasty.  

Overall,  if you are craving for ramen, this is the best place so far I've tasted. As for sushi, I would only come here once. I've had much better sushi with awesome presentation and much better selections in California before.  I still have yet to find a sushi that will replace my experienced in California. Also, if you don't tip enough. You will be called back
yelp:test:471.para:
I learned about this restaurant from an NPR segment in Charlotte and decided to visit with some friends. Here are my thoughts:

Ambiance - The restaurant has a Japanese vibe, with floor-style seating that’s actually elevated, creating a comfortable setting, especially for large groups.

Sushi - The Unagi was cooked perfectly, but the soft crab shells were average compared to others I've tried. The rice was well-cooked, neither too sticky nor clumpy, but the selection could be improved.

Presentation - The dishes are quite basic and lack visual appeal.

Sake - Prices are on the high side, with a $15 minimum.

Ramen - The broth was delicious.

Overall, if you're in the mood for ramen, this place is top-notch. However, for sushi, I’d only return once. I've enjoyed much better sushi with impressive presentation and a wider variety in California. I haven't found a sushi place that matches the quality I experienced there. Also, don't forget to tip adequately, or you might be asked to pay more.

yelp:test:475.orig:
While there were no insect carcasses in my food, I was still not very impressed with my meal at PF Chang's.  I went for a ""business lunch"" with my boss.  Who thought I would ever enjoy working more than eating??--I think this meal was a first!

I got steamed veggies and brown rice.  Now I expected it to be pretty bland, since it mentioned no sauces added at all.  But the vegetables were rubbery, not crisp like they should be after a good steaming. The rice was pretty underdone as well, so all-in-all, they got nothing right.  I tried adding some sauces to liven it up a bit, but it was too little, too late.

Perhaps the biggest disappointment was the egg drop soup.  I usually add pepper to mine because I like the extra kick, but this needed much more help than a little pepper.  It was very bland, and didn't taste like anything.  Tasteless egg in water is definitely NOT something you want to keep eating.  And, of course, there was no salt and pepper on the table, so I couldn't even enjoy it the way I like. 

Because I didn't pay, I didn't complain to the waiter, but normally this would not have passed by me.  Though the lunch prices are pretty reasonable, I still would not r
yelp:test:475.para:
During my business lunch at PF Chang's, despite the absence of any insect carcasses in my food, I remained unimpressed. The meal was supposed to be a professional affair with my boss, but I found myself questioning whether I could ever enjoy work more than eating. This meal felt like a rare exception.

I ordered steamed vegetables and brown rice. I anticipated the food to be quite plain, as it stated no sauces were added. However, the vegetables were overly soft, lacking the crispness they should have after steaming. The rice was also undercooked, making the entire dish a miss. Even when I tried to spice it up with sauces, it was too little too late.

The egg drop soup was the most disappointing part. Usually, I add pepper for a bit of kick, but this soup needed much more than just a pinch. It was extremely bland and lacked any flavor, making the tasteless egg in water a dish I wouldn't want to eat again. Additionally, there was no salt and pepper on the table, so I couldn't even season it to my liking.

Although I didn't pay, I wouldn't have hesitated to complain to the waiter under normal circumstances. Despite the reasonable lunch prices, I wouldn't recommend this meal.

yelp:test:568.orig: This is a great bar if you have kids.... I know that sounds weird but listen. They have a beach  and tiki bar in the rear with cornhole, beer pong, ping pong, horseshoes etc.... They have a stage out there for live music. Big portions of food for not alot of cash. Becoming a Friday night tradition
yelp:test:568.para: This bar is fantastic if you're bringing kids... I understand it might seem unusual, but hear me out. They've got a beach-themed area with a tiki bar, complete with cornhole, beer pong, ping pong, and horseshoes. There's also a stage for live music. The food portions are generous and won't break the bank. It's turning into a Friday night staple for us.

yelp:test:581.orig: I took my car here to get my brakes replaced.  They did the work quickly and at a good price.  I went here on a recommendation from a friend, and now I recommend it to my friends when they need work done.
yelp:test:581.para: I brought my car here for new brake pads, and the service was both swift and reasonably priced. My friend vouched for this place, and now I do the same for anyone needing automotive repairs.

yelp:test:582.orig: 4 stars for Hardee's ?!?  It's no Culver's by a long shot but that Thick Burger was damn tasty !   I don't know if the restaurant was clean but the drive thru service was good.
yelp:test:582.para: 4 stars for Hardee's? ! It falls far short of Culver's, but that Thick Burger was definitely delicious! I'm not sure about the cleanliness of the restaurant, but the drive-thru service was quite satisfactory.

yelp:test:605.orig: I was bringing my family to Cracker Barrow today a group of 6 but after hearing they fired a 73 year old Vet for handing out a Corn muffin I changed my mind...... I hope others feel the same way......
yelp:test:605.para: Today, I planned to bring my family of six to Cracker Barrel, but after learning they fired a 73-year-old veteran for giving out a corn muffin, I decided against it. I hope others share my concerns.

yelp:test:607.orig: Another chain sit down by the mall,  but not at the top of my list. The food hasn't seemed to change since I've gone here except for less options.  Waiting for a table is common unless you go at really off peak times. Recently got a burger there. Asked for well done,  and burger arrived bloody and red.  Waiter took it back and about 5 minutes brought the same burger back and was still pink on the inside.  Was offered something else,  but the others I was with were already done.  Did get a coupon for a return visit. Good deal with the 2 for $20 and an app if your food is cooked right.
yelp:test:607.para: Another restaurant chain has opened near the mall, but it's not at the top of my list. The menu hasn't changed much since I've visited, with fewer options available now. Waiting for a table is typical unless you arrive during very low-traffic hours. Recently, I ordered a well-done burger, but it arrived still very rare. The waiter took it back, and after about five minutes, the same burger was returned, still pink inside. I was offered something else, but my companions were already done eating. I did receive a coupon for a future visit. The 2 for $20 deal and the app for free food if it's cooked correctly seemed like a good offer.

yelp:test:615.orig: I've been to Monty's at least once for every meal. The omelettes are to die for, huge in quantity unique in ingredients- highly recommend the spinach and feta. The salads are the same thing, definitely large and delicious. Last night I went for dinner and got the meatless loaf, and now I want the recipe for the cashew gravy (if my memory serves me correctly, it was cashew...) to put on EVERYTHING. Amazing shakes and malts complete the perfect comfort/diner food experience.
yelp:test:615.para: I frequent Monty's for virtually every meal, and I've found their omelettes to be exceptional—both in size and in the unique blend of ingredients; the spinach and feta omelette is a standout. Their salads are equally impressive, large and tasty. Last night, I tried the meatless loaf and was so impressed that I now want the cashew gravy recipe (I believe it was made with cashews) to use on everything. The amazing shakes and malts add to the perfect diner experience, offering comfort and deliciousness.

yelp:test:627.orig:
I really dislike Menard's.  For every positive interaction I have, I have two negatives ones.  My husband and I just bought a house, so you can imagine how much time we spend here.  I prefer Home Depot but the prices are so much lower at Menard's.

In the matter of two weeks, all of this happened:

1. I bought a can of paint for our guest room.  I wanted the best paint, with the primer, all the bells and whistles.  I was covering purple.  I needed it.  The salesperson said I could pick from any four.  Yet, he could not tell me why one was rated higher or called premium over the other.  It was weird.  Like here are your options but I can not tell you what their difference really is.  And some were the same brand.

2. When painting the ceiling of said room, we open up a can of paint and notice it has clumps in it.  This paint was about six months old.  Nothing happened to it.  So we go back to Menard's.  We have shopped at several area Menard's, because we are about convenience.  The lady at the counter was SO rude.  We did not have our receipt and could not find it in their system.  We pay for most things in cash and apparently this is NOT a good idea at Menard's.  It had a Me
yelp:test:627.para:
I strongly dislike Menard's; for every positive experience, I encounter two negative ones. Since we recently bought a house, we frequently visit there. While I prefer Home Depot, Menard's offers better prices.

In just two weeks, these issues arose:

1. I purchased paint for our guest room, seeking the best option with primer and all the features. The paint was to cover purple. I needed it. The salesperson allowed me to choose from four options but couldn't explain why one was considered premium or superior to the others. It felt odd, like being given choices without understanding the differences, and some were from the same brand.

2. When painting the ceiling, we found clumps in the paint, which was about six months old and hadn't deteriorated. We returned to Menard's, having visited several locations for convenience. The counter staff were extremely rude. We didn't have our receipt and couldn't locate it in their system. Additionally, paying in cash seemed to be a problem at Menard's.

yelp:test:653.orig: I have been to The Ultimate several times for massages with Ellen and would highly recommend her.  She is very personable, friendly and professional.  I feel extremely relaxed after our sessions.  I also used Ellen for a prenatal massage when pregnant. Being as big and uncomfortable as I was, I was worried if I would be able to relax fully.  Ellen has blankets and pillows just for that reason! Super comfortable and she remembers to ask about the baby after she was born. Highly recommend!\n\nThe only reason I did not give 5 stars was that the hallway outside the room can get a bit loud if people are walking down, talking or laughing. They should maybe make that more of a quiet space with notices that people are in session.  Nothing Ellen could help though!
yelp:test:653.para:
I've visited The Ultimate multiple times for massages with Ellen, and I strongly recommend her. She's very personable, friendly, and professional, and I feel extremely relaxed after each session. I also had Ellen for a prenatal massage while pregnant. Despite being large and uncomfortable, I was worried about fully relaxing. But Ellen had blankets and pillows specifically for that, making it super comfortable. She even asked about the baby after it was born. Highly recommended!

The only reason I didn't give it five stars is because the hallway outside the room can get a bit noisy if people are walking, talking, or laughing. They might consider making it a quieter space with signs indicating that sessions are in progress. But Ellen couldn't control that!

yelp:test:662.orig: For the all hype this places gets, it sure didn't live up to it. Sure, it was busy- what place isn't on a Friday night in Wisconsin. Rail drinks were prices right- two drinks for $6.00. I ordered the lake perch- what a DISAPPOINTMENT. If you've been to Door County/eastern WI and had perch there, don't bother with Tobys perch. It was not good. My cottage cheese was warm, and my date's \""salad\"" was lettuce with salad dressing plopped on it. No veggies, croutons- nothing. The server was nice enough, for bring so overwhelmed and busy.
yelp:test:662.para: Despite the high expectations, this place fell short. On a typical Friday night in Wisconsin, it was indeed busy, but that's to be expected. The rail drinks were reasonably priced at $6 for two. However, my lake perch was a letdown. If you've tried perch in Door County or eastern Wisconsin, you won't find this one satisfactory. It was far from delicious. My cottage cheese was lukewarm, and my date's "salad" was just lettuce with dressing on the side—no vegetables or croutons. The server was polite, considering the chaos and crowd.

yelp:test:700.orig: Decent drinks + chill atmosphere + Irish Nachos (oh God yes) + lack of sketchy people grinding on you = WIN.
yelp:test:700.para: Good drinks + relaxing ambiance + Irish Nachos (oh man, yes!) + no creepy individuals bothering you = a definite win.

yelp:test:726.orig: Clybourne is the best student bar in Champaign. Unlike most of the other campus bars, Clybourne offers a multi-floored facility, with plenty of room for sitting, drinking, and dancing. Prices are awesome! Thursdays feature $1 Coronas, Tuesdays are \""Wine Nights\"" where they serve $8 bottles of wine and champagne. Sundays, my favorite, are $1 you-call-its. The music is always great and the place is slammed most nights of the week. I've hosted lots of parties there-- and I always get a ridiculous amount of booze for the prices I pay (also get a private room).
yelp:test:726.para: Clybourne stands out as the premier student bar in Champaign. It boasts a multi-level setup with ample space for sitting, drinking, and dancing, setting it apart from other campus venues. The pricing is fantastic! On Thursdays, you can enjoy $1 Coronas, while Tuesdays are dedicated to "Wine Nights" with $8 bottles of wine and champagne. Sundays are my absolute favorite, offering $1 "you-call-its." The music is consistently great, and the place is usually packed most nights. I've hosted numerous parties there, and the amount of alcohol I receive for the prices is incredible—plus, you can even rent a private room.

yelp:test:727.orig:
They seem to have everything. Obscure films, B films, foreign films, nearly every weird movie I've found out on the internet, they have it. (One time there was some anime I wanted to see but they didn't have, but they explained that all the copies out there were pirated, and they'd be happy to add it to their collection if I could find a legitimate source for them.)

Secondly... its pretty cheap if you buy a renters block.

I kind of wish there was a way to return videos without wading into campus, though.
yelp:test:727.para:
They appear to have an extensive collection, including niche and foreign films that I've discovered online. There was one instance where I wanted to watch some anime, but it wasn't available; they explained that all copies were pirated, and they would be happy to add it if I could find a legitimate source.

Secondly, the rental prices are quite reasonable with a renters block.

I wish there was a way to return videos without having to go to campus.

yelp:test:728.orig: It's like a portal into a chasm of anime, classics, world, documentary and varied films and cartoons. For Champaign, these guys really have an outstanding collection of rare films.\n\nWhat prevents me from giving it 5 starts is their stupid rule that you must have a special card and meet special requirements to rent a film from them, including being over 18 (for *ANY* film)
yelp:test:728.para: It feels like stepping into a vast universe of anime, classics, documentaries, and diverse films and cartoons. In Champaign, this place truly boasts an exceptional collection of rare movies. The only reason I can't award it five stars is their frustrating policy requiring a special card and meeting certain conditions to rent a film, with an age restriction of 18 or older for any movie.

yelp:test:739.orig: The sangria here is awful. I think it was a tequila sunrise. The food is greasy and not in a good way. The only thing good was the goat cheese. But it is goat cheese. How can you mess that up?
yelp:test:739.para: The sangria is terrible; I believe it was a tequila sunrise. The food is unappealing and greasy. The only positive aspect was the goat cheese, but even that seems off. How could they botch something as simple as goat cheese?

yelp:test:742.orig: I love this place.  My friends and I try to have a 'girl's night out' once a month and we frequent Radio Maria because of the delicious cuisine and the atmosphere.  It is relaxing and has several conversation pieces.  The service is spectacular.  This is one of my favorite local spots to dine in Champaign
yelp:test:742.para: I adore this spot. My friends and I make it a point to enjoy a 'girl's night out' every month, and we often visit Radio Maria due to its exquisite food and ambiance. The place is tranquil and offers plenty of topics for discussion. The service is outstanding. It's one of my go-to dining locations in Champaign.

yelp:test:755.orig: Wow. I have been going to this practice for 3-4 years. I have had some troubles with them in the past but this is the kicker of them all. I just called and explained to the person at the front desk that I have been having some breast pain and didn't know if I should come in earlier than my Oct. 1st  Well Woman exam. Her response was, \""Well, if you come in early you will have to pay for an office visit.\"" I said, \""well if I wait I'll just talk to her about it at my Well Woman.\"" Her reply, \""if you talk to her about it then, then you will be charged extra.\"" My reply, \""just for talking about it??\"" Her reply, \""yup, I don't know what to tell you. Just go to your primary care physician.\"" I then explained to her that this was a gynecological issue... No response. Her overall tone was brash, rude, and short. Did I mention uncaring.\n\nUnbelievable. Never, ever have I been so appalled. A woman calls and says she has breast pain and isn't sure if she should come in and this is how the front desk responds!! I'm outraged and waiting for someone to call me back from the office. I think Dr. Johnstone has the right to know how the front desk is treating her patients.
yelp:test:755.para:
I've been a patient here for 3-4 years, and while I've had some issues in the past, this interaction is the worst yet. When I called to discuss breast pain and whether I should come in before my October 1st Well Woman exam, the front desk staff was unhelpful. They said I'd have to pay for an office visit if I came early, and if I waited, I'd be charged extra for discussing it at my appointment. I asked, "Is it just for talking about it?" and was told, "Yes." They suggested I see my primary care physician instead. When I pointed out that this was a gynecological issue, there was no response. The staff's tone was dismissive, rude, and short, and they seemed uncaring.

This is unbelievable. I've never been so appalled. When a woman calls with breast pain and the front desk responds this way, it's unacceptable. I'm outraged and waiting for a call back from the office. I believe Dr. Johnstone should be informed about how the front desk is handling patients.

yelp:test:767.orig: HUGE disappointment!!!! Stopped for a quick dinner before a show. Ordered 2 burgers medium. They came out extremely well done & the buns were hard & dry. The waitress took them back to the kitchen & returned with 2 more well done burgers! What the heck?! When we told her (& showed her), she apologized & took 20% off the bill. We didn't have time for round 3. They didn't even send a manager over. $30 for an inedible meal. We will not be back. I'd recommend trying somewhere else.
yelp:test:767.para: EXTREMELY disappointed with our dinner! We stopped for a quick meal before a show and ordered two medium burgers. Unfortunately, both burgers were overcooked, and the buns were hard and dry. The waitress returned with two more overcooked burgers. This was unacceptable! She apologized and offered a 20% discount, but we couldn't stay for another attempt. No manager was present to address the issue. At $30 for inedible food, we won't be returning. I suggest trying a different place.

yelp:test:771.orig: I have been going to this IHOP every month for 4 years. Our group is anywhere from 8 to 25. There are only two places in the restaurant that accommodate groups and for the most part, we have been seated relatively quickly. Over the past year, service has gone down hill. It started taking forever to get our order taken, get our drinks, or get our food. We are a very forgiving bunch and know it's not easy to serve a large group but as service started really sliding, our last trip ended the relationship. We had about 20 people and knew we would have to wait a bit, but after 30 minutes, we inquired how long and it was like \""your waiting for a table?\""the kept sitting people at the tables that only could accommodate large groups. How can you not remember a group when they take up the whole lobby? We called a near by breakfast place and they were thrilled to have our party, which grew smaller since some left at that point. We found a new home and they will get 5 stars on my review.
yelp:test:771.para: For four years, I've been visiting this IHOP monthly with groups ranging from 8 to 25 people. Typically, we've been seated promptly in one of the two designated areas for large parties. However, over the past year, the service has significantly declined. Orders are now taking much longer to be taken, drinks served, and meals delivered. Despite being understanding, the recent poor service led us to end our custom. On our last visit with about 20 people, we had to wait 30 minutes before anyone checked on us, and when we inquired, the staff seemed indifferent, even seating other parties in our reserved area. Given that we occupy a large space, it's hard to forget us. We ended up at a nearby breakfast spot, which was delighted to accommodate our group, which had shrunk by then. We've found a new favorite and will be leaving a 5-star review.

yelp:test:804.orig:
This should have been a better experience... 

I'll begin with the food.  We arrived on a Sunday afternoon after a visit to the Phoenix Art Museum.  We ordered a BLT salad off the lunch menu and a manicotti dish.  We also included a cup of the minestrone soup for a buck.  The salad was good and was accompanied by fresh, hot bread.  The minestrone soup was outstanding.  The salad and soup were brought out early, as we requested, and we had ample time to complete the salad before our entree arrived.  The manicotti was fine and a good enough portion size that we had to box some.   So far, a good dining experience.

Then the bill arrives.  The salad was 8.50 and then entree was full price.  We questioned the bill, as the ""lunch menu"" said the salad would be 5.99 and the entree 1.50 off.  The server actually apologizes and says he'll have the manager correct the mistake.  Then he comes back and tells us ""Sorry, manager says lunch prices only apply Mon-Fri"".  Nowhere on the menu does it say lunch only applies Monday through Friday, and we were never told.  I didn't press the issue, paid the bill and off we go.  

What could have been an overall pleasant experience ruined by
yelp:test:804.para:
This should have been a better dining experience...

To start, let's discuss the food. We visited on a Sunday afternoon after seeing the Phoenix Art Museum. We ordered a BLT salad from the lunch menu and a manicotti dish, adding a cup of minestrone soup for a dollar. The salad was satisfactory and came with fresh, hot bread. The minestrone was exceptional. The salad and soup were served promptly, giving us enough time to finish the salad before our main courses arrived. The manicotti was adequate, with a good portion that we had to take home. Up to this point, the dining experience was positive.

However, the bill was a letdown. The salad cost $8.50, while the entree was at full price. We were surprised because the menu stated the salad would be $5.99 and the entree $1.50 off. The server apologized and said the manager would fix the mistake. But when the server returned, he said, "Sorry, the manager says lunch prices only apply Monday through Friday." There was no mention of this restriction on the menu, and we were not informed. I didn't argue further, paid the bill, and left. 

What could have been a pleasant experience was marred by this oversight.

yelp:test:812.orig: This has been my car wash since I lived in midtown off 3rd street and Thomas. They do a great job, and are very accommodating if they miss a spot. They tend to be somewhat expensive, but then again they are not scratching your car with machines. I used to get the side wash with my Audi because of some modifactions that kept it from being on the rails, and for $15 you couldn't get a better wash in town. \n\nI don't recommend their detail service, as they are not very complete, but for car washes A+
yelp:test:812.para: Since I resided in midtown near 3rd Street and Thomas, this has been my go-to car wash. They excel at their work and are particularly helpful if they miss any spots. While they can be pricey, they don't damage your car with machines. For my Audi, which had some modifications that prevented it from using the rail system, I opted for the side wash, and for $15, it was the best wash in town. I wouldn't recommend their detailing service, as it's not thorough, but their car washes are outstanding.

yelp:test:883.orig:
This has to be the most ghetto and disrespectful dive I've ever been to. I usually don't play the race card, but unless you are a Spanish speaking Latino you will not be treated well by the staff.

As soon as I walked up to the counter, a pregnant cashier rolled her eyes and asked dully what I wanted. I couldn't pronounce the name of the combo I wanted but I blurted out the number associated with it and it had a picture. She looked over her shoulder at one of her associates and said something. The only words I caught were ""token gringo customer.""

They shared a giggle.  They were speaking in that half-assed Spanish that has a little English mixed in. Suffice it to say I was offended and promptly cancelled the order. I have not returned since then
yelp:test:883.para:
This place is the epitome of a disrespectful and rundown establishment. I generally avoid bringing up racial issues, but if you're not a Spanish-speaking Latino, you won't receive good service from the staff.

Upon approaching the counter, a pregnant cashier gave me a dismissive look and asked monotonously what I wanted. I struggled to pronounce the name of the combo I wanted, so I blurted out the number next to the picture. She then glanced at a colleague and said something, with the words "token gringo customer" clearly audible.

They chuckled together, using a mix of broken Spanish and English. Needless to say, I felt offended and immediately canceled my order. I haven't been back since.

yelp:test:918.orig: I have had terrible luck with this lawn service recently. Please do not furnish Sergio with your credit card number; he will put the card through on PayPal, which is very hard to stop when he is processing fraudulent charges. His crew stole a valuable tree-lopping tool from me at a house I was leasing right before I moved out. Then, after I moved out, he has billed me for monthly services for two months running because, despite being informed by me on the phone, he claims that I have to terminate his services in writing. \nThis is the worst consumer experience I have had in years and I feel that this behavior has to be stopped. I'm certain most people don't count obtaining a new credit card and taking a trip to small claims court as among the experiences they are looking forward to when hiring a landscaper.
yelp:test:918.para: I've been having extremely poor experiences with this lawn service lately. Please don't give Sergio your credit card details; he processes payments through PayPal, which is difficult to reverse if he's making fraudulent charges. His team took a valuable tree-trimming tool from me at a rental property just before I moved out. Following that, they've been charging me monthly fees for two consecutive months, even after I informed them verbally that I wanted to cancel their services. This has been the most disappointing customer service experience I've had in a long time, and I believe this kind of behavior needs to be addressed. Most people don't expect to have to get a new credit card and possibly go to small claims court when they hire a landscaper.

yelp:test:960.orig: What happened to all of the coverage on the local sports?  The Arcadia News used to be very supportive and involved in Arcadia High School athletics.  No articles and only some pictures of some of the sports these days.  Shouldn't a local paper support its local high school?
yelp:test:960.para: Where has all the coverage of local sports gone? The Arcadia News used to be quite active and supportive of Arcadia High School's athletic events. These days, there are hardly any articles, just occasional photos of some sports. Doesn't a local newspaper should be more involved in supporting its local high school?

yelp:test:979.orig:
I was across the street for a Dr appointment and decided to step into the AJs after to browse since it was ""right there"". Haven't been into one in years for the same reason that I probably won't return after the recent visit: way overpriced for things I can buy elsewhere. Almost everything in the store you can buy at any regular grocery store, and pay less for it. They do carry a small number of ""gourmet"" items on the shelves, but I can find those other places, too. 

So, you'd think that their deli or bakery or something would stand out, but not that I can tell. I was going to try something from the bakery case but it was all way overpriced and totally unimpressive looking. I was there in the AM so I did try a slice of the breakfast pizza that was out in the deli. First off, it took me several minutes to be served because the staff was busily ignoring me. Then when I did finally get my slice, I went to pay and eat it, and the thing was cold and chewy. The crust was just so tough. The eggs were somewhat dried out. I was seriously underwhelmed. 

The store was practically dead the whole time I was wandering around. The staff outnumbered the patrons BY FAR. How do these p
yelp:test:979.para:
I went to a doctor's appointment across the street and decided to pop into AJs to look around, as it was "right there." I haven't visited a store like this in years for the same reason I probably won't return: the prices are too high compared to what I can find elsewhere. Most of the items in the store are available at regular grocery stores, and I can get them for less. They do have a few gourmet items, but I can find those elsewhere too.

To be honest, I expected the deli or bakery to be a standout, but I didn't see anything impressive. I was about to try something from the bakery case, but everything seemed overpriced and unappealing. I decided to try a slice of the breakfast pizza in the deli, but it took a while to be served because the staff seemed to be ignoring me. When I finally got my slice, it was cold and chewy, with a crust that was too tough. The eggs were also a bit dry. Overall, I was quite disappointed.

The store was nearly empty while I was there, with way more staff than customers. How do these places stay in business?

yelp:test:990.orig:
I've been popping into the George and Dragon nearly every Thursday since last April for trivia nights.  I like the place.  The trivia host is entertaining and the place feels worn in, but not worn down.  I feel comfortable and welcome every time I visit.  Most weeks I end up ordering a couple beers from the rather large selection.  The drink prices, while high for some people's tastes, are comparable to what I've seen in other places.  Imports are going to cost more, it's the price you pay to have a selection of Boddington's, Murphy's and Guinness all in one place, among other things.

Normally on trivia nights I don't end up getting food, as although I find their portions proportional to the prices, I don't feel I need to eat half my weight in fish and chips in one sitting.  I have no qualms with the quality on the few occasions I've grabbed some eats, for example the curry chicken is very flavorful and highly recommended.  The dragon wings are another of my favorite, spicy but not overwhelming.  The fish and chips, as previously mentioned, are served on a giant platter and have generally been excellent.

I recommend at least one visit to this bar.  Don't be scared off by the
yelp:test:990.para:
Since April last year, I've been frequenting the George and Dragon for trivia nights almost every Thursday. I enjoy the place; the trivia host is engaging, and the atmosphere feels cozy yet not dilapidated. Each visit makes me feel at ease and welcomed. Typically, I order a couple of beers from their extensive menu. While the drink prices are on the higher side for some, they are in line with what I've seen elsewhere. The variety of imports, like Boddington's, Murphy's, and Guinness, justifies the cost.

On trivia nights, I usually don't opt for food, as I find their portion sizes suitable for the prices. When I have tried their offerings, the curry chicken has been particularly flavorful and is highly recommended. The dragon wings are also a favorite, offering a spicy kick without being overpowering. The fish and chips, served in generous portions, have generally been excellent.

I highly recommend at least one visit to this bar. Don't let the initial impression deter you.

yelp:test:1000.orig: Wow. Just, wow. As a former employee of this location, I'm sorely disappointed. I used to be a hostess here and always LOVED the food. So I figured I'd take my boyfriend to grab a nice breakfast. Boy was I wrong. I ordered the huevos rancheros with chorizo (always been my favorite) and ended up with eggs and bland potatoes, with chunky sour cream (ew) and a light sprinkling of chorizo. Um, what? I paid almost 30 bucks for this? The food was bland and not good at all. I couldn't even finish my meal it was that bad. I'll never go back. How disappointing. Maybe you should stop recruiting your employees/chefs from McDonalds. The good egg has really let itself go.
yelp:test:1000.para: Wow. Truly, wow. As someone who used to work there, I'm deeply let down. I was a hostess there and always adored the food. So, I decided to bring my boyfriend for a nice breakfast. I was so disappointed. I ordered my favorite, huevos rancheros with chorizo, but received eggs and tasteless potatoes, topped with chunky sour cream (yuck) and a light dusting of chorizo. What happened? I paid nearly $30 for this? The food was bland and terrible. I couldn't even finish my meal because it was that bad. I won't return. This is such a letdown. Maybe you should reconsider hiring your staff from McDonald's. The quality has really declined.

yelp:test:1004.orig: This was my first experience eating Jack in the Box since I moved from GA to AZ 2 days ago. The service was horrible! Cashier had attitude when I told her I was still reviewing the menu. When I was ready to place my order she was very rude & sighing as if she needed me to speed up. Then I watched as she prepared her food, placed it on a tray & walked off as my food sat in the window. The drive-thru person came to see if I had been helped & proceeded to bag my food after I told him I was waiting. This place needs better service.
yelp:test:1004.para: My first Jack in the Box experience since moving from GA to AZ two days ago was quite disappointing. The service was really poor. The cashier seemed annoyed when I was still looking at the menu. When I was ready to order, she was very unfriendly and kept sighing as if I was taking too long. She prepared her food, placed it on a tray, and walked away while my order sat in the window. The drive-thru attendant had to come out and bag my food because I was still waiting. This restaurant definitely needs to improve its service.

yelp:test:1025.orig: Must have been an off day last time. These partners are phenomenal!
yelp:test:1025.para: Last time must have been a slow day, but these partners are truly outstanding!

yelp:test:1035.orig:
Have been dying to try this kosher place for some time.
Went tonight and ordered a large 3 cheese pizza.  O M G american cheese???
I asked also for baked ziti and the lady said her ziti can't keep for a week so they don't make it.
Are you kidding me?
It was 19.00 with a drink.
I put the pizza in the trunk and went to La Bella
yelp:test:1035.para: I've been eager to visit this kosher restaurant for a while now. Tonight, I decided to try it out and ordered a large three-cheese pizza. Oh my gosh, it was filled with American cheese?! When I inquired about the baked ziti, the server mentioned they don't make it because it doesn't last a week. Are you serious? The meal, including a drink, cost me 19.00. I put the pizza in my trunk and headed to La Bella instead.

yelp:test:1051.orig: I miss Karsh's (no longer live in AZ), although I really like Bea's Bakery out here.  Chompies' bakery rivaled them on some items, but Karsh's made the BEST cakes.....I got one for my daughter's Bat Mitzvah.....and smaller cakes for birthdays and such.  Absolutely YUMMMMMMMMY.  Perfect cake, perfect icing.  Great challah, too.  Their other bakery items were also quite good....rugelach, hamentashen, brownies, cookies.  I'm just glad I didn't live close to them when I lived there.  Downside...they were always crowded, and I always had to wait awhile before getting served.
yelp:test:1051.para: I miss Karsh's, which is no longer in AZ, but I really enjoy Bea's Bakery where I am now. Chompies' bakery was competitive with Karsh's on some items, but Karsh's cakes were the absolute best—like the one I got for my daughter's Bat Mitzvah and smaller cakes for birthdays. They were simply DELICIOUS, with perfect cake and icing. Their challah was also fantastic. Other items like rugelach, hamentashen, brownies, and cookies were quite good too. I'm relieved I didn't live nearby when I was in AZ, as they were always busy and I often had to wait to be served.

yelp:test:1072.orig: To be honest, this place sucks so much as compared to how it used to be. Like all vintage clothing stores, you have to dig through piles of crap to find that one diamond in the rough. Buffalo Exchange is no longer like that store. Now, you just dig through garbage and getting nothing out of it but a grimy feel and a fetid stench of indigence on your hands. I also found out, after selling some clothing here that Their selection here just sucks.\n\nThe only thing that's generally alright is their shoe selection. I got a pretty sweet pair of Nikes for $30.
yelp:test:1072.para:
To be frank, this store has declined significantly from its former glory. Much like other vintage clothing shops, you need to sift through a lot of subpar items to find a gem. Unfortunately, Buffalo Exchange has become a far cry from that. Now, it feels like you're rummaging through trash, leaving you with a sense of disgust and a lingering odor of poverty. Additionally, after selling some items, I realized their inventory is quite disappointing.

The only positive aspect is their shoe selection; I managed to get a nice pair of Nikes for $30.

yelp:test:1073.orig: New year, new clothes, time to update my closet.  A great way to sell some clothes for cash is at Buffalo Exchange.  They give you 33% for the value of the clothes or 50% for in store credit.  The staffs are so friendly.  I just love the store that doesn't smell like something died like other consignment stores.
yelp:test:1073.para: Starting the new year with fresh clothes is a great excuse to refresh my wardrobe. Selling garments for cash at Buffalo Exchange is an excellent option; they offer 33% of the item's value in cash or 50% as store credit. The staff there is incredibly friendly, and I appreciate that the store doesn't have that unpleasant odor like some consignment shops do.

yelp:test:1092.orig: Pretty good subs. The pastrami is to die for.
yelp:test:1092.para: The subtitles are quite good, and the pastrami is absolutely delicious.

yelp:test:1093.orig: Holy cinnamon all up in your face!  Cinna-cones, cinna-brooms, cinna-wreaths,  cinna-scents galore! Everything smells like cinnamon and I hate the smell of cinnamon! I even smelled like cinnamon a day after going into the store.  I burped and guess what it smelled like? CINNAMON! \n\nHappy Holidays
yelp:test:1093.para:
Oh my, the cinnamon was everywhere! From cinna-cones to cinna-brooms and cinna-wreaths, the scent of cinnamon was overwhelming. Despite everything smelling of cinnamon, I absolutely despise the aroma. I even noticed the smell lingering on me a day after visiting the store. And when I burped, it was, of course, cinnamon! 

Merry Christmas!

yelp:test:1104.orig: awesome burgers.  decent service.  good atmosphere.  it's a dive bar.  just fyi.  with good food.
yelp:test:1104.para: excellent burgers. reasonable service. pleasant ambiance. it's a casual bar, just letting you know. still, the food is quite good.

yelp:test:1112.orig: Either they need to hire more baristas or they need to work in faster pace.  I ordered a very simple drink and waited for over 5 minutes for it.  It was also during evening rush hours, but that shouldn't be the reason why my drink took a long time to make.  Not impressed at all.
yelp:test:1112.para: Alternatively, they could either increase their barista staff or operate at a quicker pace. When I ordered a straightforward drink, it took more than 5 minutes to be prepared, even though it was peak evening hours. This shouldn't justify the delay. I am thoroughly unimpressed.

yelp:test:1116.orig: I use to like Ulta. At least, I think I did. I often went to the Ulta at MetroCenter before it closed, and when it did, I had no choice but to start visiting this Ulta. If it were not for the specific makeup I needed I wouldn't bother coming here. The customer service is non-existent. These so-called makeup artists or whatever they are, shouldn't even exist. To this day, not one of them has ever offered to help me when I go to the store. They stare at me when I walk by but continue chattering away to each other, or seek out the one blonde in the store. I walk in, pick up what I need and get the heck out of there. \n\nThe stuff is overpriced. You can get the drugstore brands of makeup for way cheaper anywhere else. The coupon thing is a joke. The points are a waste. Spend hundreds of dollars for a free hair brush?! Are you kidding?!
yelp:test:1116.para:
I used to enjoy shopping at Ulta, but now I'm not so fond of it. Before the MetroCenter location closed, I frequently visited there, and after it shut down, I had no choice but to start going to this other Ulta. I only make the trip if I need a specific makeup item. The customer service is practically nonexistent; those so-called makeup experts should be eliminated. They never offer to assist me when I'm in the store, instead, they just chat among themselves or focus on the blonde employee. I enter, grab what I need, and leave as quickly as possible.

The products are overpriced, and you can find cheaper drugstore brands elsewhere. The coupon system is a joke, and the points are a waste. Spending hundreds of dollars just to get a free hairbrush? Are they serious?!

yelp:test:1123.orig: Very reasonably priced and a higher quality pedicure than I expected.  I will be returning.
yelp:test:1123.para: I found the pedicure to be of better quality than anticipated and at a very reasonable price. I plan to return.

yelp:test:1128.orig:
My wife and I used to love Arriba's, til recently when we joined some friends at the end of their table for dinner. We arrived about an hour after they did, and they were finished when we got there.
 I ordered a stuffed poblano chili dish and it really was not good at all. Bad enough that the food was bad, but when we were ready to leave, we asked the waitress for our check, so she gives us a check for the whole table.
 My wife said, ""No-we want our check only"" and the waitress said that they do not do seperate checks, which is B.S. because we always have gotten seperate checks at the Arriba's in Arrowhead. This created a big hassle for us because we never carry cash, so my wife had to pay back one of her friends for our share of the bill the following week.
 This is no way to conduct a business, and I also sent the main office an email telling them about what had happened, but they never answered the email. I guess customer satisfaction means nothing to them, so we will NEVER go back! 

 Anyplace can roast chilis, so thats nothing special for Arriba's.

 Macayos is the place from now on, and the food there is superior to Arriba's.
yelp:test:1128.para:
My wife and I used to enjoy dining at Arriba's, but our recent experience was disappointing. We arrived about an hour after our friends and found they had already finished their meal.

I ordered a stuffed poblano chili, but it was far from satisfactory. To make matters worse, when we asked for our check, the waitress handed us a bill for the entire table.

My wife protested, saying, "We just want our own check," but the waitress insisted they don't issue separate checks. This was surprising, as we had always received individual checks at the Arrowhead Arriba's. The situation caused us significant inconvenience, as we don't carry cash, and my wife had to reimburse one of her friends for our share of the bill the following week.

This poor service is unacceptable, and I've emailed the main office to express our dissatisfaction, but received no response. It seems customer satisfaction is not a priority for them, so we won't be returning.

Any restaurant can roast chilis, but that's not what sets Arriba's apart. From now on, we'll be dining at Macayos, where the food is superior.

yelp:test:1144.orig: 15 minutes to make an egg salad sandwich with only 4 orders ahead of me? When I open my bag, there is only half a sandwich? WTF? I go back and they acknowledge the mistake and proceed to make a half sandwich with and old piece of bread that was likely left over from lunch 5 hours prior.\n\nThere are too many places in this area to mess up that bad on a simple sandwich order to go back and try it again.
yelp:test:1144.para:
In just 15 minutes, I had 4 orders in front of me, yet I was expecting an egg salad sandwich. Upon checking my bag, I found only half a sandwich? What the heck? They admitted the mistake and made another half sandwich using what seemed to be leftover bread from lunchtime five hours ago.

Given the numerous options nearby, such a poor execution on a basic sandwich order makes me unlikely to give this place another chance.

yelp:test:1162.orig: Only reason I come here is because I get $5 off the total before 9am on Sunday. This recent experience, they forgot to clean the dashboard (dust, dust and more dust) and I almost drove off with the marker of my wash on my windshield?! Those are the two most important parts to clean after a car wash!!!!\n\nIf I didn't need to come here, I wouldn't. Plain and simple.
yelp:test:1162.para:
The sole reason I visit is to save $5 on my total bill before 9am on Sundays. In my recent visit, they neglected to clean the dashboard, which was full of dust, and I nearly left with the wash mark still on my windshield. Cleaning the dashboard and windshield is crucial after a car wash!

If I didn't have to come here, I definitely wouldn't. Straightforwardly put.

yelp:test:1176.orig: Maybe it was the time of day (afternoon) but something was very off today. The cheese plate arrived long after the entrees, my companion's bacon wrapped scallops seemed uncooked and raw.   The chicken schnitzel was fine.   Good beer and wine selection.  Slow service.
yelp:test:1176.para: Perhaps it was the late afternoon, but something seemed amiss today. The cheese plate was delayed, arriving well after the main courses. My friend's bacon-wrapped scallops appeared undercooked and raw. The chicken schnitzel was acceptable, though the service was rather slow. The beer and wine options were decent.

yelp:test:1180.orig:
I went to this store 4/10/2014 and was Daniel took very good care of me upgrading my phone.
I went back 4/12/2014 with my wife to return a item that was defective and upgrade my wife's phone. My wife is handicapped and had to go to the bathroom, they told her to walk over to the McDonalds which is about 100 yards away.

yelp:test:1180.para: On April 10, 2014, Daniel helped me upgrade my phone. Two days later, on April 12, 2014, I returned with my wife to exchange a defective item and upgrade her phone. My wife, who is handicapped, needed to use the bathroom, and the staff directed her to walk to McDonald's, which is about 100 yards away. My wife and I were upset by this.
