yelp:test:7553.para:
I was able to stay for free because my travel buddy's parents had timeshare points to use. While the cost for a group of seven was significantly higher than other options on the strip, we still opted for this suite. 

The suite consisted of a one-bedroom and a studio. Both had balconies with views of the strip, which was a pleasant surprise. 

In the one-bedroom:
- A fully equipped kitchen with all necessary utensils and appliances
- A spacious bathroom with dual sinks and a large bathtub
- A dining area with table and chairs
- A large TV
- A bedroom with a bed and closet
- A sofa bed in the living room
- Accommodated five people
- Additional features: an iPod dock and speakers for in-room parties

In the studio:
- A microwave and coffee maker
- A Murphy bed
- A bathroom with a shower
- A large TV, though not as big as the one in the one-bedroom
- Accommodated two people

This place is more suited for families, and we received some curious glances from other guests in the lobby who were dressed more formally. The staff was very polite, and we didn't encounter any issues.

The pool area was smaller and got quite crowded during our stay, with all the chairs and cabanas taken. However, there were still some spots available.

yelp:test:7555.orig:
We had a 4 day stay here and overall were very happy.
We got a Groupon deal.  The lady at the from desk said Expedia had best prices if you are booking at other times.
The only thing that annoyed me was that our room faced the lane where there was a dumpster that seemed to be getting rubbish in it all hours of night.  I suspect illegal dumping.  Then the dump truck comes around 630/7am.  Too early for me :) Otherwise there was no noise from other guests.  The pool is nice with free cabanas.  The kids water play area was excellent and in shade all day long.  Parking is free.  Kitchen facilities were excellent.  Rooms were clean.  Bring your own dvd's/ cds to play on the stereo and dvd player.  
Curtains blocked light very very well and there was an excellent view of the strip.
I don't think there is any wifi.  We took our own aircards...but I think you can logon to other wifi networks and pay a fee.
There is a very cheap Filipino takeaway in Hawaiian Marketplace. 

Overall, would definitely recommend if you are a family.  If you are young and single, maybe you want something more happening.
yelp:test:7555.para:
Our 4-day stay was quite enjoyable overall. We used a Groupon, and the front desk mentioned that Expedia offers the best rates at other times.

The only thing that bothered me was that our room overlooked a lane with a dumpster that seemed to be receiving trash throughout the night, which I suspect was due to illegal dumping. The dump truck also came around 6:30 to 7 AM, which was too early for my liking. Apart from that, there was no disturbance from other guests. The pool area was nice, with free cabanas available. The kids' play area was fantastic and stayed cool all day. Parking was free, and the kitchen facilities were top-notch. The rooms were clean, and we needed to bring our own DVDs and CDs for the stereo and DVD player. The curtains blocked out light very effectively, and we had a great view of the strip.

I don't think there was any free Wi-Fi, but we brought our own mobile data cards. There is a cheap Filipino takeaway in the Hawaiian Marketplace.

In summary, I would definitely recommend this place for families. If you're young and single, you might prefer a more lively location.

yelp:test:7565.orig: This is \""It's A Small World\"" on crack. Medeval themed, with a cheesy old wizard in the main tower of the castle overlooking the strip. This place ONLY gets credit for being one of the first \""themed\"" hotels in Vegas. This place is pretty old, worn and nasty. The casino, rooms, and restaurants are yuck. With this prime piece of strip property, your would think the Excalibur doesn't have much left in the tank.
yelp:test:7565.para: This place is like an over-the-top version of "It's A Small World," but with a medieval twist, featuring a cheesy old wizard in the main tower of the castle overlooking the strip. While it's recognized as one of the first themed hotels in Vegas, this establishment is quite outdated and in poor condition. The casino, rooms, and restaurants are all rather unpleasant. Given its prime location on the strip, one would expect the Excalibur to still have a lot to offer, but it seems to lack that something extra.

yelp:test:7592.orig: You get what you pay for. Cheap rates, but the service and maintenance of the hotel isn't that great. The walls in Tower I are pretty thin as well. Not sure how Tower II is. Probably not staying here again in the future.
yelp:test:7592.para: The quality matches the price. While the hotel offers low rates, the service and upkeep are lacking. The walls in Tower I are quite thin, and I'm unsure about Tower II. I likely won't be a return guest.

yelp:test:7594.orig: Spend the extra money to stay in a hotel rather then a place that smells horrible from the second you walk in the door. There is no good amenities, rom service is only open breakfast and lunch, to be honest I really have nothing good to say about the place, this is my first time staying here, but I come to Vegas at least once a month for the last 5 years and haven't had a worse experience. PS, there is no wifi
yelp:test:7594.para: I would recommend spending extra to stay in a hotel instead of one that has an unpleasant odor from the moment you enter. The place lacks good amenities, and room service is only available for breakfast and lunch. Honestly, I have very little positive to say about it. This is my first time staying here, but given that I visit Vegas monthly for the past five years, this has been my worst experience. Also, there's no Wi-Fi.

yelp:test:7612.orig: I always get the chicken caesar salad and a good plate of garlic fries.  It is fantastic.  The garlic fries is really amazing!  Ample parking with a good view of the Residence Inn by Marriott.  That hotel is magnificent at night.  GB also has two (or more) event spaces available for booking group gatherings.
yelp:test:7612.para: I consistently order the chicken Caesar salad and a generous portion of garlic fries, which are outstanding. The garlic fries are truly exceptional! There's plenty of parking, and the view of the Residence Inn by Marriott at night is spectacular. Additionally, GB offers two or more event spaces for hosting group events.

yelp:test:7618.orig: So we got to come here for their VIP night last week and being I had never been here before it was a nice surprise. We weren't sure what to expect but you started out in the club room with johnny depp and george clooney, a good start! They served appetizers and drinks, had a DJ and plenty of places to sit.  There was a picture opportunity as well but as with one or two others I wasn't sure with who the figure was supposed to be.  (hence the 4 instead of 5 stars).  As you continue room to room there is a different theme, different appetizers were served based on the theme and drinks to match.  there were about 4 different places to get a professional photo op and we had fun posing as some had props.  Each guest got a picture to take home as well which is a nice momento.  We each also got a Madame Tussauds small bottle of sparkling wine to take with us.  \nThere were plenty of fun moments throughout the night but the 4D superhero movie was probably our favorite part.  Its only 10 minutes but it was quite fun and entertaining.  Thanks to yelp for this opportunity and a night filled with memories that continue to make us laugh.
yelp:test:7618.para: Last week, we attended their VIP night for the first time, and it turned out to be a pleasant surprise. We weren't sure what to expect, but the experience began with a bang, featuring Johnny Depp and George Clooney in the club room. They offered appetizers, drinks, and a DJ, along with ample seating. There was also a photo opportunity, though I wasn't entirely sure who the figures were supposed to represent, which is why it didn't earn a full five-star rating. As we moved from room to room, each had a unique theme, with corresponding appetizers and drinks. There were about four different spots for professional photos, and we enjoyed posing with props. Each guest received a photo to keep and a small bottle of sparkling wine from Madame Tussauds. Throughout the night, there were many enjoyable moments, but our favorite was the 4D superhero movie, which, though only ten minutes long, was highly entertaining. A big thank you to Yelp for this memorable night filled with laughter.

yelp:test:7627.orig: This place is phenomenal! Real, authentic Italian cuisine. The garbage salad is one of their signature dishes. It's an amazing Cesar salad, with hearts of palm, shrimp, avocado, and tomato. It was so delicious! I also had their veal parmesan which was rich and super tasty! This place is an institution in Las Vegas. I highly recommend it!
yelp:test:7627.para: This location is outstanding! They serve genuine Italian food. Their signature dish is the garbage salad, a fantastic Caesar salad featuring hearts of palm, shrimp, avocado, and tomato. It was incredibly delicious! I also tried the veal parmesan, which was very rich and tasty! It's a well-known establishment in Las Vegas, and I strongly recommend it!

yelp:test:7635.orig: Great lunch place ...I had the cup of Matzo Ball soup it was delicious..very hot with lots of celery and carrots....my friend and I shared the corned beef sandwich which also was very good...prices are reasonable. If you come at 1 o clock you beat the lunch crowd.
yelp:test:7635.para: A fantastic spot for lunch! I tried the matzo ball soup, which was superb—very warm and packed with celery and carrots. My companion and I also enjoyed the corned beef sandwich, which was equally delightful. The prices are quite reasonable. If you visit around 1 PM, you can avoid the lunchtime crowd.

yelp:test:7653.orig:
Firefly is simply the best near-strip restaurant.  The only downside: a lot of people now know this, and the relatively small restaurant is now pretty much always packed (and I believe they do not take reservations).  However, the food and service is well worth the wait (or the risk of a wait).

The menu is HUGE and is constantly being changed and added to, and I've yet to try something that I didn't like.  I few suggestions that I enjoy: the bacon wrapped stuffed dates are a must try, along with the ham & cheese croquetas.  The firefly fries are amazing, and big enough to share, as are the calamari.  Other suggestions include the Thai beef salad, the tuna tartar and shrimp ceviche, stuffed pepper, mac n cheese, baked talapia, and the mergeuz.  Don't fill up on the entrees too much, because the tres leches cake is probably the best thing on the menu, so save room for dessert.  

Firefly is also known for its selections of sangria, infused vodkas (vodka + fresh squeezed juices), and mojitos, all of which are great - my favorites are the infused vodka on the rocks, and the passion fruit and blood orange mojitos.  

Go here with a small group and order in small batches, I'd sugg
yelp:test:7653.para:
Firefly stands out as the premier choice for near-strip dining. The only drawback is that it's now quite crowded due to its popularity, and they don't offer reservations. Despite this, the quality of food and service makes it worth the wait or the chance of a wait.

The menu is extensive and frequently updated, with no dish I've tried that I didn't enjoy. Some must-try items include the bacon-wrapped stuffed dates and the ham and cheese croquetas. The firefly fries and calamari are also outstanding and can be shared. Other recommendations are the Thai beef salad, tuna tartar, shrimp ceviche, stuffed pepper, mac and cheese, baked tilapia, and mergeuz. Be sure to leave room for dessert, as the tres leches cake is exceptional.

Firefly is also renowned for its sangria, infused vodkas (vodkas mixed with fresh juices), and mojitos, all of which are excellent. My favorites are the infused vodka on the rocks and the passion fruit and blood orange mojitos.

I recommend visiting with a small group and ordering in smaller batches.

yelp:test:7660.orig:
I type this in my hospital bed so I'm sure you know where I'm going with this. I as ate here 4/23/12 with about 5 other friends from out of town to show off how amazing this place is. And it was another great dining experience.... 

72 hours later or less and I'm in a state of what seems to be nearing death.  And it seemed none of my friends were affected but they were/are. I just happened to get it the worst!! 

I've been a firefly customer for 5 years! Never have I gone through anything like this. I may never come back and never recommend this particular firefly to
Anyone or anyone coming to visit Las Vegas... I'm still in shock this has happened.  Most expensive dining experience ever. Thanks a lot.


*** also this was no food poisoning I got for all you dim witted fools that think otherwise. Salmonella feels like and is (currently) Hell. 



SALMONELLA
yelp:test:7660.para:
I'm writing this from my hospital bed, so you can guess where I am. On April 23, 2012, I and about five friends from out of town dined at this place to highlight how fantastic it is. The experience was outstanding... 

Less than 72 hours later, I'm in a critical condition, while my friends seem fine. I got hit the hardest! 

I've been a loyal Firefly customer for five years, and this is the first time something like this has happened. I might never return, and I won't recommend this Firefly to anyone, especially not to visitors in Las Vegas. I'm still in disbelief that this occurred. It was the most expensive dining experience ever. Thanks a lot.

Also, this wasn't food poisoning; Salmonella is truly miserable. 

SALMONELLA

yelp:test:7675.orig: Negative:  This is one of the older hotels. Stayed in the Mardi Gras tower on the 16th floor. The room was dirty and several things were broken or in need of maintenance. (Hair dryer was broken, drain in shower was clogged, key card reader worked intermittently) Room also needed remodeling.   Cost for Saturday night stay $40- You get what you pay for. Air quality is poor. Casino is very smokey and the air doesn't seem to be filtered. Extra charge for internet access.\n\nPositive: Location is right on the Strip- Almost right in the middle.  Venetian, Mirage, Forum Shops, Treasure Island, etc are all close by. Monorail station is continently located right on site. Free shuttle to Rio, Bally's and Paris. Airport shuttle is $7 per person - Cash Only. Tix4Tonite Box Office is close by in the Casino Royale. Higher tier rooms are of better quality.
yelp:test:7675.para:
Negative: This is an older hotel, and I stayed in the Mardi Gras tower on the 16th floor. The room was in poor condition, with several issues needing attention, such as a broken hair dryer, a clogged shower drain, and an intermittently working key card reader. The room also required significant remodeling. The cost for a Saturday night was $40, and you get what you pay for. The air quality was poor, with the casino being very smoky and the air not seeming to be filtered. There was an extra charge for internet access.

Positive: The hotel's location is ideal, situated right on the Strip, almost in the middle. Nearby attractions include the Venetian, Mirage, Forum Shops, and Treasure Island. The monorail station is conveniently located on-site, and there's a free shuttle to Rio, Bally's, and Paris. The airport shuttle costs $7 per person, cash only. The Tix4Tonite Box Office is nearby in the Casino Royale. Higher-tier rooms offer better quality.

yelp:test:7686.orig:
Friendly service, beautiful contemporary decor and tasty food at a very reasonable price! What more can you ask for?

Keep in mind I generally don't write reviews unless I am really compelled to do so, hence this is only my second review on here.

Before our drive out to Vegas with about 15 friends, we contemplated on where we should eat. As you know, the strip has no shortage of restaurants and to be honest, we always go food hunting in Vegas with two notions in mind, any decent restaurant is pricey and the food is not the greatest. After all, you are in the middle of the desert, right?

A friend highly recommended Spago so we decided to give them a call and make the reservation. Upon arrival, we literally stepped one foot into the restaurant and headed straight to our seats. This wouldn't be a big deal normally but the restaurant was packed and normally you wait forever in Vegas. The table was immaculate and our servers were very quick to ask us what beverages we would like. Alcohol of course, easy on the rocks.

They bring around a bread tray for you to select from four different types of breads, all very soft and flavorful, along with a plate with four spread/dipping op
yelp:test:7686.para:
The restaurant offers excellent service, stunning modern decor, and delicious food at a great price! What else could you want?

I usually don't write reviews unless I have a strong reason, which is why this is my second review here.

Before our trip to Vegas with about 15 friends, we were trying to decide where to eat. As you know, the Las Vegas strip is full of restaurants, and we always expect them to be pricey and the food to be mediocre, given the location in the desert.

A friend recommended Spago, so we called to make a reservation. Upon arrival, we were immediately seated, despite the packed restaurant. Our servers were prompt in offering us drinks, and we opted for alcohol, neat. They also provided a bread tray with four types of soft, flavorful breads, accompanied by a plate of spreads and dips.

yelp:test:7687.orig: The wife and I ate here on our first trip to Las Vegas before we got married. I can still taste the ground pork and ginger pot stickers, drizzled with a soy glaze and thinly sliced scallions.  This is were we both fell in love with sushi, and for  good reasons. It was here where we dared to use chopsticks, and haven't looked back since. Thanks Wolfgang,  it was at your restaurant where are love for dining started together.
yelp:test:7687.para: On our inaugural visit to Las Vegas prior to our marriage, my wife and I dined at this establishment. I recall the flavor of the ground pork and ginger pot stickers, coated in a soy glaze and garnished with finely chopped scallions. It was here that we both developed a fondness for sushi, and for solid reasons. This was the place where we first attempted using chopsticks, and we've continued to do so ever since. Thank you, Wolfgang, as it was at your restaurant where our dining journey together truly began.

yelp:test:7710.orig: 4 of us ate here yesterday and we were very disappointed on their service and their food. The food was very salty and the serving portions were inconsistent.  This place is over priced for the quality of food they serve. I would not recommend this to anyone.
yelp:test:7710.para: Yesterday, our group of four had a disappointing experience with both the service and the food. The dishes were excessively salty, and the portion sizes varied. The prices seemed high given the quality of the food. I wouldn't suggest this place to anyone.

yelp:test:7734.orig: Wouldn't go back to this hotel.  I love dogs and animals just as much as anybody but I don't want dog hairs on the bathroom floor!  The front desk says they charge $100 for people with dogs because they do a special clean up after the pet leaves.  Well they must've missed my room!  It's really an uncomfortable stay when you have to put \""sheets\"" on the sofa and chairs because you don't want someone's pet hair all over you! Residence Inn you should make sure the housekeeper does that \""$100\"" clean up!
yelp:test:7734.para: I wouldn't recommend this hotel again. Despite loving dogs and animals, I found dog hair on the bathroom floor, which was unacceptable. The front desk mentioned a $100 charge for post-pet cleaning, but it seems my room wasn't properly cleaned. This made my stay uncomfortable, as I had to use sheets on the sofa and chairs to avoid pet hair. Residence Inn should ensure the housekeeper performs that thorough clean-up to prevent such issues.

yelp:test:7801.orig: My family and I really enjoyed our first visit to Bahama Breeze. I have been meaning to try it for some time. We went in on a Saturday afternoon and they were not too busy. The food was pretty good, but the best part of the visit was the staff. When we first walked in, one of the servers walked up to my kids who were looking and the fountain and pulled two pennies out of his own pocket for them to throw into the fountain. When we were first sat it took a couple minutes for our waiter to come to the table and two of the other servers (who had just gotten off) noticed and without us having to ask went and found our server. Our server was also very friendly and did a great job. My family and I will definitely be returning to this restaurant in the future.
yelp:test:7801.para: We had a wonderful time on our initial visit to Bahama Breeze, a place I had been eager to explore. We arrived on a Saturday afternoon when the place wasn't overly crowded. The food was satisfactory, but what truly stood out was the service. Upon entering, a server gave my children two pennies to toss into the fountain, a thoughtful gesture. After a brief wait for our server, two other servers who had just finished their shifts noticed and promptly brought our waiter to us. Our server was exceptionally friendly and attentive. My family and I are looking forward to returning to Bahama Breeze soon.

yelp:test:7802.orig: It has been a few years since we have eaten here and were looking forward to our favorite sandwiches for lunch. First let me say, that service here is hit or miss. Sometimes it is fabulous. Other times, horrible. There is no in between. This was a horrible time - waitress would not shut up, did not accept that we did not want alcoholic drinks or appetizers and tried to push them on us, she pulled a menu one of my party was holding and started flipping through it, insisted on telling us the \""specials\"" despite we knew what we wanted.... anyway - we were looking forward to the Grilled Chicken Sandwich and Portabello Mushroom Sandwich. Both were a disappointment - chicken was like rubber, bread tasted bad (not ciabatta anymore). The portabello sandwich was mashed flat as if someone sat on it and the vegetables were diced small and indistinguishable. More so - for a Saturday lunch it was dead... not the normal for this place. Usually it is busy. Looking out the window we got to watch a drunk/high gentleman purusing the parking lot, and then when we left we were confronted by a man who \""wanted to ask us questions\"" and when we refused he started swearing, dropping the f-bomb and b
yelp:test:7802.para:
After a few years away, we were excited to enjoy our go-to sandwiches for lunch. However, the service experience was inconsistent, ranging from excellent to terrible, with no middle ground. This visit was particularly bad; the waitress was incessant, pressuring us to order drinks and appetizers despite our preferences, and even took a menu from one of our party members, flipping through it without our consent. She insisted on describing the "specials" even though we knew exactly what we wanted.

We were particularly looking forward to the Grilled Chicken Sandwich and Portobello Mushroom Sandwich. Both were underwhelming. The chicken was tough and rubbery, and the bread tasted off (it wasn't the ciabatta we remembered). The Portobello sandwich was squished flat, as if it had been squashed, and the vegetables were finely chopped and indistinguishable. Additionally, the place was unusually quiet on a Saturday lunch, unlike its usual bustling atmosphere. We observed a visibly intoxicated individual wandering the parking lot through the window. Upon leaving, we were approached by a man who wanted to ask us questions, but when we declined, he became aggressive, using profanity.

yelp:test:7859.orig:
The MOST beautiful hotel.  Maybe ever.  Staying anywhere else just isn't as fun.

La Bette (yuck!) has been redone as Tryst, and is quite lovely.

Splurge on a cabana.  Don't miss the ""adult pool""... it's hiding on the other side of the casino cabana, if you're lost.  Why every pool in Vegas isn't topless-optional is a complete mystery to me.
yelp:test:7859.para:
This is without a doubt the most beautiful hotel—perhaps the best one out there. Any other place just can't compare.

Tryst, formerly La Bette, has been renovated and turned out to be quite charming.

I highly recommend splurging on a cabana stay. And do not overlook the "adult pool"—it's located on the other side of the casino cabana, and if you get lost, that's where you'll find it. It's truly perplexing why not all pools in Vegas offer a topless-optional option.

yelp:test:7886.orig: Hotel is beautiful and if you want to stay at a place where you will be treated like shit, this is the place for you. I stayed here last year and it took me an hour and a half to check in at what they like to call the VIP check in.  Believing it was an isolated instance, I came back this year. I reserved an $800 suite four months ago and it is now 5:00 pm and the room is still not ready. The staff and manager offer no accommodations or apologies and their attitude is that if I don't like paying for a room that I don't get to use, I should stay somewhere else. I assured them that I would on all future stays.
yelp:test:7886.para: The hotel is stunning, but if you desire to be treated poorly, this is the place for you. Last year, my check-in took over an hour and a half during what they term "VIP check-in." Hoping it was an isolated incident, I returned this year and booked a $800 suite four months ago. It's now 5:00 pm, and my room is still not ready. The staff and manager offer no assistance or apologies, insisting that if I'm not satisfied with paying for a room I can't use, I should find another place. I assured them I would do so for all future stays.

yelp:test:7893.orig:
This place is so huge (outside look is deceiving). Many halls and little rooms. You really need a map to get around or you'd end up in totally wrong event like I did. 

Catching cab is challenging, shuttle train thing is useless unless your destination is near the few stops(yet I can't find the entrance to station often) 

This isn't my fav conventions...
yelp:test:7893.para: This venue is much larger than it appears from the outside, with numerous halls and small rooms. A map is essential to navigate, as I accidentally attended the wrong event when I didn't have one. Getting a cab is difficult, and the shuttle train isn't helpful unless your destination is close to one of the few stops, and even then, I frequently struggle to find the station entrance. This isn't my preferred convention space.

yelp:test:7928.orig:
Everything about this place was just so-so including the service.   Nothing was really bad but nothing stands out.  Had decent lamb vindaloo (asked for extra spicy but not so spicy), chickent tikka masala, malai kofta and a couple different naans- which weren't that great.  

Still looking for a good cheap-eats Indian in Vegas.  This place is a little pricey though not as ridiculously overpriced as Gaylords.

If your craving decent Indian food and not afraid to spend a couple bucks then this place should fit the bill.
yelp:test:7928.para:
The overall experience at this restaurant was mediocre, with average service. While nothing was particularly poor, there wasn't much to commend. The lamb vindaloo was decent, though I requested extra spice and it wasn't as hot as I hoped. The chicken tikka masala, malai kofta, and naan weren't exceptional either. 

I'm still searching for a good, budget-friendly Indian restaurant in Vegas, as this one is a bit pricey, though not as outrageously expensive as Gaylords. 

If you're in the mood for decent Indian food and don't mind spending a little more, this place could be a suitable option.

yelp:test:7930.orig:
My wife and I have tried only the lunch buffet, since they do not serve from the menu during lunch.

Maybe I have been spoiled by the excellent Indian food in and around San Francisco, i.e. Pakwan, Shalimar, and others. At any rate the food at Ghandi is mediocre and overpriced: $11.99 for the lunch buffet, loaded with bland vegetarian dishes and a few chicken-scrap entrees.

Oh, well, I may try another Indian restaurant in Las Vegas, though I may just wait until the next time I'm in San Francisco.
yelp:test:7930.para:
My wife and I have only sampled the lunch buffet, as they don't offer menu items during lunch hours.

While I am accustomed to the high quality of Indian cuisine in San Francisco, such as at Pakwan and Shalimar, the food at Ghandi falls short, being both mediocre and overpriced—$11.99 for a buffet that includes mostly bland vegetarian options and a few chicken scraps.

Perhaps I'll explore other Indian restaurants in Las Vegas, or I might just wait until my next visit to San Francisco.

yelp:test:7949.orig:
In Atlantic City this would be a solid 4 stars, believe it or not. However, compared to what's happening south of the Riviera on The Strip right now, meh.

There are a couple of things to note on the good side- 
the slots are never crowded and neither are the table games
the crowd here is as unpretentious as you can get 
the history of the resort is hard to match- Dino used to be a part owner and Liberace was the headliner here shortly after the doors opened for the first time. Frank Sinatra had one of the rooms in the Monte Carlo Tower remodeled to meet his tastes during one of his runs. There are a few exhibits of the heyday of the Riviera near the Monaco Tower including a great photo of Elvis and Jerry Lee Lewis onstage together.
rooms are cheap
Peppermill is right next door

On the bad side-
it's dated inside...from the way it's decorated to the way it's operated
unless you can appreciate ""Old Vegas"" you won't think you are getting the Vegas experience here

Some new developments are underway nearby which may force the Riv to update and upgrade in order to stay relevant. For now, they are firmly in the 70s & 80s in terms of style and it's not even good enough f
yelp:test:7949.para:
In Atlantic City, this place would easily earn 4 stars, surprisingly. But when compared to what's happening down south on The Strip, it's just so-so.

On the positive side:
- The slots and table games are rarely crowded.
- The crowd is very down-to-earth.
- The resort's history is hard to beat; Dino was once a part-owner, and Liberace was a headliner shortly after opening. Frank Sinatra even had a room in the Monte Carlo Tower remodeled. There are exhibits from the Riviera's heyday, including a great photo of Elvis and Jerry Lee Lewis together.
- Rooms are affordable.
- Peppermill is right next door.

On the negative side:
- It's outdated both in design and operation.
- If you're not into "Old Vegas," you might not feel like you're experiencing the true Vegas vibe here.
- Some new developments nearby might push the Riviera to modernize, but for now, it feels stuck in the 70s and 80s, and even that isn't good enough.

yelp:test:7950.orig:
You know, I don't give a lot of single star ratings. Honestly this is the first time i've wished I could give a no star rating. I've lived in CA for years, and made many many many many trips to Vegas as it's not far away. I've stayed in hotel all up and down the strip, state line and even off strip. 

THIS HOTEL is the WORST I have ran into.

Seriously... what gives? Some of the now gone hotels from just past stateline... that no one really stopped in were nicer than the Riviera. 

I'm guessing that this mighty giant has finally just gotten old and needs to be torn down. I mean, their main attraction is an act I remember from the 80s. They let the room Frank Sanatra sang in rot with nothing happening in it. The hotel itself isn't very clean, and over all it's just a really sad experience. 

I stayed here for over a week for a convention I was attending at the Riviera. I have to say I was not impressed with their convention space either. It was limited, and wasn't a huge fan. 

The only redeeming quality surprisingly enough, was the Buffet on site. It actually was pretty decent.
yelp:test:7950.para:
I rarely give one-star ratings, but this time, I wish there was a way to give a negative one. Having lived in California for years and made numerous trips to Vegas, I've stayed in numerous hotels across the strip and beyond. This particular hotel stands out as the worst I've encountered.

What’s going on here? Some now-defunct hotels just past the state line, which no one really visited, were actually nicer than the Riviera. 

It seems this once-mighty hotel has simply aged and needs to be replaced. Their main attraction is an act from the 80s, and the room where Frank Sinatra used to sing is now dilapidated and unused. The hotel itself isn’t very clean, and overall, it’s a disappointing experience.

I stayed for over a week for a convention at the Riviera, and I wasn’t impressed with their convention space either. It was limited, and I wasn’t a big fan.

The only positive aspect was the on-site buffet, which was surprisingly decent.

yelp:test:7965.orig:
This is the Sephora at the Grand Canal Shoppes at The Venetian.

Ohhh how i LOVE this place!!!! Conveniently located at one of my FAVORITE HOTELS, they have an endless abundance of skincare, cosmetics from all sorts of good quality brand of makeup, men and women designer fragrances, makeup tools and other small makeup accessories.

I try to come here and buy something whenever I come to Vegas. So far, they have never ran out of an item i was looking for. The sale associates are really helpful but at the same time they leave you when you're just browsing or freely shopping around.



-Cynthia-
yelp:test:7965.para:
This is the Sephora at the Grand Canal Shoppes at The Venetian, a location I adore!

Situated at one of my favorite hotels, this store offers an incredible variety of skincare and cosmetics from high-quality brands, along with men's and women's designer fragrances, makeup tools, and other small accessories.

Every time I visit Las Vegas, I make it a point to stop by. So far, they've never run out of anything I've needed. The staff is very helpful, but they also give you space to browse on your own.

-Cynthia-

yelp:test:8010.orig:
I came here with my company~ I fell for their pure pressure when I initially didn't plan to join them after work. Now I'm hooked. :)

It's a prefix menu of 6 courses.. I think. I was quite tipsy ^^  I don't know what each plate consist of but it all taste pretty darn amazing. Each plate is so unique in taste.. like, it's crazy. lol.. never knew taste like that existed! Same time we are being entertained with a gorgeous belly dancer who comes out to dance all around every 30 mins or so. Bonus stars to that. 


I'll be back. Definitely great for groups.
yelp:test:8010.para:
I joined my company for dinner and was surprised by how enjoyable it was, even though I wasn't planning to stay after work. Now I'm really looking forward to going back. :)

The menu offers a selection of 6 courses or so. I was a bit tipsy, so I didn't pay much attention to the specifics of each dish, but everything tasted fantastic. Each plate had a unique flavor that was truly remarkable. It was like nothing I'd experienced before! Additionally, we were entertained by a beautiful belly dancer who performed every 30 minutes or so. That was a real bonus.

I'll definitely be returning. It's perfect for group outings.

yelp:test:8043.orig: We always walked past this restaurant on trips to Vegas and finally decided to make reservations. Reservations were very easy with open table, we didn't even have to call. The staff was courteous, however, they did not mention their team approach to serving nor did they mention what makes their dried NY steak different from the typical NY steak. \n\nThe food was delicious. My boyfriend got the dried NY steak and I had the filet mignon. For $45 a steak, you can't go wrong with Gallager's. we also ordered a side of saut\u00e9ed beans and the potato pur\u00e9e. This was more than enough food for us and left no room for dessert.
yelp:test:8043.para:
On our Vegas trips, we frequently passed this restaurant and eventually decided to make a reservation. The process was straightforward; we didn't even need to call. The staff was polite, but they didn't highlight their team-based service approach or explain the unique aspects of their dried NY steak compared to a regular one. 

The food was outstanding. My boyfriend ordered the dried NY steak, while I had the filet mignon. At $45 per steak, it was a great value at Gallagher's. We also ordered sautéed beans and potato purée, which were more than sufficient and left no room for dessert.

yelp:test:8060.orig: The hotel has been re-done and it looks great.  The room was clean and the staff was friendly.  The pool is clean and they also have a fitness room.  They have tea and coffee downstairs and coffee in the room.
yelp:test:8060.para: The hotel has undergone renovations and now appears fantastic. The room was spotlessly clean, and the staff were very welcoming. There's a clean pool and a fitness center available. They provide tea and coffee in the lobby, as well as coffee in the room.

yelp:test:8182.orig: If i could give a - star for them i would have , BAD FOOD BAD SERVICE AND BAD ATTITUDE well that just explains we went for Dinner of 7/2 and 8/18 i'm still pissed at them for the way the reacted , Variety of Sushi is a joke , i don't know how they have managed to stay in business being a LOCAL i definitely don't recommend this place
yelp:test:8182.para: If I could rate them lower, I would. The food, service, and attitude were all poor. This frustration stems from our dining experiences on 7/2 and 8/18, where we were clearly mistreated. The sushi selection is laughable, and I can't understand how they manage to stay open as a local establishment. I definitely wouldn't recommend this place.

yelp:test:8193.orig: As a Chicagoan who grew up eating at Lawry's the Vegas location does not disappoint! The service is 1st class, the food is absolutely delicious! The room has an old supper club elegance. The organization that I enjoy hosts their regular luncheons at Lawry's and I couldn't be happier!
yelp:test:8193.para: As a native Chicagoan with fond memories of dining at Lawry's in Vegas, I find the experience just as delightful. The service is top-notch, and the food is simply outstanding! The ambiance exudes a classic supper club charm. Since my organization frequently holds luncheons there, I am consistently pleased with the experience!

yelp:test:8205.orig: Horrible place!!!  Went on a Tuesday night about 12:00am.  Stayed for about an hour.  My bros and I dropped $170 and didn't see one topless girl.  Place was empty. Nasty girls sat in our lap, argued about price and left pissed off that we wouldn't pay $400 for a lap dance.  One guy in my party gave each of them a $20 for their time.  They were still pissed.  No one danced on stage.  Place sucked big time...don't waste your time!
yelp:test:8205.para: What a terrible experience! We visited around 12:00am on a Tuesday night and stayed for about an hour. My friends and I spent $170 but didn't see a single topless dancer. The place was nearly empty, and the girls who sat in our laps were unpleasant. They argued over the price and got angry when we refused to pay $400 for a lap dance. One of my friends gave each of them $20, but they were still upset. There were no performances on stage either. This place was really disappointing—definitely don't bother going!

yelp:test:8215.orig:
I hate to be the one of unpopular opinion here, but my overall experience here wasn't that great. 

Drinks were decent, amuse bouche of asparagus mousse was pretty good, and the souffles were fabulous as described.

However, neither of our entrees were good. My husband got the vegetarian crepes (the only vegetarian item on the menu) and found them pleasing at first, but overpowering after a few bites. I tasted it, too - it's like whoever created it didn't actually try to sit down and eat a whole one.

For me, the lobster was so tough and stringy that I had a difficult time cutting it with a knife. No delicious dessert can make up for that sort of problem. 

Oh, I forgot, we ordered sides as well. The potato croquettes were pretty good as long as they were piping hot. Once the temperature went more toward warm, you could taste the grease, which to me is not ideal.

I'm happy to pay a premium for a great meal/service/ambience, but I expected much better from this place, especially in Vegas where competition is stiff.
yelp:test:8215.para:
I don't want to be the one to say this, but my experience wasn't fantastic overall. The drinks were alright, and the asparagus mousse was quite good. The soufflés were excellent, as expected.

However, both of our main courses were disappointing. My husband had the only vegetarian crepe on the menu and found it initially enjoyable, but it became too strong after a few bites. I tried it too, and it seemed like the chef hadn't tasted it before making it.

For me, the lobster was extremely tough and stringy, making it hard to cut. No dessert could have fixed that issue. 

We also ordered side dishes. The potato croquettes were good when they were very hot, but once they cooled down, the grease became noticeable, which wasn't ideal.

I'm willing to pay extra for a top-notch meal, service, or ambiance, but I had higher expectations for this place, especially in Las Vegas where the competition is fierce.

yelp:test:8218.orig: High end restaurant with outstanding service.  We celebrated our anniversary there and were greeted by the manager.  As I was removing my jacket, he quickly assisted me on placing it on my chair.  \n\nOur waiter, Joshua was perfect!  He appeared at the right time to replenish our drinks, rolls and checked in periodically but not overbearing.  We had the Thanksgiving tasting which we enjoyed.  Turkey a little bland for my taste but the sides were excellent (red cabbage, au gratin potatoes).  The chef surprised us with a couple of \""extras\""...cold celery soup and multiple desserts.  All excellent.  A beautiful location with a great view of the Bellagio Fountains and the strip.  A great evening.
yelp:test:8218.para:
We marked our anniversary at an upscale restaurant with exceptional service. The manager welcomed us and promptly helped me hang my jacket on my chair as I removed it.

Our waiter, Joshua, was impeccable. He arrived just when we needed him to refill our drinks, serve rolls, and check in without being intrusive. We savored the Thanksgiving tasting menu. The turkey was a bit bland, but the side dishes were outstanding (red cabbage, au gratin potatoes). The chef also surprised us with a couple of extra treats: a cold celery soup and several desserts, all of which were delightful. The setting was stunning, offering a beautiful view of the Bellagio Fountains and the strip. It was a wonderful evening.

yelp:test:8229.orig: After posting my review I was contacted and reimbursed for the dinner portion of our visit.
yelp:test:8229.para: Following my review, I was reached out to and given a refund for the meal we enjoyed during our visit.

yelp:test:8235.orig: At one time Spanish Trail was extremely beautiful, had spectacular up to date facilities, and served incredible food. It was classy and special. Things have changed. Certain times of the year Spanish Trail can be pretty, but they're slow to replace anything dead or overgrown. Facilities aren't up to date and don't get renovated as often they should. Things that do get renovated are usually things that don't need to be renovated. The food is mediocre at best and overpriced. Just because you enjoyed something this week, it doesn't mean it will be good the next time you order it. Anything really goes on the golf course, tennis courts and fitness center. I've seen dogs using the fairway as a bathroom, kids riding their bikes all over the course, and etc. If you want some classy, special or some incredible experience, then Spanish Trail probably isn't what you're looking for, but if you just want to play somewhere different then Spanish Trail is ok.
yelp:test:8235.para: Spanish Trail once boasted stunning beauty, cutting-edge amenities, and delicious cuisine, making it a standout destination. However, things have shifted. While it can still be picturesque at certain times of the year, there's a lack of maintenance for dead or overgrown areas. The facilities are outdated and rarely renovated, and when renovations do occur, they often focus on unnecessary updates. The food quality is at best mediocre and tends to be overpriced. Just because you enjoyed your experience this week doesn't guarantee it will be the same next time. The golf course, tennis courts, and fitness center are often marred by various issues, such as dogs using the fairway as a restroom and children riding their bikes across the course. If you're seeking a truly special or incredible experience, Spanish Trail might not meet your expectations. However, if you're looking for a change of scenery, it could be a suitable option.

yelp:test:8240.orig: The speedway is fun.  Parking was pretty easy to get in and out of and the racing I got to see last year was a lot of fun.  We sat in some luxury boxes and were served free food and drinks (including beer if that's what you wanted).  I ate until I was full and had a great view of the action.  I do not have any comment on prices of food and beverage because mine was all free since I got some free VIP tickets through my work.
yelp:test:8240.para: The race track was enjoyable. Parking was convenient, allowing for easy entry and exit. Last year, I had a great time watching the races. We were seated in luxury boxes where we were treated to complimentary food, drinks, and even beer if that was preferred. I ate until I was satisfied and had an excellent view of the action. I didn't comment on the cost of food and beverages since everything was free, as I received VIP tickets through my workplace.

yelp:test:8311.orig:
I dislike Mimi's Cafe.  I always have.  I decided that, after a few years of avoidance that they would improve.  I was dead wrong.  Mimi's is still meh.  I had breakfast there with my mother while my father was in surgery down the street.  I ordered croissants, which were delicious, but the actual meal of potatoes, bacon, and eggs was horrid.  It was chewy bacon with bland eggs and oily potatoes. 

Ew.

Sorry, but I dislike Mimi's for many reasons, all of which relate to their food and sad service.
yelp:test:8311.para: I've never liked Mimi's Cafe, and my opinion hasn't changed over the years. I thought they might have improved after avoiding them for a few years, but I was mistaken. Mimi's remains unimpressive. I had breakfast there with my mother while my father was undergoing surgery nearby. The croissants were delightful, but the main meal of potatoes, bacon, and eggs was disappointing. The bacon was chewy and the eggs and potatoes were bland and greasy. Yuck. Overall, I dislike Mimi's due to their subpar food and poor service.

yelp:test:8327.orig: For how excited I was to try this place out, I left disappointed. I would say this is more of a \""date; or lets get to know each other VERY VERY VERY well\"" type of spot. My girls and I decided to do dinner there before we go clubbing one night. Dinner reservations were set at seven giving us more than enough time to eat and go for drink after.. For starters we got seated at about a half an hour after seven, the service took ages for each courses to come out, and the course sizes were a complete disappointment leaving more than half of hungry. Dessert was the best part of the meal, but for 18 dollars for what you get, it was not worth it. And biggest surprise of all was how they divided the bill amongst us. Some of the girls decided to get separate courses and share, and when the bill arrived they automatically charged per individual rather than per item like stated on the menu. Long story short we all left paying $60+ for a meal that left us hungry and disappointed. And what made it even worse is that we did not leave the restaurant till 10:30pm!!! That is how tediously slow the service was : (
yelp:test:8327.para: Despite my high expectations, I left feeling let down. This place seems more suited for a romantic or deep connection setting rather than a casual dinner out. My friends and I planned to have dinner there before heading to a club. We made reservations for 7 PM, giving us plenty of time to dine and then party. However, we were seated around 30 minutes late, and the service was excruciatingly slow, with each course taking a long time to arrive. The portions were also disappointingly small, leaving us still hungry. The dessert was the highlight, but at $18, it wasn't worth the cost. The biggest shock was the billing. Some of us ordered separate courses to share, but the bill was split per person, contrary to what was stated on the menu. In the end, we all paid over $60 for a meal that left us unsatisfied and hungry. The slow service extended our stay until 10:30 PM, making the experience even more frustrating.

yelp:test:8330.orig: Finding a good groomer is like trying to find a good mechanic or hair stylist its really hard! I saw this place numerous times since its across the street from my house so I decided to pop in. When I walked in I was not greeted and had to wait for the owner to get off the phone which was obviously a personal call. So I wait and browse. Finally about 10 mins later she asked if I needed help. I wanted to know how much an all over shave for my medium lenghth border collie lab mix would be. $110 bucks! Seriously? Seemed pretty steep. So I thank her and decide to buy some goodies for my chihuahua. When the owner asked what kind of dog I had while ordering the cookies she felt it was nessacary to ask why I would feed a chihuahua gourmet treats!! How is that any of her buisness??
yelp:test:8330.para: Selecting a reliable groomer is as challenging as finding a good mechanic or hair stylist. I frequently noticed this place due to its proximity to my home, so I decided to stop by. Upon entering, I wasn't greeted and had to wait for the owner to finish a personal call. After about 10 minutes, she inquired if I needed assistance. I asked about the cost of an all-over shave for my medium-length border collie lab mix, which was $110. That seemed quite expensive. I thanked her and proceeded to buy treats for my chihuahua. When the owner asked about the type of dog I had while I was ordering, she inquired why I was feeding a chihuahua gourmet treats. Why is that her concern?

yelp:test:8399.orig: Last time I was there was for new years. It's a nice dive bar. They sometimes have a live band.
yelp:test:8399.para: My previous visit was for New Year's Eve. It's a pleasant small bar, and they occasionally feature live music.

yelp:test:8408.orig: Good course and you are playing here for the novelty of playing on the strip. Friendly staff, no range is not a knock because there is no space to hit balls on a highway. Holes are very close to one another, again, due to space constraints. Long par 4 s are essentially the same as the short par 5s. I played a good 3-4 holes that I had to double check I had not played them before and was out of sequence on the course. Par 3s are the most memorable, island green 16 is no more than a PW. Enjoyable round and agree with prior review, book with golf now for savings.
yelp:test:8408.para: This is a great course, especially for those who enjoy the novelty of playing on a strip. The staff is very friendly, and while there isn't much space for long drives, that's not a criticism since there's no room to hit balls on a highway. The holes are quite close together, which is understandable given the space limitations. Many of the long par 4s feel similar to short par 5s. I played a few holes that I had to double-check to ensure I hadn't already played them, and they were out of sequence. The par 3s stand out the most; the island green 16 is just a pitch and wedge shot. Overall, it was an enjoyable round, and I concur with previous reviews. If you want to save, book your game with Golf Now.

yelp:test:8437.orig:
Quality of food and service was excellent.  We didn't have a reservation but the manager was very accommodating. Service was second to none.

We had the trio of fish which was like something off master chef. We also had the trout which was really well cooked, full of flavor. Desert was amazing. We had the pineapple turnover and the chocolate fondant. Presentation of all the food was beautiful.

We had a really good night and the price was also reasonable for the quality.
yelp:test:8437.para:
The food and service were outstanding. Although we didn't have a reservation, the manager was very accommodating. The service was top-notch.

We enjoyed the fish trio, which was exquisite, akin to a Master Chef creation. The trout was perfectly cooked, packed with flavor. For dessert, we had the pineapple turnover and chocolate fondant, both of which were exceptional. The presentation of all the dishes was stunning.

We had a wonderful evening, and the prices were reasonable given the quality.

yelp:test:8445.orig: this had got to be the worst sushi i have ever had..it was only mysel,f so i sit at the sushi bar.i decide to get the ayce..so the sushi dude(can't really call him a chef)just keeps making dishes for me without me ordering.i was just going to pace myself,but whatever,i figure he knows what is good..well i don't think there is  anything very good there.the only thing i actually ordered was the unagi and the dynamite.the unagi tasted like it was pre made..oh yeah, i also ordered a half  roll with unagi,cucumber and avocado which was ok.the sushi dude made me what is called a no name(half roll),which was probably the best out of everything i had.while i'm working on the dynamite and the no name,he hands me the seafood salad.(says it is really popular)well the texture of the fish was like it had been thawed and frozen, and then thawed again.yuck...i decided i was full(i couldn't stomach anymore)..the sushi guy tried to let me pay ala cart (which was nice of him once again)but the lady said that i ordered what would be more than if i ordered ala cart,even though the portions were made small for me(that's what the sushi guy said anyways).i was too tired too argue and i didnt want the sus
yelp:test:8445.para: This was undoubtedly the poorest sushi experience I've ever had. I was alone, so I sat at the sushi bar. I opted for the all-you-can-eat option, and the sushi guy, more of a preparer than a chef, kept bringing me dishes without my orders. I intended to pace myself, but I figured he knew best. Unfortunately, I didn't find much that was good. The only items I ordered were the unagi and the dynamite. The unagi tasted like it was pre-made. I also got a half roll with unagi, cucumber, and avocado, which was acceptable. The sushi guy made me a no-name roll, which turned out to be the best of everything I had. While I was eating the dynamite and the no-name roll, he handed me the seafood salad, saying it was very popular. The fish in the salad had a texture as if it had been thawed and refrozen, which was unpleasant. I decided I was full and couldn't stomach any more. The sushi guy offered to let me pay à la carte, which was kind of him, but the lady insisted that I had ordered more than if I had paid à la carte, even though the portions were small. I was too tired to argue and didn't want to cause any trouble.

yelp:test:8448.orig: Brief: Great fresh sushi, usually a wait, No Name roll!\n\nOne of my favorite sushi places in Vegas. YUM! There's such a variety and for those who don't like the extra sauces and papers there are more plain rolls that are just as tasty and fresh. If there's anything worth mentioning is about Yama is that the fish is always fresh!
yelp:test:8448.para:
Brief: Delicious fresh sushi, often a wait, especially for the No Name roll!

One of my go-to sushi spots in Vegas—absolutely delicious! They offer a wide range of options, and for those who prefer simpler fare, there are plenty of plain rolls that are just as delightful and fresh. What really stands out at Yama is the consistently fresh fish they use.

yelp:test:8457.orig: The best Sushi Restaurant I've been to yet all the way around. The staff, quality of food and service are top notch! I've tried many different All-You-Can-Eat Sushi Bars and so far I have not been able to find another that's remotely comparable!
yelp:test:8457.para: I've found the absolute best Sushi Restaurant overall, with outstanding staff, food quality, and service. Among all the All-You-Can-Eat Sushi Bars I've visited, I haven't come across one that even comes close in comparison!

yelp:test:8463.orig:
This was my first visit to this location and I can see why it is a favorite with Vegas locals for breakfast.  The place was packed and the smells of the food being cooked was terrific.  Definitely a mouth watering experience while waiting to be seated. 

The server was very friendly and kept our glasses filled with our drinks.  I ordered biscuits and gravy with a side of bacon.  The biscuits were two of the biggest biscuits that I have seen (at home or at a restaurant), yet they were light, fluffy and very tasty.  In the end, I couldn't both of them, they were so big.  As a personal preference, I do wish the gravy was a little thicker, but that didn't detract from the taste at all.  The bacon was cooked just right, a little crispy but still juicy and not over cooked at all. 

Everyone at the table agreed that their meals were very good, no complaints about the food. The seats could have been a little more comfortable and the bathrooms needed more attention, but that shouldn't dissuade anyone from enjoying a very good meal at Blueberry Hill. 

I'll come back for more on my next trip to Vegas.
yelp:test:8463.para:
My first visit to this spot confirmed why it's a go-to for locals in Vegas, especially for breakfast. The place was bustling, and the aroma of cooking food was incredible, making the wait for a table almost enjoyable. 

The server was exceptionally friendly and kept our drinks topped up. I had biscuits and gravy with bacon on the side. The biscuits were the largest I've ever seen, yet they were light, fluffy, and delicious. They were so big that I couldn't finish them all. While I preferred a thicker gravy, it didn't affect the overall taste. The bacon was perfectly cooked—crispy on the outside but still juicy and not overdone.

Everyone at the table agreed that our meals were excellent, with no complaints about the food. The seating could have been more comfortable, and the restrooms needed some attention, but these minor issues shouldn't deter anyone from having a great meal at Blueberry Hill. 

I look forward to returning on my next trip to Vegas.

yelp:test:8535.orig: This place has an identity problem. The should not pretend to be a \""vintage\"" clothing store because they are not. Their idea of vintage is a one year old pair of True Religion jeans. I brought in some really cool actual vintage 1960's and 1970's coats and a beautiful old wool suit to sell them  The twelve year old behind the counter looked at them for about 30 seconds and said \""no thanks\"". I asked her if she knew of any \""vintage\"" clothing stores in the area, not getting the dig she said, \"" I think there are some downtown on Main st.\"".  I happened to spot another place further south on Maryland pkwy called Mustang Xchange at 4800 s. Maryland pkwy.  I brought my items in and the girl there informed me the owners were not in but she looked at my items an told me the owner would definitely be interested in them and asked me to bring them back in. Buffalo Exchange needs to eliminate the \""vintage\"" in their description and get a location in the mall because thats really where they want to be. Stop pretending to be something you are not. If you want to see a cool little place go to Mustang Xchange instead.
yelp:test:8535.para: This store struggles with its identity. It shouldn't claim to be a "vintage" clothing shop since it isn't. Their definition of vintage seems to be a pair of one-year-old True Religion jeans. I brought in some genuinely vintage 1960s and 1970s coats and an old wool suit to sell. The teenager behind the counter glanced at them for about 30 seconds and said "no thanks." When I inquired if she knew of any "vintage" stores nearby, she suggested some downtown on Main Street. I noticed another place called Mustang Xchange further south on Maryland Parkway. When I brought my items there, the employee told me the owners were out but assured me they would be interested and asked me to return with them. Buffalo Exchange should remove "vintage" from its description and consider a mall location, as that's where they seem to belong. Stop pretending to be something you're not. For a truly vintage experience, visit Mustang Xchange instead.

yelp:test:8573.orig: I landed in vegas late on a Thursday night and found the line from hell at the Thrifty rental counter.  I had two birthdays waiting to be served.  I would rather pay more money and go somewhere else than stand in a line as long as I did.  Honestly, it took and hour and twenty minutes to helped.
yelp:test:8573.para: Upon arriving in Las Vegas late Thursday night, I encountered an extremely long line at the Thrifty rental desk. I had two birthdays that needed attention. I'd prefer to spend extra money and find another location rather than wait in such a lengthy line, which took over an hour and twenty minutes to be assisted.

yelp:test:8583.orig:
One of my favorite Mexican Food Restaurant's.  

Just don't sit at the rail and get the cigarette smoke from passerby's.

Fajitas rock.  Service is great and I love the salsa bar.
yelp:test:8583.para:
One of my favorite Mexican restaurants, but avoid sitting by the rail where you might inhale cigarette smoke from people walking by.

The fajitas are outstanding, and I really enjoy the salsa bar service.

yelp:test:8590.orig: Outstanding!!!  Great food and lots of it.  Now, the place isn't the prettiest place on earth, but the food is great, the service excellent, the price is great, and i'll go back anytime.  The B & G are great and huge!
yelp:test:8590.para: Absolutely fantastic! The food is delicious and plentiful. While the ambiance isn't the most visually appealing, the cuisine is top-notch, the service is superb, and the prices are very reasonable. I look forward to returning anytime. The B & G dishes are both amazing and generously sized!

yelp:test:8591.orig:
The anticipation for this party was greater than any other party.  However, so was the disappointment.  On a 94 degree day in Las Vegas, the AC broke and it was 98 degrees inside of the doll house for the duration of the party.  Although it was not their fault that the AC broke, I feel that it was a major health code violation to have those little girls sweltering inside for two hours.  If not for the extreme disappointment of 10 four year olds, I would have herded them all to McDonald's for ice-cream.  

A week prior to the party, I had confirmation that they would not serve peanut butter as my child has a severe peanut allergy.  Unfortunately they served it and my child was in danger of going into anaphalactic shock on her birthday.  

I was discounted 25 dollars off of an almost 400 dollar bill for the inconvenience and they told me that they would give me half off on my other daughter's birthday when she turns 3.  She will be turning three in August of 2010.  

I truly feel that it was the most uncompfortable birthday party that I have ever been to and I have been to countless birthday parties.  I would not have been as inclined to write this review if they would have rei
yelp:test:8591.para:
The excitement for this party surpassed any other, yet the disappointment was equally profound. On a sweltering 94-degree day in Las Vegas, the air conditioning failed, making the dollhouse a stifling 98 degrees for the entire duration of the celebration. While I understand it wasn't their fault, I believe it was a significant health hazard to keep those little girls in such heat for two hours. Had it not been for the extreme letdown of 10 four-year-olds, I would have taken them to McDonald's for ice cream instead.

A week before the party, I was assured that no peanut butter would be served, as my child has a severe peanut allergy. Unfortunately, they served it, putting my child at risk of anaphylactic shock on her birthday.

They offered a 25-dollar discount on an almost 400-dollar bill for the inconvenience and promised to give me half off on my other daughter's birthday when she turns 3, which will be in August 2010.

I found this to be the most uncomfortable birthday party I've ever attended, and I've been to many. I likely wouldn't have written this review if they had rectified the situation.

yelp:test:8595.orig: I have always been a fan of Radio Shack. Ever since my dad had his own store in the early 80's here in Las Vegas. He would send my sister Linda and I electronic gadgets that we could use in Germany. I still have my radio, tape recorder, speakers and a couple of other items and they still work!! \n\nThe Radio Shack we frequent is by Sams Club on East Tropicana. The most important thing for me is that the staff is knowledgeable and informed because I usually have questions. Every time I have been in this store I have had great customer service, the store is well maintained and the staff actually like being there which says a lot for standard operating procedures being followed and pride in what you do. Kudos to Ron, Leslie and Dee. You heard me!
yelp:test:8595.para:
I've long been a devoted fan of Radio Shack, dating back to when my father ran his store in Las Vegas during the early 80s. He would send my sister Linda and me electronic gadgets to use in Germany. To this day, I still have my radio, tape recorder, speakers, and a few other items, and they all still function perfectly!

The Radio Shack we visit is located near Sams Club on East Tropicana. What I value most is the knowledgeable and informed staff, as I often have questions. Each time I've been to this store, I've received excellent customer service, and the place is well-maintained. It's clear that the staff takes pride in their work, which speaks volumes about the store's adherence to standard operating procedures. A big thumbs up to Ron, Leslie, and Dee—heard it straight from me!

yelp:test:8610.orig: They took me on a walk in. Great pricing, super friendly staff, and my girl did a nice job. Got a fill and gel polish with hearts for valentines day for $33. Can't complain about that!
yelp:test:8610.para: I went for a walk-in appointment, which was fantastic. The prices were great, the staff was incredibly friendly, and my technician did a wonderful job. I got a fill and gel polish with heart designs for Valentine's Day, all for $33. I'm really happy with that!

yelp:test:8667.orig:
Every time I go to visit my job site I plan lunch with my girlfriend here. We have been visiting this place since 2007. It is a great find for lunch and dinner. I believe it is some of the best Mexican food in town. 

Lunch can get crowded so we usually get in around 1130 and are seated right away. Get the guac!! It is a little extra but totally worth it. I have never had bad service here and they are very attentive and the food comes out pretty fast. Not fast like microwave, but within a good amount of time for the amount of people they have sitting in there. 

I usually get shredded beef tacos or enchiladas and the love the rice. Everything is just so yummy. Oh yah and the horchata, YUM! I had bad Mexican just days before I came last Friday so I definitely needed the right stuff!
yelp:test:8667.para:
Since 2007, I've been making it a habit to have lunch with my girlfriend at this spot whenever I visit my workplace. It's become a favorite for both lunch and dinner, and I think it serves some of the best Mexican cuisine in town.

We typically arrive around 11:30 and are promptly seated. I highly recommend getting the guacamole—it's a bit extra, but it's well worth it. The service is always top-notch; they're attentive and the food comes out quickly, though not rushed. 

My usual choices are shredded beef tacos or enchiladas, and I particularly enjoy the rice. Everything is just delicious. And let's not forget the horchata—it's absolutely delightful! After tasting some poor Mexican food just a few days prior, I was thrilled to find this place.

yelp:test:8673.orig: AWESOME place to have mexican in Las Vegas.  Situated between the Strip and Fremont St., this huge restaurant is one of my favorite places to eat in Vegas.   I love their margaritas, the streak is always tasty, I love their bean dip and chips and sauces and salsa. The staff is attentive and patient(i come with my 95 year old uncle)  Really great place to eat!  Plenty of handicap an street parking.
yelp:test:8673.para: A fantastic spot for Mexican cuisine in Las Vegas, located between the Strip and Fremont Street, this expansive restaurant is one of my top choices for dining in the city. I particularly enjoy their margaritas, and the steak is consistently delicious. I also adore their bean dip, chips, and the various sauces and salsas. The staff is very attentive and patient, especially when I visit with my 95-year-old uncle. It's a really great place to eat! There's ample handicap and street parking available.

yelp:test:8677.orig: The worst restaurant I ever went to! \nTHE want to be called managers is the worst customer service you can ever have.\nIt makes you want to close the restaurants!! F rating!!!!
yelp:test:8677.para: I've had the worst experience at a restaurant I've ever been to! The so-called managers provided the poorest customer service imaginable. It's so bad that it makes me want to see this restaurant shut down! It deserves an absolute F rating!!!

yelp:test:8682.orig: I have been taking my 2 dogs here over 2 years. My dogs go for checkups and vaccines. I always call in advance and there is no to little wait Everybody is always  very kind and friendly. The price is just right they don't try to rip you off. I highly recommend it for everyone.
yelp:test:8682.para: For more than two years, I've been bringing my two dogs to this place for checkups and vaccinations. I always make a call beforehand, and there's hardly any wait. The staff is consistently very kind and friendly. The prices are fair, and they never try to overcharge. I strongly recommend it to everyone.

yelp:test:8684.orig:
Ask me a year ago to rate this place and I would give it 4 stars. But presently it's just a disappointing place. 

It's located on windmill and las vegas blvd, connected to a gas station. Interior is pretty small, you're better off ordering to go and eating at home. Sometimes the place gets really smelly.

Just your usual fast food place, order at the window and wait for them to call out your number. If you do a walk in on a tuesday you're going to end up waiting 45 minutes for some chicken -___-.  Waiting for your food is a game here, sometimes it comes out immediately and sometimes you wait forever.

As for the taste you don't come here because it's the best chicken in the world. You come here because its average and its cheap. Nothing much to say.
 
What annoys me are their prices! :( They keep raising them wtf! The sauces use to be free now they charge you for it. Also their $.50 tuesday special is no longer $.50 it's like $.80 or something. IT'S CALLED TUESDAY SPECIAL FOR A REASON.


PRO TIP! Go through the drive-thru when ordering much much more faster.
yelp:test:8684.para:
A year ago, I would have rated this place 4 stars, but now it's quite disappointing. It's situated on Windmill and Las Vegas Boulevard, right next to a gas station. The interior is quite small, and I recommend ordering to go and eating at home instead. Sometimes, the place can get really smelly.

It's just a typical fast-food joint where you order at the window and wait for your number to be called. On a Tuesday, you might have to wait up to 45 minutes for your chicken. Waiting for your food is part of the experience here—sometimes it's quick, and sometimes it's a long wait.

The food isn't exceptional, but it's average and affordable. There's not much to say about it. What really frustrates me are the rising prices. They keep going up, and it's ridiculous! The sauces used to be free, but now they charge for them. The supposed $.50 Tuesday special is now closer to $.80. It's called a "Tuesday special" for a reason.

PRO TIP: Ordering through the drive-thru is much faster.

yelp:test:8687.orig:
I only have 3 VERY important things to say:

1. Super cheap for interior and exterior cleaning.
2. Staff are pretty friendly.
3. Guys are kinda hot..........in an ex-convict kinda way!

yelp:test:8687.para:
Here are three key points I want to share:

yelp:test:8694.orig:
After hearing that the sushi chef from Sushi Mon on Sahara had moved here we had to check it out.  I do enjoy their fried oysters and dynamite.  However, the quality of the fish is just so-so.  Maybe I'm spoiled by the high quality of fish I've been eating at my new regular spot, Naked Fish http://www.yelp.com/biz/naked-fishs-sushi-and-grill-las-vegas

However about halfway into our meal, we were shocked when we saw them clean the inside of the glass sushi display case with a big blue bottle of windex.  Yes, the case with all the fish in it.  

We walked out.  That is wrong.  Won't be going back.
yelp:test:8694.para:
Upon learning that the sushi chef from Sushi Mon on Sahara had relocated, we decided to give the new place a try. I do appreciate their fried oysters and dynamite rolls, but the freshness of the fish leaves something to be desired. Perhaps my expectations are higher after experiencing the superior quality of fish at my new favorite spot, Naked Fish. 

Midway through our meal, we were stunned to witness them cleaning the glass sushi display case with a large bottle of Windex. Yes, the case that held all the fish. 

We left immediately. This is unacceptable, and we won't be returning.

yelp:test:8737.orig:

yelp:test:8737.para:
THE WORST PLACE TO LIVE IN VEGAS. EVER. AVOID IT.

Last year around this time, my roommate and I were in a rush to find a place, so we settled for this one. The initial price was reasonable, it was close to UNLV and our jobs, and there were nearby grocery stores. We should have taken more time to look for a better option.
