yelp:test:8756.orig: Had the shredded beef bowl. AWESOME! Perfect rice, well seasoned pintos, tender and lean beef all with a citrus-cilantro-mint sauce to tie it together. Chicken soup would cure the worst of colds!!!
yelp:test:8756.para: Enjoyed a delicious shredded beef bowl. It was fantastic! The rice was perfectly cooked and nicely seasoned, the pinto beans were flavorful and tender, and the beef was both tender and lean. All these elements were beautifully complemented by a zesty citrus-cilantro-mint sauce. A bowl of this chicken soup would surely alleviate even the most severe cold!

yelp:test:8780.orig: Meh is about right. This store is basically the same as the Smith's just up the street, only with higher prices and not as much selection. I come from California where everything is a ripoff ... and the prices here are just as bad if not worse. I don't remember it always being that way, but that's the way it is now. \n\nOh well. It's not like there aren't a ton of other grocery stores within a 90-second drive.
yelp:test:8780.para:
Pretty much sums it up. This store is essentially identical to Smith's just down the road, but with pricier items and less variety. Coming from California, where everything feels overpriced, I find the prices here equally, if not more, exorbitant. I can't recall it being this way before, but that's the situation now. 

No big deal though. There are plenty of other grocery stores within a short drive.

yelp:test:8858.orig: I tried this place out because it's close to where I live. Gel manicures I've gotten at other salons always last for 2 1/2 to 3 weeks. My first gel manicure I got here started peeling after 10 days, so I returned to get a polish change and gave them another shot. AGAIN, my nails started peeling this time only after 8 days!! The staff isn't very friendly either. Go elsewhere!
yelp:test:8858.para: I visited this salon due to its proximity to my home. At other salons, gel manicures typically last 2 1/2 to 3 weeks, but my first one here began peeling after just 10 days. I returned for a polish change and gave them another chance, but the nails started peeling again after only 8 days! The staff is also not very welcoming. It's best to go somewhere else.

yelp:test:8931.orig: Amazing. Delicious. I eat way too much of it! They have Shiner Bock on tap, which is another plus. Yes, it's a wait, so go with a group of friends and order some pitchers while you wait. Or get take-out or delivery if you don't have time to be social. But don't miss the goodness.
yelp:test:8931.para: Absolutely fantastic and incredibly tasty! I find myself wanting to eat more than I should. They serve Shiner Bock on tap, which is a definite bonus. There is a wait, so consider bringing a group and ordering several pitchers to enjoy while you're there. Alternatively, you can opt for take-out or delivery if you prefer to eat without the wait. Just make sure not to miss out on this delightful experience.

yelp:test:8935.orig:
I really like a good sandwich. There's just something divine about the combination of good bread, quality meat, fresh toppings, and well-chosen condiments all put together in a user-friendly package. Regrettably, Jimmy John doesn't provide that.

Start with the bread-- plain white bread with zero flavor and no character. No whole wheat option (for at least a dollar more, you can get seven grain bread for some, not all, of the sandwiches), no flatbread or wraps. This is allegedly gourmet?! Then there's the filling. Somewhere buried under the bland bread, mound of industrially shredded lettuce, and pale cardboard-tasteless tomato there's a slice or two of meat that is hard to notice. Condiment choice is narrow, and the application thereof is extremely variably, sometimes drowned in it and sometimes featuring the merest swipe. Hot sandwich choices simply don't exist. You crave a hot roast beef or hot ham with melted gruyere? Too bad. These sandwiches are a step below even national chains like Subway, where they at least provide more choices and flavor profiles, from fillings to condiments to toppings, and yes, hot sandwiches!

I suppose I understand why inexperienced, budget-consc
yelp:test:8935.para:
I genuinely enjoy a delicious sandwich. The perfect sandwich combines flavorful bread, high-quality meat, fresh toppings, and well-applied condiments in a convenient format. Unfortunately, Jimmy John's fails to deliver on this front.

Starting with the bread, it's plain white with no taste or character, and no whole wheat option is available. For an extra dollar, you can get seven-grain bread, but it's not always an option. This is supposed to be gourmet? Moving on to the filling, beneath the tasteless bread, industrial lettuce, and flavorless tomato, there's a meager amount of meat that's hard to detect. Condiment options are limited, and their application is inconsistent—sometimes there's too much, and other times, there's barely any. Hot sandwich options are non-existent. You want a hot roast beef or ham with melted Gruyère? Too bad. Jimmy John's sandwiches fall short even compared to national chains like Subway, which offer more variety and flavor profiles in terms of fillings, condiments, and toppings, including hot options!

yelp:test:8938.orig:
I will say that I do go here, though very sporadically. I gave it two stars, but it's because of my tastes, which I will explain in detail.

When I do go, it's always early in the evening. I don't like going to this bar when it's crowded, as it's excessively crowded. It's worth a trip if you're into the scene or are visiting Phoenix and want to experience the scene. This is definitely one of the Valley's landmark bars. If you're going alone and don't mind spending the evening by yourself (i.e. people-watching) it really isn't that bad. If you want to mingle with people, this bar isn't a great atmosphere for that. People generally go in cliques and you'll notice that the bar is full of clique-clusters. It definitely is not one of the friendlier bars in the Valley. It also seems to have an ""instant snob"" effect on people. 

Now, for pluses... Amsterdam does have a beautiful outdoor area, which is suitable for smokers. You can not only take your drinks out there, but there is an outdoor bar at which you can get drinks. It's a nice area to have drinks in the spring, fall and early/late summer. Most of the summer it can still top 100 degrees even late at night and winter nights
yelp:test:8938.para:
I do visit this place occasionally, but quite irregularly. I rated it two stars, but that's based on my personal preferences, which I'll elaborate on.

I usually go there early in the evening. I avoid it when it's busy, as it gets overcrowded. It's a good spot if you're into the scene or visiting Phoenix and want to experience it firsthand. This bar is definitely a landmark in the Valley. If you're alone and enjoy people-watching, it's not too bad. However, if you're looking to socialize, this isn't the best atmosphere. People tend to hang out in groups, and the bar is filled with these clusters. It's definitely not one of the more friendly bars in the Valley. It also gives off an "instant snob" vibe to some people.

On the positive side, Amsterdam has a beautiful outdoor area that's great for smokers. You can enjoy your drinks outside, and there's even an outdoor bar where you can get them. It's a pleasant spot to have drinks in the spring, fall, and early or late summer. Most of the summer, it can still be over 100 degrees even late at night, and it's chilly in the winter evenings.

yelp:test:8960.orig: The best!  I haven't been there in years and the last time we went it was a 3.5 hour wait but so worth it!  Great for a date if you want to get to know someone waiting in line so long.  \nMy advice is to arrive at 330pm so that way you can be one of the first in line and eat with the first seating at 5pm.
yelp:test:8960.para:
Absolutely fantastic! I haven't visited in a while, and the previous time, we faced a 3.5-hour wait, but it was totally worth it. It's perfect for a date if you want to get to know someone while you're both waiting in line. 

My recommendation is to get there by 3:30 PM to be among the first in line and secure a spot for the 5 PM seating.

yelp:test:8967.orig: This place is completely and overwhelmingly overhyped. The pizza was tasteless and probably one of my least favorite I've ever had. Grazie and Grimaldi's are by far greater and underrated. Pizza Bianco had dust that should warrant the attention of the health department. If I could I would give this place 4 thumbs down. Overrated!!!!
yelp:test:8967.para: This location is excessively hyped and doesn't live up to the expectations. The pizza was flavorless and among my least enjoyable. Grazie and Grimaldi's are clearly superior and underappreciated. Pizza Bianco had such poor hygiene that it should concern health officials. If possible, I'd rate it with four thumbs down. Overrated!!!!

yelp:test:8974.orig:
Had heard about Durants for years and finally went last night.  This review is not kind so if you are a fan, you should go to other reviews.

Positives:  
Atmosphere
Old school decor (straight out of the 60's)
Courteous wait staff

Negatives:
Horribly over priced-  I've had a better Ribeye at Houston's and it didn't cost $48.

Steak quality was not what I expected.  Ribeye is a well marbled steak, but these had a lot of gristle, were not nearly the quality I'd expect for the 5 star price.

5 Guys and Red Robin make much better fries....seriously, I have shoe laces that are firmer.

One person in my party complained about the lack of steak quality and had a plateful of gristle and fat on his plate.

My verdict.... I was anticipating a steak dinner that was top notch.  It was far from that.  Perhaps they just had a poor quality slab to cut the steaks from, but at $50 a steak, someone in the kitchen should gave caught it.  Plenty of other great places in Phoenix to eat a marvelous steak....and I prefer those after this dinner.
yelp:test:8974.para:
I've been hearing about Durants for a long time and finally visited last night. This review isn't positive, so if you're a fan, you might want to check out other reviews.

Pros:
- Atmosphere
- Vintage decor (right out of the 60s)
- Polite servers

Cons:
- Extremely overpriced—my Ribeye at Houston's was better and only cost $48.
- The steak quality was disappointing. The Ribeye was supposed to be well-marbled, but it had a lot of gristle and didn't meet the high expectations for a $50 steak.
- The fries from 5 Guys and Red Robin are much better; mine were as firm as shoelaces.
- One person in my group had a plate full of gristle and fat, indicating poor quality.

In conclusion, I was expecting a top-notch steak dinner, but it fell short. Maybe the steak was of poor quality, but at that price, it should have been caught. There are plenty of other great steak options in Phoenix, and I prefer those after this experience.

yelp:test:8975.orig:
As a part of the Steak Out, our most recent visit was to this Valley favorite. 

For sure: KILLER shrimp cocktail. Although there were only 4 pieces, they give new meaning to the phrase Jumbo Shrimp and, despite their size, they were not tough or iodine-y. The flavor was fresh and the cocktail sauce could clear the very worst sinuses!

The roasted garlic mashed potatoes must use REAL roasted garlic -- like, roasted in house, not just minced garlic tossed in! The sweet, earthy flavor was subtle which was perfect, because it didn't destroy your palate for the rest of the plate.

I was surprised by the wine list: not a huge. very accessible, relatively speaking.

But, we're on a quest for the best steak. This one? It gets very high marks!  Excellent seasoning on the meat. Preparation in terms of temperature was adequate (although, it was more on the medium rare side; I would argue that is the side to err on!).
yelp:test:8975.para:
During our Steak Out event, we recently dined at a local favorite in Valley. 

Firstly, the shrimp cocktail was outstanding—just four pieces, but they truly embody the term "jumbo." Despite their size, they were tender and not overly salty. The flavor was fresh, and the sauce was so potent it could clear a stuffy nose!

The roasted garlic mashed potatoes were exceptional; they must have used fresh, in-house roasted garlic. The flavor was sweet and earthy, just right—not overpowering, allowing other flavors to shine.

The wine list was a pleasant surprise, offering a good selection that was easy to navigate.

Most importantly, the steak received high praise. The seasoning was excellent, and the temperature was just right, leaning slightly towards medium rare, which I believe is the ideal choice.

yelp:test:8980.orig: Just went to the Friday night game vs Cubs.  We tried a new section-Friday's Front Row inside the restaurant in the outfield.  I was impressed.  We sat in the front row pretty much over the left outfield and you could see in the bullpen also which was kind of cool.  There is a waitress for the section and she did a great job.  Tickets were $20 per which I thought was nice.  You can also get served alcohol throughout the whole game if you are the kind of person that gets anxiety about the whole last call thing in the 7th.
yelp:test:8980.para: Last Friday, I attended a game against the Cubs in a new section called Friday's Front Row, located inside the restaurant in the outfield. I was quite impressed with the setup. We were seated near the front, almost directly over the left outfield, and even got a view of the bullpen, which was pretty neat. Each table in this section has its own waitress, and she did an excellent job. The ticket price was $20 per person, which I found to be reasonable. Additionally, you can order alcohol throughout the game, which is a nice option if you're worried about the last call in the seventh inning.

yelp:test:9029.orig:
I went to Lux for brunch with some friends and the food was pretty good. First off, the line was REALLY long, which is both good and bad. Bad, for obvious reasons, but good because it tells you that they are popular, which would usually hint at the quality of the food you will eventually consume. 

Second, they are kind enough to get drink orders while you wait in line so that you can start having your coffee, tea, juice, or whatnot, while you wait for your food. Third, the decor of Lux was cool enough to distract me while my friends and I waited for our breakfast to be prepared. Lots of retro-looking lamps on the tables combined with art from local artists made for a warm and welcoming atmosphere. 

When our food did arrive, we were all satisfied! I got the Aunt Gladys's homemade salsa over four strips of tender belly bacon, three scrambled eggs, white cheddar, and hash, which was pretty delicious. My two friends also really enjoyed their meals. I'm giving them 4 stars because I did think that their food was a bit over-priced for what you got, both in portion size and quality. I mean, it was $5 for a glass of orange juice... Other than that, I was very satisfied with the exper
yelp:test:9029.para:
I recently visited Lux for brunch with friends, and the food was quite satisfactory. The line was notably long, which, while inconvenient, suggests popularity and likely good food quality. 

Secondly, they offered drink orders during the wait, allowing us to enjoy our beverages while we waited for our meals. The decor at Lux was appealing, with retro-style lamps and local art creating a cozy and inviting ambiance. 

Our food arrived and we were all pleased. I had the Aunt Gladys's homemade salsa with bacon, eggs, and cheese, which was delicious. My friends also enjoyed their dishes. I rated it 4 stars, though I felt the prices were a bit high for the portion size and quality. For instance, a glass of orange juice cost $5. Overall, I was very content with the experience.

yelp:test:9057.orig:
This is a humble eatery, a pleasant surprise in the midst of a sordid neighborhood. The restaurant is choc-a-bloc on a weekend evening. So it is best to arrive around 7 pm, not later than that.

As indicated on their menu they start preparing the food only after the order is placed leading to a considerably long wait (45 mins to one hour). However, during the waiting period their customers have quite a few occupations like looking at the paraphernalia on the walls, sipping margaritas, devouring the crunchy tacos, listening to the loud Spanish music or looking at what other people are eating. 

Whatever their clients choose to do, there comes a time when the waiter places the hot plate on the table, they pick up the fork, take a mouthful and then there is calm in the din of Los Dos Molinos. In fact there is a near- Nirvana experience with every bite of the carnitas or enchiladas. 

At the end the brusque manner of the waiting staff is forgotten, so is the long wait and restlessness.
yelp:test:9057.para:
This quaint eatery stands out as a delightful find in an otherwise gritty neighborhood. It's bustling with activity on weekends, so it's advisable to arrive by 7 pm. 

Their menu clearly states that they start cooking only after an order is placed, which can result in a wait of about 45 minutes to an hour. During this time, patrons can engage in various activities such as admiring the wall decorations, enjoying margaritas, munching on crispy tacos, listening to the lively Spanish music, or simply observing what others are ordering.

Regardless of what they choose to do, the moment the waiter places the steaming plate on the table, everyone quiets down. Each bite of the carnitas or enchiladas offers a near-Nirvana experience. By the end, the initial impatience and the abrupt service style are long forgotten.

yelp:test:9058.orig: Always a great place, we visit Los Dos 1-2x everytime we are in Phoenix yearly. This time we gave the Mesa location a go, opposed to the original. Food and service were great as usual, however the food didnt seem as spicy as at the original Los Dos and the ambiance is not the same...has more of the standard restuarant look and feel. Not a knock at all...still amazing food regardless!!!
yelp:test:9058.para: We always enjoy visiting Los Dos, and we make it a point to go 1-2 times whenever we're in Phoenix. This time, we decided to try the Mesa location instead of the original one. The food and service were excellent, as usual. However, the food didn't seem as spicy as at the original Los Dos, and the atmosphere wasn't quite the same—it had a more typical restaurant vibe. But that's not a criticism at all; the food is still amazing!

yelp:test:9064.para: To start, we weren't offered any water all night long!!!! The food was okay, but they served appetizers with spilled sauce. The sushi was decent, earning it two stars. The cod was overly salty, but the fish itself was alright.

yelp:test:9068.orig: This was one of my early favorites when I first started living here two years ago.  I love their chips and hot sauce.  Some of the best in Phoenix.  Last two visits really missed the boat.  This last time the service was so bad that I had to chase my waiter down just to get my order delivered correctly.\n\nFood is pretty good.  Love the Baja Burro.  But, two less than great service experiences--I won't be back.
yelp:test:9068.para:
When I first moved here two years ago, this place was one of my top choices. I particularly enjoy their chips and hot sauce; they're among the best in Phoenix. Unfortunately, my last two visits were disappointing. The most recent one was particularly bad—my waiter had to be tracked down to get my order right.

The food is decent, and I really like the Baja Burro. However, with two poor service experiences, I won't be returning.

yelp:test:9077.orig:
Went here last night and the night started ok. There were only 3 other people in the place and we had the worst service ever. No drink refills or help! The mangaer/owner she didn't show any care when i talked to her and i will never eat here again. Also you could hardly get into the rest rooms because of the clutter of tables and chairs.

Food was ok but nothing to write home about or worth the price they were charging. No wonder they rely on coupons to get people in to their place.

also becareful with their happy hour specials as i asked for a $2.00 special and she brought me out a large draft and then charged me more saying i didn't ask for a bottled beer.

Horrible management and tactics! BEWARE!!!
yelp:test:9077.para:
Last night, the experience began well with just three other patrons in the establishment. However, the service was the worst I've ever encountered; there were no drink refills, and no assistance at all. When I spoke to the manager/owner, there was no indication of concern. I won't be returning. Additionally, the restrooms were difficult to access due to the clutter of tables and chairs.

The food was acceptable but not memorable or worth the price. It's no surprise they depend on coupons to attract customers.

Be cautious with their happy hour specials; I requested a $2.00 special, but was given a large draft and charged extra, as I didn't ask for a bottled beer.

Terrible management and tactics! BEWARE!!!

yelp:test:9080.orig:
Creepy.

Barbie dolls servicing men of all shapes and sizes from drunk losers to drunk high rollers in an incredibly dark, smelly warehouse. I couldn't tell if these ""girls"" were actually girls.

And we almost got tangled in a hate crime. A drunk jerk of unlimited stupidity thought a couple of guys in our group were gay and wanted to bash their heads in. We all left immediately before he could call in his KKK/Nazis brothers to help.

I hate strip clubs.
yelp:test:9080.para:
Disturbing.

Men of various types, from intoxicated underachievers to drunk high-rollers, were being serviced by Barbie-like dolls in a grimy, odor-filled warehouse. I wasn't sure if the "dancers" were actually women.

We narrowly avoided a hate crime when a foolish drunkard, brimming with ill-conceived notions, believed a few men in our group were gay and tried to attack them. We fled quickly to prevent him from summoning his KKK/Nazi allies.

I detest strip clubs.

yelp:test:9101.orig: If you like staying at the slums and love horrible customer service, I would recommend this place.  Talk about a waste of money. \n\nFrom the time that you call and reserve your hotel, the phone CSRs sound like they don't want to be at their job......Seriously.  They sound unmotivated.  Their attitude is \""\""next..\""
yelp:test:9101.para:
If you enjoy being in slum areas and appreciate poor customer service, I highly recommend this hotel. It's truly a waste of money. 

From the moment you call to reserve your room, the customer service representatives seem disengaged and uninterested. Their tone suggests they just want to move on to the next call.

yelp:test:9107.orig: The service is ok, but the food was worth it.  I like the fact that the food is not over priced like in most Vegas eateries.  The wine list is absolutely one of a kind, especially if you like German Reislings!\n\nI would come back, our food was excellent, looking forward to the next trip!
yelp:test:9107.para: The service is satisfactory, yet the food was well worth the cost. I appreciate that the menu items aren't overly priced, unlike many other restaurants in Vegas. The wine selection, particularly the German Reislings, is truly unique. I plan to return, as our dining experience was outstanding, and I'm excited for our next visit!

yelp:test:9111.orig:
Tired of overpriced hotel foods, long buffet lines, hassle of finding great places to eat...well look no further. The best Thai restaurant in Las Vegas is at Lotus of Siam and it's only a 7 min drive from the strip off Sahara. Best make reservations if you have parties of 4 or more since this place always has a wait.

Here are a few musts from the menu:

1) Thai iced tea
2) Garlic Prawns (they fry them season them and still keep the skin on...must have)
3) Duck curry (spicy levels from 1-10, we had the 8 and it was pretty spicy...so stick with 5-6 for those who just want a medium kick)

Staff's very attentive and supposedly they have a great wine selection, but I have yet to try anything. I always make a pit stop anytime I come back to Las Vegas...I found a gold mine.
yelp:test:9111.para:
Fed up with expensive hotel dining options and the hassle of long lines and searching for good eateries? Look no further. Lotus of Siam, the top Thai restaurant in Las Vegas, is just a 7-minute drive from the strip off Sahara Avenue. It's wise to make reservations, especially if you're in a group of four or more, as this place often has a wait.

Here are some must-try dishes from the menu:

1. Thai iced tea
2. Garlic Prawns (they're fried, seasoned, and kept with the skin on—don't miss out)
3. Duck curry (spicy levels range from 1 to 10; we opted for 8, which was quite spicy—go for 5-6 if you prefer a milder kick)

The staff is very attentive, and they claim to have an excellent wine selection, though I haven't tried it yet. I always make a point to stop by whenever I return to Las Vegas; I've hit the jackpot.

yelp:test:9119.orig: The best Thai food I had in long time.  I started with Sa-Tay of chicken.  Very good pickle vegetables and a delicious peanut sauce.  I enjoy it immensely.  My girlfriend had the Tom Yum Kai.  She really enjoyed the soup.  I was lucky and got to try it before she ate it up.  I agree, the soup was great.\nI had the drunken seafood noodles with spice level of 7.  It was spicy but satisfying.  The food was delicious and the spicy sauce was incredible.  We came pretty late but service was still very good.  Definitely, will be back again.
yelp:test:9119.para:
I recently enjoyed some outstanding Thai cuisine, the best in a while. I began with the chicken Sa-Tay, paired with excellent pickled vegetables and a tasty peanut sauce. I thoroughly enjoyed it. My girlfriend opted for the Tom Yum Kai, which she found very satisfying. I got to taste it before she finished her bowl, and I concur that the soup was fantastic.

For my main course, I chose the drunken seafood noodles with a spice level of 7. It was quite spicy but incredibly satisfying. The dish was delicious, and the spicy sauce was exceptional. Despite arriving late, the service remained excellent. I definitely plan to return.

yelp:test:9134.orig:
Review of Buffet:

UGH!  It was very very underwhelming. 

Maybe regular menu is great, but do not get the buffet IMHO.  About half the restaurant was eating the buffet... unfortunately I was in the idiot half of the crowd.
yelp:test:9134.para:
Review of the Buffet:

Oh no! It was extremely disappointing. 
While the regular menu might be fantastic, I don't think the buffet is worth it, in my opinion. Only about half the restaurant was enjoying the buffet, and unfortunately, I was one of that half.

yelp:test:9171.orig: I always stop by this place when I stay at the MGM. Especially for lunch. Everything on the menu is usually really great. The service is always on point and one time Emeril was there walking around signing autographs and stuff. Thats Vegas for you.
yelp:test:9171.para: Whenever I'm lodging at the MGM, I make it a point to visit this spot, particularly for lunch. The food is consistently excellent across the menu. The service is always top-notch, and there was even a time when Emeril was there, signing autographs. That's what Vegas is all about.

yelp:test:9197.orig: We bypassed the wait by grabbing seats at the bar.  Great beer selection, we went with a pitcher of fat tire which was new to us East Coasters.  Delicious burgers, huge and juicy.  We also had the deep fried pickles which were surprisingly tasty.  Overall it was a great place to sit, grab a burger and relax.
yelp:test:9197.para: We skipped the line by finding seats at the bar. They offered an impressive variety of beers, and we opted for a pitcher of Fat Tire, a new choice for us from the East Coast. The burgers were fantastic, large and incredibly juicy. We also tried the deep-fried pickles, which exceeded our expectations. In all, it was an excellent spot to sit, enjoy a burger, and unwind.

yelp:test:9208.orig:
Had dinner at the burger bar before heading to a show. There wasn't any wait on a Saturday at 7. Server did a great job greeting and taking out order.  

Loved the wide selection and choose stellar on draft. Ordered a ceasar salad which was a good sized portion to share. Ordered the custom made burger- angus beef, jack pepper cheese, with jalapeño. The burger was cooked to a perfectly to medium. Favorable and juicy. The true test that the burger stayed together when you hold with you're hands while eating it. 

Totally recommend to eat here. 

Tota
yelp:test:9208.para:
Dined at the burger bar before going to a show. There was no wait on a Saturday at 7 PM. The server was excellent, greeting us and taking our order promptly. 

We enjoyed the extensive menu and opted for the standout draft beer. We shared a Caesar salad, which was a generous portion. For the main course, we ordered a custom burger with Angus beef, jack pepper cheese, and jalapeño. The burger was cooked to a perfect medium, juicy and flavorful. It held together well when we held it, which is a testament to its quality.

I highly recommend eating here.

yelp:test:9234.orig:
Mesa Grill was extremely overpriced and the service was annoying. I understand it's Vegas, but for the prices, I expected better, quieter service. Our waiter came up every five minutes trying to take our plates, pouring water in between us and our conversations, asking questions... I understand being diligent but this was annoying. 

The pork loin was the best thing any of us got. It was definitely very good. So was the shrimp tamale. I think that's actually the best thing on the menu, but quite rich so you can split that and the pork with someone and be totally satisfied as the portions are huge.

One of us had the coffee crusted steak, and the rub was just too spicy to really enjoy the meat. The fish was bland and slightly overcooked. Desserts were awful. Seriously, how hard is it to make good churros? The donuts at a fast food restaurant are better!

If you are a fan of Bobby Flay's other restaurants -- Bar Americain is one of my favorites -- you will be very disappointed here. The quality, service and atmosphere are just so mediocre it really disappoints. Oh, and the price - I think it's more expensive than eating in his restaurant in Manhattan, which is just mind-bogglin
yelp:test:9234.para:
Mesa Grill was quite pricey and the service was quite disruptive. While I get that it's in Vegas, for the cost, I expected a more serene dining experience. Our server kept hovering, clearing our plates frequently, interrupting our conversations to offer water and ask questions. While I appreciate attentiveness, this was more of a nuisance.

The pork loin was the standout dish, truly delicious. The shrimp tamale was also excellent, perhaps the best on the menu, though quite rich and best shared. The portions are generous, so splitting it with someone would be ideal.

One person tried the coffee-crusted steak, but the spice from the rub was overpowering, making it hard to savor the meat. The fish was underwhelming, bland and slightly overcooked. The desserts were a letdown; churros were particularly disappointing, and even fast-food donuts tasted better.

If you're a fan of Bobby Flay's other establishments, like Bar Americain, you'll likely be disappointed here. The quality, service, and ambiance are subpar, and the prices are steep—more so than at his Manhattan restaurant, which is already quite pricey.

yelp:test:9293.orig: I know that this is an institution but it really isn't worth the price. I think if I were drunk at 3:00am though, then I would be writing otherwise.\n\nDon't bother unless you're drunk. Go for the hot dog.
yelp:test:9293.para: I understand this is a well-established place, but it's not worth the cost. If I were tipsy at 3 AM, my opinion might differ. So, unless you're in that state, I wouldn't recommend it. The hot dog is definitely worth trying.

yelp:test:9306.orig: Wanted to see why the reviews are so high for this place.  I have to say it was an experience to try at least once while visiting Pittsburgh.  We sat at the counter and that was a fun to eat there.  We shared a Pastrami sandwich and I thought the meat portions were small, mostly cold slaw and fries in your sandwich.  The pastrami was average and I would have liked more of that then the other items.  It was a big sandwich and enough for us.  We didn't have to order any fries, but we forgot it was in the sandwich.  The fries could be crisper and I thought they were tasty, but too soft for me.\n\nOverall, I say go there once to experience it.  There's not a lot of attention from the staff, bc the place is so busy.  I don't need to go back.   If you miss getting a chance to eat there.....then catch it the next time you visit, not a must to visit.
yelp:test:9306.para:
I wanted to understand why this place has such positive reviews, and my visit certainly lived up to the hype—it's definitely worth trying at least once when you're in Pittsburgh. We sat at the counter, which added to the charm of the experience. We shared a Pastrami sandwich, and while the portion of meat was average, I felt there was more slaw and fries than pastrami. The sandwich was substantial enough for both of us, and we didn't need to order extra fries since they were included. However, I wished the fries were crispier, though they were still quite tasty. 

Overall, I recommend visiting once to experience it, but the service can be a bit lacking due to the busy atmosphere. I don't plan on returning, and if you miss out, don't worry too much; it's not a must-visit spot.

yelp:test:9310.orig:
Monday night.  Called our order in ...picked up 15 mins later.  Walked in to pick up and place wasnt packed.  

I ordered a fish sandwich.  NOT good at all!  The fish barely covers the bread!!!  They piled on the fries and slaw.  But hardly any fish!  

Next was my SMALL STREET FRIES.  For over $4.00 I EXPECT REAL BACON..NOT IMMATATION BACON BITS!!! OMG!  I had to feed these fries to my dog!  FRICKEN GROSS!!!!!  Along with the great big pieces of pinto beans.  :(  This is horrible.  I was so looking forward to this food!  

Thanks for letting me down!
yelp:test:9310.para:
On Monday night, we placed our order and were picked up just 15 minutes later. When we arrived, the place wasn't very busy.

I ordered a fish sandwich, but it was far from satisfying. The fish was so minimal that it barely covered the bread! They loaded up on fries and coleslaw, but there was hardly any fish at all.

My street fries were also disappointingly small, costing over $4.00. I expected real bacon, not imitation bacon bits! These fries were so bad, I had to give them to my dog. They were absolutely revolting! And the large pieces of pinto beans didn't help. This meal was terrible. I was really looking forward to enjoying this food! 

Thanks for letting me down!

yelp:test:9334.orig: I love this place.  The employees are awesome and the coffee is so good.  I love the blueberry muffin too.  All of them are so nice and there are plenty of places to sit and chill.  It is easy access if on foot or bike so that's a plus too.
yelp:test:9334.para: This is a place I adore. The staff are fantastic, and the coffee is outstanding. I also really enjoy the blueberry muffin. Everyone is so friendly, and there are numerous spots to relax and unwind. It's conveniently accessible on foot or by bike, which is a bonus.

yelp:test:9354.orig: I had the California Burger. It was good but not excellent, and certainly not the best burger in Madison. I went with three other people and they agreed. We should have went to Five Guys.
yelp:test:9354.para: The California Burger I tried was decent but didn't stand out as exceptional or the top choice in Madison. My companions concurred. We probably should have opted for Five Guys instead.

yelp:test:9357.orig: Good jambalaya and ok chili (the cheese is a slice just plopped on top) and cornbread... Great beer... But that's all I could eat. I have a severe fish allergy and it was that or a few of their salads (nothing with any meat though). Very disappointing that they hadn't thought about cross contamination with allergies. I'll go back for the soup and definitely the beer but it'll only be with friends... Not by myself. And only if other people suggest it. Very disappointing.
yelp:test:9357.para: The jambalaya and ok chili (with cheese simply placed on top) and cornbread were good, along with the great beer... But that's all I managed to eat. I had a severe fish allergy, so it was either this or a few of their salads, which didn't contain any meat. It's quite disappointing that they didn't consider cross-contamination for allergies. I'll return for the soup and the beer, but only with friends... Not alone. And only if others recommend it. Overall, it was very disappointing.

yelp:test:9394.orig: I've used this hotel for years through work and have always had a positive experience.  Free WiFi, great front desk staff, big rooms and easy access to the great city of Madison. \n  I tend to be very hard on hotels but this one always leaves me satisfied.
yelp:test:9394.para: For years, I've stayed at this hotel on business, and each time, the experience has been positive. The free WiFi is reliable, the front desk staff are helpful, and the rooms are spacious. It's also conveniently located in Madison. Despite being usually critical of hotels, this one consistently meets my expectations and leaves me satisfied.

yelp:test:9400.orig: I always go for the scrambler,milk shakes, and coffee for Sunday brunch.  Really cozy diner which is unique to Madison.
yelp:test:9400.para: On Sundays, I prefer the scrambler, milkshakes, and coffee at this particularly cozy diner that stands out in Madison.

yelp:test:9411.orig:
When I first moved to Madison I was really excited to come to this restaurant because the man had hyped it up as a great Thai eatery.  When I finally visited the restaurant it definitely did not live up to the hype.

On the plus side the place is really nice and is a great place for dates and groups as it is very large.  However the food, as this is a restaurant, should also be great and unfortunately it was not.  I ordered a red curry dish which sounded great but was disappointed at first bite.  It's not that it was bad because it certainly wasn't but it just wasn't great.  There seemed to be something missing that I was not able to put my finger on.  The man ordered the pad Thai which he actually loved.  I didn't try any of it so I don't have anything to say about it.

As far as the presentation of the food however that was spot on.  I would recommend this place to anyone trying to venture out and try something different as the flavors are not in your face.  Also the staff was great and very attentive.
yelp:test:9411.para:
When I first moved to Madison, I was eager to visit this Thai restaurant after hearing how great it was from a friend. However, my experience didn't match the praise I had received.

On the positive side, the restaurant is very pleasant and suitable for romantic dinners or groups, thanks to its spacious layout. Yet, the food, which is the main draw of any restaurant, fell short of expectations. I ordered a red curry dish that seemed promising, but it wasn't as impressive as I had hoped. It wasn't bad, but it lacked something intangible. My companion enjoyed the pad Thai, but I didn't try it, so I can't comment on it.

Regarding the food presentation, it was excellent. I would suggest this place to those looking to explore new flavors, as the taste is subtle and not overpowering. Additionally, the service was top-notch and the staff was very attentive.

yelp:test:9422.orig:
These hacks couldn't make a cocktail if their lives depended on it.  They're arrogant and can't back it up.

The mojito was disgusting, with sad overworked mint.

The Sazerac was an abomination.  They shook it resulting in an over diluted drink, then added a squeeze of a lemon wedge instead of a twist of lemon peel.
yelp:test:9422.para:
These individuals lack the skills to mix even a basic cocktail, showing extreme arrogance without the ability to prove it.

The mojito was terrible, featuring underwhelming, overused mint.

The Sazerac was a mess; they shook it, making it too diluted, and then added a lemon wedge instead of the proper lemon peel twist.

yelp:test:9467.orig: So after 15 years having the best bloody marys around you changed your mix.  The watered down tomato juice out of the gun was horrible.  Drinks use to be good and over priced now they are horrible and over priced.  Won't be enjoying a cocktail here anymore.
yelp:test:9467.para: After 15 years of serving excellent bloody marys, you've altered your recipe. The canned, watered-down tomato juice was terrible. The drinks used to be decent but overpriced; now they're both bad and overpriced. I won't be stopping by for cocktails anymore.

yelp:test:9470.orig: My 1st trip to Vegas I stayed at the palms and I have to say that it was the greatest experience and best decision made by my friends and I..  The crowd and the vibe was awesome.. You get to mingle with the young rich, grown & sexy.. oh and with celebrities as well..  The rooms were very spacious with a nice view and comfortable beds..  We stayed at the play pen suit and i have to say that the stripper pole came very well in handy... I can't see myself going back to Vegas and not staying anywhere else but the palms.. highly recommend it..
yelp:test:9470.para: My first trip to Vegas, and I chose to stay at The Palms—it was an outstanding experience and the best decision my friends and I made. The atmosphere was fantastic, with a lively crowd and an energetic vibe. You can mingle with the young, wealthy crowd, mature and attractive individuals, and even some celebrities. The rooms were spacious, offering great views and comfortable beds. We stayed in the Play Pen suite, and the stripper pole was particularly useful. I wouldn't consider visiting Vegas without staying at The Palms again, and I highly recommend it.

yelp:test:9480.orig: I went to the Palms Casino thru Bookit.com.  My stay Oct 18-21 originally and it was for my 40th birthday.  First of all I only gave it 1 star for the actual room it self.  The room was clean, spacious with  a nice view of the strip.  The cons:   After I first initial night they came to clean our room at 6pm  I mean really...  but the second night we call them to come clean and they came right away and the third day we were there and extended our check out time  due to our flight leaving at 11pm that night, they never came at all!  We called them & asked for trash removal, towels & toilet paper & a guy that didn't speak any english or at least acted like he didn't brought towels up and kinda said someone would bring toilet paper he tired to leave but we ran & got the trash out our room & gave it to him to take with him.  Needless to say no one ever came to bring toilet paper or clean we used the kleenex in the bathroom.  At  check in I asked about the 2for1 drink specials that came with book.it.com the girl checking me in said they no longer did that and did not offer to accommodate me in any other way.    She did say we got free admission to the clubs in the hotel & we could  each
yelp:test:9480.para: I stayed at the Palms Casino from October 18 to 21, celebrating my 40th birthday. I rated the room only one star. While it was clean and spacious with a good view of the strip, there were significant issues. On the first night, housekeeping arrived at 6 pm to clean, which was very late. On the second night, we called for cleaning immediately, and they came promptly. However, on the third day, despite extending our stay until 11 pm for our flight, they never cleaned the room. We also requested trash removal, towels, and toilet paper. A non-English speaking staff member brought towels but failed to provide toilet paper, leaving us to use tissues from the bathroom. At check-in, I inquired about the 2-for-1 drink deal included with my booking through Bookit.com, but the staff said it was no longer available and offered no alternatives. They did mention that we received free entry to the hotel's clubs.

yelp:test:9489.orig: I went in for a tattoo during a vacation last week.  For a black and gray tattoo 3\"" x 3\"" to cost $400 with a non refundable deposit of $100 sight unseen of the drawing is not customer friendly.  You had artists sitting without appointments but would rather force me back out the door because I don't pay without knowing I will even like what you draw?  No thank you.  I had the money in my pocket in cash sweeties, but I left with it still there because I was unconvinced by your guy up front, inflated prices, and deposit policy.\nI have 20+ hours of ink and none from h&h.
yelp:test:9489.para: Last week, during my vacation, I got a tattoo. A 3" x 3" black and gray design was quoted at $400, with a non-refundable $100 deposit required upfront, even before seeing the drawing. Despite having artists available, you insisted I leave if I didn't want to pay without seeing the final design. No thanks. I had the money, but I left with it because I was unhappy with the prices, the deposit policy, and the artist's approach. I have over 20 hours of tattoos from other places, but none from H&H.

yelp:test:9495.orig: The Bellagio Pool Cafe is delicious but expensive... under a nice covered area, you can enjoy a wide variety of lunch options in your swimsuit and towel. By the time we sat down around 2:30 pm, I was starving so I ended up sampling everyone else's food in addition to my own.\n\nI had the teriyaki chicken lettuce wraps ($12.50) that came with cold noodles, pickled, veggies, and hoisen sauce. They were really yummy and a good amount of food. My uncle enjoyed the Cobb salad (about $14) that included fresh tomatoes (red and yellow), delicious avocado, etc. My brother and dad shared a tuna sandwich and a turkey sandwich with fries and cole slaw. Everyone appreciated their lunch selections and left the Cafe satisfied and happy.
yelp:test:9495.para:
The Bellagio Pool Cafe offers delightful yet pricey meals... You can dine in a pleasant covered area while wearing your swimsuit and towel. By the time we arrived around 2:30 pm, I was quite hungry and ended up trying several dishes, not just my own.

I tried the teriyaki chicken lettuce wraps ($12.50), which included cold noodles, pickled veggies, and hoisin sauce. They were delicious and generous in portion. My uncle relished the Cobb salad (around $14), featuring fresh tomatoes (both red and yellow), and a tasty avocado. My brother and dad shared a tuna sandwich and a turkey sandwich, accompanied by fries and coleslaw. Everyone was pleased with their meals and left the cafe feeling satisfied and content.

yelp:test:9517.orig:
Awesome Buffet.  

We tried the Ballagio Buffet and the Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan.   The Bellagio Buffet was the winner, by far.  

King crab legs, Short Ribs, Prime Rib.... All amazing.   I am still trying to figure out how they make any money.  Plenty of options.
yelp:test:9517.para:
Excellently Diverse Buffet Options. 

We dined at both the Bellagio and Wicked Spoon buffets at the Cosmopolitan, but the Bellagio Buffet stood out as the best by a significant margin. 

King crab legs, short ribs, and prime rib—each dish was outstanding. I'm still baffled by how they manage to turn a profit. There's such a wide array of choices.

yelp:test:9593.orig: This was my 7th time to Vegas and first time staying at the Paris. It will also be my last.... The service and the rooms are absolutely terrible!\n\nWe arrived around 11:30 am on a Weds. We knew it may be too early to check in but most hotels on the strip allow early check ins around noon. yelp:test:9593.para:
This was my seventh trip to Vegas, and my first at the Paris—turns out it will be my last. The service and accommodations were awful.

We arrived around 11:30 AM on a Wednesday, hoping for an early check-in since most hotels on the strip allow it around noon. After waiting in line for nearly 20 minutes (with only four people in front of us), we reached the counter. We provided our name and confirmation number, but the friendly attendant informed us that our reservation was for just one night, not the four we had booked, and our names weren't on the four rooms reserved for my wife's company. To make matters worse, there was a $25 early check-in fee. Our jaws dropped. We had to wait two hours for my wife's boss to arrive and resolve the issue. Finally, the nice lady (sarcasm intended) told us our rooms weren't ready, despite it being 3:30 PM, which is usually the regular check-in time. She suggested we return after an hour. An hour later, at 4:30 PM, the rooms still weren't ready.

yelp:test:9608.orig: This hotel has declined over the past years. We had a late check in and did not get the room we reserved. Understandably since we were late, however they gave us the worse room in the building. It was small and dark with absolutely no view at all. We were told by the front desk that we could have a room change in the morning, we never heard from those at the front desk as promised. Nonetheless we suffered through another night of noise and constant banging from who knows what. The walls are paper thin so good luck getting any rest. The furniture can use a makeover as well, the writing desk was burnt from possibly an iron?? I will not be staying here again regardless of deal they are having.  The reason I gave it 2 stars was the ease of checking in and the staff was very kind.
yelp:test:9608.para: This hotel has visibly deteriorated over the years. We arrived late and were not given our reserved room; instead, we received the worst room in the entire building. It was tiny and gloomy, with no view whatsoever. The front desk promised a room change the next morning, but we never heard from them. We endured another night of noise and mysterious banging. The walls are so thin that the disturbance was unbearable. The furniture also needs an update; the writing desk seemed to have been damaged by an iron. I won't be returning, no matter what deals they offer. I gave it two stars because the check-in process was smooth, and the staff were very friendly.

Monte Carlo, why did I choose to stay here?  Must be that it is located right in the middle of the strip, next to Aria and the City Center.  This used to be my wife's favorite hotel in Las Vegas.  Don't ask me why because I honestly don't know.  With many newer and older but better establishments on the strip, there's really no reason to choose Monte Carlo unless you already knew that...

the POOL has a lazy river!  It's not as long as the ones you might find at MGM, but it is sufficient enough to relax and take a moment away from the busy casino noise.  You can also rental a tube as floating device at the service counter.  But really, that's all the highlights of this hotel, unless you enjoy...

CHEAP FOOD COURT adjacent to the main elevators.  If I remember correctly, they have Starbucks, McDonald's, Manchu Wok, Rubio's, and Subway.  These are some of the choices that you might not find in other hotels on the strip.  Of course, if you want to drop a few hundred dollars, you can do at the casino, unless you knew to...

yelp:test:9644.para:
Why did I decide to stay at Monte Carlo? It’s because it’s centrally located on the strip, right between Aria and the City Center. This place used to be my wife’s go-to hotel in Las Vegas, though I can’t really explain why. With so many newer and better options available, there’s no compelling reason to pick Monte Carlo unless you already had a reason to...

The hotel does have a pool with a lazy river, though it’s not as extensive as those at MGM. Still, it’s perfect for a relaxing break from the casino’s hustle and bustle. You can also rent a tube there for floating.

The main highlight is the cheap food court near the elevators. I recall it having Starbucks, McDonald’s, Manchu Wok, Rubio’s, and Subway—options you might not find in other strip hotels. If you’re looking to spend more, you can always gamble, unless you know to...

check out Andre’s, the fine dining restaurant at Monte Carlo. I haven’t tried it myself, but according to other reviewers, it offers traditional French cuisine.

yelp:test:9649.orig: This review will be mostly written regarding the staff.  Everyone we encountered was super friendly.   From the restaurants to the Bathrooms and pool.   Our house keeping staff greeted us every morning.  We had a broken lamp which she called maintenance to take care of before we even had a chance.  When they didn't get it fixed the first day she found us to apologize and tell us she had called again.  The pool servers, although there didn't seem to be very many of them, were very helpful with picking out the right drink and bringing buckets and ice to make sure the drinks didn't get too warm in the heat.   As far as the hotel itself - it needs work.  The rooms are pretty beat up and could use some TLC. For the most part the room was clean and sufficient.  Let's face it, who spends much time in their rooms in Vegas, but it could still use something.
yelp:test:9649.para: This review primarily focuses on the staff, who were exceptionally friendly throughout our stay. We met them in various areas, including the restaurant, bathrooms, and pool. Our housekeeping staff greeted us every morning, and when we reported a broken lamp, she promptly arranged for maintenance to address it. After the first day, when the issue wasn't resolved, she personally apologized and ensured that maintenance was contacted again. The pool servers, despite being few in number, were very helpful, assisting us with selecting drinks and providing buckets and ice to keep our beverages cool in the heat. However, the hotel itself requires some improvements; the rooms are in need of some TLC, though they were generally clean and adequate. After all, who spends much time in their room when in Las Vegas, but it could still benefit from some updates.

yelp:test:9660.orig: VERY SEXY SHOW! Very Vegas! Talented performances. A must see with your hubby, partner, or boyfriend. Its got something for everyone if you know what I mean, and it definitely gets you in the mood to have some dirty fun ;o)
yelp:test:9660.para: AN INCREDIBLY ATTRACTION-INDUCING SHOW! A TRUE VEGAS EXPERIENCE! Featuring impressive talents. Absolutely worth watching with your significant other. There's entertainment for all tastes, and it's sure to spark some romantic desires ;o)

yelp:test:9698.orig:
My brother got a comped room here, so I may be a bit bias...

Best part of the suite was the bathtub, large and deep enough to fit almost anyone.  Plus, three televisions and super comfy beds.  The pool was shallow (not even 4 feet) and crowded, but it was in the middle of summer and therefore expected.  Great window shopping, like Barneys and DVF.  We didn't pay the resort fee to get wifi in our room, but the main lobby and food court had free wifi so everything was okay.  Good location, in the middle of the strip and near shopping that's more reasonable like the Fashion Show and Caesar's Palace.  Oh, and Walgreens downstairs!  An overpriced Walgreens of course, but a Walgreens nonetheless.    

My only complaint was that the telephone line to the front desk was useless.  We tried calling on three occasions and never got to a real person despite 10-15 minutes of waiting.
yelp:test:9698.para:
My brother received a complimentary room here, which might make my review a bit biased...

The standout feature of the suite was the bathtub—it was spacious and deep enough for anyone to use comfortably. Additionally, there were three TVs and very plush beds. The pool was shallow (less than 4 feet) and quite crowded, which was understandable given it was summertime. There was plenty of great window shopping, including at Barneys and DVF. We didn't pay the resort fee for Wi-Fi in our room, but the main lobby and food court offered free Wi-Fi, so we were fine. The location was ideal, situated in the heart of the strip and close to more affordable shopping at the Fashion Show and Caesar's Palace. There was even a Walgreens downstairs, though it was on the pricey side.

My main issue was with the phone line to the front desk; it was unresponsive. We tried calling three times and waited up to 15 minutes each time, but never reached a real person.

yelp:test:9704.orig: The Venetian is my favorite casino! It appears they shut off the water to the outside canal during the summer, but in the winter, it was beautiful. The canals inside ran during both seasons I went. We ate at an Italian restaurant overlooking the inside canals. It was pricey, but worth the food and service. We were also in awe of the mural on the ceiling at the entrance and how the inside makes you feel like it is always daytime. Simply amazing!
yelp:test:9704.para: I adore the Venetian casino! While the outdoor canal seems to lack water in the summer, it was stunning in the winter. The indoor canals were flowing regardless of the season. We dined at an Italian restaurant with a view of the interior canals. Although the meal was expensive, the quality of food and service made it worthwhile. We were also captivated by the grand mural above the entrance and the perpetual daylight ambiance inside. Truly incredible!

yelp:test:9711.para: We booked the honeymoon suite from Sunday to Friday two months ahead. Upon arrival, I called to confirm and asked for a bottle of champagne in the room, but was informed I needed to check in first. We upgraded our stay, and the request was repeated, only to be told there was a bottle in the ice box that I could charge to the room (not the one I requested). Despite the Venetian's beauty, we were constantly approached by solicitors asking where we were from, if we were planning to see any shows, or what kind of phone we had. I will never stay there again.

yelp:test:9722.orig: This place is all about the hotel and the shops.  It's a great place to visit and have fun.  They are more expensive than a lot of the other casinos.  The Bourbon Room (bar) is a total rip off.  Don't order a beer or a drink there.  You'll pay more than you think.
yelp:test:9722.para: This location focuses mainly on the hotel and retail outlets. It's an enjoyable destination for a visit and entertainment, though the prices are generally higher compared to other casinos. The Bourbon Room, as a bar, is particularly overpriced; avoid ordering any drinks there as the costs can be surprisingly high.

yelp:test:9735.orig:
First time staying at the Mirage, and I was very happy with the experience.  Awesome pool, cabana at Bare on the first day, ridiculously fun bartenders at Kokomo's every night that kept our party going until (gulp!) 6 in the morning...not to mention Carnegie Deli *right there*.  The RhumBar is killer, and the spa will help you ""detox so you can retox"" right up there with the best of them...We literally had everything that we needed right inside the hotel, and we appreciated that there was no smell of smoke anywhere we went.  

Rooms were comfy, and soundproof! Did not hear any of the outside noise that other yelpers here have complained about.  

Pool service was great, though I docked one star for the non-hotel guests that seem to make it in.  Club promoters seem to have no problem, though we can't really complain about the club comps that they provided our group.   Still though, makes you wonder.  With the pool that packed, they would do good to make it a bit more exclusive...
yelp:test:9735.para:
My first stay at the Mirage was a delight. The pool was fantastic, and we enjoyed a cabana at Bare on our first day. The bartenders at Kokomo's were incredibly entertaining, keeping our group going until the early hours of the morning. The Carnegie Deli was conveniently located right within the hotel. The RhumBar was outstanding, and the spa offered top-notch detox treatments. Everything we needed was right there in the hotel, and we appreciated the absence of smoke anywhere we went.

The rooms were comfortable and soundproof; we didn't hear any outside noise, unlike what other reviewers mentioned. Pool service was excellent, but I deducted a star because non-hotel guests sometimes accessed the pool. Club promoters were lenient, but we appreciated the club comps they provided. However, with the pool so crowded, it might be better to make it more exclusive.

yelp:test:9746.orig:

yelp:test:9746.para:
Last month, we decided to cancel our Aria reservation and opt for the Mirage instead. Upon arrival in Vegas on December 6th, we discovered we had been given a double bed despite requesting a king. A quick call to the Mlife counter resolved the issue, and we were promptly moved to a room with a king bed and a splendid view of the strip from a higher floor.

Our gambling experience at the Mirage was enjoyable, accounting for nearly 90% of our time there. The dealers were friendly, and the players at the tables were engaging. This was our first time staying so far north on the strip, and we found it quite appealing. Typically, we stay at Mandalay Bay, which is at the southern end, or the Aria, which is centrally located.

No matter where we stay on the strip, we always make it a point to visit BLT Burger, and we've never been let down. This time was no different; their burgers were outstanding, and I particularly enjoyed their Knight Rider shake.

We also tried Stack for dinner one evening, and it was satisfactory. The atmosphere was pleasant, and the food was quite good.

The cherry on top was that Mlife offered to cover our entire stay (excluding my wife's spa expenses), which was fantastic.

yelp:test:9764.orig:

 I had the Pisco Sour as my cocktail, the petite lettuce wedges, filet and mash potatoes. All where freak'n delicious!

yelp:test:9764.para:
My wife wanted to try a celebrity chef restaurant, and I chose this one based on a previous positive experience. We had a great time there.

I started with a Pisco Sour and enjoyed the petite lettuce wedges, filet, and mashed potatoes. Everything was absolutely delicious!

My wife keeps mentioning how fantastic the filet was. Unless you're vegetarian, this place is a safe bet. Another excellent restaurant at the Venetian is Bouchon.

As I walked by tables, I saw several larger tables with less people seated at them and empty chairs.  Hmmm.  So they really couldn't let me bring an extra guest or they really don't know how to pla
yelp:test:9768.para:
I hosted clients recently and booked the restaurant through Open Table. Initially, I reserved for four, but then decided to add one more person. They repeatedly said they couldn't accommodate an extra chair at our table. Fine.

Upon arrival, we found a private party in the lobby/bar/wait area. That was unexpected and a bit unsettling. They seated us in the lounge area where we ordered drinks, which never arrived. Our "table" was actually an end table in the lounge area, so we had to move to another table.

The wine list was extensive and quite daunting. I just wanted a simple red wine with my meat, but there was no straightforward option.

From the beginning, our table was cluttered with too many items, and the oversized service ware didn't fit well on the small table, making it hard to eat.

Before our food arrived, I went to the restroom, which was quite a trek given the restaurant's size. As I passed other tables, I noticed larger tables with fewer people and empty seats. This made me wonder if they couldn't add an extra guest or if they were managing seating inefficiently.

yelp:test:9775.orig: Fantastic food, great service.  Much more expensive than what we usually spend on dinner, but so yummy and worth it!  We both had steak for dinner, with sides of salad in the sherry ving., garlic smashed potatoes, and the pecan pie.  I wish we had room to finish the pecan pie, but could only get through half.
yelp:test:9775.para: Delicious food and excellent service, though the meal was quite pricey compared to our usual dinners. It was so tasty that it was definitely worth the cost! We both enjoyed steak, accompanied by a salad dressed in sherry vinegar, garlic mashed potatoes, and pecan pie. I regret not having enough room to finish the pecan pie; I only managed to eat half.

yelp:test:9782.orig:
***The food at The Palm Restaurant was not that great and the service was awful on our visit***

I have been to The Palm Restaurant in Downtown Los Angeles and I did not enjoy it that much.  We went for lunch and I had their steak frites and, unfortunately, they were using really poor quality beef (a New York Strip but not a good one).  You do have to use less expensive beef than dinner to serve steak but still achieve a reasonable lunch price, but most restaurants like Lucques do not settle for lower quality; instead, they just showcase a cheaper cut like hanger steak.

Since I went to the Downtown LA Palm for lunch, I did not get a chance to try their signature Prime steaks.  I could have tried them at my recent trip to the Las Vegas location (The Palm is located in the Forum Shops at Caesars Palace), but I opted for one of their other signature items instead--lobster.  I had their jumbo lobster tail and it was actually pretty good.  The lobster was huge--it was almost a pound--and the lobster meat was good--fresh, moist, lightly sweet, and fairly soft.  The seasoning of the lobster was also good--flavorful with a little bit of spice but not overpowering.

Almost everything
yelp:test:9782.para:
During my visit to The Palm Restaurant in Downtown Los Angeles, I found the food to be subpar and the service to be poor. For lunch, I ordered the steak frites, but the beef was of very low quality, despite it being a New York Strip. While it's understandable to use less expensive cuts for lunch, most restaurants, like Lucques, opt for higher quality even for lunch to maintain a good price point. 

I didn't get to try their signature Prime steaks during my Downtown LA visit, but I did have their jumbo lobster tail at a different location, The Palm in Las Vegas. The lobster was excellent; it was large, fresh, and had a nice, moist texture with a subtle sweetness. The seasoning was flavorful and just right, not too spicy.

I thought I had eaten there before and found it disappointing, but I wasn't sure. Unfortunately, it was disappointing again. The service was decent, especially with our server, but the expressions on the waiters' faces suggested they were unhappy, which was a bad sign. The food was lackluster; we ordered the Bögli burger and the lobster BLT. The burger was dry and overcooked, while the lobster BLT was okay but not exceptional—just another sandwich with lobster. The atmosphere seemed promising, but it was quite empty, so the ambiance wasn't as lively as I had expected. Prices were reasonable, but they would increase for steaks. Overall, I don't intend to return because there are so many other dining options in Vegas.

yelp:test:9805.para:
To begin with, I'd rate the casino itself a 3, but the hotel, which I won't return to, brings the overall rating down.

CASINO...
The casino is very elegant and fits its theme, but it's overly large, making it easy to get lost despite the clear signs. It has a great variety of restaurants, though most are quite pricey. Despite its size, it feels somewhat cramped and stuffy due to the numerous machines, tables, and people inside.

HOTEL...

Each floor of the hotel is beautifully designed and spacious, particularly the central area near the elevators. The rooms are just okay.

yelp:test:9855.orig: The service was friendly at the front and with our server, but this sushi bar in the basement of Bally's is just a bit disappointing. The menu isn't imaginative, and the classics just don't taste great. Speaking of the menu, the plastic-coated menus have item after item and price after price crossed off in Sharpie, and when I'm spending $60-70 on lunch, that just isn't good enough.
yelp:test:9855.para: While the service was welcoming from the front desk to our server, the sushi bar located beneath Bally's falls short of expectations. The menu lacks creativity, and even the traditional dishes are underwhelming. Moreover, the menus, which are covered in Sharpie marks, with numerous items and prices scratched out, are particularly disappointing given that I was paying around $60-70 for lunch.

The Double Down holds a special place in my heart. 

Now on to why I wrote this...I went into the Double Down the day after Christmas to meet up with some friends who were visiting from CA and it wasn't too busy, the bar was full but not really anywhere else in the bar. It took a while for the bartender to acknowledge that we were ready to drink, my boyfriend got tired of waiting so he went to the other side of the bar to get the bartenders attention. We have been there when it is shoulder to shoulder and we have had the bartenders pay more attention than this one. My boyfriend is a regular at the DD and said that every time that bartender is working, the same stuff happens...you wait forever for a drink and the dude acts like you're bugging him. This is what my problem is
yelp:test:9861.para:
This review is specifically about my experience on Monday nights. Normally, I would be effusively positive and give this place the highest rating possible because I adore the Double Down. It has been a constant in my social life since I moved here, and I've brought family, ex-husbands, and friends here, many of whom were having their first visit. I recall the days of the bras and the famous mechanical horse. The Double Down holds a special place in my heart.

However, my recent visit on New Year's Eve was disappointing. Despite the bar not being overly crowded, it took a long time for the bartender to serve us. My boyfriend, who is a frequent visitor, noted that this bartender consistently ignores customers, even when the bar is more crowded. This behavior is what I find unacceptable.

yelp:test:9962.orig: Was a big fan of the lincoln park location in chicago, so to find the same menu, at similar prices with al fresco dining overlooking the bellagio fountains was a nice treat.\n\nThe service was super fast, and the warm brie was superb.
yelp:test:9962.para: I was a big fan of the Lincoln Park location in Chicago, and finding a place with the same menu and similar prices, where I could enjoy al fresco dining while overlooking the Bellagio fountains, was a delightful surprise. yelp:test:10011.orig: This place is fantastic. The food, the service, the location right in front of the Bellagio fountains. I cannnot reccomend it enough.

yelp:test:10019.para:
I’ve looked into this before and have visited multiple times. I won’t return and I’ll stop recommending this place for several reasons. 

They add a 18% gratuity for groups of five or more, and we were six. The service was terrible; she only came by once for our order and once to bring the bill. No refills, no checks—nothing. We planned to tip 10%, but it was unexpectedly mandatory at 18%. I spoke to the manager, who didn’t apologize but instead shifted the blame onto us, saying we should have asked for him. In the end, we were blamed by the manager, and the blame was placed back on us. This indicates problems not just with the staff but with management as well. I refused and we left. He reluctantly removed the 18% and dropped the bill back on our table, but there was no apology.

The steak was overcooked for most of us, and the wine was just okay. It’s a letdown, and with so many other options available, I strongly advise being cautious if you’re a group of five or more. 

The place is also very dim, making it hard to read the menu, and the wicker chairs are uncomfortable, likely to speed up table turnover.

yelp:test:10020.orig:
WOW! 

the bf and i had made reservations here before we were off to watch jersey boys, and everything from start to finish was fabulous. We were seated right away with delicious, fresh, warm, bread to snack on before our meal. coming in I knew i wanted steak, so i ordered the ""classique"" since it's always better to be safe the first time, right? the steak is large but thin at the same time. the BUTTER on top omg, i don't think i've ever had steak like that before. it was goddamn mouthwatering. hats off to the chef for cooking it a perfect medium rare too. and the fries, wow. I am NOT a french fries person, but i ended up inhaling these thin, oddly cut fries. 

the restaurant is gorgeous on top of the great service. I had requested to be seated on the patio, but because it's so cold these days it was covered up. No worries, the view of the bellagio foundation always looks good.

yelp:test:10020.para:
WOW!

My boyfriend and I had reserved a table here before heading to see Jersey Boys, and everything from start to finish was fantastic. We were promptly seated and enjoyed some delicious, fresh, warm bread to snack on before our meal. I knew I wanted steak, so I opted for the "classique" to ensure it was a safe choice on my first visit. The steak was large but quite thin. The butter on top was incredible; I've never had steak like that before. It was truly mouthwatering, and the chef did an excellent job cooking it to a perfect medium rare. The fries were also amazing. I'm not usually a fan of fries, but these thin, oddly cut fries were so good that I ended up eating them all.

The restaurant is stunning, and the service was top-notch. Although I had requested a patio seat, it was covered due to the cold weather. No problem, as the view of the Bellagio fountain was still beautiful. 

I will definitely return the next time I'm in town.

yelp:test:10027.orig:
We ate at the bar during Andre's ""5-6-7"" happy hour.  Beers are $5, interesting cocktails $6, and appetizers $7.  The bartender who served us was excellent, crafted great drinks (I tried the Pomegranate Lemon Drop and the Cucumber Collins -- both delicious).  DH had Batch 19 beer, a Colorado prohibition-era brew recipe.  From the $7 app menu, we tried the sliders, juicy beef with roquefort on fresh house-made brioche, and added fries for $1 ... also enjoyed the charcuterie platter, combining meats, cheeses, pickles, toast, dried fruits, stone-ground mustard -- perfect bites of sweet, salty, tangy, spicy.   And chickpea panisse featured moist triangles of chickpea patties topped with a tangy tomato relish ... sort of a super-fancy deconstructed falafel.

We also ""splurged"" on the calamari petals from the regular bar menu -- that was $14. This is a nice twist on the traditional calamari rings ... here, they're flat, oval shaped pieces of squid, fried with a crunchy coating and a lemony aioli for dipping.  Mmmmm.

This bar menu is a great deal ... and it makes me want to try Andre's for dinner, because the chefs showed great care in preparing all our food.
yelp:test:10027.para:
During Andre's "5-6-7" happy hour, we dined at the bar. Beers cost $5, cocktails were $6, and appetizers were $7. Our bartender was outstanding, creating excellent drinks; I savored the Pomegranate Lemon Drop and the Cucumber Collins, both delicious. My partner enjoyed Batch 19 beer, a Colorado prohibition-era recipe. From the $7 appetizer menu, we sampled sliders with juicy beef and Roquefort on fresh, house-made brioche, and added fries for an extra dollar. We also relished the charcuterie platter, featuring a delightful mix of meats, cheeses, pickles, toast, dried fruits, and stone-ground mustard. The chickpea panisse was moist triangles of chickpea patties topped with a tangy tomato relish, akin to a gourmet deconstructed falafel.

We also indulged in the calamari petals from the regular menu, priced at $14. These were flat, oval-shaped pieces of squid, fried with a crunchy coating and served with a lemony aioli for dipping. Mmm.

This bar menu offers a fantastic value, and it has piqued my interest in trying Andre's for dinner, as the chefs clearly took great care in preparing our food.

yelp:test:10029.orig: I was with a group of 7 girls and we were looking for a somewhat low-key night. We went to V Bar and it was so much fun! yelp:test:10029.para: We had a group of seven girls seeking a low-key evening, and we ended up at V Bar, where we had a fantastic time. If you're looking to dance without feeling crowded or harassed, V Bar is definitely worth a visit!
