The food is average, at best.  It is also overpriced.  The place is best on its breakfast foods, in my humble opinion.  The omelets are huge, but again, overpriced.

The appetizer sampler platter is good, but overpriced.  Oddly enough, the onion rings on the appetizer platter are different than the onion rings as a side item.

I recommend this place for drinks in the lounge, and for breakfast on the weekends if you ar
yelp:test:10043.para:
The Peppermill is a unique establishment that's hard to put into words. It's a blend of refined and tacky elements, described as "Utterly Craptastic." Could it be that a Flamingo exploded here, giving it its outrageous pink color?

Joking aside, the standout feature of this restaurant is its decor. It exudes a cheesy, vintage Vegas vibe with its fake neon lights and artificial forest. Have you ever seen a deciduous tree in the middle of a desert? I adore the decor and always make sure to visit the 24-hour lounge to see the fire and water fountain, as well as the cocktail servers in their evening gowns.

Peppermill is a long-standing institution, with a scene from "Casino" filmed there featuring Sharon Stone.

The food, however, is merely average, and quite pricey. In my opinion, the breakfast dishes are the best. The omelets are large but also overpriced. The appetizer sampler platter is decent, though still overpriced. Interestingly, the onion rings on the sampler platter differ from those served as a side.

I suggest visiting for drinks in the lounge or for breakfast on weekends.

yelp:test:10057.orig: History, tradition, star power, kitschy vibe, massive portions, big strong drinks and decent prices......what's not to like?
yelp:test:10057.para: What could possibly be missing when you consider its rich history, age-old traditions, celebrity appeal, nostalgic atmosphere, generous servings, powerful cocktails, and reasonable costs?

yelp:test:10116.orig: the luxor's sorta-kinda-cool-from-the-outside pyramid shape wreaks havoc on the hotel rooms within.  low ceilings, angled windows that you have to lean back at a precarious angle to see out of (and that, even with the dark tint, require the curtains to be drawn at all times to keep the room from heating up to uncomfortable degrees), and ... malfunctioning plumbing.  we thought it was just our room that was cursed with a non-flushing toilet.  but friends who have stayed at the luxor in the past were quick to mention experiencing the same issue.  all i can come up with is that this is a HUGE design flaw in the pyramidal structure: none of the rooms are directly above one another, so it would seem that none of the pipes would be directly lined up in a vertical fashion, resulting in poor water flow?  clearly i am not a physicist or engineer, but that's the only thing i can think of to explain the issue, since the bathrooms on the main floor of the casino seemed to function properly.  \n\namenities in the hotel were mixed: no good food options (a mini-food court with some nasty fast food, about six starbucks, and a buffet), an ok spa, and an ok pool.  they have systematically removed an
yelp:test:10116.para:
The Luxor's pyramid-shaped exterior is intriguing, but the design wreaks havoc on the interior hotel rooms. Ceiling heights are low, and windows are angled in such a way that you need to lean back at a precarious angle to see out, and even with dark tints, the curtains must remain drawn to prevent the room from overheating. We initially thought our room had a non-flushing toilet, but friends who stayed there previously reported the same issue. It seems like a significant design flaw, as the rooms aren't directly stacked, which should have prevented vertical alignment of pipes, leading to poor water flow. While I'm not a physicist or engineer, this is the only explanation I can think of. The bathrooms on the casino floor, however, seemed to function well.

As for amenities, the offerings were mixed. There were no good food options, just a mini-food court with some unpleasant fast food and about six Starbucks locations, along with a buffet. The spa and pool were okay, but they've clearly reduced something important.

yelp:test:10143.orig: Never would have stayed here if it hadn't been one of the host hotels for a conference I was attending. It seems like some money has been put into updating the casino/entertainment area, but the rooms leave something to be desired. The room seemed clean; however, everything was so old, it had that worn out look and feel. I felt like the only one staying on my floor, which can be good and bad...good because it's quiet, bad because I felt like a scene out of the shining was just waiting to happen...There's a reason why rooms are only $50-70/night.
yelp:test:10143.para: I wouldn't have stayed here unless it was one of the host hotels for the conference I was attending. While the casino and entertainment area have been updated, the rooms are lacking. The room was clean, but everything appeared old and worn. I felt like the sole guest on my floor, which was quiet but also made me feel isolated, like a scene from The Shining was about to unfold. The low room rate of $50-70 per night explains the condition of the rooms.

yelp:test:10146.para: This establishment is old, grimy, and outdated. The guests were just as unpleasant as the room I stayed in, which had a view of a heating unit and a roof. yelp:test:10147.para:
After working at the POOL Tradeshow, I just returned from a stay that lasted almost a week. Upon arrival, the check-in lines were extremely long, which was frustrating, especially since it was summertime. I expected them to open more lines to manage the crowd better, but they didn't. After finally reaching the front, there was an issue with the credit card machine, which was understandable, but the staff member didn't offer any apology or explanation for the delay. This confirmed my initial impression that the hotel would be subpar. Thankfully, we weren't in the actual pyramid rooms, as I can't imagine staying there with a casino directly below.

We checked into our room, and the bathroom had a strong, unpleasant odor, reminiscent of a toilet that had been double-deckered (when someone defecates in the tank and leaves it there, making it permanently smelly). We even checked for any obvious signs of recent use, but the smell was unmistakable. Given our previous experience with poor service, we didn't bother to request a different room. Upon further inspection, we noticed blood spots on the beds, not just one but several visible ones. At least they could have tried to hide that. We called to change the sheets, but the situation was already so bad that we weren't optimistic about the outcome.

yelp:test:10240.orig: One of the cooler things I've done in Las Vegas lately.  $50 for 50 shots.  Shot an M16.  Very empowering.   But very scary at the same time.  3 miles from the Strip.
yelp:test:10240.para: Recently, I've had one of the more exciting experiences in Las Vegas—paying $50 for 50 shots, which included firing an M16. It was incredibly empowering, yet also quite scary. Located about 3 miles from the Strip.

yelp:test:10288.orig: I had dinner here last weekend, and decided to order the gnocchi since I had it at Bouchon in Yountville.  I thought it was either overcooked and or dry, so sent it back for another order since it was what I came here for.  The next order wasn't much better, and the waitress and manager apologized and comped me my dinner.  Even though I didn't like my food, I still give them 3 1/2 stars for trying to make it right and apologizing.  The other thing that was annoying was that we ordered bottled water, and they took it away from the table to keep it on ice.  Well the busboy or expediter kept coming over and pouring tap water from a pitcher into our glasses.  The waitress had to keep coming over and tell the busboy not too do that.The atmosphere is pleasant and my wife liked her mussels.  I will have to go back to Yountville to see if my taste buds were correct.  They insist that it is the same recipe.
yelp:test:10288.para: Last weekend, I dined here and opted for the gnocchi, having enjoyed it at Bouchon in Yountville. I found this one either overcooked or dry, so I returned it for a new order. The second attempt wasn't much better, and the waitress and manager apologized, offering to comp my meal. Despite the unsatisfactory food, I awarded them 3 1/2 stars for their efforts to rectify the situation. Another irritation was that, after ordering bottled water, it was taken to be kept cold, while a busboy kept refilling our glasses with tap water from a pitcher, which the waitress had to repeatedly stop. The ambiance was pleasant, and my wife enjoyed her mussels. I plan to return to Yountville to verify if my taste preferences were accurate, as they claim the recipe is the same.

yelp:test:10345.orig: inside the bellagio hotel and if you have the time, sit outside on the patio so you can see the water show. had lunch here. started with cesar salad with anchovies.this was one of the best cesar salads. scallops were cooked well. veal chops were cooked well however covered in tomato sauce which was not appetizing. cheese burger were done well with their signature fries. had the crab special spaghetti. came out luke warm and the spaghetti was over cooked so it was really gummy. returned that and ordered the  short rib parpadelle. again the dish came out luke warm with zero seasoning and the pasta over coked. just left the dish, had a plane to catch. will not go back
yelp:test:10345.para: At the Bellagio Hotel, if you have time, sit outside on the patio to enjoy the water show. I had lunch there. I started with a Caesar salad that included anchovies, which was one of the best Caesar salads I've had. The scallops were cooked perfectly, but the veal chops, while well-cooked, were covered in a tomato sauce that wasn't appealing. The cheeseburger and their signature fries were well-prepared. However, the crab special spaghetti arrived lukewarm and the pasta was overcooked, making it gummy. I returned the dish and ordered short rib parpadelle, which also came out lukewarm and without seasoning, and the pasta was overcooked again. I left the dish uneaten and departed to catch a flight. I won't be returning.

yelp:test:10348.orig: Ate at Olive's a few years back and returned for a business dinner, it was just as good the second time as the first. Everyone enjoyed their meals and the great service. Highly recommend the flatbreads for an appetizer and the gnocchi for dinner. Try to get a seat near the windows so you can get a view of the Bellagio fountains throughout dinner.
yelp:test:10348.para: A few years ago, I dined at Olive's and recently revisited for a business meal. The experience was just as delightful the second time around. Everyone relished their dishes and appreciated the excellent service. I strongly suggest trying the flatbreads as an appetizer and the gnocchi as a main course. If possible, secure a table by the windows to enjoy the Bellagio fountains throughout your meal.

yelp:test:10354.orig:
Review is for dinner. I actually give it 2.5 stars but they deserve to be rounded down... Menu for dinner was tiny, disappointing. Decided to go with the Caribbean jambalaya and it was ok, but the flavors were a little too coconut-y. The pina colada on the rocks-esk drink I had was ok.

 Food made me sick afterward though, maybe it was the way too sweet drinks (only had two so don't blame it on the boos). This was only at 9pm! 

I won't be back.
yelp:test:10354.para:
The review is for the dinner experience. I rate it 2.5 stars, but I think it should be rounded down. The menu was quite limited and underwhelming. I chose the Caribbean jambalaya, which was acceptable, though the coconut flavor was a bit overpowering. The pina colada I ordered was also just okay.

Unfortunately, the food made me feel unwell afterward, possibly due to the overly sweet drinks (I only had two, so it wasn't the alcohol). I found it frustrating that we spent over $100 for two people on mediocre food, and the restaurant was trying to switch to a club atmosphere, which rushed us and ruined the end of our meal with loud music. This change occurred at 9 PM! 

I won't be returning.

yelp:test:10393.orig: Very very good, expensive, but worth it. We ordered the small tasting menu. Perfect if you want a little taste of a bunch of different stuff. Waiter wasn't that friendly, but he did a very good job as far as service is concerned.
yelp:test:10393.para: It's very good and pricey, but definitely worth it. We opted for the small tasting menu, which is ideal if you want to sample a variety of dishes. The waiter wasn't particularly friendly, but he provided excellent service.

yelp:test:10404.orig: Food was good and the bar tender knows how to make sure patrons are happy.
yelp:test:10404.para: The food was excellent, and the bartender excels at ensuring that all guests are satisfied.

yelp:test:10470.orig:
De. Lish. Us. 

Delux was one of the first restaurants I went to upon moving to Phoenix and I have gone back a few times since, mainly at lunch during the work week. It's my favorite burger spot. 

The atmosphere is slightly on the pretentious side. However, it's very small and pretty cramped. Even at lunch during the week it can feel cramped at a table and there's a big chance of waiting in line awhile. I've sat both inside and outside and felt a little too close to the other tables. It's a little complicated with bigger groups also.

The food however is amazing. I always get the same thing, a delux burger and sweet potato fries. I don't care if you are scared of medium rare, you need to try this thing. It's one of the most amazing burger's I've had and I can never finish the entire thing. I'd love to have a mini one. That would be perfect. A regular order of fries comes in an adorable metal mini shopping cart. Also good to note is that by default you do not get just ketchup with your fries. Being a non tomato eater, it's nice to not have to remember to ask for another dipping sauce. 

Oh the beer list you ask? Phenomenal. Being able to order a red velvet always makes me h
yelp:test:10470.para:
When I moved to Phoenix, Delux was one of the first restaurants I visited, and I've returned a few times, mostly for lunch on weekdays. It's my go-to spot for burgers.

The ambiance is a bit on the fancy side, but it's a small, somewhat cramped space. Even during the week, it can feel crowded, and there's often a wait. I've sat both indoors and outdoors, but I feel a bit too close to the neighboring tables, especially with larger groups.

Despite the atmosphere, the food is outstanding. I consistently order the Delux burger and sweet potato fries. If you're a fan of medium-rare meat, you must try this burger; it's one of the best I've had, and I often can't finish it. I'd love a smaller version—it would be perfect. The fries come in a cute metal mini shopping cart, which is a nice touch. Also, the fries come with more than just ketchup, which is great for someone like me who doesn't eat tomatoes.

And the beer selection? Absolutely fantastic. Ordering a red velvet beer is always a treat.

yelp:test:10501.orig: Better than Wynn, but not 30% better than Wynn, considering the 30% price increase.  Amazing seafood selection.  Pesto mashed taters and apricot mousse are to die for.
yelp:test:10501.para: While it surpasses Wynn in quality, it's not 30% superior given the 30% hike in price. They offer an impressive array of seafood. The pesto mashed potatoes and apricot mousse are absolutely delicious.

yelp:test:10509.orig:
Yum.  


That little 3 letter word sums it up.  I got here at 1045am.  The breakfast buffet closes at 11am.  I suggest you get there earlier to take full advantage of what this beast has to offer.  I couldn't get an omelette, as the line for it was like at a sizzler or waiting for crab legs, but man, they looked good.  Instead I just got the normal buffet fare.  There were 3 different kinds of potatoes (sliced thinly, cubed, and baked), the bacon was crispy but still had amazing taste, multiple sausages, waffles, french toast, pancakes, chorizo, etc.  It was all amazing, even though the scrambled eggs were a bit runny (I dislike runny eggs.  A lot.).  For $16 (this includes tax), I say it is well worth it.  If only I were hungrier (or was I too hungry from waiting too long??), I would've done more than $16 worth of damage.  Instead, I only probably did $13.  Sad.

Oh yea, the orange juice was amazing.  I highly recommend it.
yelp:test:10509.para:
Yum. 

That simple three-letter word captures it all. I arrived at 10:45 AM, and the breakfast buffet closes at 11 AM. I recommend getting there early to make the most of everything on offer. Unfortunately, the omelette line was as long as at a Sizzler or waiting for crab legs, but they looked delicious. Instead, I opted for the regular buffet items. There were three types of potatoes (thinly sliced, cubed, and baked), crispy bacon with fantastic flavor, various sausages, waffles, French toast, pancakes, chorizo, and more. Everything was fantastic, though the scrambled eggs were a bit runny (I really don't like runny eggs). For $16 (which includes tax), it was definitely worth it. If I were hungrier, or perhaps if I hadn't waited so long, I might have spent more than $16. As it was, I probably consumed around $13 worth of food. Sigh.

Oh, and the orange juice was outstanding. I highly recommend it.

yelp:test:10512.orig:
Let me preface this review with a couple of things:
1. I went on a Monday at 3pm, so probably not the most ideal time to see the freshest foods and most attentive staff, but less people to fight with to get to the food
2. I live in Manhattan so I am spoiled by knowing what good food and service are
3. I understand that a buffet, even an expensive buffet will never meet the quality of a decent restaurant

With all that said, the variety and quality of food was JUST BARELY OK, after seeing several reviews I guess my expectations got a little too high.

Also of note I found a HAIR in my gravy, when I mentioned it to the waitress her extremely caviler response was some thing to the effect of ""OK, I let them know"".  No ""I'm so sorry"" or ""I really apologize"", NOTHING.

All in all not a great experience, but if you want a large quantity of food you can't beat it for 20 bucks
yelp:test:10512.para:
To start, here are a few points to consider:
1. I visited on a Monday at 3pm, which might not have been the best time to see the freshest foods and the most attentive staff, but it was quieter and less crowded.
2. Being from Manhattan, I have high standards for both food and service.
3. I understand that a buffet, even an expensive one, can't match the quality of a good restaurant.

Given these factors, the food and service were just barely satisfactory. My expectations were likely set too high based on other reviews.

Additionally, I found a hair in my gravy. When I brought it to the waitress's attention, her response was dismissive, something along the lines of "OK, I'll let them know." There was no apology or expression of regret.

Overall, it was not a great experience, but if you're looking for a lot of food at a good price, it's hard to beat the value for 20 bucks.

yelp:test:10535.orig: Lunch for two on April 12, 2012 - Thursday afternoon at 2 PM. Worst buffet Ive ever eaten at in Vegas. $48 for two - food looked decent, tasted like crap. Overcooked, over salted mushy pastas... Shrimp were soggy and limp (old), Seared salmon was very fishey, tasted oild, RIbs were half cooked and tough and VERY salty, the ceaser salad was limp and soggy, even the cheesecake was bland and pasty. HOW do you ruin cheescake? The only decent food I had was the flank steak (and I could have gotten a top flank steak anywhere else for $5.99)  I went here because I'd read good reviews online... I normally go to Sams Town or Rio. I will never go back to this buffet again it was a waste of money and time. I could barely eat the food and I am NOT a picky eater! I almost complained immediately and asked for my money back. I wish I had, as 90% of the food we took went into the trash..
yelp:test:10535.para: On April 12, 2012, Thursday at 2 PM, we had a lunch for two in Vegas. It was the worst buffet I've ever experienced. The meal cost $48 for two, and while the food looked acceptable, it tasted terrible. The pastas were overcooked and mushy, overly salted, and unappetizing. The shrimp were soggy and old, the seared salmon was fishy and oily, the ribs were undercooked and tough, and the ceaser salad was limp and soggy. Even the cheesecake was bland and unflavorful. How do you make cheesecake taste so bad? The only decent dish was the flank steak, but I could have found a better one elsewhere for less. I had read positive reviews online, usually opting for Sams Town or Rio. I won't return to this buffet; it was a waste of money and time. I struggled to eat the food, and as someone who isn't picky, I almost demanded a refund. Ninety percent of the food we took ended up in the trash.

yelp:test:10546.orig: Decent price for a buffet in Vegas.  The line was not more than 30 minutes on a Thursday night.  The food was decent.  There was nothing incredibly delicious.  The server was attentive and cheerful.  \n\nGood place to get your fat kid on.  There's a suggested 2 hour limit on your feasting though.
yelp:test:10546.para:
The buffet in Vegas offers a reasonable price. On a Thursday night, the wait was no longer than 30 minutes. The food was satisfactory, though nothing stood out as exceptionally delicious. The service was prompt and the staff was friendly. 

It's a good spot for a family with a child who needs to eat a lot. However, there's a recommended 2-hour limit to ensure others can enjoy the buffet as well.

yelp:test:10605.para: This club has terrible customer service. We joined the "General Admission" line around 9 PM, expecting guaranteed entry, but the club didn't open until 10 PM. We waited in line until about 10:30, only to be told they were overbooked and wouldn't let us in until after midnight. That's ridiculous! yelp:test:10622.orig:
My goodness, I've basically grown-up (Club-wise) with Tao. I've probably been 10 or so times and I still believe it is one of the better clubs out there. BUT, it is not as amazing as it once was. 

Now, they close off the top-level on busy nights and that causes the other two levels to get ridiculously over-crowded (and alot of the crowdedness is just due to Tao's ever-increasing popularity). But, the decor at this place is the best i've seen and the girls are always ready to let-loose and have a good time (typically not the stuck up crowd). It also has a great mix of ethnicitiies...it has everything you could ever want in a club!

And the best part of all is this guy Taoboda! He can get your entire group past the line and in for free before 11 AND all the girls get free drinks from 10-11. What an awesome hook-up!

Taoboda alone keeps this place at a 4-star club for me despite its recent downfalls in other areas.
yelp:test:10622.para:
Wow, I've practically been a regular at Tao since I was a clubber (so to speak). I've been there about a dozen times and I still think it's one of the top clubs around. However, it's not as fantastic as it used to be.

On busy nights, they close off the top level, which leads to the other floors becoming extremely crowded (a lot of this is due to Tao's growing popularity). The decor here is top-notch, and the staff is always enthusiastic and ready to party (they're not the snobby type). The club also offers a great mix of cultures and has everything you'd want in a club.

The best part? Taoboda! He can get your whole group in for free before 11 PM and gives free drinks to all the girls from 10 to 11. That's a real plus!

Despite recent declines in other areas, Taoboda alone keeps Tao at a 4-star level for me.

yelp:test:10628.orig: Don't waste you're money on bottle service at Tao in a VIP section. I've seen better quality booth seating at a Denny's. $3000 to basically wait on line like everybody else. yelp:test:10628.para: Avoid spending your money on VIP bottle service at Tao; the booth seating quality is worse than what you'd find at Denny's. yelp:test:10643.para: I've enjoyed Tao's setup, but be cautious about securing a table there. We reserved one starting at $1500, right by the DJ booth. Several of our friends had to leave our table and hang out at the bar so we could accommodate a few female guests. Eventually, we ordered a third bottle, and the management stopped interfering.

yelp:test:10678.para:
I've visited SW about six times, and it remains my top steakhouse in Sin City. Each visit has been flawless from start to finish. Shall we proceed?

Note: Secure reservations well in advance! Requesting a table with a view of the Lake of Dreams is a good idea too. This place fills up quickly, and we've never gone without a reservation.

The service here is always exceptional, as you would expect from a Steve Wynn property. Water glasses are always refilled, and the table is kept tidy, whether it's plates, silverware, or even tiny sugar packet remnants.

Firstly, the bread! Oh, the bread! While I won't say much about the baguette-style bread, I must emphasize the cheddar-bacon rolls. They are pure delight, especially if you love salt. However, there's a downside... once, I hadn't eaten all day and gobbled up almost three rolls. I was full for the rest of the meal...oops.

The salads: I recommend splitting them with someone at your table.

yelp:test:10680.orig:

The waiting area is extremely small and there are only about 6 stools in the bar, so large-ish groups like ours (5 at the time, 7 in total), can find themselves standing around for quite a bit.

Not a major issue with SW but it just shows a lack of finesse, especially when paying a minimum of $54 for an a la carte steak.

yelp:test:10680.para:
During my recent conference in Vegas, my company took us to SW Steakhouse for dinner. Although the steaks were outstanding, the rest of the meal fell short of expectations.

The waiting area is quite cramped, with only six bar stools available. This made it challenging for our group of seven to find seating, and we ended up standing for a considerable time.

Upon being seated, we waited at least 15 minutes before being attended to, despite being ready to order. The wine recommended to us was merely acceptable and not particularly impressive. Moreover, they only had two bottles, forcing us to switch mid-meal. At any quality steakhouse, I've always been informed about low wine inventory before serving, especially for a group of five to seven. While this wasn't a significant issue at SW, it highlighted a lack of attention to detail, especially given the minimum $54 price for an a la carte steak.

Now, regarding the food...

The steaks were truly exceptional, as I mentioned. A fellow diner praised the veal chop as well. I opted for the smallest steak available, a 9oz filet cooked to perfection medium rare. Another diner had the same cut, and it was equally well-prepared.

yelp:test:10688.orig:
We like Mexican food, and this was only 'food' from the standpoint that we were no longer hungry afterwards, but unfortunately also regretful for having invested time in chewing... and waiting.  Allow me to explain... The trio of salsas brought out with tortillas as we were seated were all but tasteless.  The 'made just for you, table-side guacomole' was too salty, too much lime juice, not enough avocado - the ratios just weren't right, and this was sadly the theme of the meal.  The ceviche was OK, but was almost exclusively shrimp... where was the lobster that was also supposed to be in this pricey appetizer?  Obviously, ceviche needs acid to 'cook' the protein, but the acid wasn't balanced or complex.  So the tastes of salt and lime where first, middle and last.  We've had much better for much less cost in places less exotic than Las Vegas, such as Chicago. 

The considerable lag between tortillas and 'real food' was annoying and the music was loud.  The saturation of red in the decor was interesting from the outside but more gloomy than mood-setting once we were seated and the images on the video screens were jarring and did not contribute positively to enjoying food.

yelp:test:10688.para:
We found the Mexican food to be merely filling, leaving us unsatisfied and somewhat disappointed after the wait. Let me elaborate... The salsas served with tortillas upon our seating were lacking in flavor. The table-side guacamole, meant to be fresh and made just for us, was overly salty and acidic, with insufficient avocado. This pattern of subpar quality continued throughout the meal. The ceviche was acceptable but predominantly shrimp, with no trace of the lobster that was supposed to be included in the pricey appetizer. The acid used in the ceviche was unbalanced, dominating the taste with salt and lime. We've experienced much better value and quality in less exotic locations, like Chicago, for a similar price.

The delay between the tortillas and the main course was frustrating, and the music was too loud. The red decor, while eye-catching from the outside, felt gloomy once we were seated. The video screens displayed jarring images that detracted from the dining experience rather than enhancing it.

yelp:test:10700.orig:

yelp:test:10700.para:
This past weekend was my boyfriend's birthday, and we opted for a Vegas-style celebration. We arrived at the Palm on Friday and will discuss our experience there shortly. Patience, please.

On Saturday evening, we headed to the Ghost Bar, which is located an impressive 55 floors up. While it's not the place to let loose and dance, it does offer good music, a relaxing atmosphere, and plenty of attractive people to admire.

The bar is smaller than expected, but the decor and ambiance are outstanding. The view from 55 floors above the city's bright lights is truly unforgettable—it was more than just a view; it was an experience.

The drinks are pricey but potent, and the staff is friendly. However, the bouncers are quite intimidating. The crowd was mostly regular folks, but there were two guys who tried to hit on me despite my boyfriend being right there. Thankfully, that didn't last long. Overall, it was a great night!

If you're visiting Vegas, I strongly recommend checking out the Ghost Bar. Just ensure you have a

yelp:test:10703.orig:
This is why I liked Ghostbar, and why I would go back:

Bouncers, bartenders, and overall staff was friendly
The place was clean
Tolerable club music
Beautiful view
It was not over crowded 
It did not smell bad
The music was not so loud that my ears wanted to explode
No cover for hotel guests
Air conditioning 

This is what I deducted a star:

We had purchased a Travel Zoo coupon which included dinner to Simon, and VIP to either Ghostbar or the other club at the Palms. The person at the front of Ghostbar told us that if we chose to use our VIP bracelets, then we would get two free drinks. When we went up to the bar, the bartender told us that we did not get free drinks. It did not ruin my night, but if we knew we weren't going to get any perks from the VIP bracelets, we would have used them at another place. 

This place is having an identity crisis. Are you a lounge or a club?
yelp:test:10703.para:
I enjoyed Ghostbar and would revisit for these reasons:

The staff was welcoming, from bouncers to bartenders
The venue was kept clean
The music was tolerable
The view was stunning
It wasn't overcrowded
There was no unpleasant odor
The music volume was bearable
Hotel guests didn't need to pay a cover charge
Air conditioning was available

However, I deducted a star due to this experience:

We bought a Travel Zoo coupon that included dinner at Simon's and a VIP entry to either Ghostbar or another club at the Palms. The person at the front said we'd get two free drinks with our VIP bracelets. But when we got to the bar, the bartender said we wouldn't receive any free drinks. While it didn't spoil our night, we would have used the bracelets elsewhere if we knew we wouldn't get any perks. 

It seems Ghostbar is struggling to define its identity—should it be a lounge or a club?

yelp:test:10722.orig:
I liked this show a lot.  It was my second Cirque show and it was very good.  The story was easy to follow but the dudes helping before the show I could have done without.  I know they're there to help get you in the mood for the performance but I personally didn't care for them.  

As for the show, it was fun.  I really liked the wall scene and the thing with sand.  I thought the sand part was cute and gave you a break before they came back at you with more action.  Your heart can only beat so fast for so long.  

When I'm back in Vegas, I'll definitely be going to see another Cirque show.
yelp:test:10722.para:
I enjoyed this show quite a bit. It was my second Cirque performance, and it was excellent. The storyline was straightforward, but the pre-show antics weren't to my liking. While I understand they're meant to set the mood, I personally found them unnecessary. 

Regarding the show itself, it was entertaining. I particularly appreciated the wall scene and the segment involving sand. I thought the sand part was charming and provided a nice respite before the action intensified again. After all, your heart can only race so fast for so long.

If I return to Vegas, I'll definitely make sure to catch another Cirque show.

yelp:test:10804.para:
Had to give it a star due to some issues.

Pros: The rooms are spacious and fairly comfortable. I found the pillows to be too soft. The casino is decently sized and draws a lot of locals. It wasn't overly crowded and we actually won some money there. The food court was pleasant. In the morning, there was no wait at the Coffee Bean, and after midnight, Fatburger served fresh burgers without a crowd. The pool area was great and very clean. There’s a 21 and over pool that’s private with its own bar, about 20 lounge chairs, 10 cabanas, and a few pool beds. The main pool has a sand entry and a nice view of the strip.

Cons: The carpets, while looking clean, are actually very dirty. Avoid the China Spice Restaurant at all costs! On our first night, we tried this place with a $25 discount on food but only for $50 spent, but the discount didn’t apply to drinks with alcohol. We waited 20 minutes with only 5 tables open and one server working.

yelp:test:10807.orig:
No POOL ACCESS at a 4-star where you PAY A RESORT FEE! unbelievable!
Beautiful furnishings but the beach pool is shut down in 78 degree weather. Misery during a great long weekend holiday. ANd they have the nerve to charge a $27 RESORT FEE ON TOP OF YOUR HOTEL ROOM PRICE!!!!!!
Although very far from the strip, reserved the place for Valentines weekend because it was 4 star hotel. Even encouraged 3 other friends to join up! Very unfortunate that the hotel management has decided to NOT OPEN THE POOL so it sits there in all its tempting beauty with cabanas and waterfalls all around.

Also, it's not as quiet in the room as you would expect. I can hear people in the two neighboring rooms talking.
yelp:test:10807.para:
At a 4-star hotel where you pay a resort fee, there's no pool access—unbelievable! The rooms are beautifully furnished, but the beach pool is closed on a day when the temperature is a pleasant 78 degrees. This made for a miserable long weekend. They even have the audacity to charge a $27 resort fee on top of the room price!

I booked this place for Valentine's weekend, thinking it was a 4-star hotel, and even invited three friends to join us. It's unfortunate that the pool remains closed, despite the attractive cabanas and waterfalls surrounding it. Additionally, the rooms aren't as quiet as expected; I can hear the conversations from the neighboring rooms.

yelp:test:10822.orig:

yelp:test:10822.para:
On my birthday weekend in November, we stayed at Mandalay Bay in Vegas. Late Saturday night, we were hungry and sought a deli-style sandwich, which is rare to find. The concierge suggested a place, and I checked online; I decided to give it a try.

I arrived to find the place bustling with people, though there was a line, I managed to get to the take-out window. I ordered a roast beef sandwich with clam chowder on the side. The meal was quite expensive, around $15-20, for a sandwich, chips, and a small portion of soup, but in Vegas, prices are often higher.

After meeting up with my friends at the nearby yogurt and crepe place, I regretted not getting a crepe instead.

Opening my clam chowder, it looked like a mix of water, olive oil, alfredo sauce, and soggy celery. I couldn't even tell if there were clams in it; it was that bad! I had no idea clam chowder could be like minestrone! At the Red, White, & Blue, it was definitely a letdown.

yelp:test:10847.orig:
This place has a very versatile menu and every time I go the food is delicious.

There are two; one in the Venetian and one in the Palazzo. I think that the venetian location is more private and the tables aren't so close to each other compared to the Palazzo one.

As soon as you're seated you are brought a warm basket of bread and butter to hold you over while you browse the full menu. This place wont let you down and is a must try!
yelp:test:10847.para:
This establishment offers a diverse menu, and the food is always delightful whenever I visit. There are two locations: one in the Venetian and another in the Palazzo. I find the Venetian location to be more secluded, with tables spaced further apart than at the Palazzo location.

Upon being seated, you are promptly offered a warm basket of bread and butter to tide you over while you peruse the comprehensive menu. This restaurant consistently exceeds expectations and is definitely worth trying!

yelp:test:10855.orig:
Double Stuffed Potato Spring Rolls.... amazing!

The appetizers are some of my favorites and Nadia (I think) makes a mean Texas Tea. 

I have only ever sat at the bar, so I cannot comment on the dining areas, but usually it seems so fast paced and everyone on top of their game. 

Try out this cafe if you are in the neighborhood.
yelp:test:10855.para:
Double Stuffed Potato Spring Rolls... simply outstanding!

I'm a big fan of cafes, and this one inside the Palazzo is fantastic! The bar staff are not only hilarious but also very friendly. Alex, one of the bartenders, is particularly knowledgeable; everything he recommends from the menu is always delicious.

I adore the appetizers, and I believe Nadia makes a great Texas Tea. Since I've only ever sat at the bar, I can't speak to the dining areas, but the place usually feels fast-paced with everyone working efficiently.

If you're in the area, give this cafe a try.

yelp:test:10857.orig:
Been here more than once after a night out of drinking.. But now I can say I've been here sober and not so sober!

Quick seating, although it gets busy! Friendly staff & good for kids when the sun is still up. 

Like everyone says-- it IS like a Cheesecake Factory minus the cheesecake, but in my opinion and if I'm willing to make the drive out here, I like it better! 

This time around the better half and I had :
Blue Cheese Salad - not a blue cheese fan but this was good, could have a little less dressing
Calamari - FAVORITE! I liked the added fried zucchini and onions! 
Kobe Meatballs - big meatballs, juicy and tender meatballs! Not too much sauce, comes on a bed of creamy polenta.

I unfortunately could not have any of the pasta dish but it did look good! 

Must try if you're in the strip area!
yelp:test:10857.para:
I've visited this place multiple times after a night out, but now I've been here both sober and tipsy. Quick seating, though it can get crowded! The staff is friendly, and it's kid-friendly when it's still light outside.

It's similar to a Cheesecake Factory without the cheesecake, but in my opinion, it's better, especially if I'm willing to drive out here. This time, my partner and I enjoyed:

- Blue Cheese Salad - not a big fan of blue cheese, but it was tasty; could use a bit less dressing.
- Calamari - my favorite! I loved the added fried zucchini and onions.
- Kobe Meatballs - large, juicy, and tender meatballs! Not overly saucy, served on a bed of creamy polenta.

Unfortunately, I couldn't try the pasta dish, but it looked great! You should definitely give it a try if you're in the strip area.

yelp:test:10862.orig:
This is a really cute placeit's something different. 

I had the watermelon spritzer, very sweet, but good if you like watermelon. They refill it for you too

voodoo shrimp - i usually never eat shrimp, but our waitress recommend this so i had to try it. It was really good, jumbo size shrimp smothered with tasty seasoning over corn bread that melts in your mouth!

gumbo - its thick and gooey it was decent. Tasted way better with hot sauce :)

baby back ribs -  literally fell off the bone... it was delish! it also came with cold slaw, beans, and corn. mmMMm the corn was good up until i dropped it :( But my sweet server saw the whole entire incident and fired up a new one for me right away!

Lastly, we had the field of greens... the portion was smaller than the ribs, but that's okay. every bite was yum :)
yelp:test:10862.para:
This is a unique and charming spot. 

I tried the watermelon spritzer, which was quite sweet but enjoyable if you like watermelon. They keep it topped up for you.

The voodoo shrimp was a standout; I don't usually eat shrimp, but my server recommended it, and it was fantastic—jumbo shrimp covered in a delicious seasoning, served with cornbread that's melt-in-your-mouth good.

The gumbo was thick and gooey, and it was pretty good, especially when I added some hot sauce.

The baby back ribs were absolutely delicious, falling off the bone. They came with cold slaw, beans, and corn. The corn was great until I accidentally dropped a piece, but my attentive server quickly brought me a fresh one.

Finally, we had the field of greens, which had a smaller portion than the ribs, but each bite was delightful.

yelp:test:10866.orig: I've been to the House of Blues for a few concerts now, and there are plenty of other venues that offer a better sound quality, especially in Las Vegas. \nIf you have the opportunity to see a band at another venue, I highly recommend it. The sound quality is awful, so there will be a very low chance you'll understand anything coming out of the singers mouth. It ends up being just a muffle that fades into the rest of the band.
yelp:test:10866.para: I've attended several concerts at the House of Blues, but I've found that many other venues in Las Vegas provide superior sound quality. If you get the chance to see a performance elsewhere, I strongly advise it. The sound at the House of Blues is so poor that it's highly unlikely you'll be able to make out what the singers are saying; it comes across as a muffled blend with the rest of the music.

yelp:test:10878.orig: If you like good, fresh, sandwiches, then you have to try one here at Lee's. I think the bread is what really makes the difference, it is super fresh and would taste good all by itself! Its much cheaper than any other sandwich shop and definitely seems fresher and less assembly line. I think the only thing that can be hit or miss here is the service from time to time, but that is soon forgotten with a sniff of the fresh bread.  Yes they do only accept cash but that is as they say, to keep the prices down.  I usually order the ham and turkey club and a water and i get out of there for about 5 bucks.  I also love the fresh baked baguettes...so good!
yelp:test:10878.para: If you enjoy delicious, fresh sandwiches, you should definitely give Lee's a try. The bread is what truly sets them apart; it's incredibly fresh and would be tasty on its own! Their prices are much more affordable than other sandwich shops, and the freshness is evident, unlike the mass-produced variety. The service can sometimes be inconsistent, but that's quickly forgotten when you take a whiff of the fresh bread. They only accept cash to keep costs down. My usual order is the ham and turkey club with a water, and I can leave for around five dollars. I also adore their freshly baked baguettes—they're fantastic!

yelp:test:10882.orig:
This restaurant is located in the Chinese Cultural Center and was the one restaurant that I had not been to. So after some shopping at one of the shops, we stepped in to have dinner.

We stepped in and asked for a seat for two. We were seated immediately. The place was decorated nicely and a lady playing the piano made for great ambiance.

We looked at the menu briefly and ordered our drinks, an appetizer, a soup and two main dishes. The drinks came out promptly and so did the rest of the meal. My goodness everything we ordered was very tasty.

The waiter service itself however was not even close to the decor and food. He never introduced himself, and although he took our order, our food itself was brought out by a kitchen person.

After we ordered our waiter really never came back asking if we needed anything else, except to give us our check at the end and that was after the person I was dining with got up and asked a different waiter for it.

It's amazing how a place with great food, decor, and ambiance can mess it all up by crappy waiter service.
yelp:test:10882.para:
This restaurant, situated in the Chinese Cultural Center, was the last one I hadn't visited. After some shopping, we entered to dine. We were promptly seated for two. The interior was tastefully decorated, and the piano music added to the pleasant atmosphere.

We glanced through the menu, ordered drinks, an appetizer, a soup, and two main courses. Our drinks and food arrived quickly, and everything we ordered was delicious.

However, the service fell short of expectations. The waiter didn't introduce himself and, despite taking our order, our food was brought by a kitchen staff member. He didn't check in on us throughout the meal, only returning to give the bill when prompted by my dining companion.

It's surprising how a place with excellent food, decor, and ambiance can ruin the experience with poor service.

yelp:test:10889.orig: If you live near Khoury's this has got to be your place for craft brews and/or specialty wines. They have a great selection of common craft brews all the way to hard to find US craft and international craft brews. Wednesday nights they do a craft beer sip and share which usually has a food truck involved. I was a regular all last summer and it's incredibly fun and a great social event for local Vegas residents. Thursdays they do a wine tasting night, which I have yet to go to but I'm sure is equally as fun.\n\nThe best part about this place is that you can buy a delicious craft beer and enjoy it and discuss craft beer with other knowledgable people there. If you don't want to buy a bomber they also have a solid rotation of craft beers on tap. They recently also started filling growlers which is awesome. All the guys who work there are friendly and will give answer any questions you have or give you recommendations based on what you're in the mood for. Strongly recommend this place if you love craft beer.
yelp:test:10889.para:
If you're close to Khoury's, this is the ideal spot for craft brews and specialty wines. They offer a wide range of popular craft beers, along with harder-to-find US and international options. On Wednesdays, they host a craft beer sip and share event, often featuring a food truck. Last summer, I frequented this place regularly and found it to be a fantastic social event for locals. Thursdays are dedicated to wine tastings, though I haven't tried it yet, but it's sure to be just as enjoyable.

What makes this place special is that you can purchase a tasty craft beer, enjoy it, and engage in discussions with knowledgeable folks. Even if you don't want to buy a bomber, they have a good selection of craft beers on tap. They recently began filling growlers, which is a great addition. The staff is friendly and willing to answer any questions or offer recommendations based on your preferences. I highly recommend this place if you're a fan of craft beer.

yelp:test:10890.orig: I stopped by Tryst with two of my girlfriends in Sept. and we were afraid of the long lines that we were warned of from others. We got to Wynn super early at 8:45pm and no one was line for Tryst. The club didn't open until 11:00pm and we didn't have anything to do since the longest line that Saturday night was only 30 mins. The bouncer gave us free passes to get in for free which was cool. I think Tryst is overly hyped and not particularly special inside.
yelp:test:10890.para: In September, my two friends and I visited Tryst and were concerned about the long lines we'd heard about. We arrived at Wynn at 8:45 pm and found no one waiting for Tryst. The club didn't open until 11 pm, and since the longest line that night was just 30 minutes, we had some free time. The bouncer even offered us free entry, which was great. I believe Tryst is overrated and doesn't stand out much inside.

yelp:test:10891.orig: Yep...loved it.  One of my favorite clubs along wiht Body English in vegas.  The whole layout of this place is well thought out.  The waterfall is HUGE to the entire experience.  Makes it so much more refreshing and enjoyable.  We got a table outside near the waterfall and really had a good time.  It gave us the chance to get away from the crowd and have quality time drinking with friends and when we wanted to dance we could go inside easily.  \n\nOne other thing is the bottle service here is not like any other place we have seen.  They are extremely attentive and just go far and beyond what we would expect.  Definitely coming back.
yelp:test:10891.para:
Sure...I adored it. This club, along with Body English in Vegas, is one of my top picks. The design of the place is meticulously planned. The waterfall feature is exceptionally large and enhances the overall experience, making it more refreshing and enjoyable. We sat at an outdoor table near the waterfall and had a fantastic time. It allowed us to escape the crowd and enjoy quality time with friends, and when we wanted to dance, we could easily go inside. 

Another noteworthy aspect is the exceptional bottle service here. The staff is incredibly attentive and goes above and beyond our expectations. We definitely plan to return.

yelp:test:10896.orig: My girls and I had a lot of fun at Tryst.  Really like the outdoor/indoor set up.  Waterfall is nice.  Great music. Helps when you don't have to pay for any of your drinks:-)  I would go back next time I'm in Vegas.
yelp:test:10896.para: My friends and I enjoyed ourselves a great deal at Tryst. I appreciate the versatile indoor-outdoor layout. The waterfall feature is particularly appealing, and the music is excellent. It's especially enjoyable not having to pay for any drinks. I plan to return when I'm next in Vegas.

yelp:test:10909.orig: Not the best club in Vegas but it is definitely a great place party if there is a specific event going on there. It's not that big of a club but if you're looking for a great place to go clubbing then this is a good spot.
yelp:test:10909.para: While it may not be the top club in Vegas, it's still an excellent choice for a fun party if there's a special event. Although it's not a large venue, it's a solid option if you're in the mood for a lively clubbing experience.

yelp:test:10930.orig:
Love the ambiance of Okada, the fresh sushi, and tasty entrees don't hurt either! We got some sashimi and sushi specials both of which were delectable! The spicy tuna roll was definitely the best I've ever tasted. The sashimi melts in your mouth. Just thinking about them makes me want more! 

The service was fast and friendly.  

Love that you can see the fake waterfall from the window in the main dining room.  Nice for a date or intimate dinner. I would definitely recommend  Okada for sushi on the strip.
yelp:test:10930.para:
I adore the atmosphere at Okada, and the quality of the fresh sushi and delicious entrees is outstanding! We tried the sashimi and sushi specials, both of which were incredibly tasty. The spicy tuna roll was the standout for me, and the sashimi is so tender it practically melts in your mouth. Thinking about it makes me crave more!

The service was prompt and courteous. 

I also love that you can enjoy the artificial waterfall from the main dining room window, which adds a romantic touch. It’s perfect for a date or a private dinner. I highly recommend Okada for sushi on the strip.

yelp:test:10938.orig: I keep going back to VooDoo for the great views.  This time though my meal was also great.  Our server remembered us from a previous visit and was quite helpful.  The filet was excellent.  The wine selection is very good.\n\nThe one down side was the macaroni side.  It was less than impressive.  The mashed potato side made up for it though.
yelp:test:10938.para:
I frequently return to VooDoo for its stunning views, and this time, the meal was equally delightful. Our server recognized us from a prior visit and was very accommodating. The filet was outstanding, and the wine list is quite impressive. 

The downside was the macaroni dish, which was underwhelming. However, the mashed potatoes were a pleasant surprise and improved the overall experience.

yelp:test:10967.orig:
Raucous, loud, rock-n-roll watering hole: fuck yeah!

My exact recollection of my experience here is somewhat hazy; mostly all I can remember is having a blast.  I wound up at Hogs & Heifers with a fairly big group doing a downtown pub crawl.  It was kind of a relief to find a dark, dingy cave of a bar after all the lights and 'showiness' of the casinos.  

The place wasn't too crowded when we arrived, and there was some kick-ass music blasting out of a robust sound system.  I'm not usually one for dancing (in public, anyway)... well, what happens in Vegas stays in Vegas, right? :)
yelp:test:10967.para:
A lively, noisy rock bar: totally awesome!

My memory of this place is a bit fuzzy, but what I do recall is a lot of fun. I stumbled into Hogs & Heifers with a large group for a downtown pub crawl. It was a welcome change to find a dim, gritty bar after all the flashy casinos.

When we arrived, the place wasn't overly crowded, and the sound system was pumping out great music. Usually, I avoid dancing in public, but in Vegas, right? :D

yelp:test:10993.orig: I was so excited to try this place, such great reviews.  As soon as we got there the excitement turned to disappointment.  My husband and I decided on a last minute date night when I get off work.  I had been looking at this on yelp and it was on my list.  We went last night, Sunday, and got there about 8 pm (they closed at 9 pm).\n\nFirst we walked in, was not sure where to go since it was out first time.  Someone walked by and said the hostess will be back in a few minutes.  So we waited..and waited.  About 15 minutes later a hostess arrived.  We asked to be seated outside since it was beautiful out.  She was annoyed that the table she sat us at was directly against a bench which I kept hitting my elbow on.  We asked to move (there were a lot of tables) which annoyed her even more.  About 15 minutes later our server showed up (granted now the close in 30 minutes).  We asked for a cup of ice and lemons for our water multiple times...never saw those the whole meal.  She came to the table for our order and stated they only had 4 pizza's left so if we wanted pizza we needed to order immediately.  Since we had never been there, looking at the menu for 3-4 minutes was not enough time,
yelp:test:10993.para:
I was really looking forward to this place based on all the great reviews, but my excitement quickly turned to disappointment upon arrival. My husband and I planned a last-minute date night after my shift ended, and I had been eyeing this place on Yelp. We visited on Sunday around 8 pm, just before they closed at 9 pm.

When we entered, we weren't sure where to go since it was our first time there. A passerby mentioned the hostess would be back shortly. We waited, and waited—about 15 minutes later, a hostess finally appeared. We requested an outdoor table due to the nice weather, but she seemed annoyed that the table she seated us at was right next to a bench, which kept hitting my elbow. We asked to be moved to another table, which only made her more irritable. Our server arrived about 15 minutes later, with just 30 minutes left before closing. We repeatedly asked for ice and lemons for our water, but never received them. When she took our order, she mentioned they only had four pizzas left and urged us to order immediately. Given that we were new to the place, we needed more time to look at the menu, which took about 3-4 minutes.

yelp:test:11026.orig:

Can you give a place no stars? This place has HORRIBLE reviews of JUST the HOTEL, despite their so called ""Renovations"" , so beware! And I'm not even complaining about their Hotel! I was given tours of the property and what was ""coming"" and promised how awesome the new banquet rooms would be. My first mistake.
