They were normal, boring banquet rooms, and most of the area in them wasn't even NEW, including the carpet! If that wasn't enough of a joke, the two vendor companies the Plaza referred me to, to help decorate my event, were shockingly unprofessional. 
One, called Ltevention, never returned calls or emails over a one month p
yelp:test:11026.para:
Are you a BRIDE considering a wedding at this venue? STOP!

Just look at the hotel's reviews—it's got terrible ratings, and those so-called "renovations" haven't improved anything. Be cautious! And I'm not even upset about the hotel; this rant is about the EVENTS/WEDDING department. AVOID IT! I spent six months planning with Janeen and Tricia from the Plaza, getting tours of the property and hearing about the supposedly amazing new banquet rooms. That was my first mistake.

I was even assured that I'd get 2009 event pricing for my wedding due to the renovations, which led me to choose the Plaza. Months later, I reluctantly signed a contract and paid a $500 deposit. Then, I saw the "new" banquet rooms. They were just ordinary, unexciting rooms, and much of the area wasn't even newly renovated, including the carpet! To top it off, the two vendor companies the Plaza recommended for my event were shockingly unprofessional. One, Ltevention, didn't respond to any of my calls or emails for over a month.

yelp:test:11042.orig: If there was a negative stars for this I would give it....do NOT go for lunch. We were not greeted at the door at all and had to walk around the place just to find someone who worked there.... That should have been our first clue.....when the man did seat us he smelled so bad of Cologne that we almost left before we even ordered......2 more couples walked in and stood and waited for someone to notice them, but the waiter was too busy chatting it up with the cook to notice, and I certainly wasn't about to tell him he had customers.....not my job, sorry. The lunch was just meh....the soda was flat and tasted funny, and the cheese steak was substandard at best...... Maybe if there  is nobody at the door to greet you at what appears to be a nice place it will be the clue to just walk out......I won't be returning again.
yelp:test:11042.para: If there were negative stars available, I would definitely give them... absolutely avoid this place for lunch. We weren't greeted upon entering, and we had to wander around to find anyone working there—our first red flag. When we were finally seated, the waiter smelled strongly of cologne, which was so overpowering we almost left without ordering. Two other couples had to wait as the waiter was engrossed in conversation with the cook. I didn't feel it was my place to remind him of his duties. The lunch was lackluster; the soda was flat and tasted off, and the cheese steak was at best subpar. If you see no one at the door at what seems like a decent establishment, that might be your cue to leave. I won't be coming back.

yelp:test:11071.orig:
My douchebag radar was so far off the scale here I just shut it off completely. There's stairs ALL OVER the place, (I swear, some drunk chick in stilettos is going to fling herself down one of these one day) silly fog machines and unenthusiastic go-go dancers, with security guards standing watch at every doorway. Do you really need that much security? Eh, to be fair, I did witness some drama go down. 

I would hate to live in a world where I subscribed to the thought that Axis/Radius is THE hippest nightlife destination in the Phoenix metro area. Sadly, a lot of people seem to be trapped in this mindset. The patrons walk around in a zombie-like daze. In their intense social longing to ""be someone,"" or ""find someone"" they force themselves to frequent this club hoping to be seen by the right person, maybe get a snapshot on 944 or Dirty Scottsdale .com. It is true that this is quintessential Scottsdale, but it is not representative of the entire city's scene as a whole, as some sadly write it off as. 

Highlight: Dancing to ""Sandstorm.""
yelp:test:11071.para:
My douchebag detector was completely off here, so I turned it off entirely. The place is littered with stairs (I swear, a drunk chick in stilettos might tumble down one of them someday), there are silly fog machines, and unenthusiastic go-go dancers, with security guards stationed at every entrance. Is that really necessary? To be fair, I did see some drama unfold. 

I wouldn't want to live in a world where I believed Axis/Radius was the coolest nightlife spot in the Phoenix area. Sadly, many people seem stuck in this belief. The patrons move around like zombies, desperately trying to be seen or find someone, hoping to get noticed on 944 or Dirty Scottsdale. While it's quintessentially Scottsdale, it doesn't reflect the broader city scene, as some mistakenly assume. 

Highlight: Dancing to "Sandstorm."

yelp:test:11078.orig: OMG! sushi left on the counter for 30 minutes, then served to us as though it was just made freshly? i think not! the sea eel didn't even look suitable for a photograph, but not wanting to be fussy, i tried it, and quickly spit it out! this place is more of a 1 time visit. i've been several times, and still am not impressed. that was the last try, i hope to never be starved for sushi and stuck by that place again. the service sucks at the bar, it was the bartender who served up the sour sushi too! steer clear from here, you've neen yelped! oh and the big fish tank in the floor? its not all that. although the decor keeps bringing me back-it makes me forget all the previous visits-then i quickly remember when i'm waiting for the sushi.\n\none things fer sure, if ur looking for all those candy pushers, with the burned out Ed Hardy clothes, plastic booby flashing bleached blondes or euro-transplants looking to do anyone that will get them somewhere, well there you go....because its all there.
yelp:test:11078.para: Oh my gosh! Sushi left out for 30 minutes and then served as if it were freshly made? Absolutely not! The sea eel didn't even look appetizing enough for a photo, but I tried it anyway and had to spit it out quickly! This place is only worth one visit. Despite going several times, I remain unimpressed. That will be my last try; I hope I never find myself starved for sushi and forced to return there. The service at the bar is terrible, and it was the bartender who served the sour sushi. Stay away from here; you've been warned! And that big fish tank on the floor? It's not that impressive. Although the decor keeps drawing me back, it makes me forget about the previous visits until I'm reminded when waiting for the sushi. One thing is certain: if you're looking for a place filled with candy pushers, burned-out Ed Hardy-clad individuals, bleached blondes flashing booby traps, or Euro-transplants trying to hook anyone for their benefit, you'll find it there.

yelp:test:11097.orig:
So my boyfriend and I headed over to Sushi Mon on the recommendation of my friend [our mistake since that guy doesn't even eat raw fish] one day for lunch.  We both had gotten the All-You-Can-Eat lunch.  So now begins the critique:

The fish was not fresh.  Everything had this soggy texture that comes from defrosting.  I work at a restaurant so you can't fool me.  Although the portions were decent, everything that had some kind of sauce was over done.  Our soft shell crab had so much ponzo sauce, it became overly salty.  That's the typical way of getting a customer to fill up on water and have them stop ordering food.

Overall, this place wasn't as good as we expected but we still left with a full belly.
yelp:test:11097.para:
On a recent lunch outing, my partner and I visited Sushi Mon based on a friend's recommendation, which turned out to be a misstep since that person doesn't even consume raw fish. We both opted for the all-you-can-eat lunch special. Here’s our assessment:

The fish lacked freshness and had a soggy texture, indicative of being defrosted. Given my restaurant experience, it was easy to spot. While the portions were satisfactory, the items with sauces were overcooked. Our soft shell crab was drenched in ponzo sauce, making it excessively salty. This tactic is often used to encourage customers to drink more water and stop ordering food.

In summary, the experience didn’t meet our expectations, but we left feeling satisfied.

yelp:test:11141.orig:
Bomb. 

I overstuffed myself with the shrimp cocktails and almost went green. Otherwise, the meat, fruits, gelato, desserts and seafood was fan-freaking-tastic. 

Best part about it all was that everything came out fresh and warm. No leftovers here! Services were fantastic with friendly and fast working servers. Wait and price is worth it in my opinion.
yelp:test:11141.para:
Explosion. 

I ate too many shrimp cocktails and nearly felt queasy. However, the meat, fruits, gelato, desserts, and seafood were outstanding. The highlight was that everything was served fresh and warm, with no leftovers. The service was excellent, with attentive and swift servers. In my view, the wait and cost are well worth it.

yelp:test:11143.orig:
All I can say is it's the best buffet in Vegas. 

The amount of options you have to choose from can't be beat. And the food is restaurant quality. Anything you try there you are guaranteed to like. 
The only thing I wish they worked on is the dessert. It was Ok...Some of it appeared sophisticated but most of it was nothing special. Of course I'm not comparing Wynn's desserts to Hometown Buffet...I'm only comparing it to other buffets on the strip. 
They should look into what's offered at Paris if they want to steal all their customers :)
yelp:test:11143.para: I have to say, this is the top buffet in Vegas. The variety is unmatched, and the food is of restaurant caliber. Everything I tried was delicious. The only area that could use improvement is the dessert; it was just okay, with some items appearing fancy but most not standing out. When comparing to other strip buffets, though, it holds its own. If they want to really compete, they should take a look at what Paris is offering.

yelp:test:11153.orig:
I can't say enough good things about the Wynn buffet. The food was amazing, the casino and the buffet are beautiful, and the service was excellent. After a ten dollar tip it ended up costing us about $40 per person for the whole thing, but it was well worth the price.

The thing that makes this buffet stand out in my eyes is their ability to work with people like us with food sensetivites and special dietary needs. I haven't bothered going to a buffet since I was diagnosed gluten (celiac) and dairy intolerant over two years ago. I am extremely sensetive to even the smallest amounts of gluten or dairy, so a buffet didn't seem like a good idea. After reading a few reviews on a few blogs my fiance and I decided to give it a shot, and boy are we glad we did!! The chef came out and gave us a tour of the whole buffet, showing us what was safe and what was not. They had a LOT of options for us including several deserts (which pretty much never happens), all of which were delicious!

We are already talking about our next trip to Vegas just so we can go to this buffet again!!
yelp:test:11153.para:
I have nothing but praise for the Wynn buffet. The food was outstanding, and both the casino and the buffet are stunningly beautiful. The service was top-notch. After a ten-dollar tip, the total came to about $40 per person, but it was definitely worth every penny.

What sets this buffet apart for me is their accommodating approach to guests with dietary restrictions. Since being diagnosed with gluten and dairy intolerances over two years ago, I haven't ventured to a buffet due to my extreme sensitivity to even trace amounts of these allergens. My fiancé and I decided to give it a try after reading some positive reviews, and we are so glad we did! The chef personally showed us around the buffet, highlighting safe options and ensuring we had plenty of choices, including several desserts, which is rare for a buffet. Everything we tried was delicious!

We are already planning our next trip to Las Vegas just to return to this buffet!

yelp:test:11171.orig: Trendy but LOUD! I went for a bachelorette party and they were very accommodating with a set menu but the food was below par considering the prices. The yellowtail sashimi and sliders were good but my main entree, chilean sea bass, was horrible. Overall, I wasn't impressed.
yelp:test:11171.para: Trendy yet quite loud! For the bachelorette party, the venue was very accommodating with a set menu, but the food quality didn't meet expectations given the prices. The yellowtail sashimi and sliders were enjoyable, but my main dish, Chilean sea bass, was terrible. In summary, I wasn't satisfied with the experience.

yelp:test:11177.orig: I'd fly back to Vegas just for the Truffle pasta. It was a pasta of the day, and what a glorious, glorious day that was. Er, two days (it was THAT good). I cant even remember anything else we ate (it was all delish) because we were in a heavenly like, orgasmic state. We might not have even talked the entire meal, other than about how great the pasta was. It's very likely at the top of my last meal on earth list. I love you, truffle pasta. You are the pasta of my life.
yelp:test:11177.para: The Truffle pasta in Vegas was so amazing that I'd fly back just for it. It was a special dish of the day, and it was absolutely fantastic—two days weren't enough to enjoy it fully. I can barely recall anything else we ate because it was all delicious, and we were in a blissful, almost euphoric state. We probably didn't talk much during the meal, except about how wonderful the pasta was. It's almost certainly at the top of my list for my final meal. I adore you, truffle pasta. You are the pinnacle of my pasta experiences.

yelp:test:11180.orig:
I've hit FIX every time I've visited Vegas. It's an absolutely perfect go-to spot when hitting the Bellagio for same gambling. I've always sat in the bar/lounge area which is super duper for people watching. How do cowboys take themselves seriously and why do dudes from LA all wear shirts with dragons eating birds eating butterflies? But I digress...

Kobe Cheese Fries are a must. Had the beef carpacio on last visit and was some of the best I've had. Lobster tacos were good.. but they're cold (on purpose). Was expecting warm. Crab cake sliders wash everything down nicely.

Waitresses are top notch, grade A, government certified talent. Oh, and they're pretty good at serving things, too.
yelp:test:11180.para:
Every time I visit Vegas, I head to FIX, which is the ideal spot for gambling at the Bellagio. I usually sit in the bar/lounge area, which is fantastic for people-watching. Speaking of which, why do cowboys take themselves so seriously, and why do so many guys from LA wear shirts with dragons eating birds eating butterflies?

Kobe cheese fries are a must-try. The beef carpaccio from my last visit was among the best I've ever had. The lobster tacos were decent, though they were served cold (on purpose), which caught me off guard. The crab cake sliders were perfect for washing everything down.

The waitstaff at FIX is top-notch, grade A, and highly skilled. They excel at both their service and their appearance.

yelp:test:11189.orig: Abuelo's is OK. There is nothing fantastic about it. I ordered the Juarez. I asked that the cheese enchilada be beef instead. I was told it would be no problem. That did not happen. It came out cheese. I sat at the bar.  The bartender was nice. Run of the mill service. If you come here just know you're walking into a run of the mill Mexican restaurant.
yelp:test:11189.para: Abuelo's is just average. The Juarez I ordered was disappointing, as the cheese enchilada, which I requested to be made with beef, was served with just cheese. I sat at the bar, where the bartender was friendly, but the service was typical. If you visit, expect a standard Mexican restaurant experience.

yelp:test:11202.orig: I've only gone to the Capital Grille for work-sponsored lunches and dinners so it's easier for me to rank it higher since cost isn't really an issue. If I had to pay for it myself, it would end up as a more special occasion or i-need-a-pick-me-up-lunch type of place. I really like the Capital Grille because even though the focus is on higher end meat and seafood, the vegetarian options are particularly good which is hard to come by at most restaurants in the same category. The Cobb salad (you can get vegetarian) is great because it's big, filling, and fresh. The veggie plate you can special order is a perfect entree, and though it's basically just a combination of all the side veggie dishes I think the sum is definitely greater than the parts. There are buttery roasted mushrooms covered in garlic & rosemary & thyme, grilled asparagus, sauteed spinach, and roasted tomatoes that add a wonderful sweetness and acidity to the dish.
yelp:test:11202.para: When I've visited the Capital Grille, it's always been for work-related meals, which makes it easier for me to rate it higher, given the cost isn't a concern. If I were footing the bill, it would feel more like a special treat or a quick pick-me-up lunch. What I appreciate about the Capital Grille is that, despite its emphasis on premium meats and seafood, they offer excellent vegetarian options, which is rare in similar restaurants. The Cobb salad (which can be vegetarian) is fantastic—it's generous, satisfying, and fresh. The special-ordered veggie plate is a standout dish; while it's a mix of side dishes, the combination creates a harmonious and delicious meal. The menu includes buttery roasted mushrooms seasoned with garlic, rosemary, and thyme, grilled asparagus, sautéed spinach, and roasted tomatoes, all of which contribute a delightful sweetness and tanginess to the plate.

yelp:test:11223.orig:
I visited RA for the first time last week after a long day of shopping at Fashion Show and it was fantastic!  Got a whole array of different rolls to split amongst the group.  We kept it pretty simple with spicy tuna rolls, yellowtail and scallion rolls, philadelphia rolls and the crispy tuna rolls.  Delicious and super fresh fish!

Also, the sake bombs were really great here.  The prices were very reasonable and we even convinced the table next to us to join us in the fun.

The decor is clean and modern and the waitstaff is friendly and doesn't rush you to get out (even when's there's a line of people waiting).
yelp:test:11223.para:
Last week, after a long day of shopping at Fashion Show, I visited RA for the first time and had an amazing experience! We shared a variety of rolls, including spicy tuna, yellowtail and scallion, philadelphia, and crispy tuna. The food was delicious and the fish was incredibly fresh.

Additionally, the sake bombs were fantastic, and we even convinced the neighboring table to join in. The prices were very reasonable. The ambiance was clean and modern, and the staff was friendly without being pushy, even when there was a line of people waiting.

yelp:test:11233.orig:
RA, ha ha ha ha ok enough laughing lets talk about the restaurant this location was terrible. Upon approaching the restaurant I noticed that there was hardly anyone inside. Came up to the front door and I noticed like hundreds of greasy finger prints on there glass doors, oh well so they dont like to clean there glass windows, no biggy. 

We got seated pretty quickly being that there were very little people there that night. Ordered viva las Vegas and spicy tuna and a California roll, all were pretty terrible. We also ordered garlic lemon edamame and it was pretty good but there is a pit where all the juice and chili garlic all falls into and then you're forced to fish them out with some chopsticks. 

The service was ok, the waitress really never came back after she took our order. Some other girl brought out our sushi instead and that was about it, the next time we seen our waitress was when she brought us our check. Would I come back? heck no, this place sucked all around reason for the laughter, oh well at least I got a good laugh out of it.
yelp:test:11233.para:
RA, ha ha ha ha, okay, enough laughing. Let's discuss the restaurant. This location was really bad. When I arrived, there were almost no customers inside. The glass doors had countless greasy fingerprints, indicating poor cleaning habits. No big deal, I thought.

We were seated quickly due to the low number of patrons that night. We ordered Viva Las Vegas, spicy tuna, and a California roll, and all were quite disappointing. We also had garlic lemon edamame, which was decent, but there was a pit where all the juice and chili garlic collected, requiring us to use chopsticks to retrieve the edamame.

The service was mediocre; the waitress didn't return after taking our order. Another server brought out our sushi, and that was it. We didn't see the waitress again until she brought our bill. Would I return? Absolutely not; this place was terrible. The laughter was a result of the experience, but at least I got a good laugh out of it.

yelp:test:11240.orig:
If you ever come here you must sit outside and enjoy the poolside view, even if its a little hot, you wont reget it.

My boyfriend and I came for lunch after checking into encore. We ordered the organix mix salad, and beef sliders, truffle fries.
 The food was delicious. If you get the salad, there is no need to add meat, because honestly they dont give you that much for the extra price and the salad itself is savory. 

The sliders were good, typical sliders nothing really special about them, I guess you're better off ordering a burger for the same price as the sliders.

OMGOSH the truffle fries were SO GOOd!!! Definitely would order these again! There were freshly made a d had truffle sauce and cheese over it. So bad for you but ooooo so good.

Over all the prices seemed a little steep, but it is vegas so what do you expect. The serve was good, they seemed really busy but they were attentive.
yelp:test:11240.para:
If you visit, you should definitely sit outside to enjoy the poolside view, even if it's a bit warm; you won't regret it.

My boyfriend and I dined at Encore after checking in. We had the Organix mix salad, beef sliders, and truffle fries. The food was fantastic. For the salad, there's no need to add meat since the portion is generous and the salad itself is quite flavorful.

The sliders were decent but not exceptional; they might be better replaced with a burger for the same price. 

Oh my goodness, the truffle fries were absolutely delicious! I'd definitely order them again. They were freshly made and topped with truffle sauce and cheese. They were indulgent but oh-so-tasty.

Overall, the prices felt a bit high, but that's to be expected in Vegas. The service was good; despite being busy, the staff was attentive.

yelp:test:11258.orig: Disappointed that I paid nearly twice as much when I went here as compared to my local CVS.  I know it's close to Hard Rock so they are targeting tourists but had to call corporate and send in my receipt and the latest ad so they could credit me the over charge.  I'll drive a few miles to find a CVS that charges the same price as their other stores.
yelp:test:11258.para: I was disappointed to find that the prices here were nearly double what I pay at my local CVS. Although I understand it's near Hard Rock and aimed at tourists, I had to contact corporate and submit my receipt and the current ad to get the overcharge refunded. I will go out of my way to visit a CVS that matches their other store prices.

yelp:test:11264.orig: I wish I would've read the reviews. This place is over priced. The food is Dennys status. I will never come here again.
yelp:test:11264.para: I regret not checking the reviews beforehand. The prices are too high, and the food quality is just like Dennys. I definitely won't be returning.

yelp:test:11269.orig:
I was starving on a Sunday night, and everything else at TI was closed.... so this place was my only option.

The night before, I had a carrot cake from here. It was alright, but I expected something better for a $7 carrot cake. The desserts at the Aria and Bellagio brunch buffet tasted much better than the carrot cake.

Anyways, I ordered a french onion soup and my boyfriend order a mango smoothie. It took half an hour for the soup to come out, and they still did not bring out the mango smoothie... My boyfriend asked to cancel the smoothie and the waiter said ""it is done, we are looking for a glass for it."" My boyfriend and I were confused.... is it that hard to get a glass? in a casino? where drinks are served EVERYWHERE?

one star for the french onion soup... it was okay, a little bit too salty though.
yelp:test:11269.para:
On a Sunday night, I was very hungry, and most places at TI were closed, leaving this spot as my sole choice.

The day before, I tried their carrot cake, which was decent but didn't meet my expectations for a $7 cake. The desserts at the Aria and Bellagio brunch buffet were much more appealing.

Moving on, I ordered French onion soup, and my boyfriend got a mango smoothie. The soup took about half an hour to arrive, and the mango smoothie never came. My boyfriend asked to cancel the smoothie, and the waiter replied that it was ready but they were searching for a glass. We were puzzled; isn't it easy to get a glass in a casino where drinks are served everywhere?

The French onion soup got one star—it was okay, though a bit too salty.

yelp:test:11279.orig:
Extremely overrated and not impressive, at all. 

I went here for a business lunch and I arrived a bit early. The hostesses were very rude, rather than nicely say we're not open yet, they had an attitude that was like go the **** away. Not a good start. 

When I finally get in I head to the back where yes, they have a screen setup and a sound system. But the projector is being leveled by paper towels and was amateurish at best. And the room we were in needed paint. Seriously, when you take a look around the podium was chipped, the walls had chips, and I'm thinking for a place overlooking Las Vegas Blvd that the experience was downgraded. It may have been classy a while back, but the management team needs to consider investing in a little bit of paint. 

Then we get to the wobbly tables, and the family style food that was brought out. Family style might work in Italy but this is America, and to me family style is a masquerade for a kitchen that is too slow or chokes at cranking out high volume high quality plates. In this case about the only thing good was the Caesar salad as it's hard to muck up a Caesar salad. But the rest of the food? Truly unmemorable. If I was a tourist a
yelp:test:11279.para:
This place is highly overhyped and fails to impress in any way. I arrived early for a business lunch and was greeted by rude hostesses who acted as if I was bothering them. That was a poor first impression.

Once inside, I noticed they had a screen and sound system, but the projector was poorly set up with paper towels and looked very amateur. The room needed a fresh coat of paint; the podium was chipped, and the walls had cracks. For a venue with a view of Las Vegas Blvd, the experience felt outdated. It might have been elegant in the past, but the management needs to invest in some basic improvements.

The tables were wobbly, and the family-style food was brought out. While family-style dining works in some cultures, in America, it often suggests a kitchen struggling to keep up with demand. The Caesar salad was the only standout, but the rest of the food was forgettable. If I were a tourist, I wouldn't recommend this place.

yelp:test:11284.orig:
After a long and tiring day at Magic tradeshow, the team came here to feast! I was pretty hyped since it was my first time. The 5 of us ordered the classic family style which was I believe $35 a person. Not that cheap, but do-able.

Service was utterly non-existent. Food took forever inbetween servings, we're talking about 20-25 min inbetween each dish...even appetizers..

That's pretty damn bad. As you could expect, we got full just sitting there, so had so much food non taken advantage of.

Maggiano's...not a good way to treat the customers. 

If I come back..and that's a pretty strong IF, I would hope they actually serve our table.

Meh.

-Goodfood.LA
yelp:test:11284.para:
After a long, exhausting day at the Magic tradeshow, the team headed here to enjoy a meal. It was my first time, and I was quite excited. We opted for the classic family-style menu, which came to about $35 per person. It wasn't the most affordable choice, but it was manageable.

The service was incredibly poor. There was a long wait between courses—around 20 to 25 minutes between each dish, even for appetizers. This was quite disappointing. We ended up getting full just waiting, so we had to leave a lot of food uneaten.

Maggiano's clearly isn't known for its customer service. If I return, which is unlikely, I hope they actually attend to our table.

Meh.

-Goodfood.LA

yelp:test:11300.orig: $30 for adults even though the sign outside says $21.99. This price also includes bottomless mimosas. The line is never long and you pay through a machine to get in.\n\nThe best items in the meat section were the prime rib, bacon, and bacon bits. The best desert item was carrot cake. Don't get anything red velvet-flavored. The best breakfast item was egg florentine that gushes with butter.
yelp:test:11300.para:
The price for adults is $30, despite the sign advertising $21.99; this fee comes with unlimited mimosas. There's never a long wait, and you pay via a machine to enter. 

Among the meats, the prime rib, bacon, and bacon bits stood out as the best choices. For desserts, carrot cake was the top pick, while you should avoid anything red velvet-flavored. The egg florentine, drenched in butter, was the standout breakfast item.

yelp:test:11305.orig:
I wanted to eat here because I have always heard the Rio had a great buffet...

I wish I had not wasted my time. 

I waited in line for about an hour just to pay, then another 10 minutes to be seated. 

They provided no way to crack the crab and I ended up hurting my fingers. The rest of the food tasted pretty much like cafeteria food. For 40 bucks a person, I feel is was entirely not worth it. Plus the Rio is really run down looking so I didn't even enjoy hanging around after eating.
yelp:test:11305.para: I had high hopes for the Rio's buffet based on what I'd heard, but I regret spending so much time there. The wait to pay was around an hour, and then another 10 minutes to get a table. There was no assistance in cracking the crab, which resulted in me injuring my fingers. The food mostly tasted like what you'd find in a school cafeteria. At $40 per person, it felt like a poor investment. Additionally, the restaurant's rundown appearance made the experience even less enjoyable.

yelp:test:11308.orig: Okay I've been to a few buffets in Vegas and I never thought carnival would be one of the ones I would visit off the strip ??? It was good for the price and I tried most of the different selections and to my surprise it was all good !!! I would recommend a visit off the strip and come to Rio you'll be happy ;) and you'll save some cash $$$$$$$$
yelp:test:11308.para: I've visited a few buffets in Vegas, and I never imagined Carnival would be one of them off the strip. It was a pleasant surprise; it was worth the price, and I sampled most of the options—each one was delightful! I'd suggest checking out a buffet off the strip, specifically at Rio; you won't regret it and you'll save some money too. 😊 $$$

yelp:test:11351.orig: Ugh!  I thought maybe I should try this place again before I slam it on Yelp, but after reading some of the other one- and two-star reviews, I realize I'm not nuts.  And there is no way I'm going to wait for hours to give this place another chance.  If you want to wait in line for two hours and then receive a cup of grease along with your hash browns and eggs, then Matt's is the place for you.  Disgusting!  Not to mention the bathroom is next door in a hotel room.
yelp:test:11351.para: Ugh! I considered giving this place another shot before leaving a negative review on Yelp, but after reading some of the other one- and two-star reviews, I see I’m not the only one disappointed. I definitely won’t wait for hours to try again. If you’re willing to stand in line for two hours just to get a greasy cup of coffee with your hash browns and eggs, then Matt's is your place. The food is awful, and to top it off, the bathroom is in a hotel room next door.

yelp:test:11371.orig: i have eten at Sierra Bonita several times.  The food is ALWAYS consistent, and some of the best eating in Phoenix.  The atmosphere is amazing and service is always top notch.  SB has figured out how to be a great neighborhood restaurant with world class food.  The style is southwestern with Mexico City influences - truly amazing.
yelp:test:11371.para: I've dined at Sierra Bonita multiple times, and the food remains consistently excellent, often ranking among the best in Phoenix. The ambiance is fantastic, and the service is always top-tier. Sierra Bonita has mastered the art of being a superb neighborhood restaurant while offering world-class cuisine. Their style blends southwestern flavors with Mexico City influences, creating a truly remarkable dining experience.

yelp:test:11440.orig: I will not be back to this restaurant. I placed an order for pickup last Thursday for myself and a co-worker. I had the small jerk meal and my co-worker had a side of collard greens. The chicken was hard, dry and cold. It wasn't fresh.  It was pulled from the fridge and put in the microwave. The beans were hard and rice chewy. The collard greens were bland. Very disappointing. I will not be back.
yelp:test:11440.para: I won't return to this restaurant. Last Thursday, I ordered a small jerk meal for myself and a side of collard greens for my colleague. The chicken was tough, dry, and cold; it seemed not fresh, likely pulled from the fridge and microwaved. The beans were tough, and the rice was chewy. The collard greens lacked flavor. Overall, it was very disappointing, and I have no intention of visiting again.

yelp:test:11451.orig: I used to come here all the time and I made sure I always made it here when I came to Las Vegas. However, on my most recent visit, the food was just not good. The pastas were bland and the crepes were only as good as one you can get at ihop. On a brighter note, the coq au vin was quite good as well as the prime rib. I probably won't come back as there are so many better buffet options here.
yelp:test:11451.para: I frequented this place regularly whenever I visited Las Vegas, but during my last trip, the food quality declined. The pastas were tasteless, and the crepes were no better than those at IHOP. On the positive side, the coq au vin and prime rib were delicious. Given the abundance of superior buffet choices, I doubt I'll return.

yelp:test:11529.orig:
Yuck!  I can not believe this place has got some good reviews.  I was in Vegas 3 weeks ago, went to the Tao.  The alcohol in my stomach was feeling lonely so we went to Noodle Asia after leaving the club at around 12:30AM on a Saturday night.  On a busy night, I would imagine a full staff of waiters and cooks... Not this night, 2 waiters, 2 cooks and 1 hostess.  We had two couples ahead of us in line to be seated.  
Wait time for a table- 50 minutes.  
Time after ordering our food until it arrived to our table- 45 minutes.  
Time to eat-5 minutes flat.  
Time it took for the waiter to take to print out our check- 15 minutes.    
The soup I ordered tasted like dish wash water.  
Service-  abrupt/borderline rude

Next time, I'll skip this joint and opt for room service.
yelp:test:11529.para:
Ugh! I can't believe this place has some positive reviews. I visited Tao in Vegas three weeks ago and, after leaving the club around 12:30 AM on a Saturday, we decided to go to Noodle Asia. On a busy night, I expected a full staff, but there were only two waiters, two cooks, and one hostess. We had two other couples waiting to be seated. 

We waited 50 minutes for a table, 45 minutes for our food to arrive, 5 minutes to eat, and 15 minutes for the waiter to print our check. The soup I ordered tasted like dishwater. The service was abrupt and almost rude.

Next time, I'll opt for room service instead.

yelp:test:11535.orig:
I think the MSG has f*#ked with my head.  Six visits.  Why?

Being Asian, I'm insulted that the Venetian would attempt to placate me with this mediocre excuse for a Chinese restaurant sandwiched between the poker tourney area, sports book, and restroom hall.

KISS (Keep It Simple Stupid) review:

Fried rice:  extremely oily and packed with MSG.
Dim sum: nothing special except the price.  3x what you would pay in your local Chinatown.
Noodle soups: correctly made, loaded with MSG, very little toppings, expensive.
Wok tossed noodles: should be tossed out.  Extremely oily and salty from the MSG.

To add further insult, they charge you for every day quality tea.

We all know, too much oil = restroom.  Too much MSG = lots of water = restroom.  Not a smart way for a casino to do business.  But what do I know, I'm still in my MSG coma.
yelp:test:11535.para:
I believe MSG has really messed with my perception. Six visits later, I’m puzzled as to why.

As an Asian, I find it offensive that the Venetian tries to appease me with this subpar Chinese restaurant, situated between the poker tournament area, sports book, and restroom hall.

Here’s a straightforward review:

Fried rice: overly greasy and MSG-laden.
Dim sum: not impressive, just overpriced—three times what you’d pay in your local Chinatown.
Noodle soups: properly prepared, but MSG-dense, with minimal toppings and high prices.
Wok-tossed noodles: should be discarded; excessively greasy and salty from MSG.

To compound the insult, they even charge for basic quality tea.
Too much oil means more trips to the restroom, and excessive MSG leads to lots of water intake. It’s not a smart business strategy. But then again, I’m still in my MSG-induced fog.

yelp:test:11546.orig: What an amazing display of inept service.  With some difficulty, we ordered glasses of prosecco to enjoy before dinner (The waiter did not offer to take drink orders or provide us with a by-the glass menu). The prosecco failed to arrive until well after our salads, which appeared almost instantaneously.  We had only taken a few bites of our salad, and sips of our prosecco, when the entrees arrived.  Rather than returning them to the kitchen, the waiter pressured us to relinquish our less than half-eaten salads. We didn't put up too much of a fight as the caesar salad was not particularly enticing.  RIght on the waiter's heels, the sommelier appeared with the nice bottle of chardonnay that we had ordered.  It was completely unchilled. Rather than refusing it as we should have, we allowed him to talk us into pouring a small sip with the promise that he would rapidly chill the remainder.  At that point, the waiter, sommelier, and our bottle of chardonnay disappeared into oblivion while we finished our entrees, sans wine.  Only well after we had finished picking at our entrees did the waiter reappear. We had to ask him to please fetch our wine, which he did unapologetically. As you can
yelp:test:11546.para: What a disappointing service experience we had. We struggled to place our order for prosecco to enjoy before dinner (the waiter didn't offer to take our drink orders or provide a by-the-glass menu). The prosecco arrived long after our salads, which were served almost immediately. We had barely started our salads and sipped on our prosecco when our main courses arrived. Instead of sending back the partially eaten salads, the waiter urged us to finish them. We didn't resist much, as the Caesar salad wasn't very appealing. Shortly after, the sommelier arrived with the chardonnay we had ordered, but it was completely unchilled. Rather than declining it, we let him talk us into tasting a small amount, promising he would quickly chill the rest. At that moment, the waiter, sommelier, and our wine disappeared, leaving us to finish our meals without any wine. It wasn't until we had almost finished our main courses that the waiter returned, and we had to ask him to bring our wine, which he did without an apology.

yelp:test:11556.orig:
only came here due to starvation after being on the road for 3 hour. also needed a decently nice and quick way (we were staying in Paris) to get some food in the system before the drinking in Vegas begins.

the good:
1. the first bite of my triple decker sandwich since i was starving. after a while it just tasted like any other club sandwich ive had. but i did think it was cool there was a sword toothpick to keep my sandwich together.
2. the waiter was always cheerful.
3. split checks

the average:
the french fries. they would have been much better if they were hot.

the bad:
1. there was line outside even though the restaurant was half full. this is as optimistic as i will be.
2. the service. had to flag down the waiter to order food. if you have us waiting out there im sure we'll be ready to order by the time we sit down. also took forever to get our food.
3. must ask for bread if you are ordering sandwiches/burgers. for the record the bread is ok. would have been better if they were warm.
4. the water tasted very ""tappy""
5. the waiter asked us to pay at the counter instead of him taking our checks.
yelp:test:11556.para:
I only visited this place due to hunger after being on the road for three hours, and we were in Paris. We needed to eat before heading to Vegas to drink. 

Pros:
1. The first bite of my triple-decker sandwich was satisfying given my hunger, though it eventually tasted like any other club sandwich. I found it neat that there was a sword toothpick to hold it together.
2. The waiter was consistently cheerful.
3. Splitting the bill was convenient.

Averages:
The fries could have been much better if they were served hot.

Cons:
1. Despite the restaurant being only half full, there was a line outside. This is the most optimistic thing I can say.
2. Service was slow; we had to call the waiter to place our order. We were waiting outside and likely would have been ready to order by the time we sat down. Our food took a long time to arrive.
3. We had to ask for bread if ordering sandwiches or burgers. The bread was okay but would have been better if it were warm.
4. The water tasted very "tappy."
5. The waiter asked us to pay at the counter instead of bringing our checks to us.

yelp:test:11603.orig:
Absolutely horrible! I took my boss there along with several clients and couldn't have been more disappointed. Background, I've been there a few times and been happy but my first time back in about 2 years.

The guy flipping bottles was breaking them everywhere and appeared to be whacked out on meth, I'm being serious. Then he auctioned off the drink he made for $50, are you kidding me?!?! He wasn't even adding the ingredients while performing and would just randomly pour something in a metal bar cup and then shook it up and took forever to try to rack up his ""auction"" price.

Honestly it was a joke and we left after one drink. Sad, depressing and made you have an uncomfortable feeling.
yelp:test:11603.para:
Absolutely terrible! I brought my boss and some clients there, and I was thoroughly disappointed. I had visited a few times before and enjoyed it, but this was my first return in about two years.

The bottle flipper was clearly under the influence, breaking bottles all over the place. He was auctioning a drink for $50, which seemed outrageous. He wasn't even adding the ingredients during the performance; he would just pour something into a metal cup, shake it, and take forever to build up the "auction" price.

It was a complete joke, and we left after just one drink. The experience was sad, depressing, and left us feeling uncomfortable.

yelp:test:11606.orig:
Boring... Perhaps this place is jumping at times other than when we visited but I was sorely under impressed with this place.

The food was average and nothing really stood out. And hell, all the drinks are overly expensive. $9.50 for a drink the size of a small styrofoam cup? This is Vegas right?

Anyways, the experience I'm sure is greater when its overly packed and has more going on. Perhaps if people are drunk enough when they arrive, it will mask skimp and over priced drinks, and the bland atmosphere during its off peak times.
yelp:test:11606.para:
Not very exciting... It seems like this place might be lively at other times, but I found it quite disappointing during our visit. The food was just okay, with nothing particularly impressive. Moreover, the drinks were outrageously priced—$9.50 for a small drink? This is Vegas, after all.

Surely, the experience would be better when it's bustling and more active. Maybe if people are sufficiently tipsy upon arrival, they might overlook the mediocre drinks and the dull ambiance during slower periods.

yelp:test:11610.orig: Use the coupon or else!\n Service was slow even in the low season of November ... I shutter to think how it would be in summer with the pool open and not half full of diners . \nI  have  had  better .
yelp:test:11610.para: Use the coupon, or the experience will be disappointing! The service was sluggish even during the slower month of November... Just imagine how bad it could get in the summer when the pool is bustling and not short of customers. I've had much better dining experiences elsewhere.

yelp:test:11616.orig: It's a win when you see your best friend get a grown man's ass rubbed in her face. Then have her face shoved towards his crotch. \n\nI HAVE NEVER LAUGHED SO HARD IN MY LIFE. IT WAS TOO MUCH FUN!
yelp:test:11616.para: It's such a victory to witness your best friend humiliating a grown man by rubbing his face in it and then pushing her face towards his crotch. I HAVE NEVER LAUGHED SO HARD IN MY LIFE. IT WAS ABSOLUTELY INCREDIBLY FUN!

yelp:test:11639.orig:
Came here before goin to Lights in Mandalay Bay and utilized a $50 Restaurants.com gift certificale (Totally Worth it, because if we had to pay full price, this review would be a lot lower)

That being said, the food was fine, nothing really blew us a way. We tried the Burger, Fried Trufffle Mac and Cheese, the Filet Mignon and Foie Gras. All were standard and not really worth much hype.

We even got a free dessert which was nice, it was a chocolate pudding thing with passion fruit on top but the thing was, the passion fruit on top was DISGUSTING. Who thought it was a good idea to pair those two because it was TERRIBLE. They should just QUIT AND GO HOME. Because it was TERRIBLE.

That being said, the bread was good even though it cost AN ADDITIONAL CHARGE AND..BTW...TAKES 30-40 MINUTES TO COME OUT. We got the bread after we got our food. Who does that?

In any case, will probably not revisit. TOTALLY NOT WORTH THE HYPE.
yelp:test:11639.para:
Visited this place before heading to Lights at Mandalay Bay and used a $50 Restaurants.com gift certificate (Definitely worth it, as the full price would have made this review much less favorable)

To be clear, the food was decent but nothing exceptional. We ordered the burger, fried truffle mac and cheese, filet mignon, and foie gras. All were typical and didn't live up to the hype.

We also received a complimentary dessert, a chocolate pudding with passion fruit on top. However, the passion fruit was awful, making the dessert a disaster. It was such a bad combination that it was truly terrible.

The bread was good, though it came with an extra charge and took 30-40 minutes to arrive. We got it after our main courses.

Overall, we probably won't return. This place is totally not worth the buzz.

yelp:test:11667.orig:
Was a stayin' at the Red Rock herself. Decided that BBQ was what our tummy wanted. It was busy, but not BIZEE. Our poor waitress had at least 7 tables (I don't know if that is normal, or not, but she was BIZEE). 
-1 star for the noise level
- 1 star b/c the beer ordered at the beginning of our meal got there after our entrees
- 1 star due to the noise level (LOUD!)
-1 star due to food quality: cole slaw was tasteless, beans tasted like refried beans (if I wanted refried, I woulda gone Mexican, I wanted BBQ/baked beans). The ribs were okay, little dry. Their BBQ sauce, though is yellow and thin and they didn't provide any extra for us.

The only things I enjoyed were:
1. the sweet iced tea (the beer wasn't for me)
2. the thick cut (Texas toast size) bread with butter. It was yummy and I ate 2 pieces to myself...
yelp:test:11667.para:
She was the one staying at the Red Rock and opted for BBQ to satisfy her appetite. The place was bustling, yet not overly chaotic. Our server managed at least seven tables, which seemed quite a challenge (I’m not sure if that’s usual, but she handled it with BIZEE efficiency).

We deducted one star for the noise level, another for the beer arriving after our main courses, and yet another for the excessive noise (it was really loud!). The food quality also took a hit; the coleslaw lacked flavor, and the beans tasted like refried beans (if I wanted that, I’d have gone Mexican; I was craving BBQ or baked beans). The ribs were decent but a bit dry. Their BBQ sauce was yellow and thin, and they didn’t offer any extra.

The only positives were the sweet iced tea (I didn’t enjoy the beer) and the thick, buttery bread, which I savored, eating two pieces on my own.

yelp:test:11687.orig: Love this place food is delicious
yelp:test:11687.para: I really enjoy this spot; the food is fantastic.

yelp:test:11733.orig: So sad with such good reviews I recently went to carnegie's and  ordered a turkey sandwich which was way over priced ( can you say price gouging ) 2.00 for cheese and 1.00 for veggies on a $ 19.99 dollar sandwich fries and a sandwich was $28.00 dollars not to mention they give you a packet of mustard instead of them making the sandwich ..... I will NEVER  return........ It wasn't worth it !
yelp:test:11733.para: I'm so disappointed despite all the positive reviews I read about Carnegie's. I ordered a turkey sandwich that was extremely overpriced—$2.00 for cheese and $1.00 for veggies on a sandwich that costs $19.99. The fries and sandwich together came to $28.00. They even gave me a packet of mustard instead of making the sandwich fresh. I definitely won't be going back; it wasn't worth the price!

We then had to wait 30 minutes for a server to come to us. I had to stand up and walk to the hostess and ask her to send a server to our table. He got us the remaining waters and then we had to wait another 20 minutes before we even placed our order. The table of 6 next to us arrived after, ate, and paid before we even got our food. I complained to the manager, who then sent the waiter over again. The manager told the waiter we complained, in our presence. The waiter came over and instead of apologizing, argued with us that he had come over shortly after our whole party had arrived. We were all taken aback that not only did the manager tell the waiter of our complaint in front of us while we were ea
yelp:test:11736.para: I visited this place three times, twice for takeout and once for dining in. Based purely on the takeout experience, it would have rated 4-5 stars. The food was excellent, with generous portions, and they operate 24/7. The delivery was also quick, even at 3 AM. However, during our last visit for lunch with eight people, we were seated right away despite only four of us being present. The remaining four arrived less than five minutes later, but we only received five waters when we asked for eight. We had to wait 30 minutes for a server to attend to us. I had to go to the hostess to request a server, who then brought us the remaining waters. We then waited another 20 minutes before placing our order. The table of six next to us arrived later, ate, and paid before we even got our food. I complained to the manager, who then sent the waiter back. The manager told the waiter about our complaint in front of us, and instead of apologizing, the waiter argued that he had come over shortly after our entire party arrived. We were surprised that the manager disclosed our complaint to the waiter in our presence.

of course, me and my friend (being girls) got in with no wait. . .

yelp:test:11747.para: I went with my boyfriend and another couple. My friend and I, being girls, didn't have to wait to get in, but the guys had to push their way through. The bouncers seemed to prioritize attractive people. It's always tough for guys to enter clubs in Vegas. This particular club was terrible. However, I had a good time thanks to CJ, who's the best! The drinks were extremely pricey. We visited on a Saturday night but only stayed for about an hour. The dance floor was tiny and quickly became overcrowded. The only reason it got one star was because the decor was impressive.

yelp:test:11776.orig: Rob and Heidi are my servers and they are Awesome! 6 out of five stars for sure. The 10 oz. flat iron was so good and the service was great. Not to mention the architecture in the restaurant was really cool. I recommend this place if you go to Vegas regardless of if you are staying in Mirage or not
yelp:test:11776.para: Rob and Heidi are my servers, and they are outstanding! They definitely deserve five stars. The 10 oz. flat iron steak was exceptional, and the service was top-notch. Additionally, the restaurant's architecture was really impressive. I highly recommend this place to anyone visiting Vegas, whether or not you're staying at the Mirage.

yelp:test:11778.orig:
While I was here for a CMYE (where they served some delicious fare) I also took some time and carried out from Mama Fu's. 

Inside Mama's is bright and colorful with ample table space and even a comfy booth if you're waiting for your food to go. Employees are all very sweet, smiley and helpful. It's especially nice to see how many regulars they have here! I noticed the manager greeting many of them by first name. Sweet! 

Items you must try:

Basil spring rolls: 4/5: Very fresh and healthy rolls accompanied by great peanut sauce. 

Lettuce wraps: 5/5: I have so many friends that swear by PF Changs' lettuce wraps but these would challenge them! Flavorful chicken diced with a myriad of spices envelopes in a large piece of lettuce. That's what dreams are made of, friends. 

Special crunchy noodle dish: 3/5: This dish was a special for the evening - a mammoth portion of crunchy (fried? sautéed?) noodles with carrots, snap peas and chicken. The flavors were well rounded and I loved the idea of a crunchy noodle. The issue on this one was the carry out as the sauce took much away from the crunch as I traveled home. Regardless, I would definitely order this again if I was ea
yelp:test:11778.para:
During my visit for a CMYE event, where the food was quite delightful, I also stopped by Mama Fu's to pick up some takeout. The interior of Mama's is brightly colored and spacious, with plenty of seating and a cozy booth for waiting. The staff is exceptionally friendly and accommodating. It's particularly heartwarming to see how many regular customers they have; the manager greeted several by name, which was very endearing.

Here are some dishes you shouldn't miss:

- Basil spring rolls: 4/5 - These are very fresh and healthy, served with a delicious peanut sauce.
- Lettuce wraps: 5/5 - These are a game-changer! The chicken is seasoned with a variety of spices and wrapped in large lettuce leaves. It's truly a dream come true.
- Special crunchy noodle dish: 3/5 - This was a special evening offering: a large portion of crunchy noodles with carrots, snap peas, and chicken. The flavors were well-balanced, and I loved the idea of a crunchy noodle dish. However, the sauce made it less crunchy during the journey home. Nonetheless, I would order it again if I had the chance.

yelp:test:11873.orig:
Whenever I want to sink my teeth into a great cut of beef - and Daddy's not available -  this is my favorite place on the Strip to go. 

It's old-school cool and features white tablecloth service. Don't let that scare away the caveman or cavegirl in you.  The experienced servers and management ooze enough warmth and charm to make the beast in all of us feel beautiful.  Las Vegas Magazine recently gave it rave reviews, so don't just take my word...

Start with either the seafood special platter, served on ice,  or the new tuna tartare special.  And... the filets. Ha cha cha.  Just like Charo, they're nicely aged and have caused more than one man to shake and drool. If lighter fare is more to your liking, try the crab cakes which have a nice bite to them, or the fresh sea bass which is served in a nice broth with fresh snap peas and carrots.  

Save room for dessert, because they have table-side service. I highly recommend the bananas foster and cherries jubilee choices.   Yum, yum.

For those of you wanting more of  - WHATever-  try the private dining room, perfect for hosting 20-40 of your closest friends for a night on the town. That way considerate angels
yelp:test:11873.para:
Whenever I crave a delicious cut of beef and Daddy isn't around, this is my go-to spot on the Strip. It exudes old-school charm with formal dining service, but don't worry—there's plenty for the more casual diners too. The staff is warm and welcoming, making everyone feel at home. Las Vegas Magazine recently praised it highly, so you can trust the quality.

Start with the seafood platter or the tuna tartare, and then move on to the filets, which are expertly aged and irresistible. If you prefer lighter options, the crab cakes are flavorful, and the sea bass is served in a delightful broth with fresh vegetables. Don't skip dessert; they offer table-side service, and I particularly recommend the bananas foster and cherries jubilee.

For larger groups, the private dining room is ideal for hosting up to 40 friends, ensuring a memorable evening.

yelp:test:11903.orig: This is my EVERY morning stop!  The coffee is GREAT!  The scones are decent, but probably a bit over priced.
yelp:test:11903.para: This place is my daily destination every morning. The coffee is outstanding, but the scones, while acceptable, might be a bit on the pricey side.

yelp:test:11935.orig: If you want amazing BBQ and the best service in town, head to Bobby Q! My husband and I had lunch last Sunday, our second time to visit the restaurant. The Onion Brick was delicious, the top sirloin steak enough to split and the Q Rolls over the top yummy! I loved how Jo, the manager on shift, went to every table to make sure the dining experience was the best. Thank you for making our meal over the top great by the top of the line service we received - from everyone! Can't wait till our next visit!
yelp:test:11935.para: For an outstanding BBQ experience paired with exceptional service, Bobby Q is the place to go. My husband and I dined there last Sunday, our second visit. We particularly enjoyed the Onion Brick and found the top sirloin steak so satisfying that we decided to share it. The Q Rolls were simply outstanding. I was impressed by how Jo, the on-duty manager, personally checked in on each table to ensure our dining experience was impeccable. The top-notch service, from everyone, truly elevated our meal. I'm looking forward to our next visit!

yelp:test:11949.orig: The quality of meat is poor.  They cook all their meats well done.  If you like your beef chewy...you will not be disappointed! The chimichurri is not fresh- it is made from dry ingredients.  The food quality is just poor. I recommend fogo de chao in Scottsdale. Avoid this place!
yelp:test:11949.para: The meat quality is subpar, and they always cook it well done. If you prefer your beef to be tough, you won't be let down. The chimichurri lacks freshness as it's made from dried ingredients. Overall, the food quality is poor. I suggest trying Fogo de Chão in Scottsdale instead. Steer clear of this establishment!

yelp:test:11971.orig: Very good hawaiian food. The katsu sauce is good and not too watery or BBQ like. They have Hawaiian Sun too!!! And their spam musubi is really good. \nOverall I like it because it is as close to getting real Hawaiian food off the island.
yelp:test:11971.para: The food is excellent, especially the katsu sauce, which is well-balanced and neither too watery nor BBQ-flavored. They also serve Hawaiian Sun, which is great. The spam musubi is top-notch too. In general, I enjoy it since it offers a taste of authentic Hawaiian cuisine, even if I'm not on the island.

yelp:test:11975.orig: Nice machines, not too packed, and at $10 month? Yah, I'm a fan.
yelp:test:11975.para: These machines are great, not overcrowded, and at just $10 a month? Yes, I really like them.

yelp:test:11992.orig:
Scale of 1-10 (multiple visits):
5 Food
4 Service
5 Atmosphere
4 Value

An uninspired menu w/ average barfood at best.  This place obviously doesn't serve anything that appears local, organic, original, creative, pretty, tasty, or cheap - and is more obviously just making its money by forcing itself upon a captive airport audience with no other choices.  Come on, you have to offer at least ONE of those things!  Boring boring boring place.

But that doesn't mean the service is bad, right?  Well, when I order a bottled beer and the server doesn't tell me that it's a 20 oz bottle, I'm calling bullshit.  So I see this 20 oz bottle come to me and I just sit in confusion for a moment.  I recheck the menu, recheck the label: yup, no way I would have known (not even any prices on the alcohol).  Obviously a scam to try and get people to overbuy.  So i send it back.  ""would you like anything else instead?  we have it on draft too.""  no thanks; you'll probably give it to me in a two-gallon boot and then charge me $25 for it.  So i got my food and got the hell out of here.
yelp:test:11992.para:
On a scale of 1 to 10 (based on multiple visits):

Food: 5
Service: 4
Atmosphere: 5
Value: 4

The menu is unremarkable, offering typical bar food at best. It clearly doesn't feature any locally sourced, organic, or creatively prepared dishes. Instead, it seems to rely on a captive audience with limited options. You'd expect at least one of these qualities, wouldn't you? It's a dull place overall.

However, the service isn't terrible. When I ordered a bottled beer, the server didn't mention it was a 20-ounce bottle. I received the bottle and was confused for a moment. Checking the menu and the label confirmed it was indeed a 20 ounces, with no prices listed for the alcohol. This seemed like a tactic to encourage over-purchasing. I returned the bottle and was offered a draft version instead, but I declined, suspecting it would be a larger portion and more expensive. I ended up ordering food and left quickly.

yelp:test:12023.orig: You can get better food at Denny's. And I don't even really like Denny's much.\n\nOnly good part of this buffet is the omlet guy. He's fun to watch, and the omlets are good.
yelp:test:12023.para: The food quality at Denny's is superior to other options, though I don't particularly enjoy Denny's. The only positive aspect of this buffet is the omlet station; it's entertaining to watch, and the omlets taste great.

yelp:test:12029.orig: Ok so the NY NY hotel website said this buffet was at their hotel. Walked back and forth and was informed that it's not updated and the MGM grand buffet was (obviously) at MGM grand. Someone should update NY NY's website. The food was dried up and old. The options were limited. The staff not very friendly and when you needed something there was no one around to flag down. They make you tip in advance so you never know what to expect. I tipped them so well thinking i was going to have a good time. I did not have a good time. : / The name should be MGM So-So Buffet.
yelp:test:12029.para: So, the NY NY hotel website stated that the buffet was there, but upon arriving, I was told the site wasn't up-to-date and the MGM Grand buffet was, of course, at MGM Grand. The NY NY website needs to be updated. The food was stale and limited in variety. The staff was not very welcoming, and when I needed assistance, no one was around to help. They require you to tip in advance, which makes it hard to gauge the quality. I tipped generously, hoping for a good experience, but it wasn't what I expected. : / It should be called the MGM So-So Buffet.

yelp:test:12049.orig: My husband and I were. In town for our wedding anniversary and felt like getting some pizza. After reading the reviews on Yelp we decided to try LGO... OMG we made the right decision! We had the sweetest most attentive server (Hay). Their homemade lemonade was phenomenal! It was sweet followed by a shot of sour. We decided to share the \""Gladiator\"" (we added prosciutto, spicy Fresno peppers and garlic) our jaws dropped when our food arrived. It was seriously the best pizza we've ever had in our entire lives! The flavors were incredible and you could tell how fresh all of the ingredients were. We were so tempted to order a second pizza after we finished the first. This restaurant makes us both beyond sad that we don't live in town and we began thinking up excuses to visit so we can have another visit to this one of a kind restaurant.
yelp:test:12049.para: For our wedding anniversary in town, my husband and I were craving pizza. After checking Yelp reviews, we chose LGO... And we couldn't be happier with our choice! We were greeted by the most delightful and attentive server, Hay. The homemade lemonade was outstanding—sweet, then tangy. We shared the "Gladiator" pizza, adding prosciutto, spicy Fresno peppers, and garlic. When our pizza arrived, we were amazed by its quality. It was undoubtedly the best pizza we've ever tasted, with incredible flavors and fresh ingredients. We were so tempted to order another slice after finishing our first. This place left us longing to live closer so we could visit again, and we're already brainstorming ways to make it happen.

yelp:test:12065.orig: Normally LOVE Penn Station, but today was. Greeted by a gnat infestation @ my Penn Station. Sooo troubled by that! Please get rid of the gnats. I will be back at least once, but if I have to fight the gnats for a lid & straw it will definitely be my last time. Totally willing to edit my review it fixed. yelp:test:12065.para: I usually adore Penn Station, but today was a different story. I was met with a severe gnat problem there. This is really bothering me! Please take care of the gnats. I plan to return at least once, but if I have to battle gnats for a lid and straw, it will definitely be my last visit. I'll happily revise my review if things improve. I spoke to the counter staff, who were already aware and shared their knowledge about the gnats' persistence. I'm sure other eateries have faced this issue too. yelp:test:12076.orig: Went to my first cardinal game . The roads to get to the  stadium   was very busy. Once we got  to the stadium was well organized we got in quickly.  The security was tight to get in with several people checking our tickets to get on the escalators.  We sat in the club seats which were large and comfortable . The view was great and enhanced with the large screens in the end zones . The food  was actually very good . Tried their pasta bar for 12. The crowd was loud which made for a great atmosphere cheating on the cardinals.  Had a good experience
yelp:test:12076.para: Attended my first Cardinals game, and the journey to the stadium was quite congested. Upon arrival, everything was well-organized, and we were able to enter swiftly. Security was stringent, with multiple checks on our tickets before we could use the escalators. We enjoyed the club seats, which were spacious and comfortable. The view was fantastic, enhanced by the large screens in the end zones. The food was surprisingly delicious; I tried their pasta bar for $12. The crowd was incredibly loud, creating a thrilling atmosphere, especially as we supported the Cardinals. Overall, it was a positive experience.

yelp:test:12085.orig:
What do you mean Social House is closed?!

That was my favorite sushi restaurant in Vegas! The food was great, the service was superb, the restaurant looks great and you can get a killer view of the Pirate show outside TI off the balcony. 

Where are you going Social House?! Please re-open before I head out in mid October!
yelp:test:12085.para:
Why is Social House closed already?!

It was my go-to sushi spot in Vegas! The food was fantastic, the service was outstanding, and the place looked amazing. Plus, you could enjoy a stunning view of the Pirate show at TI from the balcony.

Social House, please reopen before mid-October! I really miss it.

yelp:test:12096.orig:
Don't go here! Overpriced, overrated, and bad service. 

Environment:
I thought the cafe would be a nice dining experience overlooking the pools, but the tables are so close you might as well have a convo with your neighbor. Noisy! We had Debbie Downer for our waitress who never smiled and saw her only three times: once to take our order, another time to deliver food, and a final time to deliver the check. Um, can we get refills? She even messed up on the drink order: coffee. How do you forget coffee during brunch? 

Food:
I ordered lox and a bagel. Can't screw that up, but I will say that the bagel was small and they only gave my three rings of onion - not even a full slice of an onion! That lox and bagel was NOT worth $15. The cream cheese portion was not much...maybe a tablespoon. The tomato slice was a regular beef steak, not vine ripened and the tomato was pill-y. However, the lox was good. My bro ordered the corned beef hash which was good and meaty, and the hash browns were tasty and crunchy. Our meal came close to $70...for breakfast. 

Why two stars?
The service is bad as is the food. Avoid this place and hit the buffet or eat at another hotel. Definitely overpric
yelp:test:12096.para:
Stay away! This place is overpriced, overhyped, and has poor service.

Environment:
I expected a pleasant dining experience with views of the pools, but the tables were so close together that it felt like we were having a conversation with our neighbors. It was quite noisy. Our waitress, Debbie Downer, never smiled and we only saw her three times: once to take our order, another to bring the food, and a final time to deliver the check. We even asked for refills, but she forgot about us. She also messed up our drink order—coffee. How can you forget coffee during brunch?

Food:
I had lox and a bagel. The bagel was small, and they only gave me three rings of onion—not even a full slice. That lox and bagel combo wasn't worth $15. The cream cheese portion was minimal, maybe just a tablespoon. The tomato slice was tough and not vine-ripened, tasting more like a pill. However, the lox was good. My brother ordered corned beef hash, which was good and meaty, and the hash browns were tasty and crunchy. Our meal cost close to $70 for breakfast.

Why two stars?
