yelp:test:12102.orig:
Second time eating here in the span of 10 years and NOTHING has changed. Food once again is CRAP and service is terrible. Paid $22 for an Ahi tuna salad. Ahi looked bad. The color is one of that which fish should never be, a nice greyish tinge rather than bright red/purple. Served on a beautiful bed of shredded iceberg lettuce. What? Too cheap to buy mixed greens Bellagio? 7 very small pieces of Ahi was served on this ""salad"" so my friend and I each got a whopping 3.5. 

We also split the lobster mac & cheese which was served with a spinach salad that was simple, but decent with spinach, heirloom tomatoes, and a pesto dressing on the side. The lobster mac & cheese was certainly missing the main protein. It should have been called thick bacon/ham mac & cheese. There was hardly any lobster. We had to ask our server for our bread basket after our entrees came out 40 minutes later. A quick lunch ended up taking almost 2 hours. Even when the place emptied out, our server was still slow. 

This place is understaffed and the food is garbage. Definitely a tourist trap since it is located in the gardens & nobody will care about this review when they are starving and don't know where
yelp:test:12102.para:
After dining here for the second time in 10 years, I found no improvements. The food was subpar once again, and the service was poor. I paid $22 for an Ahi tuna salad, but the Ahi looked off, with a greyish color instead of the expected bright red or purple. It was served on a bed of shredded iceberg lettuce, which seemed like a cost-cutting measure. There were only 7 small pieces of Ahi, so my friend and I each got just 3.5 pieces in total.

We also shared the lobster mac & cheese, which came with a simple spinach salad featuring heirloom tomatoes and pesto dressing. However, the lobster was barely noticeable in the mac & cheese, making it more of a bacon or ham mac & cheese. Our bread basket arrived only after our entrees, and our meal took nearly 2 hours, despite the restaurant being mostly empty by the end.

The place is clearly understaffed, and the food quality is poor. It feels like a tourist trap, especially given its location in the gardens, where hungry visitors might not have the time or inclination to read reviews.

yelp:test:12108.orig: ok first of all... lets just start out by saying I am from LA... and lucky for me we have Chinatown and the entire San Gabriel Valley a.k.a. China! Now maybe Vegas just doesn't have too many authentic chinese restaurants but damn this was the worst dim sum I have ever had in my life! My friend took me there 2 weeks ago and well the name kinda threw me off to begin with but once I tried the shu mai... damn it was over! I didnt want to try anything else. The simplest dim sum and yet they couldnt even get it right. The beefballs were too overcooked too!  Even the tiny little pork buns were to run from. How does this place stay in business? But then again maybe they are catering to a different crowd. What really struck me as weird was the fact the place was full of asians! I mean, is this suppose to be as good as it gets in Vegas for dim sum? If so, I'd rather stop by a trader joes and pick up a pack of frozen shu mais. You will have much better luck going to the frozen food aisle at a supermarket for good dim sum. Oh one more thing.. horrible service. The employees are literally fresh off the boat! I guess thats the only thing authentic about this place, their workers! hahahaha Trust
yelp:test:12108.para:
Sure, here's a paraphrased version of the text:

To start, I'm from LA, where we have a vibrant Chinatown and the San Gabriel Valley, often referred to as "China Town." While I understand that Vegas might not have many authentic Chinese restaurants, this place served the worst dim sum I've ever tasted! My friend took me there two weeks ago, and the name initially intrigued me, but after trying the shu mai, I was thoroughly disappointed. I couldn't bring myself to try anything else. Even the simplest dim sum dishes were poorly executed; the beefballs were overcooked, and the tiny pork buns were a miss. How do they manage to stay open? Perhaps they cater to a different clientele. What really puzzled me was the place being so full of Asians. Does this mean it's the best dim sum in Vegas? If so, I'd prefer to buy frozen shu mai from Trader Joe's. You'd likely have better luck finding good dim sum in the frozen food section of a supermarket. And to top it all off, the service was terrible. The staff seemed to be new to the country, which is the only thing that felt authentic about the place. Hahahaha.

yelp:test:12113.orig:
This is the best dim sum in Las Vegas. 

1. Open kitchen. I like to watch people cook and check if they are sanitary. They're doing it right back there. Clean for a Chinese restaurant. 

2. The cart ladies can speak English. They don't just dump the dishes in my table when I point and ask, ""what is it?""

3. Food is fresh. They don't give me old food that's been around and rejected by other people. If I want the new batch, they'll give me just that. 

4. Rice is not free. Blahhh. I love rice. They come in a little portion bowl thingy. Their prices are typical for dim sum though. 

5. Food is not as great as LA dim sum, but it still has all of the items I want from a dim sum. 

I recommend you try.
yelp:test:12113.para:
This is the top dim sum place in Las Vegas. 

1. They have an open kitchen where I can see the chefs at work and ensure they maintain hygiene. It's clean for a Chinese restaurant.

2. The servers who bring the carts can speak English. They actually explain the dishes rather than just placing them on the table when I point and ask.

3. The food is fresh; I don't get old, rejected portions. If I want the freshest batch, they'll serve that to me.

4. The rice isn't complimentary, which I find disappointing since I love it. It comes in small portions, but their prices are standard for dim sum.

5. While the food isn't as impressive as LA's dim sum, it still offers all the items I expect from a dim sum meal.

I highly recommend you give it a try.

yelp:test:12157.orig:
Talk about a special occasion.  At deseos prices, we won't be back unless we win the lottery.
The food and service were excellent. Another plus? When so many other restaurants have tv's to distract you, you won't find any distractions here.
We were recommended to try the shrimp chicharonnes. It was a textural wonderland. Crunchy sweet, but creamy spice with slivered jalapeños. 
Both my wife and I had the sea bass (not Chilean btw). Mine came with 2 large delicately cooked filets, skin on, and buttery delicious. 
We rounded out the meal with the cigar desert and it lived up to its status.

We left feeling extremely full and satisfied. This was definitely a splurge for us, as it is not amenable on a middle class budget to eat here regularly. But service, food, and ambiance was worth it for a special occasion.
yelp:test:12157.para:
Discussing a memorable special occasion, we dined at a place where the prices were so high, we could only afford it if we hit the lottery. The food and service were outstanding. Unlike many other restaurants that have TVs to divert your attention, this place kept us focused on our meal.

We were suggested to try the shrimp chicharonnes, which was a delightful experience. The shrimp was crunchy and sweet, yet creamy and spicy, with slivered jalapeños adding a nice kick.

Both my wife and I enjoyed the sea bass, which was not Chilean. My portion came with two large, perfectly cooked fillets, skin-on, and was incredibly buttery and delicious.

We concluded our meal with the cigar dessert, which did not disappoint.

Leaving feeling thoroughly satisfied and full, this meal was a significant splurge for us, as it’s not within our regular budget. However, the exceptional service, food quality, and ambiance made it well worth it for a special occasion.

yelp:test:12164.orig: Excellent. Good staff, really welcoming and friendly. We had an awesome experience here. Drinks were fairly priced and poured. The piano players were quite good. Could not give it 5 stars because that is reserved for NY NY Piano Bar in Las Vegas and Andy's Pub (Piano Bar) in Oslo.
yelp:test:12164.para: Great! The staff was very welcoming and friendly, making our experience excellent. The drinks were reasonably priced and well-poured. The piano performances were quite impressive. While we enjoyed our time here, we couldn't rate it the highest because we've had even better experiences at NY NY Piano Bar in Las Vegas and Andy's Pub in Oslo.

yelp:test:12165.orig: I love the entertainment here and the drinks are always ice cold! This is a great place to take some coworkers and friends!\nBruce was very accommodating for special events!
yelp:test:12165.para: I enjoy the entertainment options here, and the drinks are consistently served ice cold. It's an excellent spot to bring coworkers and friends. Bruce was particularly helpful for special events!

yelp:test:12166.orig:
The only reason I'm giving this place two stars is because our server did a really nice job.  

The food here is seriously overpriced and not very good in my opinion.  My pulled pork sandwich was $14.50 if I recall correctly.  

You can do much, much better.  I don't know whether BLT Burger (in the Mirage) has pulled pork sandwiches, but they do have killer gourmet hamburgers, and they don't cost $14.50.  Also, the service at BLT is very professional.  Pricing there (BLT) is a bargain given the quality of the food, the quality of the service, and the location.  

Do yourself a favor.  Skip Gilley's at TI and walk next door to the Mirage and have a much nicer dining experience for less money at BLT.
yelp:test:12166.para:
I'm awarding this place two stars solely due to the server's excellent service. However, the food is excessively priced and, in my view, not very good. For instance, my pulled pork sandwich cost $14.50.

There are far better options available. BLT Burger at the Mirage offers outstanding gourmet burgers without the steep price tag. Their service is top-notch, and the prices are much more reasonable compared to the quality of food and service they provide. 

I strongly recommend you opt for BLT instead of Gilley's at TI. You'll enjoy a superior dining experience for a lower cost by walking over to the Mirage.

yelp:test:12179.orig: I was there last week with some friends for happy hour. They have margaritas $1 off and 1/2 price appetizers. The blueberry margarita was delicious!
yelp:test:12179.para: Last week, I went with some friends for happy hour, where margaritas were $1 off and appetizers were at half price. The blueberry margarita was particularly delightful!

yelp:test:12189.orig:
Eh.  I'm sorry Jim Gould's, I think you've changed and not for the better. 

Went for our anniversary dinner last night, and despite having a loud and obnoxious group of drunk out-of-town conference attendees trying to impress one another with their wit and cleavage seated right next to us, figured that the food, wine, and service would compensate.  It didn't.  At half-price, the glass of shiraz I had was overpriced, and slightly chilled. My kobe beef burger was bland and not particularly tender.  The brie on top was flavorless.  Pommes frites were good, though I'm fairly confident they were not ""truffle oil misted"" as described.  But still, yay pommes frites.  My husband's beef medallion ""special"" was itty bitty and overcooked.  Also, despite being described as a special, was listed on the regular menu, and for the price that we were charged.  So, neither the dish nor the price were ""special"". 

Which brings me to the strange service: when we made a remark about the odd ""$1 wine shot"" feature (seriously? a shot of wine?  served in a shot glass?), the waiter replied ""yeah, well, we're trying to compete with KoFusions $1 sushi.  They're really busy over there a
yelp:test:12189.para: Hmm, Jim Gould's, I believe you've changed for the worse. Last night, during our anniversary dinner, we were seated next to a noisy group of out-of-town conference attendees trying to impress each other. We hoped the food, wine, and service would make up for the distraction, but they didn't. The half-price shiraz was overpriced and slightly chilled. My kobe beef burger was bland and not very tender, and the brie on top lacked flavor. The fries were good, though I doubt they were "truffle oil misted" as advertised. On the plus side, the fries were still enjoyable. My husband's beef medallion, described as a special, was tiny and overcooked. Moreover, it was listed on the regular menu and priced the same, so neither the dish nor the price felt special. The service was also peculiar; when we mentioned the odd "$1 wine shot" promotion (really? a shot of wine in a shot glass?), the waiter explained that they were trying to compete with KoFusions' $1 sushi, which is quite busy over there.

yelp:test:12238.orig: Don't waste your money! My wife and I have always eaten there when visiting Vegas, but the price has gone way up and the food quality and selection way down. We arrived at 8pm on a Saturday night ... no line at all to get in, and the seating was only half full. That told us something right away. We went to Caesars Bacchanal buffet two nights later and it was absolutely unbelievable. I could spend a whole week just trying all the selections available, and the food quality is top notch. The price was only $2.00/ea more than the Village Seafood Buffet, and there is no comparison. Go to Bacchanal, wait 20 - 30 minutes in line, then enter heaven. We won't be back to the Village Seafood Buffet --- ever!
yelp:test:12238.para: Avoid spending your money there! My spouse and I have frequented this place during our Vegas trips, but now the prices have skyrocketed while the food quality and variety have plummeted. When we arrived at 8 pm on a Saturday, there was no queue and the restaurant was only half occupied, which was a clear sign. Two nights later, we visited Caesars Bacchanal buffet, and it was outstanding. The selection was so extensive that I could spend a week trying everything, and the food was of the highest quality. The price difference was just $2 per person compared to the Village Seafood Buffet, but the experience was worlds apart. Bacchanal is where you should go; you'll have to wait 20-30 minutes, but it's worth it. We won't return to the Village Seafood Buffet; never again!

yelp:test:12254.orig: This place tries to be like the old Mick's chain in Atlanta - an Applebee's or Ruby Tuesday, but with fresh food, executed well. Unfortunately, the food's just not that good. The Italian meatloaf isn't awful, but it's nothing to write home about. The apps were decent, but not great. My GF loves their black bean burger, though (and it IS pretty good for a non-meat burger). It's a good place to watch a game,but not as a dining destination.
yelp:test:12254.para: This establishment aims to emulate the style of the old Mick's chain in Atlanta, offering fresh food like Applebee's or Ruby Tuesday, but the food quality falls short. The Italian meatloaf is tolerable, yet unremarkable. The appetizers were satisfactory, but not exceptional. My girlfriend really enjoys their black bean burger, which is quite good for a non-meat option. While it’s a decent spot to watch sports, it’s not ideal for dining.

yelp:test:12264.orig: Simple, Neopolitan-style pizza cooked to order in their brick oven. The crust is excellent, thin and soft.\n\nThey have an espresso machine, and if you like cappucino be sure to order one after you eat. It was one of the best i've ever had.
yelp:test:12264.para: Order-up a traditional Neapolitan pizza cooked fresh in their brick oven. The crust is outstanding, thin yet tender. They also offer an espresso machine, and if you enjoy a cappuccino, make sure to try one after your meal. It was among the best I've ever tasted.

yelp:test:12307.orig:
I was eating solo this night and was starving when I was perusing the Caesars mall. I decided to go for a known quantity since I have known CF for years. I ate at the bar and had my usual soda and small chopped salad and bread. It came out to $15 bucks with tip. That's CHEAP by Vegas standards. The small salads are a good deal b/c CF gives you a huge amount of food in the main entrees and so these are just the right generous portion and most hotel rooms have no place to refrigerate or heat up your doggy bag anyways.

Bar staff was great. I think it was Tim that helped me. Always made sure to keep my glass filled. Kudos to him and he's cute to boot.

Verdict: Okay so CF is a chain that is everywhere nowadays, but it's nice to find someplace that is a known quantity, fed me in less than an hour, and isn't charging 50% more than their normal outlets and has a nice bar staff.
yelp:test:12307.para:
On this night, I was dining alone and quite hungry while exploring the Caesars mall. I opted for a familiar spot, CF, which I've known for years. I sat at the bar and ordered my usual—a soda, a small chopped salad, and some bread. The total, including tip, was $15, which is quite affordable by Las Vegas standards. The small salads are a good value because CF serves generous main courses, so the salads are just the right size. Plus, most hotel rooms don't have refrigerators or microwaves, so there's no need to worry about leftovers.

The bar staff was excellent. I believe it was Tim who attended to me; he kept my glass full throughout. Kudos to him, and he's also quite attractive.

Overall, while CF is a chain found everywhere now, it's pleasant to find a reliable place that can feed you quickly and doesn't overcharge, especially with its friendly bar staff.

yelp:test:12321.orig: How frustrating!!!! I wanted to love this place. The items on the menu sounded great. The atmosphere when we walked in was cozy, a definite upscale setting. We had a reservation for a large group, were seated right away no problem there. Immediately had waters for the table and some bread. Our server was great. \n\nUnfortunately, the suggested meal I ordered was horrible! I was debating between the fillet Oscar style, and either a fish or seafood dish. After a suggestion by our waiter  I ended up ordering the Jumbo Gulf White Shrimp dish which is followed by the description \""grilled with lemon, garlic, and fresh Jonah crab\"". By the way, this dish is $29.  I also ordered the crab and corn chowder. Damn the corn chowder was great. Rich, hot, and a good amount of crab. Sadly...my main dish was just awful. My first bite was dry and dry and more dry. I swear there was raw garlic and/or raw shallots on my plate and random crumbs of god knows what sprinkled over all of the shrimp. You would think that there would be a sauce on top of this dried grilled shrimp but there was not. How about a lemon butter sauce? No. I ate two shrimp off of my plate and quickly tried to give them away to
yelp:test:12321.para:
How disappointing!!!! I was eager to enjoy this restaurant. The menu items sounded fantastic. The ambiance upon entering was warm and upscale. We had a reservation for a large party and were promptly seated. Water and bread were promptly served. Our server was excellent. 

Unfortunately, the dish I chose was terrible! I was considering the fillet Oscar style or a fish or seafood option. After the waiter's recommendation, I opted for the Jumbo Gulf White Shrimp, described as "grilled with lemon, garlic, and fresh Jonah crab," priced at $29. I also had the crab and corn chowder, which was delicious—rich, hot, and packed with crab. However, my main course was a letdown. My first bite was extremely dry, and I suspected there was raw garlic or shallots on my plate. There was no sauce, not even a lemon butter sauce. I managed to eat just two shrimp before giving them away.

yelp:test:12358.orig: I don't get it. I ordered the chicken and waffles like everyone recommended but it was very tasteless and over cooked. Maybe I'll try it again. Just don't see it though. It was large enough for 2 people however. Maybe 3 since non of us cared for it.
yelp:test:12358.para: I'm confused. I followed the recommendations and ordered the chicken and waffles, but they were bland and overcooked. I might give it another try, though I'm not convinced. The portion was sizable—enough for two people, and possibly three if none of us enjoyed it.

yelp:test:12367.orig:
Came here on a Sunday afternoon. The place was packed and had to wait 10mins for a table. 
The waitress seemed a bit stressed (due to possible understaffing) and barely got a moment of her time. I had ordered the blt bloody Mary, nothing too special and a bit spicy for my taste. The slice of bread that comes with it - awesome idea...if there were a few more slices of bacon to go with it! 
I had ordered the fried chicken Benedict, my friend ordered the salmon scramble(I think). She had feared, after ordering, that what she'd ordered wouldn't be what's expected. As soon as the food came(ca. 15mins later), it wasn't what she'd expected and sent it back. Around 5mins. Later, her replacement meal was served. The kitchen was definitely on top of their game that day! 
I enjoyed my benedict, buuuut there was just a little too much chipotle for my taste.
yelp:test:12367.para:
Visited on a Sunday afternoon; the place was bustling, and we had to wait 10 minutes for a table. The waitress appeared stressed, likely due to a shortage of staff, and barely had time to attend to us. I ordered the BLT Bloody Mary, which wasn't particularly special and was a bit spicy for my liking. The accompanying slice of bread was a great idea, but it would have been even better with a few more slices of bacon.

My friend ordered the salmon scramble, but she was unsure about her choice. When the food arrived about 15 minutes later, it didn't meet her expectations, so she returned it. A few minutes later, her new meal was served. The kitchen seemed to be performing exceptionally well that day.

I enjoyed my Benedict, although the chipotle was a bit too strong for my taste.

yelp:test:12387.orig: celebrated our 30th wedding anniversary there-BIG mistake-the view was really the only good part.  Food was fair, prices outrageous, and overall, a very uneventful experience.  Told the manager, who offered to buy us a drink at the lounge-no thanks-couldn't wait to leave.
yelp:test:12387.para: We made a big mistake celebrating our 30th wedding anniversary there—the view was the only positive aspect. The food was merely adequate, the prices were exorbitant, and the experience was quite dull overall. We informed the manager, who offered to buy us a drink at the lounge, but we declined; we were eager to leave.

yelp:test:12390.para:

yelp:test:12439.orig:
Hello all you foodies out there :)

Today I will give you our opinion of JOES BBQ.

And I do realize food is a preference and I am a very picky person.

I realize Joes has its local following, however from a girl who has tried many of the BBQ joynts here in the greater Phoenix area I have to say.... I DONT GET IT?

I was being fair in trying Joes twice.....just to make sure it wasent an off day.

We first went to Joes pick up window a few weeks ago and tried a slab of ribs and a combo plate with chicken, ribs and some bbq beef and bbq pork.

I enjoy some good ""fall off the bone"" ribs but what I got was a slab of ""pry off the bone"" ribs.

I must say the bbq sauce was ok but the meat was tough and chewy and I was extremely dissapointed.

On the combo place the chicken was dry as were the meats.

I would like to compliment the MAC and CHEESE which is better than most and the BBQ BEANS were also tasty.

I called  Joes to ask if I could bring back the ribs, of which I ate 2 bones, and get our money back and I was transfered to a very friendly manager who talked me into letting her send us a gift card so we can try again.

She insisted their ribs are normall
yelp:test:12439.para:
Hello everyone who loves food! 😄

Today, I'll share our thoughts on JOES BBQ.

I understand that food preferences vary, and I'm quite particular. Despite JOES having a local fanbase, after trying several BBQ spots in the Phoenix area, I must admit... I just don't get it.

I gave JOES a fair chance, visiting twice to ensure it wasn't a one-time issue.

Our first visit was to the pick-up window a few weeks ago, where we ordered a slab of ribs and a combo plate with chicken, ribs, and some BBQ beef and pork.

While I enjoy tender, "fall off the bone" ribs, what I received were "pry off the bone" ribs. The BBQ sauce was decent, but the meat was tough and chewy, leaving me quite disappointed.

On the combo plate, the chicken and other meats were dry.

I did appreciate the mac and cheese, which was better than most, and the BBQ beans were also tasty.

I called JOES to ask if I could return the ribs, which I only ate two bones of, and get a refund. The friendly manager talked me into accepting a gift card instead, promising to let us try again.

She insisted that their ribs are usually better.

yelp:test:12443.orig: Prices are a bit high but the food is great and the shows are fun!
yelp:test:12443.para: The prices are a tad on the expensive side, yet the food is outstanding, and the performances are really enjoyable!

yelp:test:12462.orig: I ate at the restaurant but the selection was a little disappointing and tasted pretty generic. Beer was excellent though.
yelp:test:12462.para: I dined at the restaurant, but found the menu options a bit letdown and the food quite bland. However, the beer was outstanding.

yelp:test:12475.orig:
Having always been fascinated with human anatomy, I did toy with the idea of being a neurosurgeon.  My decision against pursuing that idea has and will continue to save(d) countless human lives (and pain and suffering caused by ensuing lawsuits and / or legal proceedings).  

Nonetheless, the subject never ceases to amaze me.  Which is why when BODIES... The Exhibition made its way to Silicon Valley, I was looking forward to perusing a variety of polymer-preserved body parts whilst recalling the materials from the Human Anatomy class that I took during my freshman year.

Allow two hours to go through the various sections (no pun intended) of the exhibition: skeletal, muscular, respiratory, circulatory, and nervous system.  Allow extra time in the circulatory system section - see what you would have looked like you are stripped off everything else but your heart, veins and arteries.  Look at what a blackened pair of lungs look like and wish that you had stuck to that new year's resolution of yours.  Touch the parts that they have so kindly taken out for the benefit of the visitors (it was a heart and a liver - it feels almost like made-in-china plastic toys *inside joke for thos
yelp:test:12475.para:
Ever since I was intrigued by human anatomy, I considered becoming a neurosurgeon. However, my decision not to pursue that path has and will continue to prevent countless lives from being lost or suffering due to potential medical errors or legal issues. 

Despite this, the subject remains endlessly fascinating. That's why I was excited to visit BODIES... The Exhibition in Silicon Valley, where I could examine various polymer-preserved body parts and recall the lessons from my freshman Human Anatomy class.

It's recommended to allocate about two hours to explore the exhibition's sections on the skeletal, muscular, respiratory, circulatory, and nervous systems. Spend extra time in the circulatory system area to see what you would look like with just your heart, veins, and arteries exposed. Take a look at the blackened lungs and reflect on any health resolutions you might have broken. Don't miss the chance to touch the heart and liver specimens, which feel almost like cheap plastic toys.

yelp:test:12479.orig: Do not eat here.  The pancakes were old and cold - just run away
yelp:test:12479.para: Avoid this place entirely. The pancakes were stale and icy cold; you should really just leave quickly.

yelp:test:12482.orig: The Cobb salad was really good. Loved the balsamic dressing. Ask for Daryl. Best waiter ever because he used to be a butler!!! He is finishing law school. Nice man.
yelp:test:12482.para: The Cobb salad was excellent, and I particularly enjoyed the balsamic dressing. Make sure to request Daryl; he's the best waiter I've ever had, having previously been a butler! He's also in the process of completing his law degree. What a nice person.

I inquire where the straws are as she is serving someone e
yelp:test:12497.para:
When we visited the exhibit, I was in terrible shape, having gone there mainly to support my boyfriend since I'd seen it earlier in the 2000s. I was feeling queasy from hunger and the sun, and too sick to eat. Despite that, I managed to notice a few things while trying not to vomit my breakfast from Bouchon Bakery onto the dolphin pool. 

A.) This place is still overpriced; fifteen bucks for a few animal cages and three unexcited dolphins? 
B.) They offer misted walkways and seating areas, which will be appreciated by the hungover, elderly, and those dealing with noisy children. I definitely benefited from that.
C.) The guy who made us take a picture was a real jerk.
D.) What are these, llamas? Where did the elephant go?

Lastly, E.) I was extremely dehydrated, so I got a Slush, which I assumed was a Slurpee from the machine it came from. After paying three dollars, the woman handed me a tiny, McDonald's-sized Styrofoam cup with red liquid, but no straws. I asked where the straws were as she was serving someone else.

yelp:test:12506.orig:
I hate this bar and grill.  Seriously.

We had some friends in town that had enjoyed Toby Keith's a few years ago and wanted to go back.  So we made the stop at Harrah's on a late Sunday afternoon.  On the way to the casino, I called ahead to make reservations.  You can't.  So I asked how busy they were, expecting the girl on the other end of the phone to tell me there would be a wait.  Instead, I was told ""We are the opposite of busy.""  Things weren't looking good already.

We were immediately seated and I enjoyed the feel of the place.  I'm not into country music but I don't mind it playing in the background.  It's pretty much an Applebee's or TGI Fridays feel, except with a country theme.  But you can only enjoy the scenery for so long....

We waited, and waited, and waited.  It took at least 15 minutes before our server even came over to greet us and get our drink orders.  Someone in my group wanted one of the specialty mixed drinks that are listed on the back of the menu (the ones that come in mason jars - 19 flipping dollars).  When my friend asked how much a 16-ounce version of the drink would be, she was told it was $12 but it would only come with a half a shot in
yelp:test:12506.para:
I really dislike this bar and grill. 

A few friends who had visited Toby Keith's a couple of years ago suggested we go there again. We decided to check it out at Harrah's on a Sunday afternoon. I called ahead to make a reservation, but found out it's not possible. When I inquired about the wait, the person on the phone said they were "the opposite of busy." That didn't bode well.

We were promptly seated, and I appreciated the ambiance. While I don't particularly like country music, I can tolerate it playing in the background. The place had a generic Applebee's or TGI Fridays vibe, with a country twist. However, the atmosphere couldn't mask the poor service we were about to experience.

We waited, and waited, and waited. It took at least 15 minutes before our server arrived to take our drink orders. One of my friends wanted a specialty drink from the menu, listed in mason jars, priced at $19. When she asked if a 16-ounce version could be made without a full shot, she was told it would cost $12 but only come with half a shot.

yelp:test:12507.orig: I love a good country song but I do not love this bar and grill.  The prices are very high for the portions you get.  Everything I have tried has been bland and overcooked.  The restaurant makes the big mistake made by many similar chains.  It tries to do too much.  There are far too many items on this menu for the staff to be able to get them all right. The real Toby Keith's in OK have smaller menus and better quality.  This is the PBR tourist trap and has almost no character.    Many better choices in town.
yelp:test:12507.para: While I enjoy country music, I'm not a fan of this bar and grill. The prices are steep for the small portions served. My experiences have been disappointing, with food that's both bland and overcooked. The restaurant falls into the common pitfall of many chain establishments by trying to cater to too many tastes. The menu is overly extensive, making it difficult for the staff to ensure accuracy. In contrast, Toby Keith's locations in Oklahoma offer more concise menus with higher quality. This place feels like a generic PBR tourist spot with little character. There are plenty of better options available in town.

yelp:test:12538.orig: I had lunch with my wife.  I ordered the beef panang with rice for $5.95, my wife ordered Sriracha Beef for $6.50.  The Sriracha Beef came with an egg roll (that I ate) and fried rice that the wife substituted with white rice.  I'm a good sized guy and I did not finish my beef panang and rice.  A nice sized portion, and it tasted great.  On a 1-10 for spicy, I ordered an 8.  Yummmm.  The wife enjoyed the Sriracha Beef, a spicy dish with veggies and cooked in Sriracha chiles.  She could not finish her portions.  The service was brisk.  They gave a free refill on the Thai iced tea!  Two people ate for about $15.50.  A very good value, tasty food, and prompt service.
yelp:test:12538.para: I had lunch with my wife. I got the beef panang with rice for $5.95, while she chose the Sriracha Beef for $6.50. Her meal included an egg roll (which I enjoyed) and fried rice, which she swapped for white rice. As a hearty eater, I didn't finish my beef panang and rice. The portion was generous, and the flavor was excellent. I requested it to be quite spicy, at about an 8 on a 1-10 scale, and it was delicious. My wife liked the Sriracha Beef, a spicy dish with vegetables cooked in Sriracha chiles, but she also couldn't finish her meal. The service was quick, and they provided a free refill on the Thai iced tea. For two people, the bill came to around $15.50, which we found to be a very good value. The food was tasty, and the service was prompt.

yelp:test:12544.orig: If you have seen him in the past you will be very disappointed.  Way less magic and a lot of just going through the motions. He thought he was funny picking on guests but we were there for illusions not comedy that isn't really.  Seating was awful. We were crammed in the stage seemed cramped too. This was sad to see after him being such an icon to Las Vegas in the past but I think he is going to be upstaged by some of the newcomers to illusions
yelp:test:12544.para: If you've seen him before, you'll likely be quite disappointed. The magic is much less impressive, and it feels more like going through the motions. He thought his jokes at guests' expense were funny, but we were there for the illusions, not comedy. The seating was terrible, and the stage felt cramped. It's sad to see this after he was such an iconic figure in Las Vegas, but I believe some newer illusionists will outshine him.

yelp:test:12572.orig: I have been here quite a few times and I love it!!!  I love the cool decor and the little market.  I like the patio area..but mostly I love their red sangria..mmm...you can buy it by the pitcher!!  I have always found everyone working there to treat us with great service...It is a favorite lunch spot of mine!
yelp:test:12572.para: I frequent this place often and adore it! The stylish decor and mini market are delightful. While I enjoy the patio, what I really cherish is their red sangria—so yummy, and you can get it by the pitcher! The staff has always been exceptionally friendly and attentive. It's a go-to spot for lunch of mine!

yelp:test:12585.orig: This place is doing something right fill the place. Low expectations in taste must be par for the course. Six of us ate there. Not one of us finished nor did one of us really enjoy the meal. Environment is nice, server was awesome but hostesses all were all a bit kitschy and stuck in their cliques. Had reservations for six and the couldn't nor would attempt to try and seat us together. No smiles, personal interaction and no interest in assisting us.\nWill not be back.
yelp:test:12585.para: Despite high hopes for the environment and service, our dining experience fell short. We had six people, and not a single one of us enjoyed the meal or finished their dishes. While the ambiance was pleasant and the server was excellent, the hostesses came across as a bit quirky and isolated. We had a reservation for six but were unable to be seated together; there was no friendly interaction or effort to help us. Given this, we won't be returning.

yelp:test:12595.orig:
As far as contemporary fine dining goes, Eleven sticks with the Big Burrito formula pretty closely. Nothing they serve is entirely challenging but for a lot of Pittsburghers, it probably appears that way.

Either way, there's no way to argue about the quality of the food. The ingredients are seasonal and local and the cooking is inspired. Eleven is probably the most upscale of the Big Burrito restaurants but the stuffiness that comes with that atmosphere is wholly missing.

I love being able to order food off a restaurant's menu and recognizing the name of the farms that supply their proteins.

The service at Eleven is exceptional and the food is great. A lot of people seem to have a problem with Big Burrito but I think they are wholly responsible for a lot of the fine dining scene in Pittsburgh. Mad Mex, as laid back and casual as it is, is a great way to introduce your palette to flavors that will lead you to bigger and much more challenging flavors. Eleven is Big Burrito's attempt at the prize at the end of that journey and I think for most people, it's sufficient.

For a more in-depth review you can read the article on my web site. http://eatinginpittsburgh.com/2011/02/
yelp:test:12595.para:
Eleven adheres closely to the Big Burrito model in contemporary fine dining. While the menu isn't particularly innovative, it likely feels that way to many Pittsburgh diners.

Regardless, the food's quality is undeniable. The ingredients are fresh and local, and the cooking is creative. Eleven is the most upscale Big Burrito establishment, yet it maintains a welcoming atmosphere without the usual formality.

I appreciate being able to order dishes and see the names of the farms that supply the ingredients.

The service and food at Eleven are outstanding. Despite some criticisms of Big Burrito, I believe the chain has significantly contributed to Pittsburgh's fine dining scene. Mad Mex, with its relaxed vibe, introduces diners to flavors that eventually lead to more complex tastes. Eleven represents the culmination of that journey, and it meets most people's expectations.

For a more detailed review, you can read the article on my website: <http://eatinginpittsburgh.com/2011/02/>

Just dead.  We had to asked the bartender to turn on and up the music 2 times.  Very frustrating when were there to celebrate my partners birthday.  However, food great.  Service great.  To me Corbin's you are providing an atmosphere not a mediation room.  Please make sure you have music on when your open.  OR did you not want us there?
yelp:test:12613.para: On a Sunday night at 7:30, I brought five people in for my partner's birthday. Upon entering, the place seemed deserted. The most disappointing aspect was the lack of energy; there was no music, making it feel lifeless. We had to ask the bartender to turn the music on and increase the volume twice. This was particularly frustrating since we were there to celebrate my partner's birthday. Despite the atmosphere, the food and service were excellent. Corbin's, you should be providing an environment, not a meditation room. Please ensure the music is playing when the place is open. Otherwise, did you not want us there?

yelp:test:12641.para:

yelp:test:12659.para:
Not very satisfied... The service and staff representation were really poor, and there was a total lack of knowledge. When we requested a change, like no spicy mayo, they seemed offended. And for $36 on four half orders of Maki Rolls, we should have been the ones to feel wronged.

We ordered two of the seven-course tasting menus, each costing around $59. The meal included three salads, two appetizers, and two main courses, all placed on a single plate. We didn't ask for each course to be split between two people, but they combined everything! Absolutely lazy!

The salads were bland, but the potskickers were fantastic. The dumplings were forgettable. The "lobster pancakes" tasted nothing like lobster and had too much mushroom. The spicy shrimp entree was good, with nice flavor and spice. The roasted flank steak was just okay, served with fried spinach, which was a nice touch. During the tasting menu, we were given a choice between fried rice and wasabi mashed potatoes for our main courses. We weren't asked about our preference and were automatically given the wasabi mashed potatoes.

I understand what they are trying to do, but you can't read the menus, literally. \nFood was hit and miss, more miss than hit. Way too much dressing/seasoning masking the actual taste of what you eat. They promote \""family style\"" but quantity can not replace quality.
yelp:test:12660.para: I didn't really pay attention to it... This place is pitch black. I get what they're aiming for, but the menus are practically unreadable. yelp:test:12679.para:
During our August trip to Las Vegas, my five friends and I dined at a Satay restaurant after a long day at the Grand Canyon. We found the place on Yelp and were drawn by the star ratings. The ambiance was pleasant and well-decorated, and we asked for an outdoor table. The menu was extensive, and we ordered Roti Canai and Vegetable Curry Samosas. Both dishes were Indian and incredibly tasty, so we ordered an extra Roti Canai.

We also enjoyed Nasi Lemak with curry chicken, served with coconut rice. The chicken was delicious, and we added a half-boiled egg and cucumber. For another dish, we had Nasi Goreng, which was shrimp and squid fried rice with a half-cooked omelet, and it was quite yummy, with flavorful shrimp. The Singapore Fried Noodles, a vegetarian dish without egg, was perfectly cooked and delicious. We tried the Green Curry, made with peppers, coconut milk, and eggplant, and found it satisfactory.

The online menu was clear and mostly had images, and we didn't find the dishes too spicy, so we requested extra chili sauce. I'm not sure about the local crowd, but we were fortunate to have this experience.

yelp:test:12683.orig: overpriced, small portions. There's far better food for the same price range.
yelp:test:12683.para: The portions are too small and the prices are high; you can find much better food at a similar cost.

yelp:test:12698.orig: I am usually not hugely into macarons, but these were excellent. I really loved the chocolate one, the frosting inside was dreamy and the texture was perfect. I also enjoyed my coffee and my meal - brioche French Toast. But I would have preferred real maple syrup instead of the caramel sauce it came with. But maybe that's just the northeasterner in me. Anyway, a good experience, with good service (although not the most pleasant atmosphere, being by a busy street/shopping center). I will be back for the macarons!
yelp:test:12698.para: While I don't typically have a big fondness for macarons, these were exceptional. I particularly adored the chocolate variety; the filling was incredibly smooth, and the texture was just right. I also savored my coffee and the brioche French toast. However, I would have preferred real maple syrup over the caramel sauce. Perhaps that's just my Northeastern taste. Overall, it was a pleasant experience with excellent service, despite the somewhat bustling atmosphere. I look forward to returning for the macarons!

yelp:test:12702.para:

yelp:test:12706.orig:
Had a tuna sandwich, which was OK, and a cup of flat coffee that I didn't finish.  This was $9.50... a bit steep. 

The layout is awful... the kitchen bisects the seating area, and all of the kitchen noise is audible (read: deafening) in the seating areas.  

I asked for milk in coffee and was told the half and half was behind me.  Half and Half is the farthest thing from milk in the universe. 

Won't be back.
yelp:test:12706.para:
I had a tuna sandwich that was just okay, and a cup of flat coffee that I didn't even finish; the total came to $9.50, which felt a bit pricey. 

The restaurant's layout is terrible—the kitchen cuts through the seating area, and the noise from the kitchen is incredibly loud and disruptive in the dining space.

When I requested milk in my coffee, I was told the half and half was right behind me, but half and half is nothing like milk—it's the opposite.

I won't be returning.

yelp:test:12727.orig: CRAVINGS BUFFET\nThis is a decent buffet in the Mirage at Las Vegas. It's definitely improved over the years. I recall going there as a kid in the early 90's, where I met tennis star, Michael Chang, and got his autograph. Wide variety of foods here, but fast forward to 2008 and beyond, where the Cravings Buffet has expanded and vastly improved. There is quite an international feel to the buffet, ranging from Americano to Mexicano to Asian (Chinese, Japanese, Vietnamese). Lots of cut meats to choose from and plenty of soups to try! Desserts included cakes, tarts, bread pudding, and a gelato bar! Drinks are free, so drink up if you're into fruit juices: orange, cranberry, apple, etc. Service was great too, as they servers regularly cleaned our tables and refilled our drinks. The food is arrayed around the the dining area in a wide circular arc, making you walk a bit to find your favorite foods (a little exercise within the buffet compound). Not a bad buffet in Las Vegas. Not the best, but hey, it's not Bellagio!
yelp:test:12727.para: The CRAVINGS Buffet at Mirage, Las Vegas, has significantly improved since my childhood visits in the early 90s, when I met tennis champion Michael Chang. Today, it offers a diverse array of cuisines, including American, Mexican, and Asian dishes (Chinese, Japanese, and Vietnamese). There's a wide selection of meats and an assortment of soups. Desserts feature cakes, tarts, bread pudding, and a gelato station. Free drinks, such as orange, cranberry, and apple juices, are available. The service is excellent, with servers keeping tables clean and refilling drinks. The food is arranged in a circular display, encouraging you to explore different options. While it's not the top buffet in Vegas, it's a solid choice, especially compared to the more upscale options like Bellagio.

yelp:test:12735.orig:
I'll start with 4 stars for the Bayside Buffet, located in Mandalay Bay, for the food. They kept the shrimp coming, they had some really killer steak, and the fruit was ripe and edible.

However, they had us standing just inside their entry area for about 15 minutes while they tried to figure out if they could accommodate our group of 10, regardless of the fact that we had told them they could just split us up and put us anywhere. We could see huge expanses of tables open. No idea what the hell was going on there. By the time we had been seated, several of the guys had already gone and eaten two plates worth of breakfast.

Drinks were served quickly enough, though there was some confusion as to who ordered what.

Price was reasonable for a buffet with the quality of food they had. But there is a lot of competition in this town. I seriously didn't need to be standing there that long, caffeine-less.
yelp:test:12735.para:
I'll give the Bayside Buffet at Mandalay Bay 4 stars for the food. The shrimp was plentiful, the steak was outstanding, and the fruit was fresh and tasty.

However, we waited about 15 minutes just inside the entry area while they tried to figure out how to seat our group of 10, despite us already knowing they could split us up. There were plenty of empty tables nearby. I'm still not sure what the issue was. By the time we were seated, a few of the guys had already finished two plates of breakfast.

Drinks were served promptly, though there was some mix-up with the orders. 

The price was fair for the quality of food, but the wait at the entry was unnecessary and left me feeling a bit cranky without my morning caffeine.

yelp:test:12789.para:
To start, here’s a quote directly from Caesar's Qua Baths and Spa’s website:

"Drawing inspiration from its water theme, the cool blue hues, slate, and stone create an ambiance as you explore Qua's various facilities or relax in the Tea Room, complete with a Tea Sommelier."

I often caution my friends against building overly grand expectations, as the subsequent disappointment can be significant. Unfortunately, I didn’t heed my own advice this time. : ) I envisioned settling in the snow room with a freshly brewed tea, prepared by the Tea Sommelier. Growing up in an area heavily influenced by Asian culture, I was particularly drawn to the health and aesthetic benefits of a custom-brewed cup of tea by a Sommelier. However, it turned out to be nothing more than instant tea packets for self-service. When I inquired about the Sommelier, the front desk had to consult management to find out what one was.

This was just one issue, but it was the final straw. I was also disappointed to find stray hairs in the brushes, which were left out in the blue lights for disinfection.

yelp:test:12845.orig: The decor is sleek and modern and the food is pretty good too. The crowd is a little pretentious but very friendly. I always have a lot of fun here and it's my alternative to Scottsdale if I don't want to get all dressed up or if I want to do a Sunday Funday.
yelp:test:12845.para: The interior is sleek and contemporary, and the cuisine is quite satisfactory as well. The atmosphere is a bit on the pretentious side, yet the people are very amiable. I consistently enjoy myself here and it serves as a relaxed alternative to Scottsdale when I don't feel like dressing up or when I'm in the mood for a casual Sunday outing.

yelp:test:12880.orig:
Mlife Black gave us a free room at The Mirage and a free meal here.  So who are we to turn down some free food?  Mr. W. and I just so happened to take my parents to Vegas for them to be tourists like good children one weekend and this offer pretty much just fell into our laps.  So let's eat some meat!!!

After having the best Brazilian BBQ in Vegas, I was hoping for a similar experience.  ""Disappointment"" seemed to be on the menu.  While the hostesses were rude and the waitress was no where to be seen majority of the time, the lovely servers with their sticks of grilled meats were always out and about between tables.  They kindly gave us these red-and-green colored things to let them know when they can bother us with more meat and when to give us a break.  They seemed pretty oblivious to this though and just kept wandering by.  I really don't mind since they're really just showing off all they had to offer and there was a pretty good variety but everything was so ridiculously dry.  

Bite after bite of beyond-well-done meats were piled onto our plates and something within the first ten bites made my stomach churn.  ""Where's the bathroom?"" I had asked politely to a snoot
yelp:test:12880.para:
Mlife Black provided us with a complimentary room at The Mirage and a free meal, so we couldn't resist taking advantage of the offer. My parents and I had planned a trip to Vegas to enjoy the city, and this deal seemed like a perfect fit. Let's indulge in some delicious meat!

After enjoying the best Brazilian BBQ in Vegas, I was eager for a similar experience. However, the meal turned out to be a letdown. The hostesses were unfriendly, and the waitress was often absent, but the servers with their meat sticks were always around. They offered us red and green tokens to signal when we wanted more food or a break, but they seemed to ignore these signals and kept checking in. Despite the abundance of options, the meat was extremely dry.

Within the first few bites, the meat was overcooked and my stomach started to feel queasy. I politely asked for the bathroom, but the response was less than helpful.

yelp:test:12884.orig: I've stayed here a few times already for business  and enjoy my stay each time. Havne't had a chance to use their spa yet but it looks really nice with the waterfall inside.  Have only tried eating at La Hacienda.  Margaritas there are good and the guacomole is made right there....but should save that review for La Hacienda.   Would love to bring the family here with me next time.    This hotel seems to be always busy.    Service and facilites overall were nice.
yelp:test:12884.para: I've visited this hotel several times for work, and I always have a pleasant stay. Although I haven't had the chance to use the spa yet, it appears very appealing, especially with its indoor waterfall. My only dining experience was at La Hacienda, where the margaritas are excellent and the guacamole is freshly made. I'll save my full review for La Hacienda. I'd really like to bring my family next time. The hotel seems perpetually busy, and both the service and facilities are quite nice.

yelp:test:12899.orig:
This is SUCH a lovely place to have breakfast!! They get 5 stars based on their vanilla yogurt alone. It's deliciously creamy and it's filled with real vanilla bean seeds. Oh.my.goodness. And for a cup of this, priced the same as a glass of iced tea, it's a steal..

My husband said he's never had fresher tasting fruit in his fruit plate. 

This place completely gets an A+ for their food. And while their prices are high, you are definitely getting your money's worth as far as quality of food and quality service. We went here a few times and really enjoyed ourselves.
yelp:test:12899.para:
This is such a delightful spot for breakfast! Their vanilla yogurt alone earns them five stars—it's wonderfully creamy and packed with real vanilla bean seeds. It's such a treat, especially considering the price, which is comparable to a glass of iced tea. 

My husband remarked that the fruit in his plate was the freshest he's ever tasted. 

The food here is outstanding, receiving an A+ rating. Although the prices are on the higher side, the quality of both the food and service justifies the cost. We visited a few times and had a wonderful experience each time.

yelp:test:12924.orig:
The two star ""I've experienced better"" rating is more than apt in this instance.

The decor of Settebello is very nice and the ovens are cool to look at. It's really easy to get all jazzed about the wood fired oven and unique toppings and flavor combinations. Hell, the website does enough boasting about how original and special the restaurant is. But it all comes down to the food and this pizza just was not good.

At the most basic level your margherita pizza should be the star. And it wasn't. The crust was flavorless and overcharred. Here's my unecessarily lengthy analogy: You know when you make grilled cheese (and c'mon, everyone makes 2 at a time, how could you eat just one?) and the first one comes out perfect but the second one comes out kinda messed up because the pan is probably too hot and there's not enough butter to help the bread brown correctly and the cheese doesn't fully melt because the thing is going to burn if you leave it on any longer? Well this is how my pizza was, it seemed hastily cooked over too high heat and lacked flavor. Not to mention the sauce was bland and the cheese was amorphous and too stringy. There was exactly one basil leaf on my pizza too
yelp:test:12924.para: The "I've experienced better" rating is fitting here. While the decor and ovens at Settebello are appealing, the hype around the wood-fired oven and unique toppings doesn't translate to great food. The margherita pizza, which should be a standout, fell short. The crust was bland and overcooked, much like when you rush to make two grilled cheeses and the second one comes out poorly. The pizza seemed to be cooked too quickly at a high temperature, lacking flavor. The sauce was tasteless, the cheese was stringy and shapeless, and there was only one basil leaf on the entire slice.

yelp:test:12928.orig: I'm def a review kind of girl but I am not sure how this place got such great reviews.  This is some of the most expensive pizza I've ever eaten...  For about $13 a person then to add meats its like an extra $2 per meat...that is crazy.  The drinks were outrageous prices.  The servers were not the friendliest I've seen. My pizza was more or less just a dough mess.  I picked up a slice and everything fell off leaving nothing but flimsy dough.  They asked if I wanted it sliced and of course I said yes but they must have meant creased instead because there were just lines in the pizza... I actually had to cut it myself.  This is def not a place I will ever be going back to.  :(
yelp:test:12928.para: While I usually enjoy reading reviews, I'm quite puzzled by the positive feedback for this place. The pizza is one of the most expensive I've ever tried—around $13 per person, with an additional $2 for each meat topping, which seems excessive. The drinks were also very pricey. The staff wasn't particularly friendly. My pizza was mostly just a doughy mess; when I picked up a slice, everything fell off, leaving only flimsy dough. They asked if I wanted it sliced, but when they cut it, it was just creased, not actually sliced. I definitely won't be returning here. :-(

yelp:test:12993.orig:
As you will see from my reviews I have eaten at high end steak places in NY, Philadelphia and DC.....this is definitely in the top 5 of all of them.   

We went here with a group and ate on a thursday night, we had no problem getting a table for 4 at 8pm with reservations.   

I had the lobster with bacon appetizer which was honestly the lowlight of my meal but still very good.   My wife had a beet salad which looked nice and a friend of mine split onion rings with the table.   The free fries were also amazing and we loved the different sauces.

Next came the main courses.   My wife ordered a filet done perfectly.   My friends GF had the halibut which was also excellent.   I had the regular rib eye and the king crap options as did my friend.   Let me just say this steak was seasoned and cooked PERFECTLY.   The king crap legs that were the side were amazing.   They were split and all of the good parts were left.   A great addition! 

We got the mashed potato sides  as well as a mushroom that was part of a forrest fire.   

I think that this is a great steakhouse and a great place to eat.   I would highly recommend this place in LV.
yelp:test:12993.para:
I've dined at some upscale steak restaurants in New York, Philadelphia, and Washington D.C., and this place ranks among the top five. We visited on a Thursday evening with a group, and we were able to secure a table for four by 8 PM with reservations, which was not an issue.

For starters, I tried the lobster with bacon, which, while not my favorite, was still quite good. My wife enjoyed a beet salad that looked appealing, and a friend shared onion rings with the rest of us. The complimentary fries were outstanding, and we relished the various sauces.

Moving on to the main courses, my wife had a perfectly cooked filet mignon, and my friend's girlfriend opted for halibut, which was also superb. I chose a regular rib eye and the king crab option, and I must say, the steak was flawlessly seasoned and cooked. The king crab legs, which were a side, were exceptional; they were split, and all the best parts were included. A fantastic addition!

We also ordered the mashed potatoes and a mushroom side that was part of a forest fire dish. Overall, I believe this is an excellent steakhouse, and I highly recommend it to anyone in Las Vegas.

yelp:test:13033.orig:
This is a hotel that could be great & maybe it was in times gone by. First Staff is great doing all they can with what they have to work with... It's still being renovated but any standard Holiday Inn would be a better deal. 

Rooms look nice but lamps don't work... They forgot the business traveler when they did the renovation... The desk in my room is by the window so can't see the TV & no plugs within 8 feet of the thing... Plus they have the nerve to charge $9.99 for internet...

The bar/restaurant is by the pool & is a giant cavern... Ordered a steak came with a case knife to cut it... Bartender is a nice fellow but the place closes at 9pm... Really!

All in all whoever owns this place or is in charge of the renovation needs to go back to Hospitality school & learn what the public wants in a hotel...
yelp:test:13033.para:
This establishment had potential but seems to fall short of expectations. The staff is commendable, working with limited resources... However, it's still under renovation, and a standard Holiday Inn offers better value. 

The rooms are aesthetically pleasing, but the lamps don't function... The renovation seems to have overlooked business travelers... My desk, positioned by the window, obstructs my view of the TV, and there are no outlets within reach... Additionally, they charge $9.99 for internet access...

The bar and restaurant, located by the pool, feels like a cavernous space... The steak I ordered came with a case knife... The bartender is friendly, but the place closes at 9 PM... Really!

Overall, the management or those overseeing the renovation need to revisit hospitality courses to understand what guests truly desire in a hotel.

yelp:test:13043.orig: Are you bored? Do you want to kill about 2 hours of your time looking at random stuff and end up walking out with things you weren't expecting to buy? Cost Plus World is for you! I don't remember how I heard about this place, but I remember my first time here. I spent about 2 hours just browsing. And now I'm a fan and still spend a good amount of time here during each visit. \n\nThis store has so much stuff. They have, picture frames, jewelry, furniture, food kitchen stuff and so much more! Everything is so colorful that my attention span is really short. I'll look at something and another thing will catch my eye and I'll completely forget what I was looking at in the first place. My favorite sections in the whole store are the food and the kitchenware. There are so many different snacks to choose from, like vegetable chips to chocolate covered waffles. And I love looking at the candy and spices from all around the world. It's a bit pricier, but you'll find some unique items if you look hard enough. On my last visit, I found a bunch of different flavored Kit Kat. I also love looking at all the mini kitchen stuff! Mini measuring cups, mini whisks, mini bowls...LOVE ALL THE MINIS!!!
yelp:test:13043.para:
Are you looking to spend a couple of hours browsing without a specific goal? Do you enjoy stumbling upon unexpected items? If so, Cost Plus World is the perfect spot for you! I can't recall exactly how I discovered this place, but my initial visit left a lasting impression. I wandered around for about two hours and became a regular, spending ample time there each time.

This store is incredibly diverse, offering everything from picture frames and jewelry to furniture and kitchen supplies, plus a wide array of food items. The vibrant colors are so captivating that I often lose track of what I was initially searching for. My favorite areas are the food and kitchenware sections. There’s an extensive selection of snacks, from vegetable chips to chocolate-covered waffles, and I adore exploring the international candies and spices. While it can be a bit pricey, you can find some truly unique items if you search thoroughly. During my last visit, I found a variety of flavored Kit Kats. I also get a kick out of all the miniature kitchen gadgets, like mini measuring cups, whisks, and bowls—LOVE ALL THE MINIS!!!

yelp:test:13066.orig:
Don't go here. The food came out cold and was way overpriced. Cheaper and tastier meals are everywhere in Vegas, so don't give this place another thought. I would suggest going to Panda Express for a more authentic experience. Yes, Panda Express = More Authentic Experience.

For a city filled with Asian gamblers, it was odd to see no other Asian person dinning at an Asian restaurant (always a big negative in my book). Maybe their frequent game play has given then enough comps to dine elsewhere, so I'll give this place the benefit of the doubt as far a demographically biased portion of my rating goes.

I ordered the prix fixe menu where the main course was braised sea bass. The sea bass was more boiled than braised. It was texturally unappealing and had no flavor. The greens that accompanied it were overcooked and essentially dead. 

I really should have just gone to the food court....
yelp:test:13066.para:
Avoid this place. The food was served cold and was excessively priced. There are plenty of cheaper and tastier options available throughout Las Vegas, so there's no reason to consider this restaurant. I recommend trying Panda Express instead, as it offers a more authentic experience. Yes, Panda Express = More Authentic Experience.

It was peculiar to see no other Asian diners at an Asian restaurant in a city with a large Asian gambling population, which is a significant negative in my opinion. I'll give them the benefit of the doubt regarding the demographic composition, but overall, it was a disappointing experience.

I ordered the prix fixe menu, which included braised sea bass as the main course. The sea bass was more boiled than braised, making it unappealing to the touch and lacking in flavor. The accompanying greens were overcooked and essentially flavorless. I should have just gone to the food court instead.

yelp:test:13093.orig:

We had heard only good things about this place, both on Yelp and from friends and co-workers that have been. We headed in and the black out curtains immediately made it feel like nighttime inside. After picking a seat at the bar we took a look at the menu and debated on the options.

The staff was very friendly and checked in on us regularly. We were so stuffed we didn't get dessert this go-round, h
yelp:test:13093.para:
A fantastic approach to reaching 300 reviews!

We'd heard nothing but positive feedback about this establishment, both from Yelp and from friends and colleagues who had visited. We entered and the blackout curtains instantly created a nighttime ambiance. We chose seats at the bar and perused the menu, discussing our choices. I ordered the Shepherd's Pie (Cottage Pie) Pasty, while he opted for the Oggie. We also decided to share a side of "chips" (fries).

One of the highlights of dining at a bar is observing the staff in action, and this place excelled at that. Not only could we watch the bartenders crafting drinks, but the kitchen was right in front of us, allowing us to see our food being prepared from start to finish!

The food took a little longer to arrive, but it was worth the wait as each dish was made fresh, and the fries were baked, not fried. Both our pasties were absolutely delicious and very satisfying! The fries were perfectly cooked, and it was a pleasant change to enjoy a great pasty and fries without the usual fried fare.

The service was top-notch, with the staff being very attentive and checking in on us regularly. We were so full that we didn't even order dessert this time.

yelp:test:13095.orig: Oh how I love Coffee Bean!  There are none where I live, so I made my co-worker come here for coffee two days in a row. I got my coffee fix with a great white chocolate mocha. Something about their drinks are better - creamier maybe? The service was decent - not exceptional fast, but fine.  They are also located conveniently above the Bouchon kiosk, so we went downstairs to grab pastries after getting coffee.
yelp:test:13095.para: I adore Coffee Bean so much! Unfortunately, none are nearby, so my colleague visited here for coffee over two days. I enjoyed a fantastic white chocolate mocha. Their drinks seem to have a richer texture. The service was satisfactory—not super speedy, but acceptable. Plus, the location is perfect, right above the Bouchon kiosk, so we went down to pick up some pastries after our coffee.

yelp:test:13173.orig: only two stars cuz the food tasted good. i had the bonzai, which is ok. i think the carls jr. teriyaki burger tastes better though. my bf got a royal red robin and it was ok for him too. we also had some coleslaw and mac n' cheese but they never brought out napkins and utensils. we asked for some and we got napkins but the guy said the utensils were being washed. we thought that was weird but w/e. halfway through our meal and we still didnt get it. when we finished, we sat around for probably 10 minutes before we were noticed. they gave us to go boxes for our stuff and asked if we needed our check but we waited another while before we got it... maybe the staff has memory issues or something... our server came by and asked us how we were doing and i mentioned that we never got our utensils so she apologized and told her manager. the manager ended up comping the whole meal so we didn't have to pay at all. i'd prolly go to red robin again, just not this location...
yelp:test:13173.para: I gave it two stars because the food was decent. I tried the Bonzai, which was alright, but I think the Carls Jr. Teriyaki Burger is better. My boyfriend had the Royal Red Robin, and it was fine for him too. We also had some coleslaw and mac and cheese, but they never brought napkins or utensils. We asked for them, and they gave us napkins but said the utensils were being washed. That seemed odd, but we let it go. We didn't receive our food until halfway through our meal, and we had to wait about 10 minutes before the staff noticed us. They offered to box up our food and asked if we needed our checks, but we had to wait a bit longer. Maybe the staff has memory issues. Our server checked on us and mentioned the lack of utensils, so she apologized and informed the manager. The manager ended up covering the entire meal for us, so we didn't have to pay. I might visit Red Robin again, just not this particular location.

yelp:test:13214.orig:
Gotta love historic theaters playing off beat, artistic, foreign, documentary, etc films. Don't expect Transformers 18 to be on the marquee here. Check Harkins website for shows, show times and upcoming films. Films usually have a short run (1-2 weeks tops) so if you see one you like make sure you jump on it while it's still playing. 

Parking for theater or anywhere on Mill: the Lot behind the condos off Ash in between 5th and 3rd, near Macayo's, the lot behind Z-Tejas off Maple, pay parking in the garage of Brickyard, east passed Urban Outfitters, more pay parking (not on weekends past a certain time - check City of Tempe for hours - off 5th and Forest Avenue - also close to lightrail station). Street parking with meters in front of House of Tricks and a mega lot that's new off University and College. 

Overall: Great alternative to your typical dinner and a movie - try a movie here, and dinner at one of the great Mill Ave dining locales (La Bocca, House of Tricks, Cafe Boa, Canteen, Rula Bula, Z-Tejas etc)
yelp:test:13214.para:
Sure, here's the paraphrased text:

Historic theaters often screen unique films like offbeat, artistic, foreign, or documentary movies. You won't find blockbuster action films here; instead, check the Harkins website for showtimes and upcoming titles. Most films have a short run (1-2 weeks), so if you find something you like, catch it quickly. 

For parking, options include the lot behind the condos on Ash between 5th and 3rd, near Macayo's, or the lot behind Z-Tejas on Maple. There's also pay parking in the Brickyard garage, east of Urban Outfitters, and more pay spots (weekdays only, check City of Tempe for details) off 5th and Forest Avenue, near the light rail station. Street parking with meters is available in front of House of Tricks and in a new mega lot off University and College.

In summary, these theaters offer a fantastic alternative to conventional dinner-and-a-movie experiences. Consider watching a film here and then enjoying dinner at one of the many great Mill Avenue restaurants like La Bocca, House of Tricks, Cafe Boa, Canteen, Rula Bula, or Z-Tejas.

yelp:test:13219.orig: Horrible.  So disappointed.  The food was old and tasted like cafeteria food.  Even the crab legs tasted off.  I am one to always try something once always give it a second chance, but I'm breaking my own rule and saying STAY AWAY!!!!
yelp:test:13219.para: Terrible experience. I'm deeply let down. The food was stale and had the same taste as cafeteria food. Even the crab legs were disappointing. Usually, I give places a second chance, but in this case, I'm breaking my own rule and strongly advise you to avoid it!!!!

yelp:test:13226.orig:
I'm a regular. A nice Greek family owns the place. They remember me and treat my family and guests like royalty.

I stopped by near closing one night after taking the kids to look at Christmas lights. To my surprise they made a couple of phone calls and next thing you know, Santa Claus was at my table.

5 stars for service. 4 stars because food quality has been inconsistent. Never bad, but one of their chefs is hands down better than the others.
yelp:test:13226.para:
I frequent this establishment, where a friendly Greek family runs the place. They recognize me and extend warm hospitality to my family and guests, treating us as honored guests.

One evening, after dropping off the kids to see the Christmas lights, I stopped by close to closing time. To my delight, they made some calls, and before long, Santa Claus appeared at my table.

The service is outstanding, earning 5 stars. However, the food quality has been a bit inconsistent, rated 4 stars overall. While it's never been bad, one of their chefs consistently delivers superior dishes compared to the others.

yelp:test:13268.orig:
I just moved to Vegas from California and I've been to three salons so far.  Jeff at Mosaic has definitely done the best job with my hair so far.

Before checking out Mosaic, I went to Tonic II and Kelly Cardenas.  In terms of the salon itself both Tonic and Kelly Cardenas are nicer and trendier as Mosaic kind of looks like a strip mall of hair stations.  

I wasn't offered a drink at Mosaic, the waiting area is small and tight.  They've crammed a clothing boutique into the lobby, don't really understand that, but whatever, I was there to get my hair cut, not for anything else.  If you're big on customer service or ambience you're definitely better off at one of the other two salons though.

Onto the haircut itself. Jeff is incredibly professional. He took the time to go over his credentials with my, which by the way, are quite impressive! Find out exactly what I want done with my hair, why I wasn't happy with my last two haircuts then explained to me why the last two stylists weren't able to achieve the look I was after.  He was very friendly and talked to me just about the entire time he was cutting my hair.  Overall, I'm pretty satisfied.  He took a bit too  much length of
yelp:test:13268.para:
I recently relocated to Vegas from California and have visited three salons so far. Jeff at Mosaic has provided the best hair service among them.

Before trying Mosaic, I went to Tonic II and Kelly Cardenas. While both Tonic and Kelly Cardenas have a nicer, trendier vibe, Mosaic feels more like a strip mall with multiple hair stations.

At Mosaic, I didn't receive a drink, and the waiting area is small and cramped. They've added a clothing boutique to the lobby, which I don't quite understand, but it's not my main concern since I was there for a haircut. If you prioritize customer service or ambiance, you might want to consider one of the other two salons.

Now, about the haircut. Jeff is very professional. He went over his impressive credentials with me and thoroughly discussed my preferences. He explained why my last two haircuts didn't meet my expectations and why the previous stylists couldn't achieve the look I wanted. He was friendly throughout the process and kept talking to me while cutting my hair. Overall, I'm quite satisfied, though he trimmed a bit more length than I intended.

yelp:test:13330.orig: JD did my VCH piercing today and I was SO nervous and he was very understanding & helped me calm down.he did a great job doing my piercing!! Very clean place and very friendly staff.  :)
yelp:test:13330.para: Today, JD performed my VCH piercing, and I was extremely anxious. However, he was incredibly patient and supportive, helping me relax. He did an excellent job with the piercing! The place was very clean, and the staff was very friendly. 😊

yelp:test:13334.orig: I was in for lunch yesterday and had a great experience! The food was really good and the service was even better! My server Melanie was very personable and helpful. Couldn't of asked for a better lunch!
yelp:test:13334.para: Yesterday, I enjoyed a fantastic lunch where the food was delicious and the service outstanding. My server, Melanie, was particularly friendly and accommodating. It was truly the perfect lunch!

yelp:test:13347.orig:
Having stayed 4 nights with an initial problem described in my first review, I have to say that there are definitely some pluses but the customer service at the front desk is still abysmal. Checking out, not one person smiled at any customer, there were no ""I hope you enjoyed your stay"" or ""Please come back soon"" type of comments to be heard. These are, IMO, essential service points at any hotel. 

On the plus side, the service when calling through the room operator is good, hangers brought up quickly, electrical issues resolved smoothly. Also, the movie theater and food court come in very handy for good entertainment and quick snacks. Valet parking attendants are courteous.

Improving front desk service, fixing the slow elevators, and adding coffee/water in rooms would bring this hotel up to the level of other hotels I've used in Las Vegas like the Signature MGM and The Venetian.
yelp:test:13347.para:
After spending 4 nights there, despite an initial issue mentioned in my first review, I must acknowledge some positive aspects. However, the front desk customer service remains extremely poor. During check-out, no one greeted or bid farewell to guests, which, in my opinion, are crucial elements of good service. 

On the bright side, the room operator service is efficient, with hangers and electrical issues handled promptly. The movie theater and food court offer great entertainment and quick snacks. Additionally, the valet parking staff is polite.

To match the standards of other Las Vegas hotels such as the Signature MGM and The Venetian, the hotel should enhance its front desk service, address the slow elevators, and provide coffee or water in the rooms.
