yelp:test:15911.para:
I booked a room there solely for a convention at Planet Hollywood, but I was let down by the "resort." The parking was a significant issue; it’s a 15-minute walk, and if you ride a motorcycle, you can’t use valet, so you’ll have to carry your bags a considerable distance. Before booking, I inquired about motorcycle parking and was assured there would be plenty, but upon arrival, I had to navigate an 800-pound motorcycle through bicycles and scooters parked haphazardly. 

Upon reaching the reservation desk, the cashier informed me that I couldn’t opt to pay cash at check-out; my credit card would be placed on "hold," essentially holding my funds as a form of ransom. Other hotels I’ve stayed at didn’t require this, and they were happy to have my credit card information without holding funds.

Navigating to the elevators, I noticed Britney Spears posters everywhere. The decor felt outdated, and the room wasn’t as clean as expected. Upon entering, the room smelled strongly of cigarette smoke, and I found an ashtray. I contacted the front desk, only to learn that they had mistakenly placed us in a smoking room.

yelp:test:15914.orig: Spent the midweek at a safety conference here. Last day a large amount of attendees contracted Norovirus and became violently ill. I will say, however, that before that incident, the room service was actually pretty good, both dinner and breakfast. The blinds in the room didn't completely block out the sunlight in the morning and you can't adjust them  horizontally because of their vertical design. We believe the Norovirus came from the food served at the conference.
yelp:test:15914.para: Attended a safety conference mid-week, and on the final day, many participants fell ill with Norovirus. Despite that, the room service had been quite satisfactory, with both dinner and breakfast being enjoyable. The issue with the blinds was that they didn't fully block morning sunlight and were vertically designed, so they couldn't be adjusted horizontally. We suspect the conference food was the source of the Norovirus outbreak.

yelp:test:15949.orig: 5-6pm is free sangria, all you can drink wine, along with appetizers.  Staff is super friendly, accomodating, and just darn wonderful.  Concierge helped us book tours.  Staff changed our room for us.  We forgot tons of stuff, and they were able to hook us up with a steamer for my blouse, hair straightener that I forgot.  Pool has a sandy beach.  Wifi free if you you're inTouch member and we got $10 free money for frig bar.  We dock one star for wiFI always being out in the morning, which was inconvenient.  Also the \""resort' is more of an overstatement as it's not a really a resort.  More a very nicely remodeled old hotel complex with 2 pools, 1 pretty lagoon, and 1 spa service area.  It's not a Scottsdale resort that you would imagine.  No bike trails, no golf course.
yelp:test:15949.para: From 5-6pm, there's complimentary sangria and all-you-can-drink wine, plus appetizers. The staff is incredibly friendly, accommodating, and wonderful; they even helped us book tours and changed our room. They provided a steamer for my blouse and a hair straightener when we forgot these items. The pool features a sandy beach area. If you're an inTouch member, you get free Wi-Fi and $10 for the mini-fridge bar. We deducted one star for Wi-Fi issues in the morning, which was inconvenient. While it's called a resort, it's more like a well-renovated old hotel complex with two pools, a lagoon, and spa services. It doesn't quite match the Scottsdale resort experience you might expect, lacking bike trails and a golf course.

yelp:test:15953.orig: STAY AWAY! My husband and I checked this place out online and every search engine had nice reviews, so we booked. Upon arrival, we went to our room, which was more like a motel. The smells in the breezeways were as if they sprayed potpourri over an existing musty stench. Our room was facing a parking lot and smelled musty. We requested another room not facing a parking lot, they moved us over to an \""oasis\"" view,which was hardly an oasis. After spending just a few minutes, we checked out. The smells were horrific. I must say the staff was very nice and refunded our money through booking.com. The lobby looked lovely but nothing like the online pictures. For $250+ a night, we took our money elsewhere.
yelp:test:15953.para: AVOID IT! We read great reviews online and decided to book, but our experience was disappointing. Upon arrival, our room, which felt more like a motel, had a musty smell, even with potpourri sprayed in the breezeways. The room faced a parking lot, adding to the unpleasant odor. We asked for a different room, and they moved us to one with an "oasis" view, but it was far from relaxing. We only stayed a short while before checking out due to the overwhelming smells. The staff was kind and refunded our booking.com payment. While the lobby was attractive, it didn't match the online photos. At $250+ per night, we opted to find a better option elsewhere.

yelp:test:15966.orig: Just finished dining here. Best meal I've had in Vegas on this vacation. Beautiful view, friendly service and incredible food. They paced the four course meal well. If you don't mind spending the little extra dough go for it, you won't be disappointed.
yelp:test:15966.para: After enjoying dinner here, this was the standout meal of my Vegas trip. The ambiance was stunning, the staff was welcoming, and the cuisine was outstanding. They managed the four-course meal perfectly. If you're willing to splurge a bit more, it's definitely worth it; you won't regret it.

yelp:test:15984.orig:
Another one of those things you have to try at least once if you are visiting Pittsburgh for the very first time.  I had seen them on Travel Channel as one of the Top 10 places in the country to Pig Out.  So when we came to Pittsburgh, PA, and was on vacation, I had to try it.  

It was as good as advertised.  They put the French Fries in the Sandwich and it is definitely quite unique.  

If I am ever back in Pittsburgh, I will definitely grab me another Primanti Brothers Sandwich to Pig Out On!!!
yelp:test:15984.para:
If you're visiting Pittsburgh for the first time, you should definitely try this place—it's one of the top spots featured on the Travel Channel for indulging. When we were on vacation in Pittsburgh, PA, I made sure to give it a try. 

It lived up to the hype; they serve French fries inside the sandwich, which is quite a unique twist. 

If I return to Pittsburgh, I'll definitely order another Primanti Brothers Sandwich to really indulge!

yelp:test:16015.orig: The Pork Empanada was AMAZING!  My mom & daughter both got the Bistec and it was wonderful!  Very tender and delicious beef.  The Cuban Sushi roll, Asian Tartare & Ginger Tataki were also very good.  The Sangria of the Day was ok.   We'll definitely go back.  A perfect place to stop before or after the theater.
yelp:test:16015.para: The Pork Empanada was outstanding! Both my mom and daughter enjoyed the Bistec, which was exceptionally tender and tasty. The Cuban Sushi roll, Asian Tartare, and Ginger Tataki were also quite good. While the Sangria of the Day was just satisfactory, we plan to return. It's an ideal spot to visit before or after the movies.

yelp:test:16041.orig: I have been back several times before writing this review update just to make sure all the inconsistency that I have been experiencing is now the way of Bagel Cafe and not just an off day they were having. Sure we all know the best breakfast in town is at the Omelet House on Charleston, but this place definitely came close behind at one point. In the last 6 months I have experienced meals here at Bagel Cafe that were just not worth the money or wait for what you got. They don't even use Boar's Head deli meats anymore! WTH?!?!?!? They use some brand I have never heard of. The taste and quality of the deli meat just isn't the same as it used to be. They claim the bagels are made fresh daily yet they are rock hard. I have never liked the bagels here, but if it's in your name.... live up to it!\n\nAs you can tell from my previous review and pictures, I really used to like this place. Consistency is
yelp:test:16041.para: I've visited Bagel Cafe multiple times before writing this review to ensure that the inconsistencies I've noticed are not just a one-off issue. I understand that loyal customers might be disappointed, but if you've been eating here since it opened, you'll agree that it's not the same. I started frequenting Bagel Cafe when I was a teenager, and the food was consistently excellent, making the long wait for a table worthwhile. While the Omelet House on Charleston is known for the best breakfast in town, Bagel Cafe was a strong contender. However, in the past six months, the meals have been disappointing, not just in taste but also in value for the price and wait time. They no longer use Boar's Head deli meats; instead, they use an unfamiliar brand. The quality and taste of the deli meat are far from what they used to be. Despite claiming to make bagels fresh daily, they are rock hard. I've never been a fan of the bagels here, but if they're in the name, they should live up to it. As you can see from my previous review and photos, I used to really enjoy this place, but consistency is key.

yelp:test:16045.orig:
5 stars for a simple market and deli with some killer good freshly prepared food.

I've been coming here for years.  I find the portions to be reasonable, and the quality of the food top notch.  Go to the counter, place  your order, and they'll call you up to do a pick up when it's ready.

Nothing like going in for a quick lunch and walking out with a bunch of grocery items, a chunk of feta, a pound of tabbouleh, and a bag of freshly baked pita breads.

I'm a fan of their food overall.  There are excellent options for vegetarians.  They also make outstanding stuffed grape leaves.  True story- during one of my pregnancies I craved these, and went twice a week to get them.  They are as good now as they were then.

There is seating here, so you can go with a small group and have lunch easily.

Don't forget to pick up some freshly prepared baklava for dessert!
yelp:test:16045.para:
Five stars for this simple market and deli that serves up some fantastic, freshly prepared food. I've been a regular customer for years, and I appreciate the reasonable portion sizes and top-notch food quality. You order at the counter, and they'll call you when your items are ready for pickup.

It's great to pop in for a quick lunch and come out with a variety of grocery items, including feta cheese, tabbouleh, and freshly baked pita breads.

I enjoy their food overall, and they offer excellent vegetarian options. Their stuffed grape leaves are outstanding; I used to crave them during pregnancy and would visit twice a week, and they remain just as delicious now.

There's seating available, so you can bring a small group and have a meal here. And don't miss out on their freshly prepared baklava for dessert!

yelp:test:16122.orig: Without a doubt one of the better (and quieter) hotel options in Vegas. Room amenities - as described by previous reviewers - are unbelievable. 5 stars if Platinum introduces a shuttle service to the Strip !
yelp:test:16122.para: Undoubtedly, this is one of the superior and more tranquil hotel choices in Vegas. The room amenities, as noted by other reviewers, are outstanding. If Platinum could add a shuttle service to the Strip, it would deserve a perfect 5-star rating!

yelp:test:16183.orig:
All my animals that have been apart of my life have come from being adopted from Arizona Humane Society.  

My last mut was only $35 to adopt but he's truly a mut so if I didn't adopt him I don't think anyone would have LOL nonetheless he's my little guy.

I like the AZ Humane Society because I know the animals are well cared for and have been given all the up to date shots that they need.  

They are netured and given a wellness exam plus you get get complimentary medicine if needed for the common colds that animals can catch at places like these.  You also get a free basic office visit at participating veternarians.

Sadly, if you have to put one of your animals down like I did about eight months ago you can do it here much cheaper than at a vet who charge astronomical prices to euthanize.

I don't get how death of a loved one and or animal is such big business.
yelp:test:16183.para:
All the animals in my life have been adopted from the Arizona Humane Society. My last mixed-breed dog was only $35 to adopt, and even though he's a mix, I'm grateful to have him. If I hadn't adopted him, I doubt anyone else would have given him a chance.

I appreciate the Arizona Humane Society because I know the animals are well-cared-for and receive all necessary vaccinations. They also provide a wellness exam and offer free medicine for common illnesses, like the colds that animals can get. Additionally, you get a free basic office visit at participating veterinarians.

Sadly, if you need to euthanize an animal, it's much more affordable here compared to a vet, where the prices for euthanasia can be extremely high. It's hard to understand how the death of a loved one or an animal can be such a profitable business.

yelp:test:16184.orig: I love the Arizona Humane Society !\n\nThey are the only organization I will adopt my pets from.  The employees are nice and truly care about the animals.  The adoption fees are reasonable and the kennels are always clean.
yelp:test:16184.para: I have a great affection for the Arizona Humane Society! It's the sole place where I would adopt pets. The staff there are very kind and genuinely concerned about the animals. The adoption costs are fair, and the kennels are consistently clean.

yelp:test:16218.orig: I've never had a bad time at Koi, I don't know why it seems so many other reviewers hated it. Yes they do add a 18% gratuity but I appreciate that cause I don't have to tabulate a tip. I love their sushi, specifically The Minnesota I think it's called. It comes out really hot with yummy spicy mayo and it is to DIE for. There's a older asian lady who works there who is a hoot! She has a great sense of humor, you really must talk to her.
yelp:test:16218.para: I've always enjoyed my visits to Koi, and I can't understand why so many reviewers found it disappointing. While they do include a 18% gratuity, I appreciate that it simplifies the tipping process for me. Their sushi is outstanding, and I particularly adore The Minnesota—it's served piping hot with delicious spicy mayo, and it's absolutely amazing. There's an older Asian lady who works there who is incredibly entertaining; she has a fantastic sense of humor, and you really should chat with her.

yelp:test:16234.orig: Terrible experience there today. I got our food to go, and it was packaged improperly. Refried beans got all over everything-- everything in the same bag and my vehicle. The lettuce on the tacos de carne asada was cooked, and the chorizo cheese dip was atrocious. The container was quite literally half filled with orange grease. It was disgusting. It's sitting, uneaten, on my counter right now, and I paid $4 for said dip.  Finally, most of the food was too salty to eat.  I was never head-over-hills for this place, but now I will never go again.
yelp:test:16234.para: Today, I had a really bad experience with my takeout order. The food was improperly packaged, causing refried beans to spill into everything, including the same bag and my car. The lettuce on the carne asada tacos was overcooked, and the chorizo cheese dip was so bad, it was practically swimming in grease. I couldn't even finish it because it was so greasy. The dip, which cost me $4, was in a container that was barely half full of orange grease. The food was also way too salty. I wasn't a fan of this place to begin with, but now I definitely won't be returning.

yelp:test:16240.orig:
This event is over-hyped and is nothing but a hipster infestation.

The amount of galleries to look at aren't much, and half of them have a snobby feel to them. Some of the street vendors can be like this as well.

Parking is absolute hell, and you must park far away from the event. It will take a while to even find parking since downtown is so convoluted.

However, a tip is to park at the Las Vegas Academy student parking area. You won't get towed for this. Besides, there's some students present who have to stay late a night for theatre rehearsals. Plus, LVA itself promotes First Friday to its students (particularly the 'art majors'), so feel free to park at LVA if you don't mind walking a bit to the event.

The food sold at First Friday is overpriced, although they do have very good funnel cakes. Still though, I suggest you save money and eat at any of the nearby restaurants instead. You get more bang for your buck that way.

Considering the type of event First Friday is, you'll find all sorts of people dressed in eccentric fashion. It's got everything from goths to rockabilly chicks. It's a great place to go people watching and even get some photo ops.

Regardless, F
yelp:test:16240.para:
This event is often exaggerated and is primarily a gathering of hipsters.

There aren't many galleries to visit, and many of them have an elitist atmosphere. Some street vendors also come across as pretentious.

Parking is a nightmare; you'll need to park far from the event area. Finding a spot can be challenging due to the complex layout of downtown.

A tip is to park at the Las Vegas Academy student lot. You won't face towing there, and you might even spot some students who stay late for rehearsals. Additionally, LVA encourages its students, especially those in art programs, to attend First Friday, so parking there is an option if you're willing to walk a bit.

The food at First Friday is pricey, but they do offer excellent funnel cakes. However, I recommend eating at nearby restaurants instead to get better value for your money.

Given the nature of the event, you'll encounter a variety of people dressed in unique styles, ranging from goths to rockabilly enthusiasts. It's a fantastic spot for people-watching and taking photos.

yelp:test:16243.orig: Good food can be quickly forgotten by bad service.  I'm sorry that you've got the table from hell, but out table is important too!\n\nThe micro brew samplers were interesting and tasty, but nothing else screamed repeat and come back here.
yelp:test:16243.para:
Quality food can easily be overshadowed by poor service. I apologize that your experience was so disappointing, but we want to ensure our table receives the attention it deserves too.

The micro brew samplers were intriguing and enjoyable, but overall, there wasn't enough to make you want to return.

yelp:test:16302.orig: Overall the food is pretty good. Worth going back. Flavorful and moist. I've been here multiple times and it's consistent. I think being consistent is one of the most important attributes of a restaurant. You can't have a great time one time and not the other. This place is better than good but don't go in with the expectation of great.
yelp:test:16302.para: The food is generally quite satisfactory and I'd consider returning. It's flavorful and well-cooked. I've visited several times and find the quality to be consistent. Consistency is key for a restaurant, as you shouldn't have varying experiences. This place exceeds the good category, but don't set your expectations too high for greatness.

yelp:test:16307.orig: This was the worst \""Japanese\"" food my husband and I have ever had. We ordered 5 maki rolls. The pieces were so small they could not be considered pieces of maki. Two of the rolls supposedly had fish, but most of the pieces of maki had no recognizable fish inside. The rolls were so poorly made that they fell apart when we picked them up with the chopsticks. The taste was terrible. The wasabi wasn't real. It had the consistency of diarrhea and was dyed green. We felt sad after the meal, and cheated out of $45. First and last time ever eating here.
yelp:test:16307.para: Our experience with the Japanese food was the worst we've ever had. We ordered five maki rolls, but the pieces were so tiny they hardly qualified as maki. Only two rolls contained any visible fish, and the rest had no discernible fish inside. The rolls were so poorly constructed that they disintegrated when we tried to pick them up with chopsticks. The taste was awful, and the wasabi was fake, resembling diarrhea and dyed green. We felt disappointed and cheated out of $45. This will be our first and last time dining here.

yelp:test:16315.orig: We used to shop there on a regular basis, as well as use the pharmacy.  Not anymore.  Tired of the long lines and 2 cashiers working and employees who are there just to make their paycheck and go home.  Managers are completely clueless and do not know how to respond to a complaint.   The pharmacy never has what I need, never calls to let you know when something is ready, even when they said, \""we will call you when it is in\"" Never, not even once.  That is extremely poor customer service and that makes people like me to stop using this store.  They need to hire a customer service guru or just someone who has some common sense to retrain every employee.   If you work someplace, own it, respect your customers or you lose business, it's that simple. To the managers constantly standing around, maybe you should be checking on your departments and customers to see if everything is going ok.  That's what makes a good store and you get repeat business.    It's to bad, this was close to home but we've decided that our last visit was the final straw, we will not be returning.
yelp:test:16315.para: We used to frequent this store regularly, including for pharmacy needs, but no longer do. The long lines with only two cashiers and employees solely focused on their shifts are frustrating. Management seems unaware of how to handle customer complaints effectively. The pharmacy frequently lacks the items I need and fails to call when they say they will, even when they promise to. This is poor customer service, which is why I no longer shop there. They need to hire someone skilled in customer service or retrain their staff with basic common sense. If you work somewhere, you must respect your customers; otherwise, you risk losing business. Managers should be more engaged, checking on departments and customers to ensure everything is running smoothly. This is what creates a good store and encourages repeat business. Unfortunately, despite its proximity to home, our last visit was the final deciding factor, and we won't be returning.

yelp:test:16316.orig: Okay. I think it's safe to say that the Cine Capri at Tempe Marketplace is the best screen to watch any movie. There's usually a couple dollar increase in the ticket price, but it's worth is if you want to enjoy the movie you are there to watch. This theater gets the most attention from staff as well so it's always clean. It's also the best place to watch a movie on opening night. Go see TRON at this theater December 16th.
yelp:test:16316.para: Certainly. It's fair to conclude that the Cine Capri at Tempe Marketplace offers the optimal movie-watching experience. While there might be a slight price hike, the enhanced quality justifies the cost, especially if you're looking to fully enjoy the film. The staff pays particular attention to this theater, ensuring it remains impeccably clean. Additionally, it's the ideal venue for catching a movie on its opening night. I recommend seeing TRON there on December 16th.

yelp:test:16323.orig: Switch really was an interesting place. I love the atmosphere, it's definitely high-end. My down-to-earth jock/geek husband wouldn't go there with me on date night, so I went with a girl friend of mine.\nThe food was really great, and the server was lovely. If you want a fun night out, and a place that's worthy of your little black dress and sky-high heels, this is it!
yelp:test:16323.para:
Certainly was an intriguing spot. I adored the ambiance; it exudes a high-end vibe. My grounded, athletic/geeky husband wouldn't accompany me for a date, so I went with a friend instead.

The cuisine was outstanding, and the waiter was delightful. If you're looking for an entertaining evening and a venue befitting your elegant attire, such as a little black dress and towering heels, this place is perfect!

yelp:test:16376.orig: This is a hard review, I've never experienced anything like this place. Usually food is either good or bad, end of story. I love the entrees , they are inspired and tasty, the chef has a deft hand with his spices and flavors (not just the usual garlic and oyster sauce) BUT (and this is a HUGE but) the appetizers have proved to be consistently disappointing. On my first visit (see previous review), I raved about the main courses but was less than impressed with the appetizers and agreed to go back again to give them a second chance.After all anyone can have an off night in the kitchen. Well, once again, major disappointment. This time I ordered the \""Award Winning\"" creamy crab puffs (AKA crab rangoon where I come from) one of my personal all time favs and some dried, I mean fried, won-tons. The crab puffs were overcooked and hard (not crispy) so much so that i had to beak off all the edges and just eat the middle which was just average. More cream than crab and very bland - no puff about it. The fried wontons were also overcooked and in addition to looking like a small marble, were as hard as one. These were the smallest wontons I have ever seen. The filling was rolled into a ver
yelp:test:16376.para: This review is quite challenging, as I've never encountered a place quite like this before. Typically, food is either excellent or poor, but that's not the case here. I adore the main courses; they are innovative and delicious, with the chef skillfully blending unique spices and flavors (not just the standard garlic and oyster sauce). However, there's a significant issue with the appetizers. During my first visit (refer to my previous review), I praised the main dishes but found the appetizers wanting, and I agreed to return for a second chance. After all, everyone can have a bad day in the kitchen. Unfortunately, my second visit was another letdown. This time, I ordered the "Award Winning" creamy crab puffs (which are known as crab rangoon in my area) and some dried, fried wontons. The crab puffs were overcooked and not crispy, making them difficult to eat. The filling was more cream than crab, and it was quite bland. The fried wontons were also overcooked, looking like small marbles and feeling as hard as one. They were the smallest wontons I've ever seen, and the filling was rolled into a very thin layer.

yelp:test:16384.orig: I almost always have a great experience here! The food has never disappointed & the portions are very generous. MOST of the time the staff is very friendly and if you show up on the weekends for breakfast, do expect a wait but you shouldn't be disappointed. \n\nToday, however, the service from my waitress Brittany wasn't great, I'd honestly give her a D+ at best, she wasn't rude by definition but she was very impersonable, she was more of an order-taker than a person of service, she'd walk by and look but really wouldn't even ask if all was good or if we needed anything, she never even stated her name(I got it from the receipt)... I needed her a few times and had to like waive her down or signal her over. I felt like my boyfriend and I were just inconvenient to her and she was JUST there to do her job, nothing more, nothing less.
yelp:test:16384.para: I typically have an excellent experience here, with the food consistently meeting my expectations and the portions being quite generous. Usually, the staff is very friendly, though you might have to wait on weekends for breakfast. However, today, my waitress Brittany fell short. While she wasn't rude, she came across as distant and more of a task executor than a genuine server. She rarely checked in to see if we needed anything or if everything was alright. She didn't even introduce herself until I saw it on the receipt. I had to call her over a few times, which made me feel like we were an inconvenience to her. Her attitude suggested she was just there to fulfill her duties, without any extra effort.

yelp:test:16394.orig: ehhh...barely edible. Went for breakfast on a Sunday morning with a party of 5, typically busy. Bad layout of restaurant...lots of booths around the perimeter and tables squished in the middle. I had 2 eggs, 2 sausage patties and 2 biscuits & gravy. Everything but the sausage was cold, the biscuits weren't homemade and the gravy tastes like raw flour. Mother-In Law's food was also cold and one order of \""toast\"" came out as bread- not toasted at all. There was no point in sending it back because no one ever checked back. My husbands food came out steaming hot, needs better timing in the kitchen. We won't be back...
yelp:test:16394.para: Ugh... barely edible. We visited for breakfast on a Sunday with a group of five, and the place was usually quite busy. The restaurant layout was poor, with many booths along the edges and tables cramped in the center. I ordered two eggs, two sausage patties, and two biscuits and gravy. The eggs and biscuits were cold, the gravy tasted like raw flour, and the biscuits weren't homemade. My mother-in-law's food was also cold, and one order of "toast" was served as un-toasted bread. There was no point in requesting a replacement since no one followed up. My husband's meal was hot, but it needed better kitchen timing. We won't be returning.

yelp:test:16448.orig:
Look, bad experiences happen to everybody sooner or later. Sometimes customers are rude and won't acknowledge it. Other times, employees have a bad day and don't handle situations appropriately.

But I have to say, after having flown United on the last four trips I took - three of them multi-leg international trips and one of them a direct flight coast-to-coast - I gotta say that United is just an awful airline.

Planes - decrepit and worn-out. Old. Every last one of them that I was on, was from the 1980s. In-flight entertainment which was primitive; playing a single movie for everyone from a Hi-8 videotape. That's just sad. Fortunately, it's the 21st century (everywhere but on United flights) so I can bring an iPod and watch a movie with my earbuds (but I can't plug it in to keep it charged!!! Because this is United - christ, the AC outlets in the lavatories don't even work. Psych!)

Flight attendants - CLEARLY hate their jobs and the customers, ALL of them. Well, except of course if they think you are a rich sugardaddy who can rescue them from their shitty jobs. I am painfully polite at all times to people who have to deal with the general public, I know it can be hard and
yelp:test:16448.para:
Surely, everyone encounters bad experiences at some point. Customers can be rude, and employees might have a tough day, leading to mishandled situations.

However, after my recent four flights with United—three multi-leg international trips and one coast-to-coast direct flight—I must say United is a poor airline.

The planes were old and worn, from the 1980s. The in-flight entertainment was basic, showing one movie to everyone from a Hi-8 videotape. That's disappointing. It's the 21st century everywhere else, but not on United flights. I can bring my iPod and watch a movie with earbuds, but I can't charge it because the outlets in the lavatories don't work. Seriously, United, even the lavatory outlets are broken. 

The flight attendants clearly dislike their jobs and customers. Except, of course, if they think you're a wealthy benefactor who can help them out of their difficult positions. I always try to be polite to people who deal with the public, knowing it can be challenging.

yelp:test:16461.orig: Well done! Had a delicious, full of flavor dinner and great customer service. We will be coming back
yelp:test:16461.para: Great job! We enjoyed a flavorful, delicious dinner with excellent service. We look forward to returning.

yelp:test:16473.orig:
Tropical themed restaurant.  Been here for buffets which were decent.  Wanting to avoid the long buffet line, we opted to be seated for the cafe.  Getting seats for 6 seemed to be a challenge.  We were directed to the back and was told someone would be waiting for us to seat us.  Alas, no one was so we just seated ourselves.  What appeared to be confusion as another server asked us if we were supposed to be seated there or not.  Turns out, it was the right place.  Anyway, we waited....hmmmm... quite a while.  It seemed longer withTWO antsy toddlers who weren't shy about declaring their state of hunger.  The waiter hurriedly walked by and said he'd be right there.  He appeared to be on the verge of a hissy fit.   
We waited AGAIN even longer.  Finally, annoyed with the wait since we had just arrived to Vegas after roadtripping 5 hours, I walked over to the waiter station and asked for someone to bring us drinks.  
A minute later, our huffy server shows up with no greeting and asks us for our drink order.  We were already ready to order.  
Again,  another long wait.  I looked at my watch and noticed it's been over 20 minutes with NO DRINKS!  This has been my worst experience at th
yelp:test:16473.para:
A tropical-themed restaurant where I've enjoyed buffets before. To avoid the long buffet line, we decided to dine in the cafe. Securing seats for six proved difficult. We were directed to the back, where we were told someone would seat us, but no one arrived, so we seated ourselves. There seemed to be some confusion as another server questioned whether we were supposed to be there. It turned out we were in the right spot. Anyway, we waited... quite a while. The wait felt even longer with two restless toddlers who were openly hungry. The waiter hurried by, promising to be right there, looking close to losing his temper. 

We waited again, even longer. Frustrated by the delay after our long drive to Vegas, I approached the waiter station and asked for someone to bring us drinks. A minute later, our irritable server appeared without a greeting, asking for our drink orders. We were already prepared to order. Another long wait ensued. Checking my watch, I noticed over 20 minutes had passed with no drinks, making this my worst experience at the restaurant.

yelp:test:16500.orig: Great food, horrible service. The bad outweighs the good. Not worth spending your cash in that dough factory. Pass
yelp:test:16500.para: The food was excellent, but the service was terrible. Overall, the negatives far outweigh the positives. I wouldn't recommend spending your money there; it's best to avoid it. Pass.

yelp:test:16501.orig: I love the food here.  And it is super convenient.  Those are 4 stars.  But the service is just painful.  Slow.  Uninspired.  Bothersome.  The sense it get is that I am interrupting them by actually wanting to spend money.  I would be a weekly customer if this weren't so.  As is I come maybe twice a year.
yelp:test:16501.para: I adore the cuisine here and find it very convenient, warranting a four-star rating. However, the service is a major letdown—it's slow, unenthusiastic, and bothersome. It feels like I'm intruding when I want to enjoy my meal and spend money. If not for this, I'd be a regular customer. Currently, I visit only about twice a year.

yelp:test:16502.orig: Note: I didn't enter this beauty, simply observed it.\nFrom the boulevard, it's quite stellar especially during the night time. Paired with the balloon and the Bellagio fountains in front, it's quite the structure with a radiance of it's own (though I wish to see the real deal en Paris, mais c'est la vie pour l'instant...)\nWhen you go see the water show, can't miss this piece on the boulevard - get a camera and take some pictures of \""Paris\""!
yelp:test:16502.para:
Note: I merely observed this beauty from afar; I didn't participate in it.

From the boulevard, it's particularly impressive, especially at night. Combined with the balloon and the Bellagio fountains, it exudes a unique radiance (though I yearn to see the real Paris someday, such is life for now...).

If you're there for the water show, don't miss this boulevard scene—grab your camera and capture a piece of "Paris"!

yelp:test:16571.orig: So my second experience was alot better!I did come hungry and I ordered one of my go to breakfast items I eat which is chicken fried steak and eggs with country potatoes. They have redeemed themself and I enjoyed a great meal with great service.I'll be back to have this again
yelp:test:16571.para: My second visit was much more satisfying. I arrived hungry and opted for one of my favorite breakfast dishes: chicken fried steak accompanied by eggs and country-style potatoes. They've improved their reputation, and I thoroughly enjoyed both the meal and the service. I plan to return to order this again.

yelp:test:16576.orig:
I have a few things to report on this place.  Since this place appeared on Restaurant Impossible it is good to report that the decor and menu are still just about the same when on the show.  Sadly, the management and higher ups haven't really changed, same mentality.

What drew us in here was a sign on the side of the street: ""All You Can Eat Pasta Bar."" Great we thought, let's go in and try it out.  Then everything seems to have gone down the toilet.  When we got inside and attempted to order the pasta bar we were told it wasn't available due to the street festival going on outside.  Hmm, funny, because there is still a sign, if not two, posted outside advertising this.  If you were not going to honor this special (which I believe runs Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday) then maybe you should have taken in the signs for that week.

When we decided we weren't going to dine here and let our waitress know our intentions we got this great, drawn out excuse why we shouldn't go.  Instead of honoring the all you can eat portion of this, they would hand you a card with options on it to fill in for the pasta bar.  Mind you, it wasn't even all you can eat, just whatever you checked on
yelp:test:16576.para:
I wanted to share some observations about this place. Since it appeared on Restaurant Impossible, the decor and menu remain largely unchanged, but unfortunately, the management and upper echelons haven't improved; they still have the same mindset.

What initially attracted us was a sign on the street advertising an "All You Can Eat Pasta Bar." We were excited to try it out. However, things quickly went downhill. Upon entering, we were informed that the pasta bar wasn't available because of a street festival outside, despite seeing multiple signs advertising it. It's peculiar that they didn't honor the special offer, which runs on Wednesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays, especially since the signs were still up.

When we decided to leave and informed our waitress, we received a lengthy, unsatisfactory explanation for not dining there. Instead of offering the all-you-can-eat option, they provided a card with various choices, but it wasn't truly all you could eat; you could only select from what was listed.

yelp:test:16590.orig:
The first thing that struck us is how cocky this young waiter was.He was probably thinking ""WE AT SWAGAT ARE THE BOMB!!"". Son, I just moved here from the San Francisco bay area.I know and cook Indian food and trust me you are NOT the bomb.Far from it.
Food was OK.Nothing exceptional and definitely not what the reviewers here are going ga ga about but that is personal choice.We tried the chicken tikka and the vindaloo which was flavorful but definitely not worth the price we were paying. Quantities were not adequate for the amount we were paying.Is Indian food really that expensive here in Madison? The prices here are ridiculously overpriced for Indian food and every single Indian restaurant has the same price range for all dishes which would make me believe that they have some sort of Indian restaurant owners union that decides on what the prices are going to be!!
Another thing that irks me is the inclusion of south Indian food along with your Rogan Josh menu which raised a big flag for us regarding the quality of the food. No serious Indian restaurant owner would EVER include a idli sambar dosa on a menu that has Rogan Josh or biryani on it.PERIOD!
Just looking at the quant
yelp:test:16590.para:
Upon our arrival, we were immediately struck by the waiter's overconfidence. He seemed to believe, "WE AT SWAGAT ARE THE BEST!!" Son, I recently moved from the San Francisco Bay Area, and I know my Indian cuisine. Trust me, you are not the best; quite the opposite. 

The food was decent but nothing special, and certainly not what the reviews here are making a fuss about. It's a matter of personal taste. We tried the chicken tikka and vindaloo, which was flavorful but not worth the price. The portions were also too small for the cost. Is Indian food really this expensive in Madison? The prices are outrageously high for the quality, and every Indian restaurant seems to have the same pricing, suggesting a price-fixing agreement among Indian restaurant owners.

What really bothers me is the inclusion of South Indian dishes like idli sambar dosa alongside traditional North Indian dishes like Rogan Josh. No serious Indian restaurant would mix these cuisines. This raises serious doubts about the quality of the food.

yelp:test:16608.orig: I met the owner, Sam when he worked at a chain prior to opening Goodfellas.  I wanted my son to have time to feel like a boy because he's stuck with his single mom and big sister all the time so I took him to a \""real\"" barber shop for the first time when he was 3 and gratefully we got Sam when we walked in.  Sam left the chain to open Goodfellas and he personally called me to tell me where he would be so we could continue coming to him.  My son is now 8 and looks forward to his visits to Goodfellas every 7-8 weeks and adores Sam.  Sam knows my family and genuinely cares for me and my children.  I always buy gift cards for the men in my family and I have never heard anything bad from them about the service they receive.  These people will treat you like family and always go above and beyond what is expected of their services.  I HIGHLY recommend them.
yelp:test:16608.para: When my son was 3, I took him to a "real" barber shop for the first time to give him a special experience, and we were fortunate to meet Sam at Goodfellas. Sam had previously worked for a chain but decided to open his own place. He personally contacted me to let me know where he would be, ensuring we could continue our visits. Now that my son is 8, he eagerly anticipates his appointments every 7-8 weeks and has a deep affection for Sam. Sam knows our family well and genuinely cares about us. I often purchase gift cards for the men in my family, and I've never heard any complaints about the service they receive. The staff at Goodfellas treat you like family and consistently exceed expectations. I strongly recommend them.

yelp:test:16630.orig: Liars. Rude. Don't fix what they say. I went with my sister and our men and they wanted it to be the best night and dinner. It was the special with the Chris Angel tickets. We were told on the phone filet mignon, and they brought out chuck steak pretending we wouldn't know it wasn't filet. That's just insulting and pathetic. $100 a plate that's ridiculous.
yelp:test:16630.para: Disregarding honesty and manners, they served us chuck steak instead of filet mignon, despite being assured over the phone that filet mignon would be served. This was part of a special package including Chris Angel tickets. The meal cost $100 per plate, which is outrageous. Their behavior is both disrespectful and inconsiderate.

yelp:test:16656.orig: This was my first time eating here and well.....it was the most disgusting soul food I've ever eaten in my life!!! I ordered fried chicken, sweet potatoes, & red beans. The chicken had no seasoning or flavor. I bet my 10 yr old brother could cook better chicken. The red beans same thing, no seasoning & nasty at that!! Sweet potatoes, where's the brown sugar butter cinnamon/nutmeg?? The soul was definately missing in this so called soul food. If u like wasting $$ on crappy food, then this is your place! Frys deli chicken tasted better than this place lol
yelp:test:16656.para: My first experience at this place was quite disappointing. The food was the most unappetizing soul food I've ever tried. I had fried chicken, sweet potatoes, and red beans. The chicken lacked any flavor or seasoning; I doubt even my 10-year-old brother could cook worse chicken. The red beans were equally flavorless and unpleasant. Where was the brown sugar, butter, cinnamon, or nutmeg on the sweet potatoes? It seemed like the soul was completely absent from this so-called soul food. If you enjoy spending money on subpar food, this might be the place for you. The fried chicken from Frys Deli tasted much better.

yelp:test:16658.orig: overpriced for overfried food. We went about an hour before closing and they took forever to bring food. just no customer service it was like you were inconvience to them being there.. I'm sure at one time this place was great at one time but no longer.
yelp:test:16658.para: The food was excessively priced and overcooked. We arrived an hour before they closed, yet our meal took a long time to arrive. There was a complete lack of customer service; it felt like we were an inconvenience to them. While this place might have been excellent at one point, it certainly isn't anymore.

yelp:test:16661.orig:

yelp:test:16661.para:
Deciding to drop by on a whim after a friend in the car mentioned she had been eager to try this place, we realized we had a few hours to spare before any commitments. So, we decided to stop in for lunch.

Upon entering the old restaurant, I immediately noticed the walls adorned with signatures from celebrities, artists, and athletes who had dined there. At 2 pm on a Wednesday, there were only two other customers, which meant our service was prompt and efficient.

We were served by a couple of friendly waitresses who suggested different dishes. I opted for the country fried steak, while my friends chose the famous fried chicken. Each order came with a few sides, and I decided to try their sweet tea. Our food arrived within 10 minutes, and the portions were enormous. My friends each received three large pieces of chicken, and my steak was as big as my face. We had generous servings of black eye peas and mac & cheese on our plates, and even the sweet tea was served in a larger-than-usual glass. None of us finished our meals.

yelp:test:16665.orig:
The service was terrible - the food was not much better. We waited forever for our drink orders, but tried to give them the benefit of the doubt because our kids had to get milk from the bar. When we had to get the chip guy to refill our drinks, I knew it was no fluke. 

We then pulled up the Yelp reviews and read all about what we were living at that moment. But as we hasn't gotten our food yet, we still had to wait.

Won't be back-ever. Wasn't all  bad, but with so many good restaurants within a couple of miles, eating here would be a waste of time and money.
yelp:test:16665.para:
The service was poor, and the food didn't fare much better. We waited an excessively long time for our drinks, but we hoped they would improve. When we had to ask the chip guy to refill our drinks, it became clear they weren't making any effort. 

We then checked Yelp reviews, which confirmed our experience. Despite not having our food yet, we still had to wait. 

I was already full from the chips and water, so I couldn't finish my main course. The only reason I took it home was because I was taught not to waste food.

We won't be returning. While the experience wasn't entirely bad, with so many excellent restaurants nearby, dining here would be a waste of both time and money.

yelp:test:16680.orig: Have enjoyed your theater many times and certainly would attend more often if it were not for the great distance. yelp:test:16680.para: I've enjoyed your theater on numerous occasions and would definitely visit more frequently if the travel distance weren't such a barrier. Entering the restaurant one is \""greeted\"" on a very cool level by a maitr D' speaking to a helper. They continued their conversation for a few minutes before seating us. Not an auspicious beginning. The menu arrives and it is their most expensive, the tasting menu. We asked for their other menus, a prix fixe and an a la carte. yelp:test:16684.para: After about two years, I returned to Aureole and enjoyed a good meal there. However, Mandalay Bay has deteriorated, much like the rest of the strip. Upon entering the restaurant, we were greeted by a sommelier and a helper who continued chatting for a few minutes before seating us. This wasn't a promising start. The menu presented was their most expensive option, the tasting menu. We inquired about the other menus, a prix fixe and a la carte. We were seated in the Swan Court, which used to incur an extra $10, but now is included with the tasting menu. When I expressed my frustration, they assured me I could choose any menu there. That was a relief. The wine list, boasting 4000 bottles, had only two Beaujolais, none of high quality. The wine prices were exorbitant, likely 400% above cost. A young sommelier eventually recommended a decent Spanish wine for $75. We opted for a la carte. The foie gras we ordered was seared, not pâté, but they corrected this. If you're firm in your choices, you can get what you want. The service was good, and the food was excellent. Overall, the place lacks any class.

yelp:test:16697.orig:
IF YOU DONT HAVE A SENSE OF HUMOR- dont go.
this place is hilairious!! Everyone there is having a blast, and everyone is always laughing... staff is really funny and there is a great ENERGY.. if you get offended easy,  you will not like this place. yelp:test:16697.para:
IF YOU CAN'T LAUGH - THIS PLACE MIGHT NOT BE FOR YOU.
IT'S ABSOLUTELY HILARIOUS! EVERYONE IS ENJOYING THEMSELVES AND LAUGHING ALL THE TIME. THE STAFF IS VERY FUNNY AND THE ENERGY IS GREAT. IF YOU EASILY GET OFFENDED, YOU'LL PROBABLY DISLIKE IT. THE STAFF MIGHT EVEN MAKE YOU WEAR A FUNNY PAPER HAT OR SOMETHING DEGRADING.

yelp:test:16703.orig: I've always wanted to try this place and I personally wouldn't go back. Food was OK, def get something bbq b/c it's better. I had the wings and they sucked. Being treated like s*** was interesting but they prob could do w/o that angle if you ask me. The atmosphere was cool and they guy working the bar was super cool! I would do the outside bar again but that's about it.
yelp:test:16703.para: I've long been curious about this place, but my experience left me unimpressed. The food was just okay; I'd recommend trying the BBQ dishes as they are better. My wings were terrible. The poor service was noteworthy, but I think they could improve by focusing less on that approach. The ambiance was nice, and the bartender was really cool. He convinced us to get the insulated cups for the slushy drinks, and his homemade mixture was unbeatable. I'd visit the outdoor bar again, but that's about the only positive aspect.

yelp:test:16707.orig:
The wings were ok but got mostly legs. I prefer wings. The cheese dip was cold but flavors were Ok. The staff is funny and friendly. The fish and chips were over cooked.   

Everything was overpriced. For 2
Cokes, 2 small margaritas, chips and cheese salsa, fish
And chips, and wings , the price was $85 !
yelp:test:16707.para: The wings were satisfactory, but there were mostly legs, which I prefer not to have. The cheese dip was chilly, though the flavors were alright. The staff were both amusing and courteous. The fish and chips were overcooked. Everything was excessively priced. For just 2 cokes, 2 small margaritas, chips and cheese salsa, the fish and chips, and the wings, the total came to an astonishing $85!

yelp:test:16733.orig:
At first thought I would have given this place 3 stars, then I actually thought about the service and dropped it down 1 star. The food is pretty good, nothing special though. The prosciutto and mozzarella was pretty good and I kind of liked the chicken parm panini, but I definitely thought the amount of chicken on the sandwich was stingy. The price isn't high so there are your 3 stars. 

Here is your review on service, SUCKED. I walked in and the waitress/hostess/bartender said hello and walked away. Then a couple minutes later she remembered that her job is to get people to a table so she told me to sit anywhere. She also was able to bring me chips instead of the side salad that was ordered and somehow I needed to turn my entire body around and stare at her to let her know I wanted to order something. She also brought my date the wrong drink, which was supposed to be cider, but instead my date took a big sip of an ale which she thought was gross. I am surprised looking back that I didn't give her a 10% tip. 

I wanted to like this place, it's in walking distance from where I live, but the brain dead waitress was able to convince me to never go back again.
yelp:test:16733.para:
Initially, I considered giving this place 3 stars, but after reflecting on the service, I lowered it to 2 stars. The food was decent, though not exceptional. The prosciutto and mozzarella were quite good, and I enjoyed the chicken parm panini, although I felt the chicken portion was too small. Given the reasonable prices, that's why I settled on 3 stars. 

Now, let's talk about the service, which was terrible. When I entered, the staff member, who could have been a waitress, hostess, or bartender, greeted me and then left. A few minutes later, she remembered her duty and told me to sit wherever I liked. She also brought me chips instead of the requested salad and only served me after I turned around and looked at her to indicate I wanted to order. Moreover, she gave my date the wrong drink; it was supposed to be cider, but it turned out to be ale, which my date found unpleasant. I was surprised I didn't give her a 10% tip. 

Despite its proximity to my home, I now find myself unwilling to return due to the inattentive and unhelpful service.

yelp:test:16759.orig: LOVE Earl of Sandwich!!!! My husband and I make this one of our stops every time we're in Vegas! The last time we were in town we stopped by Earl of Sandwich 3 or 4 times I think. Yummy sandwiches, good hours, good service most of the time, best food value in the Planet Hollywood Hotel and Casino! I'm craving it now!!! I may have to stop by on my way to the airport next time and bring some home with me. =) You think i'm kidding lol.  \n\nHighly recommend you try every sandwich on the menu once....well, as many as you can lol.  The Caribbean Jerk Chicken is amazing! The American and The Original 1762 are tops on my list also. And make sure to save room for one of their delicious ice cream cookie sandwiches!
yelp:test:16759.para:
I absolutely adore Earl of Sandwich! My husband and I always make it a point to visit whenever we're in Vegas. During our last trip, we stopped by three or four times. The sandwiches are delicious, the hours are convenient, and the service is generally great. It offers the best value for food in the Planet Hollywood Hotel and Casino! I'm already craving one now! I might even swing by on my way to the airport and bring some home. =) I'm not joking—this place is a must-try.

I highly recommend you sample every sandwich on the menu, or as many as you can fit in. The Caribbean Jerk Chicken is outstanding, and The American and The Original 1762 are my top picks. Don't forget to leave room for one of their yummy ice cream cookie sandwiches!

yelp:test:16772.orig: Ah yes, Earl of Sandwich. Every Vegas mans hangover preference. All I have to say is, FULL MONTAGUE! (and tomato soup... With lots of water, mind you) will cure that hangover.
yelp:test:16772.para: Certainly, the Earl of Sandwich is the go-to choice for Vegas men dealing with hangovers. My recommendation? FULL MONTAGUE! (plus tomato soup, but make sure to add plenty of water) to help alleviate that hangover.

yelp:test:16786.orig:
6...6....6 dollar sandwiches????
Earl doesn't mess around.  As much as I don't like writing reviews for chains, this one is an exception.   

Earl of Sandwich has brought me back from the brink after getting the drunken hangover shakes.  Conveniently located on the floor of Planet Hollywood, EoS serves Quiznos type of sandwiches, only wayyyyy better.  He's good for pregaming before a 12 hour rager.  I've had two types of sandwiches here. 

The Caprese is your standard mozzarella, tomato sandwich with balsamic reduction. The Hawaiian is also your standard chicken, ham, cheddar and BBQ sauce.  

Their broccoli soup is chunky good, and their cookie will give you diabetes.  Earl Earl mm mm good
yelp:test:16786.para:
6...6....6 dollar sandwiches???? Earl really delivers. Even though I usually avoid reviewing chains, this place is a standout. 

Earl of Sandwich has saved me from a severe hangover. Situated conveniently on the Planet Hollywood floor, their sandwiches are far superior to Quiznos. They're perfect for pre-party snacking before a long night. I've tried two types here.

The Caprese is a classic mozzarella and tomato sandwich with a balsamic reduction. The Hawaiian features chicken, ham, cheddar, and BBQ sauce. 

Their broccoli soup is chunky and delicious, and the cookie is so sweet it could give you diabetes. Earl, Earl, mm mm good.

yelp:test:16822.orig: LOVE THIS PLACE!  We eat here every Saturday as long as we are in town.  My husband eats here during the week too!  Weekday lunches are a great deal and quick!  The veggie soup is delicious.  The golden wings - Delicious... chicken satay is good too.  For an entree... we always get Pad Prik King chicken or sometimes shrimp but its always always delicious!  Have been trying to find a thai place with this dish closer to home (east valley) but haven't found one yet!  Service is terrific!  FYI for those of you who just order Pad Thai... it is very sweet here so if you don't like it sweet... order something else.  Other things we've tried that were good... pepper steak - very good - just dont eat a lot of red meat, massamum curry with chicken good... also we order everything medium to thai hot... like very spicy!
yelp:test:16822.para: I absolutely adore this place! We make it a point to dine here every Saturday when we're in town, and my husband even stops by during the week. Weekday lunches are fantastic—both affordable and quick! The veggie soup is outstanding, and the golden wings are delicious too. We usually opt for the Pad Prik King chicken or shrimp, and it's always delightful. We've been searching for a Thai restaurant with this dish in the East Valley area, but haven't found one quite like it yet! The service is top-notch. Just a heads up for those who only order Pad Thai—it's quite sweet here, so if you prefer it less sweet, try something else. Other dishes we've enjoyed include the pepper steak, which is very good, though it's not for those who don't eat much red meat. The massamum curry with chicken was also yummy. We always ask for everything to be prepared medium to Thai hot, which means very spicy!

yelp:test:16836.orig: Over-hyped and overpriced.  Located in the forum shops in Caesars, Trevi is located right in the middle of the mall. The food (Italian themed) was nothing special.  I ordered the linguine ai frutti di mare, one of their specialties, which was delicious but expensive for the small portion and lacked enough seafood.  My boyfriend's sausage pizza had onions that were way overcooked.  Overall, I will not be returning and am surprised at the poor value of their food for the great location.
yelp:test:16836.para: Overpriced and overhyped, Trevi, an Italian-themed restaurant, is situated in the middle of the Forum Shops at Caesars. We didn't have to wait, but our table was placed near the loud Greek gods water fountain, which was quite distracting. The service was slow due to the high foot traffic. The food, while tasty, was not exceptional. I enjoyed the linguine with seafood, which was delicious but too pricey for the small serving size and insufficient seafood content. My boyfriend's sausage pizza had onions that were overcooked. Given the poor value for the quality of food and the great location, I won't be returning.

yelp:test:16846.orig: Saucy. And nearby. Its convenient that it's so close. I cant stress the closeness more.
yelp:test:16846.para: So close and in such proximity. What a handy location! I really can't emphasize how convenient this proximity is enough.

yelp:test:16852.orig: First time and I wasn't impressed. Chicken is flavorless, dry and way too pricey. Will not return.
yelp:test:16852.para: On my first visit, I wasn't satisfied at all. The chicken lacked flavor, was dry, and the price was excessively high. I won't be going back.

yelp:test:16883.para: Average experience overall. The service was satisfactory, but the food left something to be desired.

yelp:test:16922.para: Little Las Vegas, filled with cultural imitations, but lacking the enjoyable atmosphere.

yelp:test:16968.orig:
This is a chain restaurant, but they are fanatical about the quality of their food and service.  It's a little pricey at around $20-$25 a plate for a dinner entree but the food is high quality.

Let's get our priorities in order:

In terms of drinks, I had a vodka tonic (Well vodka there is Smirnoff but they also carry Ketel One) and a Watermelon Margarita.  The vodka tonic was about what you'd expect.  A decent neutral drink with a splash of citrus.  The Watermelon Margarita was a little sweet for my taste but it was definitely an interesting experience and certainly strong enough and big enough.  It's a $9 drink but it comes with a sidecar caraffe that will completely refill the Margarita glass and then some so it's really like 2 margaritas for under five bucks each.

Now that that's out of the way let's discuss dessert:

I had a bite of the cheesecake which was tasty, but not award winning.    

Entrees:
I tried the NY strip and a lobster tail, both of which were well prepared though I'm not a huge fan of their spice rub.  It's not bad mind you, I just prefer my steaks either naked or marinated.  The good news is their steaks are never frozen and the quality of the cu
yelp:test:16968.para:
This is a chain restaurant that is very particular about the quality of its food and service. The meals, especially the dinner entrees, are a bit pricey, ranging from $20 to $25 per plate, but the food is of high quality.

First, let's talk about the drinks:

I started with a vodka tonic, which was made with either Well vodka (Smirnoff) or Ketel One. It was a standard, neutral drink with a touch of citrus. For the Watermelon Margarita, it was a bit too sweet for my liking, but it was an intriguing experience and quite potent. At $9, it comes with a sidecar carafe that can refill the glass multiple times, essentially giving you two margaritas for less than five dollars each.

Moving on to dessert, I sampled a piece of cheesecake that was enjoyable but not exceptional.

For the entrees, I had a NY strip and a lobster tail. Both were well-cooked, though I found their spice rub a bit overpowering. While it's not unpleasant, I prefer my steaks either unseasoned or marinated. The good news is that their steaks are always fresh, and the quality is quite good.

Eventually, I decided to stop once my boyfriend

yelp:test:17035.orig:
Recently went to a work holiday party at Arsenal Bowling Lanes. This place has been here forever and I can remember coming here as a kid when you had to keep track of your own score with paper.

Arsenal Bowling is in a very cramped space (for a bowling alley) so there's not much space to hang out and enjoy your drink behind your lane.  Srangers are constantly walking through your group and bumping into you.

The bowling balls are pretty beat up, there's not much selection, and most of the balls don't even have their weight on them.  The food is typical fried bar food and overpriced.  The drinks are very overpriced.  Only one bartender was working so the wait at the bar was terribly long.  We had to keep skipping turns for the people going for drinks becuase it took them so long to get back.

Compared to a fancy bowling alley like Jillian's in Boston, Arsenal is extremely ghettotastic.

This is really a 1-star kind of place, but I'm giving a 2nd becuase it's a Pittsburgh Classic.
yelp:test:17035.para:
Recently attended a work holiday party at Arsenal Bowling Lanes, a place I've known since childhood where we used to manually track scores with paper.

Arsenal Bowling operates in a tight space, which makes it difficult to relax and enjoy drinks near your lane. Strangers frequently interrupt your group, causing discomfort.

The bowling balls are in poor condition, with limited variety and many lacking their weights. The food is standard fried bar fare, and prices are high. Drinks are also overpriced, and there was only one bartender, leading to long waits at the bar. We often had to skip turns for those getting drinks due to the lengthy service.

Compared to fancy places like Jillian's in Boston, Arsenal feels very run-down.

Overall, this place deserves only 1 star, but I'm giving it 2 stars because it's a classic in Pittsburgh.

yelp:test:17056.orig:
I was excited to eat here after reading the reviews. Then I ate there and I was less excited. 

I was prepped for some hot spicy New Mexican food. That did not arrive on my plate. It was tasty for sure but I was lead to believe that I would experience the food I grew up with in New Mexico. I didn't. 

It is possible that my expectations were too much for this restaurant to handle.
yelp:test:17056.para: I looked forward to dining there based on the reviews, but my experience wasn't as thrilling as anticipated. I expected some authentic New Mexican cuisine, particularly spicy dishes, but those weren't served. The food was enjoyable, but it didn't match the New Mexican flavors I remember from my childhood. It’s possible that my high expectations were simply too demanding for this establishment to meet.

yelp:test:17059.orig: Taste was bland!  you are better off going to Genghis Grill instead.  YC's only has 3 meat choices and no seafood!  It was fresh, but flavorless.  You had to get the noodles in your bowl too so you get less here than you do at Genghis Grill.
yelp:test:17059.para: The food lacked flavor! I think Genghis Grill would be a better choice. YC's offers just three meat options and no seafood. While it was fresh, it was tasteless. You also receive fewer noodles when you order there compared to Genghis Grill.

yelp:test:17084.orig: One of my favorite hotels to stay in Vegas.  Be aware of the resort fees when you book, but you get lots of free stuff with the paid fee.\n\nRooms & Casino & extras all very nice
yelp:test:17084.para: I really enjoy staying at this hotel in Vegas. Just remember to check the resort fees at booking time, as they can add up. For that fee, you receive a lot of complimentary perks. The rooms, casino, and additional amenities are all quite nice.

yelp:test:17091.orig:

All the pool areas were lovely and arranged really nicely. The food event was the bomb and was done very well. 

Food was incredible!
yelp:test:17091.para:
We were only able to enjoy the pools here during the Epicurean Affair in May, a highly anticipated event that I strongly recommend attending next year. 

All the pool areas were beautifully arranged and delightful. The food event was fantastic and executed very well. 

The food was truly outstanding!
