yelp:test:17097.para: I've stayed here a few times, and it was okay until my last visit. Upon arriving at our room, we discovered wet, dirty women's underwear under the bed. We contacted the front desk, but they seemed indifferent and merely suggested we move to another room. The new room had a view, which I considered an upgrade, but when we stayed over the weekend, we noticed the room wasn't cleaned on the first day because we had forgotten to remove our "Do Not Disturb" sign. On the second day, we slept in and didn't remove the sign until around noon. When we returned to the hotel later that night, the room still hadn't been cleaned. Did they not check if guests were sleeping in? We asked to change the sheets, but instead, they just left fresh ones. This wasn't a positive experience, and I won't be staying here again.

yelp:test:17126.orig:
It pains me extremely to give Amore only 3 stars!!  We have been going to/ordering from here very often for over a year, even when I was diagnosed with Celiac and had to go gluten-free. I waited patiently only ordering Chicken Vesuvio, until they recently started carrying gluten-free products.  

Now I realize when ordering in I take the risk of being contaminated, but thankfully not only am I very aware  but as well am a bit paranoid...  I have never had a problem ordering from there gluten or otherwise, until tonight!!  I ordered gluten-free pasta and received the complete opposite in WHEAT!!  I called questioning and it was treated nonchalantly as if a pizza arrived with wrong toppings rather than the fact I was almost poisoned, which would land me in the hospital immediately...  Not only were they completely flippant about what just happened,. I even needed to be the one to bring up about being refunded!  After a brief verbal brawl I finally just gave the phone back to the delivery guy, since he was yelling for it back, he gave us our refund and I handed him back the re-made meal, there was no way I was eating their food ever again!

As I said before, I hate deducting stars
yelp:test:17126.para:
I find it incredibly distressing to rate Amore with only 3 stars! We've been frequenting this place for over a year, even when I was diagnosed with celiac disease and needed to go gluten-free. I waited patiently, ordering only the Chicken Vesuvio, until they started offering gluten-free options recently. 

While I understand the risk of contamination when ordering in, I am both vigilant and somewhat overly cautious... I've never had an issue before, but tonight, I received wheat pasta instead of gluten-free pasta. When I called to inquire, the response was dismissive, akin to a pizza with the wrong toppings rather than a serious health concern that could send me to the hospital. Not only were they nonchalant about the situation, but I even had to bring up the refund myself. After a brief verbal disagreement, the delivery person eventually refunded us and gave us a new meal, but there's no way I'll be eating their food again. 

As I mentioned earlier, I truly dislike reducing the star rating.

yelp:test:17128.orig:
I can't even comment on the food because it never came. I ordered through Grub Hub at 6:30 and they said it would be an hour. It's not 9 and still nothing. In the mean time there have been three calls to grub hub and one directly to the restaurant. Each call promised a delivery time which wasn't met. They tried blaming a little drizzle for their driver not getting here the first time, then they were slammed, then some other nonsense . On the last call to Grub Hub they said the driver was just a minute or two away and they would refund me the whole order and he would still deliver it to apologize for the wait. That was 15 minutes ago. These guys have horrible service and and always making up some bull***t excuse as to why they can't do their job. Avoid this place like the plague, as a Chicagoan, I can honestly say, no self respecting Chicago eatery would ever treat a customer like this.


EDIT: Food finally got here 9:30 .. food's cold, my soda is warm, the fries are soggy and the taste is just ok. Between the refund of my order and grubhub sending me coupons to make up for the horrible service, I was paid to eat here, and still feel like I overpayed.
yelp:test:17128.para:
I can't say anything about the food since it hasn't arrived yet. I placed my order via Grub Hub at 6:30 and was told it would take an hour. It's now 9:00, and there's still no sign of it. During this time, I made three calls to Grub Hub and one directly to the restaurant, each time receiving a delivery estimate that was never met. They initially blamed the driver's delay on a light rain, then said they were busy, and finally offered some other excuse. On the last call to Grub Hub, they promised to refund the entire order and deliver it to apologize for the wait, but that was 15 minutes ago. Their service is terrible, and they always come up with ridiculous excuses. As a Chicagoan, I can confidently say that no respectable Chicago eatery would treat customers this way. 

EDIT: The food finally arrived at 9:30. The food was cold, the soda was warm, the fries were soggy, and the taste was just okay. With the refund of my order and the coupons from Grub Hub to compensate for the poor service, I felt like I was paid to eat here, and I still feel like I overpaid.

yelp:test:17183.orig: The menu isn't large,  but the food is very tasty!  I haven't tasted any of the beers but I hear they are great.  Wait staff are always timely and attentive.
yelp:test:17183.para: While the menu is not extensive, the food is exceptionally delicious! I haven't tried any of the beers, but I've heard they are outstanding. The waitstaff is consistently prompt and attentive.

yelp:test:17206.orig: Doesn't even deserve one star!  Terrible food that we couldn't even finish. Bad service and way over priced!  Save your $$ and appetite for another place.
yelp:test:17206.para: Absolutely not worth a single star! The food was terrible and we couldn't even finish our meals. The service was poor, and the prices were way too high. Save your money and appetite for somewhere else instead.

yelp:test:17214.orig: Okay buffet. I was had a hangover and didnt have much of a appetite. Ate one small plate. We came as lunch was still being converted. Breakfast was all your typical items. Lunch had Pho. Dessert was lots of variety. $23 or so but we was in a group so got hit with gratuity and tax. Came to about $30. One plate for $30. Sounds good haha
yelp:test:17214.para:
Sure, here's the paraphrased version:

I had a hangover and wasn't very hungry, so I only ate a small plate at the buffet. We arrived when lunch was just starting, and breakfast consisted of standard items. There was Pho for lunch, and a variety of desserts. The total came to around $30, including gratuity and tax, which was about $23 for the buffet. It felt like one plate for $30, which seemed reasonable.

yelp:test:17226.orig:
Great show !!
The hour and 1/2 with Wayne went by much to fast.....
Most people agree that Wayne Brady is the best member of the ""Whose Line is it Anyway"" improv troupe on TV. 
His Las Vegas show does not diminish that idea at all. 
His comedy is great, the jokes are so fast you are laughing off the last one when the next hits you. 
His singing talent is amazing !

The night I went the people he picked from the audience were so lame - he gave them simple tasks and they could hardly speak. If someone with some guts got up on stage this show would be hilarious. Wayne plays off the people he selects and if they help him out it would be a great show.
The only part of the show I did not care for was the tribute to Sammy Davis Jr. at the end, but after all it is Vegas so I guess it could be considered OK, but it was just not for me.
The bar going into the theatre serves up some fine drinks and that adds to the enjoyment of the show.
A smaller theater adds to the closness of the audience to the show and I do not think most  audience membersare far from the stage.
Wayne Brady is well worth your time - it just seems to go by at a rocket pace .......
yelp:test:17226.para:
What a fantastic performance! The 1.5 hours spent with Wayne Brady flew by so quickly. Many consider Wayne Brady to be the standout performer on "Whose Line Is It Anyway?" and his Las Vegas show certainly lives up to that reputation. His comedy is top-notch; the jokes come so fast that you're still laughing from one when the next one hits. His singing is truly remarkable!

On the night I attended, the audience members Wayne chose were quite lackluster. They struggled with simple tasks, and it wasn't very entertaining. If someone more confident had taken the stage, the show would have been much funnier. Wayne's chemistry with the audience members he selects is key; when they contribute positively, the show is delightful.

The only aspect I didn't enjoy was the tribute to Sammy Davis Jr. at the end, but given it's a Vegas show, I suppose it's acceptable. However, it just wasn't to my taste. The bar inside the theater offers some excellent drinks, which enhance the overall experience. The intimate setting of the theater brings the audience closer to the performance, and most people are seated near the stage.

In conclusion, Wayne Brady is definitely worth seeing, as the show seems to pass by in a flash.

yelp:test:17277.orig: Weird set up, boring ppl working there and limited choices.. But whatever we just wanted to grab a drink before our flight.
yelp:test:17277.para: An unusual setup with dull employees, and a lack of options. Still, we went there just to get a drink before our flight.

yelp:test:17320.orig: Coffee talk is a nice surprise nestled in the hum drum downtown of Mesa. I have been enjoying their coffee and live talent since I was fifteen. When I was in High School it was a ritual to hit the local dollar movie and then end the night with some coffee at coffee talk. I think the best part was hitting on boys and trying to pass as being at least eighteen years old. My reasons for going to Coffee Talk have changed over the past decade, but the atmosphere and quality drinks and pastries have not changed. There is nothing better than sitting on their back patio and enjoying the cool breeze of the fall. There is something about that place that brings me a sense of relaxation. If you enjoy artistic ambiance, coffee, and live performance's then I would recommend Coffee Talk.
yelp:test:17320.para: Coffee Talk is a delightful discovery in the otherwise routine downtown area of Mesa. I've been savoring their coffee and live performances since I was fifteen. During high school, it was a tradition to watch a dollar movie and then cap off the evening with a visit to Coffee Talk. The highlight was flirting with boys and pretending to be at least eighteen. Although my reasons for visiting have evolved over the past decade, the ambiance, the quality of their drinks and pastries, remain unchanged. There's no better feeling than sitting on their back patio during the cool autumn breeze. Something about that place provides me with a sense of tranquility. If you appreciate a creative atmosphere, great coffee, and live performances, I highly recommend Coffee Talk.

yelp:test:17346.orig: My friend took me here for a birthday dinner and it was simply amazing- on par with my favorite The Mission out in Old Town Scottsdale. We shared several dishes and we really loved everything- including the delicious margaritas! The pomegranate one I had was simply one of the best I've ever had. I'm getting hungry just thinking about their amazing menu. Yummmerz!
yelp:test:17346.para: My buddy brought me to this place for my birthday dinner, and it was fantastic—right up there with my top pick, The Mission, in Old Town Scottsdale. We tried a few dishes and enjoyed them all, especially the tasty margaritas. The pomegranate margarita was outstanding, one of the best I've ever had. I'm getting hungry just thinking about their impressive menu. Yummmerz!

yelp:test:17376.orig:
Plenty of Cougars and Black dudes, it's a porno waiting to happen. 

The $7 cover was ridiculous and I wasn't going to go in...that is until the doorman gave my friend and I (a lady too) a deal. (NO, I didn't have to do ""the dirty"" in the parking lot or put anything in my mouth! Believe me this place isn't worth that.) 

I went up to the bar to get a Stella - and got my ass grabbed three times. By whom? I don't know; it was too packed to tell. (Obviously people like this place, though I'm not sure why...)

I was lucky to get a parking space right away so that was a plus, but I don't plan on coming back, so the next guy can have it.
yelp:test:17376.para:
There were plenty of older women and African American men there, making it seem like a potential adult entertainment venue. The $7 entrance fee was steep, and I wasn't about to enter, but then the doorman offered us a deal. (Rest assured, I didn't have to perform anything inappropriate in the parking lot or anywhere else!) 

I decided to go to the bar for a Stella, but ended up having my rear end touched three times. Unfortunately, it was too crowded to identify who did it. (Clearly, many people enjoy this place, though I'm not sure why.)

I was fortunate to find a parking spot right away, which was a bonus. However, I have no intention of returning, so someone else can have the place.

yelp:test:17379.orig: Being from new jersey (and having the possessive attitude over Italian food that comes with my drivers license from thy part of the country), I was worried about eating Italian in Phoenix.  The antipasta was actually really good.  The mozzarella and prosciutto were fresh and tasty.  But only 1 1/2 of the 6 people I went out with enjoyed their entree, mostly pasta dishes that were too bland and sauceless.  The desserts were tasty.  The service was polite but slow.  I'm usually pretty forgiving but this place was not great.
yelp:test:17379.para: As a New Jerseyan with a protective stance on Italian cuisine, I was apprehensive about dining Italian in Phoenix. The antipasti turned out to be quite good; the mozzarella and prosciutto were particularly fresh and delicious. However, only 1.5 out of the 6 people in my group found their main courses enjoyable, mostly due to pasta dishes that were overly bland and lacked sauce. The desserts were pleasant. The service was courteous but rather slow. Generally, I tend to be lenient, but this restaurant didn't meet my expectations.

yelp:test:17389.orig: MORE = LESS!  With a name like MORE, isn't it supposed to be MORE?  The downstairs/lower-level area at the hotel makes a HUGE area of buffet dining.  But with the center area of salads, and fruits, and breads, then about 4 stations of various drink machines, and then the hot food area/service line...you'll quickly realize the items have been duplicated two to four times throughout....making it one of the slimmest selections at a buffet I've ever been to.  Quality is just 'okay', with sub-par bakery goods.\n\nUnless you have a free buffet coupon, I would look elsewhere.
yelp:test:17389.para: LESS IS MORE!  Given the name MORE, one would expect a greater variety. The downstairs area at the hotel offers a large buffet, but the central section with salads, fruits, and breads, along with the drink stations and hot food service line, ends up having many duplicate items. This results in one of the smallest and most repetitive buffet selections I've encountered. The quality is merely average, and the bakery items are particularly disappointing. Unless you have a free buffet coupon, I recommend exploring other options.

yelp:test:17397.orig: This is the worst restaurant ive ever ate at. Nothing is edible. Well done ny strip roast. Cold food. No flavor. No smiles, except from the lady who sat us, but we were sat at an occupied table apparantley when we came back with food people were sitting there. The creme brulee didnt have torched sugar on top. I took a few bites, left hungry, and ended up sick to my stomach! If I could give it zero stars I would have....
yelp:test:17397.para: This restaurant is the worst I've ever been to. The food is inedible—except for the well-done New York strip roast, which was the only thing remotely palatable. Everything else was cold and lacked flavor. There were no smiles from the staff, except for the lady who seated us, but we were led to an occupied table. When we returned with our food, people were already sitting there. The creme brulee didn't even have its sugar caramelized on top. I took a few bites and left feeling hungry and sick to my stomach. If I could, I'd give it zero stars.

yelp:test:17466.orig: Great place to get sushi on this side of town. Servings of the raw fish in rolls and nigiri dishes are above average size. The flavor is amazing. The tiger roll is amazing because the spicy tuna doesn't over power  the other ingredients like most places do. Def recommended.
yelp:test:17466.para: This is a fantastic spot for sushi in this area. The portions of raw fish in the rolls and nigiri are particularly generous. The taste is outstanding. What sets the tiger roll apart is that the spicy tuna complements rather than dominates the other ingredients, which is a refreshing change from other places. I highly recommend it.

yelp:test:17468.orig:
I remember when this place used to be my favorite sushi restaurant in town, Koto. I've given this place a few tries. The food has improved but the service has not. AYCE susi with a taste of Hawaii. Hawaiians are known for being laidback and friendly. 

There were plenty of empty tables when we got there yet, we had to wait for a table. Really? We placed out order. Some items took forever but some we never got. I guess our previous server was finishing up his shift but didn't notify us. We tried a few nigiri, rolls, teri beef sliders, garlic edamame, ahi poke, salmon katsu and malassadas. We didn't order that much but we spent 2 hours total here.

Lunch AYCE is from 11:30am-4pm for $21.95 and dinner AYCE is from 4pm-close for $26.95. There are certain items that are only available for dinner, limit 1/person, 2 desserts/person and there's a 90-minute limitfor AYCE. With service slower than molasses, you'll easily go over 90 minutes! 

The food was good but the service really turned us off. My boyfriend is very calm and laidback and for him to even say something about the service says a lot. The female server was borderline rude. No smile on her face, no nothing. The servers don
yelp:test:17468.para:
I used to love Koto as my go-to sushi spot, but after a few visits, I noticed the service hasn't improved much, while the food has. The restaurant offers AYCE sushi with a Hawaiian twist. Hawaiians are known for their relaxed and friendly demeanor.

When we arrived, there were plenty of empty tables, yet we had to wait for a seat. Once seated, we placed our order, but some items took ages to arrive, and others never came. It seemed our previous server was wrapping up his shift without informing us. We tried several dishes, including nigiri, rolls, teri beef sliders, garlic edamame, ahi poke, salmon katsu, and malassadas. Despite ordering a reasonable amount, we spent about two hours there.

AYCE is available for lunch from 11:30 am to 4 pm for $21.95 and for dinner from 4 pm until closing for $26.95. There are some dinner-only items, a limit of one dessert per person, and a 90-minute AYCE time limit. Given the slow service, it's easy to exceed this limit.

The food was decent, but the service was what really soured our experience. My boyfriend, who is usually very laidback, commented on the poor service, which speaks volumes. The female server seemed almost rude, with no smile or friendliness.

yelp:test:17477.orig: Service is great and the atmosphere is cool.\nMy gf and I are fans of TGI Friday and have been to multiple ones in Vegas. I just hate to say but the food at this one was not nearly as good as the other ones. We were disappointed because at places like this you look for consistency but this one wasn't prepared as well as when we went to the others. The service and everything were great which is why I gave it a 4 star but I will definitely just go to the other ones.
yelp:test:17477.para: The service is excellent, and the ambiance is pleasant, but I must admit that the food here didn't measure up to our expectations. We were hoping for consistency, as we've visited several TGI Fridays in Vegas, and this one fell short. Despite the great service, I rated it 4 stars. However, I'll stick to visiting the other locations in the future.

yelp:test:17508.orig: Not sure what all the hype is about, but it's definitely not worth the hour+ wait outside.  My group had wristbands and were on some sort of guest list, but that didn't really mean anything being that there weren't really any lines and there's just a mass of people pushing their way to get in.  Why?...I really don't know.\nWhen we finally did get in, half my group of about 20 were already pissed off, not because of the wait , but because of the rude, power-tripping bouncer/security guys out front.  While waiting to get my handstamped, I saw the bouncer push some girl just because the tip of her 2nd toe had crossed the velvet rope.  \nSo not worth it, but if you're gonna bother, have a drink or 2 before so you're immune to the long wait and rude bouncers.
yelp:test:17508.para:
I'm not convinced by the excitement around this place; the hour-long wait outside is definitely not worth it. My group had wristbands and were on a guest list, but that didn't help much since there were no real lines and the crowd was pushing to get in. I'm not sure why, but that's just how it was.

Once we finally got in, about half of the 20 of us were already upset, not because of the wait, but due to the rude and overbearing bouncers. While waiting for my handstamp, I witnessed one of them push a girl because her second toe had crossed the velvet rope.

In short, it's not worth it. If you decide to go, consider having a couple of drinks beforehand to help you cope with the long wait and the rude bouncers.

yelp:test:17525.orig: Had the absolute worst service here today.  Straight from the Amy's Baking Co handbook.  As a former regular we will never go back.  Our entire table was flabbergasted at the treatment we received, it was embarrassing.  There are plenty of decent breakfast places with great service in the area that will gladly get our business in the future.  Not this place!
yelp:test:17525.para: We experienced the worst service today, straight out of the Amy's Baking Co manual. As former regulars, we won't be returning. The entire table was shocked by how we were treated; it was quite embarrassing. There are many other breakfast spots with excellent service nearby that we'll definitely patronize instead. Not this one!

yelp:test:17569.orig: Horrible! Our waiter switched when we sat down, and a new one came up and said \""I got you guys b/c I get all the pretty ladies\"" barf. We ordered before our drinks even came, service was not good. Food was ok, but not worth the ridiculous prices even at brunch.
yelp:test:17569.para: What a terrible experience! When we sat down, a new waiter joined us, and he said, "I was assigned to you guys because I always get to talk to the pretty ladies." It was really off-putting. We ordered before our drinks arrived, and the service was poor. The food was just okay, but it definitely wasn't worth the exorbitant prices, even during brunch.

yelp:test:17610.orig: A Friend of mine really wanted to come here for dinner so a group of us (guys and girls) decided what the heck.  This place is an awesome sports bar/restaurant as big flat screen TVs were everywhere.  The girls here were no Hawaiian Tropic models, but they weren't bad looking either.  One of them had stuck up attitude and that is a big minus in my book.\n\nNow to the food.  The prices were not too bad, but we didn't know what to expect. I had the Crackling Pork Shank.  It was effin HUGE! I don't care what others may have said, but it was good.  If your Asian, Filipino, Pacific Islander..whatever, you'll like this.  We ordered other dishes which were all good, but this one stood out for me.
yelp:test:17610.para:
A friend of mine was eager to join us for dinner, so a group of us—both guys and girls—decided to give it a try. This place turned out to be a fantastic sports bar and restaurant, with flat-screen TVs scattered throughout. While the women weren't models, they weren't unattractive either. One of them had a rather snobbish attitude, which I found quite off-putting.

Moving on to the food, the prices were reasonable, but we weren't sure what to expect. I tried the Crackling Pork Shank, and it was absolutely enormous! Despite what others might say, I thought it was delicious. If you're of Asian, Filipino, or Pacific Islander descent, or even if you're not, you'll probably enjoy this dish. We also ordered other items that were all tasty, but this one really stood out to me.

yelp:test:17640.orig: of all the buffets I had in Vegas this was my least favorite!
yelp:test:17640.para: Among all the buffets I tried in Vegas, this one was the least enjoyable for me!

yelp:test:17672.orig: Love this place. Family-run, family-friendly neighborhood Italian restaurant. Their take-out/delivery is so-so in my experience, so dine in--I've never had a bad meal. Their red sauce is distinctive and the pasta tastes home-made--no corners cut, nothing from a can, so far as I can tell. Warm, friendly atmosphere. Occasionally they have live music on Fridays and Saturdays. I've always gone with my 3yo in tow, and they've always been patient and kind with him. Excellent place for parents who want a civilized meal at a place where their kids will be welcome.
yelp:test:17672.para: I adore this family-owned Italian restaurant in the neighborhood. The take-out and delivery are mediocre, so I recommend dining in, where I've never encountered a subpar meal. The red sauce is unique, and the pasta seems freshly made—no shortcuts or canned ingredients, as far as I can tell. The ambiance is warm and welcoming, and they occasionally feature live music on Fridays and Saturdays. I've brought my 3-year-old regularly, and the staff has always been patient and kind with him. It's an outstanding choice for parents seeking a refined dining experience in a kid-friendly setting.

yelp:test:17687.orig: Fresh and Easy's are great.  My only issues is how quickly some of the foods from this store go bad.  Don't buy for a week from now unless it is frozen!
yelp:test:17687.para: Fresh and Easy stores are excellent, but I have one concern: some of the foods tend to spoil rather quickly. It's best to avoid purchasing items unless you plan to use them within a few days, especially if they aren't frozen.

yelp:test:17697.orig: Love this place! Wish we had one here in CA. Great vibe once you walk through that door. Fantastic drinks and goodies!!
yelp:test:17697.para: I adore this spot! I really wish we had something similar in CA. The atmosphere is fantastic the moment you step inside. The drinks and treats are outstanding!!

yelp:test:17728.orig:
Amazing restaurant, great time, incredible STEAKS! They do steaks and wine really well.
What we ordered for a group of 5:
Apps:
Beef carpaccio- fantastic! ORDER THIS!
Brushetta- no tomato, it's different spreads but delish!!
Calamari- I would skip this...had better
Pasta: 
black fettuccini- great
Orricchette w/ sausage- so good, favorite pasta.
Sides:
Mushrooms w/ onions- great
Fries- good flavor
Mashed potatoes w/ mascarpone and poached egg- so different and amazing! TRY THESE!
MEAT:
BONE INE RIBEYE FOR 2- BEST! Ordered it medium and came a little less than medium. The meat was fantastic all the way thru. Best part was the bone and you can eat it like a rib!
Filet mignon- delish
Lamb chops- incredible!

They bring you rolls with 2 spreads. One is butter, the other is whipped pork fat with rosemary, thyme, garlic, salt and pepper. TRY IT! It's so good we wanted to lick the ramekin.

I started off a little bugged because we had to wait almost 30 min after our reservation time to be seated. So we went to the bar and something about the bartender rubbed me the wrong way. He got us our drinks and kind ofnignored us for some customers that seemed like regulars. That'
yelp:test:17728.para:
What an amazing restaurant with fantastic steaks and excellent wine service! Here’s what we enjoyed for a group of five:

Appetizers:
- Beef carpaccio - absolutely fantastic! I highly recommend this.
- Brushetta - no tomatoes, just different spreads, and it was delicious!
- Calamari - I’d suggest skipping this one; it wasn’t as good as others.

Pasta:
- Black fettuccini - great
- Orricchette with sausage - so good, it was my favorite pasta.

Sides:
- Mushrooms with onions - great
- Fries - good flavor
- Mashed potatoes with mascarpone and poached egg - unique and amazing! Don’t miss these!

Main Courses:
- Bone-in ribeye for two - outstanding! It was a bit undercooked, but the meat was fantastic throughout. The bone was also delicious and edible.
- Filet mignon - delightful
- Lamb chops - incredible!

They serve rolls with two spreads: regular butter and a whipped pork fat spread with rosemary, thyme, garlic, salt, and pepper. Try it; it’s so good we wanted to clean the ramekin.

Initially, I was a bit frustrated as we had to wait almost 30 minutes past our reservation time to be seated. We went to the bar, and the bartender seemed to prioritize regulars over us, which wasn’t ideal.

yelp:test:17731.orig: Carnet Vino came highly recommended however right from the start and it was nothing but a sheer disaster.  Sure shit from poor service to the most overpriced meals and unflavorful food we were shocked.  Luckily enough we are getting this meal complementary from the casino if we had to pay out of our pockets for this meal I don't think we would've left ever paying........as other review stated kids size meal portions and lackluster flavor of the steak and even the pastas.  We had better steaks at outback or even chilies this was a joke please stay away!!!!!!!
yelp:test:17731.para: Carnet Vino was highly praised, but our experience was a complete disaster from the beginning. The service was terrible, the food was overpriced and tasteless, leaving us in shock. Fortunately, the casino offered us a complimentary meal; otherwise, we wouldn't have left without a complaint. The portions were tiny, and the steak and pasta lacked flavor. We had better steaks at Outback or Chili's; this place was a joke. Please avoid it at all costs!!!!

yelp:test:17749.orig:
It seems difficult to find a coffee shops in Tempe south of the 60. At least two have closed their doors since I've lived in Tempe during the last 5 years.

Solo has filled a much-needed niche.

They have good coffee. Really good coffee. So good that the owner/barista actually asked me how the coffee was before I left. Imagine that! A barista that cares about his pour.

The internet is free and fast (the latter might be because it is still pretty unknown... I haven't been in there and seen more than two other customers) and there are plenty of places to plug-in.

The place has a comfortable feel to it... an eclectic mix of ikea bookshelves, modern photography, vintage records and lamps, and antique furniture pieces.

One somewhat odd thing: liquid sugar. Out of a little dispenser. I ended up drizzling it down the side of my mug. Maybe its more eco-friendly than sugar packets? I dunno.

My only gripe: as of early April 2008, they are only open until 9pm, making it an unreasonable destination for a late night of studying or socializing. They say this is going to change.

They seem to be rolling things out slowly. They do accept credit cards (though a previous review ind
yelp:test:17749.para:
It appears challenging to locate coffee shops in Tempe south of Loop 60. At least two have shut down since I moved here five years ago.

Solo has filled a crucial gap.

Their coffee is excellent. The barista even inquired about the quality before I left, which is quite rare. 

Free and speedy internet is available, though it may be fast due to its relative obscurity; I've only seen two other customers there. There are plenty of outlets for charging devices.

The atmosphere is cozy, with a mix of IKEA bookshelves, modern photography, vintage records and lamps, and antique furniture.

One peculiar feature is the liquid sugar served from a dispenser. I ended up drizzling it into my mug. It might be more eco-friendly than sugar packets, but I'm not sure.

My only complaint is that they close at 9 PM as of early April 2008, which makes it unsuitable for late-night studying or socializing. They plan to extend their hours.

yelp:test:17764.orig: Went at about lunchtime on a Sunday, and there was only about a five minute wait. This is a busy little place, but seems worth the wait. The biscuits and gravy were very good, and the portions large. They have a nice selection of mini pies and the entire menu is available all day long. The waitress was very attentive and efficient, and the food was delish. I'll be back!
yelp:test:17764.para: Visited around noon on a Sunday and faced a brief wait of about five minutes. This place is quite bustling, but it's definitely worth the wait. The biscuits and gravy were excellent, and the portions were generous. They offer a variety of mini pies, and the menu is available throughout the day. The waitress was both attentive and efficient, and the food was delicious. I plan to return!

yelp:test:17768.orig: I'm reviewing the retail side of Fine's Cellars since it's out of my normal area of town and I have not eaten at its restaurant.  Let me just say this about Michael Fine, he's been in the retail end of the wine business for a long time (name a longer running wine store than Sportsmans) and he knows both a lot about wine and a lot about what wine sells.  I recently visited FC for a saturday afternoon tasting.  Now, all of the wine tasted was meant to be drunk NOW.  This wasn't a high-end tasting but that's exactly the point.  We left the tasting with two cases of good wine, wine we'll drink most evenings, and paid less than $9 a bottle.  Good luck finding a better deal anywhere in town.  Fine Cellars is serious about fair pricing on good, easy drinking wines.  Care for something more up-town?  This is your place for once-a-year Turley allocations or any number of terrific bottles.  Chateau Montelena, Schaffer, Freemark Abbey, they're all here.  Looking for something truly special?  There's a good selection of old world varietals and if you talk with Michael  he'll find something for you.  This is not the largest wine retailer in town but you won't be disappointed with the selection,
yelp:test:17768.para: I'm evaluating Fine's Cellars' retail operations as they're not in my usual area, and I haven't dined there before. Michael Fine has been in the wine retail business for a long time—hard to find a store with more experience than Sportsman's—and he has extensive knowledge of wine and what sells well. My recent Saturday afternoon tasting session confirmed this. All the wines tasted were meant for immediate consumption, which is the point. We left with two cases of good wine, suitable for most evenings, and paid less than $9 per bottle. It's hard to find a better deal in town. Fine Cellars focuses on offering fair prices for quality, easy-drinking wines. For those seeking more upscale options, this is the place for rare Turley allocations or other excellent bottles like Chateau Montelena, Schaffer, and Freemark Abbey. If you're looking for something truly special, there's a good selection of old-world varietals, and Michael can help you find the perfect choice. While it's not the largest wine retailer in town, the selection is impressive and won't disappoint.

yelp:test:17781.orig:
This was my second time trying this place. My experience was much like the first, except they were much busier this time. 

This is sushi, sashimi, and apps only. The menu has your  typical sushi and rolls, but they do have some very unique menu items and daily specials. I had two sushi orders and a spider roll, edemame to start. It was serviceable and comparable to what I've had elsewhere.

Why's they get two stars? First, I ordered my roll ""no avocado"" , as I'm allergic.  The bill even said ""no avocado"". Guess what, lots of avocado on my roll. 

Just like my first time here, I noticed that things taste funny. The fried soft shell crab in the roll tasted like old oil, while the sushi rice was too vinegary. Even the soy sauce was funky, with a chemical taste. 

Service is slightly less than what I expect from a sushi place. It's obviously family; the guy, his wife, and their kid, along with a dude int he back frying stuff up. If they would grease up the customers a little and ask if they want a drink or dessert, I'll bet that they would make more money every night. 

I need a neighborhood sushi spot, so I'm going to give them one more shot.
yelp:test:17781.para:
On my second visit to this establishment, the experience was similar to my first, though it was noticeably busier. They offer sushi, sashimi, and appetizers, with a mix of standard items and some unique options and daily specials. I ordered two sushi pieces and a spider roll, starting with edamame. The food was decent and comparable to other places I've visited.

The reason for the two-star rating is that my "no avocado" roll, which the bill specified, still contained a lot of avocado. Additionally, the flavors were off. The fried soft shell crab in the roll tasted like it was cooked in old oil, and the sushi rice was too vinegary. Even the soy sauce had a chemical taste.

The service was a bit below my expectations for a sushi restaurant. It's a family-run place—dad, mom, kid, and someone in the back cooking. If they offered a little more attention, like greasing up the customers and asking if they wanted drinks or dessert, they could potentially earn more each night.

I'm still in need of a good neighborhood sushi spot, so I'll give them another chance.

yelp:test:17783.orig: Sushi is pretty good but prices are outrageous. I bought two drinks and two rolls for happy hour and two rolls after and the bill was over $60.
yelp:test:17783.para: Sushi is quite enjoyable, but the prices are excessively high. During happy hour, I ordered two drinks and two rolls, and even added two more rolls later, and the total came to over $60.

yelp:test:17801.orig:

yelp:test:17801.para:
Womp womp womp. This place is such a letdown; I can't fathom why people frequent it or why it's always so crowded. The only explanation I can think of is the great deals for industry workers. Since I'm not a casino employee and don't appreciate paying $12 for a small, watered-down drink, I've never been impressed.

yelp:test:17852.orig: We love Zada's! Jodie makes the best Mimosa and Bloody Mary and always has a smile on her face.  Great variety and selection of healthy, fresh, and local food whether you are a vegetarian or not. The bacon is amazing as is the French toast and their Huevos. Sometimes we just grab a biscuit to go which is also a great option. \nDon't miss out on this spot! It does get crowded at high times but Jodie will make you a mimosa or there is free coffee while you wait!
yelp:test:17852.para: We adore Zada's! Jodie's mimosas and Bloody Marys are outstanding, and she always greets everyone with a cheerful smile. They offer a fantastic range of healthy, fresh, and locally sourced dishes, suitable for both vegetarians and meat-eaters alike. The bacon, French toast, and Huevos are particularly delicious. Even a quick biscuit to go is a delightful choice. Don't overlook this place; though it can get busy, Jodie ensures you get your mimosa, and there's free coffee if you're waiting!

yelp:test:17859.orig:
This place was a flop. Was visiting a friend in Chandler and found this place on mobile Yelp. Had 68-something reviews and 4/5 stars which almost always means it will be a good place. Boy I was wrong this time.

I hate those lengthy reviews talking about unimportant things so I'll stick to the main point. The restaurant itself was clean and you can sit down comfortably.

The waiter highly recommended the pork avodovo plate, which is pork that is served doused with either a green or red sauce with beans and rice on the side. I cannot take spicy food, and the waiter insisted the red version isn't spicy. My friend ordered the green version since he DID want spice.

Ended up being the other way around...the red-sauce was oil-based and it was SPICY. My friend's green one was not spicy at all, and that was a more water-based sauce. He cleaned his plate and I barely touched mine. The waiter offerred to bring something else but I refused, barely having eaten any of it. I was put off by the waiter's ""recommendations,"" and therefore assumed everything else was going to be ridiculously spicy. Plus, I shouldn't have to wait and then be delayed from leaving there for another 45 mins.
yelp:test:17859.para:
This place turned out to be a disappointment. While visiting a friend in Chandler, I came across it on Yelp. With 68 reviews and a 4/5 star rating, I expected it to be good. Unfortunately, I was wrong this time.

To the point, the restaurant was clean and the seating was comfortable. The waiter strongly suggested the pork avodovo plate, which consists of pork in either green or red sauce, served with rice and beans. Since I can't handle spicy food, the waiter assured me the red sauce wasn't spicy. My friend opted for the green sauce, as he wanted some heat.

It turned out the opposite was true—the red sauce was very spicy, while the green sauce was milder. My friend finished his plate, but I barely ate mine. The waiter offered to bring something else, but I declined. I was disappointed by the waiter's "recommendations" and assumed the rest of the food would be overly spicy. Additionally, I shouldn't have had to wait another 45 minutes before leaving.

yelp:test:17861.orig: I really like the atmosphere of this place. I think they were a little short staffed or something the night I was there because service was a little slow. But they made up for it by treating me to a margarita. Enchiladas with chicken and red sauce were quite decent!
yelp:test:17861.para: I enjoyed the ambiance here, but the service was a bit sluggish, possibly due to a shortage of staff. However, they compensated by offering me a margarita. The chicken enchiladas with red sauce were pretty good!

yelp:test:17870.orig: Drove by today and noticed that It's a Grind has been replaced with Dunkin Donuts :) (sigh)
yelp:test:17870.para: Passed by today and saw that It's a Grind has been swapped out for Dunkin Donuts (sigh).

yelp:test:17872.orig: I came in town for the week and stopped by this Coffee Bean location. I love the location at an outdoor mall. Coffee Bean is hands down better than Starbucks. I always stop at one when in CA or AZ. I love the Ultimate Mocha blended drink with coffee beans. This is similar to the Java chip at Starbucks but it taste so much better then at Starbucks. So if your in town, I recommend paying this location a visit and enjoy their coffee. At the same time catch a movie or shop while your here. I wish they would have more locations in Texas.
yelp:test:17872.para: During my week in town, I visited this Coffee Bean store at an outdoor mall, and I really enjoy it. Coffee Bean surpasses Starbucks in my opinion. I always make a point to stop by when I'm in California or Arizona. I particularly love their Ultimate Mocha blended drink, which has a taste that far exceeds that of Starbucks' Java Chip. If you're in the area, I suggest stopping by to try their coffee. You can also catch a movie or do some shopping while you're there. I wish they had more locations in Texas.

yelp:test:17893.orig: When I moved to the valley 14 years ago, University Animal Hospital was recommended to me for boarding.  They were too far away from where I lived to go to for vet visits.  I took one of my dogs there for years until she passed away.  I got two more dogs and started boarding them there as well until I came home from a trip to find 5 staples in one of my dogs hip with no explanation as to what happened other than \""we came in one morning and found her bleeding\"".  The best part - I was billed for the surgery.  Really?  They finally refunded me my money for the surgery and the management was responsive after I called.  But, I've never gone back.  This wasn't a small cut - it took 5 staples (STAPLES) to close the wound.  My regular vet tended to her afterwards.  This was a few years ago and I wrote a review on Google at that time.  But now with yelp it deserves being mentioned again.
yelp:test:17893.para: Fourteen years ago, when I relocated to the valley, University Animal Hospital was suggested for my pet's boarding needs. However, it was too distant for regular vet visits. I brought one of my dogs there for years until it passed away. Subsequently, I boarded two additional dogs there. Upon returning from a trip, I discovered that one of my dogs had five staples in its hip, with no explanation given other than "we found her bleeding when we came in one morning." Moreover, I was charged for the surgery. Really? Eventually, they refunded my money, and the management responded after I contacted them. Nevertheless, I never returned. The injury was significant, requiring five staples to close. My usual vet provided follow-up care. This incident occurred a few years ago, and I had already written about it on Google. Now, with Yelp, it deserves another mention.

yelp:test:17925.orig:
Went to Pearl tonight with my roommate after hearing rave reviews from a few people....

Walking up you can clearly tell it's a hot spot.  It looked busy, and when we walked through the door it was obvious as to why--it's very small.  The tables are super close together so if you're anything bigger than a 6 ladies...go somewhere else, seriously. I had to interrupt the next table at least 3 times in first sitting down in my seat, going to the restroom once/coming back and then leaving for the night.  It was just awkward. They also first sat us outside without even asking which we preferred (inside/out that is) 

We had looked at the menu before arriving and was very excited to try a few different things. We got the cucumber salad (very good) and seaweed salad (equally as good-and they dont add lettuce to it to make it look like more), shrimp tempura roll (good) spicy tuna (chunks of tuna were way too big and it just wasn't good), Pearl necklace (far from impressed) and the napolean dynamite (pretty good).....

All in all the sushi filled my stomach but i didn't finish either of my rolls (which is not like me).  I could see coming to this place for drinks and maybe a small plat
yelp:test:17925.para:
Tonight, I went to Pearl with my roommate following some enthusiastic recommendations. As we approached, it was evident that it was a popular spot, bustling with activity. Upon entering, it became clear why—it's quite compact, with tables placed very close together. If you're not petite, you might want to look elsewhere; I had to interrupt the next table at least three times when I first sat down, went to the restroom, and then left early due to the awkwardness. They also seated us outside without asking if we preferred to be inside or outside.

Beforehand, we had studied the menu and were eager to try several dishes. We ordered the cucumber salad (excellent), seaweed salad (also very good, without added lettuce), shrimp tempura roll (good), spicy tuna (with chunks of tuna that were too large and not enjoyable), Pearl necklace (disappointing), and the Napoleon dynamite (pretty good). 

Overall, the sushi satisfied my hunger, but I didn't finish either of my rolls, which is unusual for me. I can see this place being a good spot for drinks and a light meal.

yelp:test:17943.orig: We come here almost twice a week, and love it! This morning, while running late, I asked my husband to pick up milk for our daughter. I called whole foods and Diana was kind enough to bring the milk to customer service so my husband could run in and out w our toddler. Impressed that a large chain still has customers at the heart of their business. We will continue to shop here.
yelp:test:17943.para: We visit almost twice a week and adore this place! This morning, as we were running late, I asked my husband to get milk for our daughter. When I called Whole Foods, Diana kindly brought the milk to customer service, allowing my husband to quickly pop in and out with our toddler. I was impressed to see that a big chain still prioritizes its customers. We plan to keep shopping here.

yelp:test:17990.orig: Above and beyond the type of service you'd expect, friendly personel and Zack helped me out of a real bind. Thank you all for your great service and since finding out you are closed on Sundays I want a job! : )
yelp:test:17990.para: In addition to the excellent service I expected, the friendly staff, especially Zack, assisted me when I was in a difficult situation. I'm grateful for your great service, and now that I know you're closed on Sundays, I'm considering applying for a position with you! : )

yelp:test:18010.orig: 2 drinks, one salad, one bread and one appetizer for $60. Are you kidding me. A small dinner portion salad, ceviche that dis not have marinated shrimp and 2.50 for a small bread. We are used to pay for great food and small portions but not small salads by a movie theatre. No wonder the owners are just hanging out and the place is not as busy for a Friday night. Shame on you for treating your customers like this.
yelp:test:18010.para: Two drinks, a salad, an appetizer, and a piece of bread cost $60. Are you serious? The salad is a small serving, the ceviche lacks marinated shrimp, and the bread is only $2.50 for a small portion. We typically expect good food with smaller portions, but not a small salad from a movie theater. It's no wonder the owners are idle, and the place isn't busy on a Friday night. You should be ashamed for treating your customers this way.

After seating ourselves and ordering drinks, we noticed they didn't have a bone-in filet on their menu. yelp:test:18048.orig: Yes I'm a meat lover.  Call me a caveman, I just love to eat a big juicy steak.   Being in Hawaii we are a little limited to steakhouses but I have been to most of them at least once.  Morton's, Hy's, DK's, Ruth Chris, and also other with steak like Kincaids, Shoreside Grill, and even Ruby Tuesdays.  Well, you get the jist.   I normally will opt for a Ribeye whenever possible and then maybe a NY or T-bone. I figured he'd be the best person to ask for an honest opinion.  He recommended a few places we could try but said if given the choice we should go to CUT.  That sealed it, CUT it was.  I checked Open Table to see if I needed to book way ahead but it seemed like we should be fine booking a day in advanced.  Great considering we hardly know where we will be in Vegas day to day and hour to hour.  Onc
yelp:test:18048.para:
Sure, I'm a big fan of meat, especially steaks. Think of me as a caveman; I just can't get enough of a juicy, well-marbled steak. While we're in Hawaii, our options for steakhouses are somewhat limited, but I've tried most of them at least once. Places like Morton's, Hy's, DK's, and Ruth Chris, as well as others such as Kincaids, Shoreside Grill, and even Ruby Tuesdays. You get the idea.

Typically, I go for a Ribeye whenever I can, followed by a New York or T-bone. I prefer my meat to be juicy and flavorful, so I usually avoid the leaner cuts like filet.

Since we were planning a trip to Vegas, I wanted to have a nice date night with my wife and enjoy a great steak. I turned to my friend, a seasoned chef who had lived and worked in Vegas for years after graduating from the CIA and working at the Greenbrier, among other notable experiences. I thought he would be the best person to ask for an honest opinion. He recommended a few places, but ultimately suggested we go to CUT. That decision was made, and we headed to CUT.

I checked OpenTable to see if we needed to book far in advance, but it seemed we could manage a reservation a day or two in advance. This was perfect, considering our itinerary in Vegas was still quite fluid.

yelp:test:18061.para: This is the second time I've traveled from Glendale, only to find they were closed during the posted hours, which really frustrates me. yelp:test:18084.orig: I was in the market or a new Computer and thought I would give them a try. I went in and talked to Mr. Cady about my options. He showed me some models that where out with Linix on them. I checked them out and was very impressed!!!! I did not know that with Linix you get free  software. yelp:test:18084.para: When I was looking to buy a new computer, I decided to visit Redseven and spoke with Mr. Cady about my choices. He demonstrated some Linux-based models to me, which I found quite impressive. I was surprised to learn that Linux comes with free software. After he assembled the computer for me, which I've been using for a couple of weeks now, I'm extremely satisfied. Thank you, Redseven!

yelp:test:18095.orig:
To keep it simple: La Bocca is sexy, posh, upbeat, fun. 

The staff is always super down to earth, respectful, and attentive. I love the energy of this place.. The food? Phenomenal. Fresh ingredients.. delicious wine selection.

I'm addicted.. and going here again tomorrow night.
yelp:test:18095.para: In a nutshell, La Bocca is captivating, elegant, lively, and enjoyable. The staff is consistently down-to-earth, courteous, and attentive. I adore the place's vibrant atmosphere. As for the food, it's outstanding—made with fresh ingredients and an impressive wine list. I'm hooked and plan to return tonight.

yelp:test:18102.orig: Roberto's has the best carne asada burritos and the fixin's at the salsa bar are tasty. Red and green sauce and spicy carrots and lime wedges . Also enjoy the 3 rolled tacos with guc .I do agree with some of the reviews about the place being a mess. But that is some of the appeal to most taco shops. I mean risking your life for good tacos and burritos is exciting and I also agree this place is perfect after a late night of drinking.
yelp:test:18102.para: Roberto's offers outstanding carne asada burritos, and the salsa bar features delicious red and green sauces, spicy carrots, and lime wedges. I also appreciate the three rolled tacos with guac. While some reviews mention the place is messy, that's part of the charm for many taco spots. After all, taking a risk for great burritos and tacos is thrilling, and I concur that this place is ideal for post-drinking nights.

yelp:test:18107.orig:
i originally went here bc i was in the mood for kabobs.

but the gentleman working seemed to have no clue what i was talking about. i always thought greek places served awesome kabobs! WHAATT

anyway, i decided to go for the greek salad instead and oh my golly.....so dang good.

they really load you up with all the wonderful ingredients that make a greek salad amazing. the chicken was quite tasty as well! another great lunch spot near work.
yelp:test:18107.para:
Initially, I chose this place because I was craving kabobs. However, the staff member didn't seem to understand what I was asking for. I usually find Greek restaurants to serve fantastic kabobs, but not this time!

So, I opted for the Greek salad, and it was absolutely delicious. They generously portioned it with all the delightful ingredients that make a Greek salad so special. The chicken was also quite enjoyable! Overall, it's another excellent spot for lunch near my workplace.

yelp:test:18118.orig:
After hearing about Stacy's and hearing how great it was, I was a bit skeptical to try it.  Well.....that was 3 months and 6 visits ago!

Stacy's is great. The best BBQ here in Phoenix for sure. 

In my opinion, the meats are the real winner here. After sampling each kind of meat (except the catfish) I've decided that my favorite way to eat here is to come with a friend and order up a load of food.  The brisket and the rib tips are the best. The pork is good but pretty flavorless without the sauce. 

I always prefer to taste my BBQ without sauce to see the real flavors. Same here, I order with the sauce on the side. Although they always give me a look, they still serve it as requested. 

I happen to really like their sauce, I just like to use a little at a time rather than having the meat drowned in it. They are very liberal with the portions and their sauce so be careful not to over order. 

As for the sides. I've enjoyed their sweet potato fries and cole slaw. Was a little disappointed in the fried pickles and okra as they are breaded instead of battered and I wasn't crazy about the breading. 

As everyone has stated, its cash only and has limited parking. 

Stacy p
yelp:test:18118.para:
After initially being hesitant based on what I'd heard about Stacy's, I decided to give it a try 3 months ago, making 6 visits since then. Now, I can confidently say that Stacy's is fantastic. In my view, it's the best BBQ place in Phoenix.

The meats are truly outstanding. After trying various cuts (excluding the catfish), I've concluded that I prefer to come with a friend and order a generous amount of food. The brisket and rib tips stand out as the best. While the pork is decent, it lacks flavor without the sauce.

I always opt to taste the BBQ without sauce to appreciate the true flavors. I consistently ask for the sauce on the side, and they always accommodate my request. I particularly enjoy their sauce but prefer to use it sparingly rather than dousing the meat.

The portions are very generous, as are the servings of sauce, so be cautious not to overorder. The sides, such as sweet potato fries and coleslaw, are enjoyable, but I was a bit let down by the fried pickles and okra, which are breaded rather than battered.

Like others have noted, it's cash only and has limited parking. Overall, Stacy's is a great choice for BBQ in Phoenix.

yelp:test:18162.orig: Non-smoking establishment, despite the outdoor bar area. Food is unmemorable, service is fine, plenty of alternatives nearby.
yelp:test:18162.para: This is a non-smoking venue, though it has an outdoor bar section. The food lacks standout qualities, but the service is satisfactory. There are many other good options in the vicinity.

yelp:test:18205.orig:
One of my favorite sushi experiences everrrr.  I've been here three times on three different Vegas visits and it's always delicious.

On the last visit, we opted for a tasting menu for a party of 7.  The waiter was selling it pretty hard and we finally gave in.  Pretty glad we did too.  We asked for a lower end menu costing $50-55/head and the kitchen did a superb job.  We were able to taste way more than we would have ever imagined if we were to order a la carte.

Edamame
Rock Shrimp Tempura - (MUST GET)
Yellowtail Seviche Taquitos - (YUM!)
Yellowtail w/ jalapeno and lemongrass taradito (this is the best one)
Kanpachi w/ yuzu sea salt and black truffle oil taradito 
Tuna w/ granny smith serrano and lime taradito
Salmon w/ orange and miso taradito
Filet Mignon Robato w/ 4 kinds of sauteed mushrooms (YUUUM)
Chilean Sea Bass w/ Miso Sauce anticucho w/ Peruvian Corn (GIANT CORN-delicious fish)
Neo Tokyo roll
Green Envy roll
El Topo roll
Pacific roll
Rainbow Dragon roll

Drinks  - overall they have pretty good drinks, and if you are clever enough to score some 2 for 1 coupons, it's worth it!  I like the Samba Juice and the Lemon Samurai. :)
yelp:test:18205.para:
I've had one of my absolute favorite sushi experiences at this place. I've visited three times during my Vegas trips, and the food has never disappointed.

On my last visit, we decided to go for the tasting menu with a group of seven. The waiter was quite enthusiastic about it, and we ended up giving in. We were really happy we did. We opted for a more affordable menu priced at $50-55 per person, and the kitchen did an outstanding job. We got to sample a wide variety of dishes that we wouldn't have tried otherwise.

Here are some highlights:
- Edamame
- Rock Shrimp Tempura (a must-try)
- Yellowtail Seviche Taquitos (delicious)
- Yellowtail with jalapeno and lemongrass (the best one)
- Kanpachi with yuzu sea salt and black truffle oil
- Tuna with granny smith serrano and lime
- Salmon with orange and miso
- Filet Mignon Robato with sautéed mushrooms (amazing)
- Chilean Sea Bass with miso sauce and Peruvian corn (huge corn, very tasty fish)
- Neo Tokyo roll
- Green Envy roll
- El Topo roll
- Pacific roll
- Rainbow Dragon roll

The drinks were pretty good too. If you manage to get some 2 for 1 coupons, it's definitely worth it! I particularly enjoyed the Samba Juice and the Lemon Samurai.

yelp:test:18219.orig: I dont recall exactly what Ive had here as Ive been 2-3 times, I just like the originality. It is a fun place they truly have an eclectic menu with a lot of orginality. I also really appreciate that the bartenders had a great knowledge of all the different saki they have.
yelp:test:18219.para: While I haven't visited recently and have been here 2-3 times, I'm drawn to the place for its unique vibe. They offer a diverse and creative menu that stands out. Additionally, I admire how knowledgeable the bartenders are about the various types of sake they serve.

yelp:test:18233.orig: This place is always a stop when i am out in AZ.  Loves it!!!!!!!!!! Great burger, great fries, not too expensive, usually pretty quick.  I only wish they had in-n-out where i live.   I like to stick  with the double double and fries.  My gf likes to get her fries well done.  Its a nice option if you like them extra crispy, but regular tastes fine to me.
yelp:test:18233.para: I always make a point to visit this place whenever I'm in AZ, and I absolutely adore it! The burgers are fantastic, the fries are delicious, and it doesn't break the bank. They're usually quite speedy too. I wish we had something similar where I live. My go-to is the double double and fries. My girlfriend prefers her fries well done, and while the extra crispy option is great for her, I find the regular fries just fine.

yelp:test:18246.orig: Vraiment pas terrible et le service laisse a d\u00e9sir\u00e9
yelp:test:18246.para: Très pas mal du tout, et le service laisse à désirer.

yelp:test:18258.orig:
21 Dec 2013

This was my first time going there, and I took my girlfriend around 4:30pm on a Saturday. It was already packed, so I had a good feeling! We got seated immediately since it was just the two of us. We looked at the menu and was surprised to see that they had half off selected sushi for 1/3 of the menu--maybe more.

We ordered a salmon nigiri and seared white tuna nigiri. Hands down these were the best in the area. We also got the Gordon Gecko, Eating Nemo and Chuck Norris rolls. Eating Nemo was a glorified california roll--I wouldn't get it a second time. Gordon Gecko was okay. Chuck Norris tasted like a Doritos. Even though we didn't really like the rolls, all of the fish served was fresh!
yelp:test:18258.para:
On December 21, 2013, this was my initial visit, and I brought my girlfriend to the restaurant around 4:30 PM on a Saturday. It was already quite busy, which gave me a positive vibe. We were seated right away as it was just the two of us. We perused the menu and were surprised to find that they offered half-price sushi for a significant portion of the menu—possibly more than a third.

We ordered salmon and seared white tuna nigiri, which we deemed the best in the area. We also tried the Gordon Gecko, Eating Nemo, and Chuck Norris rolls. The Eating Nemo was essentially a California roll and wasn't something I'd order again. The Gordon Gecko was merely satisfactory, while the Chuck Norris tasted like a Doritos. Despite not enjoying the rolls much, all the fish served was fresh!

yelp:test:18261.orig: My fianc\u00e9 and I went there tonight to grab a quick drink after dinner. We were both very disappointed with the service. We waited for at least 10 minutes while waiters scurried past us at least 6 times before we even got a hello. My fianc\u00e9 ordered a house margarita and was given Cabo Wabo tequila and an extra 2 dollar charge for adding some lime juice and sweet and sour without being warned. Her drink ended up being more expensive than any other drinks on the menu and she could barely drink it because it was so poorly made. We asked the waiter and he just said...yeah that's how we do a margarita. We will not be going back.
yelp:test:18261.para: My fiancé and I stopped by for a quick drink post-dinner tonight, but we were both quite let down by the service. We had to wait around for at least 10 minutes while waiters seemed to rush past us multiple times without even acknowledging us. My fiancé ordered a house margarita, only to be served Cabo Wabo tequila and charged an extra $2 for lime juice and sweet and sour, without any prior notice. Her drink turned out to be more expensive than any other on the menu and was barely palatable due to poor preparation. When we inquired with the waiter, he simply stated that's how they make margaritas there. We definitely won't be returning.

yelp:test:18271.orig:
Dan P. wrote a very well thought out review that I agreed with upon my visit. So instead of just reiterating everything he said, I thought I would share it...

""I ate here last night and I've never been to a place that has so much potential to be a destination restaurant only to have itself shoot itself in the foot. The owner has to be blind to not see what growth could come and business to be made if he just made a few minor changes.

The atmosphere is unique and unlike anything out there. Roast your own s'mores for dessert? Hell ya! The live country music goes right in with the motif and the buildings surrounding you, damn, I felt right in my own wagon circle on the plains! Though I must admit, I don't think the cowboys nailed random revolutionary quotes and bill of rights amendments to every fixture they had. I came last night for a western experience, not to be lectured everywhere I looked like I was in high school history class.

Sadly, everything else is so poorly thought out that the charm washes right off you. You stand in line for an hour just to ORDER the food, you still get asked for a tip even though there are no servers, 20 mins to wait for the food to get read
yelp:test:18271.para:
Dan P. wrote a thoroughly considered review that resonated with me after my visit. Rather than repeating his points, I wanted to share his insights...

"The place has immense potential to become a top destination, yet it squanders its opportunities with a few minor adjustments. The ambiance is distinctive and unlike anything else, with the option to roast your own s'mores for dessert—definitely a highlight. The live country music fits the theme, and the surrounding decor made me feel like I was in my own wagon circle on the plains. However, I noticed that the cowboys didn't seem to have posted random revolutionary quotes and amendments everywhere, which was a bit off-putting. I went there for a western experience, not a history lesson.

Unfortunately, the execution is so flawed that the initial charm fades. You wait an hour just to place your order, and you're still asked for a tip despite no servers. The food takes 20 minutes to be readied."

yelp:test:18310.para: This establishment is no longer open for operations. :(

yelp:test:18354.orig:

I would suggest this to other mountain bikers as well to avoid any frustrations.  Hikers have THE RIGHT OF WAY and that is that, so let us be courteous and careful when we are zipping past families with small children and pets.  I hike that area as well with my wife and children and I sometimes get irritated at the mountain bikers that just fly by without even slowing down.  

Several trails in the area provide a variety of intensity for the people who want a challenge.  The trails can be a little technical if you are not familiar with ""baby head"" rocks sticking up, but it also prepares you for some of the other trails Arizona has to offer, like South Mountain, and Trail 100.  All of the trails are ""ride able"", however, you may encounter some technical areas or long steep climbs that will definitely challenge even advanced riders.  

I would recommend this park to anyone with small children who love to get outside and explore.  There is plenty of pic
yelp:test:18354.para:
Sometimes, I encounter hikers with loud music, making it hard for them to hear me approaching. To address this, I've attached a bell to my bike, which seems to help as hikers can now hear me coming. I think other mountain bikers should consider doing the same to prevent misunderstandings. Hikers have the right of way, and it's important to be considerate, especially when passing families with children and pets. I hike there with my family, and I often get annoyed by bikers who speed by without slowing down.

The area offers a range of trails with varying difficulty levels, catering to those seeking a challenge. Some trails can be tricky due to "baby head" rocks, but they also prepare you for more demanding trails like those in South Mountain or Trail 100. All trails are rideable, though you might face technical sections or long, steep climbs that can test even experienced riders.

I highly recommend this park to families with children who enjoy exploring the outdoors. There are plenty of opportunities for picnics and other activities.

yelp:test:18368.orig:
Beware Spencer's. Horrible customer service. 
We just had a very bad experience that ended with VISA ruling in our favor to refund our money. 
We ordered a Vent-a-hood from Spencers to be shipped to our home in California. They shipped it UPS and requested no signature on delivery. It was left at the door because no one was home. When we found it - we noticed the box was very damaged and the hood was dented. We immediately called Spencers and told them we received a damaged hood. Most vendors we have dealt with would simple say ""ship it back and we will replace it"". Not Spencers - their response was - that's not our problem - if you want a new one we will sell it to you - its your problem"" I was actually speechless that they would say that. 

We called UPS and they came right out and picked it up. UPS also told us that we can not claim the damage because only the shipper (aka SPENCERS) can claim damage as they contracted and paid for the shipping. This makes perfect sense to almost any average person. Spencers argued with us and said we accepted the damaged shipment so it is our problem. How could we accept a shipment that they (yes SPENCERS) did not require a signature f
yelp:test:18368.para:
Be cautious with Spencer's; their customer service is subpar. We recently encountered a disappointing situation that resulted in VISA ruling in our favor for a refund. We ordered a Vent-a-hood from Spencer's to be delivered to our California home via UPS, with instructions to avoid a signature on delivery. The item was left at the door when no one was home. Upon finding it, we noticed the box was damaged and the hood was dented. We contacted Spencer's, informing them of the damage, but their response was unsatisfactory. Most companies would offer to replace the item, but Spencer's said it wasn't their issue and suggested we buy a new one if we wanted one, shifting the responsibility to us.

I was taken aback by their attitude. When we contacted UPS, they promptly picked up the item and informed us that we couldn't claim the damage because Spencer's, as the shipper, was responsible for the claim. This made logical sense to most people. Spencer's, however, argued that by accepting the shipment, we acknowledged the damage, which is illogical given that they didn't require a signature.

yelp:test:18375.orig: Meh. It could have been a lot better. Way too many sale associates for the amount of employees doing custom fittings. Many store associates just walking around instead of helping other consumers in the store.
yelp:test:18375.para: Well, it wasn't great. There were far too many sales associates compared to those actually helping with custom fittings. Many of the store employees seemed to be just wandering around rather than assisting customers.

yelp:test:18376.orig: If you've never done Bikram Yoga before, this is a great place to start.  Not only are all the instructors extremely competent and inspiring, but there is a very friendly atmosphere here.  If you're in Phoenix and looking for a place to do Bikram, this is the place to go.  The room is large, well-lit, and has high ceilings with comfortable carpet and many mirrors.  There is free filtered water, and plenty of space and showers in the locker rooms.  Overall, a great place to practice yoga.  To borrow a phrase, at Bikram PV, all the women are strong, all the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average!
yelp:test:18376.para: For beginners in Bikram Yoga, this studio is an excellent choice. The instructors are not only highly skilled but also motivating, and the environment is warm and welcoming. If you're in Phoenix and seeking a Bikram Yoga studio, this is your best option. The studio features a spacious, brightly lit room with high ceilings, comfortable carpeting, and numerous mirrors. It offers free filtered water, ample space, and well-equipped locker rooms with showers. In summary, it's a fantastic place to practice yoga. As a humorous aside, at Bikram PV, all the women are strong, all the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average!

Instead of being 45 mins or so mass, it's 1.5 hr long.  I enjoy coming to this church.
yelp:test:18429.para: This church is quite pleasant, and the parking situation is satisfactory too. On Sundays, a lively teen mass begins at 5:30 PM, drawing a good crowd. I really appreciate attending this church.

yelp:test:18435.orig: We went on a Saturday afternoon, the decor was inviting. The staff wasn't  as friendly as some places we have been. However, they were not rude or anything. Just not overly friendly.The Rolls are good sized portions and the sauces are really yummy. Food overall was great!!!!!!
yelp:test:18435.para: On a Saturday afternoon, we visited and found the decor appealing. yelp:test:18447.orig:

yelp:test:18454.para:

yelp:test:18468.orig: Average. Service is slow inside.  You have to flag someone down if you sit at a table.  Food was so so, price is high for what you get.
yelp:test:18468.para: The service is rather sluggish, especially if you're seated at a table; you need to call someone over. The food quality is mediocre, and the prices feel steep given the offerings.

yelp:test:18480.orig: Everyone else has covered the burgers but I'm a shake fiend.  These are made from real ice cream in the stainless steel shake containers that are HUGE. yelp:test:18480.para: While others are enjoying the burgers, I'm a huge fan of shakes. They serve real ice cream in large, stainless steel containers. yelp:test:18538.para: This evening, I tried Captain Steve's takeout for the first time. We ordered three dishes: The Fisherman's Platter, Fried Oysters, and Small Shrimp. yelp:test:18560.para: While this store offers a charming selection and is more budget-friendly than the limited shopping choices on Mill, it wouldn't be my top pick for shopping at Pitaya. yelp:test:18599.orig:
I like Cracker Barrel. Well...at least this one. I've never been to any other location. 

No, the food isn't great (at least the lunch/dinner options), but it's not bad. It's been awhile since I've been here for breakfast, but if I recall that stuff is actually quite good (and cheap).

My dad freakin' LOVES this place. We came here for his birthday dinner recently so that's what I'm basing this review on. I got fried chicken and it came with two sides. The fried chicken was actually quite good. It was crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside, and nice & hot. Cracker Barrel gives you several different side options w/there meals (like, around 10). I had the hash brown casserole thingy, which is also a side they serve with breakfast meals. It's yummy! Basically, it's cheesy hash browns. I also got turnip greens. They were OK, but not great. They were kind of watery & lukewarm. I get the impression most of the sides at Cracker Barrel are cooked well in advance and just sit around most of the day. I also think turnip greens are most likely an unpopular side, and therefore probably sit around longer, without a fresh batch getting made.  I also had some lemonade to drink. It's basic
yelp:test:18599.para:
I enjoy Cracker Barrel, particularly this specific location. I haven't visited any other Cracker Barrel restaurants. 

While the lunch and dinner options aren't stellar, they're not terrible either. My last visit for breakfast was a while ago, but I remember the food being quite tasty and affordable.

My dad absolutely adores this place, and we celebrated his birthday dinner here recently, which is the basis for my review. I ordered fried chicken with two sides. The chicken was quite good; it was crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside, and served piping hot. They offer a variety of side dishes with their meals—about ten options. I tried the hash brown casserole, a breakfast side, which was delicious. It's essentially cheesy hash browns. I also had turnip greens, which were okay but not exceptional; they seemed a bit watery and lukewarm. I suspect most of the sides are prepared in advance and kept warm for a while. Turnip greens might be an unpopular choice, so they likely sit around longer without a fresh batch being made. I also had some lemonade, which was basic.

yelp:test:18621.orig:

yelp:test:18621.para:
